# The First Test — the event pool

**Session 3 · 23-40 AH · 644-661 CE · a 45-minute slot.**

> **THIS FILE IS NOT THE LECTURE. IT IS THE POOL YOU CUT DOWN TO ONE.**
> `DECISIONS.md` #20. Delete the rows you do not want. What survives is the evening. Overflow is
> not compressed — it rolls into the next session. Coverage is never bought by speeding up, which
> is the one thing the room objected to last time.

**How to cut.** Read top to bottom; it is already in narrative order. Delete whole cards. Keep
roughly **22 cards** for a 45-minute slot told calmly — the rest is deliberate over-build.

|---|---|
| Cards in the pool | **1459** |
| If every card were told | **≈ 2568 minutes** |
| The slot | **45 minutes** |
| So you are cutting | **about 98%** |

**Tier means:** `CORE` the evening breaks without it · `GOOD` include if time · `CUT` recorded so it
is never re-researched, not planned for delivery.

**Every card carries:** what happened, in tellable English · the date with its certainty label ·
the map move · a verbatim Arabic statement with its printed page and shamela link (or an explicit
"none in the sources we use") · one عبرت line · and whether it opens with a hands-up question.

## ذو النورين عثمان ؓ, and how the caliphate began

*Source note: [`uthman-the-man-and-the-caliphate-begins.md`](../docs/research/uthman-the-man-and-the-caliphate-begins.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### UTM/E-UM1 · The man قريش already knew
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before the hijra `[STANDARD]` *(to verify for any date)* · **Map:** مكة lights.

**What happened:** Before any of this he was a merchant of بنو أمية, one of the clans of قريش, known in
مكة for wealth and for a shyness that people remarked on. His mother was أروى bint كريز, and her mother was
البيضاء, the Prophet's ﷺ own paternal aunt — so the two men were already kin before they were anything else.
The books give him four names before they give him a single deed: ذو النورين, the man of the two hijras, the
husband of the two daughters, and Commander of the Faithful. It is worth saying out loud that every one of
those titles was given to him by the ummah, not invented afterwards.

**The statement:**
> أبو عمرو وأبو عبد الله، القرشي، الأموي؛ أمير المؤمنين، ذو النورين، وصاحب الهجرتين، وزوج الابنتين، وأمُّه أروى بنت كُرَيْز بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3503
> *English:* "Abū ʿAmr and Abū ʿAbdullāh, the Qurashī, the Umawī; Commander of the Faithful, Dhū al-Nūrayn,
> the possessor of the two hijras, the husband of the two daughters. His mother was Arwā bint Kurayz ibn
> Rabīʿa ibn ʿAbd Shams."

**عبرت:** A man is introduced by his people before he is introduced by his office.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM2 · أبو بكر ؓ asks him one question
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the earliest days in مكة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He came home troubled one day, and his aunt told him that a prophet had been sent among
his own people. He walked out still turning it over and met أبو بكر, who did not argue with him but asked him
about the idols his people worshipped — stone that does not hear, does not see, does not harm and does not
help. He said yes, by God, that is what they are. أبو بكر took him straight to the Prophet ﷺ, and he accepted
before he had time to weigh it.

**The statement:**
> فوالله ما تمالكتُ حين سمعت (٦) قوله أن أسلمت وشهدت أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3504
> *English:* "He said: By Allāh, I could not hold myself back when I heard his words — I became Muslim and
> bore witness that there is no god but Allāh alone, He has no partner."

**عبرت:** The question that opens a man is usually one he has already answered privately.

**Hands-up?** Who brought most of the earliest Muslims to the Prophet ﷺ — hands up if you know the name.

### UTM/E-UM3 · The first of the people to leave for الحبشة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Abyssinian hijra `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** arrow from مكة across the Red Sea to
الحبشة, then back, then مكة to المدینہ.

**What happened:** When the persecution in مكة grew heavy, he took his wife رقية, the Prophet's ﷺ daughter,
and crossed to الحبشة — the book says he was the first of the people to go. Later he came back to مكة, and
when the order came to leave for المدینہ he emigrated a second time. That is where the title صاحب الهجرتين
comes from: not a tribute, a record of two journeys.

**The statement:**
> وهاجر إلى الحبشة أوّلَ الناس ومعه زَوْجتهُ رقية بنت رسول اللّه ﷺ، ثم عاد إلى مكة وهاجر إلى المدينة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3505
> *English:* "He emigrated to Abyssinia first of the people, and with him his wife Ruqayya, the daughter of
> the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ; then he returned to Makka and emigrated to Madīna."

**عبرت:** A title in this tradition is usually a summary of something a man actually did.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM4 · The man who missed بدر and was counted at بدر
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 2 AH `[STANDARD]` *(to verify: the pages give the battle, not the year)* ·
**Map:** بدر lights; المدینہ stays lit.

**What happened:** When the army went out to بدر his wife رقية was dying, and the Prophet ﷺ left him in
المدینہ to nurse her. She died within days of the battle. When the spoils were divided the Prophet ﷺ assigned
him a share of بدر and the reward of بدر, and for that reason the books count him among the men of بدر. Years
later a stranger would throw the absence at his family as a charge, and this is the answer they gave.

**The statement:**
> فلما كانت وقعةُ بدرٍ اشتغلَ بتمريض ابنة رسول الله ﷺ، وأقام بسببها في المدينة، فضرب له رسول الله ﷺ بسهمه منها وأجره فيها، فهو معدودٌ فيمن شهدها.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3505
> *English:* "When the engagement of Badr came, he was occupied nursing the daughter of the Messenger of Allāh
> ﷺ and remained in Madīna on her account; so the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ assigned him his share of it and his
> reward in it, and he is therefore counted among those who were present at it."

**عبرت:** Duty in a sickroom was reckoned as service on a battlefield.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM5 · The second daughter, and the لقب
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after بدر `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** After رقية died the Prophet ﷺ married him to her sister أم كلثوم, and she too died while
married to him. The Prophet ﷺ then said that had there been a third he would have given her to him as well.
الحسن later explained the لقب in one line: nobody else is known to have closed his door on two daughters of a
prophet. The Companions had their own phrase for the same fact, and it was a phrase about rank, not about
romance.

**The statement:**
> وعن الحسن قال: إنما سمي عثمان "ذا النورين"؛ لأنا لا نعلم أحدا أغلق بابه على ابنتي نبي غيره.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1293
> *English:* "Al-Ḥasan said: ʿUthmān was called 'Dhū al-Nūrayn' only because we know of no one who closed his
> door upon two daughters of a prophet but him."

**عبرت:** The names a community gives are its own record of what it saw.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM6 · The hand the Prophet ﷺ held out for him at الحديبية
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 6 AH `[STANDARD]` *(to verify: the pages name الحديبية, not the year)* ·
**Map:** الحديبية lights, with مكة just beyond it.

**What happened:** At الحديبية the Prophet ﷺ needed a man to go into مكة and negotiate, and he chose him,
saying afterwards that if there were anyone in مكة better protected he would have sent that man instead. While
he was inside, word came that he had been killed, and the Muslims gave the pledge under the tree. He was not
there to give it. So the Prophet ﷺ put out his own right hand, said "this is the hand of ʿUthmān", struck it
against his other hand, and said "this is for ʿUthmān".

**The statement:**
> الرضوان بعد ما ذهب عثمان إلى مكة، فقال النبي ﷺ بيده اليمنى: "هذه يد عثمان" فضرب بها على يده فقال: "هذه لعثمان"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3515
> *English:* "…after ʿUthmān had gone to Makka. So the Prophet ﷺ said with his right hand: 'This is the hand
> of ʿUthmān', and struck it upon his own hand and said: 'This is for ʿUthmān.'"

**عبرت:** A man absent on an errand was not counted absent from the pledge.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM7 · The Egyptian with three charges
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after 35 AH, in مكة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Years after the killing, a man from مصر came on ḥajj, saw a group of قريش sitting, and was
told the elder among them was ابن عمر. He put three charges to him one after another: that عثمان fled at أحد,
that he was absent from بدر, that he was absent from the pledge under the tree. Each time ابن عمر answered
"yes". The man said "God is greatest", as though he had won. Then ابن عمر said: come here, let me make it
plain to you — and answered all three, ending with "now take that away with you".

**The statement:**
> وأما تغيبة (٨) عن بيعة الرضوان فلو كان أحدٌ أعزَّ ببطن مكة من عثمان لبعثه مكانه، فبعث رسول الله ﷺ عثمان وكانت بيعة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۶۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3514
> *English:* "As for his absence from the Pledge of Riḍwān: had there been anyone in the belly of Makka
> mightier than ʿUthmān, he would have sent him in his place. So the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ sent ʿUthmān, and
> the Pledge of Riḍwān was…"

**عبرت:** Three true facts, arranged to accuse, are still an accusation and not an argument.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM8 · A thousand dinars poured into a lap
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the expedition of تبوك, 9 AH `[STANDARD]` *(to verify: the pages name تبوك)* ·
**Map:** تبوك lights, north of المدینہ.

**What happened:** The army for تبوك was so hard to raise that it is remembered by its hardship. He came to
the Prophet ﷺ carrying a thousand dinars in a fold of his garment and poured them into his lap. The Prophet ﷺ
kept turning the coins over with his hand, and said twice that nothing عثمان did after that day would harm
him. The books also record camels, horses and gold given for the same army, and they do not agree on the
amounts — which is itself worth saying, because it means more than one person remembered it and each
remembered something different.

**The statement:**
> وتقدّم عن عبد الرحمن بن خباب أنه جهزهم يومئذ بثلاثمئة بعير باقتابها وأحلاسها، وعن عبد الرحمن بن سمرة أنه جاء يومئذ بألف دينار فصبَّها في حجر رسول اللّه ﷺ (فقال: "ما ضرَّ عثمانَ ما فعلَ بعد هذا اليوم" (٦) مرتين).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3505
> *English:* "It has been mentioned from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khabbāb that he equipped them that day with three
> hundred camels with their saddles and their blankets; and from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura that he came that
> day with a thousand dinars and poured them into the lap of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ — and he said: 'Nothing
> ʿUthmān does after this day will harm him', twice."

**عبرت:** Wealth is judged by what it is spent on, not by how much of it there is.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM9 · He bought the well and gave it away
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** early in المدینہ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ lights.

**What happened:** When the muhājirūn reached المدینہ they could not stomach the water. One good spring,
رومة, belonged to a man of بني غفار who sold its water by the skinful. The Prophet ﷺ offered to buy it from
him for a spring in Paradise, and the man said it was all he had. Word reached عثمان, who bought it for
thirty-five thousand dirhams, went to the Prophet ﷺ and asked for the same terms — and then gave the well to
the Muslims. أبو هريرة said afterwards that he bought Paradise twice: the day of رومة and the day of the army
of hardship.

**The statement:**
> قال: قد اشتريتها وجعلتها للمسلمين. وعن أبي هريرة قال: اشترى عثمان من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الجنة مرتين: يوم رومة، ويوم جيش العسرة.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1295
> *English:* "He said: I have bought it and made it for the Muslims. And Abū Hurayra said: ʿUthmān bought
> Paradise from the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ twice — the day of Rūma and the day of the Army of Hardship."

**عبرت:** The purchase that lasted was the one he did not keep.

**Hands-up?** What does a city need before it needs anything else? — hands up for water.

### UTM/E-UM10 · What he looked like
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his later years `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The men who saw him describe a handsome face marked with smallpox, a long beard dyed
yellow, broad shoulders and heavy joints, and arms so hairy that the hair covered his forearms. His teeth had
been bound with gold. One man who saw him preaching noticed the wrapper he had on and priced it at four
dirhams. Another said simply that he had never seen a man or a woman with a finer face.

**The statement:**
> وكان عثمان فيما بلغنا لا بالطويل، ولا بالقصير، حسن الوجه كبير اللحية أسمر اللون عظيم الكراديس بعيد ما بين المنكبين يخضب بالصفرة، وكان قد شد أسنانه بالذهب.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1292
> *English:* "ʿUthmān, as has reached us, was neither tall nor short, handsome of face, large of beard, brown
> of colour, big-jointed, broad between the shoulders; he used to dye with yellow, and he had bound his teeth
> with gold."

**عبرت:** The people who remembered him remembered a man, not a portrait.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM11 · The trait the angels are said to respect
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, in المدینہ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The Prophet ﷺ was resting at home, uncovered at the leg. أبو بكر asked leave and came in
and he did not move; عمر came in and he did not move; when عثمان asked leave he sat up and straightened his
clothes. عائشة asked him why this man and not the others. He answered with a question of his own, and it is
the sentence the whole of his reputation rests on.

**The statement:**
> "ألا أستحيي من رجل تستحيي منه الملائكة"؟. رواه مسلم.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1295
> *English:* "'Shall I not feel shame before a man before whom the angels feel shame?' — narrated by Muslim."

**عبرت:** A man's reserve can be recognised by others long before he is given any office.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM12 · Ten things he had stored with his Lord
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** in his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Late in his life he once counted out, in public, a short list of things he had kept
between himself and God. He was fourth into Islam. He never wished for another man's place. He had never
committed a shameful act, in the age of ignorance or after it. He had never touched himself with the hand
that had given the pledge to the Prophet ﷺ. And no Friday had passed since he became Muslim without his
freeing a slave — and if he had none that week, he freed two the next.

**The statement:**
> اختبأت عند ربي عشرا: إني لرابع أربعة في الإسلام، وما تعتيت ولا تمنيت، ولا وضعت يميني على فرجي منذ بايعت بها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولا مرتب بي جمعة منذ أسلمت إلا وأنا أعتق فيها رقبة، إلا أن لا يكون عندي فأعتقها بعد ذلك، ولا زنيت في جاهلية ولا إسلام قط.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1293
> *English:* "I have stored up ten things with my Lord: I am the fourth of four in Islam; I never busied
> myself in vanity and never wished [for another's place]; I never put my right hand on my private parts
> since I gave the pledge with it to the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ; no Friday has passed over me since I became
> Muslim without my freeing a slave on it, unless I had none, in which case I freed it afterwards; and I
> never committed zinā in the Age of Ignorance or in Islam, ever."

**عبرت:** A man's private accounts are kept long before anyone asks to see them.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM13 · Six names, three days, fifty men at the door
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ; the house of the شورى marked.

**What happened:** عمر, dying, refused to name a successor and refused his own son, and left the matter to
six men. صهيب was to lead the prayers meanwhile. عبد الله ibn عمر was to sit with them, advise, and be
ineligible. أبو طلحة with fifty of the أنصار was to stand at the door and let nobody in, and not to let the
third day pass without an امیر. The arrangement is as much of عمر's work as anything he did in office: he
built a machine that would produce a caliph without him.

**The statement:**
> كان عمر ﵁ قد جعل الأمر بعده شورى بين ستّة نفرٍ، وهم: عثمان بن عَفّان، وعليُّ بن أبي طالب، وطلحة بن عُبيد الله، والزبير بن العَوّام، وسعد بن أبي وَقّاص، وعبد الرحمن بن عوف ﵃.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3426
> *English:* "ʿUmar ؓ had made the matter after him a consultation among six men, and they are: ʿUthmān ibn
> ʿAffān, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbaydullāh, al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and ʿAbd
> al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf ؓ."

**عبرت:** A man who cannot choose his successor can still choose how the choosing is done.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM14 · عمر ؓ names the two it will come down to
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عمر did not pretend he had no view. He said he did not think the people would set anyone
level with عثمان and علي, and he gave his reason: both of them used to write the revelation in front of the
Prophet ﷺ as Jibrīl brought it down. Earlier still, at منى, he had asked حذيفة whom the people were looking
to, and been told plainly: عثمان. And on two consecutive pilgrimages the camel-driver's chant named first
one man and then the other.

**The statement:**
> وقد قال عمر بن الخطاب: ما أظن الناس يعدلون بعثمان وعلي أحدًا، إنهما كانا يكتبان الوحي بين يَدَيْ رسول الله ﷺ بما ينزل به جبريل عليه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3426
> *English:* "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I do not think the people will set anyone level with ʿUthmān and
> ʿAlī — for the two of them used to write the revelation before the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ, of what Jibrīl
> brought down with."

**عبرت:** A leader can say what he expects without arranging for it to happen.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM15 · Voices rise inside the house
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Behind the closed door the discussion went long and the voices rose enough to be heard
outside. أبو طلحة, standing guard, said out loud that he had expected them to push the thing away from
themselves, not to compete over it. Shortly afterwards three of the six gave up their own claims to three
others, and the matter narrowed to two.

**The statement:**
> وقال أبو طلحة: إني كنت أظن أن تدافعوها ولم أكن أظنُّ أن تنافسوها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3427
> *English:* "Abū Ṭalḥa said: I used to think you would push it away from yourselves, and I did not think you
> would compete over it."

**عبرت:** Even among the best of men, a decision under pressure sounds like a decision under pressure.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM16 · The man who took himself out of the running
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عبد الرحمن بن عوف was one of the six and could have had it. Instead he offered to give up
his own claim on condition that the others accept his choice, and he bound himself on oath before God and
Islam to appoint whichever of the two had the better right. They agreed. From that moment he was no longer a
candidate; he was the man who had to decide, and he had three days.

**The statement:**
> قلت لعبد الرحمن بن عوف: كيف بايعتم عثمان وتركتم عليا! قال: ما ذنبي قد بدأت بعلي فقلت: أبايعك على كتاب الله وسنة رسوله وسيرة أبي بكر وعمر، فقال: فيما استطعت. ثم عرضت ذلك على عثمان، فقال: نعم.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۶۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1307
> *English:* "I said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: how did you pledge to ʿUthmān and leave ʿAlī? He said: what
> is my fault? I began with ʿAlī and said: I pledge to you upon the Book of Allāh, the sunna of His Messenger
> and the conduct of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. He said: as far as I am able. Then I put that to ʿUthmān, and he
> said: yes."

**عبرت:** The surest way to be trusted with a choice is to have nothing to gain from it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM17 · Three days asking the whole city
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ, with the city itself lit rather than a
single house.

**What happened:** He did not sit and deliberate. He went out and asked المدینہ — the heads of the people and
the ordinary people, in pairs and singly, in groups, in secret and in the open. He reached the women behind
their curtains. He asked the boys in the schools. He asked riders and bedouin coming in through the gates. He
did that for three days and three nights, sleeping almost not at all, and in all of it he did not find two
men who differed.

**The statement:**
> حتى خلص إلى النساء المخدرات في حجابهنَّ وحتى سأل الولدان في المكاتب، وحتى سأل من يرد من الركبان والأعراب إلى المدينة، في مدة ثلاثة أيام بلياليها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3427
> *English:* "…until he got through to the secluded women behind their veils, and until he asked the boys in
> the schools, and until he asked whoever came in of the riders and the bedouin to Madīna — over a period of
> three days and their nights."

**عبرت:** Consultation means asking the people who will have to live with the answer.

**Hands-up?** Three days to choose a ruler for half the known world — hands up if you think that is a long
time or a short time.

### UTM/E-UM18 · The two who said otherwise, and then gave the pledge
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The record does not claim the city was unanimous. Two men are named as having counselled
عليًّا instead — عمار and المقداد, both of them among the earliest Muslims. The book names them, records
their view, and then records what they did next: they gave the pledge along with everyone else. It is the
smallest sentence in the account and it decides how the whole evening is told.

**The statement:**
> إلا ما ينقل عن عِمار والمقداد أنهما أشارا بعلي بن أبي طالب، ثم بايعا مع الناس على ما سنذكره.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3427
> *English:* "…except what is transmitted from ʿAmmār and al-Miqdād, that the two of them counselled ʿAlī ibn
> Abī Ṭālib — and then they gave the pledge along with the people, as we shall relate."

**عبرت:** Disagreeing about who should lead, and then following him, is a single act of discipline.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM19 · The fourth night, and two men woken before dawn
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the night before the بيعة, محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** On the last night, before the fourth day could dawn without an امیر, he went to his
nephew المسور and woke him: he had not closed his eyes in three nights, and he wanted علي and عثمان brought
to him. المسور asked which one first. He was told: whichever you like. He went to علي, who asked which of the
two had been sent for first, and was told the choice had been left open. Then he went to عثمان, and found
him already awake, praying his witr at dawn — and عثمان asked him exactly the same question.

**The statement:**
> أنائم يا مسور؟ والله لم أغتمض بكثير نوم منذ ثلاث، اذهب فادع لي (١) عليًا وعثمان.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3428
> *English:* "Are you asleep, Miswar? By Allāh, I have not closed my eyes in much sleep for three nights. Go
> and call ʿAlī and ʿUthmān for me."

**عبرت:** Both men wanted to know the same thing, and neither was told.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM20 · The question at the منبر, and the two answers
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** محرم 24 AH, in the Prophet's ﷺ mosque `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ, the mosque
marked.

**What happened:** He wore the turban the Prophet ﷺ had once wound on him, put on a sword, and had the call
made: the prayer is gathering. The mosque filled until عثمان, a shy man, could find nowhere to sit but at the
back. From the منبر he called علي up first and asked him one question — will you pledge on the Book of God,
the sunna of His Prophet ﷺ, and the practice of أبو بكر and عمر. علي answered that he would not bind himself
to that, but to his utmost effort and capacity. He let go of his hand, called عثمان, asked the identical
question, and عثمان answered: by God, yes.

**The statement:**
> فأخذ عبد الرحمن بيده فقال: هل أنت مبايعي على كتاب الله وسنة نبيه ﷺ وفعل أبي بكر وعمر؟ قال: اللهم لا ولكن على جهدي من ذلك وطاقتي، قال فأرسل يده وقال: قم (إلي) يا عثمان، فأخذ بيده فقال: هل أنت مبايعي على كتاب الله وسنة نبيه ﷺ وفعل أبي بكر وعمر؟ قال: اللهم نعم! فقال: فرفع رأسه إلى سقف المسجد ويده في يد عثمان فقال: اللهمَّ اسمع واشهد، اللهم اسمع واشهد، اللهم اسمع واشهد، اللهم إني قد جعلت (٥) ما في رقبتي من ذلك في رقبة عثمان.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3428
> *English:* "He took his hand and said: will you give me your pledge upon the Book of Allāh, the sunna of His
> Prophet ﷺ and the practice of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar? He said: O Allāh, no — but upon my utmost effort in that
> and my capacity. So he released his hand and said: rise to me, ʿUthmān. He took his hand and said: will you
> give me your pledge upon the Book of Allāh, the sunna of His Prophet ﷺ and the practice of Abū Bakr and
> ʿUmar? He said: O Allāh, yes. So he raised his head to the roof of the mosque, his hand in ʿUthmān's hand,
> and said: O Allāh, hear and witness; O Allāh, hear and witness; O Allāh, hear and witness. O Allāh, I have
> placed what is on my neck of that upon the neck of ʿUthmān."

**عبرت:** The office was given on a stated condition, in public, with the condition read aloud first.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM21 · The crowd at the منبر
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The people pressed in to give the pledge until they crowded him under the منبر. عبد
الرحمن sat down in the Prophet's ﷺ place on the منبر and seated the new caliph on the second step below him.
Then the whole city came forward. On the one question a later generation would argue about — whether علي
pledged first or last — ابن كثير writes both and settles neither.

**The statement:**
> وبايعه علي بن أبي طالب أولًا، ويقال آخرًا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3428
> *English:* "And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib pledged to him first — and it is said, last."

**عبرت:** Where a careful historian records two accounts and chooses neither, a later reader has no business
choosing for him.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM22 · The year they called the year of the nosebleed
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** timeline strip: 23 AH → 24 AH.

**What happened:** The books put the pledge in محرم of the year 24, three nights in, and they add something
that fixes the year in the memory: it was called the year of the nosebleed, because so many people suffered
them. The new caliph himself was kept from the pilgrimage that year by one they feared for him. The books do
not agree on the exact day of the pledge, and one of them says so in the same breath as it gives the date.

**The statement:**
> فِي الْمُحَرَّمِ مِنْهَا لِثَلَاثٍ مَضَيْنَ مِنْهُ بُويِعَ عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَفَّانَ، وَقِيلَ: غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى مَا تَقَدَّمَ، وَكَانَ هَذَا الْعَامُ يُسَمَّى عَامَ الرُّعَافِ لِكَثْرَتِهِ فِيهِ بِالنَّاسِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۵۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1143
> *English:* "In Muḥarram of it, three [nights] having passed of it, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān was given the pledge —
> and it is said otherwise, as has preceded. And this year used to be called the Year of the Nosebleed, for
> how much of it there was among the people."

**عبرت:** A year is remembered by what happened to ordinary people in it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM23 · The first prayer he led as caliph
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The pledge was given between the call to prayer and the standing for it. The muezzin had
already called العصر. So the first act of the third caliph was not a speech or an appointment: he walked out
and led the people in the prayer whose call had just been made. The books disagree about the day. They do not
disagree about the prayer.

**The statement:**
> وكان أول صلاة صلاها الخليفة أمير المؤمنين عثمان بن عفان بالمسلمين صلاة العصر، كما ذكره الشعبي وغيره.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3429
> *English:* "And the first prayer that the caliph, the Commander of the Faithful ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, prayed
> with the Muslims was the ʿAṣr prayer, as al-Shaʿbī and others have mentioned."

**عبرت:** The first duty of the office was the one that would have fallen to him anyway.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM24 · He came to the منبر as the most stricken man there
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The phrase the books use of him at that moment is not triumph but grief: of all of them,
he was the most stricken. He praised God, prayed on the Prophet ﷺ, and told the people that they were living
in a house of departure and in what was left of their lifetimes, and that they should get ahead of their
appointed times with the best they could manage. He told them to take a lesson from those who had gone, and
to throw the world away where God had thrown it. Then the people came forward to pledge.

**The statement:**
> لما بايع أهلُ الشورى عثمان خرج وهو أشدّهم كآبةً فأتى منبر النبي ﷺ فخطبَ الناس، فحمد الله وأثنى عليه وصلَّى على النبي ﷺ، وقال: إنكم في دار قلعة وفي بقية أعمار، فبادروا آجالكم بخير ما تقدرون عليه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3429
> *English:* "When the people of the consultation had pledged to ʿUthmān, he went out, the most stricken of
> them with grief, and came to the pulpit of the Prophet ﷺ and preached to the people. He praised Allāh and
> extolled Him and prayed upon the Prophet ﷺ, and said: you are in a house of departure and in the remainder
> of your lifetimes, so outstrip your appointed times with the best you are able of."

**عبرت:** The men who took this office described it as a weight before they described it as anything else.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM25 · "The first of every mount is hard"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** There is a well-known story that the new caliph froze on the منبر and could only say that
a first mount is always hard, and that if he lived they would get a proper sermon. ابن كثير refuses the
story: he says it comes from collectors of curiosities and that he never saw it with a chain he could settle
on. But in another place he transmits a sermon in which the same words are said deliberately, as an opening,
ending "we were never orators, and God will teach us." The words are his; the freezing is not established.

**The statement:**
> أيها الناس أولُ كلِّ مركبٍ صعبٌ، وإنَّ بعد اليوم أيامًا، وإن أعشْ تأتِكُم الخطبة على وجهها، وما كنا خطباء وسيُعلمُنا الله.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3528
> *English:* "O people, the first of every mount is hard; and after today there are days; and if I live the
> sermon will come to you as it should — we were never orators, and Allāh will teach us."

**عبرت:** A good story and a sound report are not the same thing, and the historians knew the difference.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM26 · A hundred more for every soldier, and a table in the mosque
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Almost the first administrative thing he did was to raise the stipend of every soldier by
a hundred dirhams over what عمر had assigned. عمر had already set a dirham a night in رمضان for every Muslim
to break the fast with, and two for the Mothers of the Believers; he kept that and increased it. And he set
out a table in the mosque itself for people who prayed there, for those in retreat, for travellers, for the
poor and the destitute.

**The statement:**
> وأمَّا قول الشعبي إنه زاد الناس مئة (مئة) -يعني في عطاء كل واحد من جند المسلمين- زاده على ما فرض له عمر مئة درهم من بيت المال وكان عمر قد جعل لكل نفس من المسلمين في كل ليلة من رمضان درهمًا من بيت المال يفطر عليه، ولأمهات المؤمنين درهمين (درهمين) فلما ولِّي عثمان أقر ذلك وزاده. واتخذ سماطًا في المسجد أيضًا للمتعبدين، والمعتكفين، وأبناء السبيل، والفقراء، والمساكين ﵁.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3430
> *English:* "As for al-Shaʿbī's words that he increased the people by a hundred each — that is, in the
> allowance of every one of the soldiers of the Muslims — he added to what ʿUmar had assigned him a hundred
> dirhams from the treasury; and ʿUmar had appointed for every soul of the Muslims, on every night of Ramaḍān,
> a dirham from the treasury to break the fast with, and for the Mothers of the Believers two dirhams; and
> when ʿUthmān was given authority he confirmed that and increased it. And he set out a table in the mosque
> as well, for the devout, those in iʿtikāf, the wayfarers, the poor and the destitute ؓ."

**عبرت:** The first thing a new government does with money tells you what it thinks money is for.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM27 · The step on the منبر
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When أبو بكر preached he refused to stand where the Prophet ﷺ had stood, and took the step
below it. When عمر came he went down another step below أبو بكر. When عثمان came he said plainly that at this
rate the thing would go on for ever — and he went up to the step the Prophet ﷺ had used. He also added the
first call to prayer on Friday, before the one made in front of the Prophet ﷺ when he sat on the منبر.

**The statement:**
> وقد كان أبو بكر إذا خطب يقوم على الدرجة التي تحت الدرجة التي كان رسول الله ﷺ يقف عليها، فلما ولِّي عمر نزل درجة أخرى عن درجة أبي بكر ﵄، فلمَّا ولِّي عثمان قال إنَّ هذا يطول فصعد إلى الدرجة التي كان يخطب عليها رسول الله ﷺ وزاد الأذان الأول يوم الجمعة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3430
> *English:* "Abū Bakr, when he preached, used to stand on the step below the step on which the Messenger of
> Allāh ﷺ used to stand; and when ʿUmar was given authority he went down another step below Abū Bakr's step;
> and when ʿUthmān was given authority he said: this will go on too long — and he went up to the step on which
> the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ used to preach. And he added the first call on the day of Jumuʿa."

**عبرت:** Humility that keeps compounding stops being humility and becomes a problem to be solved.

**Hands-up?** Two caliphs each stepped down one step. What happens by the tenth caliph? — hands up if you
see the problem.

### UTM/E-UM28 · The first case brought to the new caliph
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When عمر was struck, his son عبيد الله had gone out and killed three people in المدینہ
whom he believed had been in on it, and عمر had ordered him held so that the next caliph could judge him. So
the first case to reach the new caliph was the blood of the last one's household. علي held that justice
required the killer be killed. Others asked whether a father should be killed one day and his son the next.
عمرو بن العاص argued that the act had happened before this caliph had authority, so it was not his to judge.
He paid the blood-money for the three out of his own wealth and let the man go.

**The statement:**
> قال عثمان: أنا وليهم وقد جعلتها دية واحتملتها من مالي.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۶۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1309
> *English:* "ʿUthmān said: I am their guardian — and I have made it a blood-price and borne it from my own
> wealth."

**عبرت:** The first decision of a new authority is usually an inherited one.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM29 · The letter to every province
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the garrison cities light: الكوفة, البصرة, الشام,
مصر.

**What happened:** Early on he wrote out to the whole empire at once — not only to the governors, but
separately to the commanders of the armies, to the men who led the prayers, and to the men trusted with the
treasuries. The letter told them to command what is right and forbid what is wrong, to urge obedience to God
and His Messenger ﷺ, and to press people to follow and to leave off innovating. It is a short sentence in the
book and a picture of how the administration was actually shaped.

**The statement:**
> ثم كتب عثمان بن عفان إلى عماله على الأمصار أمراء الحرب، والأئمة على الصلوات، والأمناء على بيوت المال يأمرهم بالمعروف وينهاهم عن المنكر ويحثّهم على طاعة الله وطاعة رسوله، ويحرضهم على الاتِّباع وترك الابتداع.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3431
> *English:* "Then ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān wrote to his agents over the garrison cities — the commanders of war,
> the leaders of the prayers, and the trustees over the treasuries — commanding them to the good and
> forbidding them the objectionable, urging them to obedience to Allāh and obedience to His Messenger, and
> spurring them to following and to leaving off innovating."

**عبرت:** An empire is held together by what its letters say as much as by where its armies stand.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM30 · Governors had to stand in front of the people once a year
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة lights at ḥajj season.

**What happened:** He required every governor to come to the pilgrimage season each year, and he wrote to
the people under them that anyone with a grievance against any governor should come to the season, because
there he would take that man's right for him from his own governor. The pilgrimage was already the one time
in the year when the whole empire was in one place. He turned it into the place where an official could be
faced.

**The statement:**
> ومما كان يعتمده عثمان بن عفان أنه كان يُلْزمُ عُمَّاله بحضور الموسم كلَّ عام، ويكتب إلى الرعايا: منْ كانتْ له عند أحدٍ منهم مَظْلمةٌ فليوافِ إلى الموسم فإني آخذُ له حقَّه من عامله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3532
> *English:* "And among the things ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān relied upon was that he obliged his agents to attend the
> season every year, and he wrote to the subject peoples: whoever has a grievance against any one of them, let
> him come to the season, for I will take his right for him from his agent."

**عبرت:** Accountability needs a time and a place before it needs a rule.

### UTM/E-UM31 · حذيفة ؓ rides in from the frontier
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** an arrow from أرمينية/أذربيجان back
to المدینہ.

**What happened:** On campaign in the north, men from الشام and men from العراق were fighting in the camp —
not over plunder, but over how to recite. Each had learned from a different Companion, and men who did not
know that the recitation had been permitted in several modes were calling each other wrong, and some of them
worse than wrong. حذيفة saw enough of it to frighten him. He rode all the way back to المدینہ, went in to the
caliph, and said one sentence.

**The statement:**
> ومن مناقبه الكبار وحسناته العظيمة أنَّه جمعَ الناسَ على قراءة واحدةٍ، وكتب المصحفَ على العرضة الأخيرة، التي درسَها جبريل على رسول الله ﷺ في آخر سنيِّ حياته، وكان سبب ذلك أن حُذَيْفَة بن اليَمان كان في بعض الغزوات، وقد اجتمع فيها خلقٌ من أهل الشام، ممَّنْ يقرأُ على قراءةِ المِقْدادِ بن الأسْود، وأبي الدَّرْداء، وجماعة من أهل العراق، ممَّنْ يَقْرأُ على قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود، وأبي موسى، وجعل من لا يعلم بَسَوغان القراءة على سبعة أحرف، يفضل قراءته على قراءة غيره، وربما خَطَّأ الآخر أو كَفَّره، فأدى ذلك إلى اختلاف شديد، وانتشار في الكلام السيء بين الناس، فركبَ حُذَيْفَة إلى عثمان فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين أدْرِكْ هذه الأمةَ قبلَ أن تختلف في كتابها كاختلافِ اليهود والنصارى في كتبهم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3530
> *English:* "Among his great merits and his mighty good deeds is that he gathered the people upon a single
> reading, and wrote the muṣḥaf according to the final presentation, which Jibrīl went over with the Messenger
> of Allāh ﷺ in the last of the years of his life. The cause of that was that Ḥudhayfa ibn al-Yamān was on one
> of the campaigns, and there had gathered in it a great many of the people of Shām who read according to the
> reading of al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad and Abū al-Dardāʾ, and a company of the people of Iraq who read according
> to the reading of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd and Abū Mūsā; and one who did not know that the reading was permitted
> upon seven modes would prefer his own reading over another's, and might charge the other with error, or even
> with unbelief. That led to severe disagreement and to the spread of evil speech among the people. So Ḥudhayfa
> rode to ʿUthmān and said: Commander of the Faithful, save this umma before it differs about its Book as the
> Jews and the Christians differed about their books."

**عبرت:** A man who sees a crack from the frontier and rides to the capital about it has done the ummah a
service larger than a battle.

**Hands-up?** What do you think two Muslim armies were quarrelling about in camp? — hands up for anyone who
guesses it was the Qurʾān.

### UTM/E-UM32 · One writing, seven copies, six cities
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ at the centre, arrows to
الشام, مصر, البصرة, الكوفة, مكة, اليمن.

**What happened:** He gathered the Companions and consulted them, and they agreed. He sent to حفصة for the
pages أبو بكر had ordered collected, which had passed to عمر and then to her. He set زيد بن ثابت to write and
سعيد بن العاص to dictate, with two more of قريش present, and told them that where they disagreed they were to
write it in the tongue of قريش. Copies went to الشام, to مصر, to البصرة, to الكوفة, to مكة, to اليمن, and one
stayed in المدینہ. Then the pages went back to حفصة.

**The statement:**
> فعند ذلك جمعَ عثمانُ الصحابةَ وشاورهم في ذلك، ورأى أن يكتب المصحف على حرف واحد، وأن يجمعَ الناسَ في سائر الأقاليم على القراءة به، دون ما سواه، لما رأى في ذلك من مصلحةِ كفِّ المنازعةِ، ودفعِ الاختلافِ، فاستدعى بالصُّحف التي كان الصّديقُ أمر زيدَ بن ثابت بجمعها، فكانت عند الصديق أيام حياته، ثم كانت عند عمر، فلما توفي صارت إلى حفصة أم المؤمنين، فاستدعى بها عثمان وأمر زيد بن ثابت الأنصاري أن يكتبَ وأن يمليَ عليه سعيدُ بن العاص الأموي، بحضرة عبد الله بن الزبير الأسدي وعبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام المخزومي، وأمرهم إذا اختلفوا في شيء أن يكتبوه بلغةِ قريشٍ، فكتبَ لأهل الشام مصحفاً، ولأهل مصر آخر، وبعث إلى البصرة مصحفاً وإلى الكوفة بآخر، وأرسل إلى مكة مصحفاً وإلى اليمن مثله، وأقر بالمدينة مصحفاً.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3530
> *English:* "At that ʿUthmān gathered the Companions and consulted them about it, and saw that the muṣḥaf
> should be written upon one mode and that the people in all the regions should be gathered upon reading by it
> and nothing else, for what he saw in it of the benefit of stopping the dispute and repelling the
> disagreement. So he called for the pages that al-Ṣiddīq had ordered Zayd ibn Thābit to gather, which had been
> with al-Ṣiddīq in his lifetime, then with ʿUmar, and when he died passed to Ḥafṣa, Mother of the Believers.
> ʿUthmān called for them and ordered Zayd ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī to write, and Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ al-Umawī to
> dictate to him, in the presence of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadī and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn
> Hishām al-Makhzūmī, and he ordered them that when they differed over anything they should write it in the
> tongue of Quraysh. So he wrote a muṣḥaf for the people of Shām, and another for the people of Egypt, and sent
> a muṣḥaf to Baṣra and another to Kūfa, and sent one to Makka and its like to Yemen, and kept one in Madīna."

**عبرت:** The copy in your hands tonight has a chain of custody, and three caliphs are on it.

### UTM/E-UM33 · علي ؓ forbids exaggeration about him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** People afterwards used the burning of the differing copies against him — he burned the
Qurʾān, they said. علي, who had every reason to be heard on the subject, stood and forbade the exaggeration
in his own words: he burned nothing except before an assembly of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, and had I been
given charge of what he was given charge of, I would have done exactly what he did. In another report, more
briefly: if he had not done it, I would have.

**The statement:**
> أيها الناس! إياكم والغُلُوَّ في عثمان تقولون حرّق المصاحف، والله ما حرّقها إلا عن ملأ من أصحاب محمد ﷺ، ولو وليت مثل ما ولي لفعلتُ (مثل) الذي فعل.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3531
> *English:* "O people, beware of going to excess about ʿUthmān, saying: he burned the copies. By Allāh, he
> burned them only before a gathering of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ; and had I been given charge of the like
> of what he was given charge of, I would have done what he did."

**عبرت:** The people closest to an event were the least willing to make a grievance of it.

### UTM/E-UM34 · ابن مسعود ؓ objects, and then returns
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

**What happened:** Not everyone accepted it quietly. ابن مسعود took it hard when his own copy was taken and
burned, spoke about his own precedence in Islam over the younger man who had written the new copies, and told
his companions to keep their copies back. The caliph wrote to him, calling him to follow what the Companions
had agreed on for the sake of the common good and the keeping of one word among the Muslims. He came back to
it, and left off the disagreement. Later, in another matter entirely, he prayed four rakʿahs behind a
practice he had criticised, and gave his reason: disagreement is an evil.

**The statement:**
> وقد روي عن ابن مسعود (٥) أنه تعتّب لما أخذ منه مصحفه فحرِّق، وتكلَّم في تقدم إسلامه على زيد بن ثابت الذي كتب المصاحف، وأمر أصحابه أن يغلُّوا (٦) مصاحفهم، وتلا قوله تعالى: ﴿وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٦١] فكتب إليه عثمان ﵁ يدعوه إلى اتباع الصحابة فيما أجمعوا عليه من المصلحة في ذلك، وجمع الكلمة، وعدم الاختلاف، فأناب وأجاب إلى المتابعة وترك المخالفة ﵃ أجمعين.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3531
> *English:* "It has been related from Ibn Masʿūd that he took it amiss when his muṣḥaf was taken from him and
> burned, and spoke about his own precedence in Islam over Zayd ibn Thābit, who wrote the copies, and ordered
> his companions to conceal their copies, and recited the words of Allāh: {and whoever conceals shall come with
> what he concealed on the Day of Resurrection}. So ʿUthmān ؓ wrote to him calling him to follow the Companions
> in what they had agreed upon of the benefit in that, and the gathering of the word, and the absence of
> disagreement — and he turned back and answered to following, and left off opposing, ؓ, all of them."

**عبرت:** A disagreement that ends in returning to the community is not a wound; it is how a community stays
one.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM35 · Four rakʿahs at منى, and what ابن مسعود ؓ did about it
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 29 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة and منى.

**What happened:** At منى he prayed four rakʿahs where the Prophet ﷺ, أبو بكر and عمر had prayed two, and
people found fault with it. علي came and told him to his face that nothing new had happened and no covenant
had grown old. عبد الرحمن بن عوف told him his explanation was no excuse. To both men he answered the same
thing: it is a judgement I formed. ابن مسعود criticised it too — and then prayed four rakʿahs himself, and
when he was asked why, said that he hated disagreement.

**The statement:**
> أن عبد الله بن مسعود دخل مسجد منى فقال كم صلَّى أميرُ المؤمنين الظهرَ؟ قالوا: أربعاً، فصلَّى ابنُ مسعود أربعاً، فقالوا: ألم تُحدِّثنا أن رسول الله ﷺ وأبا بكر وعمر صلّوا ركعتين؟ فقال: نعم! وأنا أحدثكموه الآن، ولكني أكره الاختلاف.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3531
> *English:* "That ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd entered the mosque of Minā and said: how many did the Commander of the
> Faithful pray for Ẓuhr? They said: four. So Ibn Masʿūd prayed four. They said: did you not narrate to us that
> the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar prayed two rakʿahs? He said: yes, and I narrate it to you now
> — but I hate disagreement."

**عبرت:** A man may hold his opinion and still refuse to let it split the row behind the imam.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM36 · Asleep in the mosque with his cloak under his head
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الحسن البصري, who was alive in those years, says he saw the Commander of the Faithful
asleep in the mosque with his cloak folded under his head. Men came and sat down beside him, one after
another, as though he were one of them. There was no guard, no screen and no announcement. He is also
remembered ordering, from the منبر, that the pigeons people had begun keeping be dealt with and the
pellet-bows broken — the first frivolity that had appeared in المدینہ.

**The statement:**
> رأيت عثمان نائما في المجد ورداؤه تحت رأسه، فيجيء الرجل فيجلس إليه، ويجيء الرجل فيجلس إليه، كأنه أحدهم، وشهدته يأمر في خطبته بقتل الكلاب، وذبح الحمام.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1298
> *English:* "I saw ʿUthmān sleeping in the mosque with his cloak beneath his head; a man would come and sit
> with him, and a man would come and sit with him, as though he were one of them. And I witnessed him ordering,
> in his sermon, the killing of dogs and the slaughtering of pigeons."

**عبرت:** The ruler of an empire slept on the floor of a mosque and nobody thought it worth an announcement.

### UTM/E-UM37 · The boy who let a bird loose in the mosque
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A boy went into the mosque at midday with a bird to let loose while the building work was
going on, and found an old man asleep with a brick under his head. He stood staring at him because he had
never seen anyone so handsome. The man opened his eyes and asked who he was. Then he woke a servant, sent
him off, and told the boy to sit. The servant came back with a robe and a thousand dirhams; the man took off
the boy's own garment, dressed him in the robe, put the money in it and sent him home. The boy told his
father he did not know who it was — only a man asleep in the mosque. His father told him.

**The statement:**
> انطلقت وأنا غلام في الظهيرة ومعي طير أرسله في المسجد، والمسجد يُبْنى (٩)، فإذا شيخ جميل حسن الوجه نائم، تحت رأسه لبنة أو بعض لَبنة، فقمت أنظر إليه أتعجب من جماله، ففتح عينيه فقال: من أنت يا غلام؟ فأخبرته، فإذا غلام نائم قريبًا منه فدعاه فلم يُجْبه، فقال لي: ادعه! فدعوته فأمره بشيء، وقال لي: اقعد! فذهب الغلامُ، فجاء بحلَّةٍ وجاء بألف درهم، ونزع ثوبي وألبسني الحلَّة؟ وجعل الألف درهم فيها، فرجعت إلى أبي فأخبرته؟ فقال: يا بُنيَّ منْ فعلَ هذا بك؟ فقلت: لا أدري إلا أنه رجل في المسجد نائم لم أر قطُّ أحسنَ منه، قال: ذاك أميرُ المؤمنين عثمانُ بن عفان.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3526
> *English:* "I set out as a boy at midday with a bird of mine to let loose in the mosque, and the mosque was
> being built; and there was a handsome, fine-faced elder asleep, with a brick, or part of a brick, under his
> head. So I stood looking at him, wondering at his beauty — and he opened his eyes and said: who are you, boy?
> I told him. And there was a boy asleep nearby, and he called him and he did not answer, so he said to me:
> call him. I called him, and he ordered him with something and said to me: sit. The boy went off and came back
> with a robe and came back with a thousand dirhams; and he took off my garment and clothed me in the robe and
> put the thousand dirhams in it. I went back to my father and told him, and he said: my son, who did this to
> you? I said: I do not know, except that he is a man in the mosque, asleep — I never saw anyone more handsome.
> He said: that is the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān."

**عبرت:** Generosity that does not give its own name is the kind that gets remembered longest.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM38 · The whole Qurʾān in one rakʿah
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي says it is established by several routes that he recited the entire Qurʾān in a
single rakʿah. A man who had set out one night to get to the المقام before anyone else found a muffled
stranger crowding him, turned, and saw it was the caliph — who then prayed through the night, and made witr
with one rakʿah just as the dawn call was heard. He fasted the whole year. He wore his own copy of the Qurʾān
through from the length of time he kept his eyes on it. And on the day the house was surrounded, his wife
said of him: kill him or leave him, but by God he used to bring the night to life with the Qurʾān in a single
rakʿah.

**The statement:**
> قالت امرأة عثمان يوم الدار: اقتلوه أو دعوه، فوالله لقد كان يحيي الليل بالقرآن في ركعة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3527
> *English:* "ʿUthmān's wife said on the day of the house: kill him or leave him — but by Allāh, he used to
> bring the night to life with the Qurʾān in a single rakʿah."

**عبرت:** The man who gathered the ummah on one recitation was the man who spent his nights inside it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM39 · He would not wake the household
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When he got up in the night to pray, he made his own wuḍūʾ and did not wake anyone to
help him, unless he found someone already awake. People reproached him for it — could he not wake one of the
servants? He said no: the night is theirs, and it is when they rest. The same reserve went with him
everywhere; even bathing behind a locked door he would not straighten his back.

**The statement:**
> فيقول: لا! الليل لهم يستريحون فيه. وكان (١) إذا اغتسل لا يرفع المئزر عنه، وهو في بيت مغلق عليه، ولا يرفع صلبه جيدًا من شدة حيائه ﵁.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3528
> *English:* "He would say: no — the night is theirs, in which they rest. And when he bathed he would not lift
> the waist-wrapper from himself, though he was in a house locked upon him; and he would not straighten his
> back properly, from the intensity of his shame ؓ."

**عبرت:** How a man treats the people who cannot refuse him is the whole measure of the man.

### UTM/E-UM40 · The seller who felt cheated
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He bought a piece of land from a man, and the man did not come to collect the money. He
went and found him and asked why. The man said: you got the better of me, and everyone I meet tells me so.
He asked: is that what is keeping you away? The man said yes. So he told him to choose — take your land back
or take your money — and then quoted the Prophet ﷺ on the man God admits to Paradise for being easy in
buying, in selling, in paying and in asking to be paid.

**The statement:**
> أن عثمان اشترى من رجلٍ أرضًا فأبطأ عليه فلقيه فقال: ما منعكَ من قبض مالكَ؟ قال: إنك غَبْنتني، فما ألقى من الناس أحدًا إلا وهو يلومني، قال: أذلك يمنعك؟ قال: نعم! قال: فاختر بين أرضكَ ومالكَ، ثم قال: قال رسول اللّه ﷺ: "أدخل اللّه الجنةَ رجلًا كان سهلًا مشتريًا وبائعًا، وقاضيًا مقتضيًا".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3529
> *English:* "That ʿUthmān bought land from a man, and the man was slow to him, so he met him and said: what
> kept you from taking your money? He said: you got the better of me, and I meet no one but he blames me. He
> said: does that keep you back? He said: yes. He said: then choose between your land and your money. Then he
> said: the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ said: 'Allāh has admitted to Paradise a man who was easy when buying and
> selling, and when settling and when demanding settlement.'"

**عبرت:** A contract that leaves the other man ashamed has not really been completed.

### UTM/E-UM41 · Where the word for a prize comes from
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** كرمان lights, east of فارس.

**What happened:** A governor in كرمان found four thousand Muslim soldiers cut off by a flooded valley and
about to lose their chance. He called out that any man who crossed would have a thousand dirhams. They swam
it, and as each man came out he was paid, until four million dirhams had gone. His superior refused to allow
the sum, and wrote to the caliph about it. The caliph wrote back: credit it to him, for he only helped the
Muslims in the path of God. And from that day a gift for crossing was called a جائزة.

**The statement:**
> استعمل ابنُ عامر قَطَنَ بن عوف الهلالي على كرمان، فأقبل جيشٌ من المسلمين -أربعة آلاف- وجرى الوادي فقطعهم عن طريقهم، وخشي قَطَنٌ الفوتَ فقال: من جاز الوادي فله ألفُ درهم، فحملوا أنفسهم على العوم (٧)، فكان إذا جاز الرجل منهم قال قَطنٌ: أعطوه جائزَتَهُ، حتى جازوا جميعًا وأعطاهم أربعةَ آلافِ ألفِ درهم، فأبى ابنُ عامر أن يَحْسِبَها له، فكتب بذلك إلى عثمان بن عفان، فكتب عثمان: أن احْسِبْها له، فإنه إنَّما أعانَ المسلمين في سبيل اللّه. فمن ذلك اليوم سُمِّيتِ الجوائزَ لإجازةِ الوادي
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3529
> *English:* "Ibn ʿĀmir appointed Qaṭan ibn ʿAwf al-Hilālī over Kirmān. An army of the Muslims — four thousand
> — came up, and the valley ran in flood and cut them off from their road; and Qaṭan feared they would miss
> their chance, so he said: whoever crosses the valley shall have a thousand dirhams. So they put themselves to
> swimming, and whenever a man of them crossed, Qaṭan would say: give him his crossing-gift — until they had
> all crossed, and he gave them four million dirhams. Ibn ʿĀmir refused to reckon it to his account, and wrote
> about it to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān; and ʿUthmān wrote: reckon it to him, for he only helped the Muslims in the
> way of Allāh. And from that day gifts were called jawāʾiz, for the crossing of the valley."

**عبرت:** A word that survives in the language is a fossil of a decision somebody once made.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-UM42 · The years as a man who lived in them remembered them
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24–35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the whole empire lit.

**What happened:** الحسن البصري lived through those years and describes them without any argument attached:
scarcely a day passed without something good being shared out. Come for your stipends, and they were paid in
full. Come for your provisions, and they were paid in full. Come for the butter and the honey. The stipends
running, the provisions flowing, the enemy pushed away, relations between people good. He also said, flatly,
that عثمان served twelve years, and that people objected to nothing in his rule.

**The statement:**
> أدركت عثمان على ما نقموا عليه. قلَّما يأتي على الناس يومٌ إلا وهم يقتسمون فيه خيرًا، يقال لهم: يا معشر المسلمين اغدوا على أعطياتكم، فيأخذونها وافرة، ثم يقال لهم: اغدوا على أرزاقكم فيأخذونها وافرة، ثم يقال لهم: اغدوا على السمن والعسل، الأعطيات جارية، والأرزاق دارَّةٌ، والعدو منفيٌّ (٨)، وذات البين حسن، والخيرُ كثير
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3525
> *English:* "I lived through ʿUthmān's time, over which they held things against him. Scarcely a day would
> come upon the people but they were dividing some good in it. It would be said to them: company of Muslims,
> come in the morning for your stipends — and they would take them in full. Then it would be said to them: come
> in the morning for your provisions — and they would take them in full. Then it would be said to them: come in
> the morning for the clarified butter and the honey. The stipends running, the provisions flowing, the enemy
> driven off, relations between people good, and good things many."

**عبرت:** Plenty is not by itself a guarantee of peace — which is the whole of what the next session has to
explain.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-UM43 · "We pledged to the best of us and we did not fall short"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن مسعود was one of the great teachers of the الكوفة generation and was not a man who
flattered authority. He said of the day عمر died and the pledge was given that they gave it to the best among
them, and did not fall short in the choosing. In another wording: they put in charge the best of those who
remained. That is the sentence with which the evening's account of the بيعة should close, because it is a
Companion's own summary of the whole process.

**The statement:**
> لما توفّي عمر بايعنا خيرنا ولم نأل، وفي رواية بايعوا خيرهم ولم يألوا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3525
> *English:* "Ibn Masʿūd said: when ʿUmar died, we pledged to the best of us and we did not fall short. And in
> another narration: they pledged to the best of them and they did not fall short."

**عبرت:** The people who were there thought they had chosen well, and said so.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-UM44 · What علي ؓ said about him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The people who came later made a quarrel of these two men. The words the books preserve
from علي himself are not a quarrel. Asked about him, he said he was the best of them, the closest in keeping
family ties, the most reserved, the purest, and the most fearful of the Lord. He said he hoped that he and he
would be among those God describes as having every grudge taken out of their breasts, brothers on couches
facing one another. And of the killing he swore an oath: I did not kill him, I did not order it, and I was
overpowered. ابن كثير says those oaths come down by so many routes that the scholars of hadith take them as
certain.

**The statement:**
> كان عثمان ﵁ خيرنا وأوصلنا للرحم، وأشدنا حياء، وأحسننا طهورًا، وأتقانا للرب ﷿.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3496
> *English:* "ʿUthmān ؓ was the best of us, the most joining of kinship among us, the most intense of us in
> shame, the best of us in purification, and the most fearing of us toward the Lord."

**عبرت:** When two men are made into opposing parties by later generations, the safest witness is what each
said about the other.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-UM45 · Twelve years, and a man of eighty-two
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** timeline strip: 24 AH → 35 AH shaded.

**What happened:** He held the office for twelve years — قتادة and خليفة بن خياط say twelve years less
twelve days. That is by far the longest of the three caliphates so far: أبو بكر had two years, عمر a little
over ten. He was eighty-two when he died, which الذهبي marks as the sound view, though it is also said
eighty-six. Everything the room will hear next week happened inside those twelve years.

**The statement:**
> قال قتادة: ولي عثمان اثنتي عشرة سنة، غير اثني عشر يوما وكذا قال خليفة بن خياط، وغيره.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۶۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1303
> *English:* "Qatāda said: ʿUthmān ruled twelve years less twelve days. And likewise said Khalīfa ibn Khayyāṭ
> and others."

**عبرت:** The longest of the three caliphates is the one about which people know the least.

**Hands-up?** How long do you think the third caliph ruled — longer or shorter than عمر ؓ? Hands up for
longer.

---

### UTM/E-UM46 · What was engraved on his ring
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The seal a caliph used went on every letter that left المدینہ, so what was cut into it was
read in every province. His carried a line of the Qurʾān's own language about creation. A second report gives
different words. Either way, it is the shortest statement of a policy anyone has left us.

**The statement:**
> كان نقش خاتم عثمان آمنت بالذي خلق فسوى.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3525
> *English:* "The engraving of ʿUthmān's ring was: I have believed in Him who created and shaped."

**عبرت:** A man's seal says what he wants said in the rooms he will never enter.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-UM47 · The register of his household
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** across his life `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** After the Prophet's ﷺ two daughters he married several more women, and the books keep the
whole register: فاختة bint غزوان, أم عمرو bint جندب, فاطمة bint الوليد, أم البنين bint عيينة, رملة bint
شيبة and نائلة bint الفرافصة. Sons and daughters are named for each. Four wives survived him. The register is
here so the strand never has to look it up again; it is a reference list and it is not for reading aloud.

**The statement:**
> ثمَّ لما توفيت تزوَّج بأختها أم كلثوم. ثمَّ توفيت فتزوج بفاختة بنت غزوان بن جابر، فولد له منها عبيد الله الأصغر. وتزوج بأم عمرو بنت جندب بن عمرو الأزدية، فولدت له عَمراً، وخالداً، وأبانا، وعمر، ومريم. وتزوج بفاطمة بنت الوليد بن عبد شمس المخزومية. فولدت له الوليد وسعيداً. وتزوج أم البنين بنت عيينة بن حصن الفزارية، فولدت له عبد الملك، ويقال: وعتبة. وتزوج رملة بنت شيبة بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس بن عبد مناف بن قصي فولدت له عائشة وأم أبان وأم عمرو، بنات عثمان. وتزوج نائلة بنت الفرافصة بن الأحوص بن عمرو بن ثعلبة بن حصن بن ضَمْضَم بن عدي بن حيان بن كليب (١)، فولدت له مريم، ويقال: وعنبسة. وقتل ﵁ وعنده أربع: نائلة، ورملة، وأم البنين، وفاختة. ويقال: إنه طلق أم البنين وهو محصور.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3533
> *English:* "Then, when she died, he married her sister Umm Kulthūm. Then she died, and he married Fākhita
> bint Ghazwān ibn Jābir, and she bore him ʿUbaydullāh the younger. And he married Umm ʿAmr bint Jundub ibn
> ʿAmr al-Azdiyya, and she bore him ʿAmr, Khālid, Abān, ʿUmar and Maryam. And he married Fāṭima bint al-Walīd
> ibn ʿAbd Shams al-Makhzūmiyya, and she bore him al-Walīd and Saʿīd. And he married Umm al-Banīn bint ʿUyayna
> ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazāriyya, and she bore him ʿAbd al-Malik — and it is said, and ʿUtba. And he married Ramla bint
> Shayba ibn Rabīʿa ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy, and she bore him ʿĀʾisha, Umm Abān and Umm ʿAmr,
> the daughters of ʿUthmān. And he married Nāʾila bint al-Farāfiṣa ibn al-Aḥwaṣ ibn ʿAmr ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥiṣn
> ibn Ḍamḍam ibn ʿAdī ibn Ḥayyān ibn Kulayb, and she bore him Maryam — and it is said, and ʿAnbasa. And he was
> killed ؓ with four [wives]: Nāʾila, Ramla, Umm al-Banīn and Fākhita. And it is said that he divorced Umm
> al-Banīn while he was under siege."

**عبرت:** A register kept carefully by historians is itself a kind of respect.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM48 · What he had put beyond his own reach
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** خيبر and وادي القرى light faintly, north of المدینہ.

**What happened:** The books list what he had already given away permanently as صدقة: the well of أريس,
property at خيبر, property at وادي القرى — and بئر رومة, which he had bought in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime and
made a public endowment. They also record, on الواقدي's authority, very large sums with his treasurer on the
day he was killed, which were plundered. **This card is recorded and deliberately not planned for delivery:
the figure will be heard as an accusation whatever is said around it, and the estate belongs to the strand
that handles the complaints, with their full context.**

**The statement:**
> كان لعثمان عند خازنه يوم قتل، ثلاثون ألف ألف درهم وخمسمئة ألف درهم، [وخمسون] ومئة ألف دينار، فانْتُهبتْ وذهبت، وترك ألف بعير بالرَّبَذَة، وترك صدقات كان تصدق بها، بئر أريس، وخيبر، ووادي القرى، فيه مئتا ألف دينار. (وبئر رومة كان اشتراها في حياة النبي ﷺ وسبَّلها).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3493
> *English:* "ʿUthmān had with his treasurer on the day he was killed thirty million five hundred thousand
> dirhams and a hundred and fifty thousand dinars — and it was plundered and went. And he left a thousand
> camels at al-Rabadha, and left charitable endowments he had given: Bi'r Arīs, Khaybar and Wādī al-Qurā, in it
> two hundred thousand dinars. (And Bi'r Rūma he had bought in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ and made it a
> public endowment.)"

**عبرت:** What a man has given away is a truer inventory than what he has left.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-UM49 · Two notices the scholars kept about him
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** after his death `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي records two short judgements from the generation of scholars that followed. الشعبي
said that no caliph from among the Companions had gathered the whole Qurʾān except him — and added that علي
left this world without having done so. ابن سيرين said that the most learned of them in the rites of the
pilgrimage was عثمان, and after him ابن عمر. The first of the two touches a comparison between Companions and
is recorded here without being planned for delivery.

**The statement:**
> وقال ابن سيرين: كان أعلمهم بالمناسك عثمان، وبعده ابن عمر.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1297
> *English:* "Ibn Sīrīn said: the most knowing of them in the rites [of ḥajj] was ʿUthmān, and after him Ibn
> ʿUmar."

**عبرت:** The men who came after judged the Companions by what they knew, not by which party claimed them.

**Hands-up?** no

## The conquests: إفريقية, قبرص, the sea, and the end of Persia

*Source note: [`uthman-the-conquests-and-the-first-fleet.md`](../docs/research/uthman-the-conquests-and-the-first-fleet.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### UTC/E-UC1 · The year they called the year of the nosebleed
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** المحرم ۲۴ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة lights; nothing moves.

**What happened:** عثمان بن عفان ؓ was given the pledge three nights into المحرم, in the gap between
the call to the afternoon prayer and the standing for it. He came out and led the people and then went
up to the pulpit, and of all of them he was the most sorrowful in his face. That same year an illness
of bleeding ran through the people so widely that they named the year after it. He could not lead the
pilgrimage that season because of it, and عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ led it in his place.

**The statement:**
> فِي الْمُحَرَّمِ مِنْهَا لِثَلَاثٍ مَضَيْنَ مِنْهُ بُويِعَ عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَفَّانَ، وَقِيلَ: غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى مَا تَقَدَّمَ، وَكَانَ هَذَا الْعَامُ يُسَمَّى عَامَ الرُّعَافِ لِكَثْرَتِهِ فِيهِ بِالنَّاسِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۵۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1143
> *English:* "In المحرم of it, three nights having passed of it, عثمان بن عفان was given the pledge — and it is said otherwise, as has preceded — and this year used to be called the year of the nosebleed, for how much of it there was among the people."

**عبرت:** A reign begins on an ordinary afternoon, between the call to prayer and the prayer itself.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTC/E-UC2 · الإسكندرية breaks its word, and Rome comes back by sea
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۵ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Alexandria flashes; a Roman arrow from the
north-west; then the arrow is erased.

**What happened:** The emperor sent a fleet to Alexandria under a commander named منويل, and the Romans
inside the city hoped for rescue and broke the treaty they had made. عمرو بن العاص ؓ marched on them in
ربيع الأول. He took the countryside by force and the city by terms. One group of villagers came to him
afterwards and said the Romans had taken their animals and their property although they themselves had
kept faith; he made them prove what was theirs, and gave it back.

**The statement:**
> وفيها (٤) نقض أهل الإسكندرية العهدَ، وذلك أن ملكَ الروم بعث إليهم منويل الخصي (٥) في مراكب من البحر فطمعوا في النُّصْرة ونقضوا ذمتهم، فغزاهم عمرو بن العاص في ربيع الأول، فافتتح الأرض عنوةً وافتتح المدينة صلحًا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3433
> *English:* "And in it the people of الإسكندرية broke the treaty. That was because the king of الروم sent them منويل the eunuch in ships from the sea, so they hoped for the rescue and broke their covenant. عمرو بن العاص raided them in ربيع الأول, and took the countryside by force and took the city by terms."

**عبرت:** A treaty holds only as long as the weaker side believes no rescue is coming.

**Hands-up?** Who here can name the sea on the far side of that city?

---

### UTC/E-UC3 · The wall that was pulled down and not rebuilt
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۵ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Alexandria — the wall symbol is removed.

**What happened:** After he had retaken the city, عمرو بن العاص ؓ did something no conqueror usually
does. He pulled down the wall of Alexandria and left it with no wall at all. A walled port that Rome
could reach by sea and the Muslims could only reach by land was a door that would keep reopening. The
answer to a city that can be rescued from the water is either to take the water, or to take away the
thing that makes the rescue worth attempting.

**The statement:**
> وَهَدَمَ عَمْرٌو سُورَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ وَتَرَكَهَا بِغَيْرِ سُورٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۵۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1145
> *English:* "And عمرو pulled down the wall of الإسكندرية and left it with no wall."

**عبرت:** Sometimes the strongest answer to a fortification is to stop defending it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTC/E-UC4 · The fifth of the fifth
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۵–۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** an arrow west from مصر, past برقة and
طرابلس.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح was sent west from Egypt, and when he came back he wrote
to المدينة asking leave to go into إفريقية properly. عثمان ؓ put the question to the Companions who
were with him and most of them were for it. He gave the order, and attached a term to it: if God opens
it to you, the fifth of the fifth of the spoil is yours as a grant. Armies were equipped out of
المدينة to join him, and among the men who rode out were عبد الله بن عمر ؓ, عبد الله بن الزبير ؓ and
عبد الله بن عباس ؓ.

**The statement:**
> أمر عثمانُ عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سَرْح أن يغزوَ بلاد إفريقية، فإذا فتحها (١) الله عليه فله خُمس الخُمس من الغنيمة نفلًا، فسار إليها في عشرة آلاف فافتتحها سهلَها وجبلَها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3435
> *English:* "عثمان ordered عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح to raid the lands of إفريقية, and that if God opened it to him he should have the fifth of the fifth of the spoil as a grant. So he marched to it with ten thousand and took it, its plain and its mountain."

**عبرت:** A great undertaking is begun with a written term, not with a feeling.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTC/E-UC5 · جرجير, who ruled from طرابلس to طنجة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a band across North Africa from طرابلس to
طنجة, in Roman colour.

**What happened:** The man who held North Africa was called جرجير. His rule ran from طرابلس in the east
to طنجة on the ocean, and he held it as the emperor's appointee, carrying tribute to قسطنطينية every
year. When he heard the Muslims were coming he gathered not only his soldiers but the people of the
country with them, and his host reached a hundred and twenty thousand horsemen. عبد الله بن سعد sent to
him offering Islam or the treaty tax, and he refused both, and was too proud to accept either.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ مَلِكُهُمُ اسْمُهُ جُرْجِيرُ، وَمُلْكُهُ مِنْ طَرَابُلُسَ إِلَى طَنْجَةَ، وَكَانَ هِرَقْلُ مَلِكُ الرُّومِ قَدْ وَلَّاهُ إِفْرِيقِيَّةَ، فَهُوَ يَحْمِلُ إِلَيْهِ الْخَرَاجَ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1153
> *English:* "Their king's name was جرجير, and his rule ran from طرابلس to طنجة. هرقل, king of الروم, had appointed him over إفريقية, and he carried the tribute to him every year."

**عبرت:** A ruler who answers a proposal with pride has narrowed his own choices to one.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTC/E-UC6 · The ring around the Muslims at سبيطلة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** سبيطلة, two days from القيروان.

**What happened:** The two hosts came in sight of one another near سبيطلة, which was then the seat of
جرجير's rule. He ordered his army forward and they went round the Muslims until they had them ringed
about like a halo. ابن كثير, who is not a man who exaggerates a difficulty, says the Muslims stood that
day in a position more grim than any that had been seen, and more frightening for them. They fought
every morning until the call to the noon prayer, and then both sides went back to their tents, and the
next morning they did it again.

**The statement:**
> صمدَ إليهم ملك البربر جرجير في عشرين ومئة ألف، وقيل في مئتي ألف
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3435
> *English:* "جرجير the king of the Berbers came against them with a hundred and twenty thousand — and it is said, with two hundred thousand."

**عبرت:** Being surrounded is a position, not yet a defeat.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTC/E-UC7 · Two prices on two heads
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عثمان ؓ had lost touch with the army entirely and sent عبد الله بن الزبير ؓ west
with a company simply to bring back news. When he arrived the shouting and the takbīr of the Muslims
rose so much that جرجير asked what had happened, and was told reinforcements had reached them, and it
weakened his arm. Then ابن الزبير ؓ noticed the Muslim commander was not on the field, and learned that
جرجير had offered a hundred thousand دينار and his own daughter to whoever killed him. He went to the
commander and had the identical offer cried back against جرجير. After that, the books say, جرجير was
the more frightened of the two.

**The statement:**
> مَنْ قَتَلَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ سَعْدٍ فَلَهُ مِائَةُ أَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَأُزَوِّجُهُ ابْنَتِي
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1153
> *English:* "Whoever kills عبد الله بن سعد shall have a hundred thousand دينار, and I will marry him to my daughter."

**عبرت:** Fear that has been answered in kind stops being a weapon.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC8 · The young man rides at the king — as ابن كثير tells it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** سبيطلة.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن الزبير ؓ tells this himself. He looked out from behind the ranks and saw
the king on a pack-horse with two servant girls holding peacock feathers over him for shade. He asked
the commander for men to guard his back, and rode straight at him through the enemy lines — and they
let him through, because they took him for a messenger. When he was close, the king sensed it and fled
on his horse. He overtook him, ran him through with his spear, finished him with his sword, and raised
the head on his spear-point and said الله أكبر. When the Berbers saw it they scattered.

**The statement:**
> قال عبد الله بن الزبير: فنظرتُ إلى الملك جرجير من وراء الصفوف وهو راكب على برذون، وجاريتان تظلانه بريش الطواويس
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3435
> *English:* "عبد الله بن الزبير said: I looked at the king جرجير from behind the ranks, and he was mounted on a pack-horse, with two servant girls shading him with peacock feathers."

**عبرت:** An army that depends on one man in a shaded chair has one place it can be struck.

**Hands-up?** no
