### UTC/E-UC9 · The young man outthinks the king — as ابن الأثير tells it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** سبيطلة.

**What happened:** In ابن الأثير's telling the killing is the end of a plan, not a charge. ابن
الزبير ؓ said to the commander: this will go on for ever, they are on their own ground with supplies
coming and we are cut off from ours. Tomorrow let us keep our best fighters in the tents with their
horses saddled and let the rest fight the Romans past the hour when both sides usually break off, until
they are worn out. The commander put it to the senior Companions and they agreed. The next day, when
both armies had thrown down their weapons in exhaustion, the rested men came on in one charge, and
جرجير was killed. **Both tellings are ours; the two books do not agree, and we do not choose.**

**The statement:**
> وَقُتِلَ جُرْجِيرُ، قَتَلَهُ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ، وَانْهَزَمَ الرُّومُ، وَقُتِلَ مِنْهُمْ مَقْتَلَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ، وَأُخِذَتِ ابْنَةُ الْمَلِكِ جُرْجِيرَ سَبِيَّةً.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1154
> *English:* "And جرجير was killed — ابن الزبير killed him — and الروم were routed, and a great slaughter was made of them, and the daughter of the king جرجير was taken captive."

**عبرت:** When two careful historians describe one hour differently, the honest thing is to say so.

**Hands-up?** Which of those two accounts sounds more likely to you — and does it matter?

### UTC/E-UC10 · The first field on which his name was known
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن الزبير ؓ was a young man then. He had been a child of the هجرة, born to
أسماء بنت أبي بكر ؓ on the road to المدينة. After that day in North Africa he was sent back to المدينة
himself to carry the news of the victory. ابن كثير says plainly that this was the first field on which
his name became known — and the room should hold that name, because it comes back, and it comes back
hard, forty years later in مكة.

### UTC/E-UC11 · Three thousand to the horseman
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** After سبيطلة fell the armies went out through the country as far as قفصة, and then

safety, not by storm. Then the people of إفريقية made terms for two and a half million دينار. Four
fifths of the spoil was divided among the army, and both of our books give the same figures for the

### UTC/E-UC13 · The letter about قسطنطينية that our two books read differently
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۷ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a dotted line west from إفريقية to the far
shore, and a long dotted line east to قسطنطينية.

**What happened:** When إفريقية had been settled, عثمان ؓ ordered two commanders, both named عبد الله
بن نافع, to go to الأندلس by sea, and he wrote to the men who had volunteered with them. The letter
turns on قسطنطينية — the city no Muslim army had yet touched — and says it will only be opened from one
direction. **Our two books do not carry the same word for that direction.** ابن كثير reads "from the
sea"; ابن الأثير reads "from الأندلس". Both are given here; neither is suppressed.

**The statement:**
> وَكَتَبَ عُثْمَانُ إِلَى مَنِ انْتَدَبَ مَعَهُمَا: أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنَّ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةَ إِنَّمَا تُفْتَحُ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْأَنْدَلُسِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1156
> *English:* "And عثمان wrote to those who volunteered with the two of them: To proceed — القسطنطينية is only opened from the direction of الأندلس."

**عبرت:** A man may aim at a city his great-grandchildren will not live to enter, and still be right to
aim.

### UTC/E-UC14 · إفريقية pays the Muslims, and then the emperor asks for the same again
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۳ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** إفريقية turns back to Roman colour, then
neutral.

**What happened:** إفريقية had made terms with the Muslims and paid. Then the emperor sent one of his
own patricians to collect from the same people the same amount the Muslims had taken. He came ashore at
Carthage and told them what the emperor had ordered, and they refused him to his face: we pay what we
always paid, and he ought rather to have forgiven us what the Muslims took. The province never settled
after that. عبد الله بن سعد raided it a second time, and later governors raided it again, and in the
end the people of إفريقية rose.

**The statement:**
> نَحْنُ نُؤَدِّي مَا كَانَ يُؤْخَذُ مِنَّا، وَقَدْ كَانَ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يُسَامِحَنَا لِمَا نَالَهُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنَّا.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1155
> *English:* "We will render what used to be taken from us; and it would have been fitting for him to be lenient with us, for what the Muslims got from us."

**عبرت:** A distant ruler who taxes his own people for their losses will not keep them long.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC15 · The wife who reached the pavilion first
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۵ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أرمينية — قاليقلا.

**What happened:** حبيب بن مسلمة was in أرمينية with a force from الشام when a Roman army of eighty
thousand came against him. He decided to attack them at night, and his wife أم عبد الله بنت يزيد
الكلبية overheard him planning it. She asked him where they would meet afterwards, and he told her: in
the commander's pavilion. He fell on the Romans in the dark and killed whoever stood against him, and
when he reached the enemy commander's pavilion he found his wife already there ahead of him.

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۵۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1148
> *English:* "And his wife أم عبد الله بنت يزيد الكلبية heard him and said: where is your appointed place? He said: the pavilion of الموريان."

### UTC/E-UC16 · Town after town, by treaty and not by storm
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۵ AH onward `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أذربيجان, أرمينية, جرزان, تفليس, أرّان,
برذعة, شروان, الباب — each marked with a treaty symbol, not a sword.

**What happened:** The northern frontier was not stormed; it was negotiated. أذربيجان was renewed on
the terms حذيفة ؓ had made — eight hundred thousand درهم. Then, one after another: the patrician of
خلاط came in with an old letter of safe-conduct and it was honoured; the lord of مكس settled for his
lands; دبيل asked for terms when a mangonel was set against it and was given them; the patrician of
البسفرجان came in and settled for the whole of his country; جرزان and تفليس sent and made terms.
سلمان بن ربيعة took البيلقان on terms that guaranteed their lives, their property and even their city
walls.

**The statement:**
> فَصَالَحَهُمْ عَلَى صُلْحِ حُذَيْفَةَ، وَهُوَ ثَمَانُمِائَةِ أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ، وَقَبَضَ الْمَالَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1147
> *English:* "So he made terms with them on حذيفة's terms, which is eight hundred thousand درهم, and he took the money."

**عبرت:** Most of the map that changed colour in those years changed it across a table.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC17 · Describe the sea to me
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reign of عمر ؓ, told here `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ had been pressing عمر ؓ for years to let him put Muslims on ships. He said
a village of حمص was close enough to enemy country that its people could hear the dogs bark and the
cockerels crow. عمر ؓ did not answer him. He wrote instead to عمرو بن العاص ؓ, who had seen the sea,
and asked him for a description of it and of the man who rides it. What came back is one of the finest
pieces of prose in the early Arabic record.

**The statement:**
> إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ خَلْقًا كَبِيرًا يَرْكَبُهُ خَلْقٌ صَغِيرٌ، لَيْسَ إِلَّا السَّمَاءُ وَالْمَاءُ، إِنْ رَكَدَ خَرَقَ الْقُلُوبَ، وَإِنَّ تَحَرَّكَ أَزَاغَ الْعُقُولَ، يَزْدَادُ فِيهِ الْيَقِينُ قِلَّةً، وَالشَّكُّ كَثْرَةً، هُمْ فِيهِ كَدُودٍ عَلَى عُودٍ، إِنْ مَالَ غَرِقَ، وَإِنْ نَجَا بَرِقَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1158
> *English:* "I have seen a great creature ridden by a small creature; there is nothing but sky and water. If it lies still it tears the hearts; if it moves it unseats the minds. Certainty in it grows less and doubt grows more. They on it are like a worm on a stick: if it tips, he drowns; if he survives, he is dazed."

**عبرت:** Before deciding a great question, a ruler sent for a description from a man who had seen the
thing itself.

**Hands-up?** Has anyone here crossed open sea in a small boat?

### UTC/E-UC18 · I will never carry a Muslim upon it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reign of عمر ؓ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عمر ؓ read عمرو's description and refused. He wrote to معاوية ؓ that he would never
put a Muslim on that water, and added that he had been told this sea asks God's leave every day and
night to drown the earth — and how, then, should he carry armies on it? He finished with a warning not
to raise the matter with him again. ابن كثير gives the same refusal in his own words: he would not let
him carry the Muslims onto a creature which, if it were troubled, would destroy them to the last man.

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1158
> *English:* "…by the truth, I will never carry a Muslim upon it."

**عبرت:** A refusal can be the most careful decision a man in authority ever makes.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC19 · عثمان ؓ allows the sea — and attaches one condition
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۸ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the first ship symbol appears on the map of the
Roman sea.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ asked عثمان ؓ for the same permission, again and again, and in the end
عثمان ؓ gave it. But he wrote a condition into it, and the condition is the part worth remembering. Do
not pick men out for this. Do not draw lots among them. Put it to them as a choice, and whoever chooses
it willingly — carry him, and help him. Not one man went onto those first ships who had not volunteered
to go.

**The statement:**
> لَا تَنْتَخِبِ النَّاسَ وَلَا تُقْرِعْ بَيْنَهُمْ، خَيِّرْهُمْ فَمَنِ اخْتَارَ الْغَزْوَ طَائِعًا فَاحْمِلْهُ وَأَعِنْهُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1159
> *English:* "Do not pick men out, and do not draw lots among them. Give them the choice; whoever chooses the campaign willingly, carry him and help him."

**عبرت:** Permission granted with a restraint written into it is a different thing from permission
granted plainly.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC20 · You are among the first of them
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۸ AH, recalling a day in المدينة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Years before, the Prophet ﷺ had slept in the house of أم حرام بنت ملحان ؓ and woke
laughing. She asked him what made him laugh, and he said people of his nation had been shown to him
riding the midst of this sea like kings upon thrones. She asked him to pray that she be one of them,

asked again, and he said: you are among the first of them. She lived long enough to sail on this fleet.

### UTC/E-UC21 · قبرص, reached from two directions at once

### UTC/E-UC22 · The strangest treaty of the reign
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۸ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Cyprus in a third colour — neither side's.

**What happened:** The terms made with the people of Cyprus were unlike anything else in these years.
They would pay the Muslims seven thousand دينار a year — and go on paying Rome the same amount, and the
Muslims would not stop them. The Muslims would not defend them either, from Rome or from anyone behind
them. What they owed instead was information: they must tell the Muslims when a Roman force sailed
towards them, and the Muslims' road to the enemy would run through their island. It is a treaty of
neutrality and early warning, written before anyone had a word for either.

**The statement:**
> فَصَالَحَهُمْ أَهْلُهَا عَلَى جِزْيَةٍ سَبْعَةِ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ، يُؤَدُّونَ إِلَى الرُّومِ مِثْلَهَا، لَا يَمْنَعُهُمُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وَلَيْسَ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ مَنْعُهُمْ مِمَّنْ أَرَادَهُمْ مِمَّنْ وَرَاءَهُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1159
> *English:* "Its people made terms with them on a jizya of seven thousand دينار every year, while they pay the like of it to الروم — the Muslims not preventing them from that, and it not being upon the Muslims to protect them from whoever behind them might seek them."

**عبرت:** Not every arrangement in that century was a conquest; some were a careful balance written
down.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC23 · The mule on the shore at قبرص

### UTC/E-UC24 · أبو الدرداء ؓ weeps on the day of the victory
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۸ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map — this is a large-statement slide.

**What happened:** When the captives of قبرص were brought in, جبير بن نفير saw أبو الدرداء ؓ sitting
and weeping. He said to him: you weep, on a day when God has honoured Islam and its people? أبو
الدرداء ؓ struck him on the shoulder with his hand and answered him — and what he said was not about
the island at all. It was about what happens to any nation, including this one, that abandons what it
was commanded.

**The statement:**
> ويحك إن هذه كانت أمة قاهرة لهم ملك، فلما ضيَّعوا أمر الله صيَّرهم إلى ما ترى، سلّط الله عليهم السبي، وإذا سلِّط على قوم السبي فليس لله فيهم حاجة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3437
> *English:* "Woe to you — this was a nation that overcame, having a kingdom. When they wasted the command of God He brought them to what you see; God set captivity over them, and when captivity is set over a people, God has no need of them."

**عبرت:** The warning in a victory is heard by the man who is looking at the losers and thinking of
himself.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC26 · The grandsons of the Prophet ﷺ on the Caspian shore
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۰ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** an arrow from الكوفة north-east to قومس,
جرجان, طبرستان.

**What happened:** سعيد بن العاص marched out of الكوفة for طبرستان, on the far shore under the Caspian.
Both books say that nobody had raided it before. Riding with him were الحسن ؓ and الحسين ؓ, the four
Companions called the عبادلة, and حذيفة بن اليمان ؓ, among a great number of the Companions. They came

> *English:* "المدائني related that سعيد بن العاص rode out in an army in which were الحسن and الحسين, and the four عبد اللهs, and حذيفة بن اليمان, among a great number of the Companions."

**عبرت:** In one lifetime the frontier had moved from the edge of المدينة to the shore of another sea

### UTC/E-UC27 · The prayer of fear, taught on the field
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۰ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** طميسة, on the Caspian.

**What happened:** The fighting at طميسة grew so close that the army needed to pray the prayer of fear
— the shortened form, prayed in shifts, with half the men facing the enemy. The commander did not know
how to do it. He asked حذيفة بن اليمان ؓ how the Messenger of God ﷺ had prayed it. حذيفة ؓ told him,
and he prayed it exactly as he was told. A generation was already commanding armies who had to be
taught the Sunnah on the spot by the men who had seen it.

**The statement:**
> فَقَاتَلَهُ أَهْلُهَا، فَصَلَّى صَلَاةَ الْخَوْفِ، أَعْلَمَهُ حُذَيْفَةُ كَيْفِيَّتَهَا، وَهُمْ يَقْتَتِلُونَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1170
> *English:* "And its people fought him, so he prayed the prayer of fear — حذيفة taught him its manner — while they were fighting."

**عبرت:** The chain of learning was still hand to hand, and it was carried into battle.

### UTC/E-UC28 · جرجان pays what it likes, and then stops paying
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۰ AH and after `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the road through قومس, drawn and then
broken.

**What happened:** جرجان made terms for two hundred thousand. Afterwards they would send sometimes a
hundred thousand, sometimes two hundred, sometimes three hundred, and say each time: this is the terms
of our terms. Sometimes they sent nothing at all. In the end they refused outright, and the road to
خراسان through قومس could not be used except in real fear of them. A frontier on a map is a line; a
frontier on the ground is a road that is open some years and shut in others.

**The statement:**
> وَيَقُولُونَ: هَذَا صُلْحُ صُلْحِنَا، وَرُبَّمَا مَنَعُوهُ، ثُمَّ امْتَنَعُوا وَكَفَرُوا، فَانْقَطَعَ طَرِيقُ خُرَاسَانَ مِنْ نَاحِيَةِ قُومِسَ إِلَّا عَلَى خَوْفٍ شَدِيدٍ مِنْهُمْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1171
> *English:* "And they would say: this is the terms of our terms. And sometimes they withheld it. Then they refused and broke faith, and the road to خراسان by way of قومس was cut except in severe fear of them."

**عبرت:** Holding ground is a longer labour than taking it, and it is never finished.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC29 · Rome gathers as it had never gathered since Islam began

**What happened:** The conquests in the west had a consequence. When the news of what had happened in
إفريقية and on the western sea reached قسطنطينية, the emperor's own son قسطنطين came out with a
gathering that Rome had never assembled since Islam began — five hundred ships, or by another report

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1178
> *English:* "قسطنطين the son of هرقل came out with a gathering of his, the like of which الروم had not gathered since Islam began."

**عبرت:** Success at the far end of the world brings the answer to your own door.

### UTC/E-UC30 · One side at its clappers, the other at its Qur'an
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۱ AH, the night before `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map — a large statement.

**What happened:** The two fleets came in sight of one another and the wind was against the Muslims, so
both sides dropped anchor and waited out the night. ابن كثير and ابن الأثير both describe that night
and they describe it the same way. The Romans spent it at their chanting and their crossing. The
Muslims spent it reciting, and praying, and calling on God. In the morning the wind had gone.

**The statement:**
> فَبَاتُوا لَيْلَتَهُمْ وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ يَقْرَءُونَ الْقُرْآنَ وَيُصَلُّونَ وَيَدْعُونَ، وَالرُّومُ يَضْرِبُونَ بِالنَّوَاقِيسِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1179
> *English:* "And they passed their night — the Muslims reciting the Qur'an and praying and supplicating, and الروم striking the wooden clappers."

**عبرت:** What a people does in the night before tells you what they are.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC31 · The water, the water
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A man who was there told this. Before the fighting began the Muslims called across
the water and offered the Romans a choice: come out onto the land with us and let the hastier of us and
of you die there. The Romans answered with one sound, the whole fleet together, like the snort of a
single man, and what they shouted back was: the water! the water! They wanted the fight at sea, where
they had five hundred ships and centuries of practice, and the Muslims fought them there anyway.

**The statement:**
> فقلنا لهم: إنْ شئتم خرجنا نحن وأنتم إلى البر فمات الأعجل (٨) منّا ومنكم، قال فنخروا نخرةَ رجلٍ واحدٍ وقالوا: الماء الماء
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3442
> *English:* "We said to them: if you wish, we and you will go out to the land, and the more hasty of us and of you will die. He said: they snorted the snort of one man and said: the water! the water!"

**عبرت:** Each side chooses the ground it knows; the harder thing is to fight on the ground you do not.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC32 · Ships tied to ships, and the sea changing colour
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** ذات الصواري marked on the western sea.

**What happened:** They brought the ships up against each other and tied them together, hull to hull,
so that the fleets became one floating field, and then fought across them with swords and daggers, men

> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3443

**عبرت:** The cost of a victory is on the same page as the victory, when the historian is honest.

### UTC/E-UC33 · What became of the emperor's son
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** an arrow from ذات الصواري north to صقلية.

**What happened:** قسطنطين got away wounded. ابن كثير says only that he was treated for a long while
afterwards. ابن الأثير follows him further: he sailed to صقلية, and when its people asked him what had
happened and he told them, they turned on him and said he had destroyed Christendom and wiped out its
men, and that if the Arabs came now there would be nobody left to keep them off. Then, ابن الأثير says,

report.**

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1179
> *English:* "You have destroyed Christendom and wiped out its men! If the Arabs came to us, there would be no one with us to keep them off."

### UTC/E-UC34 · Twenty years, four of them at ease
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a long thin line tracing يزدجرد's flight —
المدائن, أصبهان, الري, كرمان, سجستان, مرو.

**What happened:** يزدجرد بن شهريار had inherited an empire that had stood for four centuries. He held
it in peace for four years. For the remaining sixteen he was moving — فارس, then كرمان, then سجستان,
then خراسان — writing to the kings of China and فرغانة and كابل and الخزر for help that never came, and
running out of country. Both of our books give the same arithmetic and neither softens it.

**The statement:**
> وكان مُلْكُ يزدجرد عشرين سنة، منها أربع سنين في دعة، وباقي ذلك هاربًا (٣) من بلد إلى بلد، خوفًا من الإسلام وأهله. وهو آخر ملوك الفرس في الدنيا على الإطلاق
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3445
> *English:* "The reign of يزدجرد was twenty years, four of them at ease, and the remainder of it fleeing from land to land in fear of Islam and its people. And he is the last of the kings of Persia in the world, without qualification."

**عبرت:** Four years of ease and sixteen of flight — and the throne was the same throne throughout.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC35 · Four dirhams
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a mill on the river المرغاب, near مرو.

**What happened:** At the end he was alone in a mill on a river outside مرو, and he had not eaten for
three days. The man who found him did not want his ring, whose price could not be counted, and did not
want his belt. He wanted four dirhams to let him go, and the last king of Persia did not have four
dirhams. He pulled one earring out of his ear and offered that instead. And then he said something that
the historians kept, because it is the kind of thing a man says once: I used to be told that a day
would come when I would need four dirhams — and now I have seen it.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ لَهُ: أَعْطِنِي أَرْبَعَةَ دَرَاهِمَ وَأُخَلِّي عَنْكَ، فَلَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَهُ وَقَالَ: إِنَّ خَاتَمِي لَا يُحْصَى ثَمَنُهُ فَخُذْهُ، فَأَبَى عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ يَزْدَجِرْدُ: قَدْ كُنْتُ أُخْبَرُ أَنِّي سَأَحْتَاجُ إِلَى أَرْبَعَةِ دَرَاهِمَ فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ ذَلِكَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۹۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1182
> *English:* "He said to him: give me four دراهم and I will let you go. And he had none with him, and said: my ring — its price cannot be counted; take it. He refused him. So يزدجرد said to him: I used to be told that I would one day need four دراهم — and now I have seen it."

**عبرت:** A treasure that cannot be counted is worth nothing to a man who needs four dirhams tonight.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC36 · Take me to the Arabs — they are ashamed to kill kings
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map — large statement.

**What happened:** When they closed round him he did not fight and he did not offer money again. He
argued. He told them that in the books of his own religion it is written that whoever is bold enough to
kill kings is punished with burning in this world, besides what is waiting for him afterwards. Then he
gave them a way out: do not kill me; take me to the king, or take me to the Arabs — for the Arabs are
ashamed to kill kings. They refused. They stripped him, strangled him with a bowstring and put him in
the river.

> ويحكم لا تقتلوني، فإنّا نجدُ في كتبنا أنّ من اجترأ على قتل الملوك
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3445
> *English:* "Woe to you — do not kill me, for we find in our books that whoever is bold enough to kill kings…"

**عبرت:** The last argument of the last Sasanian was that his enemies would treat him better than his
own people.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC37 · The Christians of مرو bury the last Sasanian
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مرو.

**What happened:** His body went into the river and nobody came for it. Then the bishop of مرو
gathered the Christians of the town and put it to them: the son of شهريار has been killed; and شهريار
was the son of شيرين, the believing woman whose kindness to our people you know, and the Christians
were honoured in the reign of his grandfather أنوشروان. So we should grieve for him and build him a
tomb. They agreed, and took the body out of the water, and shrouded it, and buried it.

> قُتِلَ ابْنُ شَهْرَيَارَ، وَإِنَّمَا شَهْرَيَارُ ابْنُ شِيرِينَ الْمُؤْمِنَةِ الَّتِي قَدْ عَرَفْتُمْ حَقَّهَا وَإِحْسَانَهَا إِلَى أَهْلِ مِلَّتِنَا

### UTC/E-UC38 · When كسرى perishes there is no كسرى after him

### UTC/E-UC39 · A governor of twenty-five, and the two gates of خراسان
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۹ AH onward `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** an arrow from البصرة east through فارس

**What happened:** عبد الله بن عامر بن كريز was made governor of البصرة at twenty-five years old, with

### UTC/E-UC40 · Town after town of خراسان, mostly without a battle
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** نيسابور, نسا, أبيورد, سرخس, طوس, هراة, مرو,
مرو الروذ, بلخ — each with a treaty symbol except سرخس.

**What happened:** قوهستان for six hundred thousand. نيسابور besieged for months and then settled for a
million, after one of its four quarter-commanders opened a gate. نسا and أبيورد by treaty. طوس by
treaty. هراة, باذغيس and بوشنج by treaty. And مرو, the greatest of them, for two million two hundred
thousand — the whole city by treaty except one village that was taken by force. Most of خراسان changed
hands by agreement, city by city, for money.

**The statement:**

> *English:* "And when ابن عامر had prevailed over these lands, the marzbān of مرو sent to him and made terms with him for two million two hundred thousand درهم — and it is said otherwise."

**عبرت:** Most of a map is not won in battles; it is won when the man holding it decides to write.

### UTC/E-UC41 · Where the advance stopped
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** خوارزم marked, and the arrow stops there — the
furthest point east.

**What happened:** الأحنف بن قيس ؓ went on east from بلخ to خوارزم, on the river جيحون, and could not
take it. He asked the men with him what they thought. One of them answered him with two lines of
عمرو بن معدي كرب: if you cannot manage a thing, leave it, and pass over it to what you can. So he
turned back. **In ابن كثير's telling the same verse is said at بلخ, when winter overtook them, and the
campaign was only paused.** Either way, that is where the arrow stops.

**The statement:**
> إِذَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ أَمْرًا فَدَعْهُ ... وَجَاوِزْهُ إِلَى مَا تَسْتَطِيعُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1186
> *English:* "If you cannot manage a thing, leave it — and pass over it to what you can."

**عبرت:** Knowing where to stop is part of the same skill as knowing how far to go.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC42 · Begin with the struggle against your own bellies
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map — large statement.

**What happened:** الأحنف بن قيس ؓ — the man the Arabs used as their byword for forbearance — sent
الأقرع بن حابس off against a coalition at الجوزجان, and before they rode he gave his tribesmen four
instructions. Love one another and give freely to one another, and your affairs will come out straight.
Begin with the struggle against your own bellies and your own desires, and your religion will be sound.
Do not go beyond the bounds, and your struggle will be kept safe for you.

**The statement:**
> يَا بَنِي تَمِيمٍ تَحَابُّوا وَتَبَاذَلُوا تُعْدَلْ أُمُورُكُمْ، وَابْدَءُوا بِجِهَادِ بُطُونِكُمْ وَفُرُوجِكُمْ يَصْلُحْ لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ، وَلَا تَغْلُوا يَسْلَمْ لَكُمْ جِهَادُكُمْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1186
> *English:* "O بنو تميم, love one another and give freely to one another, and your affairs will be set straight. And begin with the struggle against your bellies and your desires, and your religion will be sound for you. And do not exceed, and your struggle will be kept safe for you."

**عبرت:** The order of the two struggles was never in doubt among the people who did both.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC43 · إحرام from نيسابور
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a long line from نيسابور all the way to مكة.

**What happened:** When it was over, people said to ابن عامر: nothing has been opened to anyone as has
been opened to you — فارس, كرمان, سجستان and the whole of خراسان. He answered that he would make his
thanks for it by entering the state of إحرام for an عمرة from the very spot where he stood. And he did
— he put on إحرام in نيسابور and travelled the whole way to مكة in it. **ابن كثير adds that when he
reached المدينة, عثمان ؓ reproved him for it; ابن الأثير does not report that.**

**The statement:**
> فقال: لا جرمَ، لأجعلنَّ شُكْري لله على ذلك أن أحرم بعمرةٍ من موقفي هذا مُشمِّرًا فأحرمَ بعمرة من نيسابور
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3447
> *English:* "He said: no doubt of it; I shall make my thanks to God for that by entering إحرام for an عمرة from this place where I stand, girded up. So he entered إحرام for an عمرة from نيسابور."

**عبرت:** A large gratitude looks for a large way to be shown, and can still be told it went too far.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC44 · The idol whose eyes were handed back
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱–۳۳ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the mountain of الزور, in الداور,
سجستان.

**What happened:** عبد الرحمن بن سمرة besieged the people of الداور on the mountain of الزور, and then
made terms with them. Their idol was there — a figure of gold with two rubies for eyes. He went in to
it and broke off its hand and took out the two stones. Then he turned to their governor and handed him
the gold and the jewels back, and told him why he had done it: not to take them, but so that he would
know the thing could neither harm him nor help him.

**The statement:**
> دُونَكَ الذَّهَبُ وَالْجَوْهَرُ، وَإِنَّمَا أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُعْلِمَكَ أَنَّهُ لَا يَضُرُّ وَلَا يَنْفَعُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۹۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1188
> *English:* "Take the gold and the jewel for yourself. I only wanted to teach you that it can neither harm nor benefit."

**عبرت:** The demonstration was the point; taking the gold would have ruined the lesson.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC45 · كابل and زابلستان — the doorway that leads here
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۱–۳۴ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** كابل and غزنة marked — the eastern edge.

**What happened:** عبد الرحمن بن سمرة pushed on past زرنج to the frontier of India, and took كابل and
زابلستان, which is the district of غزنة. That is the furthest east this story goes in the lifetime of
عثمان ؓ. **Hold those two names.** The road that begins there is the road that reaches سندھ, and دہلی,
and eventually this city — and that is a later session. And even this was not held: when the affair of
عثمان ؓ became disordered, the deputy left behind at زرنج was thrown out by its people.

**The statement:**
> وَفَتَحَ كَابُلَ وَزَابُلِسْتَانَ، وَهِيَ وِلَايَةُ غَزْنَةَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۹۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1188
> *English:* "And he opened كابل and زابلستان, which is the district of غزنة."

**عبرت:** The road that ends at a place you know began as a line in a chronicle about somewhere else.

**Hands-up?** Does anyone recognise the second of those two names?

### UTC/E-UC46 · The archers of the eye
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reign of عمر ؓ, told here `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** an arrow south up the
Nile, which stops.

**What happened:** After Egypt was taken, the Muslims raided south into النوبة, and they came back
wounded, and some of them came back blind. The Nubians shot so accurately that they hit men in the eye,
and the Muslims gave them a name for it: the archers of the eye. It is one of the very few places in
that century where an advancing army simply could not get through.

**The statement:**
> رَمْيِهِمْ، فَسَمَّوْهُمْ رُمَاةَ الْحَدَقِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۳۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1077
> *English:* "…their shooting. So they named them the archers of the eye."

**عبرت:** Every expansion has a boundary somewhere, and the people who set it usually get a name for
how they did it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC47 · The treaty that went both ways
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** in the reign of عثمان ؓ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a line across the Nile south
of Egypt, in a colour used nowhere else.

**What happened:** When عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح governed Egypt he did not try again to force the
Nubians. He made terms with them instead, and the terms are unlike anything else in these years: a
number of persons to be sent north each year as a gift — and the Muslims, every year, to send south a
specified quantity of food and of clothing. Not tribute in one direction, but an exchange. عثمان ؓ
confirmed it, and so did every ruler after him, and it stood for centuries.

**The statement:**
> صَالَحَهُمْ عَلَى هَدِيَّةٍ عِدَّةِ رُءُوسٍ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ، وَيُهْدِي إِلَيْهِمُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ طَعَامًا مُسَمًّى وَكُسْوَةً، وَأَمْضَى ذَلِكَ الصُّلْحَ عُثْمَانُ وَمَنْ بَعْدَهُ مِنْ وُلَاةِ الْأُمُورِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۳۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1077
> *English:* "He made terms with them on a gift of a number of persons every year, and that the Muslims would present to them every year a specified quantity of food and clothing. And عثمان confirmed that treaty, and those who held authority after him."

**عبرت:** An arrow that stops and becomes an agreement can outlast every arrow that kept going.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC48 · The Turks test whether these people die
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۲ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بلنجر, north of the Caucasus.

**What happened:** The raids into the Caucasus had gone on long enough that the Turks began talking
among themselves. We used to be a nation no one could stand against, they said, and now this small
nation has come and we cannot stand against them. One of them said: these people do not die — nobody has
ever been killed among them on any of their raids. Another said: then why not test it? So they laid an
ambush in the thickets and shot a party as it passed, and killed them. Having proved that a Muslim can
be killed, they called their chiefs together and named a day.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ لَا يَمُوتُونَ وَمَا أُصِيبَ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ فِي غَزْوِهِمْ. وَقَدْ كَانَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ غَزُوهُمْ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ فَلَمْ يُقْتَلْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ، فَلِهَذَا ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَمُوتُونَ. فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: أَفَلَا تُجَرِّبُونَ؟
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1192
> *English:* "These people do not die, and no one of them has been struck down in their raiding. And the Muslims had raided them before that and not one of them had been killed, and for this reason they supposed that they did not die. So one of them said: will you not test it?"

**عبرت:** An army's reputation is an asset until the day somebody decides to check it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC49 · The commander who was lost at بلنجر
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۲ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بلنجر — the northern arrow stops and reverses.

**What happened:** عثمان ؓ had written to the commander at الباب warning him not to push the Muslims
into a hard place. He went on to بلنجر anyway. The Turks and الخزر met him there together and the
fighting was severe, and he was killed. The Muslims broke and split into two parties, one making for
الخزر country and one for جيلان and جرجان — and among the second were أبو هريرة ؓ and سلمان
الفارسي ؓ. The people of بلنجر took the commander's body, put it in a coffin, and were still praying
for rain beside it when these books were written.

**The statement:**
> فَأَخَذَ أَهْلُ بَلَنْجَرَ جَسَدَهُ وَجَعَلُوهُ فِي تَابُوتٍ فَهُمْ يَسْتَسْقُونَ بِهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1192
> *English:* "The people of بلنجر took his body and put it in a coffin, and they seek rain by it."

**عبرت:** Not every frontier moved outward, and the ones that stopped are part of the same map.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC50 · The first quarrel between الكوفة and الشام
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۲ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الباب, with two arrows arriving — one from
الكوفة, one from الشام.

**What happened:** After the defeat, عثمان ؓ sent reinforcements: men of الشام under حبيب بن مسلمة, to
join the men of الكوفة under سلمان بن ربيعة. Then the two commanders could not agree which of them was
in charge. Men of الشام said they had a mind to strike سلمان; men of الكوفة said then we will strike
حبيب and hold him, and if you insist there will be dead on both sides. A poet of الكوفة put it into
verse. Both of our books say the same thing about that argument, in almost the same words: it was the
first disagreement that fell between the people of الكوفة and the people of الشام.

**The statement:**
> فتنازع حبيب وسلمان في الإمرة حتى اختلفا، فكان أولَ اختلافٍ وقعَ بين أهل الكوفة وأهل الشام
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3446
> *English:* "And حبيب and سلمان contended over the command until they fell out; and it was the first disagreement that fell between the people of الكوفة and the people of الشام."

**عبرت:** Some cracks are recorded by the historians at the moment they first appear, long before
anything falls.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC51 · I am the naked warner
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۰ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** four garrison cities light at once — حمص,
دمشق, الكوفة, البصرة.

**What happened:** حذيفة بن اليمان ؓ came back from the northern front and he was frightened, and it
was not about the fighting. He had seen the men of حمص saying their recitation was better than
everyone's because they had it from المقداد; the men of دمشق saying the same; الكوفة saying the same
because they had it from ابن مسعود; البصرة saying the same because they had it from أبي موسى. He went
to عثمان ؓ and used the oldest phrase in the language for a man who has seen the enemy and run back
without stopping to dress.

**The statement:**
> أَنَا النَّذِيرُ الْعُرْيَانُ فَأَدْرِكُوا الْأُمَّةَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1172
> *English:* "I am the naked warner — so reach this nation in time."

**عبرت:** The danger that frightened the man who had fought at every front was not on any frontier.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC52 · Had it been given to me, I would have taken his road
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۰ AH and after `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map — large statement.

**What happened:** The copies were made and sent out, and in الكوفة there were men who did not like it
and who said so. Later, when علي ؓ came to الكوفة, a man stood up in front of him and found fault with
عثمان ؓ for having gathered the people onto one مصحف — expecting, presumably, to be agreed with. علي ؓ
shouted him down. He said: be quiet. He did that with a body of us present. And had the matter been put
in my charge as it was put in his, I would have taken the same road he took.

**The statement:**
> اسْكُتْ فَعَنْ مَلَأٍ مِنَّا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ، فَلَوْ وُلِّيتُ مِنْهُ مَا وُلِّيَ عُثْمَانُ لَسَلَكْتُ سَبِيلَهُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1173
> *English:* "Be silent. He did that with a body of us present; and had I been given charge of it as عثمان was given charge of it, I would have taken his road."

**عبرت:** When the men who were there refuse to quarrel about a thing, those of us who were not there
have no standing to start.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTC/E-UC53 · The ring that went into the well
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۰ AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بئر أريس, two miles from المدينة.

**What happened:** The silver ring of the Messenger of God ﷺ, the seal that had gone on the letters to
the kings, had passed to أبو بكر ؓ, then to عمر ؓ, then to عثمان ؓ, who wore it for six years. He was
sitting at the mouth of a well outside المدينة, turning it in his fingers, and it fell in. They drew
the well dry and they could not find it. He offered a great sum of money to anyone who brought it, and
it was never found, and ابن كثير writing centuries later says it has not been found to this hour. He
had another made to the same pattern.

**The statement:**
> وفي هذه السنة سقطَ خاتمُ النبيّ ﷺ من يد عثمان في بئر أَرِيس (٥)، وهي على ميلين من المدينة، وهي من أقل الآبار ماءً، فلم يدرك خبره بعد بذل مال جزيل، والاجتهاد في طلبه حتى الساعة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3439
> *English:* "And in this year the ring of the Prophet ﷺ fell from the hand of عثمان into the well of أريس, which is two miles from المدينة, and it is among the wells of least water. And no news of it was got, after much money was spent and much effort made in seeking it, until this hour."

**عبرت:** In the same years that a Persian empire was ending, a small silver ring was lost in a shallow
well and never recovered.

**Hands-up?** no

## The مصحف, and the state عثمان ؓ ran

*Source note: [`uthman-the-mushaf-and-the-state.md`](../docs/research/uthman-the-mushaf-and-the-state.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### UTM/E-MS1 · The first morning on the pulpit
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة lights. No movement.

**What happened:** When the pledge had been given, the new caliph came out to the people and climbed the
pulpit of the Prophet ﷺ. He praised God, and then said something no one expected from a man who had just
been given the command of the Muslims. He said that the first mounting of any beast is hard; that there
were days ahead; that if he lived, the address would come to them as it should. And he ended by saying
plainly that he had never been an orator, and that God would teach him.

**The statement:**
> أيها الناس أولُ كلِّ مركبٍ صعبٌ، وإنَّ بعد اليوم أيامًا، وإن أعشْ تأتِكُم الخطبة على وجهها، وما كنا خطباء وسيُعلمُنا الله.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3528
> *English:* "O people, the first mounting of any beast is hard. After today there are days to come, and if I live the address will reach you as it should. We were never orators — and God will teach us."

**عبرت:** A man who admits at the start that he is not yet equal to the office has told the truth about
every office.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-MS2 · The first case laid before the new caliph
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Before the new caliph had done anything else, a prisoner was waiting. The son of عمر ؓ
had killed three people in المدينة in the days after his father was struck, and سعد ؓ had taken the sword
out of his hand and held him. عثمان ؓ called a group of the مهاجرون and asked them what he should do. علی ؓ
told him he should put the man to death; another said his father had been killed only yesterday, was the
son to be killed today; عمرو بن العاص ؓ said God had spared him the deed. The caliph decided that as the
only next of kin of the slain man he would pardon, and pay the blood-money himself.

**The statement:**
> فلما استخلف عثمان قال له علي: أقد عبيد الله من الهرمزان، فقال عثمان: ما له ولي غيري، وإني قد عفوت ولكن أديه.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۶۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1309
> *English:* "When ʿUthmān was made caliph, ʿAlī said to him: exact retaliation from ʿUbayd Allāh for al-Hurmuzān. ʿUthmān said: he has no next of kin but me, and I have pardoned — but I shall pay his blood-money."

**عبرت:** Men of the highest rank read the same law and reached different conclusions, and the office had
to choose one of them; that is what an office is for.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-MS3 · How long the quiet lasted — three men, three answers
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24–35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The Line: the twelve years marked as one block.

**What happened:** Three separate authorities in our books are asked, in effect, the same question: how
long was this reign untroubled. الحسن البصري, who lived through it, says twelve years, and that they found
nothing in his rule to object to. الزهري says six years with nothing held against him, and adds that he
was dearer to the people than عمر ؓ had been, because عمر ؓ was hard on them and this man was gentle. قتادة
and خليفة بن خياط, counting the term itself, make it twelve years less twelve days. The three are not
contradicting each other; they are answering three different questions, and that is worth saying out loud.

**The statement:**
> وقال أبو هلال: سمعت الحسن يقول: عمل عثمان اثنتي عشرة سنة، ما ينكرون من إمارته شيئا.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1300
> *English:* "Abū Hilāl said: I heard al-Ḥasan say — ʿUthmān governed twelve years, and they found nothing in his rule to object to."

**عبرت:** The years that are remembered as trouble were a small part of the years that were lived.

**Hands-up?** Twelve years is longer than the whole caliphate of أبو بكر ؓ and عمر ؓ put together — hands up
who would have guessed that.

---

### UTM/E-MS4 · The caliph asleep in the half-built mosque
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during the rebuilding of المسجد النبوي `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** A boy went into the mosque at midday with a bird he meant to let loose, while the
building work was going on. He found an old man asleep on the ground with a brick, or part of a brick,
under his head, and stood looking at him because he had never seen a face like it. The man woke and asked
who he was, and then called a servant, who came back with a robe and a thousand dirhams. The boy was
dressed in the robe with the money wrapped in it and sent home. He told his father he did not know who it
was, only that it was a man sleeping in the mosque; and his father told him it was the Commander of the
Faithful.

**The statement:**
> فإذا شيخ جميل حسن الوجه نائم، تحت رأسه لبنة أو بعض لَبنة، فقمت أنظر إليه أتعجب من جماله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3526
> *English:* "And there was an old man, handsome, of fine face, asleep, with a brick or part of a brick under his head; so I stood looking at him, marvelling at his beauty."

**عبرت:** Rank was not something he carried about with him; a child could stand over him and not know what
he was looking at.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-MS5 · What was cut into his seal
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Rulers of that age sealed letters with a signet, and the words cut into the stone were
a kind of public statement. Two of our books record what was on his. It was not a name and not a title. It
was a sentence of the Qurʾān about God, who created and then shaped what He created. One other report
gives it as a declaration of belief in God the Mighty. Either way, what the chancery of the Muslim state
stamped on its letters for twelve years was a line about the Creator.

**The statement:**
> كان نقش خاتم عثمان آمنت بالذي خلق فسوى.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3525
> *English:* "The inscription of ʿUthmān's ring was: I have believed in the One who created and then shaped."

**عبرت:** A state says what it believes in the smallest places first.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS6 · Buying the ground around the Kaʿbah
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 26 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة lights.

**What happened:** The Sacred Mosque had become too small for the numbers coming, so he widened it. He
bought the ground from the owners. Some sold and some refused; the houses of those who refused were pulled
down anyway and the price of each was put into the public treasury for them. They shouted at him in
public, and he had them put in prison. What he said to them is the part worth keeping: nothing had made
them bold against him but his own mildness, and عمر ؓ had done exactly this to them and they had not
shouted at him. Then people interceded, and he let them out.

**The statement:**
> وقال: ما جرأكم علي إلا حلمي، وقد فعل هذا بكم عمر فلم تصيحوا عليه، ثم كلموه فيهم فأطلقهم.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1311
> *English:* "And he said: nothing made you bold against me but my forbearance — ʿUmar did this very thing to you and you did not cry out at him. Then people spoke to him on their behalf, and he released them."

**عبرت:** The same act done by a hard man and a mild man is not received the same way, and the mild man
pays for it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS7 · The sea that عمر ؓ would not let a Muslim cross
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reign of عمر ؓ, and the reversal under عثمان ؓ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The
Mediterranean coast of الشام, and the sea beyond it.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ had pressed عمر ؓ for years for permission to fight at sea, because the Romans
were close. عمر ؓ answered that a single village of حمص whose dogs and cocks he could hear was dearer to
him than everything in that sea. Then he wrote to عمرو بن العاص ؓ and asked him to describe the sea and the
man who rides it. The answer he got back is one of the strangest letters in our books, and when عمر ؓ had
read it he wrote one line back to معاوية ؓ. That line held until he died. Under the next caliph, the ban
was lifted and the Muslims put to sea.

**The statement:**
> فكتب إليه: إني رأيت خلقا كبيرا يركبه خلق صغير، إن ركد حرق القلوب، وإن تحرك أراع العقول، يزداد فيه اليقين قلة، والشك كثرة، وهم فيه كدود على عود، إن مال غرق، وإن نجا برق.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۷۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1316
> *English:* "He wrote to him: I have seen a great creature ridden by a small creature. If it is still it burns the hearts; if it moves it terrifies the minds. Certainty in it grows less and doubt grows more. They upon it are like worms on a stick: if it tips, they drown; if it escapes, they are dazed."

**عبرت:** One caliph's caution and the next caliph's boldness were both judgements, not principles, and the
books record both without deciding between them.

**Hands-up?** Hands up if you think a state that has just conquered two empires would be afraid of a boat.

### UTM/E-MS8 · Cyprus, and the woman who was promised the sea
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 27 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** قبرص lights, first island beyond the coast.

**What happened:** With the ban lifted, معاوية ؓ raided Cyprus, and he went by ship with armies. عبادة بن
الصامت ؓ went with him, and so did his wife أم حرام بنت ملحان ؓ, the aunt of أنس ؓ, whom the Prophet ﷺ used
to visit and to whom he had given the tidings that she would be among those who rode that sea. On the
island she was thrown from her mule and died. Our book says the people of the place still point to the
grave and call it the grave of the righteous woman.

**The statement:**
> فصرعت عن بغلتها فماتت شهيدة -رحمها الله، وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يغشاها ويقيل عندها، وبشرها بالشهادة، فقبرها بقبرس يقولون: هذا قبر المرأة الصالحة.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1312
> *English:* "She was thrown from her mule and died a martyr — may God have mercy on her. The Prophet ﷺ used to visit her and take his midday rest with her, and he gave her the tidings of martyrdom. Her grave is in Cyprus; they say: this is the grave of the righteous woman."

**عبرت:** A promise made in a house in المدينة was kept on an island the people of that house had never
heard of.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS9 · The mosque rebuilt, and the six doors left where they were
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 29 AH, begun in ربيع الأول `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, the mosque marked.

**What happened:** The mosque of the Prophet ﷺ was rebuilt and widened. It was built in lime brought from
بطن نخل and in carved stone; the columns were inlaid stone and the roof was teak. Our book gives the
measurements: one hundred and sixty cubits long and one hundred and fifty wide. And then it gives one more
detail, which is the reason this card is here: he made the doors six, exactly as they had been in the time
of عمر ؓ. Everything else about the building was new. The number of doors was inherited.

**The statement:**
> وجعل طوله ستين ومئة ذراع، وعرضه خمسين ومئة ذراع، وجعل أبوابه ستة، على ما كانت (عليه) في زمان عمر بن الخطاب، ابتدأ بناءه في ربيع الأول منها.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3438
> *English:* "He made its length one hundred and sixty cubits and its breadth one hundred and fifty, and he made its doors six, as they had been in the time of ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb. He began its building in Rabīʿ al-Awwal of that year."

**عبرت:** Most of governing is deciding what not to change.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS10 · The third call on the day of الجمعة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, the market place الزوراء marked.

**What happened:** Two of our three books record, in one line each and in almost the same words, that he
added a third call on the day of الجمعة, and that it was given at a place called الزوراء, by the market of
المدينة, near the mosque. That is the whole of what they say. Neither book explains why. Neither calls it
an أذان; both say "the third call". It is one of the very few permanent changes to the shape of the Muslim
week, and the books that record it do not tell us his reason.

**The statement:**
> وفي هذه السنة زاد عثمان النداء الثالث يوم الجمعة على الزَّوْراء (٤).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3440
> *English:* "And in this year ʿUthmān added the third call on the day of Jumuʿah, upon al-Zawrāʾ."

**عبرت:** Something that every Muslim city still does every week entered the world in a single sentence,
without an argument attached to it.

**Hands-up?** Hands up if you have heard the call on الجمعة given twice before the khutbah. That second one
is from this year.

### UTM/E-MS11 · Four rakʿahs at مِنى
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 29 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة and مِنى.

**What happened:** He led the Ḥajj that year. A tent was pitched for him at مِنى — the first tent he had
pitched there — and he prayed the four-rakʿah prayers in full instead of shortening them as a traveller
does. More than one Companion objected to it in the open. Our book names three of them: علی ؓ,
عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ and عبد الله بن مسعود ؓ. What ابن مسعود ؓ said about it is recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ.

**The statement:**
> فأنكر ذلك عليه غيرُ واحد من الصحابة، كعلي وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وعبد الله بن مسعود، حتى قال ابن مسعود ليتَ حظّي من أربع ركعات ركعتان متقبلتان
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3438
> *English:* "More than one of the Companions objected to it — such as ʿAlī, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf and ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd — until Ibn Masʿūd said: would that my share of four rakʿahs were two, accepted."

**عبرت:** In that generation a disagreement with the head of state about two rakʿahs was said to his face,
in public, and recorded by name.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS12 · "A view I have taken"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 29 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مِنى.

**What happened:** عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ came to argue it with him, and one of our books also puts علی ؓ in
the conversation. The argument put to him was the strongest one available: the Prophet ﷺ prayed two here
while the revelation was still coming down; أبو بكر ؓ prayed two here; عمر ؓ prayed two here; and you
yourself prayed two here for the first part of your own rule. He gave his reasons — a wife at مكة,
property at الطائف, a party from اليمن who might take his two rakʿahs as proof that the prayer at home is
two. None of the reasons was accepted. He fell silent, and then he said five words, and both books
preserve them identically.

**The statement:**
> قال فسكت عثمان ثم قال: إنما هو رأي رأيته.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3438
> *English:* "ʿUthmān was silent, then said: it is only a view I have taken."

**عبرت:** He did not claim a revelation and he did not claim authority; he called it his own opinion, and
let it be argued with.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS13 · The man who objected, and then prayed four anyway
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 29 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مِنى.

**What happened:** ابن مسعود ؓ, who had objected to the four rakʿahs, came into the mosque at مِنى and asked
how many the Commander of the Faithful had prayed for Ẓuhr. They told him four. So he prayed four. The
people around him were baffled: had he not narrated to them that the Prophet ﷺ and أبو بكر ؓ and عمر ؓ all
prayed two here? He said yes — and that he was narrating it to them again this minute. And then he gave his
reason, and in another narration he put it in three words.

**The statement:**
> فقال: نعم! وأنا أحدثكموه الآن، ولكني أكره الاختلاف.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3531
> *English:* "He said: yes — and I narrate it to you now; but I dislike disagreement."

**عبرت:** He kept his opinion and he kept the congregation, and he did not think he had to choose.

**Hands-up?** Hands up if you would have prayed two.

### UTM/E-MS14 · A historian weighs four explanations and throws one away
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the eighth century of the Hijrah, looking back at 29 AH `[SOURCED]` ·
**Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Centuries later, ابن کثیر sat down to write this same incident and found four different
explanations in circulation for why the caliph prayed four. He set them all out. The first was fear that
the bedouin would conclude the obligation itself was two rakʿahs. The second was that he had married at
مكة. The third came with a ḥadīth attached, and of that ḥadīth he wrote four words: it is not sound. The
fourth was that he judged himself Commander of the Faithful wherever he was — and of that he said there is
something in it to consider, because the Messenger of God ﷺ was the Messenger of God wherever he was, and
he did not pray four on a journey. Having done all that, he passed no judgement on the man at all.

**The statement:**
> وهذا الحديث لا يصح، وقد تزوَّجَ رسول الله ﷺ في عمرة القضاء بميمونة بنت الحارث ولم يتمّ الصلاة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3532
> *English:* "But this ḥadīth is not sound; and the Messenger of God ﷺ married Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith during the ʿUmrah of Fulfilment and did not complete the prayer."

**عبرت:** Weighing the reports and declining to condemn the man are not two different attitudes; in this
tradition they are the same one.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS15 · The soldier who rode to المدينة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 25–30 AH, on campaign toward أرمينية `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The eastern front,
then the road west to المدينة.

**What happened:** حذيفة بن اليمان ؓ was on campaign, and on that campaign the armies of الشام and the
armies of العراق were together in one camp. They fell into dispute about the Qurʾān — not about its
meaning, about its recitation. He heard what he did not want to hear. He did not write a report and he did
not raise it with the commander. He got on his mount and rode to المدينة, went in to the Commander of the
Faithful, and said one sentence.

**The statement:**
> فركب حتى أتى عثمان فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين أدرك هذه الأمة قبل أن يختلفوا في القرآن اختلاف اليهود والنصارى في الكتب. ففزع لذلك عثمان
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1299
> *English:* "So he rode until he came to ʿUthmān and said: O Commander of the Faithful, reach this umma before they differ over the Qurʾān as the Jews and the Christians differed over the Books. ʿUthmān was alarmed at that."

**عبرت:** One man decided that what he had heard in a camp was a matter for the capital, and he was right.

**Hands-up?** Hands up if you can name the Companion who started the process that produced the muṣḥaf in
your house. It was not the caliph.

### UTM/E-MS16 · Two ways of reciting, in one camp
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the same campaign `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The camp, between الشام and العراق.

**What happened:** Our book explains exactly what the quarrel was. The Syrians in that camp recited after
the reading of المقداد بن الأسود ؓ and أبو الدرداء ؓ. The Iraqis recited after the reading of
عبد الله بن مسعود ؓ and أبو موسى ؓ. Both were sound. But the men who did not know that the Qurʾān had been
given leave to be recited on seven aḥruf began to prefer their own reading over the other man's — and then
to say the other man was wrong, and in some cases to say he was an unbeliever. That is what حذيفة ؓ heard,
and that is what he rode to stop.

**The statement:**
> وجعل من لا يعلم بَسَوغان القراءة على سبعة أحرف، يفضل قراءته على قراءة غيره، وربما خَطَّأ الآخر أو كَفَّره، فأدى ذلك إلى اختلاف شديد، وانتشار في الكلام السيء بين الناس
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3530
> *English:* "And those who did not know of the permissibility of reciting upon seven aḥruf began to prefer their own reading over the reading of another, and sometimes to declare the other wrong, or to declare him an unbeliever. That led to severe disagreement and to the spread of evil speech among the people."

**عبرت:** The danger was never the two readings; it was men who did not know that both were allowed.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS17 · He gathered the Companions before he moved
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** He did not act on حذيفة ؓ's word alone. Our book says he gathered the Companions and took
counsel with them, and that only then did he form the view that the muṣḥaf should be written on a single
ḥarf and that the people of every region should be brought to recite by it and nothing else. The reason
given for the decision is not a doctrine. It is an interest, stated plainly: to stop the contention and
drive away the disagreement.

**The statement:**
> فعند ذلك جمعَ عثمانُ الصحابةَ وشاورهم في ذلك، ورأى أن يكتب المصحف على حرف واحد، وأن يجمعَ الناسَ في سائر الأقاليم على القراءة به، دون ما سواه، لما رأى في ذلك من مصلحةِ كفِّ المنازعةِ، ودفعِ الاختلافِ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3530
> *English:* "At that ʿUthmān gathered the Companions and took counsel with them in the matter, and held the view that the muṣḥaf should be written upon a single ḥarf and that the people in all the regions should be gathered upon reciting by it and nothing else — for the benefit he saw in it of stopping the contention and driving away the disagreement."

**عبرت:** The most consequential decision of the century was taken in a room full of people who were asked
first.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS18 · The leaves in the keeping of حفصة ؓ
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH, going back to 12 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** There was already a written collection, and it had a history. After the battle of
اليمامة, when so many of the reciters were killed, عمر ؓ went to أبو بكر ؓ and said he feared the Qurʾān
would go with them. أبو بكر ؓ ordered زيد بن ثابت ؓ to gather it, and he gathered it from parchments, from
palm stalks, and from the breasts of men. Those leaves stayed with أبو بكر ؓ, then with عمر ؓ, and when he
died they passed to his daughter حفصة ؓ, a wife of the Prophet ﷺ. It was to her house that the caliph sent
for them. When the copying was finished he sent them back.

**The statement:**
> فَلَمَّا نَسَخُوا الصُّحُفَ رَدَّهَا عُثْمَانُ إِلَى حَفْصَةَ، وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى كُلِّ أُفُقٍ بِمُصْحَفٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1172
> *English:* "When they had copied the leaves, ʿUthmān returned them to Ḥafṣah, and sent a muṣḥaf to every horizon."

**عبرت:** He did not create the text; he was handed it by two caliphs before him and a widow of the
Prophet ﷺ, and he gave it back when he was done.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS19 · Four men, and one instruction
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** Four men were put to the work. One was زيد بن ثابت ؓ of the أنصار, the same man
أبو بكر ؓ had used. The other three were of قريش — سعيد بن العاص, عبد الله بن الزبير ؓ and
عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام. Our books do not agree about who did which part of the job, and that
disagreement is worth admitting rather than hiding. What all of them agree on, in the same words, is the
single instruction he gave for the cases where they could not agree.

**The statement:**
> وقال: إذا اختلفتم أنتم وزيد في عربية فاكتبوها بلسان قريش، فإن القرآن إنما نزل بلسانهم.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1299
> *English:* "And he said: if you and Zayd differ over a point of Arabic, write it in the tongue of Quraysh, for the Qurʾān came down only in their tongue."

**عبرت:** A rule that settles disputes before they happen is worth more than a ruling after each one.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS20 · Where the copies went
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Seven arrows out of المدينة — الشام، مصر، البصرة،
الكوفة، مكة، اليمن — and one staying.

**What happened:** When the copying was finished the copies were sent out. One of our three books lists the
destinations one by one, and it is the only one that does. A copy was written for the people of الشام and
another for the people of مصر. One was sent to البصرة and another to الكوفة. One went to مكة and one like
it to اليمن. And one was kept in المدينة. The other two books say only that one went to every army
district, or to every horizon, and give no number at all.

**The statement:**
> فكتبَ لأهل الشام مصحفاً، ولأهل مصر آخر، وبعث إلى البصرة مصحفاً وإلى الكوفة بآخر، وأرسل إلى مكة مصحفاً وإلى اليمن مثله، وأقر بالمدينة مصحفاً.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3530
> *English:* "He wrote for the people of Syria a muṣḥaf, and for the people of Egypt another; he sent to Basra a muṣḥaf and to Kufa another; he sent to Mecca a muṣḥaf and to Yemen the like of it; and he kept one at Medina."

**عبرت:** Seven copies, sent out from one town, are the reason there is one Qurʾān in the world and not
seven.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS21 · Not one of them was in his handwriting
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** There is a question every listener will have, and our book answers it in a single
sentence without being asked. These copies were called the Imāms. Were they written by عثمان ؓ? No — and
ابن کثیر is emphatic about it: not all of them are in his hand, indeed not one of them is; they are in the
hand of زيد بن ثابت ؓ. They are called the Uthmanic muṣḥafs the way a coin is called Heraclian: after the
reign in which it was struck, not after the hand that struck it.

**The statement:**
> وليست كلها بخطّ عثمان، بل ولا واحد منها، وإنما هي بخطّ زيد بن ثابت، وإنما يقال لها المصاحف العثمانية نسبةً إلى أمره وزمانه، وإمارته، كما يقال دينار هرقلي، أي ضُرب في زمانه ودولته.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3530
> *English:* "And they are not all in ʿUthmān's hand — no, not one of them — but rather in the hand of Zayd b. Thābit. They are called the ʿUthmānic muṣḥafs only by attribution to his command, his time and his rule, as one says a Heraclian dīnār, meaning it was struck in his time and his state."

**عبرت:** The name on a thing tells you who ordered it, not who made it, and the tradition took the trouble
to say so.

**Hands-up?** Hands up who thought the مصحف عثمانی was written by عثمان ؓ.

### UTM/E-MS22 · The burning, and the reason given for it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The seven destinations again.

**What happened:** The order that went out with the copies was not only to use them. It was to burn every
muṣḥaf that disagreed with the one sent. All three of our books record it, none of them softens it, and one
of them ends the sentence flatly: that was the time in which the muṣḥafs were burned with fire. The reason
given in our other book is one clause long: so that disagreement should not arise on account of them.

**The statement:**
> وأمرهم أن يحرقوا كل مصحف يخالف المصحف الذي أرسل إليهم به، فذلك زمان حرقت فيه المصاحف بالنار.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1299
> *English:* "And he ordered them to burn every muṣḥaf that differed from the muṣḥaf he had sent to them — and that was the time in which the muṣḥafs were burned with fire."

**عبرت:** The books do not hide the hardest part of the act, and neither should anyone telling it.

### UTM/E-MS23 · "Had he not done it, I would have done it"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The burning was the part of the whole business most open to attack, then and afterwards.
Two of our books preserve what علی ؓ said about it, and they preserve it in the same words. It is seven
words in Arabic. He said that if عثمان ؓ had not done it, he would have done it himself.

**The statement:**
> قال لي عليٌّ حين حرق عثمان المصاحف: لو لم يصنعْه هو لصنعته.

> *English:* "ʿAlī said to me when ʿUthmān burned the muṣḥafs: had he not done it, I would have done it."

**عبرت:** The clearest defence of the act came from the man least suspected of wanting to defend him.

### UTM/E-MS24 · "Beware of going to excess concerning عثمان ؓ"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The short saying is not the whole of what علی ؓ said. Our book carries the long form
through a second route, and in it he is addressing a crowd, not answering one man. He tells the people not
to go to excess about عثمان ؓ and repeat that he burned the muṣḥafs. He swears that he did not burn them
except before an assembly of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ. And then he says that if he himself had held the
office that man held, he would have done the like of what he did.

**The statement:**
> أيها الناس! إياكم والغُلُوَّ في عثمان تقولون حرّق المصاحف، والله ما حرّقها إلا عن ملأ من أصحاب محمد ﷺ، ولو وليت مثل ما ولي لفعلتُ (مثل) الذي فعل.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3531
> *English:* "O people, beware of going to excess concerning ʿUthmān, saying 'he burned the muṣḥafs'. By God, he did not burn them except before an assembly of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ; and had I held the office he held, I would have done the like of what he did."

**عبرت:** He did not answer the accusation by attacking the accusers; he answered it by saying what he
himself would have done in that seat.

### UTM/E-MS25 · The objection of ابن مسعود ؓ, and how it ended
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة and المدينة.

**What happened:** The one serious objection came from عبد الله بن مسعود ؓ, and our book states it without
flinching: his own copy was taken from him and burned; he spoke of his precedence in Islam over the man
who had written the new copies; and he told his companions to hold their copies back. Then عثمان ؓ wrote to
him, calling him not to his own authority but to what the Companions had agreed was in the common interest
— one word, and no disagreement. Our book says how it ended in six words.

**The statement:**
> فكتب إليه عثمان ﵁ يدعوه إلى اتباع الصحابة فيما أجمعوا عليه من المصلحة في ذلك، وجمع الكلمة، وعدم الاختلاف، فأناب وأجاب إلى المتابعة وترك المخالفة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3531
> *English:* "So ʿUthmān ؓ wrote to him calling him to follow the Companions in the benefit they had agreed upon in that, and the gathering of the word, and the absence of disagreement — and he turned back and answered to compliance and left off opposition."

**عبرت:** A disagreement between two great men ended because one of them wrote a letter and the other read
it honestly.

### UTM/E-MS26 · The copy arrives in الكوفة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

reached الكوفة, the Companions there were glad of it. But the men attached to عبد الله بن مسعود ؓ refused
it and found fault with the people who accepted it. And then ابن مسعود ؓ himself stood up among them — not
to lead them, but to stop them. He told them it was not all as they were saying, that they had been
outstripped and plainly outstripped, and that they should go gently, according to their own lameness.

### UTM/E-MS27 · The copy he read to pieces
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The man who sent seven copies out to the cities had one of his own. What he said about
it is short. He said that if hearts were pure they would never have their fill of the speech of their Lord,
and that he hated a day to pass over him in which he did not look into the muṣḥaf. And our book adds one
sentence of its own about what that daily habit did to the physical object over twelve years.

**The statement:**
> وإني لأكره أن يأتي عليّ يوم لا أنظر في المصحف. وما مات عثمان حتى خرق مصحفه من كثرة ما يديم النظر فيه.

### UTM/E-MS28 · The ring that fell into the well
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بئر أريس, two miles from المدينة.

**What happened:** The Prophet ﷺ had a silver signet made when he began writing to the kings, because they
would not accept an unsealed letter. It passed to أبو بكر ؓ, then to عمر ؓ, then to عثمان ؓ, who wore it
six years. In the sixth year it fell from his hand into a well outside المدينة. They searched, and they
spent a great deal of money on searching, and it was never found. He had another made to the same pattern
and the same inscription, and wore that until he died — and when he was killed that one disappeared too,
and nobody ever knew who took it.

**The statement:**
> فلم يدرك خبره بعد بذل مال جزيل، والاجتهاد في طلبه حتى الساعة، فاستخلف عثمان بعده خاتمًا من فضةٍ، ونقشَ عليه "محمدٌ رسولُ الله ﷺ"، فلما قُتل عثمان ذهب الخاتم فلم يُدْرَ (٦) من أخذه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3439
> *English:* "And no news of it was reached, after the giving of abundant money and striving in seeking it, down to this hour. So ʿUthmān put in its place a ring of silver and had inscribed upon it 'Muḥammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ'. And when ʿUthmān was killed the ring went, and it was not known who took it."

**عبرت:** The one physical thing that had passed unbroken from the Prophet ﷺ through three caliphs was lost
in an ordinary accident, and no amount of money brought it back.

**Hands-up?** Hands up if you have ever dropped something into water and not got it back. Now imagine what
it was.

### UTM/E-MS29 · Two books, two different wells
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** This is a card about how we know things rather than about what happened. Our two books
both record the lost ring, and they do not tell the same story. One says the well was two miles outside
المدينة and was among the wells with least water, and that nothing was ever found in it. The other says
they had just dug a well inside المدينة as drinking water for the Muslims, that he sat at the head of it
playing with the ring until it slipped, that they drained the water out of it and still could not reach it,
that he offered a great reward, and that he grieved bitterly. Neither account can be folded into the other,
and an honest telling names which book it is following.

**The statement:**
> فَقَعَدَ عَلَى رَأْسِ الْبِئْرِ فَجَعَلَ يَعْبَثُ بِالْخَاتَمِ فَسَقَطَ مِنْ يَدِهِ فِي الْبِئْرِ، فَطَلَبُوهُ فِيهَا وَنَزَحُوا مَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ فَلَمْ يَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1173
> *English:* "He sat at the head of the well and began toying with the ring, and it fell from his hand into the well. They sought it in it and drained out the water that was in it, and could not get at it."

**عبرت:** Two careful books can preserve one event in two shapes, and saying so is more truthful than
choosing quietly.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS30 · Asking the price of bread from the pulpit
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** موسى بن طلحة said he heard the Commander of the Faithful on the pulpit while the
muʾadhdhin was already calling the iqāmah — and what he was doing in those last seconds was asking the
congregation for news, and asking them what things were costing. The report comes through الإمام أحمد. It
is a small thing, and it tells you what the office thought it was for.

**The statement:**
> سمعت عثمان بن عفان وهو على المنبر والمؤذن يقيم الصلاة وهو يستخبر الناس يسألهم عن أخبارهم، وأسعارهم (٢).

> *English:* "I heard ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān while he was upon the pulpit and the muʾadhdhin was giving the iqāmah, and he was seeking news of the people, asking them about their tidings and their prices."

**عبرت:** A ruler who wants to know the price of things has to ask somebody, and the best place to ask is
where everyone is already standing.

### UTM/E-MS31 · Fifty dirhams and a garment, for a child one night old
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** A woman used to come in to the caliph, and one day he noticed she had not come. He was
told she had given birth in the night to a boy. He sent her fifty dirhams and a full-length garment, with a
message: this is your son's stipend and his clothing, and when a year has passed over him we shall raise it
to a hundred. The child is registered at birth, at a fixed rate, with a scheduled increase. That is not
charity. That is a state with a roll.

**The statement:**
> فأرسل إليّ بخمسين درهمًا وشُقَيْقَة سنبلانية (٥)، وقال: هذا عطاء ابنك وكسوته، فإذا مرت به سنة رفعناه إلى مئة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3526
> *English:* "He sent me fifty dirhams and a full-length shuqayqah, and said: this is your son's stipend and his clothing; and when a year has passed over him we shall raise it to a hundred."

**عبرت:** The difference between a gift and a right is that a right has a date on it.

**Hands-up?** no
