### UTM/E-MS32 · "The stipends flowing, the rations pouring"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الحسن البصري lived through those years, and he began his description by saying so — and
by acknowledging, in the same breath, that people held things against the man. Then he described the
ordinary days. Scarcely a day came without something good being divided among the people. They would be
called out in the morning for their stipends and take them in full; called out again for their rations and
take those in full; and called out again for clarified butter and honey. He ends with a list of five plain
facts about the state, which is as close as our books come to a description of daily life under a caliph.

**The statement:**
> الأعطيات جارية، والأرزاق دارَّةٌ، والعدو منفيٌّ (٨)، وذات البين حسن، والخيرُ كثيرٌ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3525
> *English:* "The stipends were flowing, the rations pouring, the enemy driven off, relations between people good, and the good abundant."

**عبرت:** The years people later called a disaster were, to the man who lived in them, the most comfortable
years anyone in المدينة had known.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS33 · The treasuries
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** around 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** فارس and خراسان shaded; wealth moving west.

**What happened:** When ابن عامر opened the wide lands in the east, the land-tax coming to المدينة became
enormous and money arrived from every direction. Our book says the caliph had to set up treasuries for it
and made the stipends flow. On the same page it gives one figure for the scale of what came out of the
Persian treasuries, in a unit of account called a بدرة — and it says that each بدرة held four thousand.

**The statement:**
> وقال أبو يوسف القاضي: أخرجوا من خزائن كسرى مائتي ألف بدرة في كل بدرة أربعة آلاف.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1321
> *English:* "Abū Yūsuf the qāḍī said: they brought out from the treasuries of Kisrā two hundred thousand badrahs, in each badrah four thousand."

**عبرت:** The problem the conquests set the state was not how to win, but what to do with what had been won.

### UTM/E-MS34 · A thousand dirhams a man for swimming a wadi
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** كرمان.

**What happened:** A governor in كرمان had four thousand men cut off from their road by a flooded wadi, and
was afraid of losing the moment. So he announced that any man who got across would have a thousand dirhams.
They put themselves into the water, and as each man came out the other side he was paid on the spot. The
bill came to four million dirhams. His own superior refused to allow it against the accounts, and the
matter went to المدينة. The caliph wrote back one line. Our book says that from that day the word for such
payments — جوائز — took its name from that crossing.

**The statement:**
> فكتب عثمان: أن احْسِبْها له، فإنه إنَّما أعانَ المسلمين في سبيل اللّه. فمن ذلك اليوم سُمِّيتِ الجوائزَ لإجازةِ الوادي
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3529
> *English:* "ʿUthmān wrote: reckon it to his account, for he only helped the Muslims in the way of God. And from that day the word jawāʾiz — bounties — was so called, from the crossing of the wadi."

**عبرت:** He backed a subordinate who had spent four million without asking, because the spending had done
what it was for.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS35 · Fifty thousand written off in the street
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

### UTM/E-MS36 · "Then choose between your land and your money"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He had bought a piece of land from a man, and the man did not come for his money. When
he met him he asked why. The man told him straight: you got the better of me, and I cannot meet anybody
without being blamed for the bargain. He asked whether that was really what was stopping him, and the man
said yes. So he offered him the choice — take back your land or take the money — and then quoted a ḥadīth
about the man who is easy in buying, in selling, and in debts both ways.

**The statement:**
> قال: فاختر بين أرضكَ ومالكَ، ثم قال: قال رسول اللّه ﷺ: "أدخل اللّه الجنةَ رجلًا كان سهلًا مشتريًا وبائعًا، وقاضيًا مقتضيًا".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3529
> *English:* "He said: then choose between your land and your money. Then he said: the Messenger of God ﷺ said, 'God admitted to Paradise a man who was easy when buying and selling, and when settling a debt and calling one in.'"

**عبرت:** A contract that leaves the other man ashamed to walk down the street has not really been
concluded.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS37 · Every governor at the season, every year
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrows converging on مكة from مصر، الشام،
الكوفة، البصرة، خراسان.

**What happened:** He made a rule and kept it. Every governor was required to attend the Ḥajj season, every
year. And he wrote to the subject populations of every province telling them the same thing: if any of you
has a grievance against any one of them, come to the season. He did not say send a petition. He said come,
and I will take your right for you out of your governor's hand — with the governor standing there and the
whole Muslim world watching.

**The statement:**
> ويكتب إلى الرعايا: منْ كانتْ له عند أحدٍ منهم مَظْلمةٌ فليوافِ إلى الموسم فإني آخذُ له حقَّه من عامله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3532
> *English:* "And he wrote to the subject peoples: whoever has a grievance against any one of them, let him come to the season, for I shall take his right for him from his governor."

**عبرت:** An annual day on which the governor must stand where anyone may accuse him is worth more than a
hundred instructions sent to him in private.

**Hands-up?** Hands up if your city has anything like that today.

### UTM/E-MS38 · What عمر ؓ forbade and عثمان ؓ allowed
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The senior Companions spreading out of
المدينة to the garrison cities.

**What happened:** عمر ؓ had kept the senior Companions in المدينة. He would not let them settle in the new
cities and, our book says, not even go out on campaign — and he said why: I fear that you will see the
world, and that the world's sons will see you. The next caliph lifted that restriction and gave many of
them leave to travel and live where they wished. Both men were doing what they thought right with the same
group of people. ابن کثیر, writing much later, reads a consequence into the change, and that reading is
his own and should be given as his.

**The statement:**
> وكان عمر يحجر عليهم في ذلك، حتى ولا في الغزو، ويقول: إني أخاف أن تروا الدنيا وأن يراكم (٤) أبناؤها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3532
> *English:* "ʿUmar used to restrain them in that, not even for a campaign, and would say: I fear that you should see the world, and that the world's sons should see you."

**عبرت:** A restriction and its removal were both acts of care, and only the years afterwards showed what
each one cost.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS39 · Selling a share in Iraq for land in the Ḥijāz
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** العراق on one side, الحجاز and اليمن on the other;
an exchange arrow between them.

**What happened:** Men of المدينة held shares in the conquered land of العراق, hundreds of miles from where
they lived. The caliph told them he would get what was theirs into their hands. They asked how a share of
land could possibly be moved to them. His answer opened something new: let whoever wishes sell his share
there against what he holds in the Ḥijāz or the Yemen or any other land. Our book says they were delighted,
that God had opened for them something they had not reckoned on, that men of every tribe bought, and that
the whole exchange went through by consent on both sides with the rights properly acknowledged.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: يَبِيعُهَا مَنْ شَاءَ بِمَا كَانَ لَهُ بِالْحِجَازِ وَالْيَمَنِ وَغَيْرِهِمَا مِنَ الْبِلَادِ. فَفَرِحُوا وَفَتَحَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ أَمْرًا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي حِسَابِهِمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1170
> *English:* "He said: let whoever wishes sell it against what he holds in the Ḥijāz and the Yemen and other lands. So they rejoiced, and God opened for them a matter that had not been in their reckoning."

**عبرت:** Empires are not held together by armies alone; someone has to work out how a man in المدينة owns
a field in العراق.

### UTM/E-MS40 · The grant that was taken back
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 27 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** إفريقية.

**What happened:** After إفريقية was taken, the commander had been awarded the fifth of the fifth of the
spoil by the caliph's own grant. A delegation came from the army to complain about it. He did not defend
the grant and he did not stand on his authority. He said he had awarded it, that the matter was now in
their hands, that if they were content it stood, and if they were displeased it was returned. They said
they were displeased. He said then it is returned, and wrote to the commander to give it back and to
conciliate the men.

**The statement:**
> فقال: أنا نفلته، وذلك إليكم الآن، فإن رضيتم فقد جاز، وإن سخطتم فهو رد، قالوا: إنا نسخطه قال: فهو رد
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1314
> *English:* "He said: I awarded it to him, and that is now up to you — if you are content, it has passed; and if you are displeased, it is returned. They said: we are displeased. He said: then it is returned."

**عبرت:** A decision that can be reversed when the people it touches object is a different kind of decision
from one that cannot.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-MS41 · How Syria came into one hand
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** two years into the caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الأردن، دمشق، حمص، قنسرين،
فلسطين merging into one command.

**What happened:** Later it would be said that Syria was handed to one man as a favour. Our book sets out
how the command actually assembled, and most of the steps were عمر ؓ's. أبو عبيدة ؓ left عياض بن غنم over
his district; عياض died and عمر ؓ appointed another, and when he died عمر ؓ appointed another again;
يزيد بن أبي سفيان ؓ died and عمر ؓ put his brother معاوية ؓ in his place, so that الأردن and دمشق were
already together in عمر ؓ's lifetime. Then a governor fell ill and asked to be excused, and another died,
and their districts were joined to the same command. That is how it came to be one province, two years into
the new reign.

**The statement:**
> فَاجْتَمَعَ الشَّامُ لِمُعَاوِيَةَ لِسَنَتَيْنِ مِنْ إِمَارَةِ عُثْمَانَ، فَهَذَا كَانَ سَبَبُ اجْتِمَاعِ الشَّامِ لَهُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1178
> *English:* "So Syria came together for Muʿāwiya two years into ʿUthmān's amirate. That was the cause of Syria's coming together for him."

**عبرت:** The thing that later looked like a plan was, on the page, a series of illnesses and funerals.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### UTM/E-MS42 · "Say nothing of عثمان ؓ but good"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الربذة.

**What happened:** أبو ذر الغفاري ؓ had been required to live at الربذة outside المدينة, and everyone knew
it. A man sat in a gathering with him, assuming he must be nursing a grievance about it, and someone in the
company hinted at it to draw him out. What أبو ذر ؓ said in reply shut the subject down, and then he went on
to describe something he had seen with the Prophet ﷺ that he said he would never forget.

**The statement:**
> فقال أبو ذر: لا تقل في عثمان إلا خيرا
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۵۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1296
> *English:* "Abū Dharr said: say nothing of ʿUthmān but good."

**عبرت:** The man with the best excuse to complain refused to let anybody complain on his behalf.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS43 · The heavy bag at الربذة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الربذة, east of المدينة.

**What happened:** When his family came out to join him at الربذة, they came with a leather bag heavy
enough to weigh a man's arm down. Somebody said what everybody was thinking: look at this man who renounces
the world — see what he has got. His wife answered. It was not gold and it was not silver. It was small
copper coins, bought out of his stipend, for the household's daily needs.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ: وَاللَّهِ مَا هُوَ دِينَارٌ وَلَا دِرْهَمٌ، وَلَكِنَّهَا فَلُوسٌ، كَانَ إِذَا خَرَجَ عَطَاؤُهُ ابْتَاعَ مِنْهُ فُلُوسًا لِحَوَائِجِنَا.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1175
> *English:* "His wife said: by God, it is neither dīnār nor dirham, but coppers. When his stipend came out he used to buy coppers with it for our needs."

**عبرت:** A man can be suspected of hypocrisy over the weight of a bag of small change.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS44 · The Companion who would not step forward
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الربذة.

**What happened:** The prayer was called at الربذة, and the man in charge of the ṣadaqah there — a slave,
whose name our book gives — told أبو ذر ؓ to go forward and lead. He refused, and told the man to go forward
himself. Then he gave his reason: the Messenger of God ﷺ had told him to hear and obey even if a mutilated
slave were set over him — and, he said, you are a slave and you are not mutilated.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: لَا، تَقَدَّمْ أَنْتَ، فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - قَالَ لِي: اسْمَعْ وَأَطِعْ وَإِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْكَ عَبْدٌ مُجَدَّعٌ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1175
> *English:* "He said: no — you go forward; for the Messenger of God ﷺ said to me: hear and obey, though a mutilated slave be set over you."

**عبرت:** The man who would not be silenced about wealth was the same man who would not take precedence
over a slave.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS45 · A historian refuses to repeat a story
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the seventh century of the Hijrah, looking back at 30 AH `[SOURCED]` ·
**Map:** No map.

**What happened:** There were ugly versions of how أبو ذر ؓ came to leave الشام, and they were in
circulation long before ابن الأثیر wrote. He lists them: that معاوية ؓ reviled him, that he threatened him
with death, that he was carried from الشام to المدينة on a bare mount without a saddle-pad, that he was
banished from المدينة in a disgraceful manner. Then, having listed them, he writes six words that a
speaker can stand on. And he adds a second thought: that even if it had been sound, it would have needed
to be excused, because disciplining subjects belongs to the office.

**The statement:**
> وَنَفْيِهِ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ عَلَى الْوَجْهِ الشَّنِيعِ، لَا يَصِحُّ النَّقْلُ بِهِ، وَلَوْ صَحَّ لَكَانَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُعْتَذَرَ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ، فَإِنَّ لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُؤَدِّبَ رَعِيَّتَهُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1173
> *English:* "…and his banishment from Medina in the disgraceful manner — the transmission of it is not sound; and had it been sound, it would still have been fitting to excuse ʿUthmān, for it belongs to the imām to discipline his subjects."

**عبرت:** A historian who tells you which reports he will not carry has told you something about all the
ones he does.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS46 · "And each is sunnah"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** around 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** A punishment had to be carried out in المدينة, and there was a question about the number
of lashes, because two caliphs had used two different numbers. علی ؓ settled it on the spot, in one breath.
He said the Messenger of God ﷺ and أبو بكر ؓ gave forty, and that عثمان ؓ gave eighty. And then he said the
thing that makes this card worth the evening: each of them is sunnah — and this one is dearer to me. He did
not say the other was wrong. He said it was sunnah, and that he preferred the other.

**The statement:**
> جَلَدَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ -، وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ أَرْبَعِينَ وَجَلَدَ عُثْمَانُ ثَمَانِينَ وَكُلٌّ سُنَّةٌ وَهَذَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1168
> *English:* "The Messenger of God ﷺ flogged, and Abū Bakr, forty; and ʿUthmān flogged eighty; and each is sunnah, and this is the dearer to me."

**عبرت:** He had the words for a difference between two great men that did not require either of them to
be in the wrong, and those words are still available.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS47 · Changing a rule of evidence to stop the killing
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** around 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** A gang of young men in الكوفة broke into a house at night, and when the householder came
out at them with a sword and shouted, they killed him. A Companion and his son had seen it and testified.
The governor wrote to المدينة; the caliph wrote back ordering the killers put to death, and they were
executed at the palace gate. And out of that case a rule was adjusted: in the procedure of قسامة he took
the word of the slain man's next of kin, before an assembly of the people — and our book states the purpose
of the change in five words.

**The statement:**
> وَلِهَذَا السَّبَبِ أَخَذَ فِي الْقَسَامَةِ بِقَوْلِ وَلِيِّ الْمَقْتُولِ عَنْ مَلَإٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ لِيَفْطِمَ النَّاسَ عَنِ الْقَتْلِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1167
> *English:* "And for this reason he took, in the qasāmah, the word of the slain man's next of kin before an assembly of the people — in order to wean the people away from killing."

**عبرت:** Law is not only what is right in the case in front of you; it is also what the next man will
believe he can get away with.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS48 · A governor whose house had no door
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** the first five years of the caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** The governorships of that reign are usually spoken of only as a list of complaints. Our
book, before it comes to any of that, records what the same governor's first five years in الكوفة were
like. He was beloved to the people, it says, and it gives one detail as the proof: for five years his house
had no door on it. The card is recorded so the fact is not lost; the rest of that governorship is not
material for the hall.

**The statement:**
> وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ مَحْبُوبًا إِلَى النَّاسِ، فَبَقِيَ كَذَلِكَ خَمْسَ سِنِينَ وَلَيْسَ لِدَارِهِ بَابٌ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1167
> *English:* "…and that he was beloved to the people, and remained so for five years, and his house had no door."

**عبرت:** A ruler's house without a door says more about the state of a city than any report sent from it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS49 · Five things laid before him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الجحفة, on the road from مصر to المدينة.

**What happened:** A party from مصر camped at الجحفة with complaints. The caliph went up the pulpit and
asked, three times, which of them would go out to those people and ask what they objected to and what they
wanted. Nobody answered him. Then علی ؓ stood up and said he would go, and the caliph said: you are the
nearest of them to them in kinship. He went, they welcomed him, and he asked. They gave him five things,
and three of them were matters of administration.

**The statement:**
> قالوا: نقمنا أنه محا كتاب الله -يعني كونه جمع الأمة على مصحف- وحمى الحمى، واستعمل أقرباءه، وأعطى مروان مائة الفن وتناول أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1326
> *English:* "They said: we hold against him that he erased the Book of God — meaning his gathering the umma upon one muṣḥaf — and protected the pasture, and employed his relatives, and gave Marwān a hundred thousand, and spoke sharply against the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ."

**عبرت:** The greatest service of that reign appears at the head of the list of charges against it, and the
book itself has to stop and explain what the charge even means.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS50 · "Recite upon whichever ḥarf you wish"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الجحفة.

**What happened:** علی ؓ carried the five complaints back, and the answers came back through him. On the
first of them — the charge that he had erased the Book of God — the answer was three clauses long. The
Qurʾān is from God. I only forbade you to differ. Recite on whichever ḥarf you wish. Our book says that at
the end of that exchange the people were satisfied, made peace, and came into المدينة.

**The statement:**
> أما القرآن فمن عند الله، إنما نهيتكم عن الاختلاف فاقرؤوا على أي حرف شئتم
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1326
> *English:* "As for the Qurʾān — it is from God. I only forbade you to differ; so recite upon whichever ḥarf you wish."

**عبرت:** He answered the charge that he had narrowed the Book by telling them, in the same sentence, that
it had not been narrowed.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS51 · "Is it not so?" — and the crowd said yes
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, the mosque.

**What happened:** There was a second and fuller hearing, this time in المدينة, with the Companions present
and the call given for the congregation to assemble. He went through the objections one at a time and gave
his answer to each — the prayer in travel, the protected pasture, the recall of a man the Prophet ﷺ had
exiled, the appointment of young men, the award to a commander. And after each answer he turned to the
people standing in front of him and asked two words: is it not so? And each time, our book says, they said
yes.

**The statement:**
> وإني قد وليت وإني لأكثر العرب بعيرا وشاء، فمالي اليوم غير بعيرين لحجتي، أكذاك؟ قالوا: نعم.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1332
> *English:* "And I took office being the greatest of the Arabs in camels and sheep, and today I have nothing but two camels, for my Ḥajj. Is it not so? They said: yes."

**عبرت:** He answered in front of the only people who could contradict him, and asked them to do it.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS52 · The pasture, and who it was for
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** One of the five charges was the حِمى — the pasture closed off from general grazing.
Closing pasture was an old practice and there was nothing new in the fact of it; the charge was that he had
closed it for himself. His answer to that, in the exchange carried through علی ؓ, is one sentence with an
oath in the middle of it, and it is about purpose: not for my camels, not for my sheep, but for the camels
of the ṣadaqah — the animals held by the state on behalf of the poor.

**The statement:**
> وأما الحمى فوالله ما حميته لإبلي ولا لغنمي، وإنما حميته لإبل الصدقة.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1326
> *English:* "As for the protected pasture — by God, I did not protect it for my camels nor for my sheep; I protected it only for the camels of the ṣadaqah."

**عبرت:** The same act done for oneself and done for the treasury looks identical from the road, and that is
why it was believed.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS53 · Two camels for the Ḥajj
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** At the assembly in المدينة he answered the same charge about the pasture a second time,
and differently. He said he had closed nothing that had not been closed before him. And then he added
something that could be checked by everyone listening: when he took office he was the greatest of the Arabs
in camels and sheep, and today he owned two camels, for his Ḥajj. Then he asked the crowd whether that was
so, and they said it was.

**The statement:**
> وإني والله ما حميت إلا ما حمي قبلي
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1332
> *English:* "And by God, I have protected nothing except what was protected before me."

**عبرت:** Twelve years in the highest office in the world had left him with fewer animals than he walked in
with.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS54 · The first tent at مِنى
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 29 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مِنى.

**What happened:** It is a small notice and our book puts it in one clause, but it is the kind of detail
that fixes a scene. When he led the Ḥajj that year a tent was pitched for him at مِنى — and our book says it
was the first tent he pitched there. Before that the Commander of the Faithful had stood at مِنى with
everyone else and no canvas over him.

**The statement:**
> وضرب له بمنى فسطاطًا، فكان أول فسطاط ضربه عثمان بمنى
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3438
> *English:* "And a tent was pitched for him at Minā — and it was the first tent ʿUthmān pitched at Minā."

**عبرت:** The distance between a ruler and the crowd is measured in very small increments, and the first one
is always noticed.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS55 · The first quarrel between الكوفة and الشام
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الباب, on the Caucasus frontier.

**What happened:** On the northern frontier a Muslim commander was killed and the army broke. Reinforcements
were ordered from الشام to support the Kufan force. When they arrived, the two commanders could not agree
which of them was in charge. It came to the point where the Syrians spoke of striking the Kufan commander
and the Kufans answered that they would strike his. Both of our books call it by the same name: the first
disagreement that fell between the people of الكوفة and the people of الشام. A Kufan poet wrote four lines
about it that both books preserve.

**The statement:**
> فتنازع حبيب وسلمان في الإمرة حتى اختلفا، فكان أولَ اختلافٍ وقعَ بين أهل الكوفة وأهل الشام
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3446
> *English:* "Ḥabīb and Salmān disputed over the command until they fell out; and it was the first disagreement that occurred between the people of Kufa and the people of Syria."

**عبرت:** The line that would one day divide the umma was first drawn over which of two men should command a
frontier post.

**Hands-up?** no

### UTM/E-MS56 · "Hold fast together; do not become parties"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** late in the caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, the mosque — and the
closing map of the session.

**What happened:** Our book records what it calls the last address he delivered to an assembly. He told them
that God gave them this world to seek the next with, not to lean upon; that this one passes and that one
remains; that they should prefer what stays to what goes. Then he told them to fear God, because fear of Him
is a shield. And he ended with an instruction and a verse, and the instruction is the one that the years
after him make hard to hear.

**The statement:**
> واحذروا من اللّه الغِيَرَ، والزموا جماعتكم لا تصيروا أحزابًا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3528
> *English:* "Beware of God's reversals, and hold fast to your community together; do not become parties."

**عبرت:** The last thing he asked of them in public was the one thing they did not give him.

**Hands-up?** no

## The اصول: how a fitna is narrated from the platform

*Source note: [`the-mashajarat-and-how-to-narrate-it.md`](../docs/research/the-mashajarat-and-how-to-narrate-it.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TMA/E-MG1 · History is a branch of the science of hadith
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** No date — a rule, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** السخاوي رحمہ اللہ wrote a whole book defending history against men who despised it, and in it he quotes his own teacher البدر العيني رحمہ اللہ on what the subject actually is. History, العيني says, is one of the branches of the science of Prophetic hadith. That is not a compliment. It means history is done with the same tools — you ask who said this, and from whom, and whether the man is trusted. And العيني attaches a condition in the middle of the sentence: it is a branch of that science where the straight and level method has been kept to in it. Not otherwise.

**The statement:**
> عِلْمُ التَّارِيخُ فَنٌّ مِنْ فُنُونِ الْحَدِيثِ النَّبَوِيِّ، وَزَيْنٌ تَقَرُّ بِهِ الْعُيُونُ، حَيْثُ سُلِكَ فِيهِ المَنْهَجُ الْقَوِيمُ الْمُسْتَوِي، بَلْ وَقْعُهُ مِنَ الدِّينِ عَظِيمٌ، وَنَفْعُهُ يَتَعَيَّنُ (٤) فِي الشَّرْعِ لِشُهْرَتِهِ، غَنَيٌّ عَنْ مَزِيدِ البَيَانِ وَالتَّفْهِيمِ.
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٧٢ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/171
> *English:* "The science of history is one of the branches of the science of Prophetic ḥadīth, and an ornament at which eyes are gladdened — where the straight and level method has been kept to in it. Indeed its bearing on the religion is great, and its usefulness in the Sharīʿa is settled by its very fame, needing no further explaining."

**عبرت:** A subject is only as honest as the method kept inside it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TMA/E-MG2 · The rule of selection stated in the same passage
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a rule, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** One page further on, السخاوي states what follows from calling history a branch of hadith. Reading a history is not swallowing everything a history contains. The good matters among the forbears' traces are followed; and among their reports, what sound minds recoil from is not listened to. He states this about the reports of caliphs and kings and commanders — which is to say, about exactly the material this evening is made of.

**The statement:**
> حَيْثُ تُتَبَّعُ الأُمُورُ الْحَسَنَةُ مِنْ آثَارِهِمْ، وَلَا يَسْمَعُ مِنْهُمْ فِيمَا تَنْفِرُ عَنْهُ الْعُقُوُل المُسْتَحْسِنَةُ مِنْ أَخْبَارِهِمْ.
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٧٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/172
> *English:* "…in that the good matters among their traces are followed, and there is not listened to, of their reports, that from which sound minds recoil."

**عبرت:** To read a history well is to know what in it may be passed over in silence.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG3 · Histories carry men's merits and their faults alike
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a rule, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The clause immediately before the rule of selection names what السخاوي is describing. History gives access to the reports of scholars and ascetics and the excellent — and of caliphs and kings and commanders and nobles, their lives and their deeds in war and in peace, and whatever time has left standing of their merits, or of their faults. He concedes the second word in the same breath as the first. The books were not written to flatter, and the man defending the discipline says so while defending it.

**The statement:**
> وَمَا أَبْقَى الدَّهْرِ مِنْ فَضَائِلِهِمْ أَوْ رَذَائِلِهِمْ، بَعْدَ أَنْ أَبَادَهُمُ الْحَدَثَانِ (٣) وَأَبْلَى جَدِيدَهُمُ الْمَلْوَان (٤).
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٧٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/172
> *English:* "…and whatever time has left of their merits, or of their faults — after events had destroyed them, and after night and day had worn out what was new in them."

**عبرت:** A record that only praises is not a record.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG4 · Write history, but keep the brake on
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** No date — a rule, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** السخاوي spends a whole page arguing that rulers and viziers and commanders cannot do without history. Then, at the very end of that argument, he prices the licence. History must be attended to, written and transmitted — while guarding against المجازفة, reckless over-claiming, and against الرجم بالغيب, firing blindly at what one cannot see. Those two words name precisely the failure that turns the narrative of a fitna into a partisan one: filling the gap between two reports with a motive that neither report gives you.

**The statement:**
> فَإِذًا لَا غَنَاءَ عَنِ التَّارِيخِ، فَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُعْتَنَى بِشَأْنِهِ، وَيُكْتَبَ وَيُنْقَلَ مَعَ الِاحْتِرَازِ عَنِ الْمُجَازَفَةِ وَالرَّجْمِ بِالْغَيْبِ، بَلْ عَلَى حَسَبِ مَا تَقَدَّمَ.
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٥٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/158
> *English:* "So then, there is no dispensing with history. It ought to be attended to, and written, and transmitted — with a guarding against reckless assertion and against stoning at the unseen — rather, according to what has gone before."

**عبرت:** The gap between two reports is to be left open, not filled with a guess.

**Hands-up?** Before I tell you what happened in this year — what is the honest thing to do when two books tell you two different things?

### TMA/E-MG5 · The man who transmitted the story doubted it himself
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date fixed on the page · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A story circulated that المأمون tested الشافعي رحمہ اللہ by making him drink نبيذ. It was transmitted by المعافى بن زكريا النهرواني, through معمر بن شبيب بن شيبة. السخاوي reproduces the story — and he reproduces with it the remark المعافى himself set down the moment he had finished telling it. Allah knows best whether it is sound. The transmitter of the story is the first man on the page to doubt it.

**The statement:**
> وَقَالَ المُعَافَى عَقِبهَا: اللهُ أَعْلَمُ بِصِحَّتِهَا!
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٠٢ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/101
> *English:* "And المعافى said immediately after it: Allah knows best whether it is sound!"

**عبرت:** A man may pass a story on and still refuse to stand behind it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG6 · A calendar destroys the story about الشافعي رحمہ اللہ
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 200 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Egypt and خراسان light — two ends of the empire at once.

**What happened:** السخاوي then quotes his own teacher, الحافظ ابن حجر رحمہ اللہ, who settles the story without any appeal to the man's known conduct at all. He settles it with dates. Anyone with the least acquaintance with chronology, he writes, knows the thing is a lie — because الشافعي entered Egypt at the head of the year 200, and at that time المأمون was in خراسان. Two men cannot be put in one room across two thousand miles.

**The statement:**
> "لَا يَخْفَى عَلَى مَنْ لَهُ أَدْنَى مَعْرِفَةٍ بِالتَّارِيخِ أَنَّهَا كَذِبٌ؛ وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الشَّافِعِيَّ دَخَلَ مِصْرَ عَلَى رَأْسِ الْمِائَتَيْنِ، وَالْمَأْمُونُ إِذْ ذَاكَ بِخُرَاسَانَ، ثُمَّ
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٠٢ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/101
> *English:* "It is not hidden from anyone who has the least acquaintance with chronology that it is a lie — and that is because الشافعي entered Egypt at the head of the year 200, while المأمون at that time was in خراسان, then…"

**عبرت:** The cheapest test of a story is where its people were standing that year.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG7 · The two of them never met while المأمون was caliph
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 204 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** خراسان → العراق, one arrow; Egypt stays where it is.

**What happened:** The sentence finishes on the facing page, and it finishes the story with it. الشافعي رحمہ اللہ died in Egypt in the very year that المأمون came from خراسان down to العراق — the year 204. So the two of them never met at all while المأمون was caliph. The meeting in the story is not doubtful. It is impossible. And nobody had to weigh anyone's good name to know it.

**The statement:**
> مَاتَ الشَّافِعِيُّ بِمِصْرَ سَنَةَ دَخَلَ الْمَأْمُونُ مِنْ خُرَاسَانَ إِلَى الْعِرَاقِ، وَهِيَ سَنَةُ أَرْبَعٍ وَمِائَتَيْنِ، فَمَا الْتَقَيَا قَطُّ وَالْمَأْمُونُ خَلِيفَةٌ!
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٠٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/102
> *English:* "الشافعي died in Egypt in the very year that المأمون came from خراسان to العراق — and that is the year 204. So the two of them never met at all while المأمون was caliph!"

**عبرت:** Dates defend a reputation better than praise does.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG8 · The appeal to his known conduct comes last, and only as an ornament
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a remark, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Only after the dates have already finished the matter does ابن حجر رحمہ اللہ add the argument from the man's known conduct — the one most people would have reached for first. How is it to be believed that الشافعي رحمہ اللہ would do such a thing, when he is the man who said that if cold water would spoil his مروءة, he would drink water only hot? The order on the page is the teaching point. The almanac settles it; the remark about the man himself is placed afterwards, on a matter already closed.

**The statement:**
> وَكَيْفَ يُعْتَقَدُ أَنَّ الشَّافِعِيَّ يَفْعَلُ هَذَا، وَهُوَ الْقَائِلُ: لَوْ أَنَّ الْمَاءَ الْبَارِدَ يُفْسِدُ مُرُوءَتِي مَا شَرِبْتُ المَاءَ إِلَّا حَارًّا!
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٠٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/102
> *English:* "And how is it to be believed that الشافعي would do this, when he is the one who said: 'If cold water would spoil my مروءة, I would drink water only hot'?"

**عبرت:** Put the evidence first and the good opinion second, or you have only an opinion.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG9 · The best of people is my generation
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a hadith quoted for the rule it gives · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** السخاوي lists what dating events by their years is actually for, and the first item on his list is a hadith. The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them. His point is a practical one. The saying is useless unless you can tell which generation a man belonged to, and that is a question only a calendar answers — so that the one to be followed may be distinguished from another.

**The statement:**
> وَكَذَا مَعْرِفَةُ الْقُرُونِ الْفَاضِلَةِ الْمُشَارِ إِلَيْهَا بِقَوْلِهِ -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "خَيْرُ النَّاسِ قَرْنِي، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ، ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ" (٣) لِيَتَمَيَّزَ الْمُقْتَدَى بِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٦٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/167
> *English:* "And likewise, knowing the excellent generations, indicated by his saying ﷺ: 'The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them' — so that the one to be followed is distinguished from another."

**عبرت:** A command to follow a generation is worth nothing until you can say which generation a man stood in.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG10 · Why the ummah has to know when a period ended
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** The period in question closes at 40 AH `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map — the Line instead.

**What happened:** The next two items on السخاوي's list are the reason this evening exists at all. Chronology is for knowing the expiry of the period fixed for the خلفاء راشدون, whose سنت we were commanded to follow. And it is for making plain the time at which the innovations and the novelties first appeared. The room's instinct is that dates are bookkeeping. His answer is that a command to follow a سنت is useless without knowing whose, and until when. Tonight is the session in which that period closes.

**The statement:**
> وَمَعْرِفَةُ انْقِضَاءِ الزَّمَنِ الْمُحَدَّدِ لِلْخُلَفَاءِ الرَّاشِدِينَ الَّذِينَ أُمِرْنَا بِاقْتِفَاءِ سُنَّتِهِمْ.
> وَبَيَانُ الْوَقْتِ الَّذِي ظَهَرَتْ فِيهِ الْبِدَعُ وَالْحَوَادِثُ.
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٦٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/167
> *English:* "And knowing the expiry of the period fixed for the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, whose سنت we were commanded to follow. And making plain the time at which the innovations and the novelties appeared."

**عبرت:** The date on which a thing ended is a matter of knowledge, not of taste.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG11 · Put me in your history even among the liars
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date fixed on the page · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** السخاوي records something a scholar of Baghdad once said about الخطيب البغدادي رحمہ اللہ and his great history of that city. He wished الخطيب had mentioned him in it — and then added: even among the liars. The remark is light, and it is exactly true, and it explains a good deal about the period the evening is about to enter. The historian's book was the only door to being remembered at all. That is precisely why men pushed lies in through it.

**The statement:**
> "لَيْتَ الْخَطِيبَ البَغْدَادِيَّ ذَكَرَنِي فِي "تَارِيخِهِ" وَلَو فِي الْكَذَّابِينَ" (٣).
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١١٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/112
> *English:* "Would that الخطيب البغدادي had mentioned me in his History — even among the liars."

**عبرت:** Men want to be in the record badly enough to get into it dishonestly.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG12 · And a man who wished to die in السخاوي's lifetime
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** No date fixed on the page · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** On the same page السخاوي sets a remark made about himself beside the first one. Someone supposed that السخاوي wrote entries only for men already dead, and said he wished he might die while السخاوي was still alive, so as to get one. Recorded here so that nobody researches it twice. It is an ornament and the evening does not need it.

**The statement:**
> لَيْتَنِي أَمُوتُ فِي حَيَاةِ السَّخَاوِيِّ حَتَّى يُتَرْجِمَنِي" (٥)
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١١٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/112
> *English:* "Would that I might die in السخاوي's lifetime, so that he would write my entry."

**عبرت:** The wish to be recorded is old, ordinary and very strong.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG13 · A man who wrote a history says histories mix the lean with the fat
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** No date — a compiler's own preface · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** سبط ابن الجوزي رحمہ اللہ explains why he set out to write مرآة الزمان, and his reason is a complaint about the histories already in existence. What predominates in them, he says, is the gathering of the lean with the fat, and the flimsy with the firm, and repetition empty of any benefit. This is not an outsider attacking the discipline. It is a man who wrote a history, giving that as his reason for writing another one. It is the sentence to say aloud before narrating anything contested.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: "وَلَمَّا كَانَ الغَالِبُ عَلَى التَّوَارِيخِ جَمْعَ الْغَثِّ وَالسَّمِينِ، وَالْوَاهِي
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٣٤ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/133
> وَالْمَتِينِ، وَالتِّكرَارَ الْخَالِيَ عَنِ الفَوَائِدِ وَالْفَرَائِدِ الَّتِي يَعْجِزُ عَن جَمْعِهَا أَلْفُ رَائِدٍ، اسْتَخَرْتُ اللهَ ...
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٣٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/134
> *English:* "And since what predominates in the histories is the gathering of the lean with the fat, and the flimsy with the firm, and repetition empty of benefits and of those rarities which a thousand searchers are unable to collect — I sought God's guidance…"

**عبرت:** It is the people inside a discipline who state its weaknesses most plainly.

**Hands-up?** Who here has read something about this period and come away certain of exactly who was right?

### TMA/E-MG14 · The two things a life is read for
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a compiler's own preface · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** السخاوي quotes ابن الجوزي رحمہ اللہ from the opening of المنتظم on what histories are good for. They have many benefits, he says, and the two most important are these. If the life of a resolute man is related and the end of his affair described, it yields good management and the exercise of resolve. And if the life of a negligent man is related and his end described, it yields the fear of negligence. Two ways of reading, and both of them are reading for use.

**The statement:**
> "وَللسِّيَرِ وَالتَّوَارِيخِ فَوَائِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ، أَهَمُّهَا فَائِدَتَانِ:
> إِحْدَاهُمَا: أَنَّهُ إِنْ ذُكِرَتْ سِيرَةُ حَازِمٍ، وَوُصِفَتْ عَاقِبَةُ حَالِهِ، أَفَادَتْ حُسْنَ التَّدْبِيرِ، وَاسْتِعْمَالَ الْحَزْمِ، أَوْ [إِنْ ذُكِرَتْ] (٦) سِيرَةُ مُفَرِّطٍ، وَوُصِفَتْ عَاقِبَتُهُ، أَفَادَتْ الْخَوْفَ مِنَ التَّفْرِيطِ
> — الإعلان بالتوبيخ ص١٢٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/34/124
> *English:* "Biographies and histories have many benefits, the most important of them two. The first: that if the life of a resolute man is related and the outcome of his case described, it yields good management and the exercise of resolve; or if the life of a negligent man is related and his outcome described, it yields the fear of negligence."

**عبرت:** A life is read either for what to do or for what to fear, and rarely for anything else.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG15 · ابن كثير رحمہ اللہ says the report appears to be fabricated
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** The report is set after صفين, 37 AH `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map — this card is about a chain, not a place.

**What happened:** البدایہ carries a much-repeated report in which أبو أيوب الأنصاري ؓ, returning from صفين, is asked how he could draw his sword on people who say لا إله إلا الله, and answers that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded them to fight three named parties alongside علي ؓ. That report is the frame in which this whole period is usually handed to a reader, because it settles in advance who was right at الجمل and who was right at صفين. ابن كثير رحمہ اللہ prints it in full, with its chain — and then, in one line at the foot of the page, throws it out. It appears to be fabricated, he says, and he names the man in the chain who is the cause of it.

**The statement:**
> هذا السياق الظاهر أنه موضوع وآفته من جهة المعلى بن عبد الرحمن فإنه متروك الحديث، والله أعلم (٧).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3662
> *English:* "This wording — it is apparent that it is fabricated, and its defect comes from the direction of المعلى بن عبد الرحمن, for he is abandoned in ḥadīth. And Allah knows best."

**عبرت:** When our own historian refuses a report, we have no business repairing it for him.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG16 · A rival account is refused, and the refusal names whose account it is
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** After النهروان, 38 AH `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** الكوفة and the lower Euphrates.

**What happened:** After النهروان, البدایہ reports that a man named الخريت بن راشد الناجي broke away with a body of بنو ناجية, that علي ؓ sent معقل بن قيس الرماحي against them, and that five hundred households were taken. Then the book gives a rival version of the same affair — that the tribe had apostatised, which would make the captives lawfully taken — and refuses it on the spot. The refusal is الهيثم بن عدي's, quoted by ابن كثير: that this is the Shīʿa's own statement, and that no Arab tribe has ever been heard of as apostatising after the ردة in the days of الصديق ؓ.

**The statement:**
> قال الهيثم: وهذا قول الشيعة ولم يسمع بحيٍّ من العرب ارتدوا [عن الإسلام] بعد الردة التى كانت في أيام الصديق.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3666
> *English:* "الهيثم said: and this is the Shīʿa's own statement — and no Arab tribe has ever been heard of as having apostatised [from Islam] after the ردة that was in the days of الصدیق ؓ."

**عبرت:** A book that prints the version it rejects, and says whose version it is, has told you more than one that prints only what it likes.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG17 · ابن كثير praises a source and his editor writes against him in the footnote
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a judgement about a book · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** On the page where he begins drawing on الهيثم بن عدي, ابن كثير رحمہ اللہ praises the man's book on the خوارج — among the best that has been written on it, he says. At that exact spot the editor of the printed edition sets his own note against him: but he is a liar, abandoned. The two verdicts sit on one page, an author's above and his editor's beneath, and the reader is left holding both. Nothing in that stretch of البدایہ can therefore be used as a settled fact. What can be used is the shape of the page itself.

**The statement:**
> وهو من أحسن ما صنف في ذلك
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3662
> *English:* "And it is among the best that has been written on that."

**عبرت:** Two trained men may read the same transmitter in opposite ways, and the page prints both.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG18 · There is a great deal of confusion in this speech
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** No date — a later conversation among the traditionists · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Under a heading he calls a strange thing among strange things, ابن كثير رحمہ اللہ prints a whole exchange he found in ابن أبي خيثمة through عبد الرزاق. معمر claims that even the moderates of الكوفة put علي ؓ ahead of أبو بكر ؓ and عمر ؓ, and names سفيان الثوري among them. عبد الرزاق takes the claim to وكيع بن الجراح, who is astonished at it and laughs it off. ابن كثير prints every line of it, and then writes his own verdict underneath: there is a great deal of confusion in this speech, and perhaps the matter had become unclear to معمر.

**The statement:**
> وهذا الكلام فيه تخبيط كثير ولعله اشتبه على معمر فإن المشهور عن بعض الكوفيين تقديم عليّ على عثمان، فأمّا على الشيخين فلا، ولا يخفى فضل الشيخين على سائر الصحابة إلَّا على غبيّ، فكيف يخفى على هؤلاء الأئمة؟
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۰۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3755
> *English:* "And in this speech there is a great deal of confusion, and perhaps the matter became unclear to معمر — for what is well known of some of the Kūfans is the putting of علي ahead of عثمان; as for ahead of the two Shaykhs, no. And the merit of the two Shaykhs over the rest of the Companions is hidden from none but a dull man — so how should it be hidden from these imams?"

**عبرت:** A historian who will print a report and then say plainly that it is confused has spared his reader the work of guessing.

### TMA/E-MG20 · Seven hundred men in the house, and he forbade them to fight
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 17 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ — one house, marked.

**What happened:** The siege had run from the end of ذو القعدة to the eighteenth of ذو الحجة. On the day before the end, عثمان ؓ spoke to the Muhājirūn and Anṣār who were inside the house with him — close to seven hundred men, and البدایہ names عبد الله بن عمر ؓ, عبد الله بن الزبير ؓ, الحسن ؓ, الحسين ؓ, مروان, أبو هريرة ؓ and a great many of his own freedmen. Had he let them, ابن كثير writes, they would have defended him. Instead he put every man who owed him anything under oath to hold his hand and go home, and told his household that any slave who sheathed his sword was free. The fighting cooled from inside and grew hot from outside.

**The statement:**
> فقال لهم: أقسم على من لي عليه حق أن يكفّ يده وأن ينطلق إلى منزله، وعده من أعيان الصحابة وأبنائهم جمٌّ (غفير) وقال لرفيقه: من أغمد سيفه فهو حرٌّ.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۳۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3477
> *English:* "So he said to them: I put under oath every man who has a right owed to him by me, that he hold back his hand and go off to his house — and a great many of the notables of the Companions and their sons were with him — and he said to those about him: whoever sheathes his sword is free."

**عبرت:** A man may hold the power to be defended and refuse to use it.

**Hands-up?** If seven hundred armed men were standing in your house, what would you tell them?

### TMA/E-MG21 · الزبير ؓ hears of it outside المدینہ
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** outside المدینہ.

**What happened:** البدایہ narrates what followed the killing not through any one historian's summing-up but through the senior Companions ؓ, one after another, each with the آیت he recited when the news reached him. الزبير ؓ had left المدینہ. When word came he said إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون and asked Allah's mercy for عثمان ؓ. Then he was told that the men who had done it were sorry, and he recited from سورة يس about those whom a single cry seizes while they are still disputing, unable even to make a bequest, unable to return to their people.

**The statement:**
> ولما بلغ الزبيرَ مقتلُ عثمان -وكان قد خرج من المدينة- قال: إنا للّه وإنا إليه راجعون، ثم ترحَّم على عثمان، وبلغه أن الذين قتلوه ندموا فقال: تبًّا لهم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3488
> *English:* "And when the killing of عثمان reached الزبير — and he had gone out from المدینہ — he said: To Allah we belong and to Him we return. Then he asked mercy for عثمان. And it reached him that those who killed him had become remorseful, so he said: ruin to them."

**عبرت:** The first thing a believer says on hearing terrible news has already been given to him to say.

### TMA/E-MG22 · علي ؓ hears of it and recites an آیت about remorse
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** The news reached علي ؓ and he asked Allah's mercy for عثمان ؓ. Then he too heard that the men who had killed him had become remorseful, and he recited the آیت from سورة الحشر about Shayṭān, who says to man disbelieve, and then when the man has disbelieved says: I am quit of you, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds. Narrating this evening through the Companions' own reactions is the safest form there is, because then every judgement in the narration is theirs and not ours.

**The statement:**
> وبلغ عليًا قتلهُ فترحَّم عليه. وسمع بندم الذين قتلوه فتلا قوله تعالى: ﴿كَمَثَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ إِذْ قَالَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ اكْفُرْ فَلَمَّا كَفَرَ قَالَ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنْكَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [الحشر: ١٦]

**عبرت:** Remorse arriving after the deed is remorse that changes nothing.

### TMA/E-MG25 · حذيفة ؓ: the first of the trials, and the last of them

### TMA/E-MG26 · أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ on milk and blood — and three words after it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** After 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير رحمہ اللہ reports a saying of أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ with its chain. Had the killing of عثمان been guidance, the ummah would have milked milk by it; but it was misguidance, and so the ummah milked blood by it. Then, without pausing, in three words, he tells the reader exactly what that chain is worth: this one is broken. The verdict is set immediately beside the saying, on the same line, by the author himself. That is what a history done as a branch of hadith looks like on the page.

**The statement:**
> لو كان قتل عثمان هُدًى لاحتلبت به الأُمَّةُ لبنًا، ولكنّه كان ضلالًا فاحتلبت به الأُمَّةُ دمًا. وهذا منقطع.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3494
> *English:* "Had the killing of عثمان been guidance, the ummah would have milked milk by it; but it was misguidance, and so the ummah milked blood by it. And this one is broken [i.e. its chain is discontinuous]."

**عبرت:** A saying and the worth of its chain belong on the same page, not in different books.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG27 · حذيفة ؓ disowns it in both directions at once
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** After 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The same image of milk and blood is transmitted from حذيفة ؓ on the same page, in a longer form and with no grading remark attached to it. And his form of words is the most careful thing in the whole evening. O Allah, if the killing of عثمان was good, then I have no share in it; and if his killing was evil, then I am quit of it. He refuses to be counted in on either side of a thing he did not do — and then he gives the sign by which the matter will show itself, milk if it was good and blood if it was evil.

**The statement:**
> اللهمَّ إن كان قتل عثمان بن عفان خيرًا، فليس لي فيه نصيب؛ وإن كان قتله شرًا فأنا منه بريء، واللّه لئن كان قتله خيرًا ليحلبنه لبنًا، وإن كان قتله شرًا ليمتصن (١) به دمًا. وقد ذكره البخاري في "صحيحه" (٢).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3494
> *English:* "O Allah, if the killing of عثمان بن عفان was good, then I have no share in it; and if his killing was evil, then I am quit of it. By Allah — if his killing was good, it will surely be milked as milk, and if his killing was evil, blood will surely be sucked by it. And البخاري mentioned it in his Ṣaḥīḥ."

**عبرت:** A man may decline to be counted on either side of a thing he had no hand in.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG28 · ابن كثير says البخاري mentioned it; the editor says he could not find it there
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a disagreement about a book `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير رحمہ اللہ closes حذيفة ؓ's saying by adding that البخاري mentioned it in his Ṣaḥīḥ. At that exact point the editor of the printed edition prints his own note against him: thus he said, and I do not think it correct, for we did not come upon it in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī. So the attribution is contested on the page itself. The saying must therefore never be put on a slide as being in البخاري. The complete and costless sentence is: ابن كثير says البخاري mentioned it, and the editor of the printed edition says he could not find it there.

**The statement:**
> هكذا قال، وما أظنه صوابًا، فإننا لم نقف عليه في صحيح البخاري.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3494
> *English:* "Thus he said, and I do not think it correct, for we did not come upon it in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī." (The editor's note, not ابن كثير's.)

**عبرت:** An attribution is worth checking even when a great man made it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG29 · Forty days, or some forty, or twenty-two nights — and a Friday with no disagreement
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو القعدة–ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدینہ — the house, held.

**What happened:** Ask how long the house was under siege and the book gives three answers in one breath. Forty days, according to what is best known. And it is said, some forty days. And الشعبي said, twenty-two nights. Then, in the very next sentence and in the same voice, it gives one thing with no such hedging at all: his killing ؓ was on a Friday, with no disagreement. Read that paragraph slowly. The author is marking, word by word, exactly where certainty begins.

**The statement:**
> كانت مدة حصار (٥) عثمان ﵁ في داره أربعين يومًا على المشهور، وقيل كانت بضعةً وأربعين يومًا. وقال الشعبي: كانت ثنتين وعشرين ليلةً. ثم كان قتله ﵁ في يوم الجمعة بلا خلاف.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3489
> *English:* "The period of the siege of عثمان ؓ in his house was forty days, according to what is best known; and it is said it was some forty days; and الشعبي said it was twenty-two nights. Then his killing ؓ was on a Friday, with no disagreement."

**عبرت:** An honest record tells you where its own certainty stops.

**Hands-up?** How long do you think a caliph's house was under siege in his own city, in front of everybody?

### TMA/E-MG30 · Which hour of that Friday — and ابن كثير chooses without hiding the other
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** Friday, ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** On the same page the book goes down one level further, to the hour. سيف بن عمر from his teachers, and مصعب بن الزبير and others, say the last hour of that Friday. Others said mid-morning — and ابن كثير adds three words of his own: and this is the more likely. He does not delete the first opinion to make room for his own. He prints both and tells you which he leans to and why he is leaning rather than deciding.

**The statement:**
> قال سيف بن عمر عن مشايخه: في آخر ساعة منها، ونص عليه مصعب (٦) بن الزبير وآخرون. وقال آخرون ضحوة (نهارها)، وهذا أشبه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3489
> *English:* "سيف بن عمر said, from his teachers: in the last hour of it; and مصعب بن الزبير and others stated it expressly. And others said mid-morning — and this is the more likely."

**عبرت:** To prefer one report is not the same as to delete the other.

### TMA/E-MG31 · The year: 35, and someone said 36, and that is strange

### TMA/E-MG32 · Twelve years, less twelve days
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** المحرم 24 AH to ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map — the Line, a bar drawn.

**What happened:** Having fixed the year, the book does the arithmetic on the spot, and the arithmetic is the whole of a caliphate in one line. His caliphate was twelve years less twelve days — because the bayʿa had been given to him at the first sight of المحرم in the year 24. Twelve years is the longest of the four, and the number only exists because somebody wrote down both ends of it.

**The statement:**
> فكانت خلافته ثنتي عشرة سنة إلا اثني عشر يومًا، لأنه بويع له في مستهلّ المحرم سنة أربع وعشرين.

> *English:* "So his caliphate was twelve years less twelve days, because the bayʿa was given to him at the first of المحرم in the year 24."

**عبرت:** A length of time can only be stated by someone who recorded both of its ends.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG33 · How old he was: 63, 75, 82, 84, 88, 90
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** On the question of عثمان ؓ's age at his death, one single page of البدایہ carries a spread that runs from sixty-three to ninety. He passed eighty-two. صالح بن كيسان said eighty-two and some months. It is said eighty-four. قتادة, through أحمد, said eighty-eight or ninety, and in another narration eighty-two. هشام بن الكلبي said seventy-five — and ابن كثير remarks that this is very strange. Then he gives one stranger still: سيف بن عمر, from his teachers, saying sixty-three. Neither هشام nor سيف is a source of ours; they are named there as البدایہ's own informants.

**The statement:**
> وأغرب منه ما رواه (سيف) بن عمر عن مشايخه، وهم محمد وطلحة وأبو عثمان وأبو حارثة أنهم قالوا: قتل عثمان ﵁ عن ثلاث وستين سنة (٨).

> *English:* "And stranger still than that is what سيف بن عمر related from his teachers — محمد and طلحة and أبو عثمان and أبو حارثة — that they said: عثمان ؓ was killed at sixty-three years of age."

**عبرت:** Where the record is thin our books say it is thin, instead of choosing a number and sounding sure.

### TMA/E-MG34 · But about the place of his grave there is no disagreement

### TMA/E-MG36 · Six names for the man who led the prayer over him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدینہ — البقيع.

**What happened:** Who led the funeral prayer over the third caliph? The book answers in one sentence and the sentence contains six names. جبير بن مطعم ؓ prayed over him. And it is said الزبير بن العوام ؓ. And it is said حكيم بن حزام ؓ. And it is said مروان بن الحكم. And it is said المسور بن مخرمة ؓ. No preference is expressed, no argument is offered, and the reader is left holding all of them. It is the plainest single illustration of what these books do with a thing they do not know.

**The statement:**
> وصلى عليه جُبَيْر بن مطعم، وقيل الزبير بن العوام، وقيل حكيم بن حزام، وقيل مروان بن الحكم، وقيل المسور بن مَخْرَمة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3491
> *English:* "And جبير بن مطعم ؓ prayed over him — and it is said الزبير بن العوام ؓ, and it is said حكيم بن حزام ؓ, and it is said مروان بن الحكم, and it is said المسور بن مخرمة ؓ."

**عبرت:** Five hundred people can be present at a thing and still leave it unsettled.

**Hands-up?** A caliph is buried in his own city, with the Companions present. Should we expect the books to agree on who led the prayer?

### TMA/E-MG37 · One report converges: الزبير ؓ prayed over him, and was his وصي
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** On the same page a separate report, from قتادة through عبد الرزاق and أحمد, says that الزبير ؓ prayed over عثمان ؓ and buried him, and that عثمان ؓ had made his bequest to him. That fits an earlier report in البدایہ, from هشام بن عروة, that the bequest was indeed made to الزبير ؓ. Two independent reports leaning the same way is worth noticing — and it is worth saying aloud that noticing is all it is. A convergence is not a proof, and the book itself does not upgrade it to one.

**The statement:**
> قال: صلى الزبير على عثمان ودفنه وكان أوصى إليه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3491
> *English:* "He said: الزبير prayed over عثمان and buried him, and he had made his bequest to him."

**عبرت:** Two reports pointing the same way is a reason to lean, not a reason to declare.

**Hands-up?** no

### TMA/E-MG38 · Three days unburied, and ابن كثير's own guess at why
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** البدایہ records, attributing it to ابن جرير, that عثمان ؓ remained three days unburied after he was killed. Then ابن كثير writes قلت — I say — and gives a reason of his own: that the people had been occupied away from him by the bayʿa to علي ؓ until it was complete. Then he records that it is said two nights, and it is said he was buried that same night. Notice the punctuation of his honesty: the report is somebody else's, the explanation is marked as his own, and the alternatives follow anyway.

**The statement:**
> وقد ذكر ابن جرير (١٠) أن عثمان ﵁ بقي بعد أن قتل ثلاثة أيام لا يدفن.

> *English:* "And ابن جرير mentioned that عثمان ؓ remained, after he was killed, three days unburied." (البدایہ's own attribution to ابن جرير — not a citation of الطبری by us.)

**عبرت:** Mark your own guess as your own, and the reader can take the report without it.

### TMA/E-MG39 · Struck at the prayer, he forbade them to punish a whole tribe
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** الكوفة — the mosque.

**What happened:** علي ؓ was struck by ابن ملجم as he came out to the mosque. The people around him asked whether they should not kill the whole of مراد, the tribe the man belonged to. He refused. Hold him, he said, and keep him well in his bonds. If I die, kill him. If I live, then wounds are settled by قصاص — the same wound back, and nothing more. He is dying, and he is still holding the punishment down to exactly one man and exactly one measure.

**The statement:**
> فقال الناس: يا أمير المؤمنين ألا نقتل مرادًا كلها؟ فقال: لا ولكن احبسوه وأحسنوا إساره (٣)، فإن مت فاقتلوه وإن عشت فالجروح قصاص.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3757
> *English:* "The people said: Commander of the Believers, shall we not kill the whole of مراد? He said: No — but imprison him and keep him well bound. If I die, kill him; and if I live, then wounds are settled by retaliation."

**عبرت:** Justice keeps its shape at exactly the moment when nobody would blame you for letting it go.

**Hands-up?** The man who struck him belonged to a tribe. How many people would most rulers have punished?

### TMA/E-MG41 · Will you not appoint a successor? No
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

So this is an acknowledgement from him, at the last of his time in this world, of the merit of الصديق."

**عبرت:** A man with the power to decide what comes after him may judge that the community's own choosing is safer than his.

### TMA/E-MG42 · Established from him بالتواتر, from the pulpit of الكوفة

### TMA/E-MG43 · Seven places for his grave, in one paragraph

> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3757

**عبرت:** A book that offers seven answers is telling you honestly that it has none.

### TMA/E-MG44 · And one report in which the grave is simply lost
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** الكوفة → the country of طيِّئ, an arrow that stops.

And what is best known is that his grave is at الكوفة to this day."

**عبرت:** Our books would rather record that something is unknown than invent a place to put it.

### TMA/E-MG53 · الذهبي grades a chain down, in the middle of a virtue
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a grading, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي رحمہ اللہ is writing the merits of علي ؓ, and he is still sifting while he writes them. He gives a report of غدير خم through إبراهيم بن مهاجر بن مسمار, and then adds four words about the man: this إبراهيم — النسائي said, weak. Two lines further down he gives another report and marks its transmitter جابر الجعفي in the running text as abandoned. He is not attacking the merits. He is telling you which reports of them will bear weight.

**The statement:**
> الحديث إبراهيم هذا قال النسائي: ضعيف.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۳۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1370
> *English:* "…the ḥadīth. This إبراهيم — النسائي said: weak."

**عبرت:** A man who grades the reports he likes as carefully as the ones he dislikes can be trusted with both.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TMA/E-MG54 · And on the facing page he grades one up
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a grading, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The sifting runs both ways, which is the point. On the very next page الذهبي رحمہ اللہ gives the same hadith of من كنت مولاه by a different route — غندر, from شعبة, from ميمون أبي عبد الله, from زيد بن أرقم ؓ — and writes three words after it: this hadith is sound. Same author, same chapter, opposite verdicts, because the chains are different. That is what the work actually consists of.

**The statement:**
> هذا حديث صحيح.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۳۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1371
> *English:* "This ḥadīth is sound."

**عبرت:** The verdict follows the chain, not the liking.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TMA/E-MG55 · And on a third page he says the man was called a liar by more than one
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** No date — a grading, not an event · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A little further on, الذهبي رحمہ اللہ reports through الترمذي a report from عائشة ؓ about who was dearest to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and الترمذي himself has already marked it حسن غريب. الذهبي then adds his own note, introduced by قلت, I say: جميع — the transmitter — more than one man called him a liar. Even a report that has already been graded by somebody else gets graded again.

**The statement:**
> قلت: جميع كذبه غير واحد.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۳۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1377
> *English:* "I say: جميع — more than one has called him a liar."

**عبرت:** Nothing in this discipline is above being checked a second time.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TMA/E-MG56 · أيوب السختياني رحمہ اللہ, and the last word of the evening
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** No date — a saying of the تابعين's generation · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير رحمہ اللہ carries a saying of أيوب السختياني رحمہ اللہ, and it is where this evening ends. Whoever loves أبو بكر has set the religion upright. Whoever loves عمر has made the road plain. Whoever loves عثمان has taken light from the light of Allah. Whoever loves علي has taken hold of the firmest handhold. And whoever speaks well of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is quit of hypocrisy. Not one name is ranked against another. The last clause is the instruction, and the room leaves with it.

**The statement:**
> من أحبَّ أبا بكر فقد أقام الدين، ومن أحبَّ عمر فقد أوضح السبيل، ومن أحب عثمان فقد استنار بنور الله، ومن أحب عليًا فقد استمسك بالعروة الوثقى، ومن قال الحسنى في أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ فقد برئ من النفاق.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۰۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3755
> *English:* "Whoever loves أبو بكر has set the religion upright; whoever loves عمر has made the path plain; whoever loves عثمان has taken light from the light of Allah; whoever loves علي has taken hold of the firmest handhold; and whoever speaks well of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is quit of hypocrisy."

**عبرت:** Speaking well of all of them is not a compromise between positions; it is the position.

**Hands-up?** no
