## What was complained of, and by whom

*Source note: [`the-grievances-against-uthman.md`](../docs/research/the-grievances-against-uthman.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TGA/E-GR1 · The demand was about men, not about doctrine
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights; arrows in from Kufa, Basra and Fustat.

**What happened:** By the year 34 the objections had hardened into a delegation and a message. Men came up to Medina to argue with the caliph face to face about what he had done. Their charge was that he had dismissed many of the Companions from office and put his own kinsmen from Banu Umayya in their place. What they asked for was not a change of religion and not a change of law. They asked him to dismiss his governors and replace them with men of early precedence, and Ibn Kathir says the demand weighed on him very greatly.

**The statement:**
> وبعثوا إلى عثمان منْ يناظره فيما فعل وفيما اعتمد من عزل كثيرٍ من الصحابة وتولية جماعة من بني أمية من أقربائه، وأغلظوا له في القول، وطلبوا منه أن يعزل عمّاله ويستبدل أئمة غيرهم (من السابقين ومن الصحابة)، حتى شقَّ ذلك عليه جدًا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3455
> *English:* "And they sent to ʿUthman someone to dispute with him about what he had done and what he had relied upon, in dismissing many of the Companions and appointing a group of Banu Umayya from among his relatives; and they were harsh with him in speech, and demanded of him that he dismiss his governors and replace them with other leaders (from the early ones and from the Companions) — until that weighed on him very greatly."

**عبرت:** A quarrel about who holds office is not the same thing as a quarrel about what is true, and a room that confuses the two will misread the whole year.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR2 · Ibn Kathir states his own verdict in one clause
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir does not narrate this year coldly. Writing of the men who had been moved out of Basra and who kept up the campaign against the caliph, he stops the narrative and gives his own judgement in a single clause. He calls them the wrongdoers in what they did, and calls ʿUthman ؓ the righteous and rightly-guided one. This is the sentence the speaker quotes when the room wants him to take a side: the verdict is on the page, under the name of a recognised Sunni authority, and it does not need to be improved on from the platform.

**The statement:**
> فكان هؤلاء ممن يؤلِّب عليه ويمالئ الأعداء في الحط والكلام فيه، وهم الظالمون في ذلك، وهو البارّ الراشد ﵁.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3455
> *English:* "These were among those who incited against him and sided with his enemies in disparaging him and speaking against him; and they were the wrongdoers in that, while he was the righteous and rightly-guided one, may God be pleased with him."

**عبرت:** A settled verdict belongs to the scholar who reached it, and repeating it is not the same act as forming one.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR3 · Ibn al-Athir declines to transmit much of it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn al-Athir reaches the same year and does the opposite thing. Opening his chapter on the killing of ʿUthman ؓ, he says plainly that he has left out a great deal of the material people turned into a pretext, and that he had reasons for leaving it out. He does not argue with the reports. He simply does not carry them. Two great Sunni historians, two different methods, and both of them let the speaker stay out of the quarrel.

**The statement:**
> وَقَدْ تَرَكْنَا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْأَسْبَابِ الَّتِي جَعَلَهَا النَّاسُ ذَرِيعَةً إِلَى قَتْلِهِ لِعِلَلٍ دَعَتْ إِلَى ذَلِكَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1225
> *English:* "We have omitted much of the causes that people made into a pretext for killing him, for reasons that called for that."

**عبرت:** Leaving a report unrepeated is itself a scholarly act, and the tradition treats silence about a dispute as a discipline rather than a gap.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR4 · Five years in Kufa, his house without a door
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** Before al-Walid b. ʿUqba became a scandal he was a governor people liked. Ibn al-Athir opens the account of his dismissal by saying that he had been beloved to the people of Kufa and stayed so for five years, and that his house had no door on it. That detail is the measure of the office as it then stood: the governor of the second city of the empire lived behind an open doorway. Everything that follows happened to a man in that position.

**The statement:**
> وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ مَحْبُوبًا إِلَى النَّاسِ، فَبَقِيَ كَذَلِكَ خَمْسَ سِنِينَ وَلَيْسَ لِدَارِهِ بَابٌ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1167
> *English:* "And that he was beloved to the people, and he remained so for five years, and his house had no door."

**عبرت:** Authority that needs no door is a rarer achievement than authority that is never questioned.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR5 · A night robbery, a murder, and an execution order
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** The thing that turned Kufa against its governor began as a criminal case. Young men of the city broke into the house of Ibn al-Haysuman al-Khuzaʿi at night, he came out on them with a sword, and they killed him. Abu Shurayh al-Khuzaʿi and his son witnessed it from above. Al-Walid wrote to ʿUthman ؓ about them, ʿUthman ؓ wrote back ordering their execution, and they were put to death at the gate of the governor's palace. From that day their fathers were the governor's enemies.

**The statement:**
> فَشَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَبُو شُرَيْحٍ وَابْنُهُ، فَكَتَبَ فِيهِمُ الْوَلِيدُ إِلَى عُثْمَانَ، فَكَتَبَ عُثْمَانُ بِقَتْلِهِمْ، فَقَتَلَهُمْ عَلَى بَابِ الْقَصْرِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1167
> *English:* "So Abu Shurayh and his son testified against them, and al-Walid wrote about them to ʿUthman, and ʿUthman wrote ordering that they be killed, and he killed them at the gate of the palace."

**عبرت:** Justice carried out correctly still makes enemies, and the enemies it makes do not announce themselves at the time.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR6 · The fathers who watched, and twice found nothing
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** The bereaved fathers set watchers on the governor and waited. Word came to them that al-Walid and the poet Abu Zubayd were drinking wine, so they gathered men of Kufa and burst in on him. Ibn al-Athir records the result in four words: they saw nothing. They came out blaming each other, and the people of the city abused them for it. Al-Walid kept the whole incident from ʿUthman ؓ.

**The statement:**
> فَثَارُوا وَأَخَذُوا مَعَهُمْ نَفَرًا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ، فَاقْتَحَمُوا عَلَيْهِ فَلَمْ يَرَوْا، فَأَقْبَلُوا يَتَلَاوَمُونَ وَسَبَّهُمُ النَّاسُ، وَكَتَمَ الْوَلِيدُ ذَلِكَ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1167
> *English:* "So they rose and took with them a number of the people of Kufa and burst in upon him, and they saw nothing; and they came out blaming one another, and the people reviled them; and al-Walid concealed that from ʿUthman."

**عبرت:** A charge that fails once and is pressed again is telling you something about the accuser as well as the accused.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR7 · Four rakʿahs at dawn, and a question afterwards
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights, then an arrow to Medina.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir gives the reason for the dismissal in one sentence, and it is the sentence everyone remembers. The governor led the people of Kufa in the dawn prayer and prayed four cycles instead of two. Then he turned round to the congregation and asked whether they would like more. A man in the rows answered him. The exchange was in front of the whole mosque, and after it there was no argument left to have.

**The statement:**
> وفي هذه السنة عزل عثمانُ بن عفان الوليدَ بن عُقبة عن الكوفة، وولَّى عليها سعيد بن العاص وكان سببُ عزله أنَّه صلَّى بأهل الكوفة الصبحَ أربعًا ثم التفتَ فقال أزيدُكُمْ؟ فقال قائل: ما زلنا منكَ منذ اليوم في زيادة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3439
> *English:* "In this year ʿUthman b. ʿAffan dismissed al-Walid b. ʿUqba from Kufa and appointed Saʿid b. al-ʿAṣ over it. The cause of his dismissal was that he prayed the dawn prayer with the people of Kufa as four rakʿahs, then turned and said: 'Shall I give you more?' Whereupon someone said: 'We have had nothing but more from you since today.'"

**عبرت:** Public office is judged in public, and the prayer is the one place where a governor cannot be shielded by his office.

**Hands-up?** Before I tell you what happened in Kufa in the year 30 — who can tell me how many rakʿahs the dawn prayer has?

---

### TGA/E-GR8 · Ibn Kathir attaches a qualification to the testimony
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Immediately after telling the story Ibn Kathir adds the caution that a careful speaker must keep attached to it. The men who took the case up, he says, are reported to have had an existing enmity with al-Walid. Some of them testified that he had drunk wine; another testified only that he had seen him vomiting it. The qualification is in the book itself, and it is not an apology — it is how a historian marks the standing of the evidence he is passing on.

**The statement:**
> ثم إنّه تصدَّى له جماعةٌ يقال كان بينهم وبينه شنآن، فشَكَوْه إلى عثمان، وشهد بعضُهم عليه أنه شربَ الخمر، وشهد آخرُ أنَّه رآه يتقيَّؤها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3439
> *English:* "Then a group took him on, between whom and him there is said to have been enmity, and they complained of him to ʿUthman; and some of them testified against him that he had drunk wine, and another testified that he had seen him vomiting it."

**عبرت:** The tradition records who is accusing and why, and a report is never handed on stripped of that.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR9 · The witnesses said they had not seen him drink
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Al-Kamil tells the end of the affair differently, and the difference matters. Two of the watching fathers took the governor's signet ring off his hand while he slept and rode with it to Medina as proof. When they were put on oath, the question they were asked was whether they had actually seen him drinking. They answered no. What they could testify to was what they had wrung from his beard. That is the testimony the case rested on, and Ibn al-Athir prints the exchange in full.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: أَتَشْهَدَانِ أَنَّكُمَا رَأَيْتُمَاهُ يَشْرَبُ؟ فَقَالَا: لَا. قَالَ: فَكَيْفَ؟ قَالَا: اعْتَصَرْنَاهَا مِنْ لِحْيَتِهِ وَهُوَ يَقِيءُ الْخَمْرَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1168
> *English:* "He said: 'Do you two testify that you saw him drinking?' They said: 'No.' He said: 'Then how?' They said: 'We wrung it out of his beard while he was vomiting the wine.'"

**عبرت:** A court that asks exactly what the witness saw is doing the work; a crowd that repeats the verdict without the question is not.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR10 · The ḥadd on the caliph's own half-brother
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Al-Walid b. ʿUqba was ʿUthman ؓ's half-brother by his mother. The caliph recalled him, the prescribed punishment was carried out on him in Medina, and a new governor went to Kufa in his place. Our books do not agree on whose hand administered it. Al-Kamil records one account and then corrects it in its own voice, naming ʿAbd Allah b. Jaʿfar as the man who flogged him, at ʿAli ؓ's instruction, after al-Ḥasan ؓ had declined with a proverb. Al-Bidaya on the other hand names Saʿid b. al-ʿAṣ. Give both, or give neither.

**The statement:**
> هَكَذَا فِي هَذِهِ الرِّوَايَةِ، وَالصَّحِيحُ أَنَّ الَّذِي جَلَدَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ لِأَنَّ عَلِيًّا أَمَرَ ابْنَهُ الْحَسَنَ أَنْ يَجْلِدَهُ، فَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ: وَلِّ حَارَّهَا مَنْ تَوَلَّى قَارَّهَا!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1168
> *English:* "Thus it is in this account; but the sound version is that the one who flogged him was ʿAbd Allah b. Jaʿfar b. Abi Ṭalib — because ʿAli ordered his son al-Ḥasan to flog him, and al-Ḥasan said: 'Let him who took charge of its cool part take charge of its hot part!'"

**عبرت:** A penalty that reaches the ruler's own family is the test of whether the law is above the household.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR11 · ʿAli ؓ on forty lashes and eighty
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** At the moment of the flogging ʿAli ؓ gave his own legal position out loud, and al-Kamil preserves it. The Messenger of God ﷺ flogged forty, he said, and Abu Bakr ؓ forty, and ʿUthman ؓ eighty — and each of them is sunna. Then he said which of the two he himself preferred. It is a complete piece of fiqh delivered in a single breath, and it shows a difference of practice being handled without anybody being accused of anything.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ: أَمْسِكْ، جَلَدَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ -، وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ أَرْبَعِينَ وَجَلَدَ عُثْمَانُ ثَمَانِينَ وَكُلٌّ سُنَّةٌ وَهَذَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1168
> *English:* "ʿAli said: 'Hold. The Messenger of God ﷺ flogged, and Abu Bakr, forty; and ʿUthman flogged eighty; and each is sunna, and this is dearer to me.'"

**عبرت:** Two different practices can both be sunna, and the one you prefer is still only the one you prefer.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR12 · Two families left at feud afterwards
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** The system had worked. A complaint was carried to the capital, a governor was recalled, the punishment was carried out on the caliph's half-brother in front of the city, and a replacement was appointed. Al-Kamil then adds the cost in one clause: it bequeathed an enmity between the two families. The case was closed and the quarrel was not.

**The statement:**
> فَأَوْرَثَ ذَلِكَ عَدَاوَةً بَيْنَ أَهْلَيْهِمَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1168
> *English:* "And that bequeathed an enmity between the two households."

**عبرت:** A dispute settled by law can still leave the parties unreconciled, and unreconciled parties wait.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR13 · The new governor washes the pulpit
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** Saʿid b. al-ʿAṣ arrived in Kufa, sent al-Walid on to Medina, and washed the pulpit of the mosque. Men of Banu Umayya who had ridden out with him told him not to do it — it was a public statement about their own kinsman. Ibn al-Athir records in four words that he did not answer them. The first act of the new governor was a rebuke to his own clan.

**The statement:**
> فَقَدِمَ سَعِيدٌ الْكُوفَةَ وَسَيَّرَ الْوَلِيدَ وَغَسَلَ الْمِنْبَرَ، فَنَهَاهُ رِجَالٌ مِنْ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ كَانُوا قَدْ خَرَجُوا مَعَهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1200
> *English:* "So Saʿid came to Kufa, sent al-Walid away, and washed the pulpit. Men of Banu Umayya who had gone out with him forbade him that, but he did not answer them."

**عبرت:** A man may be appointed from a family and still refuse to govern on its behalf.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR14 · Saʿid writes about who had been swamped
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights; the Sawad shaded around it.

**What happened:** Saʿid b. al-ʿAṣ wrote to ʿUthman ؓ with a diagnosis of the city rather than a complaint about individuals. The affair of Kufa had become disordered, he wrote. The men of standing, of the great houses, and of early precedence in Islam had been overcome in numbers, and the element now dominant was later contingents and bedouin who had attached themselves after the conquests. He was describing a garrison town that had grown faster than its own leadership.

**The statement:**
> أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكُوفَةِ قَدِ اضْطَرَبَ أَمْرُهُمْ، وَغُلِبَ أَهْلُ الشَّرَفِ مِنْهُمْ وَالْبُيُوتَاتِ وَالسَّابِقَةِ، وَالْغَالِبُ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْبِلَادِ رَوَادِفُ قَدِمَتْ، وَأَعْرَابٌ لَحِقَتْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1169
> *English:* "That the affair of the people of Kufa had become disordered, and that the people of honour, of the great houses, and of early precedence among them had been overcome; and that the dominant element in those lands was later contingents that had arrived and bedouin who had attached themselves."

**عبرت:** A city can outgrow the men who founded it faster than anyone in it notices.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR15 · ʿUthman ؓ replies, preserve to each his station
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The caliph's answer is a piece of administrative writing worth reading aloud whole. Give precedence to the men of early precedence and to those through whom God opened those lands, he wrote, and let the later settlers follow after them — unless the early ones have grown slack about the truth while the newcomers have upheld it. Then he closed with an instruction that covers every case the rule does not: preserve to each man his station.

**The statement:**
> فَفَضْلُ أَهْلِ السَّابِقَةِ وَالْقُدْمَةِ وَمَنْ فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ تِلْكَ الْبِلَادَ، وَلْيَكُنْ مَنْ نَزَلَهَا مِنْ غَيْرِهِمْ تَبَعًا لَهُمْ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونُوا تَثَاقَلُوا عَنِ الْحَقِّ وَتَرَكُوا الْقِيَامَ بِهِ وَقَامَ بِهِ هَؤُلَاءِ، وَاحْفَظْ لِكُلٍّ مَنْزِلَتَهُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1170
> *English:* "Give precedence to the people of early precedence and priority and to those through whom God opened those lands; and let whoever settled there besides them follow after them — unless they have grown slack about the truth and abandoned upholding it while these others have upheld it. And preserve to each his station."

**عبرت:** Precedence is a real claim and not an unconditional one, and the condition is that the work is still being done.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR16 · The first account of the Kufan breakdown
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights; the Euphrates bank shaded.

**What happened:** Al-Kamil gives two separate accounts of how the night gatherings in Kufa broke up, and keeps them apart. In the first, the talk in the governor's evening circle turned to how generous Ṭalḥa ؓ was, and Saʿid remarked that a man with an estate like his could well afford to be. A young man then wished the Milṭaṭ — the old Sasanian land along the Euphrates — on the governor as a gift. The room turned on him, his father stood up for him, and seven named men beat them both unconscious. Those seven then went home and began to speak against ʿUthman ؓ.

**The statement:**
> فَثَارَ بِهِ الْأَشْتَرُ، وَجُنْدَبٌ، وَابْنُ ذِي الْحِنْكَةِ، وَصَعْصَعَةُ، وَابْنُ الْكَوَّاءِ، وَكُمَيْلٌ، وَعُمَيْرُ بْنُ ضَابِئٍ فَأَخَذُوهُ، فَثَارَ أَبُوهُ لِيَمْنَعَ عَنْهُ، فَضَرَبُوهُمَا حَتَّى غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِمَا، وَجَعَلَ سَعِيدٌ يُنَاشِدُهُمْ وَيَأْبَوْنَ حَتَّى قَضَوْا مِنْهُمَا وَطَرًا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1201
> *English:* "Then al-Ashtar rose against him, and Jundab, and Ibn Dhi al-Ḥinka, and Ṣaʿṣaʿa, and Ibn al-Kawwaʾ, and Kumayl, and ʿUmayr b. Ḏabiʾ, and they seized him; and his father rose to defend him, and they beat the two of them until they fell senseless, and Saʿid kept appealing to them and they refused, until they had had their fill of the two."

**عبرت:** A careless sentence about land, spoken to flatter, can cost more than the land is worth.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR17 · This Sawad is a garden for Quraysh
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights; the Sawad shaded.

**What happened:** Al-Kamil then gives the other account, and this is the famous one. In the governor's evening circle Saʿid b. al-ʿAṣ said that the Sawad — the irrigated farmland of lower Iraq — was nothing but a garden for Quraysh. Al-Ashtar answered him on the spot: was he claiming that land which God had given as spoil to the men who fought for it was a garden for him and his people? The whole Kufan grievance is in that exchange, and it is about who owned the conquest.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ سَعِيدٌ: إِنَّمَا هَذَا السَّوَادُ بُسْتَانُ قُرَيْشٍ. فَقَالَ الْأَشْتَرُ: أَتَزْعُمُ أَنَّ السَّوَادَ الَّذِي أَفَاءَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا بِأَسْيَافِنَا بُسْتَانٌ لَكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ؟
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1201
> *English:* "Saʿid said: 'This Sawad is nothing but a garden for Quraysh.' Al-Ashtar said: 'Do you claim that the Sawad, which God gave us as spoil by our swords, is a garden for you and for your people?'"

**عبرت:** Men who have fought for something will not hear it spoken of as somebody's private property.

**Hands-up?** Who conquered Iraq — the tribes who fought there, or the Quraysh who governed it? Hold the question; you are about to hear two men argue it.

### TGA/E-GR18 · The books keep the two causes apart
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The two accounts are not the same scene told twice. They have different starting points, different speakers and partly different lists of names, and Ibn al-Athir marks the join with the standard formula for an alternative report: and it is said, rather, that the cause of it was such-and-such. He sets them side by side and leaves them there. Merging them into one tidy scene would produce something that is in neither book.

**The statement:**
> وَقِيلَ: بَلْ كَانَ السَّبَبُ فِي ذَلِكَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1201
> *English:* "And it is said, rather, that the cause of that was..."

**عبرت:** Where the historians preserve two accounts, tidying them into one is a loss and not a service.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR19 · The circle closes, the talk moves home
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** Saʿid's reaction to the beating in his own majlis was to end the institution. He swore that no one would ever again sit with him in evening conversation. The men he had shut out did not stop talking; they simply moved. They began to sit in their own gatherings instead, reviling ʿUthman ؓ and Saʿid, and al-Kamil records that people gathered to them until they became many. That sentence is the hinge of the whole Kufan strand.

**The statement:**
> فَجَعَلُوا يَجْلِسُونَ فِي مَجَالِسِهِمْ يَشْتُمُونَ عُثْمَانَ وَسَعِيدًا، وَاجْتَمَعَ إِلَيْهِمُ النَّاسُ حَتَّى كَثُرُوا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1202
> *English:* "So they took to sitting in their own gatherings, reviling ʿUthman and Saʿid; and people gathered to them until they became many."

**عبرت:** Shutting a disaffected man out of your hearing does not silence him; it only removes you from the room where he speaks.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR20 · ʿUthman ؓ's written instruction about the exiled men
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrow from Kufa to Damascus.

**What happened:** Saʿid and the notables of Kufa wrote to the caliph asking that these men be removed from the city. ʿUthman ؓ ordered them attached to Muʿawiya ؓ in Syria, and wrote to Muʿawiya ؓ himself with instructions that are neither a sentence nor a pardon. Stand over them and forbid them, he wrote; if you find right guidance in them, accept it; if they defeat you, send them back to me. The caliph kept the case open and kept it his own.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّ نَفَرًا قَدْ خُلِقُوا لِلْفِتْنَةِ فَأَقِمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَانْهَهُمْ، فَإِنْ آنَسْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُشْدًا فَاقْبَلْ، وَإِنْ أَعْيَوْكَ فَارْدُدْهُمْ عَلَيَّ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1202
> *English:* "A group of men have been created for sedition, so stand over them and forbid them; and if you perceive right guidance in them, accept it; and if they defeat you, send them back to me."

**عبرت:** An order that leaves room for the man to come right is a different instrument from a sentence, and the difference is deliberate.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR21 · The exiles are lodged, fed and argued with
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Damascus lights.

**What happened:** What met the Kufan exiles in Syria was not a prison. Muawiya ؓ lodged them in the Church of Mary, continued the stipends they had drawn in Iraq on the caliph's own orders, and ate his midday and evening meals with them. Then one day he put his case to them: they were Arabs with standing and with tongues, Islam had given them rank, and their leaders were a shield over them that they should not tear. It was an argument, conducted over dinner, with the men the caliph had sent him.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ لَكُمْ أَسْنَانٌ وَأَلْسِنَةٌ، وَقَدْ أَدْرَكْتُمْ بِالْإِسْلَامِ شَرَفًا، وَغَلَبْتُمُ الْأُمَمَ وَحَوَيْتُمْ مَوَارِيثَهُمْ، وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّكُمْ نَقِمْتُمْ قُرَيْشًا، وَلَوْ لَمْ تَكُنْ قُرَيْشٌ كُنْتُمْ أَذِلَّةً، إِنَّ أَئِمَّتَكُمْ لَكُمْ جُنَّةٌ فَلَا تَفْتَرِقُوا عَنْ جُنَّتِكُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1202
> *English:* "You are a people of the Arabs with years and with tongues, and you have attained honour through Islam, and you overcame the nations and inherited what was theirs. It has reached me that you have found fault with Quraysh; and had there been no Quraysh you would have been abased. Your leaders are a shield for you, so do not separate yourselves from your shield."

**عبرت:** An administration that keeps paying the men it has removed is still treating them as citizens.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR22 · Sasaa answers the governor in his own hall
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Damascus lights.

**What happened:** Sasaa b. Suhan answered him in front of everyone, and answered the argument rather than the man. Quraysh, he said, had been neither the most numerous nor the strongest of the Arabs before Islam, so their name was no threat; and as for the shield, a shield that is pierced lets the blow through to the man behind it. Al-Kamil prints the reply in full and prints Muawiya ؓ's long answer after it. Neither man is edited.

**The statement:**
> أَمَّا مَا ذَكَرْتَ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ فَإِنَّهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ أَكْثَرَ الْعَرَبِ وَلَا أَمْنَعَهَا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَتُخَوِّفَنَا، وَأَمَّا مَا ذَكَرْتَ مِنَ الْجُنَّةِ فَإِنَّ الْجُنَّةَ إِذَا اخْتُرِقَتْ خُلِصَ إِلَيْنَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1202
> *English:* "As for what you mentioned of Quraysh — they were not the most numerous of the Arabs nor the most inviolable of them in the Age of Ignorance, that you should frighten us with them. And as for what you mentioned of the shield — a shield, once it is pierced, is got through to us."

**عبرت:** An argument that can only be won by rank has not been won.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR23 · Sasaa tells the governor to resign his post
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Damascus lights.

**What happened:** On a later night the exchange went further. Muawiya ؓ put it to the men that he had called them to nothing but the fear of God, obedience to His Prophet ﷺ, holding to the rope of God together and not splitting. Sasaa answered that he had commanded the opposite. Then he said the thing that could not be taken back: that Muawiya ؓ should step down from his office, because there were men among the Muslims with a better claim to it than his, by their fathers' standing in Islam and by their own.

**The statement:**
> فَإِنَّا نَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ تَعْتَزِلَ عَمَلَكَ فَإِنَّ فِي الْمُسْلِمِينَ مَنْ هُوَ أَحَقُّ بِهِ مِنْكَ، مَنْ كَانَ أَبُوهُ أَحْسَنَ قَدَمًا فِي الْإِسْلَامِ مِنْ أَبِيكَ وَهُوَ أَحْسَنُ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ قَدَمًا مِنْكَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1204
> *English:* "Then we command you to withdraw from your office, for among the Muslims there is one who has more right to it than you — one whose father had a better standing in Islam than your father, and who himself has a better standing in Islam than you."

**عبرت:** The demand to hand over an office is the point at which a complaint becomes a claim on power.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR24 · The governor answers by naming who appointed him
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Muawiya ؓ answered the demand by reciting his own appointments. The Messenger of God ﷺ had put him to work and brought him into his affair; then Abu Bakr ؓ appointed him; then Umar ؓ; then Uthman ؓ; and not one of them appointed him while displeased with him. Then he warned the men not to press a matter while knowing in themselves something other than what they were showing. The whole speech is on the page and it is an argument from record, not from force.

**The statement:**
> إِنِّي مُعِيدٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - كَانَ مَعْصُومًا فَوَلَّانِي وَأَدْخَلَنِي فِي أَمْرِهِ، ثُمَّ اسْتُخْلِفَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ فَوَلَّانِي، ثُمَّ اسْتُخْلِفَ عُمَرُ فَوَلَّانِي، ثُمَّ اسْتُخْلِفَ عُثْمَانُ فَوَلَّانِي، وَلَمْ يُولِّنِي أَحَدٌ إِلَّا وَهُوَ عَنِّي رَاضٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1203
> *English:* "I repeat to you that the Messenger of God ﷺ was preserved from error, and he put me in office and brought me into his affair; then Abu Bakr was made successor and appointed me; then Umar was made successor and appointed me; then Uthman was made successor and appointed me — and not one of them appointed me except while he was pleased with me."

**عبرت:** A man who can name who trusted him, and when, is answering a charge with a record rather than with anger.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR25 · He lets them go where they please
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Damascus lights.

**What happened:** The argument ended without a punishment. Muawiya ؓ came back to them, told them he had given them leave, and sent them off to go wherever they wished. He told them that if they wanted safety they should hold to their community and not let favours make them insolent, and that he would write to the caliph about them. Then he wrote to Uthman ؓ that these were men no one could be hurt by except in company with others, and asked him to keep Saeed and the men in Kufa away from them.

**The statement:**
> إِنِّي قَدْ أَذِنْتُ لَكُمْ فَاذْهَبُوا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ لَا يَنْفَعُ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ أَحَدًا أَبَدًا وَلَا يَضُرُّهُ، وَلَا أَنْتُمْ بِرِجَالِ مَنْفَعَةٍ وَلَا مَضَرَّةٍ، فَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمُ النَّجَاةَ فَالْزَمُوا جَمَاعَتَكُمْ وَلَا يُبْطِرَنَّكُمُ الْإِنْعَامُ، فَإِنَّ الْبَطَرَ لَا يَعْتَرِي الْخِيَارَ، اذْهَبُوا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ فَسَأَكْتُبُ إِلَى أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِيكُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1203
> *English:* "I have given you leave, so go wherever you wish... If you desire deliverance, then hold fast to your community and do not let favour make you insolent, for insolence does not come upon the best of men. Go wherever you wish, and I shall write to the Commander of the Faithful concerning you."

**عبرت:** Letting an opponent go is a decision with consequences, and the men who made it knew they were making it.

### TGA/E-GR26 · A month of drill at Homs, then a recantation
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Homs lights.

**What happened:** From Damascus the men went north, and Abd al-Rahman b. Khalid b. al-Walid, who held Homs, sent for them. He met them with his father's name and a threat, and then kept them a month, walking them on foot beside him every time he rode out. Each time Sasaa passed him he asked him whether he had learned that a man not mended by good is mended by hardship. In the end the men asked God's pardon and asked his, and he told them God had turned to them.

**The statement:**
> فَأَقَامَهُمْ شَهْرًا كُلَّمَا رَكِبَ أَمْشَاهُمْ، فَإِذَا مَرَّ بِهِ صَعْصَعَةُ قَالَ: يَا ابْنَ الْحُطَيْئَةِ، أَعَلِمْتَ أَنَّ مَنْ لَمْ يُصْلِحْهُ الْخَيْرُ أَصْلَحَهُ الشَّرُّ؟ مَا لَكَ لَا تَقُولُ كَمَا بَلَغَنِي أَنَّكَ قُلْتَ لِسَعِيدٍ وَمُعَاوِيَةَ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: نَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ، أَقِلْنَا أَقَالَكَ اللَّهُ. فَمَا زَالُوا بِهِ حَتَّى قَالَ: تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1204
> *English:* "So he kept them a month; every time he rode out he made them walk. And when Sasaa passed by him he would say: 'Son of al-Hutaya, have you learned that whoever is not set right by good is set right by hardship? Why do you not say what I am told you said to Saeed and to Muawiya?' And they would say: 'We repent to God — pardon us, may God pardon you.' And they kept at him until he said: 'God has turned to you.'"

**عبرت:** Discipline and pardon were the two ends of the same month, and the record keeps both.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR27 · Al-Ashtar goes to the caliph and chooses
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrow from Homs to Medina and back.

**What happened:** Abd al-Rahman then sent Malik al-Ashtar to the caliph himself. The exchange in Medina is four words long. Uthman ؓ told him to settle wherever he wished. Al-Ashtar said: with Abd al-Rahman b. Khalid. The caliph answered that it was his to decide, and he went back. The men who had been moved out of Kufa under guard ended by choosing their own place of residence.

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1204
> *English:* "And he sent al-Ashtar to Uthman, and he came to him a second time. Uthman said to him: 'Settle wherever you wish.' He said: 'With Abd al-Rahman b. Khalid.' He said: 'That is for you to decide' — and he went back to him."

**عبرت:** A punishment that ends in the man choosing his own address was never quite a punishment.

### TGA/E-GR28 · Al-Bidaya tells the removal as forbearance
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa, then Damascus.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir narrates the same removal with the emphasis elsewhere. The caliph wrote to Muawiya ؓ that he was sending him reciters of Kufa, and told him to lodge them, honour them and win them over. Muawiya ؓ did exactly that, met them, admonished them and advised them to hold with the community; their spokesman answered him with words Ibn Kathir calls ugly and outrageous, and Muawiya ؓ bore it, out of his forbearance. Only after a second attempt did he put them out of Syria.

**The statement:**
> وكتب عثمان إلى معاوية أمير الشّام أنه قد أخرج (٢) إليك قراء من أهل الكوفة فأنزلهم وأكرمهم وتألفهم. فلما قدموا أنزلهم معاوية وأكرمهم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3454
> *English:* "And Uthman wrote to Muawiya, the governor of Syria: 'I have sent out to you reciters from the people of Kufa, so lodge them, honour them, and win them over.' And when they arrived Muawiya lodged them and honoured them."

**عبرت:** The same act looks like exile from one side of the correspondence and like hospitality from the other, and both letters survive.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR29 · Ten men, or nine, and Ibn Kathir prefers nine
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** How many men were moved out of Kufa is not settled in our own books. Ibn Kathir says they were ten, then adds that it is said nine, and that nine is the more likely. He then gives names: Kumayl b. Ziyad, Malik al-Ashtar al-Nakhai, Sasaa b. Suhan and his brother Zayd, Kab b. Malik al-Arhabi, al-Aswad b. Yazid, Alqama b. Qays and others. Part of the list survives only in one manuscript, and the editor marks it.

**The statement:**
> وكانوا عشرةً، وقيل تسعة وهو الأشبه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3454
> *English:* "And they were ten; and it is said nine, and that is the more likely."

**عبرت:** A historian who cannot settle a number of ten men says so, and that habit is what makes the rest of him worth trusting.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR30 · Al-Kamil's own list of the ten
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** Ibn al-Athir gives his own list, and it overlaps with Ibn Kathir's without matching it. His ten are al-Ashtar, Thabit b. Qays al-Hamdani, Kumayl b. Ziyad, Zayd b. Suhan and his brother Sasaa, Jundab b. Zuhayr al-Ghamidi, Jundab b. Kab al-Azdi, Urwa b. al-Jad, Amr b. al-Hamiq al-Khuzai, and Ibn al-Kawwa. Several of these names will come back at the end of the story, which is why the list is worth reading out slowly.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانُوا: الْأَشْتَرَ، وَثَابِتَ بْنَ قَيْسٍ الْهَمْدَانِيَّ، وَكُمَيْلَ بْنَ زِيَادٍ، وَزَيْدَ بْنَ صُوحَانَ، وَأَخَاهُ صَعْصَعَةَ، وَجُنْدَبَ بْنَ زُهَيْرٍ الْغَامِدِيَّ، وَجُنْدَبَ بْنَ كَعْبٍ الْأَزْدِيَّ، وَعُرْوَةَ بْنَ الْجَعْدِ، وَعَمْرَو بْنَ الْحَمِقِ الْخُزَاعِيَّ، وَابْنَ الْكَوَّاءِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1205
> *English:* "And they were: al-Ashtar, Thabit b. Qays al-Hamdani, Kumayl b. Ziyad, Zayd b. Suhan and his brother Sasaa, Jundab b. Zuhayr al-Ghamidi, Jundab b. Kab al-Azdi, Urwa b. al-Jad, Amr b. al-Hamiq al-Khuzai, and Ibn al-Kawwa."

**عبرت:** The same handful of names runs through five years of trouble, which is a fact about the trouble and not only about the names.

### TGA/E-GR31 · Ibn al-Kawwa sums up four cities
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** All four cities light: Medina, Kufa, Fustat, Damascus.

**What happened:** Muawiya ؓ asked Ibn al-Kawwa, whom he called the most intelligent of his companions, to tell him about the young men of the garrison cities. The answer is four sentences, one city each, and it is the sharpest short description of the empire's temper in this whole strand. It is also a reminder that the men on the other side of the argument were not fools.

**The statement:**
> أَمَّا أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ فَهُمْ أَحْرَصُ الْأُمَّةِ عَلَى الشَّرِّ وَأَعْجَزُهُمْ عَنْهُ، وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ الْكُوفَةِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَرِدُونَ جَمِيعًا وَيَصْدُرُونَ شَتَّى، وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ مِصْرَ فَهُمْ أَوْفَى النَّاسِ بِشَرٍّ وَأَسْرَعُهُمْ نَدَامَةً، وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ الشَّامِ فَهُمْ أَطْوَعُ النَّاسِ لِمُرْشِدِهِمْ وَأَعْصَاهُمْ لِمُغْوِيهِمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1205
> *English:* "As for the people of Medina, they are the keenest of the community on mischief and the least capable of it. As for the people of Kufa, they come to the water together and go away scattered. As for the people of Egypt, they are the most persistent of people in evil and the quickest of them to regret. As for the people of Syria, they are the most obedient of people to whoever guides them and the most disobedient to whoever misleads them."

**عبرت:** Every city has a temper of its own, and a ruler who does not know it will be surprised by the same city twice.

**Hands-up?** Four cities, four tempers. Before I read this out — which of them do you think the speaker called quickest to regret?

### TGA/E-GR32 · Humran b. Aban and a marriage inside the idda
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Basra lights.

**What happened:** Two men were also moved out of Basra, and our books state the reasons plainly. Humran b. Aban had married a woman while she was still inside her waiting period. Uthman ؓ separated them, had him beaten, and sent him to Basra. That is the whole charge: a matter of the law of marriage, dealt with by the penalty, the separation and the removal.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ حُمْرَانُ بْنُ أَبَانَ قَدْ تَزَوَّجَ امْرَأَةً فِي عِدَّتِهَا فَفَرَّقَ عُثْمَانُ بَيْنَهُمَا وَضَرَبَهُ وَسَيَّرَهُ إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1206
> *English:* "And Humran b. Aban had married a woman during her waiting period, so Uthman separated the two of them, and beat him, and removed him to Basra."

**عبرت:** When a removal has a stated legal cause on the page, the speaker does not have to guess at a hidden one.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR33 · A charge against Amir b. Abd Qays, found false
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Basra, then the Syrian coast.

**What happened:** Amir b. Abd Qays was reported to Medina for refusing marriage, refusing meat, and not attending the Friday prayer. He was sent on to Muawiya ؓ, who watched him eat a thoroughly ordinary meal of tharid and concluded that the man had been lied about. He then told him the reason he had been expelled, and Amir answered all three charges: he attended the Friday prayer at the back and left early, he had left Basra while a marriage was being arranged for him, and he avoided butchers' meat for a reason of his own.

**The statement:**
> فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ عَلَيْهِ رَأَى عِنْدَهُ ثَرِيدًا، فَأَكَلَ أَكْلًا عَرَبِيًّا، فَعَرَفَ أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ مَكْذُوبٌ عَلَيْهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1206
> *English:* "And when he came to him he saw tharid before him, and he ate as an Arab eats; so he knew that the man had been lied about."

**عبرت:** A charge carried a thousand miles can be disproved at a dinner table, which says something about how it travelled.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR34 · The man who would not go back
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 33 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Syrian coast lights.

**What happened:** Muawiya ؓ, satisfied, told him to go home. Amir refused: he would not return to a town whose people had treated him as they had. He settled on the Syrian coast instead. Muawiya ؓ kept asking him what he needed and he kept answering that he needed nothing, until at last he asked for a share of Basra's heat, because fasting came too easily in Syria.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: فَارْجِعْ. قَالَ: لَا أَرْجِعُ إِلَى بَلَدٍ اسْتَحَلَّ أَهْلُهُ مِنِّي مَا اسْتَحَلُّوا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۱۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1206
> *English:* "He said: 'Then go back.' He said: 'I will not go back to a town whose people have permitted themselves against me what they have permitted themselves.'"

**عبرت:** Being cleared of a charge does not undo what the accusation cost, and the man cleared is the one who decides that.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR35 · An army turns its own governor back at al-Jaraa
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A point on the road between Kufa and al-Qadisiyya.

**What happened:** When the governors went back to their provinces after the Medina council, the people of Kufa refused to let Saeed b. al-As in. Yazid b. Qays went out to al-Jaraa, near al-Qadisiyya, with al-Ashtar and a crowd behind him. Saeed reached them and was told there was no need of him. He argued that a delegation of two men would have done the job and asked whether a thousand men with sense go out to meet one man. Then he turned round and rode back to Medina.

**The statement:**

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1209
> *English:* "Then Saeed b. al-As reached them, and they said: 'We have no need of you.' He said: 'It would have been enough for you to send one man to the Commander of the Faithful and one man to me. Do a thousand men who have minds go out to one man?'"

**عبرت:** A province that can refuse its governor at the city limit has already changed what the office means.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR36 · The caliph grants exactly what they asked, in writing
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrow from Medina to Kufa.

**What happened:** Saeed reported to Medina that the Kufans wanted a replacement and wanted Abu Musa al-Ashari. Uthman ؓ appointed Abu Musa and wrote to them saying so. The letter is not a concession dressed as a rebuke; it says he has given them the man they chose and relieved them of Saeed, and that he will lend them his own honour and spend his patience on them, so that they shall have no argument against him before God.

**The statement:**
> أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَقَدْ أَمَّرْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ مَنِ اخْتَرْتُمْ وَأَعْفَيْتُكُمْ مِنْ سَعِيدٍ، وَاللَّهِ لَأُقْرِضَنَّكُمْ عِرْضِي وَلَأَبْذُلَنَّ لَكُمْ صَبْرِي وَلَأَسْتَصْلِحَنَّكُمْ بِجُهْدِي
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1209
> *English:* "To proceed: I have set over you the man you chose, and relieved you of Saeed. By God, I will lend you my honour, and I will spend my patience on you, and I will labour to set you right."

**عبرت:** Granting a demand in full is a real answer to it, and it does not always end the quarrel.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR37 · Al-Bidaya gives an oath at the gate
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir tells the same day with different detail. The Kufans put on armour and swore that they would not let Saeed enter until the caliph removed him and appointed Abu Musa al-Ashari; al-Ashtar said that day that Saeed would not enter while they carried their swords. Saeed held back from fighting them. Ibn Kathir's summary of the caliph's answer is that he granted what they asked, to remove their excuse and cut off their pretexts.

**The statement:**
> فأجابهم عثمان إلى ما سألوا إزاحة لعذرهم، وإزالة لشبههم، وقطعًا لعللهم

> *English:* "So Uthman granted them what they had asked, to remove their excuse, to dispel their doubts, and to cut off their pretexts."

**عبرت:** Removing a man's excuse is one of the few things a ruler can do alone, and it is worth doing even when it changes nothing.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR38 · Hudhayfa ؓ predicts a bloodless day
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa mosque.

**What happened:** While the crowd was out at al-Jaraa, Hudhayfa ؓ and Abu Masud al-Ansari ؓ were sitting in the mosque at Kufa. Abu Masud said the affair would not be turned back without blood. Hudhayfa ؓ swore it would be turned back and that not a cupping-glass of blood would be spilt in it, and added that he knew nothing that day which he had not already known while the Prophet ﷺ was alive. Saeed went back to Medina and no blood was shed.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ حُذَيْفَةُ: وَاللَّهِ لَتُرَدَّنَّ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهَا وَلَا يَكُونُ فِيهَا مَحْجَمَةُ دَمٍ، وَمَا أَرَى الْيَوْمَ شَيْئًا إِلَّا وَقَدْ عَلِمْتُهُ وَالنَّبِيُّ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - حَيٌّ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1210
> *English:* "Hudhayfa said: 'By God, it shall be turned back on its heels, and there shall not be in it a cupping-glass of blood; and I see nothing today but that I knew it already while the Prophet ﷺ was alive.'"

**عبرت:** A crisis that ends without blood is still a crisis, and the men who watched it knew exactly how narrow the margin was.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR40 · Five governors at Medina give five different answers
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights; five arrows in from the provinces.

**What happened:** The caliph called in his governors — Muawiya ؓ, Abd Allah b. Sad, Saeed b. al-As, Amr b. al-As ؓ and Abd Allah b. Amir — told them they were his counsellors, and set the problem before them. Ibn Amir advised occupying the discontented with campaigning until each man had nothing on his mind beyond his own saddle-sore and the lice in his own sheepskin. It is the first of five separate recommendations, and both our books give the list.

**The statement:**
> أَرَى لَكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْ تَشْغَلَهُمْ بِالْجِهَادِ عَنْكَ حَتَّى يَذِلُّوا لَكَ وَلَا يَكُونَ هِمَّةُ أَحَدِهِمْ إِلَّا فِي نَفْسِهِ وَمَا هُوَ فِيهِ مِنْ دُبُرِ دَابَّتِهِ وَقَمْلِ فَرْوَتِهُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1210
> *English:* "I think, Commander of the Faithful, that you should occupy them with campaigning away from you, until they submit to you and none of them has any concern except himself and what he is in — the sore on his mount's back and the lice in his sheepskin."

**عبرت:** Every adviser in the room proposed the remedy that suited his own province, which is what advisers do.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR41 · Saeed's advice, and the caliph's refusal of it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Saeed b. al-As gave the hard answer: cut the disease out, sever what you fear, every people has a foundation, and when it is destroyed they scatter. Al-Kamil records the caliph's reply in nine words, and it is a refusal: this is indeed the sound opinion, were it not for what is in it. Al-Bidaya reports the same counsel as advice to uproot the mischief-makers and cut off their last man. It was not taken.

**The statement:**
> وَقَالَ سَعِيدٌ: احْسِمْ عَنْكَ الدَّاءَ فَاقْطَعْ عَنْكَ الَّذِي تَخَافُ، إِنَّ لِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ قَاعِدَةً مَتَى تَهْلِكْ يَتَفَرَّقُوا وَلَا يَجْتَمِعْ لَهُمْ أَمْرٌ. فَقَالَ عُثْمَانُ: إِنَّ هَذَا هُوَ الرَّأْيُ لَوْلَا مَا فِيهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1210
> *English:* "Saeed said: 'Cauterise the disease away from yourself, and cut off from yourself what you fear. Every people has a foundation: when it perishes they scatter and no affair holds together for them.' Uthman said: 'This is indeed the right opinion, were it not for what is in it.'"

**عبرت:** The counsel a ruler refuses tells you as much about him as the one he takes.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR43 · He said it for the man at the door
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

By God, he told the caliph, you are dearer to me than that; but I knew there was someone at the door who reports to the people what each of us says, and I wanted my words to reach them so that they would trust me, and I could then lead good to you and push harm away from you. ### TGA/E-GR44 · The caliph takes the mildest of the five counsels
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrows out from Medina to every province.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir sets out the counsels and then gives the decision. Uthman ؓ confirmed his governors in their posts, won the discontented over with money, and ordered men to be sent out on campaign to the frontiers. He rejected the proposal to break the agitation by force and the proposal to ignore it. Ibn Kathir's own summary of the decision is that he combined all the benefits together.

**The statement:**
> فعند ذلك قرَّر عثمانُ عمالَه على ما كانوا عليه، وتألَّف قلوبَ أولئك بالمال، وأمر بأن يُبعثوا إلى الغزو إلى الثغور، فجمع بين المصالح كلها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3456
> *English:* "Thereupon Uthman confirmed his governors in what they had been in, and won over the hearts of those people with money, and ordered that they be sent out to campaign on the frontiers — so he combined all the benefits together."

**عبرت:** A ruler who takes the mildest advice in the room has still made a decision, and will still be held to it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR45 · Abu Dharr ؓ quarrelled about hoarding, not the caliph
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Damascus lights.

**What happened:** Abu Dharr ؓ held that a Muslim should not own more than a day and a night's food, or what he spends in the way of God, or what he keeps for a guest, and he took the verse of Sura al-Tawba on those who hoard gold and silver in its plain sense and as binding on everyone. He stood up in Syria and told the rich to share with the poor, in the words of the verse. Al-Kamil says he kept at it until the poor were repeating it and treating it as an obligation on the rich, and the rich complained of what they were getting from them. The dispute was about property, and it started in a sermon.

**The statement:**
> فَكَانَ يَقُومُ بِالشَّامِ وَيَقُولُ: يَا مَعْشَرَ الْأَغْنِيَاءِ وَاسُوا الْفُقَرَاءَ، بَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنْفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِمَكَاوٍ مِنْ نَارٍ تُكْوَى بِهَا جِبَاهُهُمْ وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ، فَمَا زَالَ حَتَّى وَلِعَ الْفُقَرَاءُ بِمِثْلِ ذَلِكَ وَأَوْجَبُوهُ عَلَى الْأَغْنِيَاءِ، وَشَكَا الْأَغْنِيَاءُ مَا يَلْقَوْنَ مِنْهُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1174
> *English:* "He used to stand up in Syria and say: 'People of wealth, share with the poor! Give tidings to those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God of brands of fire with which their foreheads and their sides and their backs will be branded.' And he kept on until the poor became eager for the like of that and imposed it as a duty on the rich, and the rich complained of what they met from them."

**عبرت:** A man may be entirely sincere, entirely pious, and still be pressing a reading of the law that the community has not adopted.

**Hands-up?** Hands up if you have heard that Abu Dharr ؓ was exiled for opposing the caliph. Keep your hand up; we are going to read what the books actually say.

---

### TGA/E-GR46 · The test of a thousand dinars, sent by night
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Damascus lights.

**What happened:** Muawiya ؓ sent him a thousand dinars in the dark, and Abu Dharr ؓ spent the whole sum. In the morning Muawiya ؓ sent his messenger back with a story: save my body from Muawiya's punishment, I was sent to somebody else and I gave them to you by mistake. Abu Dharr ؓ answered that there was not a dinar of them left in the house, and asked for three days to gather them. Al-Kamil says that when Muawiya ؓ saw that the man's practice confirmed his preaching, he wrote to the caliph.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو ذَرٍّ: يَا بُنَيَّ قُلْ لَهُ: وَاللَّهِ مَا أَصْبَحَ عِنْدَنَا مِنْ دَنَانِيرِكَ دِينَارٌ وَلَكِنْ أَخِّرْنَا ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ حَتَّى نَجْمَعَهَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1174
> *English:* "Abu Dharr said to him: 'My son, say to him: by God, not a dinar of your dinars has remained with us this morning; but give us three days' grace until we can gather them.'"

**عبرت:** A man whose life matches his preaching is a much harder problem for an administration than a hypocrite.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR47 · Ibn al-Athir refuses the ugly versions outright
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** This is the single most valuable sentence in the whole strand. Opening the chapter on Abu Dharr ؓ's move to al-Rabadha, Ibn al-Athir lists the reports in circulation — that Muawiya ؓ abused him, threatened him with death, carried him from Syria to Medina without a saddle-pad, and that he was expelled from Medina in a disgraceful manner — and says flatly that the transmission of it is not sound. He adds that even had it been sound, an excuse would have to be made for the caliph, because an imam may discipline his subjects.

**The statement:**
> وَقَدْ ذُكِرَ فِي سَبَبِ ذَلِكَ أُمُورٌ كَثِيرَةٌ، مِنْ سَبِّ مُعَاوِيَةَ إِيَّاهُ وَتَهْدِيدِهِ بِالْقَتْلِ، وَحَمْلِهِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ مِنَ الشَّامِ بِغَيْرِ وِطَاءٍ، وَنَفْيِهِ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ عَلَى الْوَجْهِ الشَّنِيعِ، لَا يَصِحُّ النَّقْلُ بِهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1173
> *English:* "And many things have been mentioned as the cause of that — of Muawiya's reviling him and threatening him with killing, and carrying him from Syria to Medina without a saddle-pad, and banishing him from Medina in the disgraceful manner — the transmission of which is not sound."

**عبرت:** A report can be famous, detailed and vivid and still fail the test of transmission, and the historian who says so is doing his job.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR48 · And then says why he left them out
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn al-Athir finishes the thought on the next page. Such material, he says, belongs among the excuses that may be offered, not among things to be made into a means of attacking the caliph — and then he says in two words that he disliked mentioning them. A speaker who is pressed from the floor about the Abu Dharr ؓ affair can read this sentence out and stop there, because it is the position of the book itself.

**The statement:**
> لَا أَنْ يُجْعَلَ ذَلِكَ سَبَبًا لِلطَّعْنِ عَلَيْهِ، كَرِهْتُ ذِكْرَهَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1174
> *English:* "— not that it should be made a cause for attacking him. I disliked to mention them."

**عبرت:** There is a difference between not knowing a story and choosing not to repeat it, and the tradition respects the second.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR49 · The sedition has put out its muzzle
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrow from Medina to Damascus.

**What happened:** Muawiya ؓ wrote that Abu Dharr ؓ had made things difficult for him. The caliph's answer is one of the most quotable sentences of the decade: the sedition has put out its muzzle and its eyes, and nothing remains but for it to spring. So do not scratch the sore, he wrote; send Abu Dharr ؓ to me, send a guide with him, and restrain the people and yourself as much as you can.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّ الْفِتْنَةَ قَدْ أَخْرَجَتْ خَطْمَهَا وَعَيْنَيْهَا وَلَمْ يَبْقَ إِلَّا أَنْ تَثِبَ، فَلَا تَنْكَأِ الْقَرْحَ، وَجَهِّزْ أَبَا ذَرٍّ إِلَيَّ، وَابْعَثْ مَعَهُ دَلِيلًا وَكَفْكِفِ النَّاسَ وَنَفْسَكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1174
> *English:* "The sedition has put out its muzzle and its eyes, and nothing remains but that it spring. So do not scratch the sore. Equip Abu Dharr to come to me, and send a guide with him, and restrain the people and yourself as much as you can."

**عبرت:** A ruler who can see the thing coming and still cannot stop it is the ordinary condition of government.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR50 · I cannot compel men to renounce
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** The meeting between them is short and neither man gives way. The caliph said his duty was to discharge what was owed and to call the people to effort and moderation, and that it was not his duty to compel them to renunciation. Abu Dharr ؓ answered that they should not be satisfied with the rich until they gave generously, treated neighbours and brothers well and kept ties of kinship. Both positions are on the page, and neither is described as an offence.

**The statement:**
> يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ عَلَيَّ أَنْ أَقْضِيَ مَا عَلَيَّ، وَأَنْ أَدْعُوَ الرَّعِيَّةَ إِلَى الِاجْتِهَادِ وَالِاقْتِصَادِ، وَمَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ أُجْبِرَهُمْ عَلَى الزُّهْدِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1175
> *English:* "Abu Dharr, it is upon me to discharge what is upon me, and to call the subjects to striving and moderation; it is not upon me to compel them to renunciation."

**عبرت:** The state is responsible for what is owed, and piety beyond what is owed cannot be collected by an official.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR51 · Abu Dharr ؓ asks for al-Rabadha and is given it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Al-Rabadha, east of Medina, lights.

**What happened:** In al-Kamil the move is his own request, and the reason he gives is a hadith. He asked leave of the caliph to go out of Medina, because the Messenger of God ﷺ had ordered him to leave when the building reached Sal. Leave was given, he settled at al-Rabadha and built a mosque there, and the caliph assigned him a herd of camels, gave him two slaves and set a daily allowance on him — and did the same for Rafi b. Khadij ؓ, who had also left Medina for something he had heard.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ لِعُثْمَانَ: تَأْذَنُ لِي فِي الْخُرُوجِ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - أَمَرَنِي بِالْخُرُوجِ مِنْهَا إِذَا بَلَغَ الْبِنَاءُ سَلْعًا. فَأَذِنَ لَهُ، فَنَزَلَ الرَّبَذَةَ وَبَنَى بِهَا مَسْجِدًا، وَأَقْطَعَهُ عُثْمَانُ صِرْمَةً مِنَ الْإِبِلِ، وَأَعْطَاهُ مَمْلُوكَيْنِ وَأَجْرَى عَلَيْهِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ عَطَاءً
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1175
> *English:* "Abu Dharr said to Uthman: 'Will you permit me to leave Medina? For the Messenger of God ﷺ ordered me to leave it when the building reached Sal.' So he permitted him, and he settled at al-Rabadha and built a mosque there; and Uthman granted him a herd of camels, and gave him two slaves, and set a daily allowance upon him."

**عبرت:** The same departure can be a banishment in one telling and a request granted in another, and the difference is exactly what a historian is for.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR52 · Al-Bidaya carries both versions of the move
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Al-Rabadha lights.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir gives the plain administrative version and the request version side by side. The caliph called him to Medina, reproached him for some of what had come from him, tried to bring him back and failed, and ordered him to stay at al-Rabadha. And it is said, he adds, that Abu Dharr ؓ himself asked to stay there on the strength of the hadith about the building reaching Sal. He also records the instruction that went with it: to keep visiting Medina, so that he should not revert to being a bedouin after his emigration.

**The statement:**
> ويقال إنه سأل عثمان أن يقيم (بها) وقال: إن رسول الله ﷺ قال (لي): "إذا بلغ البناء سلعا (٢) فاخرج منها" (٣) وقد بلغ البناء سلعًا، فأذن له عثمان بالمقام بالرَّبَذَة، وأمره أن يتعاهد المدينة في بعض الأحيان، حتى لا يرتدّ أعرابيًا بعد هِجْرتهِ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3440
> *English:* "And it is said that he asked Uthman to stay there, and said: 'The Messenger of God ﷺ said to me: when the building reaches Sal, go out of it' — and the building had reached Sal. So Uthman permitted him to stay at al-Rabadha, and ordered him to keep visiting Medina from time to time, so that he should not revert to being a bedouin after his emigration."

**عبرت:** A ruler who removes a man and still guards his standing is not doing the same thing as a ruler who casts him out.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR53 · In Siyar he simply asks leave
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Al-Dhahabi carries a short account from Abd Allah b. al-Samit, who went in with Abu Dharr ؓ and a party of Ghifar to see the caliph by a door not used for entry. Abu Dharr ؓ greeted him and began with nothing except a question: do you reckon me one of them, Commander of the Faithful? By God I am not one of them and I shall not overtake them. Then he asked leave to go to al-Rabadha. The edition marks the chain of this report as men who are trustworthy.

**The statement:**
> أَحَسِبْتَنِي مِنْهُم يَا أَمِيْرَ المُؤْمِنِيْنَ؟ وَاللهِ مَا أَنَا مِنْهُم، وَلاَ أُدْرِكُهُمْ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۲ ص۶۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2040
> *English:* "Do you reckon me one of them, Commander of the Faithful? By God, I am not one of them, nor shall I overtake them."

**عبرت:** The man himself denied being part of the faction that later claimed him, and he denied it to the caliph's face.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR54 · Umm Dharr ؓ denies that he was banished
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Abu Dharr ؓ's own wife swore that Uthman ؓ did not banish her husband to al-Rabadha, and she gave the same reason her husband gave: the Prophet ﷺ had told him to leave Medina when the building reached Sal. Al-Dhahabi puts her denial on the page without comment, in a chapter that has already carried every other version of the story. It is the plainest contradiction in our sources of the account most people have heard.

**The statement:**
> قَالَتْ أُمُّ ذَرٍّ: وَاللهِ مَا سَيَّرَ عُثْمَانُ أَبَا ذَرٍّ - تَعْنِي إِلَى الرَّبَذَةِ - وَلَكِنَّ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ -صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ- قَالَ: (إِذَا بَلَغَ البِنَاءُ سَلْعاً، فَاخْرُجْ مِنْهَا
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۲ ص۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2052
> *English:* "Umm Dharr said: 'By God, Uthman did not banish Abu Dharr' — meaning to al-Rabadha — 'but the Messenger of God ﷺ said: when the building reaches Sal, go out of it.'"

**عبرت:** The household of the man concerned is a witness, and in this case the household says no.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR55 · Al-Hasan al-Basri رحمہ اللہ is asked the question directly
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** On the same page al-Dhahabi records a second denial, from the next generation. Ghalib al-Qattan put the question to al-Hasan al-Basri رحمہ اللہ as plainly as it can be put: Abu Saeed, did Uthman ؓ expel Abu Dharr ؓ? The answer is two words. A speaker asked the same question from the floor can give the same two words and the page they are on.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: مَعَاذَ اللهِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۲ ص۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2052
> *English:* "He said: God forbid."

**عبرت:** The generation that came immediately after did not believe the story either, and said so when asked.

### TGA/E-GR56 · At al-Rabadha he refuses an offered banner
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Al-Rabadha lights.

**What happened:** Men from Kufa came out to him at al-Rabadha and made him an offer: this man has done such and such to you, so raise a banner and we will fill it out with as many fighters as you like. His answer is the reason this card exists. People of Islam, he said, do not put that to me, and do not humiliate the ruler — for whoever humiliates the ruler has no repentance. And he added that if the ruler crucified him on the longest beam, he would hear and be patient and count it better for himself.

**The statement:**
> يَا أَهْلَ الإِسْلاَمِ، لاَ تَعْرِضُوا عَلَيَّ ذَاكُم، وَلاَ تُذِلُّوا السُّلْطَانَ؛ فَإِنَّهُ مَنْ أَذَلَّ السُّلْطَانَ فَلاَ تَوْبَةَ لَهُ، وَاللهِ لَو صَلَبَنِي عَلَى أَطْوَلِ خَشَبَةٍ أَوْ حَبْلٍ لَسَمِعْتُ وَصَبَرْتُ، وَرَأَيْتُ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ لِي
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۲ ص۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2052
> *English:* "People of Islam, do not put that to me, and do not humiliate the ruler; for whoever humiliates the ruler has no repentance. By God, were he to crucify me on the longest beam or rope, I would hear and be patient, and I would hold that to be better for me."

**عبرت:** The man with the loudest grievance in the province refused to let it be turned into a rising, and said why.

**Hands-up?** Someone has offered you an army to right your wrong. What does a Companion do with that offer?

### TGA/E-GR57 · His daughter goes into the caliph's household
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Al-Rabadha lights, then Medina.

**What happened:** Abu Dharr ؓ died at al-Rabadha, facing the Kaaba, with a passing caravan to bury him and Abd Allah b. Masud ؓ weeping among them. His daughter came out and asked them to attend him. When word reached Medina, the caliph took his daughter into his own household, and said: may God have mercy on Abu Dharr and forgive him his settling at al-Rabadha. Al-Dhahabi carries the same fact in a single line.

**The statement:**
> فَضَمَّ ابْنَتَهُ إِلَى عِيَالِهِ وَقَالَ: يَرْحَمُ اللَّهُ أَبَا ذَرٍّ وَيَغْفِرُ لَهُ نُزُولَهُ الرَّبَذَةَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۰۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1195
> *English:* "So he took his daughter into his own dependents and said: 'May God have mercy on Abu Dharr and forgive him his settling at al-Rabadha.'"

**عبرت:** How a quarrel ends is part of the record of the quarrel, and this one ended with the dead man's daughter in the other man's house.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR58 · Al-Dhahabi records the same, in one line
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Siyar closes its notice on Abu Dharr ؓ with the same detail in the briefest possible form. It is worth having both books on the same fact, because this is the point at which a listener who has heard only the grievance version is most likely to stop and ask whether he has been told the whole thing.

**The statement:**
> وَقِيْلَ: إِنَّ أَبَا ذَرٍّ خَلَّفَ بِنْتاً لَهُ، فَضَمَّهَا عُثْمَانُ إِلَى عِيَالِهِ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۲ ص۷۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2054
> *English:* "And it is said that Abu Dharr left a daughter of his behind, and Uthman took her into his own dependents."

**عبرت:** Two independent books saying the same small thing is worth more than one book saying a large one.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR59 · Hudhayfa ؓ comes back from the frontier alarmed
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Armenia and Azerbaijan, then Kufa.

**What happened:** The standardised codex began with a soldier's report. Hudhayfa ؓ came back from campaign and told Saeed b. al-As what he had seen: if the people were left alone they would differ over the Quran and never afterwards stand upon it. He had seen men of Homs claiming their reading was better than everyone else's because they took it from al-Miqdad ؓ; the people of Damascus saying the same; the people of Kufa saying it because they read with Ibn Masud ؓ; the people of Basra saying it because they read with Abu Musa ؓ. He rode to the caliph and called himself the naked warner.

**The statement:**
> لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ فِي سَفْرَتِي هَذِهِ أَمْرًا، لَئِنْ تُرِكَ النَّاسُ لَيَخْتَلِفُنَّ فِي الْقُرْآنِ، ثُمَّ لَا يَقُومُونَ عَلَيْهِ أَبَدًا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1172
> *English:* "I have seen on this journey of mine a matter such that, if the people are left alone, they will surely differ over the Quran and then never stand upon it again."

**عبرت:** The problem was not that men read differently; it was that they had begun to rank each other by it.

### TGA/E-GR60 · One codex to every horizon, and the rest burned
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrows out from Medina to Kufa, Basra, Damascus.

**What happened:** The caliph gathered the Companions, they all saw what Hudhayfa ؓ saw, and the sheets collected in Abu Bakr ؓ's time and kept by Hafsa ؓ were sent for and copied. Zayd b. Thabit ؓ, Abd Allah b. al-Zubayr ؓ, Saeed b. al-As and Abd al-Rahman b. al-Harith did the work, with the instruction that where they differed they should write in the tongue of Quraysh. The sheets went back to Hafsa ؓ, a codex went to every horizon, and what was besides it was burned. Al-Kamil says every man knew the merit of this act except some of the people of Kufa.

**The statement:**
> وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى كُلِّ أُفُقٍ بِمُصْحَفٍ، وَحَرَقَ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ، وَأَمَرَ أَنْ يَعْتَمِدُوا عَلَيْهَا وَيَدَعُوا مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ. فَكُلُّ النَّاسِ عَرَفَ فَضْلَ هَذَا الْفِعْلِ، إِلَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1172
> *English:* "And he sent to every horizon a codex, and burned what was besides that, and ordered that they rely upon it and leave what was besides it. And every one of the people knew the merit of this act, except what came from the people of Kufa."

**عبرت:** The act that a later century treats as obviously right was contested in its own week by serious men.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR61 · Ibn Masud ؓ tells his own followers to stop
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** When the codex reached Kufa the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ there were glad of it, and the followers of Abd Allah b. Masud ؓ and those who agreed with them refused it and found fault with the people. Then Ibn Masud ؓ himself stood up among them and told them to stop: not all of that — you have been outstripped plainly, so keep within your own limp. The man whose reading was at issue closed the argument down himself.

**The statement:**
> فَقَامَ فِيهِمُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ وَقَالَ: وَلَا كُلُّ ذَلِكَ، فَإِنَّكُمْ وَاللَّهِ قَدْ سُبِقْتُمْ سَبْقًا بَيِّنًا، فَارْبِعُوا عَلَى ظَلْعِكُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1172
> *English:* "Then Ibn Masud stood up among them and said: 'Not all of that! For by God, you have been outstripped plainly, so keep within the measure of your own lameness.'"

**عبرت:** A leader who stops his own followers has done something harder than winning the argument.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR62 · Ali ؓ shouts down a critic of the codex
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Kufa lights.

**What happened:** When Ali ؓ came to Kufa a man stood up and criticised Uthman ؓ for gathering the people on one codex. Ali ؓ shouted at him and said the thing that closes the subject: be silent — he did that before an assembly of us, and had I been in charge of it as Uthman ؓ was, I would have followed the same road. This is the single most useful line in the whole strand for a speaker who does not want to adjudicate.

**The statement:**
> فَصَاحَ بِهِ وَقَالَ: اسْكُتْ فَعَنْ مَلَأٍ مِنَّا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ، فَلَوْ وُلِّيتُ مِنْهُ مَا وُلِّيَ عُثْمَانُ لَسَلَكْتُ سَبِيلَهُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1173
> *English:* "He shouted at him and said: 'Be silent! He did that before an assembly of us; and had I been put in charge of it as Uthman was put in charge of it, I would have followed his very road.'"

**عبرت:** The man the objectors invoked had already rejected their objection, in public, in their own city.

### TGA/E-GR63 · The Prophet ﷺ's ring falls into a well
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Two miles from Medina.

**What happened:** In the same year the seal-ring of the Messenger of God ﷺ slipped from Uthman ؓ's hand into the well of Aris, two miles outside Medina. He had worn it six years, after Abu Bakr ؓ and Umar ؓ had worn it until they died. They drew off the water and could not find it. He offered a great sum for it, grieved bitterly, and at last had another made on the same pattern and with the same inscription. Al-Kamil says the bottom of that well was never reached.

**The statement:**
> فَطَلَبُوهُ فِيهَا وَنَزَحُوا مَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ فَلَمْ يَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِ، فَجَعَلَ فِيهِ مَالًا عَظِيمًا لِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ، وَاغْتَمَّ لِذَلِكَ غَمًّا شَدِيدًا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1173
> *English:* "So they searched for it in the well and drew off the water that was in it, and could not find it; and he set a great sum for whoever should bring it, and he grieved over that with a severe grief."

**عبرت:** Some losses in a ruler's life are not political at all, and they are still felt.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR64 · The third call to prayer on Friday
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights; al-Zawra in the market.

**What happened:** One line in al-Kamil records an administrative decision that later appeared on the objectors' lists: in this year Uthman ؓ added the third call on Friday, given at al-Zawra, a place by the market of Medina near the mosque. Al-Bidaya records it in the same year and in almost the same words. It is the whole of what our books say about it here, and a speaker should not add to it.

**The statement:**
> فِي هَذِهِ السَّنَةِ زَادَ عُثْمَانُ النِّدَاءَ الثَّالِثَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ عَلَى الزَّوْرَاءِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۴۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1175
> *English:* "In this year Uthman added the third call to prayer on Friday, at al-Zawra."

**عبرت:** The city had grown past the range of one muadhdhin, and the answer to that was an administrative one.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR65 · Ibn Masud ؓ refuses his stipend twice
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Uthman ؓ came to visit Abd Allah b. Masud ؓ in his last illness and asked him what he complained of, what he desired, and whether he should send him a doctor. Then he offered to order his stipend paid — which he had left untouched for two years — and Ibn Masud ؓ said he had no need of it. The caliph said it would be for his daughters after him. The answer was a question about whether he feared poverty for them, and a hadith about reciting Sura al-Waqia every night.

> *English:* "He said: 'Shall I not order your stipend for you?' — and he had left it for two years — and he said: 'I have no need of it.'"

**عبرت:** A grievance about money can be entirely real and the man at the centre of it still refuse the money.

### TGA/E-GR66 · Who prayed over Ibn Masud ؓ is disputed
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** al-Baqi, Medina.

**What happened:** Abd Allah b. Masud ؓ left his affairs to al-Zubayr ؓ. Ibn Kathir then records three different reports about who led the funeral prayer over him — al-Zubayr ؓ by night, with Uthman ؓ afterwards reproaching him for it; or Uthman ؓ himself; or Ammar ؓ — and closes the question with the historian's formula. He was buried at al-Baqi at somewhat over sixty years of age. If our own books cannot settle who led one funeral prayer, a speaker should be slow to settle harder things.

**The statement:**
> فيقال إنه هو الذي صلى عليه ليلًا، ثمّ عاتب عثمانُ الزبير على ذلك، وقيل بل صلَّى عليه عثمان، وقيل عمَّار، فالله أعلم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3451
> *English:* "And it is said that it was he who prayed over him by night, and then Uthman reproached al-Zubayr for that; and it is said, rather, that Uthman prayed over him; and it is said, Ammar. And God knows best."

**عبرت:** God knows best is a conclusion, not an evasion, and it is the conclusion the sources actually support here.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR67 · Ammar ؓ refuses to ride out with Ali ؓ
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** When the Egyptian party neared Medina the caliph asked Ali ؓ to go out and turn them back, and told him to take Ammar b. Yasir ؓ with him. Ammar ؓ refused. The caliph then sent Sad b. Abi Waqqas ؓ to urge him, and he refused with every refusal. Ibn Kathir attributes his hardness to an earlier disciplinary matter. This card is recorded and not planned: it is an accusation against a Companion, it turns on a report Ibn Kathir gives in a single clause, and the guardrail applies.

**The statement:**
> فقال علي لعمار فأبى عمار أن يخرج معه، فبعث عثمان سعد بن أبي وقاص أن يذهب إلى عمار ليحرِّضه على الخروج مع علي إليه، فأبى عمار كلَّ الإباء، وامتنع أشدَّ الامتناع
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3461
> *English:* "So Ali spoke to Ammar, and Ammar refused to go out with him; so Uthman sent Sad b. Abi Waqqas to go to Ammar to urge him to go out with Ali to them, but Ammar refused with every refusal, and held back with the strongest holding back."

**عبرت:** Where the books record a Companion's refusal and then explain it by a quarrel, the explanation is a report and not a verdict.

**Hands-up?** no
