### TGA/E-GR68 · Five inspectors go out to the provinces
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Five arrows out of Medina.

**What happened:** When the letters of complaint had been circulating long enough to reach Medina from every direction, the people of Medina advised the caliph to send men he trusted to the provinces to come back with the news. He sent Muhammad b. Maslama ؓ to Kufa, Usama b. Zayd ؓ to Basra, Ammar b. Yasir ؓ to Egypt and Abd Allah b. Umar ؓ to Syria, and dispersed others besides. It is the closest thing in the whole strand to a commission of inquiry.

**The statement:**
> نُشِيرُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَبْعَثَ رِجَالًا مِمَّنْ تَثِقُ بِهِمْ إِلَى الْأَمْصَارِ حَتَّى يَرْجِعُوا إِلَيْكَ بِأَخْبَارِهِمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1215
> *English:* "We advise you to send men whom you trust to the great cities, so that they come back to you with their news."

**عبرت:** A ruler who sends for the facts before acting on a rumour is doing the thing the rumour did not expect.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR69 · Four return and report nothing to object to
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Four arrows back into Medina; one does not return.

**What happened:** They all came back before Ammar ؓ, and they all said the same thing: we have found nothing to object to, people, and neither the leading men of the Muslims nor their generality have objected to anything. Ammar ؓ did not come back, and they began to think he had been murdered. Then a letter arrived from Abd Allah b. Abi Sarh in Egypt saying that a group there had won him over and attached themselves to him, and naming them: Abd Allah b. al-Sawda, Khalid b. Muljam, Sawdan b. Humran and Kinana b. Bishr.

**The statement:**
> فَرَجَعُوا جَمِيعًا قَبْلَ عَمَّارٍ فَقَالُوا: مَا أَنْكَرْنَا شَيْئًا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ وَلَا أَنْكَرَهُ أَعْلَامُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَلَا عَوَامُّهُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1216
> *English:* "They all returned before Ammar and said: 'We have not objected to anything, people; nor have the eminent among the Muslims nor their generality objected to it.'"

**عبرت:** The complaint was loud in the letters and thin on the ground, and the inquiry that discovered this changed nobody's mind.

**Hands-up?** Four inspectors go out to four provinces. How many do you think came back with a complaint?

### TGA/E-GR70 · Bring your claim to me at the season
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrows out to every province; Mecca lights.

**What happened:** The caliph then wrote to all the great cities. He held his governors to meeting him at every pilgrimage season, he wrote; the people of Medina had reported to him that men were being insulted and beaten; so let anyone who claims any of that come to the season and take his right, whether it lies against him or against his governors. Or let them give it away as charity, for God rewards those who give charity. Al-Kamil records that when this was read out in the provinces the people wept and prayed for him.

**The statement:**
> فَمَنِ ادَّعَى شَيْئًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَلْيُوَافِ الْمَوْسِمَ يَأْخُذْ حَقَّهُ حَيْثُ كَانَ مِنِّي أَوْ مِنْ عُمَّالِي، أَوْ تَصَّدَّقُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْزِي الْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ. فَلَمَّا قُرِئَ فِي الْأَمْصَارِ بَكَى النَّاسُ وَدَعَوْا لِعُثْمَانَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1216
> *English:* "So whoever claims anything of that, let him come to the pilgrimage season and take his right, wherever it lies — from me or from my governors — or let them give it away as charity, for God rewards those who give charity. And when it was read out in the great cities, the people wept and prayed for Uthman."

**عبرت:** An offer of public redress against the ruler himself is a rare thing, and it was made in writing and read aloud in every city.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR71 · The governors are called to the season and questioned
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mecca lights.

**What happened:** He summoned the governors to meet him at the season, brought Saeed b. al-As and Amr ؓ in with them, and put it to them directly: what is this complaining and this rumour? By God, he said, I fear that what is said of you is true, and that nothing of it will be fastened on anyone but me. They answered that his own inspectors had gone out and come back and that nobody had spoken to them face to face about anything.

### TGA/E-GR72 · The door that is shut will be opened
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The caliph closed that meeting with the most sombre thing he says anywhere in this strand. Every affair has a door it is entered by, he said, and this affair that is feared for the community is coming, and the door that is shut on it will surely be opened. We hold it back with gentleness and accommodation, except in the limits set by God. Then he said: blessed is Uthman if he dies without having set it moving.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ الَّذِي يُخَافُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ كَائِنٌ، وَإِنَّ بَابَهُ الَّذِي يُغْلَقُ عَلَيْهِ لَيُفْتَحَنَّ فَنُكَفْكِفُهُ بِاللِّينِ وَالْمُؤَاتَاةِ إِلَّا فِي حُدُودِ اللَّهِ، فَإِنْ فُتِحَ فَلَا يَكُونُ لِأَحَدٍ عَلَيَّ حُجَّةُ حَقٍّ، وَقَدْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنِّي لَمْ آلُ النَّاسَ خَيْرًا، وَإِنَّ رَحَى الْفِتْنَةِ لَدَائِرَةٌ، فَطُوبَى لِعُثْمَانَ إِنْ مَاتَ وَلَمْ يُحَرِّكْهَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1216
> *English:* "This affair that is feared for this community is coming, and the door that is shut upon it shall surely be opened; so we hold it back with gentleness and accommodation, except in the limits of God. And if it is opened, then let no one have a true argument against me. God knows that I have not stinted the people of good. The millstone of sedition is turning: blessed is Uthman if he dies and has not set it moving."

**عبرت:** A man may see the thing coming, refuse to be the one who starts it, and still be the one it falls on.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR73 · He audits his own gifts before three Companions
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Back in Medina the caliph called in Ali ؓ, Talha ؓ and al-Zubayr ؓ and gave them an account of himself. His two predecessors, he said, had denied themselves and their own people for God's reward; the Messenger of God ﷺ used to give to his kin; and he was among a clan in poverty, so he had stretched out his hand in some of that. Then he offered them the audit: if you see that as an error, give it back. They named two sums — fifty thousand to Abd Allah b. Khalid b. Asid and fifteen thousand to Marwan — and those were taken back from the two men, and everyone left satisfied.

**The statement:**
> فَإِنْ رَأَيْتُمْ ذَلِكَ خَطَأً فَرُدُّوهُ فَأَمْرِي لِأَمْرِكُمْ تَبَعٌ. فَقَالُوا: قَدْ أَصَبْتَ وَأَحْسَنْتَ، قَدْ أَعْطَيْتَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ خَالِدِ بْنِ أَسِيدٍ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفًا، وَأَعْطَيْتَ مَرْوَانَ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ أَلْفًا. فَأُخِذَ مِنْهُمَا ذَلِكَ، فَرَضُوا وَخَرَجُوا رَاضِينَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1217
> *English:* "'So if you see that to be an error, then give it back — my affair follows your affair.' They said: 'You have done right and done well. You gave Abd Allah b. Khalid b. Asid fifty thousand, and you gave Marwan fifteen thousand.' So that was taken from the two of them, and they were satisfied and went out satisfied."

**عبرت:** A ruler who opens his own accounts to his critics has changed the argument from suspicion to arithmetic.

### TGA/E-GR74 · He refuses a Syrian guard, twice
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights; Damascus greyed out.

**What happened:** Muawiya ؓ put two offers to the caliph before riding home. Come out with me to Syria, where the people are still in obedience, before someone falls on you whom you cannot face. Uthman ؓ answered that he would not sell the neighbourhood of the Messenger of God ﷺ for anything, even if it cost him his neck. Then send you a body of troops from Syria to stay with you against any emergency? He answered that he would not crowd the neighbours of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Muawiya ؓ told him he would be assassinated, and he answered with a verse.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: فَإِنْ بَعَثْتُ إِلَيْكَ جُنْدًا مِنْهُمْ يُقِيمُ مَعَكَ لِنَائِبَةٍ إِنْ نَابَتْ؟ قَالَ: لَا أُضَيِّقُ عَلَى جِيرَانِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ -. فَقَالَ: وَاللَّهِ لَتُغْتَالَنَّ وَلَتُغْزَيَنَّ! فَقَالَ: حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1217
> *English:* "He said: 'And if I send you an army of them to stay with you for any emergency that may befall?' He said: 'I will not straiten the neighbours of the Messenger of God ﷺ.' He said: 'By God, you will be assassinated, and you will be raided!' He said: 'God is enough for me, and He is the best trustee.'"

**عبرت:** There are protections a man may refuse because of what accepting them would cost the people around him.

**Hands-up?** He is offered an army to guard him. Do you think he took it?

### TGA/E-GR75 · Al-Bidaya reports the same refusal, and the same answer
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir gives the same two offers with the same two refusals, and attributes the account to Sayf b. Umar and others by name. The wording of the second refusal in his telling is that he feared to crowd the city of the Messenger of God ﷺ against its own people, the Emigrants and the Helpers. Having the same refusal in two of our books, in different words, is what lets the speaker state it as a fact rather than as a story.

**The statement:**
> فقال: أجَهّز لك جيشًا من الشام يكونون (٤) عندك ينصرونك؟ فقال: إني أخشى أن أضيِّق بهم بلد رسول الله ﷺ على أصحابه من المهاجرين والأنصار. قال معاوية: فوالله يا أمير المؤمنين لتُغْتالن -أو قال: لتُغْزَين- فقال عثمان: حسبي الله ونعم الوكيل
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3459
> *English:* "He said: 'Shall I equip an army for you from Syria to be with you and support you?' He said: 'I fear that I would straiten the city of the Messenger of God ﷺ with them against his companions of the Emigrants and the Helpers.' Muawiya said: 'By God, Commander of the Faithful, you will be assassinated' — or he said: 'you will be raided.' Uthman said: 'God is enough for me, and He is the best trustee.'"

**عبرت:** Two books, two wordings, one decision — that is what a corroborated fact looks like.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR76 · Muawiya ؓ's parting words to the Emigrants
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** On his way out of Medina, still in travelling clothes, Muawiya ؓ stopped before a group of the Emigrants that included Ali ؓ, Talha ؓ and al-Zubayr ؓ, and gave them a warning. Men used to contend for this authority until God sent His Prophet ﷺ, he said, and then they excelled one another by precedence and effort; if they hold to that, the affair is theirs; if they seek the world by contending, it will be stripped from them and God will give it to others. Then he told them he had left an old man among them, and asked them to take good care of him.

**The statement:**
> وَإِنِّي قَدْ خَلَفْتُ فِيكُمْ شَيْخًا فَاسْتَوْصُوا بِهِ خَيْرًا وَكَانِفُوهُ تَكُونُوا أَسْعَدَ مِنْهُ بِذَلِكَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1218
> *English:* "And I have left an old man among you, so take good care of him and stand by him, and you will be the happier for it than he."

**عبرت:** A warning given openly, before witnesses, to the men who would later be in the middle of everything.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR77 · Kufa and Syria first quarrel over a command
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Balanjar, on the Caspian frontier.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir dates the first split between the people of Kufa and the people of Syria to a command dispute on the Caspian frontier. Abd al-Rahman b. Rabia was killed at Balanjar and Salman b. Rabia was appointed over the sector; the caliph reinforced them with Syrians under Habib b. Maslama, and the two men fell out over who was in charge. A Kufan poet put the quarrel into three verses. The two halves of the army that would divide the community had already discovered each other.

**The statement:**
> فتنازع حبيب وسلمان في الإمرة حتى اختلفا، فكان أولَ اختلافٍ وقعَ بين أهل الكوفة وأهل الشام
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3446
> *English:* "So Habib and Salman disputed over the command until they fell out; and that was the first disagreement that occurred between the people of Kufa and the people of Syria."

**عبرت:** A quarrel over precedence on a distant frontier can outlive the campaign that caused it by a generation.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR78 · A governor corrected in public over a small thing
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Nishapur, then Medina.

**What happened:** Abd Allah b. Amir had taken Fars, Kirman, Sijistan and most of Khurasan, and someone told him that no man had been given openings like his. He answered that he would make his thanks to God by entering the state of ihram for an umra from where he stood — and he entered ihram from Nishapur. When he came before the caliph, Uthman ؓ reproached him for it. The most successful governor of the reign was corrected for an excess of piety.

**The statement:**
> فأحرمَ بعمرة من نيسابور، فلما قدم على عثمان لامه على إحرامه من خراسان
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3447
> *English:* "So he entered ihram for an umra from Nishapur; and when he came before Uthman, he blamed him for his entering ihram from Khurasan."

**عبرت:** A ruler who corrects his best governor over a small thing is not a ruler who was indulging his governors.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR79 · Egypt sets out in the dress of pilgrims
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Fustat, then the road north to Medina.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir says a group grew up in Egypt, among the sons of Companions, who stirred the people up against the caliph, and that the weight of it rested on Muhammad b. Abi Bakr and Muhammad b. Abi Hudhayfa. They raised about six hundred riders who went to Medina in the guise of pilgrims in the month of Rajab, in four companies, under Amr b. Budayl b. Warqa al-Khuzai, Abd al-Rahman b. Udays al-Balawi, Kinana b. Bishr al-Tujibi and Sawdan b. Humran al-Sakuni. The governor wrote ahead to warn Medina they were coming.

**The statement:**
> حتى استنفرا (٣) نحوًا من ستمئة راكب يذهبون إلى المدينة في صفة معتمرين في شهر رجب، لينكروا على عثمان
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3461
> *English:* "Until the two of them roused about six hundred riders to go to Medina in the guise of men performing umra, in the month of Rajab, to object against Uthman."

**عبرت:** A body of men can travel a thousand miles in the dress of pilgrims and still be doing something else.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR80 · How many came, and the books disagree
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the Egyptians came the second time, in Shawwal, Ibn Kathir gives the numbers in the form the historians use when they cannot settle it: the one who gives the lower figure says six hundred, the one who gives the higher says a thousand. Al-Kamil, describing the same party, says five hundred, and it is said, a thousand. The speaker should give the range and not a figure.

**The statement:**
> المُقَلِّلُ لهم يقول ستمئة، والمُكْثِرُ يقول: ألف
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3465
> *English:* "The one who reckons them fewer says six hundred; the one who reckons them more says a thousand."

**عبرت:** A crowd is always counted twice, and the two counts are part of what we know about it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR81 · Three cities, three different men they wanted instead
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Fustat, Kufa and Basra light in three colours; Medina at the centre.

**What happened:** This is the single fact that shows the movement was not one movement. Al-Kamil says that the Basrans' inclination was towards Talha ؓ, the Kufans' towards al-Zubayr ؓ, and the Egyptians' towards Ali ؓ. Al-Bidaya says exactly the same thing in its own words, adding that each party did not doubt that its own affair would be completed. Three provinces marched on the same city in the same month wanting three different successors.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ هَوَاهُمْ فِي طَلْحَةَ، وَتَقَدَّمَ نَاسٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ، وَكَانَ هَوَاهُمْ فِي الزُّبَيْرِ، وَتَرَكُوا الْأَعْوَصَ، وَجَاءَهُمْ نَاسٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ مِصْرَ، وَكَانَ هَوَاهُمْ فِي عَلِيٍّ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1218
> *English:* "And their inclination was towards Talha; and some people of Kufa came forward, and their inclination was towards al-Zubayr, and they left al-Awas; and people of Egypt came to them, and their inclination was towards Ali."

**عبرت:** A coalition that has agreed on whom to remove and not on whom to install has not agreed on anything.

**Hands-up?** Three provinces march on the capital together. How many candidates do you think they brought between them?

---

### TGA/E-GR82 · Al-Bidaya says the same, and says nobody doubted
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir gives the same three-way split and adds the detail that makes it intelligible: not one of the three groups doubted that its own affair would be completed. Each had travelled with a private certainty. That is why the coalition held together on the road and came apart the moment it had to decide anything.

**The statement:**
> وأهل مصر مصرون على ولاية علي بن أبي طالب، وأهل الكوفة عازمون على تأمير الزُّبير، وأهل البصرة مصممون على تولية طلحة. لا تشكّ كلّ فرقةٍ أن أمرها سيتمّ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3465
> *English:* "The people of Egypt were set on the appointment of Ali b. Abi Talib, the people of Kufa were resolved on making al-Zubayr commander, and the people of Basra were determined on appointing Talha — no one of the parties doubting that its own affair would be brought to completion."

**عبرت:** Certainty is cheap on the road and expensive at the destination.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR83 · Ali ؓ turns them back at al-Juhfa
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Al-Juhfa, on the road south-west of Medina.

**What happened:** As the Egyptians came close the caliph asked Ali ؓ to go out and send them home before they entered Medina. Ali ؓ went to them at al-Juhfa. Ibn Kathir says they used to hold him in the highest regard, and that he turned them back, rebuked them and reviled them, and they blamed themselves, saying: this is the man on whose account you fight the commander, and by whom you argue against him. Then he asked them what they held against the caliph.

**The statement:**
> فردَّهم وأنَّبهم وشَتَمهم، فرجعوا على أنفسهم بالملامة، وقالوا: هذا الذي تحاربون الأمير بسببه، وتحتجون عليه (٧) به
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3461
> *English:* "So he turned them back and rebuked them and reviled them, and they turned upon themselves with blame and said: 'This is the man on whose account you fight the commander and by whom you argue against him.'"

**عبرت:** The man a movement claims for itself is not always willing to be claimed.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR84 · The six things they held against him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Asked what they objected to, they gave a list, and Ibn Kathir prints it. He had made a protected pasture; he had burned the codices; he had prayed the full prayer at Mecca instead of shortening it; he had appointed young men to office and passed over the senior Companions; and he had given Banu Umayya more than other people. This is the whole charge sheet as our own book states it. A seventh item, the sheltering of al-Hakam b. Abi al-As, is raised separately.

**The statement:**
> الحمى (١)، وأنَّه حرقَ المصاحف وأنّه أتم الصلاة، وأنه ولَّى الأحداث (الولايات وترك الصحابة الأكابر) وأعطى (٢) بني أمية أكثر من الناس.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3462
> *English:* "The protected pasture; and that he burned the codices; and that he prayed the full prayer; and that he appointed young men (to the governorships and passed over the senior Companions); and that he gave Banu Umayya more than other people."

**عبرت:** A charge sheet read out in full is usually smaller than the anger attached to it.

**Hands-up?** Five complaints. Keep count on your fingers; we are about to hear all five answered.

---

### TGA/E-GR85 · Ali ؓ answers all of them, point by point
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Ali ؓ answered the list item by item on the caliph's behalf and in front of the men who had brought it. The pasture was protected for the camels of the alms, to fatten them, not for his own animals, and Umar ؓ had protected it before him. What was burned was what had been disputed; what was agreed upon in the final review was kept. The full prayer at Mecca was because he had taken a household there and intended residence. And as for the young men, he appointed none but an upright man — and the Prophet ﷺ had appointed Attab b. Asid at twenty, and Usama b. Zayd ؓ over men who objected.

**The statement:**
> فأجاب علي (٣) عن ذلك: أما الحمى فإنما حماه لإبل الصدقة لتسمن، ولم يَحْمِهِ لإبله ولا لغنمه، وقد حماه عمر من قبله.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3462
> *English:* "And Ali answered concerning that: 'As for the protected pasture, he protected it only for the camels of the alms, that they might grow fat; he did not protect it for his own camels nor for his sheep; and Umar had protected it before him.'"

**عبرت:** The best answer to a list of grievances is a list of answers, given in public, by somebody the complainants respect.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR86 · And the answer about giving to his own clan
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The last item on the list was the one that had the most force behind it: that he preferred his own people, Banu Umayya. Ali ؓ answered it too, and the answer is startling enough that a room will remember it. The Messenger of God ﷺ, he said, used to prefer Quraysh over other people; and then he swore that if the key of Paradise were in his hand he would let Banu Umayya into it.

**The statement:**
> وأما إيثارُهُ قومَه بني أمية فقد كان رسول الله ﷺ يُؤْثِر قريشًا على الناس، وواللهِ لو أن مفتاحَ الجنة بيدي لأدخلتُ بني أمية إليها.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3462
> *English:* "And as for his preferring his own people, Banu Umayya: the Messenger of God ﷺ used to prefer Quraysh over the people; and by God, if the key of Paradise were in my hand I would let Banu Umayya into it."

**عبرت:** Words spoken in one decade are quoted in the next by men who would rather they had not been.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR87 · The objection about al-Hakam b. Abi al-As
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Taif.

**What happened:** They also objected that he had taken in al-Hakam b. Abi al-As, whom the Messenger of God ﷺ had banished to Taif. The answer given, as Ibn Kathir records it, is that the Prophet ﷺ had banished him to Taif and then brought him back. The book states the objection and states the reply, and does not adjudicate between them; neither should a speaker.

**The statement:**
> وعتبوا عليه في إيوائه الحَكم بن أبي العاص، وقد نفاه رسول الله ﷺ إلى الطائف، فذكر أن رسول الله ﷺ كان قد نفاه إلى الطائف ثمَّ ردَّه، ثمَّ نفاه إليها، فال: فقد نفاه رسول الله ﷺ ثم رَدَّه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3462
> *English:* "And they reproached him for sheltering al-Hakam b. Abi al-As, whom the Messenger of God ﷺ had banished to Taif. He mentioned that the Messenger of God ﷺ had banished him to Taif, then brought him back, then banished him to it. He said: 'The Messenger of God ﷺ banished him, then brought him back.'"

**عبرت:** Where the book gives an objection and a reply and stops, the reader's job is to stop too.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR88 · He states his case with the Companions as witnesses
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina, the Prophet's Mosque ﷺ.

**What happened:** It is related that the caliph then addressed the people with all of this, in the presence of the Companions, calling them to witness as he went, and they bore witness for him where there was witness to be borne. A party of the delegation was present. When the excuses had been accepted and the objections cleared away, a group of the Companions advised him to punish the men. He pardoned them, let them go, and sent them back to their own people, and they went away disappointed.

**The statement:**
> أشار جماعة من الصحابة على عثمان بتأديبهم فصفح عنهم [وتركهم]، ﵁. وردَّهم إلى قومهم، فرجعوا خائبين من حيث أتوا، ولم ينالوا شيئًا مما كانوا أمَّلوا وراموا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3462
> *English:* "A group of the Companions advised Uthman to discipline them, but he pardoned them [and left them], may God be pleased with him, and sent them back to their own people; and they went back disappointed from whence they came, and did not attain anything of what they had hoped for and aimed at."

**عبرت:** Clemency offered from strength is still clemency, and it does not always end an agitation.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR89 · Ali ؓ advises a public apology
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Ali ؓ came back to the caliph, told him the men had gone and had heard him, and then advised him to preach a sermon to the people apologising for any favouritism that had occurred towards some of his relatives, calling them to witness that he had repented of it and would keep to the practice of the two shaykhs before him, as in the first six years. Ibn Kathir records the response in six words: he listened to this counsel and met it with hearing and obedience.

**The statement:**
> فاستمع عثمان هذه النصيحة، وقابلها بالسمع والطاعة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3462
> *English:* "So Uthman listened to this counsel and met it with hearing and obedience."

**عبرت:** Advice is only advice until it is acted on, and acting on it in public is a different thing again.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR90 · The repentance from the pulpit, and a city weeping
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina, the Prophet's Mosque ﷺ.

**What happened:** On the Friday he raised his hands in the middle of the sermon and asked God's forgiveness, saying he was the first to repent of what had come from him. He wept, and Ibn Kathir says the Muslims wept with him, every one of them, and a great tenderness came over the people for their imam. He called them to witness against himself that he would keep to what the two shaykhs, Abu Bakr ؓ and Umar ؓ, had kept to, and that he had thrown his door open to anyone who wished to come in.

**The statement:**
> وأرسل عينيه بالبكاء فبكى المسلمون أجمعون، وحصل للناس رقة شديدة على إمامهم، وأشهد عثمان الناس على نفسه بذلك، وأنه قد لزم ما كان عليه الشيخان، أبو بكر وعمر ﵄، وأنه قد سبل (١) بابه لمن أراد الدخول عليه، لا يمنع أحد من ذلك
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3463
> *English:* "And he let his eyes run with weeping, and all the Muslims wept, and a great tenderness came upon the people for their imam; and Uthman called the people to witness against himself concerning that, and that he had held to what the two shaykhs, Abu Bakr and Umar, had been upon, and that he had thrown open his door to whoever wished to come in to him, none being prevented from that."

**عبرت:** A public repentance costs a ruler more than a public defence, and he made it anyway.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR91 · Al-Kamil adds that he would set Marwan aside
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Ibn al-Athir's text of the same sermon carries an undertaking that al-Bidaya's does not. I am the first to take the admonition, he said; I ask God's forgiveness for what I have done and I repent to Him; one such as I withdraws and repents. Let your nobles come to me when I step down and give me their opinion. And by God, I will give you satisfaction, and I will set Marwan and his people aside, and I will not veil myself from you. The people wept until their beards were wet, and he wept with them.

**The statement:**
> فَوَاللَّهِ لَأُعْطِيَنَّكُمُ الرِّضَا وَلَأُنَحِّيَنَّ مَرْوَانَ وَذَوِيهِ، وَلَا أَحْتَجِبُ عَنْكُمْ! فَرَقَّ النَّاسُ وَبَكَوْا حَتَّى أَخْضَلُوا لِحَاهُمْ وَبَكَى هُوَ أَيْضًا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1222
> *English:* "By God, I will give you satisfaction, and I will set Marwan and his people aside, and I will not veil myself from you! And the people softened and wept until their beards were wet, and he wept too."

**عبرت:** The promise that would have settled the matter was made out loud, in the mosque, in front of everyone.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR92 · The edition marks the chain of that sermon
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The text of the sermon in al-Bidaya comes through al-Waqidi, and the printed edition attaches a footnote to the hadith quoted inside it saying that this is from al-Waqidi's transmission and that he is abandoned by the hadith scholars. The note is the editor's, not Ibn Kathir's, and it is reproduced here because it is the kind of thing that decides how firmly a speaker may state a detail. The repentance itself is in both our books; the exact wording rests on a weak chain.

**The statement:**
none in the sources we use

**عبرت:** Knowing which parts of a scene rest on a weak chain is what lets you narrate the rest with confidence.

### TGA/E-GR93 · Amr b. al-As ؓ calls out from the floor
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Al-Kamil places Amr b. al-As ؓ in the congregation for that sermon. Fear God, Uthman, he called out; you have ridden into difficult places and we rode into them with you, so repent to God and we will repent. The caliph's answer from the pulpit was sharp and personal, and named the grudge he thought was behind it: your cloak has been crawling since I dismissed you from office. Then a voice from another quarter called out, repent to God — and he raised his hands and said: O God, I am the first to repent.

**The statement:**
> فَنَادَاهُ عُثْمَانُ: وَإِنَّكَ هُنَالِكَ يَا ابْنَ النَّابِغَةِ! قَمِلَتْ وَاللَّهِ جُبَّتُكَ مُنْذُ عَزَلْتُكَ عَنِ الْعَمَلِ! فَنُودِيَ مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى: تُبْ إِلَى اللَّهِ. فَرَفَعَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَالَ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَوَّلُ تَائِبٍ!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1222
> *English:* "Uthman called out to him: 'Are you there too, son of al-Nabigha? By God, your cloak has been crawling with lice since I dismissed you from office!' Then a call came from another side: 'Repent to God!' So he raised his hands and said: 'O God, I am the first to repent!'"

**عبرت:** A ruler can be provoked in public and still do the right thing in the same minute.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR94 · Saeed b. Zayd ؓ says carry it through
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** When the people had wept, Saeed b. Zayd ؓ stood up and said the one thing that mattered at that moment: Commander of the Faithful, God, God, in your own case — carry through what you have said. He was asking him to hold to the undertaking. Within the hour the caliph was at home, in a room full of his own relatives, being argued out of it.

**The statement:**
> وقام إليه سعيد بن زيد فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين! الله الله في نفسك! فأتمم على ما قلت

> *English:* "And Saeed b. Zayd rose to him and said: 'Commander of the Faithful! God, God, in your own self! Carry through what you have said.'"

**عبرت:** The hardest part of a public undertaking is the first private conversation afterwards.

### TGA/E-GR95 · Naila bint al-Farafisa ؓ tells Marwan to be silent
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Inside the caliph's house.

**What happened:** Marwan b. al-Hakam asked leave to speak. From behind the curtain the caliph's wife Naila bint al-Farafisa ؓ answered before her husband could: no, be silent — by God they will kill him, and he has said something he ought not to go back on. She had read the room exactly. Marwan turned on her about her father; she answered him about his; and he turned away from her and asked the caliph again.

**The statement:**
> لَا بَلِ اصْمُتْ فَإِنَّهُمْ وَاللَّهِ قَاتِلُوهُ وَمُؤَثِّمُوهُ، إِنَّهُ قَدْ قَالَ مَقَالَةً لَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَنْزِعَ عَنْهَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1223
> *English:* "No — rather, be silent; for by God they will kill him and load him with sin. He has said something that he ought not to go back on."

**عبرت:** The person who gave the right advice that evening was the one with no office at all.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR96 · Marwan argues that repentance now is worse
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Inside the caliph's house.

**What happened:** Marwan's case was that the timing was fatal. Had you said this while you were strong, he told the caliph, I would have been the first to accept it and to help you to it. But you said what you said when the girth had reached the udders and the flood had passed the hollows, and when it is the abject man who offers the abject terms. By God, to stand firm on a fault you ask forgiveness for is better than a repentance you are threatened over. And there are men like mountains at the door.

**The statement:**
> وَاللَّهِ لَإِقَامَةٌ عَلَى خَطِيئَةٍ يُسْتَغْفَرُ مِنْهَا أَجْمَلُ مِنْ تَوْبَةٍ يُخَوَّفُ عَلَيْهَا، وَأَنْتَ إِنْ شِئْتَ تَقَرَّبْتَ بِالتَّوْبَةِ وَلَمْ تُقِرَّ بِالْخَطِيئَةِ، وَقَدِ اجْتَمَعَ بِالْبَابِ أَمْثَالُ الْجِبَالِ مِنَ النَّاسِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1223
> *English:* "By God, to persist in a fault for which forgiveness is asked is more seemly than a repentance over which one is made to fear. And you, if you wished, could have drawn near by repentance without acknowledging the fault — and there have gathered at the door people like mountains."

**عبرت:** Advice given in the language of honour can undo in ten minutes what was built in a sermon.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR97 · Marwan goes to the door and says the opposite
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The door of the caliph's house.

What is the matter with you, as though you had come for plunder — you have come wanting to tear our kingship out of our hands; get away from us; by God, if you seek us out, a matter will pass over you that you will not like. Go back to your houses; by God we are not to be overcome in what we hold.

> *English:* "You have come wanting to tear our kingship out of our hands! Get out from us. (By God, if you seek to harm us) a matter shall pass over you that will grieve you and whose outcome you will not praise. Go back to your dwellings, for by God we are not overcome in what is in our hands."

**عبرت:** One word — kingship — spoken at the door, undid a sermon that had made a whole mosque weep.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR99 · Naila ؓ counsels him to follow his two companions
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Inside the caliph's house.

### TGA/E-GR100 · She is more sincere to me than you are
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Inside the caliph's house.

Do not mention her with a single letter, or I will blacken your face for you — for by God she is more sincere to me than you are. Al-Kamil records the same exchange in almost the same words, and adds that Marwan then held his peace.

### TGA/E-GR101 · Whenever I bring one thing, Marwan brings another
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

Ali ؓ answered by describing what had happened: you spoke on the pulpit of the Messenger of God ﷺ, you gave your undertaking, and then you went into your house and Marwan went out to the people at your door and abused them. And when the caliph said he had abandoned him and emboldened the people against him, Ali ؓ gave the plainest account of his own position in the whole strand.

> *English:* "By God, I am the most of all people in defending you; but every time I bring something I think will please you, Marwan brings another, and you listen to his word and leave mine."

### TGA/E-GR102 · Ali ؓ and the water
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The caliph's house under siege.

**What happened:** After that night Ali ؓ stopped doing what he had been doing — until the caliph was denied water. Then he spoke to Talha ؓ about getting the water-skins in, and al-Kamil says he became severely angry, until the water-skins were brought in to Uthman ؓ. It is a small entry in the middle of a siege and it is worth the room's attention.

**The statement:**
> وَلَمْ يَعُدْ عَلِيٌّ يَعْمَلُ مَا كَانَ يَعْمَلُ إِلَى أَنْ مُنِعَ عُثْمَانُ الْمَاءَ. فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ لِطَلْحَةَ (أُرِيدُ أَنْ) تُدْخَلَ عَلَيْهِ الرَّوَايَا، وَغَضِبَ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا حَتَّى دَخَلَتِ الرَّوَايَا عَلَى عُثْمَانَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1224
> *English:* "And Ali did not return to doing what he had been doing, until Uthman was denied water. Then Ali said to Talha: 'I want the water-skins to be brought in to him' — and he was severely angry, until the water-skins were brought in to Uthman."

**عبرت:** Anger on behalf of a man you have stopped advising is still loyalty.

### TGA/E-GR103 · Letters forged in the names of the Companions
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Fustat, Kufa, Basra, all writing to each other.

### TGA/E-GR104 · The courier on the road, and a sealed letter
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The road from Medina to Egypt.

**What happened:** The Egyptians, riding home after being turned back, took a courier on the road and searched him, and found in his water-flask a letter in the caliph's name ordering that a party of them be killed, others crucified, and the hands and feet of others cut off. The letter carried the seal of Uthman ؓ, the courier was one of his own slaves and was on his camel. They turned round, came back with the letter, and carried it round from man to man.

**The statement:**
> فأخذوه ففتشوه، فإذا معه في إداوة كتابًا (١) على لسان عثمان فيه الأمر بقتل طائفة (منهم)، وبصلب آخرين، وبقطع أيدي آخرين منهم وأرجلهم، وكان على الكتاب طابع بخاتم عثمان، والبريد أحد غلمان عثمان وعلى جَمَله، فلما رجعوا جاؤوا بالكتاب وداروا به على الناس
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3467
> *English:* "So they seized him and searched him, and there was with him in a flask a letter in Uthman's name, in it the order to kill a party of them, and to crucify others, and to cut off the hands and feet of others of them; and upon the letter was a seal with Uthman's signet, and the courier was one of Uthman's slaves and on his camel. So when they returned they came with the letter and carried it round among the people."

**عبرت:** A forged order can do more damage in a week than a real one, because nobody has to obey it for it to work.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR105 · A seal can be forged upon a seal
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** The people put the letter to him. His answer was an oath and a legal challenge in one breath: produce evidence against me for that — otherwise, by God, I did not write it, I did not dictate it, and I knew nothing of it; and a seal may be forged upon a seal. Ibn Kathir then adds the sentence that describes the whole crisis in six words: the truthful believed him in that, and the liars called him a liar.

**The statement:**
> فقال بيِّنةٌ عليَّ بذلك وإلا فوالله لا كتبت (٢) ولا أمليت، ولا دريت بشيء من ذلك، والخاتم قد يزوّر على الخاتم، فصدَّقه الصادقون في ذلك، وكذَّبه الكاذبون
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3467
> *English:* "He said: 'Bring evidence against me for that; otherwise, by God, I did not write it, nor dictate it, nor did I know anything of it — and a seal may be forged upon a seal.' So the truthful believed him in that, and the liars called him a liar."

**عبرت:** Where a document cannot be tested, people believe it according to what they already wanted to believe.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR108 · Talha ؓ and al-Zubayr ؓ answer the same way
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights; three contingents outside.

**عبرت:** Three men, three provinces, one answer, and their sons already inside the besieged house.

### TGA/E-GR109 · This is a thing decided at night
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** The contingents left, then turned round and came back, and the people of Medina heard the cry of God is greatest in their streets. Ali ؓ asked them what had brought them back, and each province gave the same answer: we found a letter with a courier ordering us killed. Then Ali ؓ asked the question that exposed the whole arrangement — how did Kufa and Basra learn what happened to Egypt, when you had already travelled days apart? — and named it in five words.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ لَهُمْ عَلِيٌّ: كَيْفَ عَلِمْتُمْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكُوفَةِ وَيَا أَهْلَ الْبَصْرَةِ بِمَا لَقِيَ أَهْلُ مِصْرَ وَقَدْ سِرْتُمْ مَرَاحِلَ حَتَّى رَجَعْتُمْ عَلَيْنَا؟ هَذَا وَاللَّهِ أَمْرٌ أُبْرِمَ بِلَيْلٍ!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1219
> *English:* "Then Ali said to them: 'How did you learn, people of Kufa and people of Basra, what befell the people of Egypt, when you had travelled stages away, so that you came back upon us? This, by God, is a matter settled by night!'"

**عبرت:** Three separate grievances that arrive on the same day were not three separate grievances.

**Hands-up?** Three armies, three provinces, weeks apart on the road — and all three turn round in the same week. What does that tell you?

### TGA/E-GR110 · Al-Bidaya's version of the same challenge
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir gives the same confrontation with the Companions putting the question together, and the same answer coming back. How did you learn this from your companions, they asked, when you had separated and there were stages between you? This is a thing you agreed upon. And the men did not deny it. Put it however you like, they said; we have no need of this man — let him withdraw from us and we will withdraw from him.

**The statement:**
> إنما هذا أمر اتفقتم عليه، فقالوا: ضعوه على ما أردتم، لا حاجة لنا في هذا الرجل، ليعتزلنا ونحن نعتزله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3466
> *English:* "This is only a matter you agreed upon. They said: 'Put it however you wish. We have no need of this man: let him withdraw from us and we will withdraw from him.'"

**عبرت:** When men stop denying the charge and start restating the demand, the argument has changed shape.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR111 · Abd al-Rahman b. Awf ؓ takes back the alms-camels
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Ibn al-Athir opens his account of what emboldened people against the caliph with a single incident. Camels of the alms were brought to Uthman ؓ, and he gave them to one of Banu al-Hakam. Abd al-Rahman b. Awf ؓ heard of it, took them, and divided them among the people — while the caliph was in his house. One of the ten promised Paradise reversed the caliph's own disposal of public property, and no punishment followed.

**The statement:**
> فَكَانَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَنَّ إِبِلًا مِنْ إِبِلِ الصَّدَقَةِ قُدِمَ بِهَا عَلَى عُثْمَانَ، فَوَهَبَهَا لِبَعْضِ بَنِي الْحَكَمِ، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ عَوْفٍ، فَأَخَذَهَا وَقَسَّمَهَا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَعُثْمَانُ فِي الدَّارِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1225
> *English:* "Among that was that camels of the camels of the alms were brought to Uthman, and he gave them to one of Banu al-Hakam; and that reached Abd al-Rahman b. Awf, so he took them and divided them among the people, while Uthman was in the house."

**عبرت:** A community in which a senior man can reverse the ruler's disposal of public money is not a community without checks.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR112 · Jabala b. Amr al-Saidi in the street
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A street in Medina.

**What happened:** Ibn al-Athir names the first man who was insolent to the caliph in speech: Jabala b. Amr al-Saidi. The caliph passed him while he was sitting in his clan's meeting place with an iron collar in his hand. Uthman ؓ gave the greeting of peace and the company returned it. Jabala asked them why they were returning it to a man who had done such and such. Then he turned to the caliph and swore he would put the collar on his neck unless he gave up the men he kept about him, and named them.

**The statement:**
> وَاللَّهِ لَأَطْرَحَنَّ هَذِهِ الْجَامِعَةَ فِي عُنُقِكَ أَوْ لَتَتْرُكَنَّ بِطَانَتَكَ هَذِهِ الْخَبِيثَةَ: مَرْوَانَ، وَابْنَ عَامِرٍ، وَابْنَ سَعْدٍ، مِنْهُمْ مَنْ نَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ بِذَمِّهِ وَأَبَاحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - دَمَهُ. فَاجْتَرَأَ النَّاسُ عَلَيْهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1225
> *English:* "By God, I will throw this collar on your neck, or you will leave off this evil inner circle of yours: Marwan, and Ibn Amir, and Ibn Sad — among them is one whom the Quran came down blaming, and whose blood the Messenger of God ﷺ made lawful. And so the people became bold against him."

**عبرت:** The first man to be openly insolent to a ruler in the street changes what is possible for everyone who watched.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR113 · Al-Bidaya asks which inner circle he means
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A street in Medina.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir tells the same encounter and includes the caliph's reply, which al-Kamil leaves out. Which inner circle? he asked — for by God I choose the best of men. Jabala then named them: Marwan, Muawiya ؓ, Abd Allah b. Amir b. Kurayz, Abd Allah b. Sad b. Abi Sarh. Ibn Kathir ends the report by saying that Uthman ؓ turned away, and from that day the people did not cease to be bold against him.

**The statement:**
> فقال عثمان: أيّ بطانة؟ فوالله [إني] لأتخيَّر الناسَ، فقال: مروان تخيرته، ومعاوية تخيرته
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3468
> *English:* "Uthman said: 'Which inner circle? By God, I choose the best of the people.' He said: 'Marwan — you chose him; and Muawiya — you chose him.'"

**عبرت:** An accusation that has to name names can be answered; one that stays general cannot.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR114 · Amr b. al-As ؓ in the mosque, and weeping
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina, the Prophet's Mosque ﷺ.

**What happened:** Al-Bidaya carries another account of the same challenge. The caliph was preaching, and Amr b. al-As ؓ said: Commander of the Faithful, you have ridden into dangerous ground and we rode into it with you, so repent and we will repent with you. Uthman ؓ turned towards the qibla and spread out his hands. Abu Habiba, who was there, said afterwards that he never saw a day with more weeping men and weeping women in it than that one.

**The statement:**
> قال أبو حبيبة: فلم أرَ يومًا أكثر باكيًا ولا باكيةً من يومئذ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3468
> *English:* "Abu Habiba said: I never saw a day with more men weeping nor more women weeping than that day."

**عبرت:** The city was not against him; the city was in tears.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR115 · Jahjah al-Ghifari breaks the Prophet ﷺ's staff
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina, on the pulpit.

**What happened:** He was preaching one day holding the staff that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to lean on in his sermons, and Abu Bakr ؓ and Umar ؓ after him. Jahjah al-Ghifari took it out of his hand and broke it across his knee. Al-Kamil states it in one sentence and adds that the man was struck in that very place with a wasting disease. Al-Bidaya reports the same with a splinter lodging in the knee and the wound turning gangrenous.

**The statement:**
> فَأَخَذَهَا جَهْجَاهُ الْغِفَارِيُّ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَكَسَرَهَا عَلَى رُكْبَتِهِ، فَرُمِيَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ بِأَكِلَةٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1225
> *English:* "So Jahjah al-Ghifari took it from his hand and broke it across his knee, and he was struck in that very place with a gangrenous wasting."

**عبرت:** Some acts are remembered not for what they destroyed but for what they announced.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TGA/E-GR116 · Al-Bidaya on the splinter and the wound
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina lights.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir's account, through al-Waqidi, has the witness watching it happen: the staff was taken and broken across the right knee, a splinter of it went in, and the wound stayed until gangrene took him — the witness says he saw it crawling. The caliph was helped down and ordered the staff bound, and it was carried braced with metal afterwards. He went out only once or twice more before he was besieged.

**The statement:**
> فنزل عثمان (وحملوه) وأمر بالعصا فشدوها، فكانت مضببة، فما خرج بعد ذلك اليوم إلا خَرْجَة أو خرجتين، حتى حُصِر فقتل
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3468
> *English:* "So Uthman came down and they carried him, and he ordered the staff to be bound, and it was braced; and he did not go out after that day except an outing or two, until he was besieged and killed."

**عبرت:** The staff was mended with metal bands, and the thing it stood for was not mended at all.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR117 · The Friday he was stoned off the pulpit
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina, the Prophet's Mosque ﷺ.

**What happened:** On the Friday after the contingents entered Medina he led the prayer and then stood on the pulpit and appealed to them. Muhammad b. Maslama ؓ stood up to bear witness for him and was pulled down into his seat by Hukaym b. Jabala; Zayd b. Thabit ؓ stood up and was pulled down by another man. Then the whole party rose, pelted the people until they had driven them out of the mosque, and pelted the caliph until he fell from the pulpit unconscious and was carried into his house.

**The statement:**
> وَثَارَ الْقَوْمُ بِأَجْمَعِهِمْ فَحَصَبُوا النَّاسَ حَتَّى أَخْرَجُوهُمْ مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ، وَحَصَبُوا عُثْمَانَ حَتَّى صُرِعَ عَنِ الْمِنْبَرِ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ، فَأُدْخِلَ دَارَهُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1220
> *English:* "And the whole party rose and pelted the people with stones until they drove them out of the mosque; and they pelted Uthman until he was struck down from the pulpit unconscious, and he was carried into his house."

**عبرت:** The moment a mosque can be cleared by force is the moment the city has stopped governing itself.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR118 · The sons of the Companions come to the house
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The caliph's house, Medina.

**What happened:** After that Friday the crowd shut him into his house and surrounded it. Many of the Companions kept to their own houses. A number of their sons went to him, on their fathers' orders — al-Hasan and al-Husayn ؓ, Abd Allah b. al-Zubayr ؓ, who was commander of the house, and Abd Allah b. Amr ؓ — and stood arguing and fighting off anyone who tried to reach him. Ibn Kathir names them, and names their fathers' instruction as the reason they were there.

**The statement:**
> وسار إليه جماعة من أبناء الصحابة، عن أمر آبائهم، منهم الحسن والحسين، وعبد الله بن الزبير -وكان أمير الدار- وعبد الله بن عمرو، وصاروا يحاجّون عنه، ويناضلون دونه أن يصل إليه أحد منهم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3469
> *English:* "And a number of the sons of the Companions went to him, by their fathers' command, among them al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and Abd Allah b. al-Zubayr — and he was commander of the house — and Abd Allah b. Amr; and they began to argue on his behalf and to fight in his defence, that none of them should reach him."

**عبرت:** What the fathers did is recorded in what they told their sons to do.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR119 · What the besiegers actually demanded
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The caliph's house, Medina.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir states the demand plainly, and then states the thing that a room most needs to hear. They had asked him for one of two things: either that he depose himself, or that he hand Marwan b. al-Hakam over to them. And it did not occur to anyone's mind that killing was in the intention of those who had come out against him. The siege began as a political demand and nobody in the city expected it to end as it did.

**The statement:**
> فإنهم كانوا قد طلبوا منه إما أن يعزل نفسه، أو يسلِّم إليهم مروانَ بن الحكم، ولم يقع في خلد أحد أن القتل كان في نفس الخارجين
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3469
> *English:* "For they had demanded of him either that he depose himself, or that he hand over to them Marwan b. al-Hakam; and it did not occur to anyone's mind that killing was in the intention of those who had gone out against him."

**عبرت:** Nobody in that city thought it would end the way it ended, and that is the most sobering sentence on the page.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR120 · The books differ on the length of the siege
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** The caliph's house, Medina.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir says the siege went on for more than a month, and it is said forty days, until the end of it was that he was killed as a martyr. Al-Kamil counts it differently: he led the people in prayer in the mosque for thirty days after they camped on him, then they prevented him from the prayer and their own commander al-Ghafiqi led it, and the siege was forty days. Give both counts, or give neither.

**The statement:**
> وقد استمر الحصر (٥) أكثر من شهر. وقيل أربعين يومًا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3469
> *English:* "And the siege continued for more than a month; and it is said, forty days."

**عبرت:** Even the length of the most famous siege in the community's memory is recorded as a range.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR121 · Who led the prayer while he was shut in
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** Medina, the Prophet's Mosque ﷺ.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir records three answers to a simple question. He himself says that in these days al-Ghafiqi b. Harb led the people. Ibn Jarir's account is that it was Talha b. Ubayd Allah ؓ. Al-Waqidi relates that Ali ؓ also prayed, and Abu Ayyub ؓ, and Sahl b. Hunayf ؓ. Three transmissions, three answers, all printed on the same page, none of them suppressed.

**The statement:**
> والذي ذكره ابن جرير أنَّ الذي كان يصلِّي بالناس في هذه المدة وعثمان محصور، طلحة بن عبيد الله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3469
> *English:* "And what Ibn Jarir mentioned is that the one who led the people in prayer during this period, while Uthman was besieged, was Talha b. Ubayd Allah."

**عبرت:** A page that carries three answers to one question is telling you how careful you must be.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR122 · He writes to the provinces, and men set out
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrows in from Syria, Egypt, Kufa and Basra.

**What happened:** Uthman ؓ wrote to the great cities asking for help and telling them what state the people were in, and they came out on whatever mount they had. Muawiya ؓ sent Habib b. Maslama al-Fihri; Abd Allah b. Sad sent Muawiya b. Hudayj; al-Qaqa b. Amr came out of Kufa. Al-Kamil then names the men who stood up in each city urging people to go: Uqba b. Amir ؓ, Abd Allah b. Abi Awfa ؓ, Hanzala the Scribe ؓ in Kufa; Imran b. Husayn ؓ, Anas b. Malik ؓ, Hisham b. Amir ؓ in Basra. They did not arrive in time.

**The statement:**
> وَكَتَبَ عُثْمَانُ إِلَى أَهْلِ الْأَمْصَارِ يَسْتَنْجِدُهُمْ وَيَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْحَثِّ لِلْمَنْعِ عَنْهُ، وَيُعَرِّفُهُمْ مَا النَّاسُ فِيهِ. فَخَرَجَ أَهْلُ الْأَمْصَارِ عَلَى الصَّعْبِ وَالذَّلُولِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1219
> *English:* "And Uthman wrote to the people of the great cities seeking their help, and commanding them to hasten to his defence, and informing them of the state the people were in; and the people of the cities came out upon the difficult mount and the easy one."

**عبرت:** Help was on the road from four provinces, and distance decided the matter.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR123 · Ibn Saba in al-Bidaya, attributed to Sayf by name
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 34 AH `[SOURCED, and the attribution is the point]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn Kathir introduces the account of Abd Allah b. Saba by naming his source: and Sayf b. Umar mentioned that the cause of the factions banding against Uthman ؓ was a man called Abd Allah b. Saba, a Jew who professed Islam, went to Egypt and put about a doctrine of his own invention. Ibn Kathir sets the whole passage out and closes the section a page later with the historian's formula, God knows best. This card is recorded and not planned: it is tiered CUT because the attribution, not the story, is the finding.

**The statement:**
> وذكر سيف بن عمر (٦) أن سببَ تألُّبِ الأحزاب على عثمان أن رجلًا يقال له عبد الله بن سبأ كان يهوديًا فأظهر الإسلام وصار إلى مصر، فأوحى إلى طائفة من الناس كلامًا اخترعه من عند نفسه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3456
> *English:* "And Sayf b. Umar mentioned that the cause of the factions banding together against Uthman was that a man called Abd Allah b. Saba, who was a Jew, professed Islam and came to Egypt, and put into the minds of a group of people words he had invented of himself."

**عبرت:** When a book names the single transmitter an account rests on, it has told you how much weight to put on it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TGA/E-GR124 · Ibn Saba in al-Kamil, in the book's own voice
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED, and the difference is the finding]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ibn al-Athir opens his chapter on the march against the caliph with the same man and states it without naming a transmitter: the cause of that was that Abd Allah b. Saba was a Jew who professed Islam in the days of Uthman ؓ, then moved about the Hijaz, Basra, Kufa and Syria seeking to lead people astray, was expelled from Syria, and settled in Egypt. The difference between the two books on this one point is itself the finding, and it is why both cards are tiered CUT.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ سَبَبُ ذَلِكَ أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ سَبَأٍ كَانَ يَهُودِيًّا، وَأَسْلَمَ أَيَّامَ عُثْمَانَ، ثُمَّ تَنَقَّلَ فِي الْحِجَازِ ثُمَّ بِالْبَصْرَةِ ثُمَّ بِالْكُوفَةِ ثُمَّ بِالشَّامِ يُرِيدُ إِضْلَالَ النَّاسِ، فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ مِنْهُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ، فَأَخْرَجَهُ أَهْلُ الشَّامِ، فَأَتَى مِصْرَ فَأَقَامَ فِيهِمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۲۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1215
> *English:* "And the cause of that was that Abd Allah b. Saba was a Jew, and he professed Islam in the days of Uthman; then he moved about in the Hijaz, then in Basra, then in Kufa, then in Syria, seeking to lead the people astray, but he could not manage it with them, and the people of Syria expelled him; so he came to Egypt and settled among them."

**عبرت:** Two sound Sunni books can carry the same account with different degrees of commitment, and the degree of commitment is part of the evidence.

**Hands-up?** no

## The siege, and the killing of عثمان ؓ

*Source note: [`the-siege-and-the-killing-of-uthman.md`](../docs/research/the-siege-and-the-killing-of-uthman.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TSA/E-SK1 · Letters that nobody had written
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before شوال 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Three arrows leave مصر، الكوفة، البصرة and converge on المدينہ.

**What happened:** In the months before the second march, letters travelled between the garrison cities. They carried the names of the great Companions in المدينہ at the bottom, and they called on people to come and fight the caliph. The names were forged. ابن كثير says so in plain words, and he says the same of a second letter that would be produced later in عثمان ؓ's own name. What moved three armies out of three cities was paper that nobody had signed.

**The statement:**
> وزُوِّرتْ كتبٌ على لسان الصحابة الذين بالمدينة، وعلى لسان عليٍّ وطلحة والزبير، يدعون الناس إلى قتال عثمان ونُصرة الدين، وأنه أكبر الجهاد اليوم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3465
> *English:* "And letters were forged in the name of the Companions who were in المدينہ, and in the name of علي and طلحة and الزبير, calling people to fight عثمان and to help the religion, and saying that this was the greatest jihād today."

**عبرت:** A signature is easier to counterfeit than a reputation is to rebuild.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TSA/E-SK2 · Three cities, three men, one road
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** شوال 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Label the three camps outside المدينہ — ذو خشب، الأعوص، ذو المروة.

**What happened:** The parties came out saying they were going to الحج. They were not one movement. The Egyptians had علي ؓ in view, the Basrans had طلحة ؓ, and the Kufans had الزبير ؓ, and each group was certain that its own man would end the affair in its favour. None of the three had asked for any of it, and each of them, when they reached him, drove his own delegation away. They camped three stages out of المدينہ and sent men ahead to see what the city was thinking.

**The statement:**
> وأهل مصر مصرون على ولاية علي بن أبي طالب، وأهل الكوفة عازمون على تأمير الزُّبير، وأهل البصرة مصممون على تولية طلحة. لا تشكّ كلّ فرقةٍ أن أمرها سيتمّ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3465
> *English:* "The people of مصر were set on the governance of علي بن أبي طالب, the people of الكوفة determined on making الزبير commander, and the people of البصرة resolved on appointing طلحة — each faction in no doubt that its own purpose would prevail."

**عبرت:** Men who agree on whom to remove may agree on nothing else, and that is discovered afterwards.

### TSA/E-SK3 · Four books, four counts
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** شوال 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ask how many men besieged the caliph and the books will not give one answer. البدایہ reports the range honestly: the man who counts low says six hundred, the man who counts high says a thousand. الکامل says five hundred, or a thousand. سیر says four hundred; and elsewhere سیر gives a full arithmetic — six hundred Egyptians, two hundred Kufans, one hundred Basrans. ابن كثير, forty pages later, writes that they were close to two thousand fighting men. Not one of those figures matches another.

**The statement:**
> خرج أهل مصر في أربع رِفاق على أربعة أمراء، المُقَلِّلُ لهم يقول ستمئة، والمُكْثِرُ يقول: ألف.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3465
> *English:* "The people of مصر came out in four companies under four commanders — the one who reckons them few says six hundred, and the one who reckons them many says a thousand."

**عبرت:** A historian who writes down two numbers instead of one is telling you where his knowledge stops.

**Hands-up?** How many of you have heard a crowd size reported two different ways on the same day?

### TSA/E-SK4 · Turned away at أحجار الزيت
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** شوال 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mark أحجار الزيت inside المدينہ.

**What happened:** The Egyptians came to علي ؓ where he was encamped at أحجار الزيت. He had already sent his own son الحسن ؓ in to stand at the caliph's door. He did not receive them as supporters. He shouted at them, drove them off, and told them the righteous knew what the Prophet ﷺ had said about the army that had come. طلحة ؓ said the same to the Basrans and الزبير ؓ said the same to the Kufans. All three books record it.

**The statement:**
> فصاح بهم وطردهم، وقال: لقد علم الصالحون أن جيش ذي المروة وذي خُشُبٍ ملعونون على لسان محمد ﷺ، فارجعوا لا صبَّحكم الله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3466
> *English:* "He shouted at them and drove them off, and said: the righteous know that the army of ذو المروة and ذو خشب are cursed on the tongue of محمد ﷺ. Go back — may God not bring you a good morning."

**عبرت:** A man is not answerable for those who march under his name without his leave.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK5 · They travelled some days, and turned round
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** شوال 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Arrows leave المدينہ, then reverse.

**What happened:** Having been refused by all three men, the parties made a show of going home. They travelled some days on the road. Then they wheeled round together and came back, and the people of المدينہ heard nothing until they heard the takbīr from three directions at once and found the city surrounded. The Companions put one question to them that neither book records an answer to: you had separated, and there were stages of road between you — how did each of you learn what the others had found?

**The statement:**
> هَذَا وَاللَّهِ أَمْرٌ أُبْرِمَ بِلَيْلٍ!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1219
> *English:* "By God, this is a matter settled by night."

**عبرت:** A coincidence that requires three parties to be surprised in the same way at the same hour is not a coincidence.

### TSA/E-SK6 · The courier at the well
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** شوال 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mark البويب on the road from المدينہ to مصر.

**What happened:** On the road back to مصر the party stopped a rider. He was on a camel of the state herd, and he was one of the caliph's own slaves. They searched his baggage and found a letter in a water-skin, sealed with the caliph's own seal, instructing the governor of مصر to kill some of them, crucify others, and cut off the hands and feet of others. They turned the column round and carried the letter through المدينہ from one Companion's house to the next.

**The statement:**
> فأخذوه ففتشوه، فإذا معه في إداوة كتابًا (١) على لسان عثمان فيه الأمر بقتل طائفة (منهم)، وبصلب آخرين، وبقطع أيدي آخرين منهم وأرجلهم، وكان على الكتاب طابع بخاتم عثمان
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3467
> *English:* "They seized him and searched him, and with him in a water-skin was a letter in عثمان's name commanding that a party of them be killed, others crucified, and the hands and feet of others cut off; and on the letter was the impression of عثمان's seal."

**عبرت:** A document can be true in every detail of its appearance and false in the one thing that matters.

### TSA/E-SK7 · Bring proof, or hear my oath
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** شوال 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** They brought the letter to him with the leading Companions present. He did not argue about the seal or the camel. He asked for evidence, and then he swore: he had not written it, had not dictated it, and did not know of it — and a seal can be forged upon a seal. Both البدایہ and سیر note that men who knew him well accepted the oath at once. And then ابن كثير writes the sentence that explains everything that followed, in eight words: the truthful believed him, and the liars called him a liar.

**The statement:**
> فقال بيِّنةٌ عليَّ بذلك وإلا فوالله لا كتبت (٢) ولا أمليت، ولا دريت بشيء من ذلك، والخاتم قد يزوّر على الخاتم، فصدَّقه الصادقون في ذلك، وكذَّبه الكاذبون.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3467
> *English:* "He said: bring proof against me of it; otherwise, by God, I did not write it, nor dictate it, nor know anything of it — and a seal may be forged upon a seal. So the truthful believed him in that, and the liars called him a liar."

**عبرت:** When the evidence is equally consistent with two readings, people choose the reading they were already inclined to.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK8 · A historian who refuses a report
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** written in the eighth century AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير had in front of him an older history that carried a report: that the Companions in المدينہ had written to the provinces telling people to come and fight the caliph. He copies the report out. Then he writes four words about it, in his own voice: this is a lie against the Companions. He then says the same about the letter produced against عثمان ؓ. This is what a historian does when the chain is weak and the charge is grave, and it is the whole method of this course in one line on one page.

**The statement:**
> وذكر ابن جرير (٦) من هذه الطريق أن الصحابة كتبوا إلى الآفاق من المدينة يأمرون الناس بالقدوم على عثمان ليقاتلوه، وهذا كذب على الصحابة، وإنما كُتبت كتبٌ مزورةٌ عليهم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3467
> *English:* "ابن جرير mentioned by this route that the Companions wrote from المدينہ to the provinces ordering people to come to عثمان to fight him — and this is a lie against the Companions; rather, forged letters were written in their name."

**عبرت:** Copying a report and endorsing it are two different acts, and the careful writer keeps them apart.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK9 · The staff of three caliphs
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو القعدة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The Prophet's ﷺ mosque, المدينہ.

**What happened:** He was preaching, leaning on a staff. It was the staff the Prophet ﷺ had leaned on when he preached, and أبو بكر ؓ after him, and عمر ؓ after him. A man named جهجاه الغفاري came up, took it out of his hand, and broke it across his knee. A splinter went into the knee and the wound never closed. All three of our books record it. None of them adds a word of comment; they do not need to.

**The statement:**
> فأخذها جَهْجَاهُ الْغِفَارِيُّ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَكَسَرَهَا عَلَى رُكْبَتِهِ، فَرُمِيَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ بِأَكِلَةٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1225
> *English:* "And جهجاه الغفاري took it from his hand and broke it on his knee — and he was struck in that very place with gangrene."

**عبرت:** When a symbol that three men had carried can be broken over a knee in public, the thing it stood for has already gone.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK10 · Stones in the mosque
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** a Friday, ذو القعدة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The mosque and the house beside it.

**What happened:** On a Friday he stood on the منبر and appealed to the men who had come. محمد بن مسلمة ؓ stood up to testify for him and was pulled down into his seat. زيد بن ثابت ؓ stood up and was pulled down. Then the whole body of them rose and began throwing pebbles — first at the congregation, until the mosque emptied, then at the caliph, until he fell from the منبر unconscious and had to be carried into his house. الحسن البصري رحمہ اللہ said he saw so many stones in the air that he could not see the sky. > لقد رأيتهم تحاصبوا في المسجد حتى ما أبصر السماء

> *English:* "I saw them pelting one another with pebbles in the mosque until I could not see the sky."

**عبرت:** Disorder begins where order was strongest, because that is where it is most worth breaking.

### TSA/E-SK11 · Forty days, or twenty-two
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو القعدة–ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** How long was the house besieged? البدایہ says more than a month in one place and forty days in another, then adds that some said a few and forty and that الشعبي said twenty-two nights. الکامل says forty days twice. سیر says twenty-two days. Then البدایہ gives the two ends of the siege — the end of ذو القعدة to the eighteenth of ذو الحجة — and those dates do not make forty days on any reading of the month. The books have preserved the disagreement instead of tidying it away.

**The statement:**
> كان الحصار مستمرًا من أواخر ذي القعدة إلى يوم الجمعة الثامن عشر من ذي الحجة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۳۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3477
> *English:* "The siege continued from the end of ذو القعدة to Friday the eighteenth of ذو الحجة."

**عبرت:** A record that keeps its own contradictions is worth more than one that has been made tidy.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK12 · Who stood in front of the rows
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

Then they stopped him, and someone else had to stand in front of the rows in the Prophet's ﷺ mosque. **عبرت:** Where the reports differ and the matter touches men's honour, the historian sets the reports side by side and stops.

### TSA/E-SK13 · "You know I bought the well"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mark بئر رومة outside المدينہ.

Do you know that I bought the well of رومة from my own money and gave its water to the Muslims? Do you know that I bought the ground that widened this mosque? Do you know that I equipped the army of hardship? Each time men in the crowd stood up and said yes. ### TSA/E-SK14 · "So for what are they killing me?"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** From the wall he recited the hadith he had heard from the Prophet ﷺ: the blood of a Muslim is not lawful except for three things — a married man who commits zinā, a man who kills, a man who leaves his religion. Then he took each of the three and set it against his own life, and finished with a question. The report comes by more than one chain; ابن كثير traces it to أحمد and to all four Sunan and the modern editor marks the chain sound.

**The statement:**
> فوالله ما زنيتُ في جاهليةٍ ولا إسلام قطُّ، ولا تمنيتُ بدلًا بديني منذ هداني الله له، ولا قتلتُ نفسًا، فبم يقتلونني؟.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3473
> *English:* "By God, I have never committed zinā, in جاهلية or in Islam; nor have I ever wished any substitute for my religion since God guided me to it; nor have I killed anyone. So for what are they killing me?"

**عبرت:** A man who can answer the charge point by point and is still not released was never being tried on the charge.

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

### TSA/E-SK22 · The family who came at night
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mark the house of عمرو بن حزم adjoining.

**What happened:** After علي ؓ and أم حبيبة ؓ had both been turned back, the two books agree that only one channel stayed open. The household of عمرو بن حزم ؓ lived in the house that backed onto his. **عبرت:** In a general failure of nerve it is usually one household, not one city, that does the right thing.

### TSA/E-SK23 · Sent away to lead the ḥajj

### TSA/E-SK24 · The armies that arrived too late
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Four arrows converging on المدينہ from الشام، مصر، الكوفة، البصرة — all stopping short.

**What happened:** He had written to the provinces for help and the provinces had answered. Columns were on the road from الشام under حبيب بن مسلمة, from مصر under معاوية بن خديج, from الكوفة under القعقاع بن عمرو, from البصرة under مجاشع. The besiegers learned that the columns were coming and that the pilgrims meant to return and lift the siege. That is the precise moment they decided to end it. **عبرت:** Help that is on the road is not help, and the people who know it is coming will act before it arrives.

### TSA/E-SK28 · "Whoever sheathes his sword is free"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 17 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The house, with seven hundred inside.

### TSA/E-SK40 · The women who stopped them

> أنهم أرادوا حزَّ رأسه بعد قتله، فصاح النساء (٨) وضربن وجوههن، فيهن امرأتاه نائلة وأم البنين (٩)، وبناته، فقال ابن عديس: اتركوه، فتركوه.

> *English:* "They wanted to cut off his head after killing him, and the women cried out and struck their own faces — among them his two wives نائلة and أم البنين, and his daughters. So ابن عديس said: leave him. And they left him."

**عبرت:** There is usually one line even the people who have crossed every other line will not cross, and it is worth noticing where it falls.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK41 · "Is his blood lawful and his property not?"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 18 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** With the man dead in the room, one of them called out a question, and it was answered by everyone at once. They stripped the house — البدایہ says they left nothing behind, down to the drinking cups. They took what the women were wearing. One of them pulled the outer wrap off نائلة ؓ and one of the caliph's slaves killed him for it and was killed in turn. Then someone shouted to get to the treasury before anyone else did.

**The statement:**
> وذلك أنه نادى مناد منهم (١١): أيحل لنا دمُه ولا يحلّ لنا ماله، فانتهبوه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3486
> *English:* "And that was because a crier among them called out: is his blood lawful to us and his property not lawful to us? So they plundered it."

**عبرت:** A cause that has justified the first thing will find the second thing easy.

### TSA/E-SK42 · Two sacks, or a great deal
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 18 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** They ran for بيت المال. الکامل says the keepers heard them coming, knew there was nothing in it but two sacks, said to each other that these men were only after the world, and fled. البدایہ, telling the same scene, says the rebels took the treasury money and that there was a very great deal in it. The two books are in flat contradiction and neither knows about the other. This is a good place to say aloud that even the best sources disagree about the simplest facts.

**The statement:**
> فَسَمِعَ أَصْحَابُ بَيْتِ الْمَالِ كَلَامَهُمْ وَلَيْسَ فِيهِ إِلَّا غِرَارَتَانِ، فَقَالُوا: النَّجَاءَ فَإِنَّ الْقَوْمَ إِنَّمَا يُحَاوِلُونَ الدُّنْيَا!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۴۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1234
> *English:* "The keepers of the treasury heard their words — and there was nothing in it but two sacks — and said: flee, for these people are only after the world."

**عبرت:** What a movement does in the first hour after it wins tells you what it was for.

**Hands-up?** no
