### TSA/E-SK43 · Buried between المغرب and العشاء
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mark حش كوكب, east of البقيع.

**What happened:** He lay unburied — three days, says one report; two nights, says another; buried the same night, says a third. When they took him out it was between المغرب and العشاء, in fear of the men who had killed him, and the party was small. Some of them sat in the road with stones to throw at the bier, and علي ؓ sent men to stop them. He was buried in a walled garden outside البقيع called حش كوكب. Who prayed over him is given five different ways.

> وأما موضع قبره فلا خلاف أنه (دفن) بحشّ كوكب -شرقي البقيع-

> *English:* "As for the place of his grave, there is no disagreement that he was buried at حش كوكب — east of البقيع."

### TSA/E-SK44 · The shapes behind them in the dark
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the night of the burial, 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** One of the men who carried the body told the story years later to عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمہ اللہ. They had waited until dark because they were afraid that if they left him till morning the body would be mutilated. As they carried him, a mass of figures came up behind them out of the dark and they were frightened and nearly scattered. Years later, when معاوية ؓ held the caliphate, he had the wall between the garden and البقيع taken down and told people to bury their dead around the grave, until the two grounds ran together. ### TSA/E-SK48 · The shirt on the منبر of دمشق
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35–36 AH `[SOURCED — سیر, from سيف بن عمر]` · **Map:** An arrow from المدينہ to دمشق.

**What happened:** النعمان بن بشير ؓ carried two things north to الشام: the shirt the caliph had been killed in, with the blood still on it, and نائلة ؓ's severed fingers. معاوية ؓ had the shirt set up on the منبر of دمشق with the fingers hanging from it. سیر records that men of الشام swore oaths over it — not to sleep on a bed, not to come to their wives, until the killers were dead or they were — and that they wept for him for a year. Everything that followed for the next five years began in front of that منبر.

**The statement:**
> فنصب معاوية القميص على منبر دمشق، والأصابع معلقة فيه
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۰۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1344
> *English:* "And معاوية set the shirt up on the منبر of دمشق, with the fingers hanging from it."

**عبرت:** A grievance with an object attached to it does not fade the way a grievance without one does.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK49 · "The first of the trials"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** حذيفة بن اليمان ؓ, who was known among the Companions as the one the Prophet ﷺ had told about the coming trials, was dying when the news reached him. He was told what had happened and said "إنا لله". Then he put on record where he stood: if the killing was good I have no share in it, and if it was evil I am quit of it — and he gave the two outcomes in one image, of an ummah milking either milk or blood. His judgement on the event is four words long.

**The statement:**
> أول الفتن قتل عثمان، وآخر الفتن الدجال.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3493
> *English:* "The first of the trials is the killing of عثمان, and the last of the trials is the Dajjāl."

**عبرت:** Some events are not the end of a story but the beginning of a longer one.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK50 · علي ؓ's oath
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH and after `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He swore it publicly and he kept swearing it: at the door of the mosque, in his sermons, at أحجار الزيت, and on the day of الجمل. I did not kill him, I did not order it, I did not connive at it, I was not pleased with it — I forbade them and they did not listen. ابن كثير, having collected the routes, says that they amount to certainty in the judgement of many of the imams of hadith. ابن سيرين رحمہ اللہ says he knows of nobody who accuses him.

**The statement:**
> سمعت عليًا وهو بباب المسجد، أو عند أحجار الزَّيت، رافعًا صوته يقول: اللهم إني أبرأ إليك من دم عثمان.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3495
> *English:* "I heard علي at the door of the mosque, or by أحجار الزيت, raising his voice and saying: O God, I declare myself innocent before You of the blood of عثمان."

**عبرت:** A man who inherits a crisis is not the man who made it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK51 · "Like a garment clean of any stain"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ was returning from the pilgrimage when the news met her. Her verdict on it is recorded three separate ways in البدایہ, and they all say the same thing about the men who did it: you pressed him to satisfy you, and when you had left him clean as a washed garment, you killed him. And when someone put it to her that she had written letters urging people out against him, she swore on oath that she had never written them a black letter on a white page — and ابن كثير records that the chain of that oath to her is sound.

**The statement:**
> تركتموه كالثوب النقيِّ من الدَّنسِ ثمَّ قتلتموه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3498
> *English:* "You left him like a garment clean of any stain — and then you killed him."

**عبرت:** When a man has met every demand and is killed anyway, the demands were not the reason.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK52 · The man of بدر who never laughed again
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو حميد الساعدي ؓ had fought at بدر, and he had kept his distance from عثمان ؓ in the last years. When the news came he said something that both البدایہ and الکامل thought worth writing down. He did not defend himself and he did not accuse anyone. He said that they had never wanted the man killed and had not thought the matter would reach killing — and then he made a vow to God about how he would live for the rest of his life.

**The statement:**
> فلما قتل قال: واللّه ما أردنا قَتْلَه، ولا كُنّا نرى أن يبلغ منه القتلُ، اللَّهُمّ إنَّ لكَ عليّ أن لا أفعل كذا وكذا (٢) ولا أضحك حتى ألقاك.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3497
> *English:* "When he was killed he said: by God, we did not want him killed, nor did we think that the matter would reach killing. O God, I owe it to You that I will not do such and such, and will not laugh until I meet You."

**عبرت:** Many of the people who made an event possible had not wanted the event.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK53 · Three clauses that end the argument
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** a generation later `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الزہری رحمہ اللہ went to سعيد بن المسيب رحمہ اللہ, the foremost jurist of المدينہ in the generation after the Companions, and asked him straight out: will you tell me how the killing of عثمان happened? He answered in three clauses. He was killed wrongfully. Whoever failed to help him was excused. Whoever killed him was a wrongdoer. Then he went on to describe the sequence of events. The three clauses settle everything a listener needs settled and adjudicate between no two Companions at all.

**The statement:**
> قال: قتل مظلوما، ومن خذله كان معذورا، ومن قتله كان ظالما
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۰۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1349
> *English:* "He said: he was killed wrongfully; whoever failed to help him was excused; and whoever killed him was a wrongdoer."

**عبرت:** A judgement can be complete and still refuse to name a man.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK54 · "He held back his hands, then shut his door"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الشعبي said he had never heard a better elegy for عثمان ؓ than the lines attributed to كعب بن مالك ؓ — the poet of the Anṣār, one of the three whose repentance is in the Qurʾān. The first line puts the whole evening into eight words. The second line records the order he gave the men inside. The third asks what the killing bought. (البدایہ notes that سيف بن عمر attributed the same verses to a different man, المغيرة بن الأخنس — so they are attributed to كعب ؓ, not certainly by him.)

**The statement:**
> فَكَفَّ يَدَيْهِ ثُمَّ أغْلَق بابَهُ . . . وأيْقَن أنَّ اللهَ ليسَ بغافِلِ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3500
> *English:* "He held back his hands, then shut his door — and knew for certain that God is not heedless."

**عبرت:** The shortest true account of a long siege can fit in one line of verse.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK55 · The line somebody added later
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** recorded by ابن عبد البر, fifth century AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A famous elegy by حسان بن ثابت ؓ circulated with a closing couplet in it that wondered aloud about علي ؓ and ابن عفان ؓ. أبو عمر بن عبد البر رحمہ اللہ examined the poem and said plainly that the people of الشام had added that part, and that he saw no reason even to repeat it. ابن الأثیر copies the caution into الکامل. A partisan line got into a real poem, and Muslim scholars caught it, said so, and wrote it down — three hundred years before anyone in Europe did that kind of work.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ أَبُو عُمَرَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْبَرِّ، وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ بَعْضَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتِ فَقَالَ: وَقَدْ زَادَ فِيهَا أَهْلُ الشَّامِ، وَلَمْ أَرَ لِذِكْرِهِ وَجْهًا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۵۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1242
> *English:* "أبو عمر بن عبد البر, having mentioned some of these verses, said: the people of الشام added to them, and I see no reason to mention it."

**عبرت:** The people closest to the quarrel were the ones who insisted on telling you which lines were forged.

**Hands-up?** Ask the room, before telling it: if a line was added to a famous poem thirteen centuries ago, who would know?

### TSA/E-SK56 · Why المدينہ did not stop it
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** written centuries later `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير asks the question the room will ask: how was the caliph killed in المدينہ, with senior Companions living in it? He answers it in four numbered points. Most of them did not believe it would come to killing — the rebels had asked for three things and killing was the least likely. The Companions did resist, until he put them under oath. The rebels chose the week المدينہ was away at the pilgrimage and the armies had not yet arrived. And they were close to two thousand fighting men, while the fighting men of المدينہ were scattered on the frontiers.

**The statement:**
> أحدها: أن كثيرًا منهم بل أكثرهم أو كلّهم لم يكن يظنّ أنه يبلغ الأمر إلى قتله

> *English:* "The first of them: that many of them — rather most of them, or all of them — did not think the matter would reach his killing."

**عبرت:** People do not resist the disaster they cannot yet imagine.

**Hands-up?** no

### TSA/E-SK57 · الذہبی's verdict, and where the judgement goes
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** written in the eighth century AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير closes his whole chapter by quoting his own teacher الذہبی رحمہ اللہ, and says he is giving the words letter for letter. الذہبی does not assign blame to any Companion. He records what became of the killers, what became of those who stood aside, who held power afterwards and for how long — and then hands the judgement over. It is the natural place for a speaker to stop, because it is where the historian stopped.

**The statement:**
> الذين قتلوه أو ألَّبوا عليه قتلوا إلى عفو الله ورحمته، والذين خَذلوه خُذلوا وتنَغَّصَ عيشهم ... فالحكم لله العلي الكبير.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3503
> *English:* "Those who killed him, or stirred people against him, were themselves killed — to God's pardon and mercy; and those who forsook him were forsaken, and their lives were made bitter. … The judgement belongs to God, the Most High, the Most Great."

**عبرت:** The scholars who knew the most about this night are the ones who refused to pass sentence on it.

### TSA/E-SK58 · Eighty-two, or sixty-three
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 18 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** How old was he? البدایہ lists: past eighty-two, which is its own view; eighty-two and some months; eighty-four; eighty-eight or ninety; seventy-five, which it calls very strange; and sixty-three, which it calls stranger still. الکامل adds eighty-six. The caliphate is easier: twelve years less twelve days, because the bayʿah was at the head of المحرم in the year twenty-four — though الکامل knows a reckoning of twelve days less eight.

**The statement:**
> وعن هشام بن الكلبي [أنه] توفي عن خمس وسبعين سنة، وهذا غريب جدًا، وأغرب منه ما رواه (سيف) بن عمر عن مشايخه ... أنهم قالوا: قتل عثمان ﵁ عن ثلاث وستين سنة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3490
> *English:* "From هشام بن الكلبي: that he died at seventy-five years — and this is very strange; and stranger still is what سيف بن عمر transmitted from his shaykhs, that they said عثمان was killed at sixty-three years."

**عبرت:** Recorded so that nobody re-researches it; the ages are not settled and the slide should not settle them.

## علي ؓ, and the بيعة of 35 AH

*Source note: [`ali-the-man-and-the-bayah.md`](../docs/research/ali-the-man-and-the-bayah.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### ATM/E-AL1 · The cousin the Prophet ﷺ raised in his own house
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before the bi'tha `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة lights; a single household marked.

**What happened:** A year of famine came on مكة, and أبو طالب had four sons to feed. His nephew Muhammad ﷺ took
the youngest of them into his own household. So the boy who would one day be the fourth caliph grew up in that
house, before there was a Qurʾān to hear in it. His brothers were طالب, عقيل and جعفر, and there were ten years
between each of them and the next, which is why he was so much younger than the rest. His mother was
فاطمة بنت أسد, and she accepted Islam and made the hijra with the others.

**The statement:**
> وكان سبب إسلام عليّ صغيراً أنه كان في كفالة رسول الله ﷺ، لأنه كان قد أصابتهم سنةُ مجاعةٍ، فأخذه من أبيه، فكان عنده (٥)
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3541
> *English:* "The cause of علي's accepting Islam as a child was that he was in the care of the Messenger of God ﷺ, because a year of famine had struck them, so he took him from his father and he was with him."

**عبرت:** A household is where faith is first heard, and the youngest in it hears it first of all.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL2 · First of the boys, first of the women, first of the men
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the first years at مكة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** People argue about who accepted Islam first, and the argument is old. ابن كثير settles it by
refusing to rank anyone. He gives four firsts, each in its own class: علي was the first of the boys, خديجة the
first of the women, زيد بن حارثة the first of the freedmen, and أبو بكر the first of the free men. And when a
report comes to him saying علي himself claimed to be the first of all, he writes that it does not reach him with
a sound chain, and that the many reports to the same effect are rejected. Our own historian will not let the
argument start.

**The statement:**
> ويقال إنه أول من أسلم (٢) من الغلمان، كما أن خديجة أول من أسلمت (٣) من النساء، وزيد بن حارثة أول من أسلم من الموالي، وأبو بكر الصديق أول من أسلم من الرجال الأحرار (٤).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3541
> *English:* "And it is said that he was the first of the boys to accept Islam, just as خديجة was the first of the women, and زيد بن حارثة the first of the freedmen, and أبو بكر الصديق the first of the free men."

**عبرت:** When a question has four true answers, the man who insists on one is not seeking the truth.

**Hands-up?** Who do you think was the first person to accept Islam? *(Take three answers, then give the four
firsts. Do not correct anybody — all three answers will be on the page.)*

### ATM/E-AL3 · The debts and the deposits left behind in مكة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۱ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة → المدينة, with one dot staying behind for some days.

**What happened:** When the Prophet ﷺ left مكة he did not leave it clean. People had entrusted goods to him for
safekeeping, and there were debts. He left علي behind with orders: settle the debts, return every deposit to
its owner, and then follow. So the last Muslim business transacted in مكة was the handing back of other people's
property to the very people who were driving the Muslims out. He carried out what he was ordered, and then he
came.

**The statement:**
> وهاجر عليٌّ بعد خروج رسول الله ﷺ من مكة وكان قد أمره بقضاء ديونه وردّ ودائعه، ثم يلحق به، فامتثل ما أمره به
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3541
> *English:* "And علي made the hijra after the Messenger of God ﷺ had gone out from مكة; for he had ordered him to settle his debts and return the deposits entrusted to him, and then to follow him. And he carried out what he had been ordered."

**عبرت:** A trust is not cancelled by the bad conduct of the one who gave it.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL4 · The banner at بدر, at twenty years old
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بدر lights on the Line.

**What happened:** At بدر he was one of the three who went out for the single combat before the armies joined —
with his uncle حمزة and his cousin عبيدة بن الحارث — and a verse of the Qurʾān came down about those six men.
ابن عباس is reported to have said that the Prophet ﷺ handed him the banner that day, and that he was twenty
years old. As for the famous cry about the sword ذو الفقار that people repeat, ابن عساكر writes on the same page
that the report is مرسل, and that the sword was the Prophet's ﷺ own share of the spoil at بدر, given to علي
afterwards.

**The statement:**
> وقال الحكم وغيره عن مِقْسَم عن ابن عباس قال (٣): دفعَ النبيُّ الرايةَ يوم بدرٍ إلى عليّ وهو ابن عشرين سنة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3542
> *English:* "الحكم and others said, from مقسم, from ابن عباس: the Prophet handed the banner on the day of بدر to علي, and he was twenty years old."

**عبرت:** A man's first great trust is usually given to him long before he feels ready for it.

### ATM/E-AL5 · The right wing at أحد, and a face washed clean of blood
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أحد lights.

**What happened:** At أحد the army was drawn up with حمزة in the centre, المنذر بن عمرو on the left, and علي on
the right, holding the banner after مصعب بن عمير was killed. He fought hard that day. And when the battle broke
and the Prophet ﷺ was wounded in the face and his tooth broken, it was علي who washed the blood from his face.
Two years earlier he had been a young man at a duel; that day he was doing the work that anyone in a family
does when the head of it is hurt.

**The statement:**
> وغسل عن وجه النبي ﷺ الدم الذي كان أصابه من الجراح حين شُجَّ في وجهه (٨) وكُسرتْ (٩) رباعيتُه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3542
> *English:* "And he washed from the face of the Prophet ﷺ the blood that had come from the wounds when his face was cut and his tooth broken."

**عبرت:** On the worst day, the useful man is the one who does the plain nearest thing.

### ATM/E-AL6 · The banner of خيبر, and the eye that never ached again
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۷ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** خيبر lights.

**What happened:** The night before the assault the Prophet ﷺ said that he would give the banner the next day to
a man who loved God and His Messenger, and whom God and His Messenger loved. The army spent the whole night
wondering which of them it would be. In the morning he called for علي — who could hardly see, his eyes were so
sore — prayed for him, and spat into his eye. It never ached again. He was given the banner, and the fortress
fell. Years later, people noticed that he wore summer clothes in winter and winter clothes in summer, and asked
him why; he told them what the Prophet ﷺ had prayed for him on that morning.

**The statement:**
> "لأعطينَّ الرايةَ غداً رجلاً يحبُّ الله ورسولَه، ويحبُّه الله ورسولُه" فباتَ الناس [ليلتهم] يدوكون أيّهم يعطاها، فدعا علياً -وكان أرمدَ- فدعا له، وبصقَ في عينه فلم يرمد بعدها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3543
> *English:* "'I shall certainly give the banner tomorrow to a man who loves God and His Messenger, and whom God and His Messenger love.' The people spent their night wondering which of them would be given it. Then he called علي — who had sore eyes — and prayed for him and spat into his eye, and it never ached again."

**عبرت:** The man chosen for the work is not always the man who looks fit for it that morning.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL7 · The door of خيبر, and the number nobody can agree on
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** ۷ھ `[SOURCED as a disagreement]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A Jewish fighter struck his shield out of his hand, and he took hold of a door at the fortress
and used it as a shield instead, and kept it in his hand until the place was taken. Afterwards the Muslims tried
to shift the door. Here our books stop agreeing with each other. In one chain, أبو رافع says that he and seven
men could not turn it over. In another, eight could not. In a third, from جابر, it is said that only forty men
could carry it — and الذهبي notes on his page that this third chain is carried by one man alone.

**The statement:**
> قال أبو رافع: فلقد رأيتني أنا وسبعة (معي) نجتهد أن نقلب ذلك الباب على ظهره يوم خيبر فلم نستطع.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3543
> *English:* "أبو رافع said: I saw myself and seven others with me struggling to turn that door over on the day of خيبر, and we were not able to."

**عبرت:** A number that grows in the telling is the first thing a careful reader checks.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL8 · What ابن كثير refuses to let you say about him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the eighth century `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Three of the most-repeated stories about علي are thrown out on these very pages, by the Sunni
historian whose book we are reading. The claim that he himself said "I was the first to accept Islam" — not
soundly chained to him. The wording "you are my brother, my heir, my successor, and the best of those given
command after me" — forged, says ابن كثير, and contrary to what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs. The tale of
his fighting the jinn at a well near الجحفة — no basis at all, the fabrication of ignorant story-tellers.

**The statement:**
> فإنَّ في بعضها: " أنت أخي ووارثي وخليفتي وخير من أُمِّر بعدي" وهذا الحديث موضوع مخالف لما ثبت في الصحيحين (١) وغيرهما، والله أعلم (٢).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3542
> *English:* "For in some of them: 'You are my brother, my heir, my successor, and the best of those given command after me.' This hadith is forged, contrary to what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and elsewhere. And God knows best."

**عبرت:** Honouring a man and believing everything said about him are two different things, and the second is
not honour.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL9 · Left behind at تبوك, with the women and the children
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۹ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, with the army's arrow heading north to تبوك.

**What happened:** The Prophet ﷺ marched for تبوك and left علي in charge of المدينة. علي was not pleased and
said so: are you leaving me behind with the women and the children? The answer he was given is the one sentence
about him that is quoted more than any other — and it ends with a clause that closes every door it might seem
to open: except that there is no prophet after me. He stayed, and the city was kept.

**The statement:**
> فقال (٧): " ألا ترضى أن تكون مني بمنزلة هارون من موسى غير أنه لا نبي بعدي".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3543
> *English:* "He said: 'Are you not content to be to me as هارون was to موسى, except that there is no prophet after me?'"

**عبرت:** Being left behind can be the harder assignment, and it is still an assignment.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL10 · Sent to اليمن to judge, with no training in judging
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** before ۱۰ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** اليمن lights.

**What happened:** He was sent to اليمن as commander and judge, and خالد بن الوليد went with him. He told
afterwards that he objected: he was young, and he had no knowledge of judging. The Prophet ﷺ struck him on the
chest and told him to go — God would guide his heart and steady his tongue. And he said that after that day he
never doubted in a judgement between two men. Long afterwards عمر would say that he sought refuge in God from a
hard case with no أبو الحسن in the room to meet it.

**The statement:**
> بعثني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى اليمن، وأنا حديث السن، ليس لي علم بالقضاء، فضرب صدري، وقال: "اذهب فإن الله سيهدي قلبك ويثبت لسانك". قال: فما شككت في قضاء بين اثنين بعد.
> — سير أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۳۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1378
> *English:* "'The Prophet ﷺ sent me to اليمن, and I was young in years and had no knowledge of judging. So he struck my chest and said: Go — God will guide your heart and steady your tongue. And I never after that doubted in a judgement between two men.'"

**عبرت:** A man may be sent to do what he has not learned, and be taught by the doing of it.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL11 · أبو تراب — the name he liked best of all his names
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** There had been some quarrel between علي and فاطمة, and he had walked out of the house rather
than say another word. The Prophet ﷺ came looking for him, and was told he was lying down in the mosque. He came
and found him asleep on his side, his cloak fallen away, dust on him. And he began to brush the dust off him,
saying: get up, father of dust. Get up, father of dust. Long afterwards a governor ordered سهل بن سعد to curse
"أبو تراب", and سهل answered by telling him where the name came from, and that علي had no name dearer to him
than that one. مسلم narrates it.

**The statement:**
> فجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يمسح عنه التراب ويقول: "قم أبا تراب قم أبا تراب". أخرجه مسلم.
> — سير أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۲۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1366
> *English:* "And the Messenger of God ﷺ began to wipe the dust from him, saying: 'Get up, father of dust; get up, father of dust.'"

**عبرت:** The name a man is proudest of is often the one given to him on his worst morning.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL12 · The best judge among us, said عمر ؓ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۱۳–۲۳ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي puts the testimonies side by side and they take about thirty seconds to read out.
سعيد بن المسيب: not one of the Companions used to say "ask me" except علي. ابن عباس, reporting عمر: علي is the
best judge among us, and أُبَيّ the best reciter. ابن مسعود: we used to say that the best judge in المدينة was
علي. And عمر again, in one line that is worth the whole page.

**The statement:**
> وقال ابن المسيب، عن عمر، قال: أعوذ بالله من معضلة ليس لها أبو حسن.
> — سير أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۳۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1379
> *English:* "ابن المسيب said, from عمر: I seek refuge in God from a hard case with no أبو الحسن to meet it."

### ATM/E-AL13 · Nothing but the Book of God, and one sheet
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Already in his own lifetime people were saying that the household of the Prophet ﷺ had been
given some private text, some secret reading that the rest of the community did not have. He answered it from
the pulpit himself. There is nothing with us that we read except the Book of God — and this one sheet, and on it
is the ages of camels for the زكاة, and something about the compensation for wounds. Anyone who claims otherwise
has lied.

**The statement:**
> خطبنا علي، فقال: من زعم أن عندنا شيئا نقرؤه إلا كتاب الله وهذه الصحيفة، وفيها أسنان الإبل وشيء من الجراحات، فقد كذب.
> — سير أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۳۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1378
> *English:* "علي addressed us and said: 'Whoever claims that we have anything we read other than the Book of God and this sheet — and in it are the ages of camels and something about wounds — has lied.'"

**عبرت:** A claim made on a man's behalf that he himself denied is not loyalty to him.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL14 · What he said about the three who came before him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate, from the منبر at الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

**What happened:** He was caliph, at الكوفة, in the seat of his own command, and this is what he said from the
pulpit about the men who had held the office before him: the best of this Ummah after its Prophet is أبو بكر,
then عمر — and if I wished to name the third, I would name him. And as he came down from the pulpit he said:
then عثمان. Then عثمان. ابن كثير writes that this is established from him by mass transmission. It settles, in
his own voice, a question that other people have spent centuries arguing about on his behalf.

**The statement:**
> فقال: أيها الناس إن خير هذه الأمة بعد نبيّها أبو بكر، ثم عمر، ولو شئت أن أسمي الثالث لسميت. وعنه أنه قال وهو نازل من المنبر: ثم عثمان ثم عثمان.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3757
> *English:* "He said: 'O people, the best of this Ummah after its Prophet is أبو بكر, then عمر; and if I wished to name the third I would name him.' And it is transmitted from him that he said, as he came down from the منبر: 'Then عثمان, then عثمان.'"

**عبرت:** The people who honour a man most loudly are sometimes the last to accept what he actually said.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL15 · Five days, and nobody who would take it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, with three arrows in from مصر, الكوفة and البصرة.

**What happened:** The caliph was dead and the city was full of armed men from three provinces who had come to
depose him and had killed him instead. For five days المدينة had no ruler but the commander of the Egyptians.
The Egyptians pressed علي, and he kept escaping from them into the walled gardens. The Kufans looked for
الزبير and could not find him. The Basrans asked طلحة and he would not answer. So they went to سعد بن أبي وقاص,
who refused, and to ابن عمر, who refused. And they stood there, at a loss.

**The statement:**
> بقيتِ المدينةُ خمسةَ أيامٍ بعد مقتل عثمان وأميرُها الغافقيُّ بن حرب، يلتمسون منْ يُجيبهم إلى القيام بالأمر.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3546
> *English:* "المدينة remained five days after the killing of عثمان, its commander being الغافقي بن حرب, while they looked for someone who would answer them and undertake the affair."

**عبرت:** A community that has torn down its government discovers that nobody wants to be the next one.

**Hands-up?** If you had been in المدينة that week, and they came to your door — would you have said yes?

### ATM/E-AL16 · A bolted garden door in المدينة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة; one walled garden marked.

**What happened:** He did not want it. He said so more than once, and when they kept coming he went out of the
city into the walled garden of بني عمرو بن مبذول and bolted the door behind him. They came anyway. They knocked,
and then they came in over him, and they had brought طلحة and الزبير with them. Their argument was one sentence
long: this affair cannot go on without a commander. They did not leave him until he agreed.

**The statement:**
> وفر منهم إلى حائط بني عمرو بن مبذول، وأغلق بابه فجاء الناس فطرقوا الباب وولجوا عليه، وجاءوا معهم بطلحة والزبير، فقالوا له: إن هذا الأمر لا يمكن بقاؤه بلا أمير، ولم يزالوا به حتى أجاب.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۹۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3545
> *English:* "And he fled from them into the walled garden of بني عمرو بن مبذول and bolted its door. The people came and knocked at the door and came in upon him, and they brought طلحة and الزبير with them. They said to him: 'This affair cannot go on without a commander.' And they did not leave him until he agreed."

**عبرت:** The man who runs from office is usually the one most fit to hold it, and least likely to enjoy it.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL17 · One day — or we kill them all tomorrow
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة under armed occupation.

**What happened:** This is the sentence that explains the whole week. The provincials gathered the people of
المدينة and told them: you are the people of the شورى, you bind the imamate, your ruling binds the Ummah. So
choose a man and we will follow you. And we have given you until the end of today. If you have not finished by
then, tomorrow we kill علي, and طلحة, and الزبير, and a great many people besides. **That is the room in which
the fourth caliph was chosen.** Everything that follows for five years is already in that sentence.

**The statement:**
> وَقَدْ أَجَّلْنَاكُمْ يَوْمَكُمْ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَفْرُغُوا لَنَقْتُلَنَّ غَدًا عَلِيًّا وَطَلْحَةَ وَالزُّبَيْرَ وَأُنَاسًا كَثِيرًا!
> — الكامل في التاريخ ج۲ ص۵۵۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1245
> *English:* "'And we have given you the term of your day; and by God, if you have not finished, we shall kill tomorrow علي and طلحة and الزبير and many people besides.'"

**عبرت:** A decision taken with a sword at the door is still a decision, but nobody afterwards agrees what it
meant.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL18 · Better a minister than a commander
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** They told him there had to be an imam. He told them he had no need of their affair, and
whomever they chose he would accept. They said they would choose nobody else. They came back to him again and
again, and at last they told him they knew of no one with a longer precedence in Islam or a closer kinship to
the Messenger of God ﷺ. And he gave them the answer that says exactly how he saw himself: do not do it — I will
be better to you as a minister than I will be as a commander.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: لَا تَفْعَلُوا فَإِنِّي أَكُونُ وَزِيرًا خَيْرًا مِنْ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَمِيرًا.
> — الكامل في التاريخ ج۲ ص۵۵۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1243
> *English:* "He said: 'Do not do it; for I shall be a better minister than I shall be a commander.'"

**عبرت:** Knowing which of the two you are is a rarer gift than either.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL19 · Not in secret, and nowhere but the mosque
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة; the mosque marked.

**What happened:** When at last he agreed, he set one condition, and it was about where. He was in his house —
or in that walled garden — and men were ready to take his hand there and then. He refused. My بيعة will not be
a hidden thing, and it will be nowhere but in the mosque. So he walked to the mosque, in a plain waist-wrapper
and a silk turban, carrying his own sandals in his hand and leaning on his bow, and climbed the pulpit, and they
gave it to him where the whole city could see.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: فَفِي الْمَسْجِدِ، فَإِنَّ بَيْعَتِي لَا تَكُونُ خُفْيَةً وَلَا تَكُونُ إِلَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
> — الكامل في التاريخ ج۲ ص۵۵۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1243

### ATM/E-AL20 · The first hand was a withered hand
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The first man to come forward and give his hand was طلحة, and the right hand he put out had

crowd who read omens saw it and said out loud: to God we belong — the first hand to give the بيعة is a withered
hand. This affair will not be completed. Both our books record the remark, though they disagree about who made
it. Nobody in that mosque forgot it afterwards.

**عبرت:** A hand is honoured for what it lost and where it lost it; reading a fate into it is the crowd's work,
not God's.

### ATM/E-AL21 · Three dates for one بيعة — and why
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED as a disagreement]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Ask our books what day he was given the بيعة and you get three answers. Saturday the
nineteenth of ذو الحجة. Thursday the twenty-fourth for the first hand and Friday the twenty-fifth for the rest.
Friday with five nights of the month remaining. And ابن الأثير, having given his own date, quietly supplies the
reason they differ: whatever day the hands were actually given, the people reckoned his reign from the day
عثمان was killed. A historian's problem, and a real one, and the honest thing is to say so.

**The statement:**
> وَبُويِعَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ لِخَمْسٍ بَقِينَ مِنْ ذِي الْحِجَّةِ، وَالنَّاسُ يَحْسِبُونَ بَيْعَتَهُ مِنْ [يَوْمِ] قُتِلَ عُثْمَانُ.
> — الكامل في التاريخ ج۲ ص۵۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1246

**عبرت:** When two dates disagree, the honest report keeps both and says which is which.

### ATM/E-AL22 · Not until the people give it

brought ابن عمر, who said exactly the same thing, and would not name a guarantor. الأشتر offered to strike his

### ATM/E-AL23 · The men who are said to have held back — and the list that contradicts itself
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED as a disagreement]` · **Map:** No map.

page he gives الواقدي's account, which names seven completely different men and then says that not one of the
Anṣār held back at all. ابن الأثير repeats the ten and adds that they were عثمانية. Three lists, and they do not
fit together.

> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3546

**عبرت:** Where the reports disagree, the safest thing a Muslim can say about a Companion is: I do not know.

### ATM/E-AL24 · طلحة ؓ and الزبير ؓ — what the books will not settle
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED as a disputed report]` · **Map:** المدينة → مكة, four months later.

**What happened:** Both of them gave the بيعة. That much every account agrees on. What is disputed is how. One
account has علي offering them a choice — if you wish, give it to me; if you wish, I will give it to you — and
them answering, no, we give it to you. Another has them brought in under guard and saying afterwards that they
had feared for their lives. الزبير is reported to have said he gave it with the sword-edge at his neck. And
ابن الأثير, having set all of it out, writes four plain words: **وفي الزبير اختلاف** — concerning الزبير there
is disagreement. Four months later both men left for مكة.

**The statement:**
> ثُمَّ جِيءَ بِالزُّبَيْرِ فَقَالَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ وَبَايَعَ، وَفِي الزُّبَيْرِ اخْتِلَافٌ

> *English:* "Then الزبير was brought, and he said the like of that and gave the بيعة. And concerning الزبير there is disagreement."

**عبرت:** When the record itself says "there is disagreement", a man who announces a verdict has left history
for something else.

### ATM/E-AL25 · The first sermon, and the men who shouted it down
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة; the mosque.

**What happened:** From the pulpit, his first sermon as caliph. God has sent down a guiding Book that makes clear
the good and the evil, so take the good and leave the evil. God has made sanctities that nobody can claim not to
know — and He has set the sanctity of a Muslim above all of them. And you will be questioned even about the
ground you walk on and the animals in your care. Then, before he had come down, the armed provincials at the
back of the mosque answered him in verse: take it, and beware, أبو الحسن — we twist this affair as a rope is
twisted. And he answered them in the same metre.

> اتقوا الله عباده في عباده وبلاده، فإنكم مسؤولون (حتى) عن البقاع والبهائم

> *English:* "Fear God, His servants, in regard to His servants and His lands; for you will be questioned even about the places and the beasts."

**عبرت:** A ruler's first speech tells you what he intends; the crowd's first answer tells you what he will get.

### ATM/E-AL27 · Sound advice on one day, deliberate bad advice on the next
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۵–۳۶ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** المغيرة بن شعبة came in and advised him: leave عثمان's governors where they are; once their
obedience has reached you, then replace whom you like. The next day he came back and advised the exact opposite:
dismiss them all now, so you learn who obeys you. علي put the two pieces of advice to ابن عباس, who said: he
counselled you sincerely yesterday and deceived you today. When that reached المغيرة, he did not deny it. Yes,
he said. I gave him sincere advice; and when he would not take it, I deceived him. Then he left for مكة.

**The statement:**
> فبلغ ذلك المغيرةَ فقال: نعم نصحتُه فلما لم يقبل غششتُه ثم خرج المغيرة فلحق بمكة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3548
> *English:* "That reached المغيرة, and he said: 'Yes — I counselled him sincerely, and when he would not accept it I deceived him.' Then المغيرة went out and joined مكة."

**عبرت:** A man who will deceive you the day after you refuse him was never truly advising you.

### ATM/E-AL28 · ابن عباس ؓ describes the next five years, before they happen
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۵ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الشام and العراق both flash.

killed our man. They will stir people up against you, الشام will break away, and so will العراق — and I do not

**عبرت:** Counsel refused is not counsel wasted; it becomes the record by which the decision is understood.

### ATM/E-AL29 · A governor turned back at تبوك by men on horses
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۶ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة → تبوك, and the arrow stops dead.

**What happened:** He appointed سهل بن حنيف over الشام in place of معاوية, and سهل rode north. At تبوك — still
hundreds of miles short of دمشق — horsemen met him on the road. Who are you? A governor. Over what? Over الشام.
And they said: if عثمان sent you, welcome. If it was anybody else, go back. He said: have you not heard what has
happened? They said: yes. We have heard. And he turned around and rode back to المدينة. **Nobody drew a sword.
The empire simply declined to be governed.**

**The statement:**
> فقالوا: إن كان عثمانُ بعثَكَ فحيَّهلا بك، وإن كانَ غيرُه فارجعْ. فقال: أوما سمعتُم الذي كان؟ قالوا: بلى، فرجع إلى عليٍّ.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3549
> *English:* "They said: 'If عثمان sent you, then welcome to you; and if it was someone other than he, then go back.' He said: 'Have you not heard what has happened?' They said: 'Yes.' And he went back to علي."

**عبرت:** A state ends not when its capital falls but when its orders stop being obeyed on the road.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL30 · Turned back at زبالة; مصر split three ways
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۳۶ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Three arrows out of المدينة — one stopped at زبالة, one reaching مصر and fragmenting, one reaching البصرة.

**What happened:** Five governors went out; two arrived and held. عمارة بن شهاب, riding for الكوفة, was met at
زبالة by طليحة بن خويلد — the same طليحة of the ردة, now riding for عثمان's blood — who told him to turn around
or lose his neck, and he turned around. قيس بن سعد got into مصر only by telling the horsemen at أيلة that he was
one of عثمان's own broken party. And when he got there the province had already split into three: one part with
him, one part withdrawn at خرنبا, and one part saying we are with علي so long as he does not take retaliation
from our brothers.

**عبرت:** When a province begins bargaining with its own governor, the bargaining has already replaced the

### ATM/E-AL31 · A shirt on the pulpit of دمشق
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۵–۳۶ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة → دمشق; دمشق lights and stays lit.

**What happened:** النعمان بن بشير rode out of المدينة carrying the shirt عثمان had been killed in, still stained
with his blood. It was brought to معاوية in الشام, and he set it on the pulpit where the people could see it,
and called them to take up the vengeance. And they wept around that pulpit — ابن كثير says they went on weeping
around it for a year. When the messenger from دمشق came to المدينة months later he put a number on it: sixty
thousand old men weeping beneath عثمان's shirt, and they have clothed the pulpit of دمشق in it. Against that,
a letter of appointment carried by one man on a camel had no chance at all.

**The statement:**
> وَتَرَكْتُ سِتِّينَ أَلْفَ شَيْخٍ تَبْكِي تَحْتَ قَمِيصِ عُثْمَانَ، وَهُوَ مَنْصُوبٌ لَهُمْ قَدْ أَلْبَسُوهُ مِنْبَرَ دِمَشْقَ.

> *English:* "'And I have left sixty thousand old men weeping beneath the shirt of عثمان, set up for them — they have clothed the منبر of دمشق in it.'"

**عبرت:** A grief that is looked at every day does not heal; it hardens into a demand.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL32 · A sealed scroll with nothing written inside it
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر–ربيع الأول ۳۶ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** دمشق → المدينة.

**What happened:** In the third month after the killing, معاوية sent a man of بني عبس to المدينة with a sealed
scroll addressed to علي, and told him to carry it held high as he came in. People followed him through the
streets to see it. علي broke the seal and there was no letter inside. So he asked the messenger: what is behind
you? The man asked whether he was safe, and was told that a messenger is not killed. Then he delivered the real
message, which was that الشام would accept nothing but retaliation — and he named the neck it wanted. And علي
answered: am I not bereaved as عثمان's own kin are bereaved? O God, I declare myself quit before You of the
blood of عثمان.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: أَمِنِّي يَطْلُبُونَ دَمَ عُثْمَانَ، أَلَسْتُ مَوْتُورًا كَتِرَةِ عُثْمَانَ؟ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَبْرَأُ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ دَمِ عُثْمَانَ!
> — الكامل في التاريخ ج۲ ص۵۶۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1256
> *English:* "He said: 'Is it from me that they seek the blood of عثمان? Am I not bereaved as عثمان's own kin are bereaved? O God, I declare myself quit before You of the blood of عثمان!'"

**عبرت:** An empty letter carried in public says more than a full one delivered in private, and that is what it
was for.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL33 · Out of المدينة, and never back
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۶ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة dims; the arrow goes to البصرة, and the capital marker moves to الكوفة and stays there.

**What happened:** ابن عباس advised him not to leave المدينة for العراق, and he refused the advice. He appointed
a deputy over the city — the books do not agree which man — and marched out at the head of an army. He never
came back. From that year the pulpit he preached from is the pulpit of الكوفة; his seat of command is at
الكوفة; the trouble that ends his life comes out of الكوفة; and he is buried there. **Our books nowhere record
a decision to move the capital.** It simply moved, because he did, and then he could not return.

**The statement:**
> ونهى ابن عباس علياً فيما أشار عليه أن يقبل من هؤلاء الذين يحسِّنون إليه الرحيل (٣) إلى العراق، ومفارقة المدينة، فأبى عليه ذلك كله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3549
> *English:* "And ابن عباس forbade علي, among the counsel he gave him, to accept from those who were making the departure to العراق and the leaving of المدينة look good to him. But he refused him all of that."

**عبرت:** The capital of Islam left المدينة without anyone deciding that it should, and it never returned.

the marker.)*

### ATM/E-AL34 · One flask of perfume, and nothing else
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He stood on the pulpit and swore to the whole congregation — by God, beside whom there is no
god — that he had taken nothing of their wealth, neither little nor much, except this. And he pulled a small
flask of perfume out of the sleeve of his shirt, and said: a Persian landholder gave it to me as a gift. He was
the ruler of an empire that ran from Egypt to Persia. سفيان الثوري, a hundred years later, put it in one line:
he never laid one brick on another; his grain used to come to him from المدينة in a sack.

**The statement:**
> أيها الناس! والله الذي لا إله إلا هو ما رزأتُ (٤) من مالكم [لا] قليلًا ولا كثيرًا إلَّا هذه - وأخرج قارورة من كُمِّ قميصه فيها طيب -. فقال: أهداها إليَّ الدهقان
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3742
> *English:* "'O people — by God, beside whom there is no god, I have taken nothing from your wealth, neither little nor much, except this' — and he brought out from the sleeve of his shirt a flask with perfume in it — and said: 'The dihqān gave it to me as a gift.'"

**عبرت:** The account a ruler gives of himself is worth exactly as much as the state of his own house.

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate, at الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** He lost a coat of mail on the road to صفين, and later found it in the hands of a Christian
man. So he took him to court — to شريح, the judge he had himself appointed. He came in and sat down beside the
judge, and explained why: if my opponent were a Muslim I would sit with him, but he is a Christian. Then he made
his claim. شريح turned to him and asked the ordinary question: Commander of the Faithful, have you any evidence?
And علي laughed and said, شريح is right, I have none. So the judge gave the armour to the Christian. The man
walked a few steps, came back, and said: I bear witness that these are the judgements of prophets. The
Commander of the Faithful brings me in to his own judge, and his judge rules against him. And he accepted Islam,
and told them the armour had been علي's all along. الشعبي says that a man who saw him later saw him fighting at
النهروان, on علي's side.

**The statement:**
> فقال: أما أنا فأشهد أن هذه أحكام الأنبياء، أمير المؤمنين يدنيني إلى قاضيه [وقاضيه] يقضي عليه، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدًا عبده ورسوله، الدرع والله درعك يا أمير المؤمنين
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3745
> *English:* "He said: 'As for me, I bear witness that these are the judgements of the prophets. The Commander of the Faithful brings me near to his judge, and his judge rules against him. I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger. The coat of mail, by God, is your coat of mail, Commander of the Faithful.'"

**عبرت:** A law that binds the man at the top is the only law anyone else can be asked to respect.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL36 · The markets, the whip, and the weeping girl
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He walked the markets himself, alone, as caliph — with a whip in his hand, not to beat anyone
but to be seen. Give full measure and weight. Do not inflate the meat to make it look bigger. Nothing floating
dead is sold in our market. Sell, and do not swear by God over it — an oath moves the goods and wipes out the
blessing. One day he came on a slave-girl crying: a man had sold her dates for a dirham and her owners had sent
her back with them, and he would not take them. And علي told the man: take your dates and give her back her
dirham, for she has no say in this. Then he went on walking.

**The statement:**
> علي: خذ تمرك وأعطها درهمًا فإنها ليس لها أمر، فدفعه، فقلت: أتدري من هذا؟
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3745
> *English:* "'…علي: Take your dates and give her a dirham; she has no say in the matter.' So he paid it. I said: 'Do you know who that is?'"
>
> *(The two words «فقال له» that open this sentence stand at the foot of ج۷ ص۵۹۸ —
> (Shamela index 3744). The sentence straddles the page break; quote it from ص۵۹۹ as above.)*

**عبرت:** Government is not only what is decided in the hall; it is what happens to the weakest person in the
market that morning.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL37 · The treasury swept out, and prayed in
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the treasury was full he did not leave it full. He had it distributed until there was
not a dinar or a dirham left in it — saying, to the gold and the silver as he went: deceive somebody other than
me. Then he had the empty room sprinkled with water and prayed two rakʿas in it. He used to do that: sweep out
the treasury himself and pray in it, hoping that the room would bear witness for him on the Day of Judgement
that he had not held the Muslims' money back from them.

**The statement:**
> وقال أبو حيان التيمي: حدثني مجمع، أن عليا -رضي الله عنه- كان يكنس بيت المال ثم يصلي فيه، رجاء أن يشهد له أنه لم يحبس فيه المال عن المسلمين.
> — سير أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۴۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1384
> *English:* "أبو حيان التيمي said: مجمع narrated to me that علي used to sweep out the treasury and then pray in it, hoping that it would bear witness for him that he had not held back the money in it from the Muslims."

**عبرت:** Public money is a trust that is kept by being given out, not by being guarded.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL38 · Today is the training-ground; tomorrow is the race
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He was known for his speech, and this is the shape of it. The world has turned its back and
given notice of farewell; the Hereafter has come forward and looked into view; today is the training-ground and
tomorrow is the race. Each of the two has children, he said on another day, so be children of the Hereafter and
not of the world. And the thing I most fear for you is two things — the following of desire, and the lengthening
of hope.

**The statement:**
> أما بعد فإن الدنيا قد أدبرت وآذنت بوداع، وإن الآخرة قد أقبلت وأشرفت باطلاع، وإن المضمار اليوم وغدًا السباق
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۰۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3748
> *English:* "To proceed: the world has turned its back and given notice of farewell, and the Hereafter has come forward and looked out into view. Today is the training-ground and tomorrow is the race."

**عبرت:** A man who knows which day he is living in does not confuse practice with the event.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL39 · Do not put a screen between yourself and the people
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He wrote a commission for one of his men taking up a district, and in it is the clearest piece
of governance advice in the whole book. Do not let your screen be long over the people in your charge. When
governors screen themselves off from the governed, it is a branch of narrowness and of knowing little. The
screen cuts off the knowledge of what lies on the other side of it — so the great matter becomes small in the
governor's eyes, and the small becomes great, and the good is made to look ugly, and the ugly is made to look
good, and truth gets mixed with falsehood.

**The statement:**
> أما بعد فلا يطولن حجابك على رعيتك، فإن احتجاب الولاة عن الرعية شعبة الضيق، وقلة علم بالأمور
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۰۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3750
> *English:* "To proceed — let not your screen be long over your subjects; for the screening of governors from the subjects is a branch of narrowness and of little knowledge of affairs."

**عبرت:** A ruler who cannot be reached will soon be told only what he wishes to hear.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL40 · Four witnesses, three beards: what he actually looked like
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** — `[SOURCED as a disagreement]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** People who saw him with their own eyes described him, and الذهبي puts four of those
descriptions side by side on one page. أبو رجاء العطاردي: an old man, bald at the crown, thickly haired, of
middle height, heavy of belly, with a great beard. سوادة بن حنظلة: with a yellow beard. الشعبي: with a white
beard — I never saw a greater beard than his. أبو جعفر الباقر: very dark, large-eyed, nearer to short. And on
the same page is the explanation of the beards: محمد ابن الحنفية says his father dyed it with henna once, and
then left it off.

**The statement:**
> وقال الشعبي: رأيت عليا أبيض اللحية، ما رأيت أعظم لحية منه، وفي رأسه زغيبات.
> — سير أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۲۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1367
> *English:* "الشعبي said: I saw علي with a white beard — I never saw a greater beard than his — and on his head a little down."

**عبرت:** Even four men who were in the room describe it differently; that is what it means to know the past
through people.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL41 · فاطمة ؓ, and the house after her
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** ۲ھ onwards `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** فاطمة was his first wife, married after بدر, and he married no one alongside her; she died six
months after her father ﷺ. She bore him الحسن and الحسين — and محسن, who died young — and زينب and أم كلثوم,
and it was أم كلثوم whom عمر married. After her death he married a number of wives. ابن جرير counts fourteen
sons and seventeen daughters in all; الواقدي says the line went on through five of them only. And when الحسن was
born and his father had named him حرب — war — the Prophet ﷺ came and renamed him.

**The statement:**
> فقال: "أروني ابني، ما سمَّيتموه؟ " فقلت: سميته حربًا، فقال: "بل هو حسن"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3696
> *English:* "He said: 'Show me my son. What have you named him?' I said: 'I have named him حرب.' He said: 'No — he is حسن.'"

**عبرت:** A name given in one generation is heard in the next; it is worth choosing carefully.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL42 · Feed him, and give him drink
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۱۷ رمضان ۴۰ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** He went out to the dawn prayer as he did every morning, with a whip in his hand to wake the
sleepers, and he was struck down at the door. The men around him wanted to kill the tribe the killer came from.
He refused: no — imprison him, and treat his captivity well. If I die, kill him; and if I live, then wounds are
a matter of retaliation, and I am the guardian of my own blood. His daughter أم كلثوم stood there saying: what
is between me and the dawn prayer? My husband عمر was killed at the dawn prayer, and my father at the dawn
prayer.

**The statement:**
> فقال: لا ولكن احبسوه وأحسنوا إساره (٣)، فإن مت فاقتلوه وإن عشت فالجروح قصاص.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3757
> *English:* "He said: 'No; but imprison him and treat his captivity well. If I die, kill him; and if I live, then wounds are subject to retaliation.'"

**عبرت:** Justice is measured at the moment when a man has every excuse to abandon it.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL43 · No successor named
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** رمضان ۴۰ھ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** They asked him, as he was dying, to name the next caliph. He would not. I leave you, he said,
as the Messenger of God ﷺ left you; if God wills good for you, He will gather you on the best of you, as He
gathered you on the best of you after the Messenger of God ﷺ. ابن كثير reads that last clause as his
acknowledgement, at the very end of his life, of the merit of أبو بكر — and that reading belongs to ابن كثير,
who says it on the page in his own voice.

**The statement:**
> فقال: لا ولكن أترككم (٤) كما ترككم رسول الله ﷺ، فإن يرد الله بكم خيرًا يجمعكم على خيركم كما جمعكم على خيركم بعد رسول الله ﷺ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3757
> *English:* "He said: 'No; but I leave you as the Messenger of God ﷺ left you. If God wills good for you He will gather you upon the best of you, as He gathered you upon the best of you after the Messenger of God ﷺ.'"

**عبرت:** A man who will not bind those who come after him trusts something larger than his own arrangements.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL44 · A grave nobody can point to
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان ۴۰ھ `[SOURCED as unresolved]` · **Map:** الكوفة, with a question mark.

**What happened:** الحسن prayed over his father and he was buried — and where, our books cannot say. ابن كثير
lists the seat of the caliphate, a chamber near the congregational mosque, البهوفة, الكناسة, the open country,
the wall of the mosque. الذهبي says he was buried by the palace of the command at الكوفة and the grave was
deliberately hidden, so the خوارج would not dig it up. Another report says الحسن moved him to المدينة. And a
third says the box was carried on a camel that was lost in the country of طيئ, and the tribe took it thinking
there was money in it, and buried the dead man in their own land — **and his grave is not known to this day.**
That last sentence is our own historian's.

**The statement:**
> فلما وجدوا بالصندوق (٩) ميتًا دفنوه في بلادهم فلا يعرف قبره إلى الآن
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3757
> *English:* "And when they found a dead man in the box, they buried him in their own country; and his grave is not known to this day."

**عبرت:** The men this Ummah remembers best are often the ones whose graves it cannot find.

**Hands-up?** no

### ATM/E-AL45 · God knows best whether we were right or wrong
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Somebody asked him, during his own reign, what covenant the Prophet ﷺ had left him about the
caliphate. And he answered: none — nothing beyond what he left to everybody. The people fell on عثمان and killed
him, and there were men in that business whose state and whose conduct were worse than mine. Then I saw that I
was the most entitled of them to this affair, and I took it up. And then the last seven words, which are the
safest sentence anyone can carry out of this evening: God knows best whether we were right or wrong.

**The statement:**
> ثم إني رأيت أني أحقهم بهذا الأمر، فوثبت عليه، فالله أعلم أصبنا أم أخطأنا.
> — سير أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۴۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1380
> *English:* "'Then I saw that I was the most entitled of them to this affair, so I took it up. God knows best whether we were right or wrong.'"

**عبرت:** If the man himself would not claim certainty about his own decision, nobody after him is entitled to
claim it for him.

**Hands-up?** no

## وقعة الجمل

*Source note: [`the-battle-of-the-camel.md`](../docs/research/the-battle-of-the-camel.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TBO/E-JM1 · The letters that went to الشام and came back empty
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ lights, a line to دمشق that stops.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had been given the بيعة at المدینہ and he began doing what a caliph does. He
appointed governors to the provinces and he wrote to الشام. The letters went again and again and
nothing came back. It was the third month after the killing before a messenger came from دمشق at
all, and what he brought was not an answer but a report of what he had seen there: sixty thousand
grey-haired men weeping under the shirt of the murdered caliph, hung on the pulpit. علي ؓ heard him
out and answered by clearing himself before Allah of that blood.

**The statement:**
> فقال عليٌّ: اللهم إنّي أبرأ إليك من دم عثمان
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3550
> *English:* "علي said: O Allah, I declare myself free before You of the blood of عثمان."

**عبرت:** When one side stops replying, the argument has already left the room where it could have
been settled.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM2 · The son who asked his father to stop
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The army for الشام was drawn up, the standard given, the officers named, the
deputy left over المدینہ. Everything was ready except the leaving. Then علي ؓ's own son الحسن ؓ came
to him and asked him, plainly and in front of people, to drop the whole thing, because what was in it
was the blood of Muslims and division among them. His father did not take the advice. The son would
say the same thing twice more before the year was out.

**The statement:**
> وجاء إليه ابنهُ الحسنُ بن علي فقال: يا أبتِ دَعْ هذا فإنّ فيه سفكَ دماءِ المسلمين، ووقوع الاختلاف بينهم، فلم يقبل منه ذلك
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3550
> *English:* "And his son الحسن بن علي came to him and said: Father, leave this, for in it is the
> shedding of the blood of the Muslims and the falling of division among them. But he did not accept
> that from him."

**عبرت:** The counsel that is hardest to take is usually the one given by someone with nothing to
gain from giving it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM3 · The wives of the Prophet ﷺ stay on at مكة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 – ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة lights.

**What happened:** The wives of the Prophet ﷺ had gone out that year to the حج, and ابن كثير says
plainly why: they were getting away from the trouble. While they were at مكة the news came that the
caliph had been killed at المدینہ. So instead of going home they stayed where they were. Around them
مكة began to fill: men of بنو أمية who had fled المدینہ, the governor of اليمن with his money, the
governor of البصرة with his.

**The statement:**
> وكان أزواج النبي ﷺ (أمهات المؤمنين) قد خرجْنَ إلى الحج في هذا العام فراراً من الفتنة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3550
> *English:* "And the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, the mothers of the believers, had gone out to the حج
> that year, fleeing the فتنة."

**عبرت:** People who leave a place to avoid trouble often find that the trouble follows the road they
took.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM4 · Two Companions ask leave for عمرة, and go
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الأول–ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** an arrow from المدینہ to مكة.

**What happened:** طلحة ؓ and الزبير ؓ came to علي ؓ and asked his permission to go to مكة for عمرة,
and he gave it. They left, and a great many people left with them. Nothing about the request was
irregular and nothing about the permission was grudging. That is worth saying out loud, because what
followed has been told for centuries as if it began with a rebellion; it began with a permission.

**The statement:**
> واستأذنه طلحةُ والزبيرُ في الاعتمار، فأذن لهما فخرجا إلى مكة وتبعهم خلقٌ كثيرٌ، وجمٌّ غفيرٌ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3551
> *English:* "And طلحة and الزبير asked his leave for عمرة and he gave them leave, and they went out
> to مكة, and a great many people and a vast crowd followed them."

**عبرت:** A parting can be entirely correct at the moment it happens and still be the beginning of
everything that goes wrong afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM5 · I will not go out to fight this year
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** علي ؓ called the people of المدینہ out to march and they were slow. He sent for
عبد الله بن عمر ؓ in particular and urged him. The answer he got was not a refusal of obedience: if
the city goes, I go, hearing and obeying — but I am not going out to fight this year. علي ؓ pressed
him for a guarantor, and when he would not give one, stood as his guarantor himself. Then, when
ابن عمر ؓ was later accused of slipping away to الشام, علي ؓ was the man who said he was
trustworthy.

**The statement:**
> فقال: إنما أنا رجلٌ من أهل المدينة، إن خرجوا خرجت على السمع والطاعة، ولكن لا أخرج للقتال في هذا العام
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3551
> *English:* "He said: I am only a man of the people of المدینہ. If they go out, I go out in hearing
> and obedience — but I will not go out to fight this year."

**عبرت:** Standing aside is a position a man can be asked to account for, and some of the best of them
took it.

**Hands-up?** Has anyone here ever been in a dispute where the honest answer was "I am not going to
take a side"?

### TBO/E-JM6 · Six hundred camels and six hundred thousand dirhams
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** اليمن and البصرة arrows into مكة.

**What happened:** يعلى بن أمية came up to مكة from اليمن, where he had been عثمان ؓ's governor, with
six hundred camels and six hundred thousand dirhams. عبد الله بن عامر came from البصرة with a great
deal of money of his own. When the march was decided, يعلى spent the lot on it, and six hundred men
who had no mount and no equipment were carried on six hundred camels. Both our books give the same
figures, to the camel.

**The statement:**
> وجهز الناس يعلى بن أمية فأنفق فيهم ستمئة بعير وستمئة ألف درهم (٤)، وجهزهم ابن عامر أيضاً بمال كثير
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3551
> *English:* "And يعلى بن أمية equipped the people and spent on them six hundred camels and six
> hundred thousand dirhams; and ابن عامر too equipped them with much wealth."

**عبرت:** Movements are made of conviction, but they travel on somebody's money, and it is worth
knowing whose.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM7 · Three roads argued at مكة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** three arrows out of مكة — الشام, المدینہ, البصرة.

**What happened:** At مكة the question was not whether to move but where. One party said الشام, and
was told معاوية ؓ already has that in hand. One said المدینہ, to ask the caliph himself to hand over
the men who killed عثمان ؓ. One said البصرة, where there was strength to be gathered and where some
of those men were. The argument ran, and البصرة won it. Every one of the three roads was a different
history, and this is the fork the whole evening hangs on.

**The statement:**
> فَاسْتَقَامَ الرَّأْيُ عَلَى الْبَصْرَةِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۷۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1260
> *English:* "So the view settled upon البصرة."

**عبرت:** A decision taken in a crowded room, quickly, can decide the shape of a hundred years.

**Hands-up?** Before I tell you which road they took — which would you have argued for?

### TBO/E-JM8 · The mothers of the believers will go no further
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة.

**What happened:** The other wives of the Prophet ﷺ had agreed to a journey as far as المدینہ. When
the destination changed to البصرة they drew back and said they would go nowhere but المدینہ. حفصة ؓ
had agreed to go, and her brother عبد الله بن عمر ؓ stopped her. So the party that went to البصرة
went without them. Both of our books record this the same way, and it is not a small detail.

**The statement:**
> فلما اتفق الناس على المسير إلى البصرة رجعن عن ذلك وقلن: لا نسير إلى غير المدينة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3551
> *English:* "And when the people agreed on travelling to البصرة, they drew back from that and said:

### TBO/E-JM9 · A camel called عسكر, at a price nobody agrees
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

name was عسكر. About the price the sources simply do not agree, and neither book pretends otherwise.

### TBO/E-JM10 · The Day of Wailing at ذات عرق
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** ذات عرق on the road out of مكة.

**What happened:** The wives of the Prophet ﷺ travelled with أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ as far as a place
called ذات عرق, and there they parted from her. They wept, and the people wept with them. ابن الأثیر
says no day was ever seen with more weeping men and weeping women in it, and he says what they were
weeping for: not for a person and not for a parting, but for Islam. The day was given a name and kept
it. They called it the Day of Wailing.

> وَتَبِعَهَا أُمَّهَاتُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِلَى ذَاتِ عِرْقٍ، فَبَكَوْا عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، فَلَمْ يُرَ يَوْمٌ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ بَاكِيًا وَبَاكِيَةً مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ، فَكَانَ يُسَمَّى يَوْمُ النَّحِيبِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1261
> *English:* "And the mothers of the believers went with her as far as ذات عرق, and they wept over
> Islam; and no day was seen with more weeping men and weeping women than that day, and it was called
> the Day of Wailing."

**عبرت:** The generation that lived it knew what it was losing while it was still losing it.

### TBO/E-JM11 · The dogs of الحوأب
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الحوأب, on the road to البصرة.

**What happened:** The party came by night to a watering place and dogs barked at them out of the
dark. أم المؤمنين ؓ asked what the place was called and was told: الحوأب. She struck her hand on her
hand and said she thought she was going back, and when they asked why, she told them what the
Messenger of Allah ﷺ had once said to his wives about the dogs of الحوأب. She made her camel kneel
and said, take me back. They stayed around her a day and a night. Then her sister's son told her the
man had lied about the name, and then the cry went up that علي ؓ's army had come — and they moved on.

**The statement:**
> ما أظنني إلا راجعة، قالوا: ولم؟ قالت: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول (لنسائه): "ليت شعري أيتكن التي تنبحها كلاب الحَوْأَب" (٣)، ثم ضربت عضدَ بعيرها فأناخته، وقالت: ردّوني ردّوني، وأنا والله صاحبة ماء الحَوْأب.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3552
> *English:* "I do not think I am anything but returning. They said: why? She said: I heard the
> Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to his wives, 'Would that I knew which of you it is at whom the dogs of
> الحوأب will bark.' Then she struck her camel's foreleg and made it kneel and said: take me back,
> take me back — by Allah, I am the woman of the water of الحوأب."

**عبرت:** A warning can be recognised, believed, and then argued away by the people standing nearest
to you.

> going, while the companions of أم المؤمنين were holding their hands back and refusing to fight."

### TBO/E-JM18 · A truce, and one question sent to المدینہ
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a line from البصرة back to المدینہ.

**What happened:** When the fighting had hurt both sides enough, they called for a settlement and
wrote it down. The terms turned on a single question of fact, and they agreed to send a man to
المدینہ to ask it: were طلحة ؓ and الزبير ؓ compelled into the بيعة, or not? If compelled, the
governor leaves البصرة. If not compelled, the two of them leave it. The قاضي of the city, كعب بن
سور, carried the question, and he put it to the people of المدینہ on a Friday.

**The statement:**
> فلما عضتهم الحرب تداعَوْا إلى الصلح على أن يكتبوا بينهم كتاباً ويبعثوا رسولاً إلى أهل المدينة يسأل أهلها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۰۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3554
> *English:* "And when the war bit them they called one another to a settlement, that they should
> write a document between themselves and send a messenger to the people of المدینہ to ask them."

**عبرت:** Men who have just been fighting can still write a fair procedure, if anyone asks them to.

**Hands-up?** If you had been in المدینہ that Friday and been asked that question in public — would
you have answered?

### TBO/E-JM20 · Not a hair left in his face

### TBO/E-JM21 · Who killed you? My pillow
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ربيع الآخر 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة, دار الرزق.

### TBO/E-JM25 · What do you want, and what if they refuse?
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الأولى 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Twice on the way, once at الربذة and once outside البصرة, a man stood up and asked

ladder with the same four rungs. We want a settlement. If they will not answer, we leave them and

### TBO/E-JM26 · The seated is better than the standing
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الأولى 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** علي ؓ sent to الكوفة for men and the governor there, أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ, held the
city back. He did it from the pulpit, in front of the caliph's own envoys, and he did it by quoting
the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on فتنة: the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing
better than the one walking, the one walking better than the one riding. Then he told them to sheathe
their swords, take the heads off their spears and cut their bowstrings.

### TBO/E-JM36 · A book that refuses its own report
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** What علي ؓ said to الزبير ؓ at that meeting is one of the most famous exchanges in
this whole story. It is worth knowing how our own books handle it. ابن كثير writes it out in full,
and then, with no gap and no apology, adds that there is something to be examined in the whole
account. He then names the version he does consider preserved, and his editor notes that the chain of
that one is weak. ابن الأثیر, on the other side, tells the same scene straight through and grades
nothing.

**The statement:**
> ووالله لا أقاتلكَ، وفي هذا السياق كله نظر.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۱۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3564
> *English:* "And by Allah I will not fight you. And in the whole of this account there is something
> to be examined."

**عبرت:** A historian you can trust is one who tells you which of his own pages he is not sure of.

**Hands-up?** no

**What happened:** The champion was taken alive and brought to علي ؓ, and he asked to be spared. The

ordered away and executed. It is one of the only executions in the whole day, and it was not for
fighting on the other side; it was for the men he had killed at the rein.

**The statement:**
> فقال: استبقني يا أمير المؤمنين، فقال: أبعد ثلاثة تقتلهم؟
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۲۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3568
> *English:* "He said: spare me, أمير المؤمنين. He said: after three men you killed?"

**عبرت:** Mercy was the rule of that day, and the exceptions to it were counted.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM47 · The camel brought down
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the camel falls; the battle ends.

**What happened:** Somebody understood that the battle would not stop while the camel stood, and that
أم المؤمنين ؓ had become a target for archers. Our books name two possible authors of the order and
choose neither. A man went in and cut the animal's legs and it went down, and the sound it made is the
one thing everybody who was there remembered. The moment it fell, the army around it broke, and the
battle was over.

**The statement:**
> فسُمع له عجيج ما سُمع أشد ولا أنفذ منه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۲۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3570
> *English:* "And a bellowing was heard from it, than which nothing harsher or more piercing was ever
> heard."

**عبرت:** It ended the way it began — in one moment, decided by one man, and the rest of them only
found out afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no
