### TBO/E-JM48 · No pursuit, no finishing off, no houses
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The instant the camel fell, علي ؓ's crier went through the army with three orders.
Nobody chases a man who is running. Nobody finishes off a man who is wounded. Nobody goes into the
houses. Both books record that this had in fact been the rule on both sides from the beginning of the
day — and that neither side would begin the fighting, so that the argument would be on its side. Then
he sent men to carry the هودج out from among the dead and pitch a tent over it.

**The statement:**
> ونادى منادي عليٍّ في الناس: إنه لا يتبع مدبر ولا يُذفَّفُ على جريحٍ، ولا تُدخل (٥) الدور
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۲۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3570
> *English:* "And علي's crier called out among the people: no fleeing man is pursued, no wounded man is
> finished off, and no houses are entered."

**عبرت:** How a victory is handled in the first hour tells you more than how it was won.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM49 · How are you, mother?
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** With the dead still on the ground, the men of rank came one after another to greet
أم المؤمنين ؓ in the tent. Her own brother came and asked whether she had been wounded. And then
علي ؓ came, the man whose army had just broken hers, and the whole exchange is three short sentences.
How are you, mother. Well. May Allah forgive you. In ابن الأثیر there are two more words from her:
and you.

**The statement:**
> وجاء إليها عليُّ بن أبي طالب (أمير المؤمنين) مسلِّماً فقال: كيف أنت (يا أمَّهْ؟) قالت: بخير فقال: يغفر الله لك.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۲۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3570
> *English:* "And علي بن أبي طالب came to her to greet her and said: how are you, mother? She said:
> well. He said: may Allah forgive you."

**عبرت:** That is how the two of them spoke to each other on the worst day of both their lives, and
anyone who tells the story otherwise is not reading the books.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM50 · Which of you would like her as his share?
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Some of the men on the winning side came to علي ؓ and asked him to divide the
defeated side's property among them as spoils. He refused. When they pressed him and said it made no
sense that their blood was lawful and their property was not, he put one question to them, and the
room went quiet. It is the shortest argument in the whole story and it settled the matter.

**The statement:**
> فقال: أيكم يحب أن تصير أم المؤمنين في سهمه؟ فسكت القومُ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۲۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3571
> *English:* "He said: which of you would like أم المؤمنين to fall to him as his share? And the people
> were silent."

**عبرت:** He ended the argument by making them finish their own sentence.

### TBO/E-JM51 · He prayed over both armies
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** outside البصرة.

**What happened:** علي ؓ stayed outside البصرة for three days. He let the people come out and bury
their dead. He walked among the bodies himself, and whenever he passed a man he knew he asked mercy
for him. Then he prayed the funeral prayer over the dead — over both sides. Everything found in the
defeated camp was carried into the mosque of البصرة and anyone who recognised something of his own
took it, except state weapons.

**The statement:**
> وأقام علي بظاهر البصرة ثلاثاً ثمَّ صلَّى على القتلى من الفريقين
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۲۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3571
> *English:* "And علي stayed outside البصرة three days, then prayed over the slain of both parties."

**عبرت:** He buried them as Muslims because that is what they were, and the whole guardrail of this
evening is in that one sentence.

widow of one of them met him and prayed that his children be orphaned as hers had been. He answered

him why.

discipline the room will recognise.

### TBO/E-JM53 · A hundred lashes for insulting her
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

with an order: a hundred lashes to each of them, and strip them of their clothes. Whatever else the
two armies disagreed about, the man who had just defeated her army would not let his own soldiers
insult her.

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** غرة رجب 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

### TBO/E-JM56 · Twenty years, in two mouths
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** On the day of the battle القعقاع بن عمرو ؓ went in to أم المؤمنين ؓ and she said to
him that she wished she had died twenty years before that day. He left her, walked across to علي ؓ,
and علي ؓ said to him that he wished he had died twenty years before that day. ابن كثير records علي ؓ
saying the same thing to his son الحسن ؓ in the middle of the fighting, and the son answering: father,
I used to forbid you this.

**The statement:**
> قَالَتْ: وَاللَّهِ لَوَدِدْتُ أَنِّي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ بِعِشْرِينَ سَنَةً. وَخَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا فَأَتَى عَلِيًّا، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَلِيٌّ: وَاللَّهِ لَوَدِدْتُ أَنِّي مِتُّ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْيَوْمِ بِعِشْرِينَ سَنَةً.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1300
> *English:* "She said: by Allah, I wish I had died twenty years before this day. And he went out from
> her and came to علي, and علي said to him: by Allah, I wish I had died twenty years before this day."

**عبرت:** Neither of them thought they had won anything, and they said so on the same afternoon in the
same words.

### TBO/E-JM57 · Not thirty Companions were there
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير stops after the battle to answer a question the room will certainly have:
how much of the generation was actually in this. He quotes ابن سيرين, who says the Companions were
tens of thousands and fewer than thirty of them were present. He quotes الشعبي, who names four and
says call him a liar if you find a fifth. And then he corrects الشعبي on his own page, listing more
names — and then offers the most charitable reading of what الشعبي may have meant.

**The statement:**
> قال: هاجت الفتنة وأصحاب رسول الله ﷺ عشرات ألوف فلم يحضرها منهم مئة، بل لم يبلغوا ثلاثين.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۲۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3573
> *English:* "He said: the فتنة broke out while the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were tens of
> thousands, and not a hundred of them were present at it — indeed they did not reach thirty."

**عبرت:** The overwhelming majority of that generation was not in this fight at all, and that fact by
itself answers most of what gets asked about it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM58 · What the two historians refused to write down
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** no date — this is a remark about method `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Both of the books this evening is built on stop the story to tell the reader what
they left out. ابن كثير says that what he has given is a summary from ابن جرير out of the authorities
of the subject, and that the fabricated reports against the Companions circulated by partisans are not
in it. ابن الأثیر says he mentioned nothing in the affair of the Camel except what أبو جعفر mentioned,
because people have stuffed their histories to suit themselves.

**The statement:**
> لَمْ أَذْكُرْ فِي وَقْعَةِ الْجَمَلِ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَرَهُ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ، إِذْ كَانَ أَوْثَقَ مَنْ نَقَلَ التَّارِيخَ، فَإِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ حَشَوَا تَوَارِيخَهُمْ بِمُقْتَضَى أَهْوَائِهِمْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۱۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1307
> *English:* "I have not mentioned in the affair of the Camel anything but what أبو جعفر mentioned,
> since he was the most reliable of those who transmitted history — for people have stuffed their
> histories according to their own inclinations."

**عبرت:** Eight hundred years ago they were already warning each other that this particular story
attracts liars.

**Hands-up?** no

### TBO/E-JM61 · المدینہ heard before sunset
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** The people between مكة and المدینہ and البصرة learned of the battle on the day it

### S/E-SF1 · The palace he refused to live in
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** Monday 12 رجب 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights as علي ؓ's seat; the arrow from البصرة.

**What happened:** When the fighting at الجمل was over, علي ؓ saw أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ on her road
back to مكة and then went up from البصرة to الكوفة. The city offered him its governor's residence,
the White Palace. He would not take it. He said that عمر بن الخطاب ؓ had disliked living in it, and
that was enough for him. He lodged instead in the open ground, prayed two rakʿahs in the great
mosque, and preached.

**The statement:**

> فدخلها علي يوم الإثنين لثنتي عشرة ليلةً خَلَتْ من رجب سنةَ ستٍّ وثلاثين فقيل له: انزل بالقصر الأبيض، فقال: لا! إن عمر (بن الخطاب) كان يكره نزوله فأنا أكرهه كذلك
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٣٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3583
> *English:* “He entered it on Monday, twelve nights having passed of رجب in the year thirty-six. He was told: lodge in the White Palace. He said: no — عمر disliked lodging in it, so I dislike it likewise.”

**عبرت:** A man takes the capital and the first thing he does is decline the comfortable house.

**Hands-up?** no

### S/E-SF2 · A friend asks for the errand
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a line from الكوفة to دمشق.

**What happened:** علي ؓ decided to send a letter to معاوية ؓ calling him to the same بيعة that
المهاجرون and الأنصار had given. جرير بن عبد الله البجلي ؓ asked to be the messenger, because there
was old friendship between himself and معاوية ؓ, and he thought he could bring the بيعة back.
الأشتر objected in front of the whole council, and said plainly that he feared جرير ؓ's own
sympathies lay the other way. علي ؓ overruled him and sent جرير ؓ.

**The statement:**

> قال جرير بن عبد الله: أنا أذهب إليه (يا أمير المؤمنين) فإن بيني وبينه ودًا، فآخذ لك منه البيعة (٤)، فقال الأشتر: لا تبعثه يا أمير المؤمنين فإني أخشى أن يكون هواه معه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٣٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3583
> *English:* “جرير بن عبد الله said: I will go to him, for there is friendship between me and him, and I will take the بيعة from him for you. الأشتر said: do not send him, O أمير المؤمنين, for I fear that his inclination is with him.”

**عبرت:** The man who is trusted by both sides is the natural envoy and also the easiest to suspect.

**Hands-up?** no

### S/E-SF3 · A shirt and two fingers on the pulpit
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED — الکامل only]` · **Map:** دمشق lights.

**What happened:** Before any letter reached الشام, النعمان بن بشير ؓ had already carried the shirt
عثمان ؓ was killed in up from المدينة, and with it the severed fingers of his wife نائلة. معاوية ؓ
laid the shirt on the pulpit of the mosque of دمشق and called the troops in. They wept over it, day
after day, with the fingers hanging on the cloth. And men swore that water would not touch them
except for necessity and that they would not sleep on bedding until the killers of عثمان ؓ were
dead.

**The statement:**

> وَضَعَ مُعَاوِيَةُ الْقَمِيصَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ، وَجَمَعَ الْأَجْنَادَ إِلَيْهِ، فَبَكَوْا عَلَى الْقَمِيصِ مُدَّةً وَهُوَ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ، وَالْأَصَابِعُ مُعَلَّقَةٌ فِيه
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٢٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1318
> *English:* “معاوية put the shirt on the منبر and gathered the troops to him, and they wept over the shirt for a time while it was on the منبر, and the fingers hanging on it.”

**عبرت:** Once a grievance has been made into an object that a crowd can see, argument arrives too late.

**Hands-up?** Has anyone here ever tried to reason with a room that has already been shown a photograph?

### S/E-SF4 · Two sons give opposite advice
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED — الکامل only]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عمرو بن العاص ؓ had left المدينة before عثمان ؓ was besieged and was living near
الأردن when the news came. He called his two sons and asked them what he should do. عبد الله ؓ told
him to keep his hand back and sit in his house until the people had settled on an imam. محمد told
him he was one of the fangs of the Arabs and could not sit while this was decided without his
voice. Their father answered them both in one sentence and then went to معاوية ؓ.

**The statement:**

> أَمَّا أَنْتَ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ فَأَمَرْتَنِي بِمَا هُوَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي آخِرَتِي وَأَسْلَمُ لِي فِي دِينِي، وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ فَأَمَرْتَنِي بِمَا هُوَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دُنْيَايَ، وَشَرٌّ لِي فِي آخِرَتِي.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٢٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1317
> *English:* “As for you, O عبد الله, you have ordered me to what is better for me in my آخرة and safer for me in my دين; and as for you, O محمد, you have ordered me to what is better for me in my دنيا and worse for me in my آخرة.”

**عبرت:** A man can name the better counsel exactly and still walk the other way.

### S/E-SF5 · One condition, repeated for a year
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

عثمان ؓ, so that they may be killed. Until then there is no بيعة, and if you will not, we fight
you.

### S/E-SF6 · Two of his own men quarrel in front of him

### S/E-SF7 · A bridge built out of fear
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو القعدة 36 AH `[SOURCED — الکامل only]` · **Map:** الرقة on the الفرات; the army crosses.

**What happened:** The army came up the الفرات to الرقة and needed to cross. The townsmen had pulled
their boats to their own bank and refused to make a bridge. علي ؓ moved off to cross by the bridge
at منبج instead and left الأشتر behind. الأشتر called across the water and swore that if they did
not build a bridge he would come in among them with the sword. They looked at one another, said
that this was الأشتر and he was likely to keep his oath or do worse, and built the bridge.

**The statement:**

> أُقْسِمُ بِاللَّهِ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَعْمَلُوا جِسْرًا يَعْبُرُ عَلَيْهِ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِأُجَرِّدَنَّ فِيكُمُ السَّيْفَ، وَلَأَقْتُلَنَّ الرِّجَالَ، وَلَآخُذَنَّ الْأَمْوَالَ!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٣٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1322
> *English:* “I swear by God, if you do not build a bridge for أمير المؤمنين to cross on, I will bare the sword among you, and I will kill the men, and I will take the property!”

**عبرت:** A reputation does the work of an army, which is why men guard it so carefully.

**Hands-up?** no

### S/E-SF8 · The vanguard that arrived from behind
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو القعدة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** عانات, هيت, and قرقيسياء on the river.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had sent twelve thousand men ahead under زياد بن النضر الحارثي and
شريح بن هانئ. Marching along the far bank they learnt that معاوية ؓ was already out with the armies
of الشام, and judged that they must not stay with a river between themselves and their own side.
The people of عانات refused them a crossing. They crossed at هيت instead, and by the time they
rejoined the army it had passed them, so that the vanguard came up at the rear. علي ؓ said one dry
sentence and then accepted their reasoning.

**The statement:**

> فقال علي: مقدمتي تأتي من ورائي؟ فاعتذروا إليه بما جرى لهم، فعذرهم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٤٠ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3586
> *English:* “علي said: my vanguard comes to me from my rear? They excused themselves to him for what had happened, and he excused them.”

**عبرت:** A commander who lets a subordinate explain himself keeps the next honest report.

**Hands-up?** no

### S/E-SF9 · The monk, and how a history book handles a story
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو القعدة 36 AH `[SOURCED, and graded on the page]` · **Map:** البليخ, near الرقة.

**What happened:** At a place called البليخ on the bank of the الفرات, a monk is reported to have
come down from his cell with a book his forefathers had handed down. He read it out, and it
described an unlettered prophet and then a man of that prophet's ummah who would pass by this very
river commanding right and forbidding wrong. علي ؓ wept and thanked God for being remembered in the
books of the righteous. The monk went with him and was killed at صفين, and they found his body and
buried it. And the book that records this also records who carried the report, and the name is one
the scholars rejected.

**The statement:**

> فمضى الراهب معه وأسلم فكان مع عليّ حتى أصيب يوم صفين.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٣٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3585
> *English:* “So the monk went with him and accepted Islam, and he was with علي until he was struck down on the day of صفين.”

**عبرت:** The books keep the story and the objection to the story on the same page, and that is why
they can be trusted.

**Hands-up?** How do we know a thing in a history book actually happened?

### S/E-SF10 · The only watering place on the river
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** صفين on the الفرات; the ford marked; the two camps.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ's army reached the ground first and chose it with care. It was level and
open, and it held the single watering place on that whole stretch of the الفرات. He drew his lines
so that the ford was inside them and put أبو الأعور السلمي on it with orders to keep everyone else
off. When علي ؓ came up he had to camp away from the water, and when his men went down to drink
they were driven back at the spear point.

**The statement:**

> وَأَخَذَ شَرِيعَةَ الْفُرَاتِ، وَلَيْسَ فِي ذَلِكَ الصُّقْعِ شَرِيعَةٌ غَيْرَهَا، وَجَعَلَهَا فِي حَيِّزِهِ، وَبَعَثَ عَلَيْهَا أَبَا الْأَعْوَرِ السُّلَمِيَّ يَحْمِيهَا وَيَمْنُعُهَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٣٤ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1323
> *English:* “And he took the watering place of the الفرات — and there is no watering place in that tract but it — and made it inside his own lines, and posted أبو الأعور السلمي on it to guard it and keep others off.”

**عبرت:** The side that arrives first chooses the ground, and the ground decides much of the rest.

**Hands-up?** no

### S/E-SF11 · The council that split over the water
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the ford lights.

had put the argument to you, and your vanguard attacked us first, and now you have kept the people
from the water. معاوية ؓ put it to his council and the council split. عمرو بن العاص ؓ said let them
drink, and told him to look to what was between himself and God. الوليد بن عقبة and

down to reinforce the ford.

> *English:* “عمرو بن العاص said: leave the people and the water alone. They will not go thirsty while you are watered — but by something other than water. So look to what is between you and God.”

**عبرت:** In every council there is one voice asking what this will look like before God, and the

### S/E-SF12 · Two men who may not have been there
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 36 AH `[SOURCED — disputed on the page itself]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The harshest words in the quarrel over the water are put in the mouths of
الوليد بن عقبة and عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح. And on the very same page that reports them, the
historian records the objection that neither of those two men was at صفين at all. He does not
choose between the report and the denial. He writes both down and moves on, and leaves the reader
holding the doubt, which is exactly what a history is for.

**The statement:**

> وَقَدْ قِيلَ: إِنَّ الْوَلِيدَ وَابْنَ أَبِي سَرْحٍ لَمْ يَشْهَدَا صِفِّينَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٣٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1324
> *English:* “And it has been said: الوليد and ابن أبي سرح were not present at صفين.”

**عبرت:** A report and the doubt about it travel together, and a man who repeats only the first half
has changed the report.

**Hands-up?** no

### S/E-SF13 · What happened when the water changed hands
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 36 AH `[SOURCED — the two books differ]` · **Map:** the ford changes colour.

**What happened:** The Iraqis fought their way onto the ford and took it. And here the two histories
part. One says the two armies then simply shared the water, crowding together at it without a hard
word between them. The other says the Iraqis swore they would let no Syrian drink, and that علي ؓ
had to send an order to his own army to take what they needed and leave the rest alone. Both books
are on the shelf and neither is hiding anything, and the honest thing is to say that they differ.

**The statement:**

> فَقَالُوا: وَاللَّهِ لَا نُسْقِيهِ أَهْلَ الشَّامِ! فَأَرْسَلَ عَلِيٌّ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ: أَنْ خُذُوا مِنَ الْمَاءِ حَاجَتَكُمْ وَخَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ نَصَرَكُمْ بِبَغْيِهِمْ وَظُلْمِهِمْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٣٦ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1325
> *English:* “They said: by God, we will not give the people of الشام to drink of it! So علي sent to his companions: take from the water what you need and leave them to it, for God gave you the victory by their transgression and wrongdoing.”

**عبرت:** It is easy to refuse to do to others what was done to you, until the day you have the power.

**Hands-up?** no

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–37 AH `[SOURCED — and disputed inside the same chapter]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The men who had sat with the Prophet ﷺ numbered in the tens of thousands. When
the fitna came, محمد بن سيرين said, not a hundred of them were present at it, and they did not reach
thirty. Another report says that of all the men of بدر only خزيمة بن ثابت ؓ was found at صفين, with
two more added on a later authority. And a third report in the very same chapter says the army had
eighty men of بدر in it. The chapter keeps all three and settles none.

**The statement:**

> قال: هاجت الفتنة وأصحاب رسول الله ﷺ عشرات الألوف فلم يحضرها منهم مئة، بل لم يبلغوا ثلاثين.

> *English:* “He said: the fitna broke out while the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ were tens of thousands, and not a hundred of them were present at it — indeed they did not reach thirty.”

**عبرت:** The generation that knew the Prophet ﷺ best is the generation that mostly stayed out of this.

### S/E-SF22 · The orders he gave before the lines closed
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** end of المحرم 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. Large statement slide.

**What happened:** When the truce ran out علي ؓ had a herald cry to the Syrian camp at sunset that
he had waited for them and was now casting back to them on equal terms. Then he gave his own army
its orders, and they were almost all prohibitions. Do not begin the fighting. If you rout them, do
not kill a man who turns his back and do not finish off a wounded man. Do not uncover a nakedness
and do not mutilate a corpse. Do not enter a house or take property. And do not lay a hand on a
woman, even if she abuses your commanders and your best men.

**The statement:**

> فَإِذَا هَزَمْتُمُوهُمْ فَلَا تَقْتُلُوا مُدْبِرًا، وَلَا تُجْهِزُوا عَلَى جَرِيحٍ، وَلَا تَكْشِفُوا عَوْرَةً، وَلَا تُمَثِّلُوا بِقَتِيلٍ، وَإِذَا وَصَلْتُمْ إِلَى رِحَالِ الْقَوْمِ فَلَا تَهْتِكُوا سِتْرًا وَلَا تَدْخُلُوا دَارًا، وَلَا تَأْخُذُوا شَيْئًا مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ، وَلَا تُهَيِّجُوا امْرَأَة
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٤٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1334
> *English:* “And when you have routed them, do not kill a man who turns his back, and do not finish off a wounded man, and do not uncover a nakedness, and do not mutilate a slain man; and when you reach the people's quarters, do not tear a curtain, and do not enter a house, and do not take anything of their property, and do not stir up a woman.”

**عبرت:** The rules a man keeps against his own side in a civil war are the measure of him.

### S/E-SF23 · Five ranks tied together so they cannot run

their own legs together with their turbans, rank by rank, so that running away would be physically

### S/E-SF28 · The prayer for the outcome he might lose
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. Large statement slide.

**What happened:** At dawn علي ؓ prayed الفجر in the last of the dark and led the army out, and as
the two lines faced each other he prayed aloud. The prayer runs long, over the roof of the sky and
the courses of the sun and moon and the mountains set as pegs. And then it comes to the two possible
endings of the day, and asks for a different thing in each, and the thing he asks for if he wins is
the stranger of the two.

**The statement:**

> إن أظهرتنا على عدونا فجنبنا البغي والفساد وسددنا للحق، وإن أظهرتهم علينا فارزقني (٤) الشهادة وجنب بقية أصحابي من الفتنة.

> *English:* “If You give us the upper hand over our enemy, then keep us far from transgression and corruption and set us straight for the truth; and if You give them the upper hand over us, then grant me martyrdom, and keep the rest of my companions far from the fitna.”

**عبرت:** A man on the edge of battle asking first not to be corrupted by winning has understood
something about victory.

### S/E-SF29 · He reached the tent and was killed there

driven the Syrian left back onto معاوية ؓ's own tent. معاوية ؓ threw the men sworn on death at him,
and the Iraqi right broke and ran, leaving him with two or three hundred reciters lying flat on the
ground. الأشتر came up, reached them, and told him to hold where he was, and that it was better for

surrounded, and was killed.

### S/E-SF31 · Where is your flight from death
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Thursday, صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the broken right wing re-forms.

caught الأشتر riding past toward the trouble and gave him a message to carry to the running men. The

**عبرت:** A running army is not short of courage, it is short of a sentence it cannot answer.

### S/E-SF32 · Eleven banners of Hamdān

### S/E-SF40 · The one-eyed man and the young Syrian
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED — الکامل only]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** هاشم بن عتبة بن أبي وقاص ؓ carried علي ؓ's banner and had lost an eye years before
at اليرموك. A young Syrian of غسان kept riding out chanting that علي ؓ had killed ابن عفان and
cursing as he went. هاشم ؓ did not fight him. He told him that this talk had a reckoning after it and
this fighting an accounting. The young man argued back, was answered point by point, asked whether
there was repentance for him, was told yes, and went home. When his own side told him the Iraqi had
tricked him, he said no, he gave me sincere counsel.

### S/E-SF43 · The night they called the snarling
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the night of Thursday to Friday, 10 صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. Large statement slide.

### S/E-SF44 · Put the battlefield behind your back
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ليلة الهرير `[SOURCED — الکامل only]` · **Map:** the lines rotate through the night.

### S/E-SF45 · The مصاحف go up on the spears
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Friday forenoon, صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. Full-bleed image slide.

**What happened:** By the middle of Friday morning the Syrian ranks were coming apart. الأشتر had the
right wing and was driving it through them with علي ؓ behind him, and most of the line had broken and
was close to rout. And at that exact moment the Syrian army lifted copies of the Qur'an above their
spear points, all along the line, and called across the ground. This is between us and you. The
people are finished. Who is left for the frontiers?

**عبرت:** The Book was raised at the exact hour it was most useful to raise it, and that timing is the
whole of what happened next.

### S/E-SF46 · The man who proposed it, and why
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Friday, صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Both our books name the man who proposed it and both give his reasoning, and the
reasoning is entirely open. He said it would do two things at once. It would unite his own side and
divide the other. If they all accepted, the fighting stopped that hour. If they split over it, some
saying we must answer and some saying we must not, then they would fail and their wind would go out

### S/E-SF51 · Seventy thousand, and nobody agrees
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED — irreconcilably disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** How many died at صفين cannot be settled. On a single page of a single book you are
given seventy thousand dead, made up of forty-five thousand from one side and twenty-five thousand
from the other, and then a second reckoning that gives twenty thousand and forty thousand instead.
The same page cannot agree how long the armies lay there either, offering seven months, nine months,
a hundred and ten days, and the author's own count of seventy-seven. He ends it the way an honest man
ends it.

**The statement:**

> قلت: ومقتضى كلام أبي مخنف أنه كان من مستهلّ ذي الحجة في يوم الجمعة لثلاث عشرة خلت من صفر وذلك سبعة وسبعون يومًا، فالله سبحانه أعلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٦٦ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3612
> *English:* “I say: what أبو مخنف's account requires is that it was from the first of ذو الحجة to Friday, thirteen nights having passed of صفر — and that is seventy-seven days. And God, glory be to Him, knows best.”

**عبرت:** A book that tells you where its own numbers stop being reliable is worth more than one that does not.

**Hands-up?** How many people do you think died? — then give the two figures and the disagreement.

his name is not on the paper.

**The statement:**

> لَا صَحِبَتْنِي يَمِينِي، وَلَا نَفَعَتْنِي بَعْدَهَا شِمَالِي، إِنْ خُطَّ لِي فِي هَذِهِ الصَّحِيفَة
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٦٧١ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1360
> *English:* “May my right hand never keep me company, and may my left never profit me after it, if a name of mine is written in this صحيفة.”

**عبرت:** The men who most wanted the war to end and the men who most wanted it to continue were in
the same camp, wearing the same colours.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### S/E-SF59 · Praise be to God — and to God we return
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** علي ؓ wanted عبد الله بن عباس ؓ as his arbiter and was refused. He proposed
الأشتر and was told the man had set the earth on fire. The reciters would have nobody but
أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ, on the ground that he was equally distant from both sides. أبو موسى ؓ had
withdrawn from the whole war and was living apart. They sent a man to fetch him, and his two answers
to the two pieces of news are the exact measure of what he thought of the appointment.

**The statement:**

> فلما قيل له إن الناس قد اصطلحوا قال: الحمد لله، قيل له: وقد جُعلت حكمًا، فقال: إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٦٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3615
> *English:* “When it was said to him, the people have made peace, he said: praise be to God. It was said to him, and you have been made an arbiter: he said, إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون.”

**عبرت:** The man who wanted the office least was the one they insisted on, and he knew exactly what
was being handed to him.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### S/E-SF60 · Two great parties, and one claim
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the closing of the chapter `[SOURCED — البخاري ومسلم]` · **Map:** No map. Large statement slide.

**What happened:** The historian does not end his account of صفين with a judgement on the two sides.
He ends it with hadith. The first is the one البيهقي applied to this battle by name, in which the
Prophet ﷺ foretold two great parties fighting with a great slaughter between them, and then said four
words about what the two parties would have in common.

**The statement:**

> لا تقوم الساعة حتى تقتتل فئتان عظيمتان يقتل بينهما مقتلة عظيمة ودعواهما واحدة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٦٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3613
> *English:* “The Hour will not come until two great parties fight one another, and there is a great slaughter between them, and their claim is one.”

**عبرت:** Their claim is one — both armies were calling to the same thing, which is what makes this a
tragedy and not a conquest.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### S/E-SF61 · He withheld that one from me
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the closing of the chapter `[SOURCED — مسلم]` · **Map:** No map. Large statement slide. **The closing line of the strand.**

**What happened:** The last thing the historian puts at the end of صفين, before turning to the
arbitration, is a hadith about three requests. The Prophet ﷺ asked his Lord for three protections for
this ummah. Two were granted. The third was not. He says it plainly and without explanation, and the
whole year of صفين is the answer to why he says it.

**The statement:**

> سألت ربي أن لا يهلك أمتي بسنة عامة فأعطانيها، وسألته أن لا يسلط عليهم عدوًا من غيرهم (٢) فيستبيح بيضتهم فأعطانيها، وسألته أن لا يسلط بعضهم على بعض فمنعنيها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٤٦٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3615
> *English:* “I asked my Lord that He not destroy my ummah by a general famine, and He granted it to me; and I asked Him that He not set an enemy from outside them over them to violate them wholesale, and He granted it to me; and I asked Him that He not set them one upon another, and He withheld that from me.”

**عبرت:** The one danger the Prophet ﷺ could not have lifted from this ummah is the one it brings on
itself.

**Hands-up?** no

---

## التحكيم, the first خوارج, and النهروان

*Source note: [`the-arbitration-and-the-nahrawan.md`](../docs/research/the-arbitration-and-the-nahrawan.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TAA/E-KH1 · The Qur'an readers with swords on their shoulders
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH, at صفين `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** صفين lights; the Euphrates line from الرقة.

**What happened:** When the copies of the Qur'an went up on the spears at صفين, the men who came to علي ؓ
demanding that he answer them were not the waverers in his army. They were its most devout wing — the men the
army itself called the قُرّاء, the Qur'an readers, who carried their swords on their shoulders and fasted and
prayed more than anyone around them. ابن كثير names them in a single clause and adds what they later became.
Everything that follows in this evening begins with these men, and they begin as the best of the camp.

**The statement:**
> فجاءته الخوارجُ ونحن ندعوهم يومئذ القُرّاء وسيوفهم على عواتقهم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3610
*English:* "Then the خوارج came to him — and in those days we used to call them the قُرّاء, the Qur'an readers
— with their swords on their shoulders."

**عبرت:** Certainty about God is not the same thing as knowledge of what God requires today.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH2 · علي ؓ says the raised copies are a stratagem
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** علي ؓ told his army plainly that the copies had not been raised out of reverence. He said
the men who raised them neither recited them nor acted by them, and that the whole gesture was a device to
stop a battle they were losing. The army heard him and refused him. He was the commander, and he was
overruled by his own most religious troops. مالك الأشتر, recalled from the fighting, told them to their faces
what he thought had just happened to them.

**The statement:**
> ويحكم والله إنهم ما رفعوها أنهم يقرؤونها ولا يعملون بما فيها وما رفعوها إلا خديعة ودهاءً ومكيدة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3610
*English:* "Woe to you! By God, they did not raise them because they recite them or act by what is in them.
They raised them only as a deception, a cunning and a stratagem."

**عبرت:** A leader can be right and still be overruled by the people he leads.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "If a man raises the Qur'an in the middle of a battle — must you stop?"

---

### TAA/E-KH3 · سهل بن حنيف ؓ tells the army to suspect itself
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** While علي ؓ argued that the raised copies were a trick, a Companion of Badr stood up and
argued the other way, and he did it from memory rather than from theory. He reminded the army of الحديبية,
where the believers had been certain they were right and certain they should fight, and where the Prophet ﷺ
had made a truce anyway. His conclusion was not that علي ؓ was wrong. It was that men in a battle are the
worst judges of their own certainty.

**The statement:**
> يا أيها الناس اتهموا أنفسكم فلقد رأيتنا يوم الحديبية - يعنى (١) الصلح الذي كان بين رسول الله وبين المشركين - ولو نرى قتالًا لقاتلنا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3610
*English:* "O people, suspect your own judgement. We saw ourselves on the day of الحديبية — meaning the truce
that was made between the Messenger of God and the polytheists — and had we seen a way to fight, we would
have fought."

**عبرت:** The strongest feeling of being right is the weakest evidence of it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH4 · الأشتر is called back from a fight he is winning
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** مالك الأشتر was at the front when the order came to stop. He sent back word that he needed
a little more time. The messenger returned a second time to say that if he did not come back, the men around
علي ؓ would abandon him or worse. الأشتر came back and said what he thought of the men who had made him come.
He also refused, later, to let his name be written on the document at all.

**The statement:**
> خُدعتم والله فانخدعتم، ودُعيتم إلى وضع الحرب فأجبتم، يا أصحاب السوء كنا نظن صلاتكم زهادة في الدنيا وشوقًا إلى لقاء الله، فلا أرى فراركم إلا إلى الدنيا من الموت، يا أشباه النيب الجَلالة ما أنتم بربانيين بعدها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3612
*English:* "You were deceived, by God, and you let yourselves be deceived. You were called to lay down the
war and you answered. O you evil company — we used to think your prayer was renunciation of this world and
longing to meet God; now I see your flight is only to the world, away from death."

**عبرت:** An army that will not obey in the hour of decision has already lost the decision.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH5 · Each side appoints one man
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The arbitration was not settled in an afternoon. ابن كثير says it came after letters and
exchanges too long to recount, and that its shape was simple: each of the two commanders would name one man,
and the two men together would look for what was best for the Muslims. معاوية ؓ named عمرو بن العاص ؓ at once.
On the other side the appointment was taken out of the commander's hands.

**The statement:**
> ثم تراوض الفريقان بعد مكاتبات ومراجعات يطول ذكرها على التحكيم، وهو أن يحكم كل واحد من الأميرين - علي ومعاوية - رجلًا من جهته
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3615
*English:* "Then the two parties, after letters and exchanges too long to recount, came to terms upon the
arbitration — that is, that each of the two amirs, علي and معاوية, should appoint a man from his own side."

**عبرت:** A procedure agreed under pressure carries the pressure inside it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH6 · علي ؓ is not allowed to choose his own arbiter
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** علي ؓ wanted عبد الله بن عباس ؓ. The قُرّاء refused and would accept only أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ.
He then offered مالك الأشتر, and they answered that الأشتر was the man who had set the whole war alight. He
told them to do as they wished. ابن كثير, four centuries later, could not write the sentence down without
putting his own regret into the middle of it in four words.

**The statement:**
> فوكّل معاوية عمرو بن العاص، وأراد عليّ أن يوكل عبد الله بن عباس - وليته فعل - ولكنه منعه القُرّاء [الخوارج] ممن ذكرنا وقالوا: لا نرضى إلا بأبي موسى الأشعري
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3615
*English:* "So معاوية appointed عمرو بن العاص; and علي wanted to appoint عبد الله بن عباس — would that he had
done it — but the قُرّاء [the خوارج] whom we have mentioned prevented him, and said: we will accept none but
أبو موسى الأشعري."

**عبرت:** The right to choose your own representative is not a formality; it is most of the outcome.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH7 · الأحنف بن قيس asks to be second or third
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الأحنف بن قيس, the most respected head of تميم and famous for patience and judgement, told
علي ؓ that the other side would only be matched by a man of the same kind — one who could come close and pull
back at will. He asked to be made the arbiter. When that was refused he asked to be made second, or third, so
that he could at least untie whatever the other man tied. He was not taken.

**The statement:**
> والله لقد رميت بحجر، إنه لا يصلح لهؤلاء القوم إلا رجل منهم، يدنو منهم حتى يصير في أكفهم، ويبتعد حتى (٦) يصير بمنزلة النجم، فإن أبيت أن تجعلني حكمًا فاجعلني ثانيًا أو ثالثًا، فإنه لن يعقد عقدة إلا أحلها (٧)، ولا يحل عقدة عقدتها إلا عقدت لك أخرى مثلها أو أحكم منها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3615
*English:* "If you refuse to make me the arbiter, make me second or third, for he will tie no knot but I
shall untie it, and he will untie no knot that I have tied but I shall tie you another like it, or firmer."

**عبرت:** Offers of help refused in the calm hour are remembered in the hard one.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH8 · أبو موسى ؓ is fetched out of his retirement
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ had taken himself out of the war altogether and was living apart. The
messengers found him and told him first that the people had made peace, and he praised God for it. Then they
told him that he had been made one of the two arbiters, and he said the words a Muslim says at a death. He
was then brought to علي ؓ, and the document was written.

**The statement:**
> فلما قيل له إن الناس قد اصطلحوا قال: الحمد لله، قيل له: وقد جُعلت حكمًا، فقال: إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3615
*English:* "When it was said to him: the people have made peace — he said: praise be to God. It was said to
him: and you have been made an arbiter — he said: إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون."

**عبرت:** The man who sees the weight of an office most clearly is often the one who least wants it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH9 · The quarrel over one line of the document
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Wednesday 13 صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The scribe began: *this is what علي بن أبي طالب, أمير المؤمنين, has agreed upon.* عمرو بن
العاص ؓ stopped him and said the title could not stand, because علي ؓ was the Syrians' opponent and not their
commander. الأحنف said write nothing else. علي ؓ ended it himself by ordering the title erased, and he gave a
precedent for doing so: at الحديبية the Prophet ﷺ had allowed *محمد بن عبد الله* to replace *محمد رسول الله*
rather than lose the treaty.

**The statement:**
> فقال علي: امح أمير المؤمنين (٢) واكتب هذا ما قاضى عليه علي بن أبي طالب ثم استشهد علي بقصة (٣) الحديبية حين امتنع أهل مكة [من قوله] "هذا ما قاضى عليه محمد رسول الله" فامتنع المشركون من ذلك وقالوا: اكتب هذا ما قاضى عليه محمد بن عبد الله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3616
*English:* "علي said: erase أمير المؤمنين, and write: *this is what علي بن أبي طالب has agreed upon*. Then علي
cited the case of الحديبية, when the people of مكة refused the words *this is what محمد the Messenger of God
has agreed upon*."

**عبرت:** A man secure in his position can afford to give up its title; the title was never what held it.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "Where have you heard of a name being rubbed off a treaty before?"

---

### TAA/E-KH10 · The same page gives the opposite account
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Having given that account, ابن كثير immediately records another, from الهيثم بن عدي's book
on the خوارج, in which the refusal never came from the Syrian side at all. In this version الأشعث بن قيس ؓ
carried the draft to معاوية ؓ with the title in it, and معاوية ؓ said that if he accepted the title he would
not be fighting at all — but ordered علي ؓ's name to be written, and written first, because of his precedence
in Islam. The book prints both and settles neither.

**The statement:**
> لو كان أمير المؤمنين لم أقاتله، ولكن ليكتب اسمه، وليبدأ به قبل اسمي لفضله وسابقته
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3616
*English:* "Had he been أمير المؤمنين I would not have fought him; but let his name be written, and let it be
put before mine, for his excellence and his precedence in Islam."

**عبرت:** When a careful book gives two accounts and chooses neither, the honest retelling gives two as well.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH11 · What the document actually bound them to
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Wednesday 13 صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The document was short and its operative rule was one sentence: whatever the two arbiters
find in the Book of God, they act on; whatever they do not find there, they take from the سنة — the just
سنة, the one that gathers and does not divide. It set a term, رمضان; a meeting place, دومة الجندل; an escort
of four hundred for each; and a fallback year and place if the meeting failed. It was written on a Wednesday,
thirteen nights into صفر, in the year thirty-seven. Both of our books give the same date.

**The statement:**
> إنا ننزل عند حكم الله وكتابه ونحيي ما أحيى الله ﷿، ونميت ما أمات الله، فما وجد الحكمان في كتاب الله - وهما أبو موسى الأشعري وعمرو بن العاص - عملا به، وما لم يجدا في كتاب الله فالسنة العادلة الجامعة غير المتفرقة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3616
*English:* "We submit to the judgement of God and to His Book … Whatever the two arbiters — and they are أبو
موسى الأشعري and عمرو بن العاص — find in the Book of God, they act by it; and what they do not find in the
Book of God, then the just, uniting, undividing سنة."

**عبرت:** Men can agree on the rule and still not agree on anything the rule decides.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH12 · الأشتر will not have his name on it
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the document was finished, the witnesses were called to sign. مالك الأشتر was asked to
put his name on it and refused in the strongest words he could find. الأشعث بن قيس ؓ told him to come in and
not set himself apart; he answered that he had seen the victory and they had not. His name is absent from the
list in both of our books.

**The statement:**
> لَا صَحِبَتْنِي يَمِينِي، وَلَا نَفَعَتْنِي بَعْدَهَا شِمَالِي، إِنْ خُطَّ لِي فِي هَذِهِ الصَّحِيفَةِ [اسْمٌ عَلَى صُلْحٍ وَلَا مُوَادَعَةٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۷۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1360
*English:* "May my right hand never keep company with me, and may my left never profit me after it, if a name
of mine is written in this document upon a peace or a truce."

**عبرت:** A man may refuse to endorse a decision and still obey it; those are two different acts.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH13 · علي ؓ, having consented, holds himself to it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Told that الأشتر would not accept what was in the document, علي ؓ answered with the sentence
that governs everything he does for the next year. He had not wanted the arbitration and had not wanted them
to want it. But they had forced his consent, and consent once given could not be withdrawn and an
acknowledgement once made could not be altered — unless God were disobeyed and His Book transgressed. That
last clause is the hinge on which he later declares the arbiters' verdict void.

**The statement:**
> وَأَنَا وَاللَّهِ مَا رَضِيتُ وَلَا أَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ تَرْضَوْا، فَإِذَا أَبَيْتُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ تَرْضَوْا فَقَدْ رَضِيتُ، وَإِذَا رَضِيتُ فَلَا يَصْلُحُ الرُّجُوعُ بَعْدَ الرِّضَا، وَلَا التَّبْدِيلُ بَعْدَ الْإِقْرَارِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1361
*English:* "By God, I did not consent, nor did I wish you to consent. But since you refused anything but to
consent, I have consented; and having consented, it is not lawful to go back after consent, nor to alter
after acknowledgement."

**عبرت:** A promise is not less binding for having been extracted.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH14 · The twenty witnesses who cannot be counted
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Both of our books list the men who witnessed the document. البدایہ names ten from each
side. الکامل names nine and seven, and several of the same men carry different tribal names in the two lists.
ابن عباس ؓ heads البدایہ's list and is absent from الکامل's. The card is recorded so that the pool holds the
fact — and so that no future artifact prints "the twenty witnesses" as though the number were known.

**The statement:** none in the sources we use — the two lists are set side by side in §5 of this note and
cannot be quoted as one.

**عبرت:** A list that two careful books copy differently is a list neither of them could check.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH15 · One man shouts, and a movement has its name
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH, on the way back from صفين `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the road from صفين back
toward الكوفة.

**What happened:** الأشعث بن قيس ؓ went through the camp reading the document aloud to each tribe. When he
reached a group of بنو تميم, a man named عروة بن أُذَينة stood up, asked whether they were making men judges
in the affair of God, shouted that there is no judgement but God's, and struck the hindquarters of الأشعث ؓ's
mount with his sword. الأشعث ؓ's people were furious and الأحنف بن قيس came to apologise. The slogan spread
through the army in a day, and the party took its first name from it: المحكِّمة.

**The statement:**
> تُحَكِّمُونَ فِي أَمْرِ اللَّهِ الرِّجَالَ؟ لَا حُكْمَ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ! ثُمَّ شَدَّ بِسَيْفِهِ فَضَرَبَ بِهِ عَجُزَ دَابَّةِ الْأَشْعَثِ ضَرْبَةً خَفِيفَةً
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1361
*English:* "Do you make men judges in the affair of God? There is no judgement but God's! Then he drew his
sword and struck with it the hindquarters of الأشعث's mount, a light blow."

**عبرت:** A slogan that fits on one breath will outrun every argument made against it.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "Has anyone here heard the phrase لا حكم إلا لله?"

---

### TAA/E-KH16 · ابن كثير refuses the خوارج's own version of their origin
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** — `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The خوارج themselves told the story differently. In their account the first man to raise
the slogan was not an unknown from تميم but their own leader, عبد الله بن وهب الراسبي. ابن كثير records the
claim, from الهيثم بن عدي's book, and then rejects it in two words of his own: the correct view is the first.
It is a small example of a historian handling a group's account of itself.

**The statement:**
> قال الهيثم بن عدي: والخوارج يزعمون أن أول من حكم عبد الله بن وهب الراسبي. (قلت): والصحيح الأول
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3618
*English:* "الهيثم بن عدي said: and the خوارج claim that the first to say *there is no judgement but God's*
was عبد الله بن وهب الراسبي. (I say): and the correct view is the first."

**عبرت:** Every movement improves the story of its own beginning; the historian's work is to check it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH17 · The army comes home whipping each other
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37 AH, the road to الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the road from صفين to الكوفة.

**What happened:** The march home was not a march of one army. الکامل says they came back as enemies who
detested one another, taking a different road from the one they had come by, quarrelling the whole way and
beating one another with whips. One side called the other enemies of God who had gone soft in God's affair;
the other side answered that they had deserted their imam and split the community. The quarrel arrived at
الكوفة before the army did.

**The statement:**
> وَعَادُوا وَهُمْ أَعْدَاءٌ مُتَبَاغِضُونَ (وَقَدْ فَشَا فِيهِمُ التَّحْكِيمُ) يَقْطَعُونَ الطَّرِيقَ بِالتَّشَاتُمِ وَالتَّضَارُبِ بِالسِّيَاطِ، يَقُولُ الْخَوَارِجُ: يَا أَعْدَاءَ اللَّهِ أَدْهَنْتُمْ فِي أَمْرِ اللَّهِ، وَيَقُولُ الْآخَرُونَ: فَارَقْتُمْ إِمَامَنَا وَفَرَّقْتُمْ جَمَاعَتَنَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۷۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1362
*English:* "And they came back as enemies detesting one another, cutting the road with abuse and with beating
one another with whips. The خوارج would say: O enemies of God, you were pliant in the affair of God! And the
others would say: you have parted from our imam and split our community!"

**عبرت:** An unresolved argument does not stay where it started; it travels with the people who had it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAA/E-KH18 · At the gate of الكوفة, twelve thousand turn aside
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights; حروراء marked just outside it.

**What happened:** علي ؓ rode into الكوفة. A large part of his army did not. They refused to live in the same
town as him and camped at a place called حروراء, close enough to be seen, and the name stuck to them for a
generation: الحرورية. Our books count them differently — twelve thousand, or sixteen, or fewer, or eight
thousand of the Qur'an readers. What is not disputed is that this was the first time such a body had ever
broken off from a Muslim army over a point of principle.

**The statement:**
> فَلَمَّا رَجَعَ عَلِيٌّ خَالَفَتِ الْحَرُورِيَّةُ وَخَرَجَتْ، كَانَ ذَلِكَ أَوَّلَ مَا ظَهَرَتْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۷۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1362
*English:* "And when علي returned, the حرورية dissented and went out. That was the first appearance of them."

**عبرت:** The first time a thing happens in a community, it fixes the pattern for every time after.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH19 · They appoint a commander of war and a commander of prayer
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37 AH, at حروراء `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** حروراء.

**What happened:** At حروراء they did not merely protest. They set up a government. A crier announced that
شبث بن ربعي التميمي commanded the fighting and عبد الله بن الكوّاء اليشكري led the prayer; that the caliphate
itself would be decided by شورى once they had won; that allegiance was to God alone; and that their programme
was the enjoining of good and the forbidding of wrong. الکامل alone preserves the announcement.

**The statement:**
> وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ عَلِيٌّ مِنْ صِفِّينَ فَارَقَهُ الْخَوَارِجُ، وَأَتَوْا حَرُورَاءَ، فَنَزَلَ بِهَا مِنْهُمُ اثْنَا عَشَرَ أَلْفًا، وَنَادَى مُنَادِيهِمْ: إِنَّ أَمِيرَ الْقِتَالِ شَبَثُ بْنُ رِبْعِيٍّ التَّمِيمِيُّ، وَأَمِيرَ الصَّلَاةِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْكَوَّا الْيَشْكُرِيُّ، وَالْأَمْرُ شُورَى بَعْدَ الْفَتْحِ، وَالْبَيْعَةُ لِلَّهِ - عَزَّ وَجَلَّ -، وَالْأَمْرُ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ، وَالنَّهْيُ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1367
*English:* "Their caller proclaimed: the commander of the fighting is شبث بن ربعي التميمي, and the commander
of the prayer is عبد الله بن الكوّاء اليشكري; and the command is a شورى after the victory; and the allegiance
is to God — عز وجل; and the enjoining of good and the forbidding of wrong."

**عبرت:** A protest becomes a rival state the moment it appoints someone to lead its prayer.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH20 · The charge against him, in their own words
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH, at حروراء `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ later asked a man who had been there what exactly these people had held
against علي ؓ, and his answer is preserved with a sound chain. They said he had stripped off a shirt that God
had clothed him in and a name that God had named him by, and had then gone and judged in the religion of God
— when there is no judgement but God's. It is worth hearing exactly, because it is an argument and not an
insult.

**The statement:**
> انسلخت من قميصٍ ألبَسَكهُ اللهُ، واسمٍ سمّاك له اللهُ ثم انطلقت فحكمت في دين الله ولا حكم إلا لله
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3621
*English:* "You stripped off a shirt God had clothed you in, and a name God had named you by; then you went
and made a judgement in the religion of God — and there is no judgement but God's."

**عبرت:** Men who begin from a true premise can still reach a conclusion that kills.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH21 · "Speak, O مصحف"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH, in الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had it announced that no man should come in to him but one who carried the Qur'an in
his memory. When the house was full of readers he called for a great copy, set it in front of him, struck it
with his hand and told it to speak to the people. They called back that it was ink on paper and that it is
men who speak by what they have carried from it. That was his whole argument, and he had made them say it
themselves.

**The statement:**
> دعا بمصحف إمام عظيم فوضعه بين يديه فجعل يصكه بيده ويقول: أيها المصحفّ حدث الناس فناداه الناس (فقالوا) يا أمير المؤمنين ما تسأل عنه إنما هو مداد في ورق، ونحن نتكلم بما روينا منه، فماذا تريد
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3621
*English:* "O مصحف, speak to the people! And the people called out to him: O أمير المؤمنين, what are you
asking it? It is only ink on paper, and we are the ones who speak by what we have transmitted from it."

**عبرت:** A text does not apply itself; someone must always read it, and that is where the responsibility
lies.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "If the Qur'an is the judge — who reads it out?"

---

### TAA/E-KH22 · "We did not make men the judges"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH, at حروراء `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** علي ؓ went out to حروراء himself. He asked who their spokesman was and what had brought them
out, and they said: your arbitration at صفين. He reminded them who had forced it. Then he answered the
principle directly: no man had been made a judge over God's affair; the Qur'an had been made the judge — and
the Qur'an is writing between two covers which does not speak, and men are the ones who speak by it. He also
explained the delay written into the document: so the ignorant might learn and the learned be confirmed.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّا لَسْنَا حَكَّمْنَا الرِّجَالَ، إِنَّمَا حَكَّمْنَا الْقُرْآنَ، وَهَذَا الْقُرْآنُ إِنَّمَا هُوَ خَطٌّ مَسْطُورٌ بَيْنَ دَفَّتَيْنِ، لَا يَنْطِقُ إِنَّمَا يَتَكَلَّمُ بِهِ الرِّجَالُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1369
*English:* "We did not make men the judges; we made the Qur'an the judge. And this Qur'an is only writing
inscribed between two covers — it does not speak; it is men who speak by it."

**عبرت:** The slogan and the answer to it are both in the same sentence: everything depends on who is
speaking for the Book.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH23 · Their best argument, put to ابن عباس ؓ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37 AH, at حروراء `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** علي ؓ sent عبد الله بن عباس ؓ ahead to debate them and told him not to answer until he
arrived. ابن عباس ؓ could not hold back. He argued from the verse about the two arbiters sent between a man
and his wife. They answered him with the distinction that is the strongest thing they ever said: you do not
treat the blood of Muslims the way you treat game and crops and a marriage. And they added a second point
that is harder still — that a man who was fighting them yesterday cannot be an impartial judge of them today.

**The statement:**
> تَجْعَلُ الْحُكْمَ فِي الصَّيْدِ وَالْحَرْثِ، وَبَيْنَ الْمَرْأَةِ وَزَوْجِهَا كَالْحُكْمِ فِي دِمَاءِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ؟ وَقَالُوا لَهُ: أَعَدْلٌ عِنْدَكَ عَمْرُو بْنُ الْعَاصِ، وَهُوَ بِالْأَمْسِ يُقَاتِلُنَا؟ فَإِنْ كَانَ عَدْلًا فَلَسْنَا بِعُدُولٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1368
*English:* "Do you make the judgement in game and in crops, and between a woman and her husband, like the
judgement in the blood of the Muslims? … Is عمرو بن العاص an equitable man in your eyes, when only yesterday
he was fighting us?"

**عبرت:** Do not answer a serious objection with a weak proof; it is the proof that will be remembered.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH24 · Four thousand come back — or two, or all of them
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** حروراء empties toward الكوفة.

**What happened:** The debate at حروراء lasted three days with the Book open between them. Then some of them
came back. How many is one of the places where our books plainly disagree. The soundest report says four
thousand returned repentant, ابن الكوّاء among them. A second route in the same book says two thousand. الکامل
says علي ؓ came out himself, answered them, told them to go back into their city — and every last one of them
went in.

**The statement:**
> فواضعوا عبد الله الكتاب ثلاثة أيام، فرجع منهم أربعة آلاف كلهم تائب، منهم ابن الكوا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3621
*English:* "So they laid the Book open with عبد الله for three days, and four thousand of them returned, all
of them repentant — among them ابن الكوّاء — until he brought them in to علي."

**عبرت:** An argument patiently held can turn thousands; it will not turn everyone.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH25 · The three things he promised them
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH, in الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Men stood up during his sermons and shouted the slogan at him. He called it a true word by
which a false thing was intended, and then, instead of arresting anyone, he announced his policy in three
clauses: we will not bar you from the mosques of God; we will not withhold your share of the public revenue
while your hands are with ours; and we will not strike first. He kept all three until they began killing
people on the roads.

**The statement:**
> أَمَا إِنَّ لَكَمَ عِنْدَنَا ثَلَاثًا مَا صَحِبْتُمُونَا: لَا نَمْنَعُكُمْ مَسَاجِدَ اللَّهِ أَنْ تَذْكُرُوا فِيهَا اسْمَهُ، وَلَا نَمْنَعُكُمُ الْفَيْءَ مَا دَامَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ مَعَ أَيْدِينَا، وَلَا نُقَاتِلُكُمْ حَتَّى تَبْدَأُونَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1374
*English:* "Know that you have three things from us so long as you keep company with us: we will not bar you
from the mosques of God, that you may remember His name in them; we will not withhold the فيء from you so
long as your hands are with ours; and we will not fight you until you begin against us."

**عبرت:** The measure of a government is what it grants to those who denounce it.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "What would a ruler today do with men who call him a disbeliever in his
own mosque?"

### TAA/E-KH26 · A man interrupts the sermon with a verse
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37 AH, in الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** One of them stood up while علي ؓ was speaking, put a finger in each ear, and recited the
verse *if you associate others with God, your work will be brought to nothing.* علي ؓ answered him with
another verse: *so be patient; God's promise is true, and let not those who have no certainty unsettle you.*
الشافعي رحمہ اللہ transmitted the scene as happening during the prayer itself; ابن جرير corrected it to the
sermon. ابن كثير prints both and does not force a choice.

**The statement:**
> وقد ذكر ابن جرير (٤) أن هذا [الكلام إنما قاله] وعلي في الخطبة [لا في الصلاة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3623
*English:* "And ابن جرير has mentioned that he said this [only] while علي was giving the خطبة, not in the
prayer."

**عبرت:** Two reliable men can carry the same scene with the setting moved, and a careful book will show you
both.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH27 · سعد بن أبي وقاص ؓ will not come out of the desert
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** As the arbitration approached, the son of سعد بن أبي وقاص ؓ rode out to his father's sheep
in the desert to fetch him. He argued that his father was a Companion, one of the six of the شورى, the only
great man who had kept clean of everything the community disliked — and therefore the most entitled of all
men to the caliphate. سعد ؓ refused, and gave a hadith as his reason. He never went, and he never claimed
anything.

**The statement:**
> إنه ستكون فتنة خير الناس فيها الخفي التقي" والله لا أشهد شيئًا من هذا الأمر أبدًا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3624
*English:* "There will be a فتنة; the best of people in it is the hidden, God-fearing man." — "By God, I will
never witness anything of this affair."

**عبرت:** In a time of division, the man who takes no side may be the one keeping his religion whole.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "Is standing aside from a quarrel courage, or cowardice?"

### TAA/E-KH28 · المغيرة ؓ asks each arbiter the same question
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** رمضان 37 AH, at دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** دومة الجندل / أذرح, midway between
الكوفة and الشام.

**What happened:** المغيرة بن شعبة ؓ was among the onlookers who had kept out of the war. He told the Quraysh
around him that he could find out in advance whether the two arbiters would agree. He went to عمرو ؓ and asked
how he saw men like himself who had stayed out of the fighting, and got one answer; he went to أبو موسى ؓ and
asked the same question, and got the opposite. He came back and told them what the outcome would be.

**The statement:**
> لَا يَجْتَمِعُ هَذَانِ عَلَى أَمْرٍ وَاحِدٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1371
*English:* "These two will not come together on one thing."

**عبرت:** Ask two men the same simple question and you will learn more than from a week of negotiation.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH29 · أبو موسى ؓ refuses to be bought
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 AH, at دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عمرو ؓ spent the private sessions building a case for معاوية ؓ — the wronged caliph's next
of kin, a good administrator, the brother of a Mother of the Believers, a scribe of the Prophet ﷺ — and ended
by hinting that there would be something in it for أبو موسى ؓ himself. أبو موسى ؓ refused the whole argument.
Nobility was not the qualification, he said, or the house of أبرهة would have the best claim; and if it went
by the nobility of قريش he would give it to علي ؓ. As for the hint: he would not take a bribe in the judgement
of God.

**The statement:**
> فَإِنَّ هَذَا لَيْسَ عَلَى الشَّرَفِ تَوَلَّاهُ أَهْلُهُ، وَلَوْ كَانَ عَلَى الشَّرَفِ لَكَانَ لِآلِ أَبَرْهَةَ بْنِ الصَّبَّاحِ، إِنَّمَا هُوَ لِأَهْلِ الدِّينِ وَالْفَضْلِ، مَعَ أَنِّي لَوْ كُنْتُ مُعْطِيَهُ أَفْضَلَ قُرَيْشٍ شَرَفًا أَعْطَيْتُهُ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، وَأَمَّا قَوْلُكَ: إِنَّ مُعَاوِيَةَ وَلِيُّ دَمِ عُثْمَانَ فَوَلِّهِ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ، فَلَمْ أَكُنْ لِأُوَلِّيَهُ وَأَدَعَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ الْأَوَّلِينَ، وَأَمَّا تَعْرِيضُكَ لِي بِالسُّلْطَانِ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ خَرَجَ مُعَاوِيَةُ لِي مِنْ سُلْطَانِهِ كُلِّهِ لَمَا وَلَّيْتُهُ، وَمَا كُنْتُ لِأَرْتَشِيَ فِي حُكْمِ اللَّهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1371
*English:* "If it went by nobility it would belong to the house of أبرهة بن الصباح. It belongs only to the
people of religion and merit. And besides, if I were giving it to the noblest of قريش I would give it to علي
بن أبي طالب … By God, if معاوية came out of his whole dominion for me, I would not give it to him. I am not
one to take a bribe in the judgement of God."

**عبرت:** A man may be outmanoeuvred and still be incorruptible; the two are not the same failure.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH30 · ابن عمر ؓ will not pay for the caliphate
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** رمضان 37 AH, at دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو موسى ؓ proposed عبد الله بن عمر ؓ as a candidate both sides could accept. عمرو ؓ refused,
saying the office needed a man who eats and feeds. ابن عمر ؓ was sitting there in his usual abstraction, and
ابن الزبير ؓ nudged him to attend to what was being said about him. He answered that he would never pay
anything for it — and then turned on عمرو ؓ and told him not to push the Arabs back into a second فتنة after
they had already struck each other with swords.

**The statement:**
> لا والله لا أرشو عليها شيئًا أبدًا، ثم قال: يا ابن العاص إن العرب قد أسندت إليكَ أمرَها بعدما تقارعت بالسيوف، وتشاكت (٣) بالرماح، فلا تردنهم في فتنة مثلها أو أشدّ منها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3625
*English:* "No, by God, I will never pay a bribe for it. — O son of العاص, the Arabs have committed their
affair to you after they have struck one another with swords and pierced one another with spears; do not turn
them back into a فتنة like it, or worse."

**عبرت:** The office sought by paying is the office least safe in the hands that paid.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH31 · The one thing the two men agreed
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 AH, at دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Every name was refused. معاوية ؓ was refused by أبو موسى ؓ; عمرو ؓ's own son was refused by
أبو موسى ؓ; ابن عمر ؓ was refused by عمرو ؓ. What was left was the only formula both could sign: depose both
men and hand the question back to the community as a شورى, as عمر ؓ had left it. They shook on it and went out
to the assembly to announce it.

**The statement:**
> فلما اجتمع الحكمان تراوضا على المصلحة للمسلمين، ونظرا في تقدير أمور ثم اتفقا على أن يعزلا عليًا ومعاوية ثم يجعلا الأمر شورى بين الناس ليتفقوا على الأصلح لهم منهما أو من غيرهما
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3625
*English:* "Then they agreed to depose علي and معاوية, and then to make the affair a شورى among the people, so
that they might agree upon the fittest for them of the two, or of anyone else."

**عبرت:** An agreement reached only by eliminating every alternative is rarely an agreement at all.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH32 · "Do not speak first"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 AH, at دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** As أبو موسى ؓ stepped forward to speak, عبد الله بن عباس ؓ took hold of him and warned him.
If they had truly agreed, he said, let the other man say it first and then confirm it after him — because
what is given in private may be withdrawn in public. أبو موسى ؓ said they were agreed, and went forward.
الکامل's own comment on him, in four words, is that he was an unwary man. This warning is in الکامل and not in
البدایہ.

**The statement:**
> وَيْحَكَ! وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ قَدْ خَدَعَكَ، إِنْ كُنْتُمَا اتَّفَقْتُمَا عَلَى أَمْرٍ فَقَدِّمْهُ فَلْيَتَكَلَّمْ بِهِ قَبْلَكَ، ثُمَّ تَكَلَّمْ بِهِ بَعْدَهُ، فَإِنَّهُ رَجُلٌ غَادِرٌ وَلَا آمَنُ أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدْ أَعْطَاكَ الرِّضَا بَيْنَكُمَا، فَإِذَا قُمْتَ فِي النَّاسِ خَالَفَكَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1372
*English:* "Woe to you! By God, I think he has deceived you. If the two of you have agreed on something, put
him forward and let him speak it before you, then speak it after him … I am not safe from his having given
you agreement between the two of you and then contradicting you when you stand up before the people."

**عبرت:** Advice is only useful before the step, and that is exactly when it is hardest to hear.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH33 · The two speeches
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 AH, at دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو موسى ؓ rose first, praised God, and announced what they had agreed: both men deposed,
the community to choose afresh. Then he said: and I have deposed علي and معاوية. He stepped aside. عمرو ؓ took
his place, praised God, said that this man had said what they had heard and had deposed his own principal —
and that he too deposed علي ؓ, and confirmed his own principal معاوية ؓ as the next of kin of عثمان ؓ and the
claimant of his blood. Our two books give the two speeches in almost identical words.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّ هَذَا قَدْ قَالَ مَا سَمِعْتُمُوهُ وَخَلْعَ صَاحِبَهُ، وَأَنَا أَخْلَعُ صَاحِبَهُ كَمَا خَلَعَهُ، وَأُثْبِتُ صَاحِبِي مُعَاوِيَةَ، فَإِنَّهُ وَلِيُّ ابْنِ عَفَّانَ، وَالطَّالِبُ بِدَمِهِ، وَأَحَقُّ النَّاسِ بِمَقَامِهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1372
*English:* "This man has said what you have heard, and has deposed his own principal; and I depose his
principal as he has deposed him, and confirm my own principal معاوية — for he is the next of kin of ابن عفان
and the claimant of his blood, and the most entitled of people to his place."

**عبرت:** Two men can keep the same words and mean two different agreements by them.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH34 · The onlookers say what happened, so that we do not have to
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 AH, at دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The assembly broke up in noise. سعد ؓ said to أبو موسى ؓ that he had been no match for عمرو ؓ
and his devices. أبو موسى ؓ asked what he was supposed to do. ابن عباس ؓ told him there was no blame on him —
the blame was on whoever had put him forward. And ابن عمر ؓ looked at the two of them and said what the affair
of this community had come to. Every verdict on this day in our books is a named Companion's; none of it needs
to be ours.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ سَعْدٌ: مَا أَضْعَفَكَ يَا أَبَا مُوسَى عَنْ عَمْرٍو وَمَكَايِدِهِ! فَقَالَ أَبُو مُوسَى: فَمَا أَصْنَعُ؟ وَافَقَنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ ثُمَّ نَزَعَ عَنْهُ! فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: لَا ذَنْبَ لَكَ يَا أَبَا مُوسَى، الذَّنْبُ لِمَنْ قَدَّمَكَ فِي هَذَا الْمَقَامِ. قَالَ: غَدَرَ فَمَا أَصْنَعُ؟ فَقَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ: انْظُرُوا إِلَى مَا صَارَ أَمْرُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ! صَارَ إِلَى رَجُلٍ مَا يُبَالِي مَا صَنَعَ وَإِلَى آخَرَ ضَعِيفٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1372
*English:* "سعد said: how weak you were, O أبو موسى, against عمرو and his devices! … ابن عباس said: there is
no fault on you, O أبو موسى; the fault is on whoever put you forward in this station … And ابن عمر said: look
at what the affair of this community has come to! It has come to a man who does not care what he does, and to
another who is weak."

**عبرت:** When those who were present have already spoken, the one who comes later should quote and not add.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH35 · "اجتهاد errs and is right"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** — `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير does not narrate the outcome as a simple betrayal. He sets out what عمرو ؓ was
weighing: that to leave the community with no imam at all, in that condition, would open a longer and wider
corruption than the disagreement they already had. Then he closes the whole affair with the formula by which
Sunni scholarship handles disputes among Companions — a judgement was exercised, and a judgement can hit or
miss.

**The statement:**
> فأقرَّ معاوية لما رأى [في] ذلك من المصلحة، [فاجتهد] والاجتهاد يخطئ ويصيب
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3626
*English:* "So he confirmed معاوية, for what he saw in that of benefit; [he exercised اجتهاد] and اجتهاد errs
and is right."

**عبرت:** To say that a man may have erred is not to say that he betrayed; the difference is the whole of
this subject.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH36 · A hadith that would have settled it — and is forged
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** — `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** There is a report, transmitted with a chain through البيهقي, in which the Prophet ﷺ is said
to have foretold two arbiters who would go astray and lead astray. If it were sound it would settle the whole
question. ابن كثير declares it a منكر report whose attribution to the Prophet ﷺ is forged, and gives two
reasons: علي ؓ would never have agreed to the arbitration had he known such a thing, and the man in the chain,
زكريا بن يحيى, was declared worthless by ابن معين.

**The statement:**
> فإنه حديث منكر ورفعه موضوع
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3626
*English:* "For it is a منكر hadith, and its attribution to the Prophet is forged."

**عبرت:** The report that settles an argument too neatly is the one to examine first.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH37 · علي ؓ declares the verdict void
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37–38 AH, in الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة; an arrow drawn toward الشام.

**What happened:** When the news came back, علي ؓ stood up in الكوفة, recited the verse of a man whose counsel
was rejected until the morning after, and told them plainly: I gave you my judgement on these two men and on
this arbitration, and you refused it. He then declared the two arbiters' ruling void on the ground written
into the document itself — they had judged by neither the Book nor the سنة — and called the army to march on
الشام. He wrote to the men at النهر to come and join him.

**The statement:**
> إِلَّا أَنَّ هَذَيْنِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ اللَّذَيْنِ اخْتَرْتُمُوهَمَا حَكَمَيْنِ قَدْ نَبَذَا حُكْمَ الْقُرْآنِ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمَا، وَأَحْيَيَا مَا أَمَاتَ الْقُرْآنُ، وَاتَّبَعَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا هَوَاهُ بِغَيْرِ هُدًى مِنَ اللَّهِ، فَحَكَمَا بِغَيْرِ حُجَّةٍ بَيِّنَةٍ، وَلَا سُنَّةٍ مَاضِيَةٍ، وَاخْتَلَفَا فِي حُكْمِهِمَا، وَكِلَاهُمَا لَمْ يَرْشُدْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1377
*English:* "Except that these two men whom you chose as arbiters have flung the judgement of the Qur'an behind
their backs, and given life to what the Qur'an put to death, and each of them followed his own desire without
guidance from God; they judged without clear proof or established سنة, and they differed in their judgement,
and neither of them was rightly guided."

**عبرت:** A ruling agreed under conditions is void when the conditions are broken — but saying so is easier
than being believed.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH38 · Their answer: confess to unbelief first
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** النهروان marked east of the Tigris.

**What happened:** علي ؓ's letter reached them at النهر. Their reply closed the door. He had not been angry for
his Lord, they wrote, only for himself; if he would testify against himself that he had committed كفر by
agreeing to the arbitration, and begin again with repentance, then they would look into the matter between
them. Otherwise they had repudiated him on equal terms. When he read it, he gave up on them.

**The statement:**
> فَإِنَّكَ لَمْ تَغْضَبْ لِرَبِّكَ، وَإِنَّمَا غَضِبْتَ لِنَفْسِكَ، فَإِنْ شَهِدْتَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ بِالْكُفْرِ، وَاسْتَقْبَلْتَ التَّوْبَةَ، نَظَرْنَا فِيمَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ، وَإِلَّا فَقَدْ نَبَذْنَاكَ عَلَى سَوَاءٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1378
*English:* "You were not angry for your Lord; you were angry only for yourself. If you bear witness against
yourself to كفر and take up repentance afresh, we will consider what is between us and you; and if not, we
have repudiated you on equal terms."

**عبرت:** A demand that a man declare himself a disbeliever is not a condition for peace; it is a refusal of
it.

**Hands-up?** no
