### TAA/E-KH39 · They leave الكوفة one by one
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** شوال, 37–38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** small arrows leaving الكوفة, converging on the
bridge at النهروان.

**What happened:** They met in private houses. Four men were offered the command and all four refused it;
عبد الله بن وهب الراسبي took it, saying he took it neither out of desire for the world nor left it out of fear
of death, and they gave him the pledge on the tenth of شوال. They rejected a plan to seize المدائن as
impossible and settled on the bridge at النهروان instead. And they agreed to leave the city singly and in
secret, so that their families could not stop them. They spent the last night in worship.

**The statement:**
> هَاتُوهَا، أَمَا وَاللَّهِ لَا آخُذُهَا رَغْبَةً فِي الدُّنْيَا، وَلَا أَدَعُهَا فَرَقًا مِنَ الْمَوْتِ. فَبَايَعُوهُ لِعَشَرٍ خَلَوْنَ مِنْ شَوَّالٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1375
*English:* "Bring it here. By God, I do not take it out of desire for this world, nor do I leave it out of
dread of death. — And they gave him the pledge on the tenth night of شوال."

**عبرت:** Sincerity organises as carefully as ambition does, and that is precisely why it is dangerous when
it is wrong.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH40 · What leaving cost them
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** They did not slip away from nothing. البدایہ says they went out from among fathers and
mothers, uncles and aunts, and left all their kin behind. Some families caught their sons on the road and
dragged them back and shamed them out of it; some of those later ran away again and rejoined. عدي بن حاتم ؓ
went after his own son طرفة and could not catch him. He buried him after النهروان.

**The statement:**
> فخرجوا من بين الآباء والأمهات والأخوال والخالات (٨) وفارقوا سائر القرابات
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3629
*English:* "So they went out from among fathers and mothers and uncles and aunts, and parted from all their
kin."

**عبرت:** What a man is willing to lose tells you how certain he is — and certainty is not the same as being
right.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH41 · عبد الله بن خباب ؓ is asked for a hadith
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, on the road near النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the النهروان canal.

**What happened:** On the road they stopped a man leading a donkey with his wife on it. He told them he was
عبد الله بن خباب, son of the Companion خباب بن الأرت ؓ. They said he had nothing to fear and asked him for a
hadith from his father. He gave them one about a فتنة in which a man's heart dies as his body dies. They said
that was exactly the hadith they had asked for — and then examined him on أبو بكر ؓ, on عمر ؓ, on عثمان ؓ, and
on علي ؓ before and after the arbitration. He answered well of all of them. They told him he was judging men
by their names and not their deeds.

**The statement:**
> أَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ خَبَّابٍ صَاحِبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - فَقَالُوا لَهُ: أَفْزَعْنَاكَ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ. قَالُوا: لَا رَوْعَ عَلَيْكَ، حَدِّثْنَا عَنْ أَبِيكَ حَدِيثًا سَمِعَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - تَنْفَعُنَا بِهِ. فَقَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - أَنَّهُ قَالَ: " «تَكُونُ فِتْنَةٌ يَمُوتُ فِيهَا قَلْبُ الرَّجُلِ كَمَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا بَدَنُهُ، يُمْسِي فِيهَا مُؤْمِنًا وَيُصْبِحُ كَافِرًا، وَيُصْبِحُ كَافِرًا وَيُمْسِي مُؤْمِنًا» ". قَالُوا: لِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ سَأَلْنَاكَ، فَمَا تَقُولُ فِي أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ؟ فَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِمَا خَيْرًا. قَالُوا: مَا تَقُولُ فِي عُثْمَانَ فِي أَوَّلِ خِلَافَتِهِ وَفِي آخِرِهَا؟ قَالَ: إِنَّهُ كَانَ مُحِقًّا فِي أَوَّلِهَا وَفِي آخِرِهَا. قَالُوا: فَمَا تَقُولُ فِي عَلِيٍّ قَبْلَ التَّحْكِيمِ وَبَعْدَهُ؟ قَالَ: إِنَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْكُمْ، وَأَشَدُّ تَوَقِّيًا عَلَى دِينِهِ، وَأَنْفَذُ بَصِيرَةً. فَقَالُوا: إِنَّكَ تَتَّبِعُ الْهَوَى، وَتُوَالِي الرِّجَالَ عَلَى أَسْمَائِهَا لَا عَلَى أَفْعَالِهَا، وَاللَّهِ لَنَقْتُلَنَّكَ قَتْلَةً مَا قَتَلْنَاهَا أَحَدًا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1380
*English:* "They said: what do you say of عثمان at the beginning of his caliphate and at its end? He said: he
was in the right at its beginning and at its end. They said: what do you say of علي before the arbitration
and after it? He said: he knows God better than you do, and is more careful of his religion, and of more
penetrating insight."

**عبرت:** A man was killed for refusing to condemn anyone; that is what the position had become.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH42 · The date, the pig, and the throat
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** While he was in their hands, a ripe date fell from a palm and one of them put it in his
mouth; another told him he had taken it without right or price, and he spat it out. Then a pig belonging to a
protected non-Muslim crossed their path and one of them struck it with his sword; the others called it
corruption in the earth, and the man went and made the owner content. Then they laid عبد الله بن خباب ؓ down
and cut his throat, and killed his wife, who was with child. Both of our books put the date and the pig
immediately before the killing, deliberately.

**The statement:**
> فَسَقَطَتْ مِنْهُ رُطَبَةٌ، فَأَخَذَهَا أَحَدُهُمْ فَتَرَكَهَا فِي فِيهِ، فَقَالَ آخَرُ: أَخَذْتَهَا بِغَيْرِ حِلِّهَا وَبِغَيْرِ ثَمَنٍ، فَأَلْقَاهَا. ثُمَّ مَرَّ بِهِمْ خِنْزِيرٌ لِأَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ، فَضَرَبَهُ أَحَدُهُمْ بِسَيْفِهِ، فَقَالُوا: هَذَا فَسَادٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ. فَلَقِيَ صَاحِبَ الْخِنْزِيرِ فَأَرْضَاهُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1380
*English:* "A ripe date fell, and one of them took it and put it in his mouth. Another said: you have taken it
without its being lawful to you and without price — so he threw it away. Then a pig belonging to the people
of the ذمة passed them, and one of them struck it with his sword. They said: this is corruption in the earth.
So he met the owner of the pig and satisfied him."

**عبرت:** Scruple about a date and no scruple about a life is not piety with a flaw in it; it is a different
thing wearing piety's clothes.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "Can a man be scrupulous about small things and reckless with great ones?"

### TAA/E-KH43 · The envoy who was killed for asking
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When reports of the killings reached علي ؓ he did not move the army. He sent one man, الحارث
بن مرة العبدي, with instructions to find out what had actually happened and write back plainly, holding
nothing from him. The moment الحارث came near enough to ask, they killed him. الکامل says they gave him no
respite at all.

**The statement:**
> فأرسل علي إلى الخوارج رسولًا من جهته وهو الحارث (٦) بن مرة العبدي، فقال: اخبر لي خبرهم، واعلم لي أمرهم واكتب إلي به على الجلية، فلما قدم عليهم قتلوه ولم ينظروه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3631
*English:* "So علي sent to the خوارج a messenger of his own, الحارث بن مرة العبدي, and said: bring me their
news, and learn me their affair, and write to me of it as it plainly is. And when he came to them they killed
him and gave him no respite."

**عبرت:** The refusal to be questioned is the last stage before the refusal to be lived with.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH44 · The army turns round
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, at النُّخيلة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the arrow toward الشام swings east to
النهروان.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had mustered for الشام — sixty-five thousand from الكوفة and three thousand two
hundred from البصرة — and had told the army to forget these people and march west. The army refused. They
would not leave men behind them who killed unarmed families while their own were undefended. الأشعث بن قيس ؓ,
whom everyone had assumed sympathised with the dissenters, stood up and asked for the same thing. علي ؓ agreed
to deal with النهروان first.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ النَّاسُ يَرَوْنَ أَنَّ الْأَشْعَثَ يَرَى رَأْيَهُمْ ; لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ يَوْمَ صِفِّينَ: أَنْصَفَنَا قَوْمٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ. فَلَمَّا قَالَ هَذِهِ الْمَقَالَةَ عَلِمَ النَّاسُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَرَى رَأْيَهُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1381
*English:* "And people used to think that الأشعث held their opinion, because he used to say on the day of
صفين: *a people who call to the Book of God have dealt fairly with us.* But when he made this statement, the
people knew that he had not held their opinion."

**عبرت:** A danger at your back decides your plans more surely than a danger in front of you.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH45 · The astrologer on the road
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH, on the march `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the march from الكوفة, across the bridge.

**What happened:** On the way an astrologer met him and told him to march at one particular hour of the day
and no other, or he and his men would come to harm. علي ؓ deliberately marched at a different hour, and said
why: we march trusting in God, relying on Him, and giving the lie to the astrologer. Afterwards, when the
battle was won, he added the second half of the reason — had he marched at the appointed hour, the ignorant
would have said the hour had done it.

**The statement:**
> فلقيه هنالك منجم فأشار عليه بوقت من النهار يسير فيه ولا يسير في غيره فإنه [إن سار في غيره] يخشى عليه فخالفه علي فسار على خلاف ما قال [المنجم وقال: نسير ثقة باللّه وتوكلًا عليه وتكذيبًا لقول المنجم]
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3632
*English:* "So علي went against him and marched contrary to what he had said [the astrologer; and he said: we
march trusting in God and relying upon Him, and giving the lie to the word of the astrologer]."

**عبرت:** It is not enough to reject a superstition; you must be seen to reject it, or your success will
confirm it.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "Who tells the army when it is a good day to march?"

### TAA/E-KH46 · "Hand over the killers, and I will leave you"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, at النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the two armies either side of the canal.

**What happened:** Facing them across the water, علي ؓ did not demand submission or repentance. He demanded a
narrow thing: hand over the men who killed our brothers, so that I may take the penalty for them, and then I
will leave you alone and go to الشام, and perhaps God will turn your hearts. Their answer made the battle
inevitable. All of us killed them, they said, and all of us hold your blood and theirs lawful.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّا حَكَّمْنَا، فَلَمَّا حَكَّمْنَا، أَثِمْنَا، وَكُنَّا بِذَلِكَ كَافِرِينَ وَقَدْ تُبْنَا، فَإِنْ تُبْتَ فَنَحْنُ مَعَكَ وَمِنْكَ، وَإِنْ أَبَيْتَ فَإِنَّا مُنَابِذُوكَ عَلَى سَوَاءٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1382
*English:* "We arbitrated; and when we arbitrated we sinned, and by that we were disbelievers, and we have
repented. So if you repent, we are with you and of you; and if you refuse, we repudiate you on equal terms."

**عبرت:** A demand narrow enough to be met is a mercy; refusing it is a choice.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH47 · "Am I to bear witness against myself to كفر?"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, at النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** They told him to their faces that by agreeing to the arbitration he had become a
disbeliever, that they themselves had repented of it, and that he must do the same before they would rejoin
him. His answer is the sentence to end the scene on: after belief in the Messenger ﷺ, after the emigration
with him, after the years of striving — am I now to testify against myself to unbelief? He turned away from
them. He also warned them that a chicken killed over such a cause would be grave with God.

**The statement:**
> أَبْعَدَ إِيمَانِي بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - وَهِجْرَتِي مَعَهُ وَجِهَادِي فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَشْهَدُ عَلَى نَفْسِي بِالْكُفْرِ! لَقَدْ ضَلَلْتُ إِذًا، وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُهْتَدِينَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1382
*English:* "After my faith in the Messenger of God ﷺ, and my emigration with him, and my striving in the way
of God — am I to bear witness against myself to كفر? I should then indeed have gone astray, and I should not
be among the rightly guided."

**عبرت:** A lifetime of service is not a bargaining chip to be surrendered to whoever shouts loudest.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH48 · The banner of safety
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, at النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a banner planted between the two lines.

**What happened:** Before the fighting علي ؓ gave أبو أيوب الأنصاري ؓ a banner and had him call out that anyone
who came to it was safe, and anyone who simply went home to الكوفة or المدائن was safe, and that the only men
wanted were the killers. Most of the army opposite walked away. One of their own commanders, فروة بن نوفل
الأشجعي, took five hundred horse out because he could not see what they were fighting علي ؓ for. Of four
thousand, our books say a thousand or fewer — or eighteen hundred — were left.

**The statement:**
> من جاء إلى هذه الراية فهو آمن، ومن انصرف إلى الكوفة والمدائن فهو آمن، إنه لا حاجة لنا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3632
*English:* "Whoever comes to this banner is safe, and whoever withdraws to الكوفة or to المدائن is safe; we
have no need of you —" (البدایہ completes it: "except for those who killed our brothers").

**عبرت:** Give a man an honourable way out and most men will take it; the ones who stay have chosen.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH49 · "They have not crossed the bridge"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH, at النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the bridge over the canal.

**What happened:** A scout came back and reported that the enemy had crossed the water. علي ؓ said they had
not. A second scout, frightened of getting close, reported the same thing, and men around him began to doubt
him openly. He said again: by God they have not crossed; their places of falling are on this side of the
bridge; and not ten of you will be killed, and not ten of them will survive. When they rode forward and found
them uncrossed, the army shouted the takbīr.

**The statement:**
> وَاللَّهِ مَا عَبَرُوهُ، وَإِنَّ مَصَارِعَهُمْ لَدُونَ الْجِسْرِ، وَوَاللَّهِ لَا يُقْتَلُ مِنْكُمْ عَشْرَةٌ، وَلَا يَسْلَمُ مِنْهُمْ عَشْرَةٌ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1383
*English:* "By God, they have not crossed it; their places of falling are on this side of the bridge. And by
God, not ten of you will be killed, and not ten of them will be spared."

**عبرت:** Composure under contradiction from your own side is a commander's rarest quality.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH50 · An hour, and it was over
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, at النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** النهروان lights and then goes out.

**What happened:** علي ؓ ordered his men not to strike first. The others came on shouting *to Paradise, to
Paradise* and threw themselves at his cavalry. The horse split left and right, the archers took their faces
with arrows, the horse wheeled back on them from both wings and the infantry came in with spears. الکامل says
they were destroyed within the hour, as though someone had said to them: die — and they died. Seven men were
killed on علي ؓ's side. Both of our books say seven.

**The statement:**
> فَتَنَادَوْا: الرَّوَاحَ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ! وَحَمَلُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ، فَافْتَرَقَتْ خَيْلُ عَلِيٍّ فِرْقَتَيْنِ: فِرْقَةٌ نَحْوَ الْمَيْمَنَةِ، وَفِرْقَةٌ نَحْوَ الْمَيْسَرَةِ، وَاسْتَقْبَلَتِ الرُّمَاةُ وُجُوهَهُمْ بِالنَّبْلِ، عَطَفَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَيْلُ مِنَ الْمَيْمَنَةِ وَالْمَيْسَرَةِ، وَنَهَضَ إِلَيْهِمُ الرِّجَالُ بِالرِّمَاحِ وَالسُّيُوفِ، فَمَا لَبِثُوا أَنْ أَنَامُوهُمْ. فَلَمَّا رَأَى حَمْزَةُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ الْهَلَاكَ نَادَى أَصْحَابَهُ: أَنِ انْزِلُوا! فَذَهَبُوا لِيَنْزِلُوا، فَلَمْ يَلْبَثُوا أَنْ حَمَلَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَسْوَدُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ الْمُرَادِيُّ، وَجَاءَتْهُمُ الْخَيْلُ مِنْ نَحْوِ عَلِيٍّ، فَأُهْلِكُوا فِي سَاعَةٍ، فَكَأَنَّمَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ مُوتُوا فَمَاتُوا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1384
*English:* "And they were destroyed in an hour — as though it had been said to them: die, and they died."

**عبرت:** Courage without judgement buys nothing at all; it only decides the hour.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH51 · The man with the stunted arm
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, after the battle `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the bank of the canal.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had told his companions, before any of this began, that a people would come out who
would pass through the religion as an arrow passes through the game, and that their sign would be a man among
them with a stunted arm. After the battle he sent men to look for the body. Some said it was not there. He
said: by God I did not lie and I was not lied to. It was found in a hollow on the bank among forty or fifty
dead, and the arm was as described. He prostrated a long prostration.

**The statement:**
> اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ مَا كَذَبْتُ وَلَا كُذِبْتُ، لَوْلَا أَنْ تَنْكُلُوا عَنِ الْعَمَلِ لَأَخْبَرْتُكُمْ بِمَا قَصَّ اللَّهُ عَلَى لِسَانِ نَبِيِّهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - لِمَنْ قَاتَلَهُمْ مُسْتَبْصِرًا فِي قِتَالِهِمْ، عَارِفًا لِلْحَقِّ الَّذِي نَحْنُ عَلَيْهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۹۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1386
*English:* "God is greatest! I did not lie and I was not lied to. Were it not that you would hold back from
working, I would tell you what God has related on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ for whoever fought them with
insight in fighting them, knowing the truth that we are upon."

**عبرت:** He would not tell them the reward, in case knowing it made them stop working for it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH52 · أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ cross-examines a witness
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after 40 AH, in المدينة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** After the killing of علي ؓ, a man who had been at النهروان came in to أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ.
She made him promise to tell her the truth and then questioned him: about the men علي ؓ had fought, about what
they had held against him, about ذو الثدية, and finally about what علي ؓ had said standing over the body. He
told her علي ؓ had said only *God and His Messenger spoke the truth.* She accepted that, and added a warning
about everything else that was being said. أحمد alone transmits the report and ابن كثير calls its chain sound.

**The statement:**
> يرحم الله عليا إنه كان لا يرى شيئًا يعجبه إلا قال صدق الله ورسوله، فيذهب أهل العراق يكذبون عليه ويزيدون عليه في الحديث
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3622
*English:* "May God have mercy on علي. He would never see a thing that pleased him but he said: *God and His
Messenger spoke the truth.* And the people of العراق go and lie about him and add to the report."

**عبرت:** The first people to warn us that reports about this period are inflated are the people who lived
through it.

**Hands-up?** Before telling this: "Who in this room would know how to check a story about something they did
not see?"

### TAA/E-KH53 · "Our brothers who wronged us"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** After the battle علي ؓ was asked directly what these people had been. Were they idolaters?
He said: it was from idolatry that they fled. Were they hypocrites, then? He said: the hypocrites hardly
remember God at all, and these prayed all night. Then what were they, أمير المؤمنين? He said: our brothers,
who wronged us — so we fought them for their wrong against us. He fought them and refused to unbelieve them,
and both halves of that are the record.

**The statement:**
> النهروان أمشركون هم؟ فقال: من الشرك فروا، قيل: أفمنافقون؟ قال: إن المنافقين لا يذكرون الله إِلَّا قليلًا. فقيل: فما هم يا أمير المؤمنين؟ قال: إخواننا بَغَوا علينا فقاتلناهم ببغيهم علينا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
*English:* "Are they polytheists? He said: it is from polytheism that they fled. It was said: are they
hypocrites, then? He said: the hypocrites do not remember God but little. It was said: then what are they, O
أمير المؤمنين? He said: our brothers who wronged us, so we fought them for their wrong against us."

**عبرت:** You may have to fight a man without being permitted to expel him from the religion.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH54 · The wounded are sent home to their own tribes
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH, after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Four hundred of the defeated were found alive and wounded. علي ؓ had them handed over to
their own clans to be nursed. He took no fifth of anything captured: weapons and mounts actually used in the
fighting were divided among the Muslims, and everything else — goods, servants, household property — was
returned to the owners, down to a cooking pot that was brought to him last of all and that he sent back.

**The statement:**
> أن عليًا لم يخمس ما أصاب من الخوارج يوم النهروان ولكن رده إلى أهله (٥) كله حتى كان آخر ذلك مرجل أتي به فرده
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3633
*English:* "That علي took no fifth of what he took from the خوارج on the day of النهروان, but returned it to
its owners, all of it — until the last of it was a cooking pot brought to him, and he returned it."

**عبرت:** How a victor treats the property of the defeated says what he thought he was fighting for.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH55 · "They are in the loins of men"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** His men came to him congratulating him: praise God, who has cut off their last trace.
He said: not at all. They are in the loins of men and the wombs of women, and when they come out they will
seldom meet anyone without gathering to overcome him. He also walked among the dead saying: wretchedness to
you — he who deceived you has harmed you. Asked who deceived them, he said: Satan, and a soul that commands
evil.

**The statement:**
> كلا واللّه إنهم لفي أصلاب الرجال وأرحام النساء، فإذا خرجوا من بين الشرايين فقلما يلقون أحدًا إِلَّا ألفوا (٦) أن يظهروا عليه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3634
*English:* "Never, by God — they are in the loins of men and the wombs of women; and when they come out from
between the arteries, seldom do they meet anyone but they gather to overcome him."

**عبرت:** An idea is not killed on a battlefield; only the men holding it that day are.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH56 · The victory that changed nothing
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH, at النُّخيلة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the arrow toward الشام fades out.

**What happened:** النهروان was won in an hour and the march on الشام was supposed to follow immediately. علي ؓ
told the army to turn from where they stood and go. They asked to go home first — arrows spent, swords blunt,
spearheads gone. He camped them at النُّخيلة and told them not to visit their families. Within days the camp
emptied man by man until only a few notables were left, and he went back into الكوفة with his plan broken.
Meanwhile the Syrians had pledged معاوية ؓ as caliph, and he only grew stronger.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ أَهْلُ الشَّامِ يَنْتَظِرُونَ بَعْدَ صِفِّينَ أَمْرَ الْحَكَمَيْنِ، فَلَمَّا تَفَرَّقَا بَايَعَ أَهْلُ الشَّامِ مُعَاوِيَةَ بِالْخِلَافَةِ، وَلَمْ يَزْدَدْ إِلَّا قُوَّةً، وَاخْتَلَفَ النَّاسُ بِالْعِرَاقِ عَلَى عَلِيٍّ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۰۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1395
*English:* "And when the two parted, أهل الشام gave معاوية the pledge as caliph, and he only increased in
strength; and the people in العراق differed over علي."

**عبرت:** A battle won inside your own house is not a victory; it is the cost of not having settled the
argument earlier.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH57 · The hadith علي ؓ recited to the army before it marched
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH, before النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** As the army moved, علي ؓ told them what he had heard from the Prophet ﷺ — that a people
would come out of this community whose recitation would make theirs look like nothing, and whose prayer and
fasting would make theirs look like nothing, and who would recite the Qur'an supposing it was for them when
it was against them. He said he hoped these were the people, because they had shed forbidden blood; and he
told them to march in the name of God. The report is in صحيح مسلم.

**The statement:**
> يخرج قوم من أمتي يقرؤون القرآن ليس قراءتكم إلى قراءتهم بشيء، ولا صلاتكم إلى صلاتهم بشيء، ولا صيامكم إلى صيامهم بشيء، يقرؤون القرآن يحسبون أنه لهم وهو عليهم
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
*English:* "There will come out of my community a people who recite the Qur'an — your recitation compared to
theirs is nothing, nor your prayer compared to their prayer, nor your fasting compared to their fasting. They
recite the Qur'an supposing it is for them, and it is against them."

**عبرت:** The measure of a reading of the Book is not how much of it a man has memorised.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAA/E-KH58 · The editor who disagrees with ابن كثير in a footnote
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** — `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير collects twelve chains from علي ؓ alone for the hadiths about this group and says
such a thing reaches the degree of تواتر. The editor of this printing appends a signed footnote disagreeing:
there is evident exaggeration in that, he writes, because most of these routes are weak. The card is recorded
so that nobody in a later pass mistakes the footnote for the book — and as a reminder that a printed page has
two authors.

**The statement:**
> في قوله: ومثل هذا يبلغ حد التواتر، فيه مبالغة ظاهرة، ذلك أن أكثر هذه الطرق ضعيفة، كما سيأتي
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
*English:* "In his words *and the like of this reaches the degree of تواتر* there is evident exaggeration,
since most of these routes are weak, as will come."

**عبرت:** Read the footnotes: the page you are holding was edited by someone with opinions of his own.

**Hands-up?** no

## What the Prophet ﷺ is reported to have said about the خوارج

*Source note: [`the-khawarij-in-the-prophetic-reports.md`](../docs/research/the-khawarij-in-the-prophetic-reports.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TKI/E-KR1 · What علي ؓ answered when asked what they were
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** النهروان lights, east of the Tigris

**What happened:** As soon as the fighting was over men came to علي ؓ with the question the whole room
will be carrying. Were these people idolaters? He said no: it was idolatry they had fled from. Were they
hypocrites, then? He said no: the hypocrites hardly remember Allah at all, and these men did nothing but
remember Him. Then what were they? He gave them a single sentence and stopped there. البدایہ places this
exchange at the head of the chapter and says openly that it takes it from ابن جرير and others.

**The statement:**
> قيل: فما هم يا أمير المؤمنين؟ قال: إخواننا بَغَوا علينا فقاتلناهم ببغيهم علينا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
> *English:* "It was said: then what are they, O commander of the believers? He said: our brothers who transgressed against us, so we fought them for their transgression against us."

**عبرت:** The man who had just fought them refused both of the easy names for them, and the sentence he
chose cost him more than either.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKI/E-KR2 · A chapter of reports, and a count of twelve
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** البدایہ's own arrangement `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير stops the narrative at this point and opens a separate chapter for the
Prophetic reports about these people. He begins with علي ؓ, and before he gives a single report he counts
his evidence: twelve different men narrate this from علي ؓ, and he names all twelve. He then says what
that number means to him, and he says it before he has proved anything, which is his way of telling the
reader where the chapter is going.

**The statement:**
> فهذه اثنتا عشرة طريقًا إليه سرَاها بأسانيدها وألفاظها، ومثل هذا يبلغ حد التواتر (٤).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
> *English:* "These are twelve routes to him, which I shall relate with their isnads and their wordings; and the like of this reaches the degree of تواتر."

**عبرت:** Counting the routes before telling the story is not a scholar's fussiness; it is what makes the
story usable a thousand years later.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: how many separate people would have to tell you the same thing before you
would repeat it yourself?

### TKI/E-KR3 · The first report is مسلم's, from a man in the army
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking; quoted by علي ؓ before النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The first of the twelve comes through زيد بن وهب الجهني, who was not a bystander — he
was in the army that marched out. He heard علي ؓ address the troops and quote the Prophet ﷺ on the men
they were about to meet. The description is not of wickedness. It is of worship so intense that the
soldiers listening would be embarrassed to compare their own.

**The statement:**
> "يخرج قوم من أمتي يقرؤون القرآن ليس قراءتكم إلى قراءتهم بشيء، ولا صلاتكم إلى صلاتهم بشيء، ولا صيامكم إلى صيامهم بشيء، يقرؤون القرآن يحسبون أنه لهم وهو عليهم".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
> *English:* "A people will come out of my ummah who recite the Qurʾān — your reciting is nothing beside their reciting, your prayer nothing beside their prayer, your fasting nothing beside their fasting. They recite the Qurʾān supposing that it is for them, and it is against them."

**عبرت:** The warning was never about men who prayed too little.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR4 · A sign given before anyone had been killed
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** In the same address علي ؓ gave the army something that could be checked afterwards. He
said there was a man among them with an upper arm and no forearm, and on the end of that arm something
shaped like a nipple with white hairs on it. He said it before the two lines met, in front of an army of
witnesses, and it could only go one of two ways.

**The statement:**
> وآية ذلك أن فيهم رجلًا له عَضُد ليس له ذراع، على رأس عضده [مثل] حلمة الثَّدي، عليه شعرات بيضى،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
> *English:* "And the sign of that is that among them is a man with an upper arm and no forearm, on the end of his upper arm something like the nipple of a breast, with white hairs on it,"

**عبرت:** A claim made in advance, in public, about something that can be looked at, is a different kind
of claim from one made afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR5 · The order to march, and what it cost
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** before النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the army turns from the road to الشام

**What happened:** علي ؓ told the army plainly what he was choosing. They were about to set off for الشام,
and he was turning them instead against men who would be left behind among their own families and
property. He said he hoped these were the people the Prophet ﷺ had described, gave his reason — blood
unlawfully shed and herds raided — and ordered the march.

**The statement:**
> وتتركون هؤلاء يخلفونكم في ذراريِّكم وأموالكم، و [اللّه] إني لأرجو أن يكونوا هؤلاء القومَ، فإنَّهم قد سفكوا الدَّم الحرام وأغاروا في سرح الناس، فسيروا على اسم اللّه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3635
> *English:* "…and leave these people behind you among your children and your property — and by Allah I hope that these are the people, for they have shed forbidden blood and raided the people’s grazing herds. So march, in the name of Allah."

**عبرت:** The nearer danger was the one at home.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR6 · Their own commander orders the scabbards broken
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the bridge at النهروان

**What happened:** On the other side the order given was to throw down the spears, draw the swords and
break the scabbards, so that no man could sheathe his sword again. Their commander عبد الله بن وهب
الراسبي gave the reason himself: he was afraid that if the two sides got close enough to talk, his men
would be talked round, as they had been talked round once before at حروراء. So he made turning back
impossible.

**The statement:**
> ألقوا الرماح وسُلّوا سيوفكم واكسروا جفونَها (١) فإني أخاف أن يناشدوكم كما ناشدوكم يوم حروراء،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3636
> *English:* "Throw down the spears and draw your swords and break their scabbards, for I fear that they will appeal to you as they appealed to you on the day of حروراء,"

**عبرت:** A man who must destroy his own line of retreat before the argument starts already knows the
argument can be lost.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: why would a commander break his own men's scabbards?

### TKI/E-KR7 · Two men lost
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The route in مسلم reports the outcome in a single clause: the men on the other side
fell one on top of another, and of علي ؓ's army only two men were lost that day. البدایہ gives no total
for the other side anywhere in this chapter.

**The statement:**
> وما أصيب من الناس يومئذ إِلَّا رجلان، فقال (٢) علي: التمسوا فيهم المُخْدَج (٣)، فالتمسوه فلم يجدوه، فقام على بنفسه حتى أتى ناسًا [قد قتل] بعضهم على بعض، فقال: أخروهم فوجدوه مما يلي الأرض (٤) فكبر [علي] ثم قال: صدق الله وبلغ رسوله.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3636
> *English:* "And of the people, only two men were lost that day."

**عبرت:** The lopsidedness of the day is part of why the men who won it needed the sign so badly.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR8 · علي ؓ gets down and searches the bodies himself
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the fighting stopped he told them to find the maimed man. They searched and came
back with nothing. He did not send them again from where he stood — he went himself, walked to a place
where the bodies had fallen on each other, and told them to pull the bodies back. The man was underneath,
against the ground. He said the takbīr, and then one sentence.

**The statement:**
> فقام على بنفسه حتى أتى ناسًا [قد قتل] بعضهم على بعض، فقال: أخروهم فوجدوه مما يلي الأرض (٤) فكبر [علي] ثم قال: صدق الله وبلغ رسوله.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3636
> *English:* "So he rose himself until he came to some people fallen one upon another, and said: move them back — and they found him next to the ground. Then علي made takbīr and said: Allah has spoken truly and His Messenger has conveyed."

**عبرت:** He would not accept his own men's report until he had seen it with his own eyes.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR9 · عبيدة السلماني makes the caliph swear, three times
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** With the body in front of them, عبيدة السلماني stood up and put the commander of the
believers on oath. By Allah beside whom there is no god — did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah
ﷺ yourself? He swore that he had. عبيدة made him swear a second time, and a third. مسلم records the
exchange, and البدایہ prints it as the end of its first route.

**The statement:**
> فاستحلفه ثلاثًا وهو يحلف له أنه سمعه من رسول الله ﷺ، هذا لفظ مسلم. وقد رواه أبو داود (٥) عن الحسن بن علي الخلال، عن عبد الرزاق (٦) بنحوه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3636
> *English:* "He made him swear three times, and each time he swore to him that he had heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

**عبرت:** The caliph of the day was asked for his source, in public, by a man who had just fought beside
him — and answered.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR10 · «For me to fall from the sky»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** علي ؓ's caliphate, 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Before narrating this hadith on another occasion, علي ؓ laid down a rule about his own
speech that men remembered afterwards. What he reports from the Prophet ﷺ is one thing, and he would
rather fall out of the sky than tamper with it. What he says on his own account, in war, is another
thing, and there he said plainly that war is deception.

**The statement:**
> إذا حدَّثتكم عن رسول الله ﷺ فلأن أخرَّ من السماء أحبُّ إليَّ من أن أكذب عليه، وإذا حدثتكم فيما بيني وبينكم فإنّ الحربَ خدعةٌ،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3636
> *English:* "When I narrate to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then for me to fall from the sky is dearer to me than that I should lie about him; and when I speak to you of what is between me and you — then war is deception."

**عبرت:** He drew the line himself, between the two kinds of thing a leader says.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR11 · «Young in years, foolish in mind»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** This is the wording the room is most likely to have heard before, and البدایہ says both
البخاري and مسلم carry it. The men described are young, they say the best things that people say, they
recite — and the recitation goes no further than their throats. The image that follows is of an arrow
that goes straight through the animal and out the other side, carrying nothing of it away.

**The statement:**
> "يخرجُ قومٌ في آخر الزمان أحداث الأسنان، سفهاء الأحلام، يقولون من قول خير البريَّة (يقرؤون القرآنَ لا يجاوز حناجرهم - قال عبد الرحمن لا يجاوز إيمانهم حناجرهم -) يمرقون من الدين كما يمرق السهم من الرَّميَّة (٩)،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3636
> *English:* "There will come out a people at the end of time, young in years, foolish in mind. They speak with the speech of the best of creation — they recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass beyond their throats (عبد الرحمن said: their faith does not pass beyond their throats). They pass clean out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game,"

**عبرت:** Saying the best things that people say is named in the report as one of their marks, not as
their defence.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKI/E-KR12 · The arrow that comes out clean
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو سعيد الخدري ؓ preserved the image worked out in full. A hunter shoots, the arrow
passes clean through the animal, and he picks it up and looks at it part by part — the feathers, the
shaft, the binding, the iron head — looking for one trace of what it went through. There is nothing on
any of them. It went through so fast it outran the blood.

**The statement:**
> يمرقون من الدين كما يمرق السهم من الرَّمِيَّة فينظر في قُذَذِهِ (٥) فلا يوجد فيه شيء، ثم ينظر في نضيَّتِهِ (٦) فلا يوجد فيه شيء"، ثم ينظر في رضافه (٧) فلا يوجد فيه شيء، ثم ينظر في نصله فلا يوجد فيه شيء، قد سبق الفرث والدم،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3651
> *English:* "They pass clean out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game: one looks at its flight-feathers and finds nothing on them, then looks at its shaft and finds nothing on it, then looks at its binding and finds nothing on it, then looks at its head and finds nothing on it — it has outstripped the dung and the blood."

**عبرت:** Passing through a thing at speed and passing through it are not the same as taking anything
from it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR13 · «If he is among them… and if he is not»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** In طارق بن زياد's account the sign was put to the army as a wager that cut both ways.
If the described man was among the dead, they had killed the worst of people. If he was not, they had
killed the best of people. Men who had just spent a day killing other Muslims heard that and wept. Then
the man was found, and they went down in prostration, and علي ؓ went down with them.

**The statement:**
> إن كان فيهم [فقد] قتلتم شر الناس، وإن لم يكن فيهم فقد قتلتم خير الناس"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3637
> *English:* "If he is among them, you have killed the worst of people; and if he is not among them, you have killed the best of people."

**عبرت:** The same act was to be either the best thing they had done or the worst, and nothing they felt
about it decided which.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR14 · «A word of truth by which falsehood is intended»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after the تحكیم, 37–38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the slogan «لا حكم إلا لله» was raised against him, علي ؓ did not dispute the
words. He agreed with them and refused what was being built on them, in five words that the tradition has
kept ever since. مسلم records it through عبيد الله بن أبي رافع, who says he was present.

**The statement:**
> قالوا: لا حكمَ إِلَّا للّه، قال علي: كلمةُ حقّ أريدَ بها باطل، إن رسول الله ﷺ وصف ناسًا إني لأعرف صفتهم في هؤلاء "يقولون الحقَّ بألسنتهم لا يجاوز هذا منهم - وأشار إلى حلقه - من أبغض خلق اللّه، منهم أسود. إحدى يديه طُبْيُ (٦) شاة أو حلمة ثدي" فلما قتلهم علي بن أبي طالب قال: انظروا فنظروا فلم يجدوا شيئًا فقال: ارجعوا فانظروا فواللّه ما كذَبْتُ ولا كُذبْتُ - مرتين أو ثلاثًا - فوجدو (٧) في خَرِبَة، فأتوا به عليًّا حتى وضعوه بين يديه، قال عبيد اللّه: وأنا حاضر ذلك من أمرهم، وقول علي فيهم. زاد يونس في روايته: قال بُكير: وحدَّثني رجل عن ابن حنين أنه قال: رأيت ذلك الأسود. تفرد به مسلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3637
> *English:* "They said: judgement belongs to none but Allah. علي said: a word of truth by which falsehood is intended."

**عبرت:** A slogan can be true in every word and still be doing work that is not true.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: can a sentence be completely true and still be being used for something
false?

### TKI/E-KR15 · The description in مسلم: the throat, and the hand
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** In the same report علي ؓ said he recognised in the men in front of him a description
the Prophet ﷺ had given: people who speak the truth with their tongues and it goes no further than the
throat, and among them a black man with one hand like the teat of a ewe. He was not reasoning from
resemblance. He was matching a list he had been given.

**The statement:**
> "يقولون الحقَّ بألسنتهم لا يجاوز هذا منهم - وأشار إلى حلقه - من أبغض خلق اللّه، منهم أسود. إحدى يديه طُبْيُ (٦) شاة أو حلمة ثدي"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3637
> *English:* "They speak the truth with their tongues, and it does not pass beyond this of them — and he pointed to his throat — of the most hateful of Allah’s creation to Him; among them is a black man, one of his two hands is like the teat of a ewe, or the nipple of a breast."

**عبرت:** Truth on the tongue was never counted, by itself, as truth in the man.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR16 · «I have not lied, and I have not been lied to»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The search did not go smoothly. In several of the routes the body cannot be found at
first, and the army comes back empty-handed once, twice, three times. Each time علي ؓ sends them out
again with the same oath, and the routes differ on what he was doing while he said it — one has him
sweating, one weeping, one in the worst distress the narrator ever saw in him.

**The statement:**
> فواللّه ما كذَبْتُ ولا كُذبْتُ - مرتين أو ثلاثًا - فوجدو (٧) في خَرِبَة، فأتوا به عليًّا حتى وضعوه بين يديه، قال عبيد اللّه: وأنا حاضر ذلك من أمرهم، وقول علي فيهم. زاد يونس في روايته: قال بُكير: وحدَّثني رجل عن ابن حنين أنه قال: رأيت ذلك الأسود. تفرد به مسلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3637

### TKI/E-KR22 · The maimed man had a name, and they knew him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map — the page does not name the city

**What happened:** The most concrete thing in the whole chapter comes from أبو مريم, through أبو داود. The
man they went looking for among the dead was not a stranger. He had sat with them in the mosque by night
and by day. He was poor, and أبو مريم used to see him among the destitute at علي ؓ's own table. أبو مريم
had given him a hooded cloak of his own. His name was نافع, and they called him ذو الثدية.

**The statement:**
> إن كان ذاك المُخْدج لمعنا يومئذ في المسجد نجالسه بالليل (٥) والنهار، وكان فقيرًا، ورأيته مع المساكين يشهد طعامَ عليٍّ مع الناس، وقد كسوتُه برنسًا لي. قال أبو مريم: وكان المُخْدج يسمى نافعًا ذا الثُّدية، وكان في يده مثل ثدي المرأة، على رأسه حَلَمةُ مثل حَلَمة الثَّدي عليه شعرات مثل سبالة السِّنَّور.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۹۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3641
> *English:* "That maimed man was with us that day in the mosque; we used to sit with him by night and by day, and he was poor. I saw him among the destitute, present at علي’s food along with the people, and I had clothed him in a hooded cloak of mine. أبو مريم said: the maimed man was called نافع ذو الثدية; in his hand was the like of a woman’s breast, on its end a nipple like the nipple of a breast, with hairs on it like a cat’s whiskers."

**عبرت:** The man the warning was about had been sitting in their mosque, eating at their table, wearing
a coat one of them had given him.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: how close do you think this man had been to the people who ended up
looking for his body?

They pass clean out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game — they do not come back until the arrow returns to its notch. They are the worst of creation and of created things; blessed is he who kills them and whom they kill. They call to the Book of Allah and they are nothing of it. Whoever fights them is nearer to Allah than they are. They said: Messenger of Allah, what is their mark? He said: the shaven head."

### TKI/E-KR33 · «Be just, O Messenger of Allah»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** at الجعرانة, dividing the هوازن spoils `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الجعرانة

**What happened:** جابر ؓ says he saw it with his own eyes and heard it with his own ears. The Prophet ﷺ
was at الجعرانة, distributing silver out of a cloth held by بلال ؓ, handing it out to the people. A man
stood up in front of everyone and told him to be just. The answer is one sentence, and the room will
never forget it.

**The statement:**
> فقال رجل: يا رسول الله، اعْدِلْ، فقال: "وَيْلَكَ ومَنْ يَعْدِلُ إذا لم أَعْدل؟ لقد خِبت إن لم أكن أعدل"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3646
> *English:* "A man said: Messenger of Allah, be just. He said: "Woe to you — and who is just if I am not just? I have failed if I am not just."

**عبرت:** The first man to make this accusation made it to the one person in history it could not be
true of.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: what would you say to a man who told the Prophet ﷺ to his face to be
fair?

### TKI/E-KR34 · «Allah forbid that people should say I kill my own companions»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** at الجعرانة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عمر ؓ asked for permission to deal with the man on the spot, and was refused — not
because the man was harmless, but for a reason about what the thing would look like afterwards. And then
the Prophet ﷺ said where this man's kind were going, in the words the chapter keeps returning to.

**The statement:**
> فقال عمر: يا رسول اللّه دعني أقتل هذا المنافق، فقال: "معاذ اللّه أن يتحدَّثَ الناس أني أقتل أصحابي، إن هذا وأصحابه يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز حناجرهم، أو تراقيهم، يمرقون من الدين مروق (٢) السهم من الرمية".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3646
> *English:* "عمر said: Messenger of Allah, let me kill this hypocrite. He said: "Allah forbid that people should talk of it, that I kill my own companions. This man and his companions recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass their throats — or: their collarbones; they pass clean out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game."

**عبرت:** He would not buy a small silence at the price of what men would say about him afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR35 · «علي killed the devil of the rock-pool»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after النهروان, 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** سعد بن أبي وقاص ؓ, who took no part in any of the fighting of these years, heard that
علي ؓ had killed the خوارج and said one strange sentence about it. البدایہ gives it in three forms, and
records البيهقي's gloss that سعد ؓ meant علي ؓ's men killed the man by his order. The book also records
البخاري's remark that one of the narrators is unknown outside this report.

**The statement:**
> سمعت سعد بن أبي وقاص يقول: "قتل عليٌّ شيطان الرَّدهة" قال (الحافظ أبو بكر) البيهقي (١٠): يريد واللّه أعلم قتله أصحاب علي بأمره.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3647
> *English:* "I heard سعد بن أبي وقاص say: "علي killed the devil of the rock-pool." البيهقي said: he means — and Allah knows best — that علي’s companions killed him by his order."

**عبرت:** A man who had refused to take part in any of it still said out loud what he thought had been
done.

### TKI/E-KR36 · «Twenty of the Companions told me»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو سعيد الخدري ؓ was asked about these people and answered with the hadith, and then
with something else: twenty or so of the Prophet's ﷺ own Companions had told him that علي ؓ was the one
who fought them. The narrator adds a detail that dates the telling — he saw أبو سعيد ؓ in old age, his
hands trembling, still saying it.

**The statement:**
> قال أبو سعيد: فحدَّثني عشرون أو بضع (٥) وعشرون من أصحاب النَّبِيّ ﷺ أن عليًا ولي قتلهم. قال: فرأيت أبا سعيد بعدما كبر ويديه ترتعش ويقول: قتالهم عندي أحل من قتال عدتهم من الترك.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3649
> *English:* "أبو سعيد said: twenty, or some twenty-odd, of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ narrated to me that علي was the one who undertook the killing of them. He said: and I saw أبو سعيد after he had grown old, his hands trembling, saying: fighting them is more lawful in my eyes than fighting the like number of Turks."

**عبرت:** Twenty men who had been with the Prophet ﷺ were still alive to say which side this was.

### TKI/E-KR37 · The gold from اليمن, and four men of نجد
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ's lifetime `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** اليمن → the Prophet ﷺ; the chiefs of نجد

**What happened:** علي ؓ sent a piece of gold up from اليمن, still in the earth it came out of. The Prophet
ﷺ divided it between four chiefs of نجد, and قريش and the أنصار were angry: he gives it to those men and
leaves us. He answered in three words — I am reconciling their hearts. Then a man came forward out of the
crowd, and أبو سعيد ؓ, who was watching, describes his face.

**The statement:**
> فغضبت قريش والأنصار. قالوا: يعطي صناديد أهل نجد ويدعنا؟ قال: "إنما أتألفهم".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3649
> *English:* "He said: قريش and the أنصار were angry. They said: he gives it to the chiefs of نجد and leaves us? He said: "I am only reconciling their hearts."

**عبرت:** The complaint about an unfair division came first from men who accepted the answer, and then
from one who did not.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR38 · «Fear Allah, O محمد»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ's lifetime `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو سعيد ؓ kept the man's face: sunken eyes, a bulging forehead, a thick beard, high
cheekbones, his head shaved. He came up to the Prophet ﷺ in front of everyone and told him to fear Allah.
The answer was a question, and it is the sharpest sentence in the chapter. البدایہ names him ذو الخويصرة
التميمي and says some called him حرقوص.

**The statement:**
> فقال: يا محمد اتق الله فقال: "من يطع اللّه إذا عصيته؟ يأمنني على أهل الأرض ولا تأمنوني"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3649
> *English:* "He said: O محمد, fear Allah. He said: "Who obeys Allah if I disobey Him? He entrusts me over the people of the earth and you do not trust me?"

**عبرت:** The man who came to teach him piety had been sent by no one, and had studied nothing but his
own certainty.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR39 · «Out of the stock of this man» — and what it does not mean
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking; ابن كثير's gloss `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** As the man walked away the Prophet ﷺ said that out of his stock would come a people
who recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass their throats, who kill the people of Islam and leave the
idolaters alone. البدایہ says البخاري narrated it — and then ابن كثير writes a gloss that stops the
sentence being read as a slur on a family line. It does not mean the man's descendants. It means men of
his shape and his description, in any time and any place.

**The statement:**
> "إن من ضئضئ (١) هذا قومًا يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز حناجرهم، يمرقون من الإسلام مروق السَّهم من الرميَّة يقتلون أهل الإسلام ويدعون أهل الأوثان، لئن أنا أدركتهم لأقتلنهم قتل عاد".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3650
> *English:* "Out of the stock of this man there will be a people who recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass their throats; they pass clean out of Islam as the arrow passes out of the game; they kill the people of Islam and leave the worshippers of idols. If I live to see them I will kill them as عاد were killed."

**عبرت:** ابن كثير says plainly that no one knows a single one of them to be of that man's line — the
likeness was never a lineage.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR40 · «Their mark is the shaven head»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the direction of المشرق

**What happened:** Asked twice in this chapter for a mark by which they could be known, the answer both
times is about the head, not the heart: they shave it. البدایہ gives one of these routes as البخاري's. In
the same wording the direction is given too — they come out from the direction of the east.

**The statement:**
> "يخرجُ أناسٌ من قِبَلِ المشرقِ يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز تَرَاقيهم يمرقون من الدين كما يمرقُ السهم من الرَّميَّة، ثم لا يعودون فيه حتى يعود السَّهم على فُوقه" قيل: ما سيماهم؟ قال: "سيماهم التحليق أو التسبيد" (٩)
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3650
> *English:* "People will come out from the direction of the east; they recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass their collarbones; they pass clean out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game, and then they do not return to it until the arrow returns upon its notch. It was said: what is their mark? He said: their mark is the shaven head, or the close-cropped head."

**عبرت:** The only outward mark given is a thing anyone can copy, which is why the reports spend their
length on conduct instead.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR41 · «Our best reciters have come out against us with their swords»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A man called يزيد الفقير came to أبو سعيد الخدري ؓ with the question the whole evening
is really about. Among us, he said, are men who recite the Qurʾān better than any of us, pray more than
any of us, keep family ties better than any of us, and fast more than any of us — and they have come out
against us with their swords. أبو سعيد ؓ did not argue with him. He gave him the hadith and stopped.

**The statement:**
> قلت لأبي سعيد: إنَّ منَّا رجالًا هم أقرؤنا للقرآن، وأكثرنا صلاة، وأوصلنا للرَّحم، وأكثرنا صومًا، خرجوا علينا بأسيافهم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3651
> *English:* "I said to أبو سعيد: among us are men who are the best of us at reciting the Qurʾān, and the most of us in prayer, and the best of us at keeping kinship, and the most of us in fasting — and they have come out against us with their swords."

**عبرت:** The question was asked in the first century in exactly the words a man would use today, and it
was answered with a report rather than an argument.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: does a man's worship tell you whether he is right?

### TKI/E-KR43 · One man who heard it and then saw it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ's lifetime, then النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو سعيد الخدري ؓ is the one man in the chapter who gives both halves in a single

**عبرت:** One witness heard the prediction and saw the thing predicted, and lived long enough to be asked
about both.

### TKI/E-KR44 · A report about أبو بكر ؓ and عمر ؓ that the edition rejects
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ's lifetime `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** البدایہ prints a report in which أبو بكر ؓ and then عمر ؓ are each sent to kill a man
found praying in a valley, and each comes back unwilling because of how the man looked at his prayer. The
edition's editor rejects it in the footnote: the isnad is weak and the wording itself carries plain
نكارة — how could either of them be unwilling to carry out an order to kill? **Recorded so that it is
never re-researched; not for delivery.**

**The statement:**
> وفي ألفاظ الحديث نكارة ظاهرة إذ كيف يكره أبو بكر وعمر قتل من أمر النَّبِيّ ﷺ في قتله.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3648
> *English:* "…and in the wordings of the hadith there is plain objectionableness — for how could أبو بكر and عمر be unwilling to kill one whom the Prophet ﷺ had ordered to be killed?"

**عبرت:** The apparatus of the printed book is doing the same work the chapter itself does: telling you
which report will not carry weight.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR45 · سلمان ؓ warns a man who is later found among the dead
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** before النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A man asked سلمان الفارسي ؓ to move his tent nearer so that they could hear hadith from
him. سلمان ؓ answered that he had heard good of him — that he went light in the way of Allah, fought the
enemy and served the Companions — and then added one condition: if only he does not turn out to be one of
those people the Messenger of Allah ﷺ described. The narrators say that man was later found among the
dead at النهروان. **The isnad runs through الهيثم بن عدي, whom the edition calls a liar and abandoned.
Recorded, not delivered.**

**The statement:**
> فإن أخطأتك واحدة أن تكون من هؤلاء القوم الذين ذكرهم لنا رسول اللّه ﷺ قالوا: فوجد ذلك الرجل قتيلًا في أصحاب النهروان (٢).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3654
> *English:* "…if only one thing does not overtake you: that you be one of those people the Messenger of Allah ﷺ described to us. They said: and that man was found slain among the men of النهروان."

**عبرت:** A good story with a broken chain is still a broken chain — which is the lesson, and the reason
the card exists.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR46 · «I will not add a thing to it for you»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the hand points east

**What happened:** يسير بن عمرو went in to سهل بن حنيف ؓ and asked him for what he had heard from the
Prophet ﷺ about the حرورية. سهل ؓ set his terms first: I will narrate what I heard, and I will not add a
thing to it for you. Then he gave it, pointing with his hand. Asked whether a mark had been mentioned, he

**The statement:**
> قال: أحدثك ما سمعت من النَّبِيِّ ﷺ لا أزيدك عليه شيئًا، سمعت رسول الله ﷺ "يذكر قومًا يخرجون من هاهنا - وأشار بيده نحو العراق - يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز حناجرهم، يمرقون من الدين كما يمرق السهم من الرَّميَّة" قال: قلت هل ذكر لهم علامة؟ قال: هذا ما سمعت لا أزيد عليه [شيئًا].
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۰۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3654
> *English:* "He said: I will narrate to you what I heard from the Prophet ﷺ; I will not add to it a thing for you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention a people who come out from over there — and he pointed with his hand towards العراق — "they recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass their throats; they pass clean out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game." I said: did he mention a mark for them? He said: this is what I heard; I add nothing to it."

**عبرت:** He was asked for more and had no more, and said so — which is why what he did have is still
worth something.

**Hands-up?** no

> "سيخرج ناس من أمتي [من] قبل المشرق يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز تراقيهم، كلَّما خرج منهم قرن قُطِع حتى عدها زيادة على عَشر مرَّات، كُلَّما خرج منهم قرن قُطع حتى يخرج الدجال في بقيَّتهم]
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3656
> *English:* "People of my ummah will come out from the direction of the east; they recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass their collarbones; every time a horn of them comes out it is cut off — until he counted it more than ten times — every time a horn of them comes out it is cut off, until the دجال comes out among the remnant of them."

**عبرت:** The edition's footnote calls this isnad weak, and البدایہ prints the report anyway with that
mark on it — which is how the material should be handled from a platform too.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR52 · أبو ذر ؓ, and a second Companion who volunteers
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** مسلم carries this from أبو ذر ؓ. What makes it worth a card is what the narrator does
next: he went and found رافع بن عمرو الغفاري ؓ and asked him about the strange thing he had heard from أبو
ذر ؓ — and رافع ؓ said he had heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself. البدایہ adds that البخاري
did not narrate this one.

**The statement:**
> "إن بعدي من أمتي - أو سيكون بعدي من أمتي - قوم يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز حلاقيمهم يخرجون من الدين كما يخرج السهم من الرَّميَّة لا يعودون فيه [هم] شر الخلق والخليقة".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3656
> *English:* "After me there will be of my ummah — or: there will come after me of my ummah — a people who recite the Qurʾān and it does not pass their gullets; they go out of the religion as the arrow goes out of the game and do not return to it. They are the worst of creation and of created things."

**عبرت:** A man who hears something surprising goes and finds a second person who was there — which is
the whole method, in one movement.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR53 · «The worst of my ummah, killed by the best of my ummah»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ speaking `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ's report of it is the shortest and the most weighted sentence in the
chapter. البدایہ takes it from البزار by two routes, notes that one of the narrators was spoken of, and
then says the two isnads support one another — and that it is غريب as a hadith of hers.

**The statement:**
> ذكر رسول الله ﷺ الخوارج فقال: "شِرارُ أمتي يقتلهم خيار أمتي" (٤).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3657
> *English:* "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the خوارج and said: "the worst of my ummah, whom the best of my ummah will kill."

**عبرت:** Both halves of the sentence are inside the ummah, and that is the whole weight of it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR54 · عائشة ؓ will not take it on report — she sends for witnesses
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة, in its seven divisions

**What happened:** عائشة ؓ asked مسروق whether he had any knowledge about ذو الثدية, the man علي ؓ had
struck down among the حرورية. He said no. She told him to go and write down for her the testimony of the
men who had been there. He went back to الكوفة, which in those days was laid out in seven divisions, and
took the testimony of ten men from each division — seventy men. He brought it to her and read it out. Her
first question was whether every one of them had seen the body with his own eyes.

**The statement:**
> قالت: فاكتب لي بشهادة من شهدهم، فرجعت إلى الكوفة وبها يومئذ أسباع فكتبت شهادة عشرة من كل سُبع، ثم أتيتها بشهادتهم فقرأتها عليها، قالت: أكل هؤلاء عاينوه؛ قلت: لقد سألتهم فأخبروني بأن كلهم قد عاينه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3658
> *English:* "She said: then write down for me the testimony of those who witnessed them. So I returned to الكوفة — and in those days it was in seven divisions — and I wrote the testimony of ten men from each division, and then I brought her their testimony and read it to her. She said: did all these see him with their own eyes? I said: I asked them, and they told me that every one of them had seen him."

**عبرت:** She would not accept a thing she wanted to be true until seventy men had been asked whether
they saw it themselves.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: how would you go about checking a report, if you were in المدینہ and it
happened in العراق?

### TKI/E-KR55 · «May Allah have mercy on علي — he was upon the truth»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the testimony had been read to her she wept. When the weeping stopped, she said
two things: one about علي ؓ, and one about what had been between them. البدایہ prints them in that order
and adds nothing to either.

**The statement:**
> قالت: رحم اللّه عليًّا لقد كان على حق، وما كان بيني وبينه إِلَّا كما يكون بين المرأة وأحمائها.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3658
> *English:* "She said: may Allah have mercy on علي — he was upon the truth; and there was nothing between me and him but what is between a woman and her husband’s kin."

**عبرت:** She settled it herself, in her own words, and nobody after her needs to settle it again.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR56 · Why ابن كثير gathered all of it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** البدایہ's own statement `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** At the end of the Companions' reports ابن كثير stops and says what the chapter was for.
He did not collect all these routes to settle a quarrel about who was right in the fighting. He collected
them so that anyone who comes upon them will see that the thing is true, and that it stands among the
greatest proofs of prophethood.

**The statement:**
> أوردنا هذه الطرق كلّها ليعلم الواقف عليها أن ذلك حق وصدق وهو من أكبر دلالات النبوة، كما ذكره غير واحد من الأئمة فيها، واللّه تعالى أعلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3658
> *English:* "…we brought all these routes so that whoever comes upon them may know that this is truth and veracity, and that it is among the greatest of the proofs of prophethood, as more than one of the imams has said about it; and Allah most high knows best."

**عبرت:** The chapter is offered as evidence about the Prophet ﷺ, not as a verdict about the men who
fought.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR57 · «The mender of the sandal»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Prophet ﷺ's lifetime `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو سعيد ؓ says they were sitting waiting for the Prophet ﷺ, and when he came out they
walked with him. His sandal-strap broke; علي ؓ stayed behind to mend it, and the rest walked on. Then the
Prophet ﷺ stopped and waited for him, and said that among them was a man who would fight over the
interpretation of the Qurʾān as he himself had fought over its sending down. The men craned to see who —
أبو بكر ؓ and عمر ؓ were sitting there — and he told them.

**The statement:**
> "إن منكم من يقاتل على تأويل القرآن كما قاتلت على تنزيله" فاستشرفنا لها وفينا (٥) أبو بكر، وعمر فقال: "لا، ولكنه خاصفُ النعل"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3659
> *English:* "Among you is one who will fight over the interpretation of the Qurʾān as I fought over its sending down. So we craned for it — and أبو بكر and عمر were among us — and he said: "No; but it is the mender of the sandal."

**عبرت:** The fight that was coming was named as a fight over how the Book is read, and the man for it
was named too.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR58 · The famous report ابن كثير will not accept
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** البدایہ's own grading `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The report in which علي ؓ says he was ordered to fight three groups — الناكثون,
القاسطون, المارقون — is the most quoted sentence of this whole period. البدایہ prints it, prints five or
six chains for it, and then states its own verdict in one clause: strange and objectionable, and not one
of the routes is free of weakness. **The gloss the book gives of the three words names Companions on two
sides, and belongs to §Not for the hall, not to a slide.**

**The statement:**
> فإنه حديث غريبٌ ومنكرٌ، على أنه قد روي من طرقٍ عن علي وعن غيره، ولا تخلو واحدة منها عن ضعف.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3659
> *English:* "…for it is a hadith غريب and منكر — although it has been narrated by several routes from علي and from others, not one of them is free of weakness."

**عبرت:** The most quoted line is not always the best attested one, and the book says which is which.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR59 · «To all appearance, fabricated»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** البدایہ's own grading `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Three pages later a much longer version of the same report appears, with a great deal
more in it. ابن كثير disposes of it in a single sentence and names the man he holds responsible for it.
That sentence is the speaker's entire answer if this passage is ever quoted at him: the book we are
reading says it is fabricated.

**The statement:**
> هذا السياق الظاهر أنه موضوع وآفته من جهة المعلى بن عبد الرحمن فإنه متروك الحديث، والله أعلم (٧).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3662
> *English:* "This account is, to all appearance, fabricated, and its affliction comes from المعلى بن عبد الرحمن — for he is متروك الحديث; and Allah knows best."

**عبرت:** Four different gradings in eleven pages — متواترة, غرابة شديدة, غريب ومنكر, موضوع — from one
author, on one subject.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR60 · «Every innovated thing is an innovation»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after النهروان, at النُّخَيلة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** النخيلة, outside الكوفة

**What happened:** Coming back from النهروان علي ؓ told the army to turn straight round and march on الشام.
They asked for time: the arrows were spent, the swords blunt, the spearheads worn. He camped them at
النخيلة and told them to stay in camp — and they slipped away a few at a time until almost nobody was
left. He stood up and delivered a khutba that البدایہ prints over three full pages. **البدایہ's own
attribution for it is الهيثم بن عدي from عيسى بن داب, and that must travel with any use of it.**

**The statement:**
> وكل مُحْدثةٍ بدعةٌ وكل مُحْدثٍ مُبْتدعٌ، ومن ابتدع فقد ضيَّع، وما أحدث محدثٌ بدعةً إِلَّا ترك بها سنةً،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3664
> *English:* "…and every innovated thing is an innovation, and every innovator is one who innovates; and whoever innovates has ruined; and no innovator innovated an innovation but that he abandoned a sunnah by it,"

**عبرت:** He had just fought men who were certain they were restoring the religion, and this is what he
said to the army that was left.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR61 · The two things he said he feared most
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Near the end of the same khutba علي ؓ names the two things he fears most for the people
in front of him, and they are not enemies. ابن كثير's verdict on the whole address is printed
immediately after it: great, eloquent, beneficial, gathering good and forbidding evil.

**The statement:**
> ألا وإن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم اثنان طول الأمل واتباع الهوى، فأما طول الأمل فيُنْسِي الآخرة، وأما اتباع الهوى فيبعد عن الحق
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3665
> *English:* "Know that the two things I fear most for you are long hope and the following of desire: as for long hope, it makes one forget the hereafter; and as for following desire, it takes one far from the truth."

**عبرت:** After a year of fighting, the two dangers he named were both inside the men listening.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR62 · A second rising, over the same complaint reversed
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** after النهروان `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بنو ناجية, southern العراق

**What happened:** البدایہ reports from الهيثم بن عدي that after النهروان a man called الخِرِّيت بن راشد
الناجي came to علي ؓ and made the opposite argument: you fought the men of النهروان for rejecting the
arbitration, and you say you hold to your own undertakings — but the two arbitrators agreed on removing
you, so you are removed, and I have removed you and معاوية both. He went off with a following, معقل بن
قيس was sent after him, and the affair ended in a mass of killing, five hundred households taken, a
governor who bought them and freed them and then absconded to الشام over the price, and علي ؓ confirming
the freeing and pulling the man's house down. **CUT: it belongs to the النهروان aftermath strand, and its
isnad is الهيثم's.**

**The statement:** none in the sources we use

**عبرت:** The argument that had just been fought over came back the next season with the terms reversed.

### TKI/E-KR63 · The year of النهروان is disputed inside the book
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37 or 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** البدایہ narrates the battle under the year 37, and then says on the last page of that
year that ابن جرير reports most of the historians putting it in 38, and declared 38 correct. ابن كثير adds
his own three words. **Any slide must show 38 and mark the disagreement.**

**The statement:**
> كان في سنة ثمان وثلاثين وصححه ابن جرير، قلت: وهو الأشبه كما سننبه عليه في السنة الآتية إن شاء اللّه تعالى.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3667
> *English:* "…it was in the year thirty-eight, and ابن جرير declared that correct. I say: and that is the more likely, as we shall point out under the coming year, if Allah most high wills."

**عبرت:** Two years for one battle, on one page, and the author tells you which he prefers and why.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKI/E-KR64 · خباب بن الأرت ؓ, and the seat عمر ؓ gave him
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** died 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة

**What happened:** The obituaries for that year open with خباب بن الأرت ؓ, who had accepted Islam before
the house of الأرقم and was one of those tortured for it. البدایہ records that he came in one day upon
عمر ؓ, who honoured his seat and said no man had a better right to it except بلال ؓ. خباب ؓ answered that
بلال ؓ had someone to protect him and he himself had nobody — and then he told him what they had done to
him, and uncovered his back to show it.

**The statement:**
> قال الشعبي: دخل [خباب] يومًا على عمر فأكرم مجلسه وقال: ما أحد أحق بهذا المجلس منك إِلَّا بلال، فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين إن بلالًا كان يؤذى وكان له من يمنعه، وإني كنت لا ناصر لي، واللّه لقد سلقوني يومًا في نار أججوها ووضع رجل رجله على صدري فما اتقيت الأرض إِلَّا بظهري،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3667
> *English:* "الشعبي said: خباب came in one day upon عمر, and he honoured his seat and said: no one has a better right to this seat than you, except بلال. He said: commander of the believers, بلال was tormented, but he had someone to protect him; and I had no helper. By Allah, one day they scorched me in a fire they had kindled, and a man set his foot on my chest, and I met the ground with nothing but my back —"

**عبرت:** The men who had carried Islam through its first years were still alive to see this one, and
this is what their bodies looked like.

**Hands-up?** no
