## مصر, the raids, and the fraying of the command

*Source note: [`egypt-and-the-fraying-of-the-command.md`](../docs/research/egypt-and-the-fraying-of-the-command.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### EAT/E-EG1 · The frontiers come apart after the arbitration
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The whole map dims at its edges; الكوفة stays lit.

**What happened:** After the fighting at النهروان, the trouble did not end. It spread. A great many men who had been with علي ؓ now stood against him, and the outlying provinces stopped answering. One tribe broke away in the south. A messenger from الشام walked into البصرة and started taking pledges. The highland districts went their own way, and the men who collected the land-tax began to think they need not pay it at all. ابن كثير sets all of it down in a single sentence he takes from الشعبي, and that sentence is the shape of the next two years.

**The statement:**
> لما قتل علي أهل النهروان خالفه قوم كثير، وانتقضت أطرافه، وخالفه بنو ناجية، وقدم ابن الحضرمي إلى البصرة، وانتقض أهل الجبال (٢)، وطمع أهل الخراج في كسره
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٣٢ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3678
> *English:* "When ʿAlī killed the people of al-Nahrawān, a great many opposed him, his outlying territories came apart, Banū Nājiya opposed him, Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī came to al-Baṣra, the people of the highlands broke away, and the people of the land-tax set their hopes on breaking it."

**عبرت:** A victory inside the house does not restore the house.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### EAT/E-EG2 · Who held what before the blow fell
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Light مكة, المدينة, اليمن, البصرة, الكوفة and مصر in one colour and الشام in another.

**What happened:** Before anything else is told, the room needs the board. علي ؓ held مكة, المدينة, اليمن, البصرة, مصر and الكوفة, and he was living in الكوفة himself. Four of those provinces were in the hands of four brothers, the sons of العباس. معاوية ؓ held الشام. That is the whole picture, and ابن كثير sets it out as a list before he narrates a single event of the year.

**The statement:**
> وكان نائب مكة قثم بن العباس، وعلى المدينة تمام بن عباس، وقيل سهل بن حنيف، وعلى البصرة عبد الله بن عباس، وعلى قضائها أبو الأسود الدؤلي، وعلى مصر محمد بن أبي بكر، و (علي بن أبي طالب) أمير المؤمنين (مقيم) بالكوفة، ومعاوية بن أبي سفيان مستحوذ على الشام.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢١ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3667
> *English:* "His deputy over Mecca was Qutham b. al-ʿAbbās, over Medina Tammām b. ʿAbbās — and it is said Sahl b. Ḥunayf — over al-Baṣra ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAbbās, over its judgeship Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī, and over Egypt Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr; and ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, Commander of the Faithful, was resident at Kūfa, while Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān held the upper hand in Syria."

**عبرت:** A map is a claim about obedience, and obedience is what was being lost.

**Hands-up?** Which of these provinces do you think was the richest?

---

### EAT/E-EG3 · The governor he wished he had kept
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مصر flashes, then الكوفة.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had put قيس بن سعد بن عبادة ؓ over مصر and then taken him off it and given it to محمد بن أبي بكر ؓ. ابن كثير says plainly that he regretted the change, because قيس ؓ was a match for the men on the other side and the young governor was not. Then he records what the other side thought of the same man, and it is the sharpest compliment in the whole window.

**The statement:**
> وكان معاوية يقول: (واللّه) لقيس بن سعد عند علي أبغض إلي من مئة ألف مقاتل بدله عنده
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3671
> *English:* "Muʿāwiya used to say: by God, Qays b. Saʿd at ʿAlīʼs side is more hateful to me than a hundred thousand fighting men in his place at his side."

**عبرت:** One right man in the right post is worth more than an army, and the cost of moving him is only seen afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### EAT/E-EG4 · Why مصر was worth a war
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مصر fills with colour; an arrow of revenue runs from it.

**What happened:** مصر was not a symbol. It was money. الکامل states the calculation without any decoration: whoever held مصر could pay for the war, because of the size of what مصر yielded in land-tax. That is why a province a thousand miles from الكوفة decided the next two years, and why both sides thought about it before they thought about anything else.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ يَرْجُو أَنَّهُ إِذَا ظَهَرَ عَلَيْهَا ظَهَرَ عَلَى حَرْبِ عَلِيٍّ لِعِظَمِ خَرَاجِهَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٦ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1395
> *English:* "And he hoped that if he prevailed over it he would prevail in the war with ʿAlī, because of the greatness of its land-tax."

**عبرت:** Wars are decided where the revenue is, not where the argument is.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### EAT/E-EG5 · Mix firmness with gentleness
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A line from نصيبين to الكوفة, then south towards مصر.

**What happened:** علي ؓ called الأشتر down from نصيبين, told him what was happening in مصر, and said there was no one else for it. Then he gave him an instruction that is worth more than the appointment. He said he would have been content to send him with no instruction at all; and then he gave one anyway, in four clauses, about when to be gentle and when not to be.

**The statement:**
> لَيْسَ لَهَا غَيْرُكَ فَاخْرُجْ إِلَيْهَا، فَإِنِّي لَوْ لَمْ أُوصِكَ اكْتَفَيْتُ بِرَأْيِكَ، وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ، وَاخْلِطِ الشِّدَّةَ بِاللِّينِ، وَارْفُقْ مَا كَانَ الرِّفْقُ أَبْلَغَ، وَتَشَدَّدْ حِينَ لَا يُغْنِي إِلَّا الشِّدَّةُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٤ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1393
> *English:* "There is none for it but you, so go out to it; for had I given you no instruction at all I would have been content with your own judgement. Seek help from God. Mix firmness with gentleness; be gentle for as long as gentleness goes further; and be firm at the point where nothing but firmness will serve."

**عبرت:** Authority is knowing which of the two the hour requires.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG6 · A drink of honey at القلزم
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The line towards مصر stops dead at القلزم on the Red Sea.

**What happened:** الأشتر never reached مصر. On the road he came to القلزم, where the man in charge of the land-tax met him, offered him hospitality, gave him food, and then gave him a drink of honey. He died of it. When the news reached الشام a remark went round that the books have kept, and it is the kind of thing soldiers say.

**The statement:**
> الخراج فقدم إليه طعامًا وسقاه شرابًا من عسل فمات منه، فلما بلغ ذلك معاوية وعمرًا وأهل الشام قالوا: إن لله جنودًا من عسل.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٦ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3672
> *English:* "…the land-tax; and he brought him food and gave him a drink of honey to drink, and he died of it. When that reached Muʿāwiya and ʿAmr and the people of Syria they said: God has armies made of honey."

**عبرت:** The best-chosen man can be taken off the board before he arrives, and a plan that rests on one man rests on nothing.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG7 · The historian who would not say more
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** There was a report that the death at القلزم had been arranged in advance. ابن كثير does not hide the report. He names the historian he takes it from, sets it down in full, and then, in his own voice, refuses to certify it in four words. Only after that does he add what the position would have to be if the report were sound. He never says that it is. This is how a careful book handles a charge against a great man, and it is how we will handle every charge in this session.

**The statement:**
> وقد ذكر ابن جرير في "تاريخه" (١) أن معاوية كان قد تقدم إلى هذا الرجل في أن يحتال على الأشتر ليقتله (٢) ووعده على ذلك بأمور ففعل ذلك، وفي هذا نظر، وبتقدير صحته فمعاوية يستجيز قتل الأشتر لأنه من قتلة عثمان
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٦ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3672
> *English:* "Ibn Jarīr has mentioned in his History that Muʿāwiya had instructed this man to contrive against al-Ashtar so as to kill him, and had promised him things for it, and that he did so. In this there is something to look into; and supposing it sound, then Muʿāwiya held the killing of al-Ashtar permissible because he was one of the killers of ʿUthmān."

**عبرت:** A historian who writes "in this there is something to look into" has taught us more than one who answers every question.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG8 · Two reports, and a book choosing between them
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الکامل has two different reports of what علي ؓ said when the news of الأشتر reached him. In one he says something short and cold; in the other he grieves aloud and calls for the weeping women. ابن الأثير does not print both and walk away. He says which one is sounder, and he gives his reason — a man does not give a province to somebody he dislikes.

**The statement:**
> فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ عَلِيًّا مَوْتُهُ قَالَ: لِلْيَدَيْنِ وَلِلْفَمِ! وَكَانَ قَدْ ثَقُلَ عَلَيْهِ لِأَشْيَاءَ نُقِلَتْ عَنْهُ. وَقِيلَ: إِنَّهُ لَمَّا بَلَغَهُ قَتْلُهُ قَالَ: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ! مَالِكٌ وَمَا مَالِكٌ، وَهَلْ مَوْجُودٌ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ؟ لَوْ كَانَ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ، لَكَانَ قَيْدًا أَوْ مِنْ حَجَرٍ، لَكَانَ صَلْدًا! عَلَى مَثَلِهِ فَلْتَبْكِ الْبَوَاكِي! وَهَذَا أَصَحُّ ; لِأَنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ كَارِهًا لَهُ لَمْ يُولِهِ مِصْرَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1394
> *English:* "When his death reached ʿAlī he said: for the two hands and for the mouth! — for he had grown heavy upon him on account of things reported of him. And it is said that when his killing reached him he said: to God we belong and to Him we return! Mālik, and what a Mālik! Is there found the like of that? Had he been of iron he would have been a fetter, or of stone, a solid rock! For one like him let the weeping women weep. And this is the sounder, because had he disliked him he would not have given him charge of Egypt."

**عبرت:** Weighing two reports with a stated reason is the historianʼs whole craft.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG9 · The letter that consoled a hurt governor
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** محمد بن أبي بكر ؓ had been hurt when another man was sent over his head to مصر. علي ؓ wrote to him about it, and the letter does two things at once. It tells the young man that the change was no judgement on his courage, and it praises the dead man generously in the same breath. Then it tells him to hold on and prepare for war.

**The statement:**
> أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي مَوْجَدَتُكَ مِنْ تَسْرِيحَيِ الْأَشْتَرَ إِلَى عَمَلِكَ، وَإِنِّي لَمْ أَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ اسْتِبْطَاءً لَكَ فِي الْجِهَادِ وَلَا ازْدِيَادًا مِنِّي لَكَ فِي الْجِدِّ، وَلَوْ نَزَعْتُ مَا تَحْتَ يَدِكَ لَوَلَّيْتُكَ مَا هُوَ أَيْسَرُ عَلَيْكَ مَؤُونَةً مِنْهُ وَأَعْجَبُ إِلَيْكَ وِلَايَةً، إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ وَلَّيْتُهُ أَمْرَ مِصْرَ كَانَ لَنَا نَصِيحًا، وَعَلَى عَدُوِّنَا شَدِيدًا، وَقَدِ اسْتَكْمَلَ أَيَّامَهُ وَلَاقَى حِمَامَهُ، وَنَحْنُ عَنْهُ رَاضُونَ، فَرَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، وَضَاعَفَ لَهُ الثَّوَابَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٦ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1395
> *English:* "To proceed: word has reached me of your resentment at my dispatching al-Ashtar to your province. I did not do it out of any thought that you were slow in the struggle, nor to ask more effort of you; and had I taken away what is under your hand I would have given you charge of something lighter in burden and more pleasing to you as a governorship. The man whom I had given charge of the affair of Egypt was a sincere counsellor to us and hard upon our enemy; he has completed his days and met his appointed end, and we are well pleased with him — may God be pleased with him and double his reward."

**عبرت:** A commander who explains himself to a subordinate loses nothing and keeps a man.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG10 · Blessed in haste, blessed in deliberation
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Before the army moved, the two men who would take مصر argued about method, and the argument is preserved. One wanted speed, the other wanted letters first. Neither insulted the other. Each named the gift the other had. And then the one who had wanted speed accepted the slower plan and said plainly that it would end in war anyway — which it did.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّكَ يَا ابْنَ الْعَاصِ بُورِكَ لَكَ فِي الشِّدَّةِ وَالْعَجَلَةِ، وَأَنَا بُورِكَ لِي فِي التُّؤَدَةِ. قَالَ عَمْرٌو: افْعَلْ مَا تَرَى فَمَا أَرَى أَمْرَنَا يَصِيرُ إِلَّا إِلَى الْحَرْبِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1396
> *English:* "You, son of al-ʿĀṣ, have been blessed in firmness and in speed, and I have been blessed in deliberateness. ʿAmr said: do as you see fit — I do not see our affair ending in anything but war."

**عبرت:** Two men who name each otherʼs strengths can disagree without breaking.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG11 · "Not for that did we rise"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مصر — a cluster in the delta lights up.

**What happened:** A letter went ahead of the army into مصر, to the men there who had not given علي ؓ the pledge. It thanked them, urged them on, and promised them a share in the rule that was coming. مسلمة بن مخلد الأنصاري ؓ answered for himself and for his colleague, and he accepted everything in the letter except that one clause, which he threw back.

**The statement:**
> وَأَمَّا مَا ذَكَرْتَ مِنَ الْمُوَاسَاةِ فِي سُلْطَانِكَ، فَتَاللَّهِ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَمْرٌ مَا لَهُ نَهَضْنَا، وَلَا إِيَّاهُ أَرَدْنَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1396
> *English:* "As for the share in your rule which you mentioned — by God, that is a thing for which we did not rise, and it is not what we wanted."

**عبرت:** A man is known by the part of the offer he refuses.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG12 · Kill who fights, pardon who turns away
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** An arrow from فلسطين down into مصر.

**What happened:** Six thousand men went south. The charge given to their commander at the parting is on the page, and it is not what a listener expects of a civil war. Fear God. Be gentle. Do not hurry. Fight the man who fights you and let the man who turns away go. Call the people to peace. And when you have won, favour the ones who stood with you.

**The statement:**
> وأوصاه بتقوى اللّه والرفق والمهل (والتؤدة)، وأن يقتل من قاتل ويعفو عمن أدبر، وأن يدعو الناس إلى الصلح والجماعة، فإذا أنت ظهرت فليكن أنصارك آثر
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3673
> *English:* "And he charged him with the fear of God, with gentleness, with unhurriedness and deliberation; that he should kill whoever fought and pardon whoever turned away; and that he should call the people to peace and to unity; and: when you prevail, let those who helped you be the most favoured of people with you."

**عبرت:** Even inside a civil war the rules of war were still being written down and handed over.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG13 · "Stand aside — I do not want a victory over you"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Before the fighting, عمرو بن العاص ؓ wrote to the governor of مصر and told him to leave. The letter is not a threat so much as an argument: the province has already turned, they will hand you over the moment it becomes hard, and I would rather you were not here. It ends, without irony, by calling itself sincere advice.

**The statement:**
> أما بعد فتنح فإني لا أحب أن يصيبك مني ظفر، فإن الناس قد اجتمعوا بهذه البلاد على خلافك ورفض أمرك، وندموا على اتباعك، فهم مسلموك لو قد التقت حلقتا البطان (٤)، فاخرج منها فإني لك لمن الناصحين والسلام.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3673
> *English:* "To proceed: stand aside, for I do not wish any victory of mine to fall upon you. The people of these lands have agreed upon opposing you and casting off your authority, and they regret having followed you; they will hand you over once the two loops of the girth meet. So go out of it, for I am one who counsels you sincerely. Peace."

**عبرت:** The hardest warning to hear is the one that turns out to be accurate.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG14 · كنانة بن بشر and the squadrons
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مصر: a small force meets a larger one north of الفسطاط.

**What happened:** The governor of مصر sent كنانة بن بشر out in front with two thousand men. The Syrian commander did not send his whole force at once; he sent squadron after squadron, and كنانة charged each one as it came and drove it back on the men behind. So they surrounded him instead. When he saw it he got off his horse, and his men got off with him, and he recited a verse of the Qurʾān about the appointed term, and fought until he was killed.

**The statement:**
> فترجل عند ذلك كنانة وهو يتلو ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ كِتَابًا مُؤَجَّلًا﴾ الآية [آل عمران: ١٤٥]، ثم قاتل حتى قتل.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3674
> *English:* "At that Kīnāna dismounted, reciting: "It is not for any soul to die except by Godʼs leave, at a term appointed" — then he fought until he was killed."

**عبرت:** A man who has settled the question of when he will die fights differently from a man who has not.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG15 · The man in the ruin
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 38 AH, on الواقدي's dating as البدایہ gives it `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مصر changes colour on the map.

**What happened:** When كنانة fell, the rest scattered. محمد بن أبي بكر ؓ was left walking on the road alone. He found a ruin at the side of it and sat down inside. A search party asked some labourers whether anyone had passed; one of them mentioned a man sitting in that ruin. They brought him out nearly dead of thirst. His own brother was in the other army and went to its commander to try to stop what followed. It did not stop. He was killed, and مصر changed hands.

**The statement:**
> وتفرق أصحاب محمد بن أبي بكر عنه ورجع يمشي فرأى خربة فأوى إليها ودخل عمرو بن العاص فسطاط مصر وذهب معاوية بن حُدَيْج في طلب محمد بن أبي بكر فمر بعلوج في الطريق فقال لهم: هل مر بكم أحد تستنكرونه؟ قالوا: لا! فقال رجل منهم: إني رأيت رجلًا جالسًا في هذه الخربة، فقال: (هو) هو ورب الكعبة: فدخلوا عليه فاستخرجوه منها - وقد كاد يموت عطشًا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3674
> *English:* "The companions of Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr scattered from him and he went back on foot; he saw a ruin and took shelter in it. ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ entered the Fusṭāṭ of Egypt, and Muʿāwiya b. Ḥudayj went out in search of Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr. He passed some labourers on the road and said to them: has anyone passed you whom you did not know? They said: no. But one man among them said: I saw a man sitting in that ruin. He said: it is he, by the Lord of the Kaʿba. So they went in upon him and brought him out of it — and he had nearly died of thirst."

**عبرت:** The son of the first خليفة died alone in a ruin, and the books do not soften it.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG16 · عائشة ؓ and the roast meat
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** The dead governor was her brother. When the news reached المدينة, عائشة ؓ grieved severely and took his household into her own house. His small son القاسم grew up among them — the same القاسم who became one of the seven jurists of المدينة. And الکامل adds one domestic detail that carries the whole weight of it: from that day until she died she never ate roast meat.

**The statement:**
> وَأَخَذَتْ عِيَالَ مُحَمَّدٍ إِلَيْهَا، فَكَانَ الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ فِي عِيَالِهِمْ، وَلَمْ تَأْكُلْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ شِوَاءً حَتَّى تُوُفِّيَتْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1398
> *English:* "And she took Muḥammadʼs household to herself — al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr was among their household — and from that time she never ate roast meat until she died."

**عبرت:** Every casualty in this war was somebodyʼs brother, and the house that took in the orphans is where you see it.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG17 · The woman who was married to جعفر ؓ, أبو بكر ؓ and علي ؓ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** — `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أسماء بنت عميس ؓ was the mother of the governor who had just been killed. She had emigrated to الحبشة with جعفر بن أبي طالب ؓ and borne him three sons. After جعفر ؓ was killed at مؤتة she married أبو بكر الصديق ؓ, and محمد was born to them. After أبو بكر ؓ died she married علي ؓ, and محمد grew up in his house. One woman ties the three households together, which is why this death was felt in all three.

**The statement:**
> أسماء بنت عميس، ولما احتضر الصديق أوصى أن تغسله فغسلته، ثم لما انقضت عدتها تزوجها علي فنشأ [محمد] في حجره، فلما صارت إليه الخلافة استنابه على بلاد مصر بعد قيس بن سعد بن عبادة كما قدمنا، فلما كانت هذه السنة بعث معاوية عمرو بن العاص فاستلب منه بلاد مصر وقتل محمد بن أبي بكر كما تقدم، وله من العمر دون الثلاثين [سنة وحزنت عليه عائشة وعلي وغيرهما]، ﵀ ورضي عنه. أسماء بنت عميس (١) بن معبد (٢) بن الحارث الخثعمية [وهي أم محمد المذكور] أسلمت [قديمًا]، بمكة وهاجرت مع زوجها جعفر بن أبي طالب إلى الحبشة وقدمت معه إلى خيبر، ولها منه عبد الله، ومحمد، وعون. ولما قتل جعفر بمؤتة تزوجها بعده أبو بكر الصديق فولدت منه محمد بن أبي بكر أمير مصر (٣)، ثم لما مات الصديق تزوجها بعده علي بن أبي طالب فولدت له يحيى وعونًا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٣٤ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3680
> *English:* "Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays b. Maʿbad b. al-Ḥārith al-Khathʿamiyya — she is the mother of the Muḥammad mentioned. She accepted Islam early, at Mecca, and emigrated with her husband Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib to Abyssinia and came with him to Khaybar; by him she had ʿAbdallāh, Muḥammad and ʿAwn. When Jaʿfar was killed at Muʾta, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq married her after him and she bore him Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr, the commander of Egypt; then when al-Ṣiddīq died, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib married her after him and she bore him Yaḥyā and ʿAwn."

**عبرت:** These households were not parties to each other; they were one family, and that is the fact the quarrels were laid on top of.

**Hands-up?** How many of these three names did you know were one household?

### EAT/E-EG18 · The muster nobody came to
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الجرعة, between الكوفة and الحيرة.

**What happened:** While مصر was still holding, علي ؓ stood up in الكوفة, told the people what was happening, and named a place and a day: come out with us to الجرعة. Next morning he went out and camped there early. He waited until the sun was overhead. Not one man came. He went back into the city, and that evening he sent for the chiefs, and the books say he was grieving.

**The statement:**
> وَقَالَ: اخْرُجُوا بِنَا إِلَى الْجَرَعَةِ، وَهِيَ بَيْنَ الْكُوفَةِ وَالْحِيرَةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْغَدُ خَرَجَ إِلَى الْجَرَعَةِ، فَنَزَلَهَا بُكْرَةً وَأَقَامَ بِهَا حَتَّى انْتَصَفَ النَّهَارُ، فَلَمْ يَأْتِهِ أَحَدٌ، فَرَجَعَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٠٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1398
> *English:* "And he said: come out with us to al-Jarʿa — it is between Kūfa and al-Ḥīra. When the morrow came he went out to al-Jarʿa and camped there early and stayed there until midday, and not one man came to him, so he went back."

**عبرت:** An army is not a number on a register; it is the men who actually walk out of the gate.

**Hands-up?** What would you do if you called and nobody came?

---

### EAT/E-EG19 · The lizard and the hyena
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38–39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** This is the sermon the room will remember, and it is in both of our books in almost the same words, which is itself worth saying aloud. He told الكوفة that every time they heard a column was coming, each man of them went into his house and shut the door behind him the way a lizard goes into its hole and a hyena into her den. Then he said that whoever trusted them had been deceived, and whoever left them had drawn the losing arrow, and he ended with the verse of return.

**The statement:**
> يا أهل الكوفة! كلما سمعتم بمنسر (٢) من مناسر أهل الشام انجحر كل [امرئ] منكم في بيته، وغلق عليه بابه. انجحار الضب في جحره، والضبع في وجاره، المغرور والله من غررتموه، ولَمن فارقكم فاز بالسهم الأخيب (٣)، لا أحرار عند النداء، ولا إخوان ثقة عند النجاة، إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون، ماذا منيت به منكم، عُميٌ لا تبصرون، وبُكْمٌ لا تنطقون، وصم لا تسمعون، إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٣٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3681
> *English:* "People of Kūfa! Every time you hear of a column among the columns of the Syrians, every man of you burrows into his house and shuts his door upon himself, the way a lizard burrows into its hole and a hyena into its den. Deceived, by God, is the man you have deceived; and whoever parts from you has drawn the losing arrow. No free men at the call, and no brothers to be trusted at the moment of rescue. To God we belong and to Him we return. With what have I been afflicted in you — blind who do not see, dumb who do not speak, deaf who do not hear! To God we belong and to Him we return."

**عبرت:** A ruler can hold the treasury, the pulpit and the seal and still not hold the people.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG20 · Fifty nights of asking
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the news of مصر finally came, علي ؓ got up and told the people how long he had been asking them. It was not a figure of speech. He counted the nights — something over fifty — and described exactly how they had answered: grumbling like a tired camel, sinking to the ground, and finally sending out a small party that walked as though it were being driven to its death.

**The statement:**
> دَعَوْتُكُمْ إِلَى غِيَاثِ إِخْوَانِكُمْ مُنْذُ بِضْعٍ وَخَمْسِينَ لَيْلَةً، فَتَجَرْجَرْتُمْ جَرْجَرَةَ الْجَمَلِ الْأَشْدَقِ، وَتَثَاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ تَثَاقُلَ مَنْ لَيْسَتْ لَهُ نِيَّةٌ فِي جِهَادِ الْعَدُوِّ وَلَا اكْتِسَابِ الْأَجْرِ، ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَيَّ مِنْكُمْ جُنَيْدٌ مُتَذَانِبٌ، كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى الْمَوْتِ وَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ، فَأُفٍّ لَكُمْ! ثُمَّ نَزَلَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٠ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1399
> *English:* "I have been calling you to the rescue of your brothers for something over fifty nights, and you have grumbled the grumbling of a slack-jawed camel and sunk heavily to the ground like men who have no intention of struggling against an enemy nor of earning a reward; then there came out to me from among you a little troop, hanging back, as though they were being driven to death with their eyes open. Fie upon you! Then he came down."

**عبرت:** Help that arrives late is not help, and the counting of the nights is how the loss gets measured.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG21 · "Neither my she-camel nor my he-camel"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** A messenger came into البصرة from الشام with a letter, lodged with a tribe, and called the city to change sides. Speeches were made on both sides; the room filled with men taking positions. Then الأحنف بن قيس stood up. He did not argue with anybody. He said one proverb and walked out, and the books preserved it because everybody in the city understood exactly what he meant.

**The statement:**
> قَامَ الْأَحْنَفُ فَقَالَ: لَا نَاقَتِي فِي هَذَا وَلَا جَمَلِي. وَاعْتَزَلَ الْقَوْمَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١١ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1400
> *English:* "al-Aḥnaf rose and said: neither my she-camel nor my he-camel is in this — and he withdrew from the people."

**عبرت:** Not every quarrel between Muslims requires you to pick a side, and some of the wisest men in the أمة did not.

**Hands-up?** Is it always right to take a side?

### EAT/E-EG22 · The treasury carried to a neighbourʼs house
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة — the الحدان quarter.

**What happened:** The acting governor of البصرة could not hold his own city. One tribe was sheltering the man from الشام; another would not commit. So he asked a chief of الأزد to give protection to himself and to the Muslimsʼ treasury, and the answer was: bring it to my house. He moved the money there — and moved the pulpit too, and prayed the Friday prayer in that quarterʼs mosque, and fed the people.

**The statement:**
> فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى صَبْرَةَ بْنَ شَيْمَانَ الْحُدَّانِيِّ الْأَزْدِيِّ يَطْلُبُ أَنْ يُجِيرَهُ وَبَيْتَ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. فَقَالَ: إِنْ حَمَلْتَهُ إِلَى دَارِي أَجَرْتُكُمَا. فَنَقَلَهُ إِلَى دَارِهِ بِالْحُدَّانِ، وَنَقَلَ الْمِنْبَرَ أَيْضًا، فَكَانَ يُصَلِّي الْجُمُعَةَ بِمَسْجِدِ الْحُدَّانِ وَيُطْعِمُ الطَّعَامَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٢ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1401
> *English:* "So he sent to Ṣabra b. Shaymān al-Ḥuddānī al-Azdī asking him to give protection to himself and to the treasury of the Muslims. He said: if you carry it to my house I will protect you both. So he moved it to his house at al-Ḥuddān, and moved the pulpit too, and he used to pray the Friday prayer in the mosque of al-Ḥuddān and feed the people."

**عبرت:** When the state weakens, the tribe is what is left standing, and that is exactly the arrangement Islam had come to replace.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG23 · An Abyssinian mother at the gate
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة — قصر سنبيل.

**What happened:** When the fighting in البصرة turned, the men from الشام shut themselves in a fortified house. One of them was عبد الله بن خازم, who had been commanding their horse. His mother came to the place and ordered him to come down. He refused. So she told him what she would do in front of everybody if he did not — and he came down, and lived. Everyone else in that house died.

**The statement:**
> فَأَتَتْهُ أُمُّهُ عَجْلَى، وَكَانَتْ حَبَشِيَّةً، فَأَمَرَتْهُ بِالنُّزُولِ، فَأَبَى، فَقَالَتْ: وَاللَّهِ لَتَنْزِلَنَّ أَوْ لَأَنْزِعَنَّ ثِيَابِي! فَنَزَلَ وَنَجَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1402
> *English:* "Then his mother ʿAjlā came to him — she was an Abyssinian — and ordered him to come down, and he refused. She said: by God, you will come down or I will tear off my clothes! So he came down, and was saved."

**عبرت:** The books keep the small human turns as carefully as the battles, because that is often where a life is decided.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG24 · The fire at قصر سنبيل
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة flares and then goes quiet.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had sent two men in turn to break the revolt in البصرة without a battle. The first was killed. The second, جارية بن قدامة, brought most of his own tribe back over, and then drove the rest into a fortified house and set it alight. ابن كثير is careful to record that he warned them first and gave them their excuse, and that they would not come out. The count of the dead is given two ways in our own books, forty and seventy, and we say so.

**The statement:**
> وَأَحْرَقَ جَارِيَةُ الْقَصْرَ بِمَنْ فِيهِ، فَهَلَكَ ابْنُ الْحَضْرَمِيِّ وَسَبْعُونَ رَجُلًا مَعَهُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1402
> *English:* "And Jāriya burned the palace with those in it, and Ibn al-Ḥaḍramī perished, and seventy men with him."

**عبرت:** The method a government uses to win at home is remembered longer than the winning.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG25 · What the fire cost
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38–39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** فارس, كرمان and the eastern districts go dark one by one.

**What happened:** ابن كثير does not leave the fire as an incident. He follows it. When the news of what had been done got around the provinces, it disturbed people, hearts turned, and they differed over the caliph. Then the land-tax stopped coming in from most of those districts, and فارس went further and threw its governor out. That chain — an act, a reputation, a revenue — is stated by the historian himself and not inferred by us.

**The statement:**
> فلما (٤) اشتهر هذا الصنيع في البلاد شَوَّش ذلك (٥) قلوب كثير من الناس على علي (٦)، واختلفوا على علي، ومنع أكثر أهل تلك النواحي خراجهم، ولاسيما أهل فارس فإنهم تمردوا وأخرجوا عاملهم سهل بن حنيف
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٣٦ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3682
> *English:* "And when this deed became notorious through the lands it troubled the hearts of many of the people against ʿAlī, and they differed over ʿAlī, and most of the people of those regions withheld their land-tax — and especially the people of Fāris, for they rebelled and drove out their governor Sahl b. Ḥunayf."

**عبرت:** What a government does in one city is heard in every province, and the bill arrives as unpaid tax.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG26 · "Come, let me study the Book with you"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** A man who had fought beside علي ؓ at الجمل and at صفين walked in with thirty riders and told him to his face that he would not obey him and would not pray behind him, and that he was leaving in the morning. علي ؓ asked him why, and heard the answer out. Then he did not reach for a sword. He offered the man a sitting: let us read the Book together and discuss the Sunnas, and perhaps you will come to see what you now reject. The man said he would come back. He left that night instead.

**The statement:**
> هَلُمَّ أُدَارِسُكَ الْكِتَابَ، وَأُنَاظِرُكَ فِي السُّنَنِ، وَأُفَاتِحُكَ أُمُورًا أَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِهَا مِنْكَ، فَلَعَلَّكَ تَعْرِفُ مَا أَنْتَ لَهُ الْآنَ مُنْكِرٌ، قَالَ: فَإِنِّي عَائِدٌ إِلَيْكَ. قَالَ: لَا يَسْتَهْوِيَنَّكَ الشَّيْطَانُ، وَلَا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ الْجُهَّالُ، وَاللَّهِ لَئِنِ اسْتَرْشَدْتَنِي وَقَبِلْتَ مِنِّي لَأَهْدِيَنَّكَ سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٤ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1403
> *English:* "Come, let me study the Book with you, and debate the Sunnas with you, and open to you matters I know better than you — perhaps you will come to know what you now reject. He said: I will come back to you. He said: let Satan not lead you away, and let the ignorant not make you light-headed. By God, if you seek right guidance of me and accept it from me I will guide you to the path of right direction."

**عبرت:** The first answer to a man who has left the community is an open book, not a drawn sword.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG27 · Do not wrong the people of the qibla
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A column moves from الكوفة south-east towards الأهواز.

**What happened:** A commander was sent after the breakaway group with two thousand men. Before he went, علي ؓ gave him his orders, and they are four short clauses. Fear God as far as you can. Do not commit an outrage against the people of the qibla. Do not oppress the people under the covenant. Do not be arrogant. That is the whole charge, given to a man riding out against Muslims who had renounced him.

**The statement:**
> اتَّقِ اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتَ، وَلَا تَبْغِ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْقِبْلَةِ، وَلَا تَظْلِمْ أَهْلَ الذِّمَّةِ، وَلَا تَتَكَبَّرْ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٧ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1406
> *English:* "Fear God as much as you are able, and do not wrong the people of the qibla, and do not oppress the people of the dhimma, and do not be arrogant — for God does not love the arrogant."

**عبرت:** Who the enemy is does not change what you are allowed to do to him.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG28 · The man who satisfied every faction
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أسياف البحر, on the Gulf coast below البصرة.

**What happened:** When the pursuit closed on him, the leader of the breakaway had a problem: the people around him wanted four different things. So he told each group what it wanted to hear. To the خوارج he said he held their view. To the others he said the arbitration had deposed the caliph. To the partisans of عثمان ؓ he said privately that he agreed with them. And to the men who had stopped paying zakāh he said: keep your hands closed on it and give it to your relatives. The book sums it up in three words.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ لِمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْخَوَارِجِ: أَنَا عَلَى رَأْيِكُمْ وَإِنَّ عَلِيًّا، لَمْ يَنْبَغِ لَهُ أَنْ يُحَكِّمَ. وَقَالَ لِلْآخَرِينَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ: إِنَّ عَلِيًّا حَكَّمَ وَرَضِيَ، فَخَلَعَهُ حَكَمُهُ الَّذِي ارْتَضَاهُ، وَهَذَا كَانَ الرَّأْيُ الَّذِي خَرَجَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْكُوفَةِ وَإِلَيْهِ كَانَ يَذْهَبُ. وَقَالَ سِرًّا لِلْعُثْمَانِيَّةِ: أَنَا وَاللَّهِ عَلَى رَأْيِكُمْ، قَدْ وَاللَّهِ قُتِلَ عُثْمَانُ مَظْلُومًا. فَأَرْضَى كُلَّ صِنْفٍ مِنْهُمْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1407
> *English:* "He said to those with him of the Khawārij: I hold your view, and ʿAlī ought not to have accepted arbitration. And he said to the others of his companions: ʿAlī accepted arbitration and was content, and the arbiter he approved deposed him — and this was the view he had gone out of Kūfa upon and held to. And he said secretly to the ʿUthmāniyya: I, by God, am of your view; by God ʿUthmān was killed wronged. And he said to those who withheld the alms: keep your hands closed upon your alms and give them to your own kin. So he satisfied every one of their kinds."

**عبرت:** A man who agrees with everybody has a position of his own and is hiding it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### EAT/E-EG29 · "Their religion does not forbid them blood"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The Gulf coast below البصرة.

**What happened:** In those districts there were many Christians who had entered Islam. Then they watched Muslims fight Muslims for two years. الکامل records, without comment and without softening it, what they said as they went back to what they had left. It is one sentence, and it is the bill for the fitna written in the currency that matters most.

**The statement:**
> وَاللَّهِ لَدِينُنَا الَّذِي خَرَجْنَا مِنْهُ خَيْرٌ مِنْ دِينِ هَؤُلَاءِ، لَا يَنْهَاهُمْ دِينُهُمْ عَنْ سَفْكِ الدِّمَاءِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1407
> *English:* "By God, the religion we came out of is better than the religion of these people — their religion does not forbid them the shedding of blood."

**عبرت:** Every quarrel among believers is watched by somebody who is deciding whether to believe.

**Hands-up?** What do you think our arguments look like from outside?

### EAT/E-EG30 · A banner of safe-conduct before the battle
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أسياف البحر.

**What happened:** When the government column finally came up with the breakaway camp, the commander did not attack. He planted a banner of safe-conduct and announced that anyone who came in was safe, with one stated exception: the leader himself and the men who had already fought a pitched battle against them. Most of the people who were not of his tribe walked away, and the fighting that followed was much smaller than it would have been. The wording of the proclamation as printed is awkward and must be checked against a page image before it is quoted anywhere.

**The statement:**
> نَصَبَ رَايَةَ أَمَانٍ وَقَالَ: مَنْ أَتَاهُمْ مِنَ النَّاسِ فَهُوَ آمِنٌ، إِلَّا الْخِرِّيتُ وَأَصْحَابُهُ الَّذِينَ حَارَبُونَا أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1407
> *English:* "He set up a banner of safe-conduct and said: whoever of the people comes to them is safe, except al-Khirrīt and those of his companions who fought us the first time."

**عبرت:** An amnesty offered before the fighting saves more men than any victory after it.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG31 · The parting on the road
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** From أسياف البحر back towards فارس.

**What happened:** After the fighting the commander sorted the survivors. Those who had left Islam were offered it again, and those who returned were released with their families. The men who had withheld the zakāh paid two years of it. The Christians and their households were carried off as captives. Their Muslim neighbours walked along the road with them to see them off, and what happened at the farewell is on the page.

**The statement:**
> وَأَمَّا النَّصَارَى وَعِيَالُهُمْ فَاحْتَمَلَهُمْ مُقْبِلًا بِهِمْ، وَأَقْبَلَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مَعَهُمْ يُشَيِّعُونَهُمْ، فَلَمَّا وَدَّعُوهُمْ بَكَى الرِّجَالُ وَالنِّسَاءُ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ، حَتَّى رَحِمَهُمُ النَّاسُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1408
> *English:* "As for the Christians and their households, he carried them off with him; and the Muslims came along with them, escorting them, and when they took leave of one another the men and the women wept to one another, until the onlookers pitied them."

**عبرت:** The people who lose most in a civil war are usually the ones who were never a party to it.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG32 · Five hundred people bought and set free
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أردشيرخُرَّه, in فارس.

**What happened:** The column of captives passed a governor on its road. Five hundred people, women and children among them, called out to him by name and begged him to buy them and free them. He swore an oath in front of everybody that he would give them away in charity. Then he bought the whole five hundred for half a million, and freed them, and did not ask a single one of them to help him pay for it.

**The statement:**
> فَبَكَى النِّسَاءُ وَالصِّبْيَانُ وَصَاحَ الرِّجَالُ: يَا أَبَا الْفَضْلِ! يَا حَامِيَ الرِّجَالِ (وَمَأْوَى الْمُعْضَبِ) ، وَفَكَّاكَ الْعُنَاةِ، امْنُنْ عَلَيْنَا وَاشْتَرِنَا وَأَعْتِقْنَا! فَقَالَ مَصْقَلَةُ: أُقْسِمُ بِاللَّهِ لَأَتَصَدَّقَنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ! إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْزِي الْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1408
> *English:* "The women and the children wept and the men cried out: O Abū al-Faḍl! O protector of men, refuge of the hard-pressed, loosener of captives — be gracious to us, and buy us, and set us free! Maṣqala said: I swear by God I will give you away in charity! God rewards those who give in charity."

**عبرت:** A generous oath is easy to swear in front of a crowd and hard to pay for afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG33 · The freeing stood, and the price became a debt
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** He could not pay. He brought a fifth of the money, then fled across to الشام. علي ؓ heard of it and said three things about him in one breath, and they are not all condemnation: he acted as a chief acts, he fled as a slave flees, he betrayed as a profligate betrays. And then, having said it, he gave a ruling. The five hundred stayed free. The unpaid price became a debt on the man who had freed them. Nobody was returned to captivity because a governor had absconded.

**The statement:**
> وَأَجَازَ عِتْقَ السَّبْيِ وَقَالَ: أَعْتَقَهُمْ مُبْتَاعُهُمْ وَصَارَتْ أَثْمَانُهُمْ دَيْنًا عَلَى مُعْتِقِهِمْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٢٠ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1409
> *English:* "And he let the freeing of the captives stand, and said: the man who bought them freed them, and their price has become a debt upon the one who freed them."

**عبرت:** A state that is losing a war can still give a just ruling, and that is the measure of whether it is still a state.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG34 · Five risings in five months
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Five pins east and north-east of الكوفة, appearing one after another.

**What happened:** الکامل keeps a ledger for this year that البدایہ does not keep. After النهروان the risings did not stop; they came in a line, one every month or so, each with its own leader and a couple of hundred men, and each was put down. الدسكرة in the fourth month, ماسبذان in the fifth, جرجرايا in the sixth, البندنيجين in the seventh, and شهرزور in رمضان. Five in five months, and none of them large.

**The statement:**
> لَمَّا قُتِلَ أَهْلُ النَّهْرَوَانِ خَرَجَ أَشْرَسُ بْنُ عَوْفٍ عَلَى عَلِيٍّ بِالدَّسْكَرَةِ فِي مِائَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ سَارَ إِلَى الْأَنْبَارِ، فَوَجَّهَ إِلَيْهِ عَلِيٌّ الْأَبْرَشَ بْنَ حَسَّانَ فِي ثَلَاثِمِائَةٍ فَوَاقَعَهُ، فَقُتِلَ أَشْرَسُ فِي رَبِيعٍ الْآخَرِ سَنَةَ ثَمَانٍ وَثَلَاثِينَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٢١ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1410
> *English:* "When the people of al-Nahrawān were killed, Ashras b. ʿAwf went out against ʿAlī at al-Daskara with two hundred men, then marched to al-Anbār; so ʿAlī sent against him al-Abrash b. Ḥassān with three hundred, and he engaged him, and Ashras was killed in Rabīʿ al-Ākhir of the year thirty-eight."

**عبرت:** A movement is not finished when its army is beaten; it is finished when its argument stops recruiting.

### EAT/E-EG35 · The forty wounded men carried into الكوفة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Five فرسخ outside الكوفة.

**What happened:** The last of that yearʼs risings came within five farsakh of the city. علي ؓ sent to invite them in and they refused; he went out himself, and called them again, and they refused again, and they were killed. Fifty men asked for safe-conduct and got it. And forty of the wounded — men who had that morning been trying to kill him — were carried into الكوفة on his order and treated until they recovered.

**The statement:**
> فَقَتَلَهُمْ أَصْحَابُ عَلِيٍّ، وَلَمْ يَسْلَمْ مِنْهُمْ غَيْرُ خَمْسِينَ رَجُلًا اسْتَأْمَنُوا فَآمَنَهُمْ. وَكَانَ فِي الْخَوَارِجِ أَرْبَعُونَ رَجُلًا جَرْحَى، فَأَمَرَ عَلِيٌّ بِإِدْخَالِهِمُ الْكُوفَةَ وَمُدَاوَاتِهِمْ حَتَّى بَرَأُوا.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٢٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1412
> *English:* "So ʿAlīʼs companions killed them, and none of them came off safe but fifty men who asked for safe-conduct and were given it. And among the Khawārij were forty wounded men, and ʿAlī ordered that they be brought into Kūfa and treated until they were well."

**عبرت:** The way the victor treats the wounded is the only part of a battle that is entirely his own choice.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG36 · A hundred men who broke their scabbards
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** عين التمر, west of الكوفة.

**What happened:** A Syrian column came down on the outpost at عين التمر. Its commander had given most of his thousand men leave, so a hundred were left. They set their backs to the village wall, broke the scabbards of their swords so that there could be no sheathing them, and fought. A neighbouring chief sent his son with fifty men. When the Syrians saw the dust of fifty they took it for a relief army and ran, and the hundred chased them and killed three.

**The statement:**
> وَوَاقَعَ مَالِكٌ النُّعْمَانَ، وَجَعَلَ جِدَارَ الْقَرْيَةِ فِي ظُهُورِ أَصْحَابِهِ، وَكَتَبَ مَالِكٌ إِلَى مِخْنَفِ بْنِ سُلَيْمٍ يَسْتَعِينُهُ، وَهُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْهُ، وَاقْتَتَلَ مَالِكٌ وَالنُّعْمَانُ أَشَدَّ قِتَالٍ، فَوَجَّهَ مِخْنَفُ ابْنَهُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ فِي خَمْسِينَ رَجْلًا، فَانْتَهَوْا إِلَى مَالِكٍ وَقَدْ كَسَرُوا جُفُونَ سُيُوفِهِمْ وَاسْتَقْتَلُوا، فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ أَهْلُ الشَّامِ انْهَزَمُوا عِنْدَ الْمَسَاءِ، وَظَنُّوا أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَدَدًا، وَتَبِعَهُمْ مَالِكٌ فَقَتَلَ مِنْهُمْ ثَلَاثَةَ نَفَرٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٢٤ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1413
> *English:* "Mālik engaged al-Nuʿmān and put the wall of the village at his companionsʼ backs, and wrote to Mikhnaf b. Sulaym asking help of him, for he was near him; and Mālik and al-Nuʿmān fought a very hard fight. So Mikhnaf sent his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān with fifty men, and they came up to Mālik — and they had broken the scabbards of their swords and set themselves to fight to the death. When the Syrians saw them they were routed at evening, thinking that a relief force had come to them; and Mālik followed them and killed three of them."

**عبرت:** Numbers decide fewer battles than people think; the appearance of help decides a great many.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG37 · The garrison that was not there
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** هيت and الأنبار, on the Euphrates.

**What happened:** A column of six thousand came to هيت and found it empty, and went on to الأنبار. The garrison there was supposed to be five hundred and had melted to a fraction of that, and the commander who should have been holding it had marched off in another direction on his own initiative, without orders. Thirty men and their leader were killed, and the townʼs money went back to الشام on the raidersʼ horses. الکامل is the book that says why, and names the man.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ سَبَبُ تَفَرُّقِهِمْ أَنَّهُ كَانَ عَلَيْهِمْ كُمَيْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ، فَبَلَغَهُ أَنَّ قَوْمًا بِقَرْقِيسْيَا يُرِيدُونَ الْغَارَةَ عَلَى هِيتَ، فَسَارَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِغَيْرِ أَمْرِ عَلِيٍّ، فَأَتَى أَصْحَابُ سُفْيَانَ وَكُمَيْلٌ غَائِبٌ عَنْهَا، فَأَغْضَبَ ذَلِكَ عَلِيًّا عَلَى كُمَيْلٍ، فَأَتَى إِلَيْهِ يُنْكِرُ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٢٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1414
> *English:* "The cause of their scattering was that Kumayl b. Ziyād was over them, and word reached him that a people at Qarqīsiyā meant to raid Hīt, so he marched against them without ʿAlīʼs order; and Sufyānʼs men came while Kumayl was absent from it. That angered ʿAlī against Kumayl, and he came to him rebuking him for it."

**عبرت:** A good officer acting without orders can cost more than a bad one obeying them.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG38 · "You cannot spare me, nor yourselves"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** النخيلة, outside الكوفة.

**What happened:** When the news came from الأنبار, علي ؓ did not send anybody. He rode out himself and made camp at النخيلة, outside his own city. The people came after him and told him he need not do this — they would spare him the trouble. He gave them one sentence in reply, and it is the shortest summary of those two years that either book contains.

### EAT/E-EG39 · "Get away! Get away!"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** تيماء, on the road from الشام to the الحجاز.

### EAT/E-EG40 · Pursue no fugitive, finish no wounded man
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الجزيرة, around نصيبين.

**What happened:** A raid came into الجزيرة. An officer at هيت was warned by a colleague at نصيبين, rode up with six hundred horse, beat the raiders and took their camp, and killed a great many. Then, with the field his and the enemy running, he gave the order the books thought worth recording — and it costs a commander a large part of his victory to give it.

> *English:* "And he ordered that no man in flight be pursued and that no wounded man be finished off."

**عبرت:** Victory is the moment at which restraint becomes voluntary, which is why it is the moment that is remembered.

### EAT/E-EG41 · Only the horses and the weapons
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** From نصيبين across the Euphrates to بعلبك, and back through الرقة.

**What happened:** One of علي ؓʼs men crossed the Euphrates and raided deep into the other side, as far as بعلبك, and on the way home stripped the district of الرقة of livestock, horses and weapons. علي ؓ wrote to him about it, and the letter does two opposite things in one breath: it forbids him to take the peopleʼs property, allowing only what they were fighting with — and then praises the raid itself.

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٢٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1417

**عبرت:** Praise for the man and a limit on the method can be written in the same sentence.

### EAT/E-EG43 · To the Tigris, and back again
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A short arrow from الشام to the Tigris, and a return arrow.

**What happened:** In the middle of the year of columns, معاوية ؓ came out himself with a heavy force and rode east until he was in sight of the Tigris. Then he turned round and went home. **عبرت:** Not every advance is meant to arrive; some are meant only to be seen.

### EAT/E-EG44 · A ḥajj led by neither side
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة.

**What happened:** Both sides sent a man to lead the ḥajj that year, and both men reached مكة, and neither would give way to the other. There was no battle. They agreed instead on a third man, of the family that had held the keys of the Kaʿba since before Islam, and he led the prayers and the ḥajj and the season passed. **عبرت:** Two men who cannot yield to each other can still both yield to a third, and the season is saved.

### EAT/E-EG45 · Prisoners exchanged by letter

Then a letter arrived from معاوية ؓ proposing an exchange — his men for the men of علي ؓʼs who were in his hands. The exchange was made. ### EAT/E-EG46 · "More like Anūshirwān than any we have seen"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** فارس and كرمان come back into colour on the map.

**What happened:** فارس had thrown its governor out and stopped paying. علي ؓ asked his council for a name, and they gave him one: a man of hard judgement who understood administration. He was sent with four thousand horse, and within a season the province was paying again and quiet. What the conquered people of that province said about him afterwards is the line worth carrying, because it is a compliment from the people who had least reason to pay one.

> *English:* "…than the conduct of Kisrā Anūshirwān — the conduct of this Arab, in gentleness and in careful management and in knowing what is coming."

**عبرت:** A province is held by administration, not by armies, and the people being administered know the difference.

### EAT/E-EG47 · A raid to السند in the middle of a civil war
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** An arrow from البصرة east, past كرمان, to السند and القيقان.

**What happened:** This is the card that connects this evening to a later one. While the provinces were fraying and the columns were riding, a volunteer force went out east, by the order of علي ؓ, all the way to the land of السند. It took spoils and captives, and its commander distributed a thousand head in one day, and then stayed on campaign out there for years. He was still fighting in those hills when he was killed, long after the war behind him had ended.

**The statement:**
> وَفِيهَا تَوَجَّهَ الْحَارِثُ بْنُ مُرَّةَ الْعَبْدِيُّ إِلَى بِلَادِ السِّنْدِ (غَازِيًا مُتَطَوِّعًا بِأَمْرِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلِيٍّ، فَغَنِمَ وَأَصَابَ غَنَائِمَ وَسَبْيًا كَثِيرًا، وَقَسَّمَ فِي يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ أَلْفَ رَأْسٍ وَبَقِيَ غَازِيًا) إِلَى أَنْ قُتِلَ بِأَرْضِ الْقِيقَانِ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ، إِلَّا قَلِيلًا سَنَةَ اثْنَتَيْنِ وَأَرْبَعِينَ أَيَّامَ مُعَاوِيَةَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٢٩ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1418
> *English:* "And in it al-Ḥārith b. Murra al-ʿAbdī set out for the lands of al-Sind, raiding as a volunteer by the order of the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī; he took spoils and captives in great number, and distributed a thousand head in a single day, and remained on campaign until he was killed in the land of al-Qīqān, he and those with him except a few, in the year forty-two, in the days of Muʿāwiya."

**عبرت:** The road that would one day reach this country was already being opened while the centre was at its weakest.

**Hands-up?** Which direction do you think Islam first came to this land from?

### EAT/E-EG48 · A man on the minbar asking where عثمان ؓ was
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A column moves from الشام down to المدينة.

**What happened:** Three thousand men rode from الشام to المدينة. The governor left before them and went to الكوفة, and nobody in the city fought. The commander went up onto the minbar of the Prophet ﷺ and called out to the Anṣārī clans by name, and then asked, twice, where his old man was — meaning عثمان ؓ. Then he told them what he would have done if he had not been given orders. He took the pledge, and pulled down houses.

**The statement:**
> فساروا من الشام حتى قدموا المدينة - وعامل علي عليها يومئذ أبو أيوب - ففر منهم أبو أيوب فأتى عليًا بالكوفة، ودخل بسر المدينة ولم يقاتله أحد، فصعد منبرها فنادي على المنبر: يا دينار ويا نجار ويا رزيق شيخي شيخي عهدي به هاهنا بالأمس فأين هو؟ - يعني عثمان بن عفان - ثم قال: يا أهل المدينة والله لولا ما عهد إليّ معاوية ما تركت بهما محتلمًا إلَّا قتلته
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٣٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3684
> *English:* "They marched from Syria until they came to Medina — and ʿAlīʼs governor over it that day was Abū Ayyūb — and Abū Ayyūb fled from them and came to ʿAlī at Kūfa. Busr entered Medina and no one fought him; he climbed its pulpit and called out from the pulpit: O Dīnār! O Najjār! O Zurayq! My old man, my old man — I knew him here only yesterday, so where is he? — meaning ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān. Then he said: people of Medina, by God, had it not been for what Muʿāwiya charged me with, I would not have left in the two of them one who had reached manhood without killing him."

**عبرت:** Five years after the killing of عثمان ؓ, the grief for him was still moving armies.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG49 · جابر ؓ asks أم سلمة ؓ what to do
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** The commander sent word to بنو سلمة that they had no safe-conduct from him until they produced جابر بن عبد الله ؓ. جابر ؓ did not decide for himself and did not run. He went to أم سلمة ؓ, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, told her plainly that he thought this was a pledge of misguidance and that he feared he would be killed, and asked her what she saw. She told him to give it — and she gave him her reason: she had already told her own son and her son-in-law to give it.

**The statement:**
> فَانْطَلَقَ جَابِرٌ إِلَى أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - فَقَالَ لَهَا: مَاذَا تَرَيْنَ؟ إِنَّ هَذِهِ بَيْعَةُ ضَلَالَةٍ، وَقَدْ خَشِيتُ أَنْ أُقْتَلَ. قَالَتْ: أَرَى أَنْ تُبَايِعَ، فَإِنِّي قَدْ أَمَرْتُ ابْنِي عُمَرَ وَخَتَنِي ابْنَ زَمْعَةَ أَنْ يُبَايِعَا، وَكَانَتِ ابْنَتُهَا زَيْنَبُ تَحْتَ ابْنِ زَمْعَةَ، فَأَتَاهُ جَابِرٌ فَبَايَعَهُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٣٢ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1421
> *English:* "So Jābir went to Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — and said to her: what do you see? This is a pledge of misguidance, and I fear to be killed. She said: I see that you should give the pledge, for I have ordered my son ʿUmar and my son-in-law Ibn Zamʿa to give it. So Jābir came to him and gave him the pledge."

**عبرت:** In a confusing hour a believer does not decide alone; he asks someone with more knowledge than he has.

**Hands-up?** Who would you ask?

### EAT/E-EG50 · "Not to a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة.

**What happened:** The column went on to مكة. أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ was there, and he was afraid he would be killed — he had been one of the two arbiters, and the men coming in were from the side that had gained by the arbitration. البدایہ records that the commander told him, in as many words, that he would not do such a thing to a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and let him alone.

**The statement:**

> *English:* "Then he went on until he came to Mecca, and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī feared that he would kill him; but Busr said to him: I would not do that to a companion of the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace — and he let him be."

**عبرت:** Even at the worst of it, the rank of صحبة was a wall that most men would not climb over.

### EAT/E-EG51 · The man of كنانة who asked to die first
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** اليمن.

**What happened:** The column reached the اليمن. The governor had gone to الكوفة, and his two small sons had been left in the desert in the keeping of a man of كنانة. When the soldiers came for the children, the man who was keeping them did not hand them over and did not argue about politics. He asked one question and made one offer, and they took the offer and then killed the children anyway.

> *English:* "The Kinānī said to him: why do you kill these two, who have committed no offence? If you are going to kill them, then kill me with them. So he killed him, and killed them after him."

### EAT/E-EG52 · "A rule that stands only by killing children"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** اليمن.

**What happened:** Afterwards the women of كنانة came out. One of them spoke, and الکامل wrote down what she said. She did not take a side in the war. She said that the men were one thing and these two were another, that such a thing had not been done in the جاهلية and had not been done in Islam, and then she named the kind of authority that needs it. Nobody answered her.

**The statement:**
> يَا هَذَا! قَتَلْتَ الرِّجَالَ فَعَلَامَ تَقْتُلُ هَذَيْنِ؟ وَاللَّهِ مَا كَانُوا يُقْتَلُونَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ وَالْإِسْلَامِ! وَاللَّهِ يَا ابْنَ أَبِي أَرْطَاةَ إِنَّ سُلْطَانًا لَا يَقُومُ إِلَّا بِقَتْلِ الصَّبِيِّ الصَّغِيرِ، وَالشَّيْخِ الْكَبِيرِ، وَنَزْعِ الرَّحْمَةِ، وَعُقُوقِ الْأَرْحَامِ لَسُلْطَانُ سُوءٍ!
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٣٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1422
> *English:* "You there! You have killed the men — so on what ground do you kill these two? By God, they were not killed in the Jāhiliyya nor in Islam! By God, son of Abī Arṭāt, a rule that stands only by the killing of the small child and the aged man, and by the stripping away of mercy, and by the severing of kinship — that is an evil rule!"

**عبرت:** Power that has to reach for a child has already told you what it is.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG53 · The historianʼs reservation
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** At the end of that whole account, ابن كثير stops and speaks in his own voice about the report he has just given. He does not delete it and he does not endorse it. He says it is well known among the specialists in campaign history — and then that, as far as he is concerned, its soundness is open to question. Exactly how much of the account his reservation covers, the page does not say, and we will not pretend to know.

> ويقال إن بسرًا قتل خلقًا من شيعة علي في ميسره هذا، وهذا الخبر مشهور عند أصحاب المغازي والسير، وفي صحته عندي نظر والله تعالى أعلم.

**عبرت:** "Well known" and "sound" are two different things, and the scholars kept the difference visible on the page.

### EAT/E-EG54 · "He has perished — so to whom shall we pledge?"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH, after the killing of علي ؓ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** نجران, then مكة.

**What happened:** علي ؓ sent four thousand men in two columns after the raiders. One of them reached نجران, killed men there, and chased the column ahead of him as far as مكة. When he got there he told the people of مكة to give the pledge to the Commander of the Faithful — and they answered him with a question he had not been expecting, because the news had reached مكة before it reached him.

**The statement:**
> وَهَرَبَ بُسْرٌ وَأَصْحَابُهُ مِنْهُ، وَاتَّبَعَهُ جَارِيَةُ حَتَّى أَتَى مَكَّةَ فَقَالَ: بَايِعُوا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. فَقَالُوا: قَدْ هَلَكَ فَلِمَنْ نُبَايِعُ؟ قَالَ: لِمَنْ بَايَعَ لَهُ أَصْحَابُ عَلِيٍّ. فَبَايَعُوا خَوْفًا مِنْهُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٣٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1422
> *English:* "And Busr and his companions fled from him, and Jāriya followed him until he came to Mecca and said: give the pledge to the Commander of the Faithful. They said: he has perished — so to whom shall we pledge? He said: to the one to whom ʿAlīʼs companions have pledged. So they pledged, out of fear of him."

**عبرت:** A man can be chasing an enemy for a ruler who is already dead, and not know it.

### EAT/E-EG55 · أبو هريرة ؓ goes back to leading the prayer
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** The column came on to المدينة. أبو هريرة ؓ was leading the people in prayer when it arrived and he left the city; the commander said aloud that he would have killed him if he had found him. Then he told the people of المدينة to pledge to الحسن بن علي ؓ, and they did. He stayed one day. Then he went back to الكوفة — and أبو هريرة ؓ came back and went on leading the prayer.

**The statement:**
> ثُمَّ سَارَ حَتَّى أَتَى الْمَدِينَةَ وَأَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ يُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ، فَهَرَبَ مِنْهُ، فَقَالَ جَارِيَةُ: لَوْ وَجَدْتُ أَبَا سِنَّوْرٍ لَقَتَلْتُهُ. ثُمَّ قَالَ لِأَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ: بَايِعُوا الْحَسَنَ بْنَ عَلِيٍّ فَبَايَعُوهُ، وَأَقَامَ يَوْمَهُ، ثُمَّ عَادَ إِلَى الْكُوفَةِ وَرَجَعَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٣٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1422
> *English:* "Then he marched until he came to Medina, where Abū Hurayra was leading the people in prayer, and he fled from him. Jāriya said: if I found Abū Sinnawr I would kill him. Then he said to the people of Medina: give the pledge to al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī — and they gave it to him. He stayed his day, then returned to Kūfa, and Abū Hurayra went back to leading them in prayer."

**عبرت:** Armies came and went through المدينة for two years, and the congregation formed again behind the same man each time they left.

### EAT/E-EG56 · The truce: العراق to one, الشام to the other
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** A line drawn between العراق and الشام; both sides go quiet.

**What happened:** After long letters back and forth, a truce was made. The terms were simple and they are worth saying slowly, because they are the shape of the next forty years of the ummahʼs map: the war is set down; العراق belongs to one and الشام to the other; and neither of them enters the otherʼs country on a raid. الکامل is the only one of our two books whose pages here carry it, and we say so when we say it.

**The statement:**
> وَفِيهَا جَرَتْ مُهَادَنَةٌ بَيْنَ عَلِيٍّ وَمُعَاوِيَةَ بَعْدَ مُكَاتَبَاتٍ طَوِيلَةٍ عَلَى وَضْعِ الْحَرْبِ، وَيَكُونُ لَعَلِيٍّ الْعِرَاقُ، وَلِمُعَاوِيَةَ الشَّامُ، لَا يَدْخُلُ أَحَدُهُمَا بَلَدَ الْآخَرِ بِغَارَةٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٣٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1424
> *English:* "And in it a truce came about between ʿAlī and Muʿāwiya, after long correspondence, on the laying down of the war: that al-ʿIrāq should be ʿAlīʼs and Syria Muʿāwiyaʼs, neither of the two entering the otherʼs country on a raid."

**عبرت:** A war that cannot be won is eventually put down, and the line where it is put down becomes a border.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG57 · The map at the end of the evening
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The full closing map: الكوفة and the east in one colour, الشام and مصر in the other, the الحجاز between.

**What happened:** This is the closing map, and the room should be able to read it without being told anything. مصر has changed colour since the opening map. الشام never changed at all. الحجاز has been ridden through twice in one year by men from both sides. And the four provinces still held are held by four brothers of one house. The governor list that ابن كثير gives for the end of 38 is the single sentence that carries it.

> *English:* "As for Egypt, it had settled into the hand of Muʿāwiya, and he appointed ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ over it as his deputy — and God knows best."

**عبرت:** Two years earlier this was one state with one governor list, and the list is how you see what was lost.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG58 · The Companion who withdrew from both sides
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح ؓ had been one of the scribes of the revelation and then governor of مصر before all of this, and he had led the fleet at ذات الصواري. When عثمان ؓ was besieged he was pushed out of مصر. And then he did something the books record in a single clause: he withdrew from علي ؓ and from معاوية ؓ alike and took no part. He died in the dawn prayer, between the two salutations.

> *English:* "Then when ʿUthmān was besieged, Muḥammad b. Abī Ḥudhayfa overcame him and drove him out of Egypt; and he died in this year, withdrawn from ʿAlī and from Muʿāwiya alike, in the dawn prayer, between the two salutations."

**عبرت:** Some of the best of them chose to hold neither side, and the books record that as a life well ended.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG59 · "All of us killed him"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37–38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** النهروان.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن خباب was born in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ and was known as a good man. He was killed by the group that had broken away. When علي ؓ came he did not demand that the whole group answer for it; he made them an offer that would have ended the matter without a battle — hand over the men who did it, and the rest of you are safe. They gave him an answer that made the offer impossible.

**The statement:**
> عبد الله بن خباب بن الأرت (٦). ولد في حياة (٧) النَّبِيّ ﷺ وكان موصوفًا بالخير، قتله (٨) الخوارج كما قدمنا (بالنهروان) في هذه السنة، (فلما جاء علي قال لهم: أعطونا قتلته ثم أنتم آمنون فقالوا: كلنا قتله فقاتلهم).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٢٢ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3668
> *English:* "ʿAbdallāh b. Khabbāb b. al-Aratt. He was born in the lifetime of the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, and was described as a good man. The Khawārij killed him, as we have related, at al-Nahrawān in this year. When ʿAlī came he said to them: hand over to us his killers and then you are safe. They said: all of us killed him. So he fought them."

**عبرت:** A group that will not give up its wrongdoers has made their crime its own.

### EAT/E-EG60 · خباب بن الأرت ؓ, the first man buried outside الكوفة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** خباب بن الأرت ؓ had been enslaved before Islam, had accepted it before the house of الأرقم, had been tortured for it — عمر ؓ once told him no man had a better right to sit in that place except بلال ؓ, and he answered that بلال ؓ at least had a clan to protect him and he had none. He was at بدر and at every battle after it. He died at الكوفة in this window, sixty-three years old, and he was the first man buried outside the city.

> *English:* "He said: and he died at Kūfa in this year at the age of sixty-three, and he was the first man to be buried outside Kūfa."

**عبرت:** The generation that had been tortured in مكة was now dying in the garrison cities they had built.

### EAT/E-EG61 · The verse about the neighbour they let burn
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** After the burning at البصرة, verses went round the city, and the books kept them. They are not about the caliphate or the arbitration or who was right. They are about a tribe that had taken a man under its protection and then stood by while he burned — which, in that society, was the worst thing that could be said about anybody. That is how the event was remembered by the people who saw it.

**The statement:**
> رَدَدْنَا زِيَادًا إِلَى دَارِهِ ... وَجَارُ تَمِيمٍ دُخَانًا ذَهَبْ لَحَى اللَّهُ قَوْمًا شَوَوْا جَارَهُمْ ... وَلَمْ يَدْفَعُوا عَنْهُ حَرَّ اللَّهَبْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧١٣ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1402
> *English:* "We gave Ziyād back his house, and Tamīmʼs protected neighbour went off as smoke. May God disfigure a people who roasted their own neighbour and did not keep from him the heat of the flame."

**عبرت:** A community is judged afterwards not by which side it took but by whom it failed to protect.

**Hands-up?** no

### EAT/E-EG62 · The deputy who held الكوفة whenever he left it
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو مسعود البدري ؓ — عقبة بن عمرو — was present at العقبة and is counted among the leading Companions. The detail worth keeping is administrative and it is the sort of thing that never reaches a slide: whenever علي ؓ left الكوفة to go and fight, this was the man he left in charge of it. He is called "البدري" because he settled at the water of بدر, and البدایہ says he was not present at the battle itself, "according to the sound view".

**The statement:**
> وهو من سادات الصحابة وكان ينوب لعلي بالكوفة إذا خرج منها إلى القتال
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج٧ ص٥٣٨ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3684
> *English:* "He is one of the leading Companions, and he used to act as ʿAlīʼs deputy at Kūfa whenever he went out of it to fight."

**عبرت:** Behind every commander in the field there is a name nobody remembers, holding the city he left behind.

**Hands-up?** no

## The killing of علي ؓ

*Source note: [`the-killing-of-ali.md`](../docs/research/the-killing-of-ali.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TKO/E-QA1 · The year the obedience came apart
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة and الشام both lit; the line between them dark.

**What happened:** ابن كثير does not begin this year with the killing. He begins by telling the
reader what kind of year it was: matters had come apart, the army had grown unsteady, the people of
العراق held back from standing with their commander, and the affair of the people of الشام grew
strong. In the same breath he says who their commander was, in the strongest words the book has for
any living man. Then he says what all of it did to him — he came to dislike life and to wish for
death, and used often to ask what was keeping back the most wretched of them.

**The statement:**
> العراق [وغيرهم]، ونكلوا عن القيام معه، واستفحل أمر أهل الشام … هذا وأميرهم علي بن أبي طالب خير أهل الأرض في ذلك الزمان، أعبدهم وأزهدهم، وأعلمهم وأخشاهم لله ﷿، ومع هذا كله خذلوه وتخلوا عنه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3686
> *English:* "…ʿIrāq [and others]; they held back from standing with him, and the affair of the people of الشام grew strong … and this though their commander was علي بن أبي طالب, the best of the people of the earth in that age, the most devoted in worship, the most abstinent, the most knowledgeable and the most fearing of God ﷿ — and with all of this they failed him and drew away from him."

**عبرت:** A people can have the best man of its age at its head and still lose him, by refusing to stand with him.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA2 · A truce, and two halves of one ummah
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** a line drawn between العراق and الشام.

**What happened:** On the same page-run البدایہ reports, on ابن جرير's authority, that a truce was
concluded in this year after letters too long to set down. The terms were that neither side would
enter the other's territory with an army, a raid or a campaign. The sentence the book preserves is
short, and it states the reason for the truce before it states the terms. Report it as the book
reports it, and go no further than the book goes.

**The statement:**
> أما بعد فإن الأمة قد قتل بعضها بعضًا فلك العراق ولي الشام فأقر بذلك علي ﵁.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۳۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3685
> *English:* "To proceed: the ummah has killed some of itself, so العراق is yours and الشام is mine — and علي ؓ affirmed that."

**عبرت:** When an ummah has spent itself upon itself, even its settlements are written in the language of loss.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA3 · The historian who would not certify a famous report
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Before he reaches the killing, ابن كثير narrates a campaign into the حجاز and
اليمن with a heavy charge attached to it, and he narrates it through the chain by which he received
it. Then he stops, in his own voice. He says that although the report is well known among the people
of the مغازي and the سير, in his own view there is something to look into concerning whether it is
sound. This is a historian declining to certify a story that everyone of his own time already knew.

**The statement:**
> وهذا الخبر مشهور عند أصحاب المغازي والسير، وفي صحته عندي نظر والله تعالى أعلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۳۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3684
> *English:* "This report is well known among the people of the مغازي and the سير, but in my view there is something to look into concerning its authenticity, and God most high knows best."

**عبرت:** A report can be famous for six hundred years and still not be established.

**Hands-up?** Who here has heard a story about the past so often that they never once asked where it came from?

### TKO/E-QA4 · This beard will be dyed from this head
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

**What happened:** البدایہ gathers, chain after chain, a set of reports that علي ؓ knew how he would
die and said so aloud. The core of them is one sentence he used to say with his hand at his beard —
that this would be dyed from this. The book does not treat all these chains alike, and the cards
that follow show it sorting them. What is common to all of them is that the man went out to the
prayer every morning knowing.

**The statement:**
> والذي فلق الحبة وبرأ النسمة لتخضبن هذه من هذه للحيته من رأسه فما يحبس أشقاها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3686
> *English:* "By Him who split the grain and created the soul, this shall surely be dyed from this — his beard, from his head — so what is keeping back the most wretched of them?"

**عبرت:** A man who expects the blow does not stop going out to the prayer.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA5 · The same saying, stripped of its chain
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** before رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الکامل carries the same saying but does not run the chains البدایہ runs. It gives
the content by itself, says only that it comes down by more than one route, and then adds a plain
gloss so that no reader can mistake the two pronouns. The two books are therefore not transmitting
identical material here, and if both are used that should be said aloud. This is what a compiler
looks like when he is summarising rather than examining.

**The statement:**
> وَقِيلَ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَجْهٍ: إِنَّ عَلِيَّا كَانَ يَقُولُ: مَا يَمْنَعُ أَشْقَاكُمْ أَنْ يُخَضِّبَ هَذِهِ مِنْ هَذِهِ؟ يَعْنِي لِحْيَتَهُ مِنْ دَمِ رَأْسِهِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۳۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1426
> *English:* "And it is said, by more than one route, that علي used to say: what prevents the most wretched of you from dyeing this from this? — meaning his beard, from the blood of his head."

**عبرت:** Two sound books can carry the same saying and still not be saying the same thing about how it reached them.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA6 · الکامل's one report, through أنس ؓ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينہ lights briefly.

**What happened:** In place of البدایہ's bank of chains, الکامل offers a single report through أنس
بن مالك ؓ. علي ؓ was ill, and أبو بكر ؓ and عمر ؓ, sitting with him, said they did not think he
would live. The Prophet ﷺ came in and looked into his face, and said three things about his death.
الکامل gives it and passes on without comment.

**The statement:**
> " لَنْ يَمُوتَ هَذَا الْآنَ، وَلَنْ يَمُوتَ حَتَّى يُمْلَأَ غَيْظًا، وَلَنْ يَمُوتَ إِلَّا مَقْتُولًا»
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۳۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1426
> *English:* "This one will not die now; he will not die until he is filled with anger; and he will not die except slain."

**عبرت:** What was said over a sickbed was carried for thirty years and only understood at the end.

**Hands-up?** no
