### TKO/E-QA7 · The خوارج tell him he is going to die
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** before رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

**What happened:** A party of the خوارج came to علي ؓ and told him to fear God, for he was going to
die. He answered by swearing that he would not die in that manner at all — he would be killed, by a
blow on this, which would dye this — and he pointed to his beard as he said it. He called it a
covenant covenanted and a decree decreed, and ended with the Qur'anic phrase about the one who
invents a lie. The reply refuses the threat without denying the death.

**The statement:**
> لا والذي فلق الحبة وبرأ النسمة، ولكن مقتول من ضربة على هذه تخضب هذه - وأشار بيده إلى لحيته - عهد معهود وقَضاء مقضي، وقد خاب من افترى.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3686
> *English:* "No — by Him who split the grain and created the soul, but rather killed, by a blow upon this, which shall dye this — and he pointed with his hand to his beard — a covenant covenanted and a decree decreed; and he who invents a lie has failed."

**عبرت:** Being warned of your death by your enemies changes nothing about the hour that was fixed for it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA8 · The most wretched of the former, and of the later
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Among the reports البدایہ collects is a short exchange with the Prophet ﷺ. He
asked علي ؓ who the most wretched of the former peoples was, and علي ؓ answered with the man of
ثمود who hamstrung the she-camel. Then he was asked about the most wretched of the later ones, and
he handed the question back — God and His Messenger know best. The answer he was given was one word.

**The statement:**
> قال رسول الله ﷺ لعلي: "من أشقى الأولين؟ " قال: عاقر الناقة، قال: "فمن أشقى الآخرين؟ " قال الله ورسوله أعلم، قال: "قاتلك".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3689
> *English:* "The Messenger of God ﷺ said to علي: who is the most wretched of the former peoples? He said: the hamstringer of the she-camel. He said: and who is the most wretched of the later ones? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: the one who kills you."

**عبرت:** The worst deed of an entire age can be done by one man, in one moment, at a mosque door.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA9 · The book weighs the chain in front of the reader
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH, in the book's own voice `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** البدایہ reports one more of these foretellings — that the ummah would deal
treacherously with him after the Prophet ﷺ — and then, instead of leaving it standing, quotes two
authorities on it in succession. البخاري is quoted on the narrator: in this particular hadith of
his there is something to look into. البيهقي is quoted saying only that it has come by another
chain, if that chain is preserved. The reader is shown the weighing and not merely the result.

**The statement:**
> قال البخاري (٢): ثعلبة بن يزيد الحمَّاني في حديثه هذا نظر.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3689
> *English:* "البخاري said: as for ثعلبة بن يزيد الحمّاني — in this hadith of his there is something to look into."

**عبرت:** Our books do not hand down every report at one strength, and they say which is which on the page.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA10 · «If it is sound» — a scholar refusing to overreach
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH, in the book's own voice `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Having narrated the same report, البيهقي is quoted a second time, now on what it
would mean. He does not say what it means. He says that if it is sound, it may be that what is
intended is the going-out of those who went out against him, and then his killing — and he inserts
«and God knows best» into the middle of his own sentence. That is two conditions placed on one
interpretation, in one line.

**The statement:**
> قال البيهقي: فإن صح فيحتمل أن يكون المراد به والله أعلم في خروج من خرج عليه ثم في قتله.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3689
> *English:* "البيهقي said: if it is sound, it may be that what is meant by it — and God knows best — is the going-out of those who went out against him, and then his killing."

**عبرت:** «If it is sound» is an entire discipline compressed into three words.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA11 · He will not name a successor
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** In these same reports the people put to him the question the room has already met
once, with عمر ؓ: will you not appoint a successor? His answer is the one they will recognise — he
leaves them as the Messenger of God ﷺ left them. They pressed him: and what will you say to your
Lord when you meet Him, having left us untended? He answered that he would say he had been made
successor over them for as long as God willed, and then taken, and that they were left to God.

**The statement:**
> فقالوا: يا أمير المؤمنين ألا تستخلف؟ فقال: لا ولكن أترككم كما ترككم رسول الله ﷺ.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3686
> *English:* "They said: Commander of the Faithful, will you not appoint a successor? He said: no, but I leave you as the Messenger of God ﷺ left you."

**عبرت:** Declining to appoint an heir is itself a position, and two of the four caliphs took it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA12 · «Let none be killed for me but my killer» — said in advance
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** In two of these chains the people around him offer, in advance, to deal with the
killer's people when the day comes. He forbids it before anything has happened, and he binds them by
God to it. He will give the same instruction again when he is actually lying wounded, which is the
strongest thing that can be said about it from any platform: the books have him saying it both
before and after. One killer, one life, and no one else.

**The statement:**
> فقال أنشدكم بالله أن يُقتل بي غير قاتلي.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3686
> *English:* "He said: I adjure you by God that none be killed for me but my killer."

**عبرت:** The limit on revenge was set before there was anything to take revenge for.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA13 · The last Friday sermon
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

**What happened:** البدایہ closes its chapter of foretellings with a sermon and one line of the
narrator's about it. The دعاء at the end of it asks for relief on both sides — that they be relieved
of him and he of them. Then the narrator adds a sentence that needs no commentary: he did not pray
the next Friday. That is the last Friday of a caliphate of nearly five years, and the book lets the
narrator's flat sentence carry the whole of it.

**The statement:**
> اللهم سئمتهم وسئموني، وكرهتهم وكرهوني، اللهم فأرحهم مني وأرحني منهم. قال: فما صلى الجمعة الأخرى حتى قتل ﵁ وأرضاه.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3689
> *English:* "O God, I have wearied of them and they of me, and I have come to dislike them and they me; O God, so relieve them of me and relieve me of them. He said: and he did not pray the next Friday before he was killed ؓ."

**عبرت:** Weariness of one's own people is a grief from which the righteous are not spared.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA14 · The same دعاء, in a harder wording
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The same supplication comes down a second time, independently, in the سیر, from
محمد ابن الحنفية through ابن سعد. There it is attached to something specific — his repeated attempts
to march out to الشام and the people's repeated refusal to move, four times over. But the wording is
not البدایہ's. البدایہ's asks for relief; this one asks for an exchange, and the second half of the
request is the harder of the two sentences. Show the difference; do not smooth it.

**The statement:**
> اللهم إني قد مللتهم وملوني، وأبغضتهم وأبغضوني، فأبدلني بهم خيرا منهم، وأبدلهم بي شرا مني.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1424
> *English:* "O God, I have wearied of them and they of me, and I have come to dislike them and they me; so give me in exchange for them someone better than them, and give them in exchange for me someone worse than me."

**عبرت:** A people that will not follow a good leader is asking, without knowing it, for the next one.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA15 · Three men, three cities, one night
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة, دمشق and الفسطاط light together.

**What happened:** Three men of the خوارج met and fell to talking about their dead at النهروان, and
asked one another what use there was in surviving them. Each then took a name. عبد الرحمن بن ملجم
took علي ؓ; البرك بن عبد الله التميمي took معاوية ؓ; عمرو بن بكر التميمي took عمرو بن العاص ؓ. They
bound themselves that no man would fall back from the man he had taken until he had killed him or
died in the attempt, and they fixed one night for all three — the seventeenth of رمضان — each in the
city where his man was.

**The statement:**
> فقال ابن ملجم: أمّا أنا فأكفيكم علي بن أبي طالب. وقال البرك: وأنا أكفيكم معاوية. وقال عمرو بن بكر: وأنا أكفيكم عمرو بن العاص. فتعاهدوا وتواثقوا أن لا ينكص رجل منهم عن صاحبه حتى يقتله أو يموت دونه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3690
> *English:* "ابن ملجم said: as for me, I will suffice you for علي بن أبي طالب. البرك said: and I will suffice you for معاوية. عمرو بن بكر said: and I will suffice you for عمرو بن العاص. So they covenanted and pledged one another that not one of them would fall back from the man he had taken until he killed him or died before him."

**عبرت:** Three men who believed themselves the only true Muslims left planned three killings in one sitting.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA16 · Why they said they were doing it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** النهروان lights, then goes dark.

**What happened:** The reason they gave one another is stated plainly in both books, and it is
النهروان. They mourned their own dead of that day, said those dead had feared no blame in God's
cause, and asked what was left worth staying alive for. Out of that came the sentence that is the
whole logic of the night — sell ourselves, reach the leaders of error, kill them, relieve the lands
of them, and take our brothers' blood-debt back from them. The men they had just called the leaders
of error included two Companions of the Prophet ﷺ.

**The statement:**
> فلو شرينا أنفسنا فأتينا أئمة الضلال فقتلناهم فأرحنا منهم [العباد و] البلاد، وأخذنا منهم ثأر إخواننا؟
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3690
> *English:* "So if we were to sell our own selves, and come to the leaders of error and kill them, and so relieve the [worshippers and the] lands of them, and take from them the blood-debt of our brothers?"

**عبرت:** The most dangerous sentence in this whole strand is the one in which men decide for themselves who the leaders of error are.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA17 · Who the killer had been before that night
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the caliphate of عمر ؓ, 13–23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مصر lights.

**What happened:** الذهبي gives the man a full notice, and it is not the notice a room expects. On
the authority of ابن يونس in his history of مصر, this was a man who had been present at the conquest
of مصر and had taken his plot of land there among the notables. He was one of those who had read the
Qur'an and studied فقه, and he had read the Qur'an with معاذ بن جبل ؓ himself. He was counted among
the worshippers.

**The statement:**
> شهد فتح مصر، واختط بها مع الأشراف، وكان ممن قرأ القرآن، والفقه … قرأ القرآن على معاذ بن جبل، وكان من العباد
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1427
> *English:* "He was present at the conquest of مصر, and took his plot there among the notables; he was one of those who had read the Qur'an and the فقه … he read the Qur'an under معاذ بن جبل, and he was among the devoted worshippers."

**عبرت:** Reciting the Qur'an and praying at night did not, by themselves, keep a man from the worst deed of his century.

**Hands-up?** Before I read this out — what kind of man would you expect the killer of علي ؓ to have been?

### TKO/E-QA18 · عمر ؓ moved his house next to the mosque
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the caliphate of عمر ؓ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الفسطاط lights.

**What happened:** The same notice carries a detail that is hard to hear. عمر ؓ is reported to have
written to عمرو بن العاص ؓ in مصر with an instruction about this man: bring his house close to the
mosque, so that he can teach the people the Qur'an and فقه. Room was made for him at his house, and
his neighbour is named. That is a caliph personally arranging a teaching post for the man who, some
thirty years later, would kill the fourth caliph.

**The statement:**

### TKO/E-QA55 · How old he was — four answers
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The books do not fix his age. الکامل lists sixty-three, then fifty-nine, then
sixty-five, then fifty-eight, and says the first is the soundest. البدایہ reaches sixty-three too,
from أبو جعفر الباقر, and notes that الواقدي and ابن جرير both held it correct, while a report from
جعفر الصادق gives fifty-eight, and other reports give sixty-five and sixty-eight. That a man of this
standing has four ages in the record is a fact about how the past reaches us.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ عُمُرُهُ ثَلَاثًا وَسِتِّينَ سَنَةً، وَقِيلَ: كَانَ عُمْرُهُ تَسْعًا وَخَمْسِينَ، وَقِيلَ: خَمْسًا وَسِتِّينَ، وَقِيلَ: ثَمَانِيًا وَخَمْسِينَ. وَالْأَوَّلُ أَصَحُّ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1435
> *English:* "And his age was sixty-three years; and it is said his age was fifty-nine; and it is said sixty-five; and it is said fifty-eight. And the first is the soundest."

**عبرت:** Where the sources give four ages and mark one as soundest, that is honesty, not confusion.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA56 · Four years and nine months
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the Line: a short bar beside the long ones.

**What happened:** البدایہ states the length of the caliphate in one clause: four years and nine
months. الکامل states exactly the same length by subtraction — five years less three months. Set
that beside the two years of أبو بكر ؓ, the ten of عمر ؓ and the twelve of عثمان ؓ, and the room can
see with its eyes what kind of years these had been.

**The statement:**
> وكانت خلافته أربع سنين وتسعة أشهر.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3696
> *English:* "And his caliphate was four years and nine months."

**عبرت:** The shortest of the four caliphates was the one spent almost entirely inside the fitna.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA57 · The bargain the killer offered, and the answer he got
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When علي ؓ died, الحسن ؓ sent for the killer, and the man tried to trade. He had
given God a covenant at the الحطيم to kill both علي ؓ and معاوية ؓ, or die in the attempt; let me go
to the second, and if I fail, or succeed and survive, God is my surety that I will come back and put
my hand in yours. The answer was six words: no, by God — not until you see the Fire. He was brought
forward and killed, and the people then wrapped the body in matting and burned it.

**The statement:**
> فقال له الحسن: كلا والله حتى تعاين النار، ثم قدمه فقتله ثم أخذه الناس فأدرجوه في بواري ثم أحرقوه بالنار
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3696
> *English:* "الحسن said to him: no, by God — not until you see the Fire. Then he brought him forward and killed him; then the people took him, wrapped him in matting, and burned him with fire."

**عبرت:** A man who has bound himself by a covenant to kill will offer the same covenant to his victim's son.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA58 · «And it is said» — the version with mutilation
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** البدایہ records a second account of the execution, again under «and it is said»,
in which the hands and the feet were cut off and the eyes put out first, and the man went on reciting
سورة العلق through it. When they came to cut out his tongue he was distressed, and said that he
feared an hour might pass over him in which he did not remember God. The page closes the account with
«and God knows best». It is recorded here so that nobody researches it twice; it is not planned for
the hall, because the instruction the dead man gave forbade exactly this.

**The statement:**
> ثم جاؤوا ليقطعوا لسانه فجزع وقال: إني أخشى أن تمر عليَّ ساعة لا أذكر الله فيها
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3696
> *English:* "Then they came to cut out his tongue, and he was distressed and said: I fear that an hour may pass over me in which I do not remember God."

**عبرت:** A report that contradicts the dying man's own instruction is carried by the book under «it is said», and that is where it stays.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA59 · The same night, in دمشق
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 17 رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** دمشق lights beside الكوفة.

**What happened:** The second of the three men kept the appointment. As معاوية ؓ came out for the
dawn prayer that same morning, البرك بن عبد الله rushed him with a sword — some say a poisoned dagger
— and the blow fell in his hip. He was seized. He told معاوية ؓ he had news to give him: my brother
has killed علي بن أبي طالب this night. Perhaps he did not manage it, معاوية ؓ said. No — علي has no
guard with him. He was ordered killed.

**The statement:**
> فإنه حمل عليه وهو خارج إلى صلاة الفجر في هذا (٢) اليوم فضربه بالسيف، وقيل بخنجر مسموم، فجاءت الضربة في وركه فجرحت أليته
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3694
> *English:* "He rushed at him as he was going out to the dawn prayer on that day and struck him with a sword — and it is said, with a poisoned dagger — and the blow came in his hip and wounded it."

**عبرت:** The same hour, in two cities eight hundred miles apart, two Companions were struck at the door of the dawn prayer.

**Hands-up?** Did the other two men keep the appointment that night?

### TKO/E-QA60 · The physician's two choices
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 17 رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ sent for a physician, whom الکامل names السَّاعِدِيّ and البدایہ calls only
the physician. The man gave him two options and no third: I heat an iron and set it where the sword
went, or I give you a draught that will cure you and end your having children — for your wound is
poisoned. He answered that he had no endurance for the fire, and that as for children, يزيد and عبد
الله were enough to keep his eye cool. He drank it, and recovered, and no child was born to him
afterwards.

**The statement:**
> اخْتَرْ إِمَّا أَنْ أُحْمِيَ حَدِيدَةً فَأَضَعُهَا مَوْضِعَ السَّيْفِ، وَإِمَّا أَنْ أَسْقِيَكَ شَرْبَةً تَقْطَعُ مِنْكَ الْوَلَدَ وَتَبْرَأُ مِنْهَا، فَإِنَّ ضَرْبَتَكَ مَسْمُومَةٌ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1431
> *English:* "Choose: either I heat an iron and place it where the sword struck, or I give you a draught which will cut off offspring from you and by which you will be cured — for your wound is poisoned."

**عبرت:** One night's work by one man reached into a household for the rest of a lifetime.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA61 · What that one night left behind in every mosque
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** from 40 AH onward `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** دمشق, then everywhere.

**What happened:** Out of that morning came a permanent change in how a Muslim ruler prayed in
public. معاوية ؓ ordered the مقصورات — the screened enclosure in the mosque — and a night-watch, and
guards standing at his head while he was in prostration. الکامل says plainly that he was the first
to do it in Islam. البدایہ reports the same and gives the same reason. An assassination at a mosque
door in الكوفة changed the architecture of mosques in الشام.

**The statement:**
> وَأَمَرَ مُعَاوِيَةُ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ بِالْمَقْصُوَرَاتِ، وَحَرَسِ اللَّيْلِ، وَقِيَامِ الشُّرَطِ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ إِذَا سَجَدَ، وَهُوَ أَوَّلُ مَنْ عَمِلَهَا فِي الْإِسْلَامِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1432
> *English:* "And معاوية ordered at that point the screened enclosures, and the night-watch, and the standing of the guard at his head when he prostrated — and he was the first to institute that in Islam."

**عبرت:** A ruler who can no longer pray unguarded among his people has already lost something that no guard returns.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA62 · «You wanted me, and God wanted خارجة»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 17 رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الفسطاط lights.

**What happened:** The third man sat waiting for عمرو بن العاص ؓ that night, and عمرو ؓ did not come
out: he had a pain in his stomach. His chief of police went out in his place to lead the people in
the prayer, and was struck down for him and killed. When the man was brought in and understood what
he had done, the sentence that was spoken over him became a proverb that Arabs used for centuries
afterwards. البدایہ reports two versions of who said it — the assassin, or عمرو ؓ himself.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ عَمْرٌو: أَرَدْتَنِي وَأَرَادَ اللَّهُ خَارِجَةَ. فَقَدَّمَهُ عَمْرٌو فَقَتَلَهُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1432
> *English:* "عمرو said: you wanted me, and God wanted خارجة. Then عمرو had him brought forward and killed."

**عبرت:** A stomach-ache decided which of two men was alive at sunrise.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA63 · Who خارجة was — and the books do not agree
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 17 رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The man who died in another man's place is named differently in our books.
البدایہ and الکامل call him خارجة بن أبي حبيبة, of بني عامر بن لؤي, chief of عمرو ؓ's police. The سیر
gives a different father and a fuller notice: خارجة بن حذافة بن غانم, who had صحبة, was present at
the conquest of مصر, commanded a quarter of the reinforcements عمر ؓ sent, and was over the police of
مصر — and it says plainly that the خارجي killed him in مصر thinking he was عمرو.

**The statement:**
> قال ابن ماكولا: له صحبة، وشهد فتح مصر … وكان على شرطة مصر في خلافة عمر، وفي خلافة معاوية، قتله عمرو بن بكير الخارجي بمصر
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1426
> *English:* "ابن ماكولا said: he had companionship of the Prophet ﷺ, and was present at the conquest of مصر … and he was over the police of مصر in the caliphate of عمر and in the caliphate of معاوية; عمرو بن بكير the خارجي killed him in مصر."

**عبرت:** The man killed by mistake that night had his own thirty years of service, and the books give them to him.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA64 · الذهبي's ruling, refusing both extremes
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the later judgement of the scholars `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي sets out where أهل السنة stand on the killer, and he does it by refusing two
positions at once — the خوارج, who called him the best of the ummah, and those at the other extreme
who make him the most wretched creature in the hereafter. He then groups him with a list of killers:
the killer of عثمان ؓ, of الزبير ؓ, of طلحة ؓ, of سعيد بن جبير رحمہ اللہ, of عمار ؓ, of خارجة, of
الحسين ؓ. Of all of these, he writes, we disown them and hate them for God's sake — and we commit
their affairs to God.

**The statement:**
> وحكمه حكم قاتل عثمان، وقاتل الزبير، وقاتل طلحة، وقاتل سعيد بن جبير، وقاتل عمار، وقاتل خارجة، وقاتل الحسين، فكل هؤلاء نبرأ منهم ونبغضهم في الله، ونكل أمورهم إلى الله عز وجل.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۸۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1428
> *English:* "And his ruling is the ruling of the killer of عثمان, the killer of الزبير, the killer of طلحة, the killer of سعيد بن جبير, the killer of عمار, the killer of خارجة, and the killer of الحسين — all of these we disown and hate for God's sake, and we commit their affairs to God, Mighty and Majestic."

**عبرت:** Disowning a deed and leaving the doer's final account to God are two separate acts, and the ʿulamā did both.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA65 · A poet praised the killer, and the ummah answered him
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the generation of the تابعين `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A خارجي poet of the following generation wrote two lines praising the blow as the
act of a God-fearing man. Both books carry them — and الکامل carries, straight after, the long
answer of بكر بن حماد التاهرتي, which takes the praise apart line by line and then throws the poet's
own words back at him with one noun changed. The answer opens by telling the killer what he actually
pulled down.

**The statement:**
> قُلْ لِابْنِ مُلْجَمَ وَالْأَقْدَارُ غَالِبَةٌ ... هَدَمْتَ لِلدِّينِ وَالْإِسْلَامِ أَرْكَانَا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1434
> *English:* "Say to ابن ملجم — and the decrees prevail — you have pulled down pillars of the religion and of Islam."

**عبرت:** The ummah did not leave the praise of a murderer unanswered, and the answer is in the same books as the praise.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA67 · What he left, and a book grading its own report
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The same address ends with the estate. By God, he left neither gold nor silver
except seven or eight hundred, which he had set aside — الکامل says for a servant-girl, البدایہ says
for a servant. Then البدایہ does the thing that makes it a history book: having reported it through
its own chain, it turns round and grades it — this is very strange, and there is something objected
to in it. A second chain of the same address, through أحمد and without the money at all, is graded
حسن in the printed edition's footnote.

**The statement:**
> والله ما ترك صفراء ولا بيضاء إلا ثمانمئة أو سبعمئة أرصدها لخادم … وهذا غريب جدًّا وفيه نكارة، والله أعلم.

> *English:* "By God, he left neither gold nor silver, except eight hundred or seven hundred which he had set aside for a servant … And this is very strange, and in it is something objected to, and God knows best."

**عبرت:** A historian who narrates a report and then grades it down has told you two things, and the second is the more useful.

**Hands-up?** no

### TKO/E-QA68 · The pearl on his treasurer's daughter
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** أبو رافع, the freedman of the Messenger of God ﷺ, was his treasurer over بيت
المال. علي ؓ came in one day and saw أبو رافع's daughter adorned, and on her a pearl he recognised
as belonging to the treasury. He asked where she got it, and said he would cut off her hand. أبو
رافع, seeing he was in earnest, said at once that he had adorned her with it himself. علي ؓ's answer
was about his own house: when he married فاطمة ؓ he had no bedding but a ram's skin, slept on it at
night and fed his camel on it by day.

> فَرَأَى عَلَيْهَا لُؤْلُؤَةً كَانَ عَرَفَهَا لِبَيْتِ الْمَالِ، فَقَالَ: مِنْ أَيْنَ لَهَا هَذِهِ؟ لَأَقْطَعَنَّ يَدَهَا!

> *English:* "And he saw upon her a pearl which he recognised as belonging to the بيت المال, and he said: from where did she get this? I will cut off her hand!"

**عبرت:** A treasury is guarded first against the people closest to the man who guards it.

### TKO/E-QA69 · One loaf, cut into seven, and then a lot drawn
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أصبهان, then الكوفة.

**عبرت:** Fairness that will divide a single loaf is fairness that can be trusted with a province's revenue.

### TKO/E-QA71 · Two skins of honey, priced at three dirhams
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** His governor over أصبهان came back with money and skins of honey and ghee. أم
كلثوم بنت علي ؓ sent to the governor asking for some, and he sent her one skin of each. Next day the

governor until he told him, then sent to his daughter and took the two skins back — and, seeing they

### TKO/E-QA72 · The caliph loses a lawsuit to a Christian
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after صفين, 37–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة, the court of شريح.

**What happened:** He found a coat of mail of his in the hands of a Christian man and brought him
before his own judge, شريح — and sat down beside the man, saying that had his opponent been a Muslim
he would have made himself level with him in the same way. He claimed the mail. The Christian said it
was his own. شريح asked the caliph for his evidence; he had none, and he laughed. The Christian took
the mail and walked off — then came back, said that these are the judgements of prophets, and
accepted Islam.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ شُرَيْحٌ لَعَلِيٍّ: أَلَكَ بَيِّنَةٌ؟ قَالَ: لَا - وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ - فَأَخَذَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ الدِّرْعَ وَمَشَى يَسِيرًا، ثُمَّ عَادَ وَقَالَ: أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ هَذِهِ أَحْكَامُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1439
> *English:* "شريح said to علي: have you evidence? He said: no — and he was laughing. So the Christian took the coat of mail and walked a little way, then came back and said: I bear witness that these are the judgements of the prophets."

**عبرت:** A ruler who can lose a case in his own court has built something no army can.

**Hands-up?** What would have happened, in most of the world in that century, to a man who took a ruler to court?

---

### TKO/E-QA73 · «The most abstinent of people in this world»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the caliphate of عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمہ اللہ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Two generations later, in the presence of عمر بن عبد العزيز رحمہ اللہ, people were
talking about the ascetics — who among them had renounced the most. He gave his answer in one
sentence and named a caliph. الکامل places this judgement at the end of the whole file of reports
about his manner of living, as the summing-up of them.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: أَزْهَدُ النَّاسِ فِي الدُّنْيَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1439
> *English:* "عمر said: the most abstinent of people in this world was علي بن أبي طالب."

**عبرت:** The verdict on how a man lived was given by people who had nothing to gain from giving it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA74 · «He never laid one brick upon another»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** سفيان's summary of his estate is three parallel clauses and a detail. He never laid
a baked brick upon a baked brick, nor a mud brick upon a mud brick, nor a reed upon a reed — and his
grain used to be brought to him from المدينہ in a sack. الکامل adds that he would seal the sack of
barley-flour he ate from, saying he did not like anything to enter his stomach that he did not know
about.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّ عَلِيًّا لَمْ يَبْنِ آجُرَّةً عَلَى آجُرَّةٍ، وَلَا لَبِنَةً عَلَى لَبِنَةٍ، وَلَا قَصَبَةً عَلَى قَصَبَةٍ، وَإِنْ كَانَ لَيُؤْتَى بِحُبُوبِهِ مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ فِي جِرَابٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1439
> *English:* "علي never built a baked brick upon a baked brick, nor a mud brick upon a mud brick, nor a reed upon a reed; and his grain used to be brought to him from المدينہ in a sack."

**عبرت:** Five years of ruling العراق left no building behind with his name on it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA75 · What عمر ؓ said about him in the شورى
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينہ.

**What happened:** الکامل reaches back to the شورى of 23 AH for one exchange. When the six had left
the wounded عمر ؓ, he said that if they gave the office to الأجلح he would take them along the road.
His son عبد الله asked the obvious question — then what stops you appointing him? The answer was
four words long: I dislike to carry it living and dead.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: إِنْ يُوَلُّوهَا الْأَجْلَحَ يَسْلُكُ بِهِمُ الطَّرِيقَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ ابْنُهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: فَمَا يَمْنَعُكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (مِنْ تَوْلِيَتِهِ) ؟ قَالَ: أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَتَحَمَّلَهَا حَيًّا وَمَيِّتًا.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1438
> *English:* "He said: if they give it to الأجلح, he will take them along the road. His son عبد الله said to him: then what prevents you, Commander of the Faithful, (from appointing him)? He said: I dislike to bear it both living and dead."

**عبرت:** A man may hold a high opinion of someone and still refuse to make the choice on the ummah's behalf.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA76 · What he looked like, and how he carried himself
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الکامل gives a full physical description — dark-complexioned, with large heavy
eyes, thick-bearded, bald at the front, closer to short than tall, with the muscle of the arm and of
the leg thick and the wrist and ankle fine. Then it closes the description with three details that
are not about the body at all: he was among the best-looking of people, he never dyed his grey, and
he smiled a great deal.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ مِنْ أَحْسَنِ النَّاسِ وَجْهًا، وَلَا يُغَيِّرُ شَيْبَهُ، كَثِيرَ التَّبَسُّمِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1436
> *English:* "And he was among the best of people in face, and he did not change his grey hair, and he smiled much."

**عبرت:** The books remembered that the man at the centre of five years of war smiled a great deal.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA77 · The first caliph both of whose parents were هاشمي
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الکامل notes one fact of lineage that is easy to state and easy to remember. He was
the first caliph whose father and mother were both of بنو هاشم — his father أبو طالب بن عبد المطلب,
his mother فاطمة بنت أسد بن هاشم. And, the book adds, down to the time of its own writing only two
others held the office with both parents هاشمي: his son الحسن ؓ, and محمد الأمين.

**The statement:**
> وَهُوَ أَوَّلُ خَلِيفَةٍ، أَبَوَاهُ هَاشِمِيَّانِ، وَلَمْ يَلِ الْخِلَافَةَ إِلَى وَقْتِنَا هَذَا مَنْ أَبَوَاهُ هَاشِمِيَّانِ غَيْرُهُ، وَغَيْرُ الْحَسَنِ وَلَدِهِ، وَمُحَمَّدٍ الْأَمِينِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1436
> *English:* "And he is the first caliph both of whose parents were هاشمي; and down to our own time none has held the caliphate both of whose parents were هاشمي except him, and his son الحسن, and محمد الأمين."

**عبرت:** A fact of descent is easy to check and easy to state, which is why the books state it exactly.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA78 · Fourteen sons and seventeen daughters
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Both books count his children the same way, which after so many disagreements is
worth saying aloud: fourteen sons and seventeen daughters. Both also agree on where the line
continued — through five of them only: الحسن ؓ, الحسين ؓ, محمد ابن الحنفية, العباس, and عمر. البدایہ
attributes its count to ابن جرير and the line of descent to الواقدي.

**The statement:**
> فَجَمِيعُ وَلَدِهِ أَرْبَعَةُ عَشَرَ ذَكَرًا، وَسَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ امْرَأَةً، وَكَانَ النَّسْلُ مِنْهُمْ لِلْحَسَنِ، وَالْحُسَيْنِ، وَمُحَمَّدِ ابْنِ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ، وَالْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ الْكِلَابِيَّةِ، وَعُمَرَ بْنِ التَّغْلِبِيَّةِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۴۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1437
> *English:* "So the whole of his children were fourteen males and seventeen females; and the line among them continued through الحسن, الحسين, محمد ابن الحنفية, العباس son of the كلابية, and عمر son of the تغلبية."

**عبرت:** Where two books agree exactly on a number, that is worth saying, because they so often do not.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA79 · The بيعة of الحسن ؓ, in the same year
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** In the same year, after his father's killing, الحسن ؓ was given the بيعة. The
first man to give it was قيس بن سعد الأنصاري ؓ, who said: stretch out your hand, I give you the
pledge on the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet, and on fighting those who make lawful what
is forbidden. الحسن ؓ took the first two and left the third — on the Book of God and the Sunnah of
His Messenger, for those two cover every condition. The people then gave the pledge.

**The statement:**
> وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ بَايَعَهُ قَيْسُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ الْأَنْصَارِيُّ، وَقَالَ لَهُ: ابْسُطْ يَدَكَ أُبَايِعْكَ عَلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَسُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ، وَقِتَالِ الْمُحِلِّينَ. فَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ: عَلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَسُنَّةِ رَسُولِهِ فَإِنَّهُمَا يَأْتِيَانِ عَلَى كُلِّ شَرْطٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1440
> *English:* "And the first to give him the pledge was قيس بن سعد الأنصاري, who said to him: stretch out your hand, I pledge you on the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet, and on fighting those who make lawful what God forbade. الحسن said: on the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger — for those two come over every condition."

**عبرت:** The first sentence of the new caliphate declined to write war into the pledge.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TKO/E-QA80 · Forty nights later
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** شوال 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الکامل closes the year with its obituaries, and the first of them is الأشعث بن قيس
الكندي, who died forty nights after the killing, and over whom الحسن ؓ prayed. The سیر, elsewhere and
for its own reasons, records that the killer had spent his last night in conversation with الأشعث in
his mosque. Neither book joins those two facts to each other. Neither may we: the card exists so
that the material is on the record and so that no one re-researches it, not so that an inference is
drawn from it.

**The statement:**
> وَفِيهَا مَاتَ الْأَشْعَثُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ الْكِنْدِيُّ بَعْدَ قَتْلِ عَلِيٍّ بِأَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً، وَصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1440
> *English:* "And in it died الأشعث بن قيس الكندي, forty nights after the killing of علي; and there prayed over him…"

**عبرت:** Two facts standing next to each other on the calendar are not, by themselves, one fact.

**Hands-up?** no

## الحسن ؓ, the handover, and عام الجماعة

*Source note: [`the-caliphate-of-hasan-and-the-year-of-unity.md`](../docs/research/the-caliphate-of-hasan-and-the-year-of-unity.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TCO/E-HS1 · علي ؓ refuses to name a successor
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

**What happened:** ابن كثير begins the chapter on الحسن ؓ's caliphate by reaching back one page, to علي ؓ lying struck by the blow of ابن ملجم. The men around him ask him to name the man who will come after him. He will not. He tells them he leaves them exactly as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left them, without an appointment, and that if Allah wills good for them He will gather them upon the best of them, as He gathered them once before. Everything that follows this evening happens because nothing was settled in advance.

**The statement:**
> قد ذكرنا أن عليًا ﵁ لما ضربه ابن ملجم قالوا له: استخلف يا أمير المؤمنين. فقال: لا ولكن أدعكم كما ترككم رسول الله ﷺ - يعني بغير استخلاف - فإن يرد الله بكم خيرًا يجمعكم (١) على خيركم كما جمعكم على خيركم بعد رسول الله ﷺ.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3761
> *English:* "We have already mentioned that when Ibn Muljam struck ʿAlī ؓ they said to him: appoint a successor, Commander of the Believers. He said: No — rather I leave you as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left you — meaning, without appointing a successor. If Allah wills good for you He will gather you upon the best of you, as He gathered you upon the best of you after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

**عبرت:** A man who has the power to decide the future may still judge that the community's own choosing is safer than his choosing for it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCO/E-HS2 · The first man to come forward at الكوفة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** The burial is finished and the Muslims of الكوفة are standing without a commander. One man walks out of the crowd first: قيس بن سعد بن عبادة ؓ of the Anṣār, son of the chief of الخزرج. He does not make a speech. He asks الحسن ؓ to stretch out his hand, and he names the terms he is giving allegiance upon — the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ.

**The statement:**
> كان أول من تقدم إلى الحسن بن علي ﵁ قيس بن سعد بن عبادة فقال له: ابسط يدك أبايعك
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3762
> *English:* "The first to come forward to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ؓ was Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah. He said to him: stretch out your hand, I give you allegiance."

**عبرت:** A community in shock is held together by whoever is willing to move first, in the open, and say what he is committing to.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCO/E-HS3 · He said nothing, and the people followed
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** The most striking detail in the report is what الحسن ؓ did not do. He gave no answer at all. قيس ؓ took his hand while he was silent, and the people of الكوفة came forward behind قيس ؓ and did the same. ابن كثير fixes the day precisely: it was the day علي ؓ died. From that day the command was his.

**The statement:**
> فسكت الحسن فبايعه ثم بايعه الناس بعده، وكان ذلك يوم مات علي
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3762
> *English:* "Al-Ḥasan was silent, so he took his allegiance, and the people gave allegiance after him. That was on the day ʿAlī died."

**عبرت:** A man may be handed an office he never asked for, and be answerable for it from that same hour.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCO/E-HS4 · Three reports about the day علي ؓ died
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير will not settle the date, and he says so on the page. One report has علي ؓ dying on the very day he was struck, a Friday, the seventeenth of رمضان of the year forty. A second has him dying two days after the blow. A third puts his death in the last ten days of رمضان. The historian records all three and moves on.

**The statement:**
> وكان موته يوم ضرب على قول وهو يوم الجمعة السابع عشر من رمضان سنة أربعين، وقيل إنما مات بعد الطعنة (٢) بيومين، وقيل مات في العشر الأخير من رمضان، ومن يومئذ ولي الحسن بن علي
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3762
> *English:* "His death, on one report, was the day he was struck — a Friday, the seventeenth of Ramaḍān of the year forty; and it is said he died two days after the blow; and it is said he died in the last ten days of Ramaḍān. From that day al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī held the command."

**عبرت:** An honest historian will leave three readings standing rather than manufacture one.

**Hands-up?** Who expects a history book to give you exactly one date?

---

### TCO/E-HS5 · The condition he attached to his own بيعة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** Before he would accept anybody's allegiance, الحسن ؓ stated a condition of his own and swore to it. He would not take their hands except upon what he was about to say. They asked what it was. He told them: you make peace with whoever I make peace with, and you fight whoever I fight. This is the hinge of the whole evening — the possibility of a settlement was inside the allegiance from the first day, and it was stated in front of everybody.

**The statement:**
> قَالُوا: مَا هُوَ؟ قَالَ: تُسَالِمُوْنَ مَنْ سَالَمْتُ، وَتُحَارِبُوْنَ مَنْ حَارَبْتُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2874
> *English:* "They said: what is it? He said: you make peace with whomever I make peace, and you fight whomever I fight."

**عبرت:** A man who states his condition at the beginning owes nobody an apology when he acts on it at the end.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCO/E-HS6 · An assembly the like of which had not been heard of
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** The gathering that came to give him allegiance was enormous, and ابن كثير says he knows of nothing like it. The editor's manuscript supplement on the page gives the reason in plain words: the people inclined toward الحسن ؓ with an overwhelming inclination, in love and in obedience, because he was the son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

**The statement:**
> فاجتمعوا اجتماعًا عظيمًا لم يسمع بمثله [لأن الناس مالوا إلى الحسن ميلًا عظيمًا محبة وطاعة إذ هو ابن بنت رسول الله ﷺ وريحانته]
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3762
> *English:* "They assembled in a great assembly the like of which had not been heard of [because the people inclined to al-Ḥasan with a great inclining, in love and obedience, since he is the son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his sweet basil]."

**عبرت:** The size of a crowd tells you what it loves; it does not tell you what it will do under pressure.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCO/E-HS7 · It was never in his intention to fight
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير states, as his own judgement in the running text and in one short clause, what الحسن ؓ wanted from the start. He did not intend to fight anybody. The men around him overbore him. Everything the army then does — the march, the camp, the vanguard — is done over the top of its own commander's opinion.

**The statement:**
> ولم يكن في نية الحسن أن يقاتل أحدًا، ولكن غلبوه على رأيه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3762
> *English:* "It was not in al-Ḥasan's intention to fight anyone; but they overbore him in his opinion."

**عبرت:** A man can hold the title and still be carried along by the people he is supposed to be leading.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCO/E-HS8 · Forty thousand who had sworn unto death
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** أذربيجان lights; الكوفة stays lit.

**What happened:** ابن الأثیر opens the year by telling you what force was standing ready. Forty thousand men of علي ؓ's army had given him allegiance unto death, once what he had been telling them about the people of الشام became clear to them. He was equipping himself to march when he was killed. ابن الأثیر ends the sentence not with a military assessment but with a theological one: when Allah wills a thing there is no turning it back.

**The statement:**
> كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلِيٌّ قَدْ بَايَعَهُ أَرْبَعُونَ أَلْفًا مِنْ عَسْكَرِهِ عَلَى الْمَوْتِ لَمَّا ظَهَرَ مَا كَانَ يُخْبِرُهُمْ بِهِ عَنْ أَهْلِ الشَّامِ، فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَتَجَهَّزُ لِلْمَسِيرِ قُتِلَ، عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَمْرًا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1445
> *English:* "Forty thousand of his army had given the Commander of the Believers ʿAlī allegiance unto death, when what he used to tell them about the people of Syria became clear. And while he was equipping himself to march, he was killed — peace be upon him — and when Allah wills a thing there is no turning it back."

**عبرت:** An army raised for one man's plan does not pass automatically to the man who comes after him.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS9 · The vanguard: twelve thousand, and a competing report
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** الكوفة → المدائن, the road north.

**What happened:** البدایہ gives the sequence plainly. قيس بن سعد ؓ was holding أذربيجان with forty thousand fighting men; when علي ؓ died he pressed hard for the march on الشام; الحسن ؓ removed him from أذربيجان, put عبيد الله بن عباس over it, and gave قيس ؓ the vanguard of twelve thousand, following behind with the main body. الکامل gives the same twelve thousand and then, in the editor's round brackets, a different arrangement altogether: that عبد الله بن عباس had the vanguard and قيس ؓ led his scouts.

**The statement:**
> وَجَعَلَ قَيْسَ بْنَ سَعْدِ بْنِ عُبَادَةَ الْأَنْصَارِيَّ عَلَى مُقَدِّمَتِهِ فِي اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ أَلْفًا، (وَقِيلَ بَلْ كَانَ الْحَسَنُ قَدْ جَعَلَ عَلَى مُقَدِّمَتِهِ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، فَجَعَلَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ عَلَى مُقَدِّمَتِهِ فِي الطَّلَائِعِ قَيْسَ بْنَ سَعْدِ بْنِ عُبَادَةَ)
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1445
> *English:* "And he put Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah al-Anṣārī over his vanguard with twelve thousand. (And it is said rather that al-Ḥasan had put ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās over his vanguard, and ʿAbd Allāh put Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah over his own vanguard among the scouts.)"

**عبرت:** Two careful books can preserve two different chains of command for the same week, and an honest reader keeps both.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS10 · Where معاوية ؓ was — and the five-day march
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** مسكن and جسر منبج both marked.

**What happened:** The two chronicles place معاوية ؓ at مسكن, having come out with the people of الشام. سیر places him instead at جسر منبج, and then tells you he covered the distance from جسر منبج to مسكن in five days. These are not contradictions to be merged: they are one advance seen at two stages, and they are kept side by side.

**The statement:**
> فَأَقْبَلَ مِنْ جِسْرِ مَنْبِجٍ إِلَى مَسْكَنَ فِي خَمْسَةِ أَيَّامٍ، فَسَلَّمَ إِلَيْهِ الحَسَنُ الأَمْرَ، وَبَايَعَهُ حَتَّى قَدِمَا الكُوْفَةَ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2872
> *English:* "So he came on from Jisr Manbij to Maskin in five days; and al-Ḥasan handed the command over to him and gave him allegiance, until the two of them came to al-Kūfah."

**عبرت:** Distance on a map is the quiet fact behind every decision a commander makes in a hurry.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS11 · The false cry in the camp at المدائن
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدائن lights.

**What happened:** الحسن ؓ has halted at المدائن and is camped outside the town. A crier raises a shout among the men: قيس بن سعد has been killed. It was not true. The camp goes off like a struck match. The men plunder one another's belongings, then plunder their own commander's pavilion, and finally wrench out from under him the rug he is sitting on.

**The statement:**
> فبينما هو في المدائن معسكرًا بظاهرها، إذ صرخ في الناس (٧) صارخ: ألا إن قيس بن سعد بن عبادة قد قتل، فثار الناس فانتهبوا أمتعة بعضهم (٨) بعضًا حتى انتهبوا سرادق الحسن، حتى نازعوه بساطًا كان جالسًا عليه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3762
> *English:* "And while he was encamped outside al-Madāʾin, a crier cried out among the people: Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah has been killed! So the people surged and plundered one another's goods, until they plundered al-Ḥasan's own pavilion — until they wrenched from under him a rug he was sitting upon."

**عبرت:** One sentence, shouted by one man, can undo an army that no enemy has yet touched.

**Hands-up?** Has anyone here seen a rumour travel faster than the truth?

### TCO/E-HS12 · «فَانْفِرُوا» — the cry as الکامل heard it
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدائن.

**What happened:** ابن الأثیر records the same moment with one extra word in the shout. The crier does not only announce a death; he gives an order — rush out. And ابن الأثیر adds what the night did to الحسن ؓ inwardly: from it his dislike of these men grew, and his dread of them with it.

**The statement:**
> نَادَى مُنَادٍ فِي الْعَسْكَرِ: أَلَا إِنَّ قَيْسَ بْنَ سَعْدٍ قُتِلَ فَانْفِرُوا. فَنَفَرُوا بِسُرَادِقِ الْحَسَنِ، فَنَهَبُوا مَتَاعَهُ حَتَّى نَازَعُوهُ بِسَاطًا كَانَ تَحْتَهُ، فَازْدَادَ لَهُمْ بُغْضًا وَمِنْهُمْ ذُعْرًا
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1445
> *English:* "A crier cried in the camp: Qays ibn Saʿd has been killed, so rush out! And they rushed upon al-Ḥasan's pavilion and plundered his goods, until they wrenched from under him a rug that was beneath him — so he increased in hatred of them and in dread of them."

**عبرت:** What a leader learns about his followers in one hour can settle what he does with them for a year.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS13 · He was stabbed at المدائن — and the books do not agree
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدائن.

**What happened:** In the same disorder الحسن ؓ was stabbed by one of his own side. Beyond that bare fact our books settle nothing. البدایہ has him stabbed as he mounted. سیر, in one notice, says a man of بنو أسد stabbed him in the back with a poisoned dagger. In a second notice سیر names the attacker ابن أُقيصر. In a third it is a man of the خوارج, whom the people then fell on and killed. A fourth report has him stabbed while he was praying, months earlier. Nothing but "he was stabbed at المدائن" can be stated with confidence.

**The statement:**
> فَشَدَّ النَّاسُ عَلَى حُجْرَةِ الحَسَنِ، فَنَهَبُوْهَا حَتَّى انْتُهِبَتْ بُسطُهُ، وَأَخَذُوا رِدَاءهُ، وَطَعَنَهُ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي أَسَدٍ فِي ظَهرِهِ بِخِنْجَرٍ مَسْمُوْمٍ فِي أَلْيَتِه
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2872
> *English:* "The people fell upon al-Ḥasan's chamber and plundered it, until his rugs were plundered and they took his cloak; and a man of Banū Asad stabbed him in his back with a poisoned dagger, in his buttock."

**عبرت:** Where the sources give four names for one attacker, the honest thing is to name none.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS14 · The خوارج attacker, killed on the spot
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدائن.

**What happened:** سیر's shortest telling of the same scene comes from عوانة بن الحكم and puts the twelve thousand and the false cry in a single breath. In this version the man who leapt on الحسن ؓ with the dagger was of the خوارج, and the men of the camp fell on him and killed him where he stood. And then the sentence that changes everything: so الحسن ؓ wrote to معاوية ؓ about a peace.

> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2871
> *English:* "So the people plundered al-Ḥasan's pavilion, and a man of the Khawārij leapt upon him and stabbed him with the dagger; and the people leapt upon that man and killed him."

**عبرت:** The letter that ended the fighting was written by a man who had just been stabbed by his own army.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS15 · «فَيَزعُمُوْنَ» — الذهبي holds a report at arm's length
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A further report in سیر has the wound falling in his hip and leaves him ill of it for months. الذهبي does not narrate this flatly; he introduces it with the verb "they claim". That single word is the historian marking his own distance from what he is about to transmit, on the page, in front of the reader.

**The statement:**
> فَيَزعُمُوْنَ أَنَّ الطَّعْنَةَ وَقَعَتْ فِي وَرِكِهِ، فَمَرِضَ مِنْهَا أَشهُراً
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2878
> *English:* "And they claim the thrust fell in his hip, and he was ill of it for months."

**عبرت:** One verb can carry a scholar's whole verdict on a report.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS16 · The White Palace, and a man rebuking his own camp
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدائن — the White Palace of Kisrā.

**What happened:** Wounded, plundered by his own men, الحسن ؓ withdrew into the White Palace of Kisrā at المدائن. And there he said the sentence that gives you the whole night in one line: the curse of Allah be upon you, people of a town — I knew there was no good in you; yesterday you killed my father, and today you do this to me. This is safe to tell in full: it is a commander rebuking his own camp, and it charges no Companion with anything.

**The statement:**
> فَتحوَّلَ، وَنَزَلَ قَصرَ كِسْرَى الأَبْيَضَ، وَقَالَ: عَلَيْكُم لَعنَةُ اللهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ قَرْيَةٍ، قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنْ لاَ خَيرَ فِيْكُم، قَتلتُم أَبِي بِالأَمسِ، وَاليَوْمَ تَفْعَلُوْنَ بِي هَذَا.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2872
> *English:* "So he moved, and came down in the White Palace of Kisrā, and said: the curse of Allah be upon you, people of a town — I knew there was no good in you. Yesterday you killed my father, and today you do this to me."

**عبرت:** A man who has been wronged by his own side is entitled to say so plainly, and still owe them his protection.

**Hands-up?** no

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدائن.

### TCO/E-HS21 · A blank sheet, sealed at the foot
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مسكن → الكوفة.

**What happened:** ابن الأثیر adds a detail the other chronicle does not carry. The two envoys had been sent before الحسن ؓ's letter even arrived, and they carried with them a blank sheet, sealed at its foot with معاوية ؓ's own seal. The message with it was one line: write into this sheet whatever conditions you wish, and they are yours.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ قَدْ أَرْسَلَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَامِرٍ وَعَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ سَمُرَةَ بْنِ حَبِيبِ بْنِ عَبْدِ شَمْسٍ إِلَى الْحَسَنِ قَبْلَ وُصُولِ الْكِتَابِ وَمَعَهُمَا صَحِيفَةٌ بَيْضَاءُ مَخْتُومٌ عَلَى أَسْفَلِهَا، وَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ: أَنِ اشْتَرِطْ فِي هَذِهِ الصَّحِيفَةِ الَّتِي خَتَمْتُ أَسْفَلَهَا مَا شِئْتَ فَهُوَ لَكَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1446
> *English:* "He had sent ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah ibn Ḥabīb ibn ʿAbd Shams to al-Ḥasan before the letter arrived, and with them a blank sheet sealed at its foot, and he wrote to him: stipulate in this sheet whose foot I have sealed whatever you wish, and it is yours."

**عبرت:** A blank page with a seal already on it is the strongest offer one side can make, and the hardest to enforce afterwards.

### TCO/E-HS25 · «مَنْ لِي بِأُمُوْرِ المُسْلِمِيْنَ؟»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مسكن.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ answers عمرو ؓ with the reason he will not fight this battle, and the narrator interrupts his own report to say that in this exchange معاوية ؓ was the better of the two men. If these kill those and those kill these, معاوية ؓ asks, who is left to me for the affairs of the Muslims, who for their women, who for their little ones? The narrator's aside compares the two men in this exchange, and in nothing wider.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ لَهُ مُعَاوِيَةُ - وَكَانَ وَاللهِ خَيْرَ رَجُلَيْنِ -: أَيْ عَمْرُو! إِنْ قَتَلَ هَؤُلاَءِ هَؤُلاَءِ، وَهَؤُلاَءِ هَؤُلاَءِ، مَنْ لِي بِأُمُوْرِ المُسْلِمِيْنَ، مَنْ لِي بِنِسَائِهِم، مَنْ لِي بِضَيْعَتِهِم؟!
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2878
> *English:* "Muʿāwiyah said to him — and by Allah he was the better of the two men: O ʿAmr! If these kill those, and those kill these, who is left to me for the affairs of the Muslims, who for their women, who for their little ones?"

**عبرت:** A ruler's first question about a battle he can win is what will be left of the people afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS26 · «اذْهَبَا إِلَى هَذَا الرَّجُلِ» — the instruction to the envoys
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مسكن → الكوفة.

**What happened:** Having said that, معاوية ؓ sent the two men of قريش — عبد الرحمن بن سمرة ؓ and عبد الله بن عامر بن كريز — with an instruction that gives them no script at all: go to this man, put it to him, speak to him, and ask it of him. They went with authority to agree, not with terms to impose.

**The statement:**
> فَبعثَ إِلَيْهِم بِرَجُلَيْنِ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ؛ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بنِ سَمُرَةَ، وَعَبْدِ اللهِ بنِ عَامِرِ بنِ كُرَيْزٍ، فَقَالَ: اذْهَبَا إِلَى هَذَا الرَّجُلِ، فَاعْرِضَا عَلَيْهِ، وَقُوْلاَ لَهُ، وَاطْلُبَا إِلَيْهِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2878
> *English:* "So he sent to them two men of Quraysh: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samurah and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Kurayz, and said: go to this man, and put it to him, and speak to him, and ask it of him."

**عبرت:** An envoy sent with room to agree can end a war that an envoy sent with demands will prolong.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS27 · «وَإِنَّ هَذِهِ الأُمَّةَ قَدْ عَاثَتْ فِي دِمَائِهَا»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

We, the sons of عبد المطلب, have taken of this wealth; and this ummah has run riot in its own blood. He puts his own house's share of the world first, and the ummah's bloodshed second, in the same breath.

> فَقَالَ لَهُمَا الحَسَنُ بنُ عَلِيٍّ: إِنَّا بنُو عَبْدِ المُطَّلِبِ قَدْ أَصَبنَا مِنْ هَذَا المَالِ، وَإِنَّ هَذِهِ الأُمَّةَ قَدْ عَاثَتْ فِي دِمَائِهَا.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2878
> *English:* "Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī said to them: we, the sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, have taken of this wealth; and this ummah has run riot in its own blood."

**عبرت:** A man who begins by naming what his own family has received is in a position to be believed about everything else.

### TCO/E-HS29 · Inside the house: what he put to عبد الله بن جعفر ؓ
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة → المدينة marked ahead.

**What happened:** Before the settlement was closed الحسن ؓ put it to his own family. He held عبد الله بن جعفر ؓ by the garment to keep him seated and told him what he had resolved: to go to المدينة and settle there, and to leave معاوية ؓ and this affair to one another. His reasons are four, and he lists them as a man lists damage — the trial has gone on too long, blood has been shed, kinship and the roads have been cut, and the frontiers have been left unguarded.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: قَدْ رَأَيْتُ أَنْ أَعمَدَ إِلَى المَدِيْنَةِ، فَأَنْزِلَهَا، وَأُخَلِّيَ بَيْنَ مُعَاوِيَةَ وَبَيْنَ هَذَا الحَدِيْثِ، فَقَدْ طَالتِ الفِتْنَةُ، وَسُفِكَتِ الدِّمَاءُ، وَقُطعَتِ الأَرْحَامُ وَالسُّبُلُ، وَعُطِّلَتِ الفُرُوْجُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2873
> *English:* "He said: I have seen that I should make for al-Madīnah and settle there, and leave Muʿāwiyah and this affair to each other. For the trial has grown long, and blood has been shed, and ties of kinship and the roads have been cut, and the frontiers left unguarded."

**عبرت:** The cost of a long quarrel is not counted in battles; it is counted in roads, in kinship, and in borders nobody is watching.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS32 · And الحسين ؓ submits
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** الحسن ؓ was angered, and when الحسين ؓ saw the anger he closed the argument himself, in one sentence that gave his brother everything: you are the eldest of علي ؓ's sons, and you are his successor, and our affair follows your affair. This is the best-shaped scene in the whole strand for a hall — a disagreement inside a family, settled by deference, with nobody outside it accused of anything.

> فَلَمَّا رَأَى الحُسَيْنُ غَضَبَهُ، قَالَ: أَنْتَ أَكْبَرُ وَلَدِ عَلِيٍّ، وَأَنْتَ خَلِيفَتُهُ، وَأَمْرُنَا لأَمْرِكَ تَبَعٌ.

**عبرت:** A disagreement ends well when one of the two decides that the relationship is worth more than the argument.

### TCO/E-HS33 · «اسْكُتْ، أَنَا أَعْلَمُ بِالْأَمْرِ مِنْكَ»

The words inside the round brackets are the editor's supplement from a manuscript witness, and they are printed exactly so.

> *English:* "(I adjure you by Allah, that you should believe Muʿāwiyah's account and belie your father's account! So al-Ḥasan said to him): Be silent — I know this affair better than you."

**عبرت:** The man carrying the responsibility usually knows something the man advising him does not.

### TCO/E-HS34 · «وَالصَّوَابُ مَعَ الحَسَنِ» — ابن كثير gives his verdict
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** البدایہ compresses the family argument into a single sentence and then does something it rarely does: it states a verdict in the author's own voice. الحسين ؓ blamed his brother for this opinion, and he did not accept it from him; and the correct position, ابن كثير says, is with الحسن ؓ — and he promises to give his proof shortly. The proof he means is a hadith of البخاري, four lines further down the page.

**The statement:**
> وقد لام الحسين أخا (٢) الحسن على هذا الرأي فلم يقبل منه، والصواب مع الحسن ﵁ كما سنذكر دليله قريبًا.

**عبرت:** A historian who states a verdict and then names his evidence is doing the reader a service; the evidence is the part that matters.

### TCO/E-HS36 · The same three terms in الکامل
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** فارس — دارابجرد.

**What happened:** ابن الأثیر gives the identical three conditions and spells the place-name correctly: what الحسن ؓ asked of معاوية ؓ was the contents of the treasury of الكوفة, five million; the land-tax of دارابجرد in فارس; and that علي ؓ not be abused. Two books, one list — which is why these three can be stated to a room with confidence.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ الَّذِي طَلَبَ الْحَسَنُ مِنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُ مَا فِي بَيْتِ مَالِ الْكُوفَةِ، وَمَبْلَغُهُ خَمْسَةُ آلَافِ أَلْفٍ، وَخَرَاجَ دَارَابَجِرْدَ مِنْ فَارِسَ، وَأَنْ لَا يَشْتُمَ عَلِيًّا

**عبرت:** When two independent books give the same three items, you are as close to the document as history lets you get.

### TCO/E-HS37 · سیر states three different terms
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED, the lists differ]` · **Map:** فسا and دارابجرد; المدينة.

**What happened:** سیر's list is not the chronicles' list, and the differences are real. It explains what the money was for — to settle his debt and his standing obligations, and to support himself and his family. It repeats the condition about علي ؓ not being reviled in his hearing. And it adds فسا beside دارابجرد, with the land-tax of both carried to him every year at المدينة. The three lists must never be merged into one four-item list.

**The statement:**
> ثُمَّ كَاتَبَ مُعَاوِيَةَ فِي الصُّلْحِ عَلَى أَنْ يُسِلِّمَ لَهُ ثَلاَثَ خِصَالٍ: يُسلِّمَ لَهُ بَيْتَ المَالِ فَيَقْضِي مِنْهُ دَيْنَهُ وَمَوَاعِيدَهُ وَيَتحمَّلَ مِنْهُ هُوَ وَآلُهُ، وَلاَ يُسَبَّ عَلِيٌّ وَهُوَ يَسَمَعُ، وَأَنْ يُحملَ إِلَيْهِ خَرَاجُ فَسَا وَدَرَابْجِرْدَ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ إِلَى المَدِيْنَةِ، فَأَجَابَهُ مُعَاوِيَةُ، وَأَعْطَاهُ مَا سَأَل
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2872
> *English:* "Then he corresponded with Muʿāwiyah over a peace, on condition that he hand over three matters to him: that he hand over the treasury, so that he might settle from it his debt and his promised obligations and support himself and his family from it; and that ʿAlī not be reviled while he hears it; and that the land-tax of Fasā and Dārābjird be carried to him every year to al-Madīnah. So Muʿāwiyah answered him and gave him what he asked."

**عبرت:** Three books that agree on the shape of an agreement and differ on its items are telling you the document itself is gone.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS38 · A fourth term, in سیر only
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** سیر alone records a further undertaking: that if anything befell معاوية ؓ while الحسن ؓ was still alive, he would name him and put the command to him. ### TCO/E-HS40 · Were the terms kept? — our own books say opposite things
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED, and the safe list contradicts itself]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** This card exists so that nobody re-derives the point and puts half of it on a slide. سیر says the treasury was handed over and that معاوية ؓ refrained from reviling علي ؓ in الحسن ؓ's hearing. الکامل says the opposite about that same condition, and adds that the people of البصرة withheld the land-tax of دارابجرد. البدایہ, on the pages read, says nothing at all about whether the terms were kept. Two authorities of our own safe list state opposite things and neither grades the other. **None of this is narrated from the platform.**

**The statement:**
> وَوَفَّى مُعَاوِيَةُ لِلْحَسَنِ بِبَيْتِ المَالِ، وَكَانَ فِيْهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ سَبْعَةُ آلاَفِ أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ؛ فَاحتَمَلهَا الحَسَنُ، وَتَجَهَّزَ هُوَ وَأَهْلُ بَيْتِهِ إِلَى المَدِيْنَةِ، وَكَفَّ مُعَاوِيَةُ عَنْ سَبِّ عَلِيٍّ وَالحَسَنُ يَسَمَعُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2872
> *English:* "And Muʿāwiyah fulfilled to al-Ḥasan regarding the treasury — and there were in it that day seven million dirhams; al-Ḥasan carried them off, and he and his household prepared to go to al-Madīnah. And Muʿāwiyah refrained from reviling ʿAlī while al-Ḥasan could hear."

**عبرت:** Where the sources we trust contradict each other outright, the honest course is to say so and stop.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS41 · The amnesty, seen in how it was used
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة lights.

**What happened:** Neither chronicle lists a general amnesty among the stipulations, but both show it working afterwards, which is better evidence than a list. Months later, at البصرة, أبو بكرة الثقفي ؓ stopped an execution by citing the settlement itself by name: الحسن ؓ made peace with معاوية ؓ over what the companions of علي ؓ had done, wherever they were — so you have no way against them, nor against their father.

**The statement:**
> وَقَدْ صَالَحَ الْحَسَنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ عَلَى مَا أَصَابَ أَصْحَابَ عَلِيٌّ حَيْثُ كَانُوا، فَلَيْسَ [لَكَ] عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا عَلَى أَبِيهِمْ سَبِيلٌ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۱۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1454
> *English:* "And al-Ḥasan made peace with Muʿāwiyah over what the companions of ʿAlī had done, wherever they were; so [you] have no way against them nor against their father."

**عبرت:** The real test of an agreement is whether a stranger, far away, can hold someone to it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS42 · The sermon at الكوفة, and one word shouted back
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** Before the handover الحسن ؓ preached to the people of العراق and laid the choice in front of them without softening it. It is not doubt or regret that turns us away from the people of الشام, he told them; we used to fight them with soundness and patience, and soundness has been mixed with enmity and patience with panic. معاوية ؓ has called us to a matter with no honour in it and no fairness; if you want death we will return it to him, and if you want life we will accept and take your terms for you. The crowd shouted one word back from every side.

**The statement:**
> فَنَادَاهُ النَّاسُ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ: الْبَقِيَّةَ الْبَقِيَّةَ! وَأَمْضَى الصُّلْحَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1447
> *English:* "And the people called out to him from every side: survival, survival! And he carried the peace through."

**عبرت:** He put the choice to them in the open, and the answer they gave is the reason the settlement was his to make.

**Hands-up?** What do you think the crowd shouted back?

### TCO/E-HS43 · سیر heard a different word
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** سیر records the same sermon, almost word for word, and then records the crowd's answer differently — not «الْبَقِيَّةَ» but «التَّقِيَّةَ». And it adds a clause الکامل does not carry: when they had left him alone, he carried the peace through. The two words are one letter apart and the note keeps both.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: فَنَادَاهُ القَوْمُ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانبٍ؛ التَّقِيَّةَ التَّقِيَّةَ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2877
> *English:* "He said: and the people called out to him from every side: caution, caution."

**عبرت:** A single letter of difference between two manuscripts can change what a crowd is remembered as saying.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS44 · «إِنَّهُ سَخِيٌّ بِنَفْسِي عَنْكُمْ ثَلَاثٌ»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** When the settlement was made, الحسن ؓ stood up among the people of العراق and told them, without heat, the three things that made him content to be finished with them: your killing of my father, your stabbing of me, and your plundering of my baggage. He is not accusing an enemy. He is describing his own army.

**The statement:**
> فَلَمَّا اصْطَلَحَا قَامَ الْحَسَنُ فِي أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ فَقَالَ: يَا أَهْلَ الْعِرَاقِ إِنَّهُ سَخِيٌّ بِنَفْسِي عَنْكُمْ ثَلَاثٌ: قَتْلُكُمْ أَبِي، وَطَعْنُكُمْ إِيَّايَ، وَانْتِهَابُكُمْ مَتَاعِي.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1446
> *English:* "When the two had made peace al-Ḥasan stood among the people of Iraq and said: O people of Iraq, three things make me content to be quit of you: your killing of my father, your stabbing of me, and your plundering of my baggage."

**عبرت:** A man is entitled to name what was done to him, once, plainly, and then leave.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS45 · «إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ أُمَرَاؤُكُمْ وَضِيفَانُكُمْ»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** In the sermon in which he announced his decision to hand over the command, الحسن ؓ described himself and his household in two words: we are your commanders and we are your guests. He repeated it, says ابن الأثیر, until there was nobody left sitting in the assembly who was not weeping aloud.

**The statement:**
> أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ أُمَرَاؤُكُمْ وَضِيفَانُكُمْ، وَنَحْنُ أَهْلُ بَيْتِ نَبِيِّكُمُ الَّذِينَ أَذْهَبَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمُ الرِّجْسَ وَطَهَّرَهُمْ تَطْهِيرًا.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1447
> *English:* "O people: we are only your commanders and your guests, and we are the household of your Prophet, from whom Allah removed impurity and purified them thoroughly."

**عبرت:** A leader who calls himself a guest of his own city has already decided he can leave it.

### TCO/E-HS46 · قيس بن سعد ؓ will not take the order
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the vanguard's camp, north of المدائن.

**What happened:** الحسن ؓ sent word to the commander of his vanguard, قيس بن سعد ؓ, to hear and obey معاوية ؓ. قيس ؓ refused to accept it. He withdrew from the obedience of both men together, and stood apart with those who followed him. البدایہ adds, in the same sentence, that he reconsidered the matter shortly afterwards and gave معاوية ؓ his allegiance.

**The statement:**
> وبعث الحسن بن علي إلى أمير المقدمة (٣) قيس بن سعد أن يسمع ويطيع [لمعاوية]، فأبى قيس بن سعد من قبول ذلك، وخرج عن طاعتهما جميعًا، واعتزل بمن أطاعه ثم راجع الأمر فبايع معاوية بعد قريب كما سنذكره.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3763
> *English:* "And al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī sent to the commander of the vanguard, Qays ibn Saʿd, that he should hear and obey [Muʿāwiyah]. Qays ibn Saʿd refused to accept that, and went out of the obedience of both of them together, and withdrew with those who obeyed him; then he reconsidered the matter and gave Muʿāwiyah allegiance shortly after, as we shall mention."

**عبرت:** The first man to give the allegiance was the last man to give it up — and he gave it up in the open, not by slipping away.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS47 · قيس ؓ writes his own terms, and asks for no money
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ sent قيس ؓ the same device he had sent الحسن ؓ: a document sealed at the foot, write in it what you like. قيس ؓ wrote one thing into it — safety for himself and for the partisans of علي ؓ regarding the blood and the property they had taken in the fitna. And in that document of his he asked for no money at all. معاوية ؓ gave him what he asked, and قيس ؓ and those with him entered his obedience.

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1449
> *English:* "Qays stipulated for himself and for the partisans of ʿAlī safety concerning the blood and property they had taken; and he asked no money in that document of his. And Muʿāwiyah gave him what he asked."

**عبرت:** A man handed a blank page asked for nothing on it except protection for other people.

**Hands-up?** Given a blank page and any terms you liked, what would you have written?

### TCO/E-HS50 · «السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

### TCO/E-HS51 · عمرو ؓ's advice on the minbar at الكوفة

**عبرت:** A plan to humiliate a man in public is a plan that can only be tested in public.

### TCO/E-HS52 · What he actually said

**عبرت:** He answered the plan against him by saying the truest thing in the room and sitting down.

### TCO/E-HS55 · «تَركْتُ لِمُعَاوِيَةَ إِرَادَةَ إِصلاَحِ المُسْلِمِيْنَ»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

### TCO/E-HS57 · «كَرِهْتُ الدُّنْيَا»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** He was asked afterwards what had moved him to do what he did. His answer named two things: he had come to dislike the world, and he had found the people of الكوفة a people whom nobody ever trusts without being beaten. Not one of them agrees with another in opinion or inclination; my father met terrible things from them; and — the last line — it is the land that will be ruined fastest.

**The statement:**
> قِيلَ لِلْحَسَنِ: مَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى مَا فَعَلْتَ؟ فَقَالَ: كَرِهْتُ الدُّنْيَا وَرَأَيْتُ أَهْلَ الْكُوفَةِ قَوْمًا لَا يَثِقُ بِهِمْ أَحَدٌ أَبَدًا إِلَّا غُلِبَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1448
> *English:* "It was said to al-Ḥasan: what moved you to what you did? He said: I came to dislike the world, and I found the people of al-Kūfah a people whom no one ever trusts without being overcome."

**عبرت:** A commander's hardest judgement is about his own side, and he is usually the last person allowed to say it aloud.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS59 · «كَانَتْ جَمَاجِمُ العَربِ فِي يَدِي»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** جبير بن نفير put it to him directly: they say you want the caliphate. His answer is the best single sentence in the whole strand. The chiefs of the Arabs were in my hand — making peace with whom I made peace and fighting whom I fought — and I left it for Allah. Should I then snatch it back with the help of the goatherds of الحجاز?

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: كَانَتْ جَمَاجِمُ العَربِ فِي يَدِي، يُسَالِمُوْنَ مَنْ سَالَمْتُ، وَيُحَاربُوْنَ مَنْ حَاربْتُ، فَتركْتُهَا للهِ، ثُمَّ أَبْتَزُّهَا بِأَتْيَاسِ الحِجَازِ (١) ؟
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۷۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2882
> *English:* "He said: the chiefs of the Arabs were in my hand, making peace with whomever I made peace and fighting whomever I fought — and I left it for Allah. Shall I then snatch it back with the he-goats of the Ḥijāz?"

**عبرت:** A man who gave up power when he had it is not likely to scheme for it when he does not.

**Hands-up?** no
