### TCO/E-HS60 · «وَفِيْهِ انْقطَاعٌ» — the historian marks a broken chain
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Among the reports of what الحسن ؓ said to the men who reproached him, سیر carries one that runs on into a dream and a prediction about the future. الذهبي transmits it and then, in three words at the end, tells the reader what is wrong with it: there is a break in the chain. This is what a historian's own caution looks like, printed on the page, in the middle of a story he is telling.

**The statement:**
> سَمِعَهُ مِنْهُ: أَبُو سَلَمَةَ التَّبُوْذَكِيُّ، وَفِيْهِ انْقطَاعٌ (٢) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2880
> *English:* "Abū Salamah al-Tabūdhakī heard it from him — and in it there is a break in the chain."

**عبرت:** The most useful thing a scholar writes is often the sentence in which he tells you not to rely on what he has just transmitted.

### TCO/E-HS61 · When the handover happened — four answers
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

A slide may show the spread; it may not choose one.

**عبرت:** A turning point in history can be certain in substance and uncertain in date, and both are worth saying aloud.

### TCO/E-HS62 · How long was the caliphate of الحسن ؓ?
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن الأثیر does the arithmetic honestly. On the view that he handed over in ربيع الأول, the caliphate was five months and about half a month. On the view of ربيع الآخر, six months and something. On the view of جمادى الأولى, seven months and something. And then: and Allah knows best.

> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1447
> *English:* "And the caliphate of al-Ḥasan, on the view of those who say he handed the command over in Rabīʿ al-Awwal, was five months and about half a month; on the view of those who say Rabīʿ al-Ākhir, six months and something; on the view of those who say Jumādā al-Ūlā, seven months and something. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best."

**عبرت:** Notice that the disagreement about the number is not a disagreement about the event; it follows from the disagreement about the date.

### TCO/E-HS63 · سیر's figure: seven months and eleven days

> *English:* "Al-Kalbī said: al-Ḥasan was given allegiance, and he held it seven months and eleven days; then he handed the command to Muʿāwiyah."

**عبرت:** The most precise figure in a set of figures is not automatically the most reliable one.

**عبرت:** A historian who writes "the well-known view is" is telling you there is another one.

### TCO/E-HS69 · The same hadith, in سیر's wording
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

> *English:* "This son of mine is a chief, and perhaps Allah will reconcile through him two parties of the Muslims."

**عبرت:** Two sound books can preserve one hadith in two wordings; quoting each as it stands is the discipline that keeps both honest.

### TCO/E-HS70 · الحسن البصري cites the hadith at the moment of the صلح
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

> *English:* "Al-Ḥasan said: and I certainly heard Abū Bakrah saying —"

### TCO/E-HS71 · ابن كثير refuses a report he does not like the smell of
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة — the حج of 40.

**What happened:** ابن جرير reported that المغيرة بن شعبة ؓ forged a letter in معاوية ؓ's name in order to lead the حج of the year forty. ابن كثير prints the report and then refuses it outright, on the page, giving his reasons: this is not accepted, and it is not to be thought of المغيرة ؓ; we drew attention to it only so that it be known to be false; the Companions are of higher standing than this. This is a model, in our own safe list, of a historian declining a report.

**عبرت:** Finding a report in an old book is not the same as the report being true, and the great historians say so themselves.

### TCO/E-HS72 · «لَبَدَأْتُ بِقِتَالِكَ» — the letter at القادسية

### TCO/E-HS75 · Who معاوية ؓ appointed in 41
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** دمشق, الكوفة, البصرة.

**What happened:** The shape of the new administration is set out plainly in البدایہ. فضالة بن عبيد ؓ was made judge of الشام, and after him أبو إدريس الخولاني. قيس بن حمزة commanded his guard. His secretary and the man over his affairs was a Byzantine, سرجون بن منصور الرومي. الکامل adds المغيرة بن شعبة ؓ over الكوفة — over the prayer, after the land-tax was taken from him — and عبد الله بن عامر over البصرة at the end of the year.

**The statement:**
> فولَّى معاوية قضاء الشام لفَضالة بن عُبيد، ثم بعده لأبي إدريس الخَوْلاني. وكان على شرطته قيس بن حمزة. وكان كاتبه وصاحب أمره سَرْجون (٣) بن منصور الرومي.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۸ ص۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3769
> *English:* "Muʿāwiyah appointed Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd over the judgeship of Syria, and after him Abū Idrīs al-Khawlānī. Over his guard was Qays ibn Ḥamzah. His secretary and the man in charge of his affairs was Sarjūn ibn Manṣūr al-Rūmī."

**عبرت:** The moment a government starts appointing judges and secretaries is the moment a contest has turned into a state.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS76 · «ويقال» — the first guard, and sealed letters
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED, reported]` · **Map:** دمشق.

**What happened:** ابن كثير records, and marks it as a report rather than a fact by opening with "and it is said", two small administrative firsts attributed to معاوية ؓ: that he was the first to keep a bodyguard, and the first to bind letters and seal them. Two little details, and between them they tell you that the office had changed shape.

**The statement:**
> ويقال: إنَّ معاوية أولُ من اتَّخذ الحرس، وأول من حزم الكتب وختمها.

> *English:* "And it is said that Muʿāwiyah was the first to take a bodyguard, and the first to bind letters and seal them."

**عبرت:** The habits a ruler adopts for his own safety become, in time, the shape of the office itself.

### TCO/E-HS77 · المغيرة ؓ over الكوفة — the prayer, not the money
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة, مصر.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ meant to put عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص over الكوفة. المغيرة بن شعبة ؓ warned him: you would be putting the son over الكوفة and the father over مصر, and yourself between the lion's two fangs. So معاوية ؓ appointed المغيرة ؓ instead. Then عمرو ؓ came in and warned that المغيرة ؓ over the land-tax would be impossible to audit — so the land-tax was taken from him and he was left with the prayer.

**The statement:**
> فَعَزَلَهُ عَنِ الْخَرَاجِ وَاسْتَعْمَلَهُ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1453
> *English:* "So he removed him from the land-tax and appointed him over the prayer."

**عبرت:** Separating the man who leads the prayer from the man who handles the money is an old idea, and it was tried early.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS78 · «لَمْ يُعْطُوكَ بَيْعَتَهُمْ عَلَى قَتْلِ الْأَطْفَالِ»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة → الكوفة.

**What happened:** بسر بن أبي أرطاة, governor of البصرة, had seized the elder sons of زياد to force their father to come in, and threatened to kill them. أبو بكرة الثقفي ؓ went to معاوية ؓ at الكوفة and put it to him in one sentence: O معاوية, the people did not give you their allegiance upon the killing of children. معاوية ؓ asked what he meant, heard the answer, and wrote out an order for their release.

**The statement:**
> يَا مُعَاوِيَةُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ لَمْ يُعْطُوكَ بَيْعَتَهُمْ عَلَى قَتْلِ الْأَطْفَالِ! قَالَ: وَمَا ذَاكَ يَا أَبَا بَكْرَةَ؟
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۱۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1454
> *English:* "O Muʿāwiyah, the people did not give you their allegiance upon the killing of children! He said: and what is that, Abū Bakrah?"

**عبرت:** An allegiance has limits, and a man who knows them can say so to the ruler's face.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS79 · The ride back, and the sun going down
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة → البصرة, the desert road.

**What happened:** أبو بكرة ؓ had asked بسر for a few days' grace, and he had ridden to الكوفة and back to get the order. He reached البصرة on the appointed day. بسر had brought the sons of زياد out at sunrise and was waiting for sunset to kill them, and a crowd had gathered. Then a man appeared on a hard-driven mount, dismounted, waved his garment and said الله أكبر, and the people said it with him — and he ran the last stretch on his own feet and reached بسر before the killing, and handed him the letter, and they were released.

**The statement:**
> وَعَادَ فَوَصَلَ الْبَصْرَةَ يَوْمَ الْمِيعَادِ وَقَدْ أَخْرَجَ بُسْرٌ أَوْلَادَ زِيَادٍ مَعَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ يَنْتَظِرُ بِهِمُ الْغُرُوبَ لِيَقْتُلَهُمْ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۱۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1454
> *English:* "And he returned and reached al-Baṣrah on the appointed day; and Busr had brought out the sons of Ziyād at sunrise, waiting for sunset with them in order to kill them."

**عبرت:** One man who will not let a thing happen, and who is willing to ride, can be the whole difference.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS80 · The charge أبو بكرة ؓ gave the new ruler
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ asked أبو بكرة ؓ whether he had any charge to lay upon him. He said yes, and gave him one, and البدایہ prints it in full: look to yourself and to your flock and do righteous work, for you have taken on something enormous — the stewardship of Allah among His creation. Fear Allah; you have a limit you will not pass, and behind you a pursuer coming fast.

**The statement:**

> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۸ ص۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3770
> *English:* "Yes: I charge you, O Commander of the Believers, to look to yourself and to your flock and to do righteous work — for you have taken upon yourself something enormous, the stewardship of Allah among His creation. So fear Allah."

**عبرت:** The people who tell a new ruler the truth in his first year are worth more to him than the ones who tell him he is secure.

### TCO/E-HS81 · بسر at the minbar of البصرة — recorded, not planned
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

This note records what the book records and adjudicates nothing about it; it is not for the hall, and it is kept here so that nobody re-derives it under pressure from the floor.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرَةَ: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا لَا نَعْلَمُكَ إِلَّا كَاذِبًا.

> *English:* "Abū Bakrah said: O Allah, we know you only as a liar."

**عبرت:** Some things in the record are true, well attested, and still not the speaker's business to raise.

### TCO/E-HS82 · الذهبي throws out a whole class of reports
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the sources themselves `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

### TCO/E-HS83 · And distinguishes weak from forged
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the sources themselves `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Immediately after throwing out the forgeries, الذهبي does not stop the examination — he draws a second line. There are also narrated among the virtues of معاوية ؓ weak things that can be tolerated, and he begins to list those separately. Forged, weak-but-tolerable, and sound are three categories, not one.

> *English:* "And there are narrated among the virtues of Muʿāwiyah weak things that may be tolerated, among them —"

**عبرت:** "Weak" and "forged" are not the same verdict, and a careful scholar refuses to blur them even when it would be convenient.

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the sources themselves `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

### TCO/E-HS85 · Why the reports are unbalanced
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the sources themselves `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي diagnoses the whole literature in one question. A man is raised in a province where he sees almost nobody except someone extravagant in love or excessive in hatred — so, he asks, from where is fairness and balance to reach him? He has just said the same of both sides: of الشام, raised on one loyalty, and of العراق, raised on the other.

**The statement:**
> فَبِاللهِ كَيْفَ يَكُوْنُ حَالُ مَنْ نَشَأَ فِي إِقْلِيْمٍ، لاَ يَكَادُ يُشَاهِدُ فِيْهِ إِلاَّ غَالِياً فِي الحُبِّ، مُفْرِطاً فِي البُغْضِ، وَمِنْ أَيْنَ يَقَعُ لَهُ الإِنْصَافُ وَالاعْتِدَالُ؟
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۱۲۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2737
> *English:* "So, by Allah, what is the state of one who grew up in a region in which he hardly sees anyone but a man extravagant in love or excessive in hatred — and from where is fairness and balance to reach him?"

**عبرت:** Where a man was raised shapes which reports reached him, and how they reached him.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS86 · The Companions who took neither side
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the sources themselves `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, الطائف.

### TCO/E-HS87 · «وَلَهُ هَنَاتٌ وَأُمُوْرٌ، وَاللهُ المَوْعِدُ»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the sources themselves `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي's own summing-up of معاوية ؓ is worth studying as a model of how to speak about a contested figure. He praises what is praiseworthy — this man led and governed the world by the completeness of his mind, the abundance of his forbearance, the breadth of his spirit, and the strength of his judgement — he says plainly that others of the Companions were far better than him, and then he closes the account with six words and leaves the rest where it belongs.

**The statement:**
> وَلَهُ هَنَاتٌ وَأُمُوْرٌ، وَاللهُ المَوْعِدُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۱۳۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2742
> *English:* "And he has lapses and matters against him; and with Allah is the appointment."

**عبرت:** It is possible to say a man's good and acknowledge his faults without setting yourself up as his judge.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS89 · Who first put الشام under him — عمر ؓ or عثمان ؓ?
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 18–35 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** دمشق, الشام entire.

Whether it was عمر ؓ or عثمان ؓ who first made the whole of الشام a single command under him, سیر does not leave open: إسماعيل بن أمية says عمر ؓ, and الذهبي answers with the word scholars use to settle a contested transmission.

**عبرت:** Who appointed whom, and when, is the sort of small question that later quarrels are built on — which is why the historians settle it carefully.

### TCO/E-HS95 · «كَانَ أَشْبَهَهُم بِالنَّبِيِّ»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** childhood `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** أنس بن مالك ؓ, who served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years and knew every face in that house, said of الحسن ؓ that he was the most like the Prophet ﷺ of all of them. It is the one sentence that explains why the people of الكوفة came to him in such numbers, and why the uncle at المدائن would not touch him.

**The statement:**
> وَقَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: قَالَ أَنَسٌ: كَانَ أَشْبَهَهُم بِالنَّبِيِّ - عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاَةُ وَالسَّلاَمُ - الحَسَنُ بنُ عَلِيٍّ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۴۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2857
> *English:* "Al-Zuhrī said: Anas said: the most resembling of them to the Prophet ﷺ was al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī."

**عبرت:** Some of what a man carries through his life was settled before he could speak.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS96 · أبو بكر الصديق ؓ carries him on his shoulder
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the caliphate of أبو بكر ؓ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** عقبة بن الحارث says أبو بكر ؓ led them in the ʿAṣr prayer, then went out walking with علي ؓ, and saw الحسن ؓ playing with the boys. He picked him up and put him on his shoulder and began reciting a line — by my father, the one who resembles the Prophet ﷺ, and does not resemble علي — and علي ؓ was smiling. البخاري records it.

**The statement:**
> بأَبِي شَبِيْهٌ النَّبِيّ ... لَيْسَ شَبِيْهٌ بِعَلِيّ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۴۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2857
> *English:* "By my father — the one resembling the Prophet, not resembling ʿAlī."

**عبرت:** The affection between these households is as well attested as anything that later came between their followers.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS97 · عمر ؓ enters the two boys on the ديوان
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the caliphate of عمر ؓ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** When عمر ؓ set up the register of stipends, he entered الحسن ؓ and الحسين ؓ at their father's rate, for their kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and fixed five thousand dirhams for each of them. سیر has a second notice which says instead that he entered them with the men of بدر — the two notices differ in what they say he matched them to.

**The statement:**
> أَنَّ عُمَرَ لَمَّا دَوَّنَ الدِّيْوَانَ، أَلْحقَ الحَسَنَ وَالحُسَيْنَ بِفَرِيضَةِ أَبِيهِمَا؛ لِقَرَابَتِهِمَا مِنْ رَسُوْلِ اللهِ -صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - فَرَضَ لِكُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا خَمْسَةَ آلاَفِ دِرْهَمٍ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۵۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2867
> *English:* "When ʿUmar compiled the register, he attached al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn to their father's stipend, for their kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and fixed for each of them five thousand dirhams."

**عبرت:** The state's earliest paperwork shows you exactly what it valued and by how much.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS98 · حج on foot, and dividing his wealth with Allah
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** his lifetime `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدينة → مكة.

**What happened:** ابن عباس ؓ said الحسن ؓ made twenty-five ḥajj on foot, with his riding-beasts led along beside him, and that he divided his wealth with Allah three times — to the point of giving away one shoe and keeping the other. A second report inside سیر itself, from ابن جدعان, says fifteen. The number is disputed; the practice is not.

**The statement:**
> وَلَقَدْ حَجَّ الحَسَنُ بنُ عَلِيٍّ خَمْساً وَعِشْرِيْنَ حَجَّةً مَاشِياً، وَإِنَّ النَّجَائِبَ لَتُقَادُ مَعَهُ، وَلَقَدْ قَاسَمَ اللهَ مَالَهُ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2868
> *English:* "And al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī performed twenty-five pilgrimages on foot, with the fine mounts being led alongside him; and he divided his wealth with Allah three times."

**عبرت:** A man who had walked to مكة twenty-five times with his own horses led beside him was not a man who found it hard to hand something over.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS99 · «وَأَحبُّوهُ أَشَدَّ مِنْ حُبِّ أَبِيْهِ»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** جرير بن حازم gives the whole political situation of رمضان 40 in one sentence: علي ؓ was killed, so the people of الكوفة gave allegiance to الحسن ؓ — and they loved him more strongly than they had loved his father. It is the sentence that makes what happened next hard to explain and important to tell.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ جَرِيرُ بنُ حَازِمٍ: قُتِلَ عَلِيٌّ، فَبَايَعَ أَهْلُ الكُوْفَةِ الحَسَنَ، وَأَحبُّوهُ أَشَدَّ مِنْ حُبِّ أَبِيْهِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2871
> *English:* "Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim said: ʿAlī was killed, and the people of al-Kūfah gave allegiance to al-Ḥasan, and they loved him more intensely than they loved his father."

**عبرت:** A city can love a man deeply and still fail him inside seven months.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS100 · What he told الكوفة from its own minbar
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** سیر preserves a short sermon he gave at الكوفة, and it reads like a description of everything that was about to go wrong around him. Forbearance is an ornament, dignity is manliness, haste is folly, folly is weakness, sitting with base people is a disgrace, and mixing with the corrupt is a cause of suspicion.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّ الحِلْمَ زِينَةٌ، وَالوَقَارَ مُرُوءةٌ، وَالعَجَلَةَ سَفَهٌ، وَالسَّفَهَ ضَعْفٌ، وَمُجَالَسَةَ أَهْلِ الدَّنَاءةِ شَيْنٌ، وَمُخَالَطَةَ الفُسَّاقِ رِيْبَةٌ (١) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۶۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2871
> *English:* "Forbearance is an ornament, dignity is manliness, haste is folly, folly is weakness, sitting with base people is a disgrace, and mixing with the corrupt is a cause of suspicion."

**عبرت:** He preached forbearance to a city that had none, and then practised it in front of them.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS101 · The generation was going: عثمان بن طلحة ؓ and the key of the Kaaba
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مكة.

**What happened:** Among those who died in the first year of معاوية ؓ's rule was عثمان بن طلحة ؓ, of عبد الدار — the man from whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the key of the Kaaba on the day of the conquest, and to whom he then returned it, reciting the verse about restoring trusts to their owners, and saying: take it, ʿUthmān, as a lasting and inherited right; none shall take it from you but a wrongdoer. صفوان بن أمية ؓ died at مكة in that same year.

**The statement:**
> وهو الذي أخذ رسول الله ﷺ منه مفتاح الكعبة عام الفتح، ثم ردَّه إليه وهو يتلو قوله تعالى: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا﴾ [النساء: ٥٨]
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۸ ص۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3772
> *English:* "And he is the one from whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the key of the Kaaba in the year of the conquest, then returned it to him while reciting the words of Allah: 'Indeed Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners.'"

**عبرت:** The men who had seen the conquest of مكة with their own eyes were dying out in the very year the caliphate became a kingship.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS102 · عاتكة بنت زيد ؓ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** She was the sister of سعيد بن زيد ؓ, one of the ten. She was married to عبد الله بن أبي بكر ؓ, who was killed at الطائف; then to عمر بن الخطاب ؓ, her cousin, who was killed; then to الزبير بن العوام ؓ, who was killed at وادي السباع. When علي ؓ sent to marry her she refused, saying she feared for him that he would be killed. البدایہ notes: and had she married him, he would have been killed as well. She died in the first year of معاوية ؓ's rule.

**The statement:**
> فلما بعث إليها علي بن أبي طالب ليتزوَّجها قالت له: إني أخشى عليك أن تُقتل، فأبت أن تتزوَّجه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۸ ص۱۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3773
> *English:* "And when ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib sent to her to marry her, she said to him: I fear for you that you will be killed — and she refused to marry him."

**عبرت:** One woman's household holds the whole history of that generation's losses.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS103 · لبيد بن ربيعة ؓ, who gave up poetry
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** The poet لبيد بن ربيعة ؓ — one of the great names of pre-Islamic Arabia, a Companion — died in this year, and it is said he died on the very day معاوية ؓ entered الكوفة. الکامل gives his age as a hundred and fifty-seven years, notes the competing report that he died in the caliphate of عثمان ؓ, and closes the notice with one clause: he abandoned poetry from the day he accepted Islam.

**The statement:**
> وَقِيلَ: مَاتَ فِي خِلَافَةِ عُثْمَانَ، وَلَهُ صُحْبَةٌ، وَتَرَكَ الشِّعْرَ مُذْ أَسْلَمَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۱۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1458
> *English:* "And it is said he died in the caliphate of ʿUthmān. He had companionship with the Prophet ﷺ, and he abandoned poetry from the time he accepted Islam."

**عبرت:** The greatest poet of his age stopped writing, and it is the one thing the chronicle chooses to record about him.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS104 · While all this happened: عقبة بن نافع ؓ goes west
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41–50 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** إفريقية — the map jumps west, to برقة and beyond.

**What happened:** In this same year عمرو بن العاص ؓ appointed his own cousin عقبة بن نافع over إفريقية. الکامل then runs his career forward in a single paragraph: غدامس in 42, districts of the السودان in 43, ودان, most of the land of the Berbers — and he is the man who laid out القيروان in the year fifty. The quarrel in العراق was not the whole of what the ummah was doing that year.

**The statement:**
> وَفِي هَذِهِ السَّنَةِ اسْتَعْمَلَ عَمْرُو بْنُ الْعَاصِ عُقْبَةَ بْنَ نَافِعِ بْنِ عَبْدِ قِيسٍ، وَهُوَ ابْنُ خَالَةِ عَمْرٍو، عَلَى إِفْرِيقِيَّةَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۱۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1457
> *English:* "And in this year ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ appointed ʿUqbah ibn Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd Qays — who was his maternal cousin — over Ifrīqiyah."

**عبرت:** While one province argued about who should lead, another was being opened.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCO/E-HS105 · The following year, 42
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 42 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** اللان in the north; المدينة and مكة.

**What happened:** The year after the settlement reads like an ordinary year of government. The Muslims raided اللان and the Romans. معاوية ؓ appointed مروان بن الحكم over المدينة and خالد بن العاص over مكة; المغيرة بن شعبة ؓ remained over الكوفة with شريح as its judge. The machinery had started turning again, which is exactly what عام الجماعة had been for.

**The statement:**
> وَفِيهَا وَلَّى مُعَاوِيَةُ مَرْوَانَ بْنَ الْحَكَمِ الْمَدِينَةَ، وَوَلَّى خَالِدَ بْنَ الْعَاصِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ مَكَّةَ، فَاسْتَقْضَى مَرْوَانُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ نَوْفَلٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۳ ص۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1459
> *English:* "And in it Muʿāwiyah appointed Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam over al-Madīnah and Khālid ibn al-ʿĀṣ ibn Hishām over Makkah; and Marwān made ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal his judge."

**عبرت:** The proof that a peace has held is that the next year is dull.

**Hands-up?** no

## The فضائل of علي ؓ, and what ابن كثير does with each report

*Source note: [`the-fadail-of-ali-as-the-books-report-them.md`](../docs/research/the-fadail-of-ali-as-the-books-report-them.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TFO/E-FA1 · A chapter that spends six pages refusing one report
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** written in the 8th century AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The book this course is reading has a chapter on the merits of علي ؓ. It is not
a collection of everything the author could find. He puts one famous report — the story of the
roasted bird — through six pages, lays out more than ninety chains for it, quotes his own teacher
saying not one of them is sound, notes that a great scholar wrote a whole volume collecting it and
another wrote a whole volume refuting it, and then says that in his heart there remains a question
about it even though its routes are many. That is what it looks like when a historian weighs rather
than collects.

**The statement:**
> وبالجملة (٤) ففي القلب من صحة هذا الحديث نظر وإن كثرت طرقه، والله أعلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3729
> *English:* "In sum: in the heart there is a question over the soundness of this hadith, even though
> its routes are many, and God knows best."

**عبرت:** Many people repeating a thing is not the same as the thing being true.

**Hands-up?** How many reports do you think a careful historian throws away for every one he keeps?

---

### TFO/E-FA2 · The nearest of the ten in kinship
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** before the Hijra `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mecca lights.

**What happened:** The first merit the book names is not a saying at all. It is blood. Of the ten
Companions given the glad tidings of Paradise, علي ؓ is the closest in lineage to the Messenger ﷺ:
his father أبو طالب was the Prophet ﷺ's full paternal uncle, so the two men were first cousins. His
mother was فاطمة بنت أسد, herself of بنو هاشم. The author then runs the family tree back through
عبد المطلب and هاشم and قصي to عدنان, and gives the birth-names behind the famous ones.

**The statement:**
> من ذلك أنه أقرب العشرة المشهود لهم بالجنة نسبًا من رسول الله ﷺ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3699
> *English:* "Among them is that he is, of the ten given the glad tidings of Paradise, the nearest in
> lineage to the Messenger of God ﷺ."

**عبرت:** A man's place in a story often begins with where he was born, not with what he chose.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TFO/E-FA3 · فاطمة بنت أسد ؓ, the first of her line
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** before the Hijra `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** His mother has her own notice. The genealogist الزبير بن بكار records that she
was the first woman of بنو هاشم to bear a child to a man of بنو هاشم — so her son was Hāshimī on
both sides. She accepted Islam, and she made the Hijra.

**The statement:**
> قال الزبير بن بكار (١): وهي أول هاشمية ولدت هاشميًا. وقد أسلمت وهاجرت.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3700
> *English:* "الزبير بن بكار said: and she was the first Hāshimī woman to bear a Hāshimī child. And she
> accepted Islam and emigrated."

**عبرت:** The books keep the names of the women too, and a course that skips them is skipping the
book.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TFO/E-FA4 · Four firsts, not one
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the first years at Mecca `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mecca lights.

**What happened:** People argue about who accepted Islam first, and the argument has been going on
for twelve hundred years. The book answers it by dividing it. خديجة ؓ was the first of the women.
أبو بكر ؓ was the first of the free men. زيد بن حارثة ؓ was the first of the freedmen. And علي ؓ is
said to be the first of the boys — he accepted Islam early, and, on the well-known view, before he
had reached the age of puberty. Each of the four is first, in his own class.

**The statement:**
> وأما علي ﵁ فأنه أسلم قديمًا وهو دون البلوغ على المشهور، ويقال: إنه أول من أسلم من الغلمان، كما أن خديجة أول من أسلم من النساء، وأبو بكر الصديق أول من أسلم من الرجال الأحرار، وزيد بن حارثة أول من أسلم من الموالي.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3700
> *English:* "As for علي ؓ, he accepted Islam early, while below the age of puberty, according to the
> well-known view. And it is said he was the first of the boys to accept Islam, just as خديجة was the
> first of the women, and أبو بكر الصديق the first of the free men, and زيد بن حارثة the first of the
> freedmen."

**عبرت:** Most arguments about who was first dissolve the moment you ask: first among whom?

**Hands-up?** Who has heard this question argued? Keep your hand up if you have heard an answer that
satisfied everyone in the room.

---

### TFO/E-FA5 · A narrator dismissed in three words
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** the reports, not the events `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A report was circulating in which علي ؓ claims priority for himself, and it came
through a man called حبّة ibn جوين. The author disposes of the chain with a pun on the man's name
that has been quoted ever since: حِبّة is not worth a ḥabba — a grain. Then he refuses the same
narrator again, twice more on the same page, and adds plainly that he is weak.

**The statement:**
> ورواه بعضهم عن مسلم الملائي، عن حبَّة بن جُوين، عن علي - وحِبَّة لا يساوي حَبَّة -.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3701
> *English:* "And some narrated it from مسلم الملائي, from حبّة ibn جوين, from علي — and حِبّة is not
> worth a grain."

**عبرت:** In this tradition a report is only ever as strong as the weakest man who carried it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TFO/E-FA6 · A report about علي ؓ that the book calls a lie
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reports, not the events `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** One report has علي ؓ saying that he worshipped God with the Messenger ﷺ for seven
years before anybody else worshipped Him. The author does not soften it and does not leave it for
the reader to judge. He writes five words and moves on. He then refuses a second report of the same
kind, and a third, one of them on the authority of البخاري himself. And he gives a summary over the
whole field: many hadiths have come saying علي ؓ was the first of this umma to accept Islam, and not
one of them is sound.

**The statement:**
> وهذا لا يصح أبدًا وهو كذب.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3701
> *English:* "And this is not sound at all; it is a lie."

**عبرت:** Praise invented for a great man is not praise; it is a lie told in his name.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TFO/E-FA7 · What he said from the pulpit of الكوفة
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate, 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights.

**What happened:** Against the reports he has just refused, the author sets one he says is
established by mass transmission. علي ؓ, as Commander of the Faithful, on the pulpit of his own
capital, before his own people, said: the best of this umma after its Prophet is أبو بكر, then عمر.
And he added that had he wished to name the third, he would have named him.

**The statement:**
> وقد ثبت عنه بالتواتر أنه قال على منبر الكوفة: أيها الناس: إن خير هذه الأمة بعد نبيها أبو بكر ثم عمر، ولو شئت أن أسمي الثالث لسميت (٤).
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3701
> *English:* "And it is established from him by tawātur that he said on the pulpit of الكوفة: O
> people, the best of this umma after its Prophet is أبو بكر, then عمر; and had I wished to name the
> third, I would have named him."

**عبرت:** When a man's own words are on record, they are worth more than anything said about him
afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA8 · Left behind in Mecca to return other people's property
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the Hijra, 1 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Mecca lit, the road to Medina drawn.

**What happened:** On the night of the Hijra علي ؓ stayed behind in Mecca, and the book gives the
reason in a single clause that is easy to miss. The people of Mecca had been leaving their valuables
with the Messenger ﷺ for safekeeping, because among his own people he was known as al-Amīn, the
trustworthy. Those deposits had to go back to their owners. The men who had driven him out of the
city were also the men whose property he refused to leave with.

**The statement:**
> وقد خلفه رسول الله ﷺ ليؤدي ما كان عنده ﵇ من ودائع الناس، فإنه كان يُعرف في قومه بالأمين، فكانوا يودعونه (الأموالَ و) الأشياءَ النفيسةَ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3702
> *English:* "And the Messenger of God ﷺ left him behind to discharge the deposits of the people
> which were with him, for he was known among his people as al-Amīn, and they used to deposit with
> him wealth and precious things."

**عبرت:** A trust is discharged even to the people who are trying to kill you.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA9 · The name given to a man asleep in the dust
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** at Medina `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina, the mosque.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had a disagreement at home and went out to the mosque and fell asleep on
the ground, and the dust stuck to his skin. The Messenger ﷺ came, found him lying there, and began
brushing the dust off him, calling him أبو تراب — father of dust. The author records this precisely
because, generations later, the name was used against him as a taunt; and the answer to the taunt is
that the Messenger ﷺ gave it, and the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥs.

**The statement:**
> فجاء رسول الله ﷺ فوجده نائمًا وقد لصق التراب بجلده فجعل ينفض عنه التراب ويقول: "اجلس أبا تراب (٤) ".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3703
> *English:* "And the Messenger of God ﷺ came and found him asleep with the dust clinging to his
> skin, and began brushing the dust off him and saying: 'Sit up, أبو تراب.'"

**عبرت:** A name given in affection can survive being turned into an insult.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA10 · The brotherhood — reported everywhere, authenticated nowhere
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after the Hijra `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina.

**What happened:** When the Messenger ﷺ paired the Muslims off as brothers, one report has علي ؓ
coming to him with his eyes streaming, saying: you have made brothers of your Companions and left me
without one. And the answer: you are my brother in this world and the next. The author gives the
story, names eight or nine separate Companions through whom it travels — and then says of the whole
family of reports that not one of the chains will bear a proof. This is the clearest case in the
chapter of a beautiful story that a careful reader still refuses to build on.

**The statement:**
> وأسانيدها كلها ضعيفة لا يقوم بشيء منها حجة والله أعلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3703
> *English:* "And their chains are all weak; no proof stands on any of them, and God knows best."

**عبرت:** There is a difference between a story worth telling and a report worth relying on, and a
careful man keeps the difference in view.

**Hands-up?** no

**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 2 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بدر lights.

> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3704
> *English:* "And the Messenger of God ﷺ handed him the banner that day, and he was twenty years old
> — الحكم said it, from مقسم, from ابن عباس."

**عبرت:** Responsibility in that generation went to whoever could carry it, not to whoever had

### TFO/E-FA12 · «لا سيف إلا ذو الفقار» — where the famous line comes from
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 2 AH, and long after `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بدر.

**What happened:** Everyone in this room has heard the couplet: there is no sword but ذو الفقار and
no youth but علي. The book gives it, and then gives ابن عساكر's verdict on it in the same breath.
The chain is broken. And the sword itself was the Messenger ﷺ's own share of the spoils at بدر, in
his own hand that day — it passed to علي ؓ only afterwards. So even the picture in the couplet is
out of sequence.

**The statement:**
> قال الحافظ ابن عساكر (٦): وهذا مرسل وإنما تنفل رسول الله ﷺ سيفه ذا الفقار (٧) يوم بدر ثم وهبه لعلي بعد ذلك.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۵۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3704
> *English:* "الحافظ ابن عساكر said: this is mursal; the Messenger of God ﷺ took ذو الفقار as his own
> share of the spoils at بدر and then gave it to علي afterwards."

**عبرت:** The lines everyone can recite are usually the ones nobody has checked.

**Hands-up?** Who here can recite the couplet? Now — who knows where it comes from?

### TFO/E-FA13 · The night the army could not sleep
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 7 AH, at خيبر `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** خيبر lights.

**What happened:** At خيبر the Messenger ﷺ said that in the morning he would give the banner to a man
who loves God and His Messenger and whom God and His Messenger love; a man who does not flee; and
God will grant the victory at his hands. The army spent that night surging and turning over which of
them it would be. عمر ؓ said afterwards that he had never wanted command in his life except on that
one night. In the morning it was given to علي ؓ. The author says this is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ
collections — the highest thing he says about anything in the whole chapter.

> فبات الناس يدوكون (٢) أيهم يعطاها حتى قال عمر: ما أحببت الإمارة إلا يومئذ، فلما أصبح أعطاها عليًا ففتح الله على يديه.

> *English:* "So the people passed the night surging over which of them would be given it, until عمر
> said: I never desired command except on that day. And when morning came he gave it to علي, and God
> granted victory at his hands."

**عبرت:** A word of praise from the Messenger ﷺ was worth more to those men than any command.

any one of them for himself would be dearer to him than red camels — the Arabs' way of naming the

walked out, saying he would not enter that house again.

> should have all the sun has risen upon."

**عبرت:** A man who knows what he heard with his own ears does not need to be told what to say.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA24 · The author throws away most of what he found about the marriage
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the reports, not the events `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The chapter on the marriage ends with a confession that tells you more about the
book than any single story in it. Many rejected and fabricated reports had come down on this
subject, and he had passed over them so the book would not grow long with them. One report he does
print — a full scene of the betrothal — he prints and then labels rejected, on the spot.

**The statement:**
> وقد ورد في هذا الفصل أحاديث كثيرة منكرة وموضوعة أضربنا عنها لئلا يطول الكتاب بها.

> *English:* "And in this section many rejected and fabricated hadiths have come down, which we have
> passed over lest the book grow long with them."

**عبرت:** What a historian leaves out is part of what he is telling you.

**Hands-up?** no

**عبرت:** Two reports that look like a contradiction are often two moments in the same life.

### TFO/E-FA29 · A hand on the thigh, and a rebuke
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 10 AH, at Medina `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina.

**What happened:** أبو سعيد الخدري ؓ had sworn to himself that he would report the whole business
when he reached Medina. He went to the Messenger ﷺ and began listing what they had suffered. He got
about halfway. Then a hand came down on his thigh, and he was told: less of your talk against your
brother. He said afterwards that he sat there thinking, may your mother lose you — you have been in
the wrong all day and did not know it.

### TFO/E-FA32 · «من كنت مولاه فعلي مولاه»

preserved one.

### TFO/E-FA36 · How many stood — and why the books do not agree

> Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'Whoever's mawlā I am, علي is his mawlā.'"

**عبرت:** An honest record keeps the numbers it was given, even when they disagree.

### TFO/E-FA41 · «لا والله ما صح شيء من ذلك»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the 8th century AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** That story about the bird is one of the most widely repeated reports in the
literature. الحاكم, a great collector, said more than thirty people narrated it and that it was
soundly established from three Companions. الذهبي — the author's own teacher — is quoted answering
both claims. To the first: separate out from those thirty one trustworthy man with a sound chain. To
the second, he does not hedge at all.

**The statement:**
> قال شيخنا أبو عبد الله: لا والله ما صح شيء من ذلك.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3725
> *English:* "Our shaykh أبو عبد الله [الذهبي] said: no, by God, nothing of that is sound."

**عبرت:** A large number of chains can mean a report travelled widely, and nothing more than that.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA42 · Two books, written on opposite sides of one short report
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 3rd–5th centuries AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The author mentions, almost in passing, that he has seen a whole volume by
الطبري — the historian and Qur'anic commentator — collecting every route and wording of that one
report. And then a large volume by القاضي الباقلاني rejecting it, in chain and in text. That is what
this tradition looks like from the inside: two great scholars, each spending a book on a single
sentence, and a third scholar reading both and telling you where he lands.

**The statement:**
> ورأيت فيه مجلدًا في جميع طرقه وألفاظه لأبي جعفر بن جرير الطبري المفسر صاحب التاريخ، ثم وقفت على مجلد كبير في رده وتضعيفه سندًا ومتنًا للقاضي أبي بكر الباقلاني المتكلّم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۸۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3729
> *English:* "And I have seen a volume on all its routes and wordings by أبو جعفر ibn جرير الطبري, the
> exegete, the author of the History. Then I came upon a large volume rejecting and weakening it, in
> chain and in text, by القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني the theologian."

**عبرت:** This is a tradition in which a single sentence can be worth two books of argument, and
still not be settled.

**Hands-up?** How much do you think has been written, in fourteen centuries, about one sentence?

> *English:* "It is established in الصحيح that it was revealed concerning علي and حمزة and عبيدة among
> the believers, and عتبة and شيبة and الوليد ibn عتبة among the disbelievers."

**عبرت:** The true thing is usually smaller and more specific than the claim it replaces.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TFO/E-FA50 · أبو بكر ؓ moves along the bench
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** at Medina `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina, the mosque.

**What happened:** The Messenger ﷺ was sitting in the mosque with his Companions around him when
علي ؓ came in, gave the greeting, and stood looking for somewhere to sit. The Messenger ﷺ looked
round at their faces to see who would make room. أبو بكر ؓ, who was on his right, shifted over and
said: here, أبو الحسن. And أنس ؓ, who was watching, says they saw the gladness in the Messenger ﷺ's
face. Then he turned to أبو بكر ؓ and said one sentence.

**The statement:**
> "يا أبا بكر إنما يعرف الفضل لأهل الفضل [ذوو الفضل] ".
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3737
> *English:* "'أبو بكر, only the people of merit recognise merit in the people of merit.'"

**عبرت:** Recognising another man's worth is itself a mark of worth.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TFO/E-FA51 · «أنا مدينة العلم وعلي بابها» — taken apart by name
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reports, not the events `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** This is probably the most quoted sentence about him after غدير خم. The author
prints it, prints الترمذي's grading of the shorter form as strange and rejected, and then prints
ابن عدي's account of exactly how it came into circulation, including the name of the man it is known
from and the claim that another narrator stole it from him. He closes with أبو الفتح الأزدي's verdict
over the whole subject.

**The statement:**
> وقال أبو الفتح الأزدي (٥): لا يصح في هذا الباب شيء.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3738
> *English:* "And أبو الفتح الأزدي said: nothing in this chapter is sound."

**عبرت:** A sentence can be famous for a thousand years and still never have been said.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TFO/E-FA52 · «علي أقضانا» — what عمر ؓ actually said about his learning
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during عمر ؓ's caliphate, 13–23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina.

**What happened:** Having refused the famous hadith, the author immediately supplies what does
stand, and it is better than the hadith. عمر ؓ used to say: علي is the best judge among us, and
أُبَيّ is the best reader of the Qur'an among us. And he used to say something else, which is the
sentence a room remembers: I seek refuge with God from a hard problem with no أبو الحسن for it.

**The statement:**
> وقد ثبت عن عمر أنه كان يقول: علي أقضانا وأبيٌّ أقرؤنا للقرآن. وكان عمر يقول: أعوذ بالله من معضلة ولا أبو حسن لها.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3739
> *English:* "And it is established from عمر that he used to say: علي is the best judge among us, and
> أُبَيّ is the best reader of the Qurʾān among us. And عمر used to say: I seek refuge with God from a
> hard problem with no أبو الحسن for it."

**عبرت:** The true praise, from a man who worked beside him, outlasts the invented praise.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA53 · Sent to judge in Yemen, and too young for it
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 10 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Yemen.

**What happened:** He was sent to Yemen to judge between people, and he said so plainly: I was young
in years and I had no knowledge of judging. He was struck on the chest and prayed for — God will
guide your heart and make your tongue firm. And he said afterwards that he never doubted in a
judgement between two men again.

**The statement:**
> فضرب في صدري وقال: "إن الله سيهدي قلبك ويثبت لسانك" قال: فما شككتُ في قضاء بين اثنين بعد.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3739
> *English:* "So he struck my chest and said: 'God will guide your heart and make your tongue firm.'
> And I never doubted in a judgement between two people afterwards."

**عبرت:** The men who did the work of that generation began by saying honestly that they were not
ready for it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA54 · «جاء علي؟» — the last morning
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الأول 11 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** Medina.

**What happened:** أم سلمة ؓ swore to it. In those last days they came to visit him morning after
morning, and he kept asking: has علي come? She thought he had been sent on some errand. When he
came, everyone left the room and sat outside by the door; she was nearest to it. And علي ؓ leaned
over him and they spoke quietly together. He passed away that same day.

**The statement:**
> فأكب عليه عليٌّ، فجعل يسارُّه ويناجيه، ثم قبض من يومه ذلك، فكان أقرب الناس به عهدًا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3740
> *English:* "And علي leaned over him and began speaking to him quietly and confidentially. Then he
> passed away that same day, and so he was the last of the people to have covenant with him."

**عبرت:** The last conversation of a life is remembered by whoever was nearest the door.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA55 · «والحديث ضعيف» — the hadith of the three groups
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reports, not the events `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** There is a hadith, quoted constantly whenever the wars of his caliphate come up,
in which he is said to have been commanded to fight three named groups — and commentators identify
them as the people of الجمل, the people of الشام, and the خوارج. It is the single most convenient
text anybody has for settling those wars from one side. The author names it, gives the standard
identification, and then grades it in three words, and this course goes no further than he does.

**The statement:**
> وفسروا الناكثين بأصحاب الجمل والقاسطين بأهل الشام والمارقين بالخوارج، والحديث ضعيف.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3742
> *English:* "And they explained the الناكثين as the people of الجمل, the القاسطين as the people of
> الشام, and the المارقين as the خوارج. And the hadith is weak."

**عبرت:** The text that would settle the argument most conveniently is the one to examine most
carefully.

**Hands-up?** no

### TFO/E-FA56 · A vial of perfume in his sleeve
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** during his caliphate, 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** He stood before the people as Commander of the Faithful and swore by God, other
than whom there is no god, that he had taken nothing from their wealth, little or much — except
this. And he pulled a small glass vial of perfume out of his sleeve and said that a Persian
landholder had given it to him as a gift. Then he went to the treasury and told them: take.

**The statement:**
> أيها الناس! والله الذي لا إله إلا هو ما رزأتُ (٤) من مالكم [لا] قليلًا ولا كثيرًا إلَّا هذه - وأخرج قارورة من كُمِّ قميصه فيها طيب -.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3742
> *English:* "O people! By God, other than whom there is no god, I have taken nothing from your
> wealth, little or much, except this — and he brought out from the sleeve of his shirt a small vial
> containing perfume."

**عبرت:** A ruler who can account for every item he owns has already answered most of the questions
that will ever be asked of him.

**Hands-up?** What would a ruler have to produce, today, to make that claim in public?

## The people: the Companions who stood back

*Source note: [`the-companions-who-stood-back.md`](../docs/research/the-companions-who-stood-back.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TCW/E-SB1 · Ten thousand dead and almost no Companions present
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED]` — the month of the battle is not on the fetched
pages `[STANDARD]` *(to verify)* · **Map:** البصرة lights; nothing moves.

**What happened:** When the fighting at the Camel was over, the count of the dead was about ten
thousand men, five thousand from each of the two armies. The wounded were past counting. But when
the historians ask how many of the Prophet's ﷺ own Companions were in either army, the answer is
startling. They were tens of thousands of men alive in the world that year, and of all of them not a
hundred were on that field. One of the earliest reporters says they did not even reach thirty.

**The statement:**
> وقال الإمام أحمد: حدَّثنا إسماعيل، حدَّثنا أيوب، عن محمد بن سيرين قال: هاجت الفتنة وأصحاب رسول الله ﷺ عشرات ألوف فلم يحضرها منهم مئة، بل لم يبلغوا ثلاثين.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ جـ۷ ص۴۲۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3573
> *English:* "Imām Aḥmad said: Ismāʿīl related to us, Ayyūb related to us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: the fitna broke out while the Companions of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ were tens of thousands, and not a hundred of them were present at it — rather they did not reach thirty."

**عبرت:** The best-instructed generation in the history of this ummah, faced with a fight between
its own, overwhelmingly chose not to be in it.

**Hands-up?** How many of the Prophet's ﷺ Companions do you think fought at the Camel — hands for
more than a thousand, hands for fewer than a hundred?

---

### TCW/E-SB2 · The four who came through the fitna safe
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Later scholars kept a short list of the famous men who came out of these years
untouched by what happened in them. Wakīʿ names four. Every one of them is a man the room already
knows from the conquests and from the Prophet's ﷺ own lifetime. Not one of them is obscure, and not
one of them is a man who could be called too weak or too young to matter.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ وَكِيْعٌ: سَلِمَ مِنَ الفِتْنَةِ مِنَ المَعْرُوْفِيْنَ: سَعْدٌ، وَابْنُ عُمَرَ، وَأُسَامَةُ بنُ زَيْدٍ، وَمُحَمَّدُ بنُ مَسْلَمَةَ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۵۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2480
> *English:* "Wakīʿ said: those of the well-known men who came through the fitna safe were Saʿd, Ibn ʿUmar, Usāma ibn Zayd and Muḥammad ibn Maslama."

**عبرت:** The word used of them is not that they were right, but that they came through safe — and
those are two different claims.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB3 · Saʿd ؓ among his sheep, and his son's rebuke
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة lights; a pin outside it for the
pasture.

**What happened:** The conqueror of Iraq, the commander at Qādisiyya, one of the ten and one of the
six of the shūrā, had taken himself out to his sheep. His son ʿUmar came riding out to him. Saʿd ؓ
saw him coming and said aloud that he took refuge with God from the evil of this rider. The son
reached him and asked how his father could be content to live like a bedouin among his animals while
the people were contending over rule at Medina. Saʿd ؓ struck him on the chest and told him to be
quiet, and then told him why.

**The statement:**
> فَضَرَبَ صَدْرَ عُمَرَ وَقَالَ: اسْكُتْ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ -صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ- يَقُوْلُ (٢) : (إِنَّ اللهَ -عَزَّ وَجَلَّ- يُحِبُّ العَبْدَ التَّقِيَّ، الغَّنِيَّ، الخَفِيَّ (٣)) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۱ ص۱۰۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1528
> *English:* "He struck ʿUmar's chest and said: Be quiet — for I heard the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ say: God, mighty and majestic, loves the servant who is God-fearing, self-sufficient, obscure."

**عبرت:** A man can be told by his own household that his stillness is cowardice and still know what
he is standing on.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB4 · A sword with two eyes and a tongue
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Saʿd ؓ was asked, again and again, to come out and take a side. His answer went
past the question. He said he made no claim to the caliphate at all, that he had done his fighting
and knew what fighting was, and that he would not destroy himself over a better man than himself.
Then he named his condition. He would fight when someone brought him a sword that could see and
speak — a sword that would say, of the man in front of him, whether he was a believer or not.

**The statement:**
> لاَ أُقَاتِلُ حَتَّى يَأْتُوْنِي بِسَيْفٍ لَهُ عَيْنَانِ وَلِسَانٌ، فَيَقُوْلَ: هَذَا مُؤْمِنٌ، وَهَذَا كَافِرٌ (٣) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۱ ص۱۱۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1544
> *English:* "I will not fight until they bring me a sword that has two eyes and a tongue, so that it says: this is a believer, and this is an unbeliever."

**عبرت:** He did not say that both sides were wrong. He said that a sword cannot tell them apart,
and that he would not be the one holding it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB5 · The sword that turns aside from a Muslim
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A second son of Saʿd ؓ, ʿĀmir, came to him with the same request, and this time
it was more than a request. He wanted his father to be at the head of men. Saʿd ؓ answered him with
a question of his own, and then with a second image for the same refusal. He would take a sword when
he was given one that could not cut a Muslim.

**The statement:**
> أَيْ بُنَيَّ! أَفِي الفِتْنَةِ تَأْمُرُنِي أَنْ أَكُوْنَ رَأْساً؟ لاَ وَاللهِ، حَتَّى أُعْطَى سَيْفاً، إِنْ ضَرَبْتُ بِهِ مُسْلِماً نَبَا عَنْهُ، وَإِنْ ضَرَبْتُ كَافِراً قَتَلَهُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۱ ص۱۱۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1545
> *English:* "My son! Is it in the fitna that you order me to be a head? No, by God — not until I am given a sword which, if I strike a Muslim with it, turns aside from him, and if I strike an unbeliever, kills him."

**عبرت:** The pressure to take a side came from inside the house before it came from anywhere else.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB6 · ʿUmar ؓ's last word about Saʿd ؓ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 23 AH `[STANDARD]` *(to verify — the page does not date it)* ·
**Map:** المدينة · الكوفة.

**What happened:** When ʿUmar ؓ was dying he set the matter in the hands of six men and gave an
instruction about one of them by name. If the choice fell on Saʿd ؓ, well and good. If it did not,
then whoever became caliph was to make use of him. And then ʿUmar ؓ said the thing he wanted on the
record, because he had removed Saʿd ؓ from Kūfa and everybody knew it. He had not removed him for
weakness and he had not removed him for treachery.

**The statement:**
> وَقَالَ: مَنِ اسْتَخْلَفُوْهُ فَهُوَ الخَلِيْفَةُ بَعْدِي، وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْ سَعْداً، وَإِلاَّ فَلْيَسْتَعِنْ بِهِ الخَلِيْفَةُ بَعْدِي، فَإِنَّنِي لَمْ أَنْزَعْهُ -يَعْنِي: عَنِ الكُوْفَةِ- مِنْ ضَعْفٍ وَلاَ خِيَانَةٍ (٢) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۱ ص۱۱۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1544
> *English:* "And he said: whomever they appoint, he is the caliph after me. If it falls to Saʿd, then so; and if not, let the caliph after me seek his help — for I did not remove him, meaning from Kūfa, for weakness or for treachery."

**عبرت:** A reputation cleared in advance is worth more than a defence made afterwards.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB7 · Two of the four were at the arbitration
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37–38 AH `[STANDARD]` *(to verify)* · **Map:** أذرح.

**What happened:** Refusing to fight did not mean going away. Two of the four men on the short list —
Saʿd ؓ and Ibn ʿUmar ؓ — were present when the two arbitrators met. The report is a single line and
says nothing about what either of them did there. Saʿd ؓ is separately placed on that journey by
another report in the same chapter, which mentions in passing that the party was held fifty nights
at Sargh because plague had fallen on Syria.

**The statement:**
> ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ: عَنْ عَمْرٍو قَالَ: شَهِدَ سَعْدٌ وَابْنُ عُمَرَ الحَكَمَيْنِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۱ ص۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1522
> *English:* "Ibn ʿUyayna, from ʿAmr, who said: Saʿd and Ibn ʿUmar were present at the two arbitrators."

**عبرت:** Standing out of a fight is not the same as staying away from the problem.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB8 · Do not fall upon my brothers
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** not dated on the page; after the fighting began `[STANDARD]`
*(to verify)* · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** A man in Saʿd ؓ's hearing had made a habit of reviling ʿAlī ؓ and Ṭalḥa ؓ and
al-Zubayr ؓ. Saʿd ؓ had fought in the army of none of them. And it was Saʿd ؓ who kept stopping the
man's mouth, with one sentence, and the sentence names them as his own.

**The statement:**
> أَنَّ رَجُلاً كَانَ يَقَعُ فِي عَلِيٍّ، وَطَلْحَةَ، وَالزُّبَيْرِ، فَجَعَلَ سَعْدٌ يَنْهَاهُ، وَيَقُوْلُ:
> لاَ تَقَعْ فِي إِخْوَانِي.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۱ ص۱۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1542
> *English:* "A man used to fall upon ʿAlī, Ṭalḥa and al-Zubayr, and Saʿd kept forbidding him, saying: Do not fall upon my brothers."

**عبرت:** The men who would not fight for either side are also the men who would not let either side
be insulted.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB9 · I held my hand back and did not regret
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** The son of ʿUmar ؓ lived through all of it and was asked about it for forty
years. His answer is one sentence long and it has two halves, and the second half is the part people
forget. He says he held his hand back. He says he never regretted it. And then, without being asked,
he says that the man who fights for the truth is better than he is.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ: كَفَفْتُ يَدِي، فَلَمْ أَندَمْ، وَالمُقَاتِلُ عَلَى الحَقِّ أَفْضَلُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۳ ص۲۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2822
> *English:* "Ibn ʿUmar said: I held my hand back, and I did not regret it — and the one who fights for the truth is better."

**عبرت:** He would not take back his own choice and he would not turn it into a charge against
anybody else.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB10 · A whole house worth less than a hundred dirhams
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** not dated on the page `[STANDARD]` *(to verify)* · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The same man who transmitted the sentence about holding back also visited Ibn
ʿUmar ؓ at home and did what a visitor does not usually do. He priced the contents. Every piece of
furniture in the house of the son of the second caliph, taken together, was not worth a hundred
dirhams. The two reports sit side by side on the page, and the second explains why nobody could
allege that the first was self-interest.

**The statement:**
> وَلَقَدْ دَخَلْتُ عَلَى ابْنِ عُمَرَ، فَقَوَّمْتُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فِي بَيْتِهِ مِنْ أَثَاثٍ مَا يَسْوَى مائَةَ دِرْهَمٍ (٢) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۳ ص۲۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2822
> *English:* "And I entered upon Ibn ʿUmar and priced every piece of furniture in his house: it was not worth a hundred dirhams."

**عبرت:** A man who wants nothing is very hard to accuse of wanting something.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TCW/E-SB11 · Umm al-Muʾminīn ؓ asks why he stayed silent
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** not dated on the page; after 36 AH `[STANDARD]` *(to verify)* ·
**Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** Long afterwards, ʿĀʾisha ؓ put a question to Ibn ʿUmar ؓ about the journey she
had made to Basra. She asked what had prevented him from forbidding her. He gave her a plain answer
about what he had judged at the time and about a man whose view he thought she would not go against.
The report ends there. Neither the book nor we go any further with it.

**The statement:**
> قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ لابْنِ عُمَرَ: مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَنْهَانِي عَنْ مَسِيْرِي؟
> قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ رَجُلاً قَدِ اسْتَوْلَى عَلَيْكِ، وَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّكِ لَنْ تُخَالِفِيْهِ - يَعْنِي: ابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ -.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۳ ص۲۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2820
> *English:* "ʿĀʾisha said to Ibn ʿUmar: What kept you from forbidding me my journey? He said: I saw a man who had prevailed with you, and I supposed you would not go against him — meaning Ibn al-Zubayr."

**عبرت:** The question she asked is the one the silent men had to live with: was there a word I
could have said earlier.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB12 · The caliphate offered, and one man in the way
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** after the death of يزيد — conventionally 64 AH `[STANDARD]`
*(to verify — the page gives only the event, not the year)* · **Map:** المدينة · المشرق lit faintly.

**What happened:** Twenty-eight years later the caliphate was lying in the road. Yazīd was dead, the
Umayyads were fighting each other for it, and Marwān came to Ibn ʿUmar ؓ and asked for his hand,
calling him the lord of the Arabs and the son of their lord. Ibn ʿUmar ؓ asked one practical
question: what would be done about the people of the east, who would not accept him. Marwān told him
the obvious answer, that they would be beaten until they gave the pledge. And Ibn ʿUmar ؓ closed the
conversation.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: وَاللهِ مَا أُحِبُّ أَنَّهَا دَانَتْ لِي سبعِيْنَ سَنَةً، وَأَنَّهُ قُتلَ فِي سَيْفِي رَجُلٌ وَاحِدٌ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۳ ص۲۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2825
> *English:* "He said: By God, I would not wish it to submit to me for seventy years, at the cost of one single man being killed by my sword."

**عبرت:** He had refused to fight for someone else's right; he was not going to start fighting for
his own.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB13 · What will you do about لا إله إلا الله
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reason is dated to the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime; the withdrawal to 36–40
AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Years before any of this, on a raid, Usāma ؓ had struck down a man who spoke the
shahāda as the sword came down, because he judged that the man had said it to save himself. The
Prophet ﷺ asked him what he would do about those words on the Day of Rising, and kept asking. Usāma ؓ
never forgot it. When the fighting between Muslims began, al-Dhahabī says the debt was paid — the man
held his hand back and kept to his house, and al-Dhahabī adds one word of his own about the choice.

**The statement:**
> قُلْتُ: انْتَفَعَ أُسَامَةُ مِنْ يَوْمِ النَّبِيِّ -صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ- إِذْ يَقُوْلُ لَهُ: (كَيْفَ (٣) بِلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۵۰۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2480
> اللهُ يَا أُسَامَةُ) . فَكَفَّ يَدَهُ، وَلَزِمَ مَنْزِلَهُ، فَأَحْسَنَ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۵۰۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2481
> *English:* "I say: Usāma profited from the Prophet's ﷺ day, when he said to him: 'What will you do about لا إله إلا الله, Usāma?' So he held back his hand and kept to his house — and he did well."

**عبرت:** One sentence from the Prophet ﷺ, taken seriously for thirty years, decided a man's whole
conduct in the worst year of his life.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB14 · Muḥammad ibn Maslama ؓ and his wooden sword
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة, then الربذة east of it.

**What happened:** Muḥammad ibn Maslama ؓ was a man of Badr and of every battle after it, and the
man ʿUmar ؓ used to send out whenever a governor was complained of. He was not present at the Camel
and he was not at Ṣiffīn. What he did instead is the detail nobody forgets. He made himself a sword
out of wood, and he moved out of Medina to Rabadha on the Iraq road, and he stayed there.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ -رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ- مِمَّنِ اعْتَزَلَ الفِتْنَةَ، وَلاَ حَضَرَ الجَمَلَ، وَلاَ صِفِّيْنَ؛ بَلِ اتَّخَذَ سَيْفاً مِنْ خَشَبٍ، وَتَحَوَّلَ إِلَى الرَّبَذَةِ، فَأَقَامَ بِهَا مُدَيْدَةً (٢) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۳۶۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2349
> *English:* "And he — may God be pleased with him — was among those who withdrew from the fitna. He was not present at al-Jamal, nor at Ṣiffīn; rather he took to himself a sword of wood, and moved out to al-Rabadha, and stayed there a short while."

**عبرت:** He did not put the sword down. He carried one that could not kill, so that everybody who
looked at him understood the position without asking.

**Hands-up?** A man refuses to fight. Does he leave his sword at home, or carry one?

### TCW/E-SB15 · Break your sword and sit in your house
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الربذة.

**What happened:** Travellers passing Rabadha came upon his tent, and one of them said what
everybody said to these men: come out to the people, command what is right, forbid what is wrong.
Muḥammad ibn Maslama ؓ answered by telling them what the Prophet ﷺ had told him to do when this day
came. Then he added four words about what he had actually done with the instruction.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: قَالَ لِي النَّبِيُّ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ -: (يَا مُحَمَّدُ، سَتُكُوْنُ فُرْقَةٌ، وَفِتْنَةٌ، وَاخْتِلاَفٌ، فَاكْسِرْ سَيْفَكَ، وَاقْطَعْ وَتَرَكَ، وَاجْلِسْ فِي بَيْتِكَ) . فَفَعَلْتُ مَا أَمَرَنِي (٢) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۳۷۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2351
> *English:* "He said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: O Muḥammad, there will be division, and fitna, and disagreement — so break your sword, and cut your bowstring, and sit in your house. And I did what he ordered me."

**عبرت:** Sitting still was, for him, not the absence of an order. It was the order.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB16 · Strike Uḥud with it until it breaks
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 36–40 AH `[SOURCED, second wording]` · **Map:** أحد, then الربذة.

**What happened:** The same instruction is carried in the same chapter in a second, longer form,
through a different chain, and the two are not identical. In this one the Prophet ﷺ hands him a
sword and gives him the whole of its working life in a sentence. Fight the idolaters with it. Then,
when the Muslims turn on one another, take it to the rock of Uḥud and strike until it breaks. Then
sit at home, and wait.

**The statement:**
> أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ -صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ- أَعْطَى مُحَمَّدَ بنَ مَسْلَمَةَ سَيْفاً، فَقَالَ: (قَاتِلْ بِهِ المُشْرِكِيْنَ، فَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ المُسْلِمِيْنَ قَدْ أَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ، فَاضْرِبْ بِهِ أُحُداً حَتَّى تَقْطَعَهُ، ثُمَّ اجْلِسْ فِي بَيْتِكَ حَتَّى تَأْتَيَكَ يَدٌ خَاطِئَةٌ، أَوْ مَنِيَّةٌ قَاضِيَةٌ (٣)) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۳۷۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2353
> *English:* "The Prophet ﷺ gave Muḥammad ibn Maslama a sword and said: Fight the idolaters with it. Then, when you see the Muslims turning upon one another, strike Uḥud with it until you break it; then sit in your house until there comes to you an erring hand, or a decreeing death."

**عبرت:** Two chains carry one instruction in two shapes, and an honest telling gives both rather
than choosing the better story.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB17 · Ḥudhayfa ؓ knew one man the fitna would spare
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** before 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** Ḥudhayfa ؓ was the Companion the others went to about the fitna, because the
Prophet ﷺ had told him what was coming. He said once that there was nobody at all over whom he did
not fear the fitna, except one man. Those who heard him came to Medina and found a tent pitched,
and in it was Muḥammad ibn Maslama ؓ. In another telling of the same scene the man
himself explains his rule in one line: he would take no part in anything of their garrison towns
until the matter cleared up however it cleared up.

**The statement:**
> هِشَامٌ: عَنِ ابْنِ سِيْرِيْنَ، عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ، قَالَ:
> مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلاَّ وَأَنَا أَخَافُ عَلَيْهِ الفِتْنَةَ إِلاَّ مَا كَانَ مِنْ مُحَمَّدِ بنِ مَسْلَمَةَ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعتُ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ -صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ- يَقُوْلُ: (لاَ تَضُرُّهُ الفِتْنَةُ) (٥) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۳۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2352
> *English:* "Ḥudhayfa said: There is no one over whom I do not fear the fitna, except Muḥammad ibn Maslama — for I heard the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ say: the fitna will not harm him."

**عبرت:** The man least afraid of the coming trouble was the one who had been told exactly what to
do when it arrived.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB18 · A man from Jordan breaks into his house
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 43 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدينة.

**What happened:** Muʿāwiya ؓ came, and the people of Syria with him. News of what Muḥammad ibn
Maslama ؓ had done reached a wretched man of the people of Jordan, and the report names exactly what
it was that reached him. It was his sitting back — from ʿAlī and from Muʿāwiya both. The man forced
his way into the house and killed him. The same chapter separately records four named authorities
and a group giving his death as Ṣafar of the year 43, and gives his age as seventy-seven.

**The statement:**
> فَبَلَغَ رَجُلاً شَقِيّاً مِنْ أَهْلِ الأُرْدُنِّ صَنِيْعُ مُحَمَّدِ بنِ مَسْلَمَةَ - جُلُوْسُهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ وَمُعَاوِيَةَ - فَاقْتَحَمَ عَلَيْهِ المَنْزِلَ، فَقَتَلَهُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۲ ص۳۷۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2353
> *English:* "And news reached a wretched man of the people of Jordan of what Muḥammad ibn Maslama had done — his sitting back from ʿAlī and from Muʿāwiya — so he broke in upon him in his dwelling and killed him."

**عبرت:** Refusing both sides did not buy him safety. The report names his sitting back as the very
thing that brought the man to his door.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB19 · A sword on the shoulder, stopped in the street
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** not dated on the page; before الجمل, 36 AH `[STANDARD]`
*(to verify)* · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** Al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays set out, meaning to join ʿAlī ؓ and help him.
Abū Bakra ؓ met him on the way and asked where he was going. Al-Aḥnaf told him the truth — that he
was going to help the cousin of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ. Abū Bakra ؓ told him to turn round, and
gave him a reason that was not an opinion and not a calculation. It was a ḥadīth he had heard
himself, and when he had heard it he had asked the Prophet ﷺ the obvious objection, and been
answered.

**The statement:**
> قال: خرجت وأنا أريد هذا الرجل، فلقيني أبو بكرة، فقال: أين تريد يا أحنف؟ قال: قلت: أريد نصر ابن عم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، يعني عليا، قال: فقال لي: يا أحنف ارجع، فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إذا تواجه المسلمان بسيفيهما، فالقاتل والمقتول في النار " قلت: يا رسول الله هذا القاتل، فما بال المقتول؟ قال: " إنه كان حريصا على قتل صاحبه ".
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۳ ص۸, الهامش · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2617
> *English:* "He said: I went out intending to join this man, and Abū Bakra met me and said: Where are you going, O Aḥnaf? I said: I intend to help the cousin of the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ — meaning ʿAlī. He said to me: O Aḥnaf, go back, for I heard the Messenger of Allāh ﷺ say: 'When two Muslims face one another with their swords, the killer and the killed are both in the Fire.' I said: Messenger of Allāh, this is the killer — but what of the one killed? He said: 'He was eager to kill his companion.'"

**عبرت:** He did not argue about who was in the right. He said what the two swords do to the two men
holding them, and left it there.

**Hands-up?** A man is on his way to help the side he believes is right. What would stop you?

### TCW/E-SB20 · Where is the one who held back?
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH, days after the battle `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** Days after the battle, the people of Basra came in to give the pledge, and the son
of Abū Bakra ؓ came with them. ʿAlī ؓ took his hand and then asked after his father by a name, and
the name was a comment: where is the one who held back? The son said his father was ill and that he
was eager for whatever pleased the Commander of the Faithful. ʿAlī ؓ told him to walk ahead. Then the
caliph walked to the sickbed of the man who had told people not to fight for him, and visited him,
and heard his excuse, and accepted it.

**The statement:**
> فقال له علي: أين المتربص (٦)؟ -يعني أباه- فقال: إنه والله مريض يا أمير المؤمنين، وإنه (٧) على مسرتك لحريص. فقال: امش أمامي، فمضى إليه فعاده، واعتذر إليه أبو بكرة فعذره
> — البدایہ والنہایہ جـ۷ ص۴۲۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3571
> *English:* "ʿAlī said to him: Where is the one who held back? — meaning his father. He said: By God, he is ill, O Commander of the Faithful, and he is eager for what pleases you. He said: Walk ahead of me. So he went to him and visited him in his illness, and Abū Bakra excused himself to him, and he accepted his excuse."

**عبرت:** The man who won the battle walked to the house of the man who would not fight in it, and
the visit was the answer to the question.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB21 · A province offered, and declined for another man
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة lights and stays lit.

**What happened:** Having accepted his excuse, ʿAlī ؓ then offered Abū Bakra ؓ the government of
Basra itself — the largest command in Iraq, handed to a man who had publicly told people not to
take up arms. Abū Bakra ؓ declined it. He gave a reason of policy rather than of piety: the city
needed a man of the caliph's own house whom the people would settle to. And he named one. ʿAlī ؓ
took the advice and appointed Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ.

**The statement:**
> وعرض عليه البصرة (فامتنع وقال: رجل من أهلك يسكن إليه الناس،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ جـ۷ ص۴۲۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3571
> وأشار إليه بابن عباس فولاه على البصرة)،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ جـ۷ ص۴۲۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3572
> *English:* "And he offered him Basra, but he declined and said: a man of your own house, whom the people will settle to — and he pointed him to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he appointed him over Basra."

**عبرت:** Refusing to fight for a man did not mean refusing to advise him.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB22 · The colonnade he would not pray in
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the governorship of زياد, after 45 AH `[STANDARD]` *(to verify)* ·
**Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** A man brought timber into Basra to sell. The governor wanted it, the man would
not sell, and the governor took it from him and built with it the colonnade of the great mosque of
Basra. Abū Bakra ؓ — who was the governor's own brother by their mother — never prayed under that
roof. He kept it up until the colonnade came down.

**The statement:**
> جَلَبَ رَجُلٌ خَشَباً، فَطَلَبَهُ زِيَادٌ، فَأَبَى أَنْ يَبِيْعَهُ، فَغَصَبَهُ إِيَّاهُ، وَبَنَى صُفَّةَ مَسْجِدِ البَصْرَةِ.
> قَالَ: فَلَمْ يُصَلِّ أَبُو بَكْرَةَ فِيْهَا حَتَّى قُلِعَتْ (٤) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۳ ص۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2616
> *English:* "A man brought in timber, and Ziyād asked for it, and he refused to sell it, so he seized it from him and built with it the colonnade of the mosque of Basra. He said: and Abū Bakra never prayed in it until it was pulled down."

**عبرت:** The man who would not draw a sword against a wrong still refused, every single day, to
stand under it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TCW/E-SB23 · The one thing he feared living to see
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** before his death, which the same chapter gives as 51 or 52 AH
`[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** Abū Bakra ؓ was injured at a burial and carried home unconscious, and his
children — twenty of them, sons and daughters — cried out over him. He came round and told them to
stop, and said something that alarmed them more than the injury had: that there was no soul whose
departure was dearer to him than his own. They asked him why, and he told them what he was afraid of
outliving.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ: إِنِّيْ أَخْشَى أَنْ أُدْرِكَ زَمَاناً لاَ أَسْتَطِيْعُ أَنْ آمُرَ بِمَعْرُوْفٍ، وَلاَ أَنْهَى عَنْ مُنْكَرٍ، وَمَا خَيْرٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ (٣) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جـ۳ ص۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2616
> *English:* "He said: I fear to live to see a time in which I can neither command what is right nor forbid what is wrong — and there is no good on that day."

**عبرت:** What frightened him was not dying in the fitna but surviving into a silence he could not
break.

**Hands-up?** no
