### POT/E-PH55 · Al-Jamal: the arrow, and then the safe-conduct
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرہ.

**What happened:** ابن سعد رحمہ اللہ says that مروان fought hardest of all on the day of الجمل; and that when he saw the rout he shot طلحۃ ؓ with an arrow and killed him. He was wounded himself that day, carried to a woman's house and treated there, and went into hiding. Then علي ؓ gave him security, and he gave علي ؓ the بیعہ, and was sent back to المدینہ. The book records every part of that without a word of comment, including the last part.

**The statement:**
> وَقَاتَلَ يَوْمَ الجَمَلِ أَشَدَّ قِتَالٍ، فَلَمَّا رَأَى الهَزِيْمَةَ (٢) ، رَمَى طَلْحَةَ بِسَهْمٍ، فَقَتَلَهُ، وَجُرِحَ يَوْمَئِذٍ، فَحُمِلَ إِلَى بَيْتِ امْرَأَةٍ، فَدَاوَوْهُ، وَاخْتَفَى، فَأَمَّنَهُ عَلِيٌّ، فَبَايَعَهُ، وَرُدَّ إِلَى المَدِيْنَةِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3087
> *English:* "He fought hardest of all on the day of al-Jamal; and when he saw the rout he shot Ṭalḥah with an arrow and killed him. He was wounded that day and was carried to a woman's house, and they treated him, and he went into hiding. Then ʿAlī gave him safe-conduct, and he gave him the bayʿah, and he was sent back to Madīnah."

**عبرت:** A man who has the power to take revenge and gives safe-conduct instead has ended something that fighting could not end.

**Hands-up?** no

### POT/E-PH56 · "A close kinship inclines me toward him"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرہ.

**What happened:** الشافعي رحمہ اللہ reports that after the rout on the day of الجمل, علي ؓ asked after مروان — the man who had just killed طلحۃ ؓ — and this is what he said about him. Tell it immediately after the previous card and say nothing over it. Every person on both sides of that field was somebody's cousin, and this one sentence is the shape of the whole fitna.

**The statement:**
> يَعْطِفُنِي عَلَيْهِ رَحِمٌ مَاسَّةٌ، وَهُوَ مَعَ ذَلِكَ سَيِّدٌ مِنْ شَبَابِ قُرَيْشٍ (٤) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3085
> *English:* "A close kinship inclines me toward him; and with that, he is a chief among the young men of Quraysh."

**عبرت:** Kinship does not end when the fighting starts, and men who had fought each other that morning still knew exactly whose cousin they were.

**Hands-up?** no

### POT/E-PH57 · Al-Ḥasan ؓ and al-Ḥusayn ؓ prayed behind him
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after this window `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** جعفر الصادق رحمہ اللہ, from his father, records something the room needs to hear tonight: الحسن ؓ and الحسين ؓ used to pray behind مروان, and did not repeat the prayer afterwards. The two grandsons of the Prophet ﷺ knew everything the room has just heard about the man, and still stood in his congregation and counted the prayer valid.

**The statement:**
> جَعْفَرُ بنُ مُحَمَّدٍ: عَنْ أَبِيْهِ: كَانَ الحَسَنُ وَالحُسَيْنُ يُصَلِّيَانِ خَلْفَ مَرْوَانَ، وَلاَ يُعِيدَانِ (٣) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3086
> *English:* "Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father: al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn used to pray behind Marwān, and did not repeat the prayer."

**عبرت:** A grievance against a man does not cancel the prayer behind him, and the people with the greatest grievance were the ones who showed it.

**Hands-up?** If you had a serious complaint against the imām of your masjid — would you still pray behind him?

### POT/E-PH58 · "I have read the Book of God for forty years"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** late in his life `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** مالك رحمہ اللہ records that مروان once stopped and reflected on where his life had brought him, and said it aloud: forty years of reading the Book of God, and this is what I have ended in — the shedding of blood, and this business. It is the man's own verdict on himself, and the book prints it without adding anything.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ مَالِكٌ: تَذَكَّرَ مَرْوَانُ، فَقَالَ: قَرَأْتُ كِتَابَ اللهِ مِنْ أَرْبَعِيْنَ سَنَةً، ثُمَّ أَصْبَحْتُ فِيمَا أَنَا فِيْهِ مِنْ هرقِ الدِّمَاءِ وَهَذَا الشَّأْنِ (١) ؟!
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3087
> *English:* "Mālik said: Marwān reflected and said: I have read the Book of God for forty years, and then I have come to be in what I am in — the shedding of blood, and this business?"

**عبرت:** Reading the Book for forty years does not by itself keep a man out of what he later finds himself in.

**Hands-up?** no

### POT/E-PH59 · The name the people gave him

It is from the tradition, not from us; it is unkind; and it belongs in the briefing rather than on a slide.

> *English:* "He had force, courage, cunning and shrewdness; red of face, short, with a short neck, thin-necked, with a large head and beard; he was nicknamed 'thread of falsehood'."

**عبرت:** People give a ruler a name of their own, and it usually records what they thought of him rather than what he was called at court.

### POT/E-PH60 · al-Walīd b. ʿUqbah ؓ — a Companion with slight companionship

**What happened:** الوليد بن عقبة ؓ was of بنو أمية and became Muslim at the conquest of Makkah. الذهبي رحمہ اللہ heads him simply as the commander and describes his standing with exactness: his companionship was slight and his transmission small. He is a Companion, and carries ؓ — and he is not one of the great ones, and the book does not pretend otherwise.

**The statement:**

> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3021
> *English:* "He had slight companionship, and small transmission."

**عبرت:** The tradition ranks its own without flattening them, and being counted among the Companions was never a claim that all of them were equal.

### POT/E-PH61 · ʿUthmān's ؓ half-brother, and a father executed after Badr
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 2 AH for the father; 8 AH for his Islam `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بدر, then مکہ.

**What happened:** Two facts sit in one line of the book and the room should hear them together. الوليد ؓ is عثمان's ؓ brother by the same mother — which is precisely the relation that made his later appointment a grievance. And his father, عقبة بن أبي معيط, was among those the Prophet ﷺ ordered put to death after بدر. A man whose father was executed at بدر, who accepted Islam at the فتح, and who ends as governor of الکوفہ: that whole arc is on one page of our own source.

**The statement:**
> وَهُوَ أَخُو أَمِيْرِ المُؤْمِنِيْنَ عُثْمَانَ لأُمِّهِ، مِنْ مُسْلِمَةِ الفَتْحِ؛ بَعَثَهُ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ - صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - عَلَى صَدَقَاتِ بَنِي المُصْطَلِقِ (١) ، وَأَمَرَ بِذَبْحِ وَالِدِهِ صَبْراً يَوْمَ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3021
> *English:* "He is the brother of the Commander of the Believers ʿUthmān by his mother, and one of those who became Muslim at the conquest. The Messenger of God ﷺ sent him over the ṣadaqāt of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, and ordered his father to be put to death on the day of…"

**عبرت:** Islam opened a door that a man's own history did not close, and the sons of its enemies were admitted through it.

none in the sources we use

### POT/E-PH64 · Four rakʿahs at fajr

### POT/E-PH65 · The ḥadd carried out in Madīnah
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** in ʿUthmān's ؓ caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** الوليد ؓ was brought to عثمان ؓ. Two men testified — one of them حمران — that he had drunk wine, and another that he had seen him vomit; عثمان ؓ said, he did not vomit it until he had drunk it. Then the caliph ordered the punishment carried out, and the order went down the line: to علي ؓ, from him to الحسن ؓ, and from him to عبد الله بن جعفر ؓ, who flogged him while علي ؓ counted aloud. At forty علي ؓ said hold, and gave the reason — the Prophet ﷺ flogged forty, أبو بكر ؓ forty, عمر ؓ eighty, and all of it is sunnah, and this is dearer to me. The caliph's own half-brother and governor was flogged in المدینہ, and the Prophet's ﷺ family carried it out.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: يا علي قم فاجلده، فقال علي: قم يا حسن فاجلده، فقال الحسن: ول حارها من تولى قارها - فكأنه وجد عليه - فقال: يا عبد الله بن جعفر، قم فاجلده، فجلده - وعلي يعد - حتى بلغ أربعين، فقال: أمسك، ثم قال: جلد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين، وجلد أبو بكر أربعين، وعمر ثمانين، وكل سنة، وهذا أحب إلي.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۱۵ (the printed edition's footnote, quoting مسلم ۱۷۰۷) · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3023
> *English:* "He said: ʿAlī, stand and flog him. ʿAlī said: Ḥasan, stand and flog him. Ḥasan said: give its hot part to whoever took its cool part — as though he was displeased at it. So he said: ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar, stand and flog him. And he flogged him — ʿAlī counting — until he reached forty. Then he said: hold. Then he said: the Prophet ﷺ flogged forty, and Abū Bakr flogged forty, and ʿUmar eighty; and all of it is sunnah, and this is dearer to me."

**عبرت:** A law that is carried out on the ruler's own brother is a law; carried out on everyone else only, it is something else.

**Hands-up?** Before I tell you what happened next — what do you expect a caliph to do when the accused is his own brother?

### POT/E-PH66 · A strong chain, and a verse that will not carry it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** a scholar's judgement `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The pages carry a report, through ابن عباس ؓ, of an exchange in which الوليد boasted to علي ؓ of being sharper of spear and more fluent of tongue, and علي ؓ told him to be quiet; and the report ends by saying that a verse came down about it. الذهبي رحمہ اللہ does not let it stand. He grants that the chain is strong — and then refuses the conclusion anyway, because the context of the verse shows it is speaking about the people of the Fire. He adds that it is also said the exchange was with the father, not the son. This is a model of the method the whole course is teaching, and it cost a classical scholar a report he could easily have kept.

**The statement:**
> قُلْتُ: إِسْنَادُهُ قَوِيٌّ، لَكِنَّ سِيَاقَ الآيَةِ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّهَا فِي أَهْلِ النَّارِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3023
> *English:* "I say: its chain is strong, but the context of the verse indicates that it is about the people of the Fire."

**عبرت:** A sound chain settles who said a thing, not what a verse of the Qurʾān means, and a careful scholar keeps those two questions apart.

**Hands-up?** no

> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3024
> *English:* "…to Ibn Masʿūd: be silent about these words — the best guidance is the guidance of Muḥammad ﷺ, and the worst of affairs are those newly introduced."

### POT/E-PH68 · "Along with his fisq — and may God pardon him"
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** a scholar's judgement `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** الذهبي رحمہ اللہ does not leave the man as a single charge. In the same breath as naming his fault he asks God to pardon him, and then records the other half: brave, and one who stood up to the duty of jihād. Elsewhere on the page he calls him generous, much praised, and a poet. If the first half of that sentence is quoted from the platform, the second half goes with it.

**The statement:**
> وَكَانَ مَعَ فِسْقِهِ - وَاللهُ يُسَامِحُهُ - شُجَاعاً، قَائِماً بِأَمْرِ الجِهَادِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۱۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3023
> *English:* "Along with his fisq — and may God pardon him — he was brave, and one who stood up to the matter of jihād."

**عبرت:** A fault is named without being made into the whole of a man, and the naming is followed by a prayer for him.

**Hands-up?** no

### POT/E-PH69 · He withdrew to al-Jazīrah and fought with neither party
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الجزیرہ, north of العراق; الرقّہ marked.

**What happened:** He governed الکوفہ for عثمان ؓ and fought on the Syrian frontier. Then, after the killing of his brother عثمان ؓ, he withdrew to الجزیرہ and fought with neither of the two parties. He is a second name for the list the room met earlier: the men who stood out of it. The book gives no year for his death, and nobody should supply one — ابن عساكر رحمہ اللہ did not give it either, and all that is recorded is that his grave is near الرقّہ.

**The statement:**
> وَوَلِيَ الكُوْفَةَ لِعُثْمَانَ، وَجَاهَدَ بِالشَّامِ، ثُمَّ اعْتَزَلَ بِالجَزِيْرَةِ بَعْدَ قَتْلِ أَخِيْهِ عُثْمَانَ، وَلَمْ يُحَارِبْ مَعَ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الفَرِيْقَيْنِ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۴۱۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/3022
> *English:* "He governed Kūfah for ʿUthmān and fought in Syria; then he withdrew to al-Jazīrah after the killing of his brother ʿUthmān, and did not fight alongside either of the two parties."

**عبرت:** The brother of the killed caliph stayed out of the fighting that was waged in his brother's name, and the book records it without a word of comment.

**Hands-up?** no

### POT/E-PH70 · A death date the sources do not give
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** not established `[SOURCED]` — the sources do not fix it · **Map:** الرقّہ.

**What happened:** الذهبي رحمہ اللہ notes that this man has long notices in the history of Damascus, and that even so his date of death is not given there. Our note therefore carries no year for him at all, only that his grave is near الرقّہ. This is worth one sentence from the platform tonight, because a room that has been handed dates all evening should see one place where the sources stop and the honest answer is that we do not know.

**The statement:**
none in the sources we use

**عبرت:** A tradition that records what it does not know is more trustworthy on everything else it records.

**Hands-up?** no

## The people: the generation thins — who died, year by year

*Source note: [`the-deaths-of-the-generation-23-40ah.md`](../docs/research/the-deaths-of-the-generation-23-40ah.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TDO/E-DG1 · The book keeps a register of the dead
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 23–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. The timeline strip only, with the years that carry a register marked.

**What happened:** Every so often, at the end of a year, the historian stops narrating and writes a list. He names the men and women who died that year, gives each a line or two, and moves on. In the years we are looking at tonight, that list is the quietest thing in the book and the heaviest. It is where you see the generation that had seen the Prophet ﷺ going, one name at a time, in the same years the trouble arrives. And the book is honest about the list. Some years it has one. Some years it has none at all.

**The statement:**
> ثم قال: ذكر من توفي في خلافة عمر بن الخطاب ﵁:
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۷۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3420
> *English:* "Then he said: an account of those who died during the caliphate of عمر بن الخطاب ﵁."

**عبرت:** A community that counts its dead by name is a community that knows what it is losing.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TDO/E-DG2 · The eye that was put back, and the grave عمر ؓ climbed into
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** The first name in the register for the last year of عمر ؓ's caliphate is قتادة بن النعمان ؓ. He was at بدر. At أحد his eye was struck so hard it fell onto his cheek, and the Prophet ﷺ put it back, and after that it was the better of his two eyes. He was one of the known archers, and he had led عمر ؓ's vanguard when عمر ؓ came up to the Shām. He died at sixty-five, and عمر ؓ himself went down into the grave. The book adds, in the same breath, that some say he died the year before. Even here it will not pretend to more than it knows.

**The statement:**
> توفي في هذه السنة على المشهور عن خمس وستين سنة، ونزل عمر في قبره، وقيل إنه توفي في التي قبلها.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۷۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3420
> *English:* "He died in this year, by the better-known account, at sixty-five, and عمر went down into his grave — and it is said he died in the year before it."

**عبرت:** The man who buried him would be buried himself within the year.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG3 · The first man to be killed in the path of Allah
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 23 AH, in the register of عمر ؓ's caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** بطن نخلة, south of مكة.

**What happened:** In the same list there is a short line for واقد بن عبد الله الحنظلي ؓ. He became a Muslim before the Prophet ﷺ ever entered the house of الأرقم. He was at بدر and everything after it. And the book gives him one distinction in four words: he was the first man killed in the path of Allah, at بطن نخلة, in the party of عبد الله بن جحش ؓ. That was before بدر — before there was a battle to be killed in. He lived on through all of it and died in his bed in عمر ؓ's caliphate.

**The statement:**
> وهو أول من قتل في سبيل الله ﷿ ببطن نخلة، مع عبد الله بن جحش حين قتل عمرو بن الحَضْرمي، توفي في خلافة عمر ﵁.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۷۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3424
> *English:* "And he is the first who was killed in the path of Allah, at بطن نخلة, with عبد الله بن جحش, when عمرو بن الحضرمي was killed. He died in the caliphate of عمر ﵁."

**عبرت:** The first blood of the community was shed in a skirmish nobody remembers, by a man who outlived every battle that followed.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG4 · سودة ؓ keeps her place by giving up her day
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 23 AH, in عمر ؓ's caliphate `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** The register for عمر ؓ's caliphate ends with the women. أم المؤمنين سودة بنت زمعة ؓ was the first the Prophet ﷺ married after خديجة ؓ. The book says of her only that she fasted much and stood much in prayer, and then tells the one thing everybody knows about her: that in her old age she asked not to be parted from him, and offered her day to عائشة ؓ, and he accepted. عائشة ؓ said the verse of النساء about a woman fearing her husband's turning away came down about سودة ؓ. She died in عمر ؓ's caliphate.

**The statement:**
> سَوْدَة بنت زَمْعَة (٣) القرشية العامرية أم المؤمنين، أول من دخل بها رسول الله ﷺ بعد خديجة ﵂، وكانت صَوَّامةً قَوَّامة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۷۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3425
> *English:* "سودة بنت زمعة القرشية العامرية, Mother of the Believers, the first the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took after خديجة ﵂; and she was much given to fasting and to standing in prayer."

**عبرت:** She asked for nothing except to still be counted among them.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG5 · The man who chased the هجرة dies a Muslim
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** قُدَيد, on the coast road between مكة and المدینہ.

**What happened:** In the first year of عثمان ؓ's caliphate the book records one death, and it is a good one. سراقة بن مالك بن جعشم ؓ is the man who rode after the Prophet ﷺ and أبو بكر ؓ when they came out of the cave of ثور — there was a hundred camels on each head and he wanted the money. His horse's legs went into the ground, and he called out for safety, and أبو بكر ؓ wrote him a guarantee of safe-conduct with the Prophet ﷺ's leave. He became a Muslim later. Twenty-four years after the ride he is a name in the death register of المدینہ.

**The statement:**
> وهو الذي اتَّبع رسول الله ﷺ وأبا بكر وعامر بن فهيرة وعبد الله بن أُرَيْقط الدّيلي حين خرجوا من غار ثور قاصدين المدينة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3433
> *English:* "He is the one who followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and أبو بكر and عامر بن فهيرة and عبد الله بن أريقط الديلي when they came out of the cave of ثور making for المدینہ."

**عبرت:** The chase and the safe-conduct were one morning; the whole of a man's life came after it.

**Hands-up?** Who was chasing the Prophet ﷺ and أبو بكر ؓ on the road out of مكة — and what happened to him afterwards?

### TDO/E-DG6 · Five years for one death — سيد القراء
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH, and four other years `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** أبي بن كعب ؓ is one of the very greatest of them — the Prophet ﷺ's own reciter. The book files his death under the year thirty, on الواقدي's authority. And in the same place the printed edition notes four other years that have been reported for him: nineteen, twenty, twenty-two, thirty-two. Thirteen years of uncertainty about when the greatest reciter of the Qurʾān died — and nobody hides it, because nobody was ever pretending the list was a government register. It is a record of what was reported.

**The statement:**
> وممن ذكر شيخنا أبو عبد الله الذهبي (٥) أنه توفي في هذه السنة - أعني سنة ثلاثين:
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۹۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3440
> *English:* "And among those whom our shaykh أبو عبد الله الذهبي mentioned as having died in this year — that is, the year thirty:"

**عبرت:** A date we cannot fix is not a fact we have lost; it is a report we are refusing to invent.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG7 · The uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, and the night at بدر
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ — البقيع.

**What happened:** العباس بن عبد المطلب ؓ was older than his nephew by two or three years. He was taken prisoner at بدر, fighting on the other side, and he ransomed himself and two of his brothers' sons. The book keeps the night of that captivity: the Prophet ﷺ could not sleep, and when they asked him why, he said he could hear العباس groaning in his ropes. A man got up and loosened the ropes until the groaning stopped, and then the Prophet ﷺ slept. He died at eighty-eight, and عثمان ؓ prayed over him, and he was buried at البقيع.

**The statement:**
> فقال "إني أسمع أنين العباس في وثاقه فلا
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3447
> *English:* "He said: 'I hear the groaning of العباس in his bonds, and I cannot —'"

**عبرت:** He was a prisoner of war that night and the honoured elder of the community afterwards; mercy did the whole of that distance.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG8 · عمر ؓ asks for rain through the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** told inside العباس ؓ's obituary, 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ — the prayer-ground.

**What happened:** Inside the obituary the book puts a report from البخاري. In a year of drought عمر ؓ went out to pray for rain, and he took العباس ؓ out with him, and he said aloud before the people what he was doing and why: when we were in drought we used to ask through our Prophet ﷺ, and now we ask through his uncle. And they were given rain. It is the clearest picture in the sources of what العباس ؓ's standing actually was, and it is put in his death notice rather than in a chapter of his own.

**The statement:**
> وقال: اللهم إنّا كنّا إذا قحطنا توسّلنا إليك بنبينا فتسقينا، وإنا نتوسل إليك بعمِّ نبينا، قال: فيسقون.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3448
> *English:* "And he said: O Allah, when we were struck by drought we used to seek a means to You through our Prophet and we were given rain; and we now seek a means to You through the uncle of our Prophet. He said: and they would be given rain."

**عبرت:** The caliph stood in the open and told the people exactly what he was doing, in words they could repeat.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG9 · Two caliphs get off their horses
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** in العباس ؓ's obituary, 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** One line in the same notice: when عمر ؓ and عثمان ؓ passed العباس ؓ while they were riding, they would get down out of respect for him. Two men who between them ruled from طرابلس to خراسان, dismounting in a street of المدینہ for an old man of their own city. The book says only «ويقال» — it is said — and does not press it further.

**The statement:**
> ويقال: إن عمر بن الخطاب وعثمان بن عفان كانا إذا مرا بالعباس وهما راكبان ترجّلا إكرامًا له.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3449
> *English:* "And it is said that عمر بن الخطاب and عثمان بن عفان, when they passed العباس while riding, would dismount out of honour for him."

**عبرت:** Authority that still dismounts for age has not yet become kingship.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG10 · Three years, two months, one man
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32, 33 or 34 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** When the book comes to write down the day العباس ؓ died, it gives us: a Friday, the twelfth night — of رجب, or it is said of رمضان — in the year thirty-two, at eighty-eight years old. عثمان ؓ prayed over him. And then: and it is said the year thirty-three, and it is said the year thirty-four. For the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ, in the city of the Prophet ﷺ, with a caliph leading the prayer. The record keeps every version it received and settles none of them.

**The statement:**
> ودفن بالبقيع وقيل توفي سنة ثلاث وثلاثين، وقيل سنة أربع وثلاثين، وفضائله ومناقبه كثيرة جدًا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3449
> *English:* "And he was buried at البقيع. And it is said he died in the year thirty-three, and it is said the year thirty-four. And his merits and virtues are very many."

**عبرت:** Honesty about a date costs nothing and buys everything else.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG11 · «هو كُنَيف مليء علمًا»
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** in ابن مسعود ؓ's obituary, 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن مسعود ؓ was a very small man. Standing, he came level with a man who was sitting down. The book says عمر ؓ once looked at how short he was, and watched him walk away, and then said the sentence that has followed him ever since: he is a small vessel filled to the brim with knowledge. Beside it the book puts حذيفة ؓ's word — that he never saw anyone whose manner and bearing and way of carrying himself were closer to the Prophet ﷺ's than ابن مسعود ؓ's.

**The statement:**
> وقال عمر بن الخطاب ﵁ -وقد نظر إلى قصره وكان يوازي بقامته الجلوس- فجعل يتبعه ثمَّ قال: هو كُنَيف (٧) مليء علمًا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3450
> *English:* "And عمر بن الخطاب ﵁ — having looked at his shortness, for standing he was level with a seated man — followed him with his eyes and then said: he is a small vessel filled with knowledge."

**عبرت:** They measured a man by what he carried, not by what he looked like carrying it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG12 · «ما تشتكي؟ قال: ذنوبي»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** ابن مسعود ؓ came back from العراق on hajj, stopped at الربذة and buried أبو ذر ؓ there, then came on to المدینہ and fell ill. عثمان ؓ came to visit him. What do you complain of? My sins. What do you desire? My Lord's mercy. Shall I send you a doctor? The doctor is the one who made me ill. Shall I order your stipend paid — and he had not drawn it for two years — I have no need of it. It will be for your daughters. Do you fear poverty for my daughters? I have told them to read سورة الواقعة every night.

**The statement:**
> قال: ألا آمر لك بعطائك؟ -وكان قد تركه سنتين- فقال: لا حاجة لي فيه. فقال: يكون لبناتك من بعدك. فقال: أتخشى على بناتي الفقر؟
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3451
> *English:* "He said: shall I not order your stipend paid to you? — and he had left it two years — He said: I have no need of it. He said: it will be for your daughters after you. He said: do you fear poverty for my daughters?"

**عبرت:** A man on his deathbed was asked what he wanted and could not think of anything he wanted.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG13 · Nobody is sure who prayed over ابن مسعود ؓ
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** المدینہ — البقيع.

**What happened:** He made الزبير ؓ the executor of his will. And then the book gives us three accounts of his funeral prayer and refuses to pick one. It is said الزبير ؓ prayed over him at night, and that عثمان ؓ afterwards reproached him for it. It is said rather that عثمان ؓ prayed over him. It is said عمار ؓ did. And Allah knows best. He was buried at البقيع at a little past sixty. This is what a report looks like when the historian will not tidy it.

**The statement:**
> وقيل بل صلَّى عليه عثمان، وقيل عمَّار، فالله أعلم. ودفن بالبقيع عن بضع وستين سنة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3451
> *English:* "And it is said rather that عثمان prayed over him; and it is said عمار — and Allah knows best. He was buried at البقيع at a little over sixty."

**عبرت:** Where the reports differ, the book prints all of them and stops — and so do we.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG14 · A hundred men of بدر were still alive
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** When death came to عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ he left four hundred dinars to every man still living who had been at بدر. The book tells us how many that was: about a hundred. They took it — عثمان ؓ took it and علي ؓ took it. And علي ؓ said to him: go, son of عوف; you got the clear part of this world and outran its dross. He left a large sum to each of the Mothers of the Believers as well, and عائشة ؓ used to say, may Allah give him to drink of السلسبيل.

**The statement:**
> ولما حضرته الوفاة أوصى لكل رجل ممن بقي من أهل بدر بأربعمئة دينار -وكانوا مئة- فأخذوها حتى عثمان وعلي
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3452
> *English:* "And when death came to him he bequeathed to every man remaining of the people of بدر four hundred dinars — and they were a hundred — and they took it, even عثمان and علي."

**عبرت:** Thirty years after بدر there were a hundred of them left, and somebody had to count.

**Hands-up?** How many men of بدر do you think were still alive in the year 32?

### TDO/E-DG15 · Gold cut up with axes until their hands blistered
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ — البقيع.

**What happened:** After all that giving, عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ still left a great estate. The book describes the dividing of it in one picture: gold that had to be cut up with axes until the men's hands blistered. A thousand camels. A hundred horses. Three thousand sheep grazing at البقيع. One of his four wives settled her quarter of an eighth of the estate for eighty thousand. عثمان ؓ prayed over him, سعد بن أبي وقاص ؓ helped carry the bier, and he was buried at البقيع at seventy-five.

**The statement:**
> ثمّ تركَ بعد ذلك كلِّه مالًا جزيلًا، من ذلك ذهبٌ قُطِّعَ بالفُؤوس حتى مجلت (١) أيدي الرجال، وتركَ ألفَ بعيرٍ ومئةَ فرسٍ، وثلاثةَ آلافِ شاةٍ تَرْعى بالبقيع.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3453
> *English:* "Then after all of that he left abundant wealth: among it gold that was cut up with axes until the men's hands blistered; and he left a thousand camels and a hundred horses and three thousand sheep grazing at البقيع."

**عبرت:** The wealth of the conquests had reached the houses of المدینہ, and the men who remembered hunger were the ones dividing it.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG16 · The historian refuses the story he has just told
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH, inside عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ's obituary `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** In the same notice there is a famous story: a caravan of seven hundred camels comes into المدینہ, the city shakes with the noise, عائشة ؓ says she heard the Prophet ﷺ say عبد الرحمن ؓ would enter Paradise crawling — and when it reaches him he gives the whole caravan away. The book tells it twice, from two chains. Then it writes one sentence about the chain: only عمارة بن زاذان الصيدلاني transmits it, and he is weak. > واللّه لقد سلقوني يومًا في نار أججوها ووضع رجل رجله على صدري فما اتقيت الأرض إِلَّا بظهري، ثم كشف عن ظهره فإذا هو برص ﵁
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3667
> *English:* "By Allah, they laid me one day in a fire they had kindled, and a man put his foot on my chest, and I met the ground only with my back. Then he uncovered his back, and it was white-scarred."

**عبرت:** The men who bore the beginning were still walking around المدینہ with the marks on them.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG34 · «إن إخواني مضوا ولم يأكلوا من دنياهم شيئًا»
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة.

**What happened:** When خباب ؓ was dying, Companions came in to visit him, and they gave him the good news anyone would give: rejoice — tomorrow you meet the loved ones, محمد ﷺ and his company. And he answered them with the thing that was actually on his mind. My brothers went ahead and ate nothing at all of this world. And its fruit has ripened for us, and here we are, picking it. That is what troubles me. He died at الكوفة at sixty-three, and he was the first man buried outside that city.

**The statement:**
> فقال: واللّه إن إخواني مضوا ولم يأكلوا من دنياهم (٥) شيئًا، وإنا قد أينعت لنا ثمرتها فتحن نهدبها (٦)،
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3667
> *English:* "He said: by Allah, my brothers went on and ate nothing of their world; and its fruit has ripened for us and we are plucking it —"

**عبرت:** The thing that frightened him at the end was not the torture; it was the comfort.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG35 · The first grave outside الكوفة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة. Light the city.

**What happened:** خباب ؓ was tortured at مكة before there was a community to protect him. He made the هجرة, he was at بدر and everything after it. And he died in a garrison city in العراق that had not existed when he became a Muslim — and he was the first man to be buried outside it. The distance that one sentence covers is the distance the whole course is trying to show: from a fire in the sand at مكة to a new cemetery on the edge of a new city, in one lifetime.

**The statement:**
> قال: وتوفي بالكوفة في هذه السنة عن ثلاث وستين سنة، وهو أول من دفن بظاهر الكوفة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3668
> *English:* "He said: and he died at الكوفة in this year, at sixty-three years of age; and he was the first to be buried outside الكوفة."

**عبرت:** The cities they died in did not exist when they became Muslims.

**Hands-up?** no

### TDO/E-DG41 · The number the book will not settle

### TDO/E-DG46 · أسماء بنت عميس ؓ — three houses
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** filed in the 38 AH register `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الحبشة → المدینہ.

**What happened:** أسماء بنت عميس ؓ became a Muslim early at مكة and went to الحبشة with her husband جعفر بن أبي طالب ؓ, and came back with him at the time of خيبر. When جعفر ؓ was killed at مؤتة she married أبو بكر الصديق ؓ, and bore him محمد. When أبو بكر ؓ died — and by his own bequest it was she who washed his body — she married علي بن أبي طالب ؓ, and bore him يحيى and عون. One woman's household is three of the central houses of Islam in a single lifetime.

> ولما قتل جعفر بمؤتة تزوجها بعده أبو بكر الصديق فولدت منه محمد بن أبي بكر أمير مصر (٣)، ثم لما مات الصديق تزوجها بعده علي بن أبي طالب فولدت له يحيى وعونًا

**عبرت:** The families of that generation were tied to each other more tightly than the quarrel between them.

### TDO/E-DG48 · The years with no register at all
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 24–29, 31, 33–36, 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. The timeline strip with the empty years marked.

**What happened:** For most of the years in this stretch the book keeps its list of the dead. For some of them it keeps none — not a short one, none at all. Nothing for twenty-four through twenty-nine, nothing for thirty-one, nothing for thirty-three to thirty-six, nothing for forty. Some of the greatest of them died inside those gaps. We should be honest about this from the platform: what we are reading is what reached the historian, laid out year by year, and where nothing reached him he has written nothing.

none in the sources we use

### TDO/E-DG49 · Read the list slowly
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 23–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** The closing map for this strand: المدینہ · الربذة · الكوفة · البصرة · صفين · مصر, each with a name and a year.

**What happened:** Put the years side by side and say the names in order. Twenty-three: قتادة ؓ, and عمر ؓ himself. Twenty-four: سراقة ؓ. Thirty: أبي بن كعب ؓ. Thirty-two: العباس ؓ, ابن مسعود ؓ, عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ, أبو ذر ؓ. Thirty-six: طلحة ؓ and الزبير ؓ, on one Thursday. Thirty-seven: خباب ؓ, his son, خزيمة ؓ, عمار ؓ. Thirty-eight: سهل بن حنيف ؓ, صهيب ؓ. In seventeen years the room that had actually seen the Prophet ﷺ emptied out — and the arguing was loudest in exactly the years the room was emptying.

**The statement:**
> وبالجملة فقد كان فيهم أعيانٌ ومشاهيرُ يطولُ استقصاؤهم وفيما ذكرناه كفايةٌ، واللّه تعالى أعلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3671
> *English:* "In sum, among them were notables and well-known men whom it would be long to enumerate, and what we have mentioned is sufficient — and Allah, exalted be He, knows best."

**عبرت:** The quarrels of those years were being carried on by fewer and fewer of the people who had been there at the beginning.

**Hands-up?** Which of the Companions you have heard of tonight do you think were still alive in the year forty?

## The statements bank — slide-ready, by speaker

*Source note: [`great-statements-and-dialogues-23-40ah.md`](../docs/research/great-statements-and-dialogues-23-40ah.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### GSA/E-ST1 · The answer to a man who told him he would be killed
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35 AH, المدینہ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ lights; nothing else moves.

**What happened:** Before the siege closed, a man came to عثمان ؓ and told him plainly what was
going to happen: he would be assassinated, and his house would be attacked. It was not a warning he
could act on and it was not offered as one. الذهبي records the exchange in two lines, and the whole
of عثمان ؓ's reply is four words.

**The statement:**
> قال: يا أمير المؤمنين والله لتغتالن ولتغزين قال: حسبي الله ونعم الوكيل.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۸۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1331
> *English:* "He said: Commander of the Faithful, by God you will be assassinated and you will be attacked. He said: God suffices me, and He is the best disposer of affairs."

**عبرت:** A man's answer to a warning he cannot act on tells you what he is made of.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST2 · The mosque he had bought, and was kept out of
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو القعدة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the Prophet's mosque and the house, side by side.

**What happened:** The men besieging the house would not let عثمان ؓ into the mosque to pray. He
reminded them who had paid for the ground they were standing on — he had bought the extension out of
his own property and given it to the Muslims. They did not answer him, and he did not force the
point. He turned away and called God to witness three times.

**The statement:**
> فاشتريتُها من خالص مالي، فجعلتُها بين المسلمين، وأنتم تمنعوني أن أصلي فيه ركعتين
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3471
> *English:* "I bought it from my own pure wealth and made it common to the Muslims — and you forbid me to pray two rakʿahs in it."

**عبرت:** A crowd that has decided does not hear an argument, however good.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST3 · Three words, three times, and then he turned away
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو القعدة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map — a statement slide.

**What happened:** Having asked the crowd whether they remembered the well of رومة, and the army he
had equipped, and the ground the mosque stood on, and having had each question answered and then
ignored, عثمان ؓ stopped arguing. ابن كثير gives what he said instead. It is the point at which the
case for the defence is closed and handed over.

**The statement:**
> اللهم اشهد، اللهم اشهد، اللهم اشهد، ثم انصرف.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۲۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3470
> *English:* "O God, bear witness; O God, bear witness; O God, bear witness — then he turned away."

**عبرت:** There is a moment when a man stops defending himself to people and starts addressing God.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST4 · I will not be the first to shed Muslim blood
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH, the house under siege `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ, the house marked.

**What happened:** عثمان ؓ had men inside the house and more outside it who would have fought for
him, and the الشام army was a fortnight's ride away. He refused all of it. Asked to let his own
people take up arms, he gave the reason, and it is not tactical: he would not be the first successor
of the Messenger ﷺ to hold the community together by killing people in it. He then released the men
who were defending him from any obligation to fight.

**The statement:**
> أما أن أخرج فأقاتل فلن أكون أولَ من خَلَفَ رسول الله ﷺ في أمته بسفك الدماء
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۳۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3476
> *English:* "As for going out and fighting — I will not be the first to succeed the Messenger of God ﷺ over his ummah by shedding blood."

**عبرت:** A precedent is set once and then belongs to everybody who comes after.

**Hands-up?** yes — *who here would have fought, if he had let them?*

### GSA/E-ST5 · The order that emptied his own defence
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the house.

**What happened:** ابن الأثیر preserves the sentence that made the defence of the house collapse.
It was not a failure of loyalty and it was not a shortage of men; it was an instruction from the man
inside. Anyone who fought was told in advance that he fought on his own account.

**The statement:**
> فَإِنِّي لَا آمُرُ أَحَدًا بِقِتَالِكُمْ، فَمَنْ قَاتَلَكُمْ فَبِغَيْرِ أَمْرِي قَاتَلَ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۵۳۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1227
> *English:* "I command no one to fight you; whoever fights you fights without my command."

**عبرت:** The house fell because of a decision taken inside it, not a weakness outside it.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST6 · The three refusals
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ with الشام marked to the north.

**What happened:** Three ways out were put to عثمان ؓ and he refused each in turn. He would not
leave المدینہ, because it was the city of his هجرة. He would not go to الشام, because he was
ashamed to arrive as a frightened fugitive asking protection of the people he governed. And he would
not fight. ابن كثير sets the three out on one page.

**The statement:**
> وأما القتال فإني أرجو أن ألقى الله وليس يهراق بسببي محجمة (٥) دم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3487
> *English:* "As for fighting — I hope to meet God with not a cupping-glass of blood spilt on my account."

**عبرت:** He was not out of options; he had ruled each of them out himself.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST7 · The charge he said he was keeping
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the siege `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map.

**What happened:** The men in the house asked him directly whether he would fight, and he said no,
and gave a reason that had nothing to do with the odds. A charge had been laid on him by the
Messenger of God ﷺ and he was holding to it. حذيفة ؓ's narration of the same sentence, four pages
later, is shorter still.

**The statement:**
> إن رسول الله ﷺ عهد لي عهدًا فأنا صابر عليه
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3493
> *English:* "The Messenger of God ﷺ made a covenant with me, and I am bearing it patiently."

**عبرت:** What looks like passivity from outside can be obedience from inside.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST8 · The shirt, told three times
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime; delivered in the 35 AH block `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map.

**What happened:** ابن كثير carries the report that the Prophet ﷺ told عثمان ؓ that God might
clothe him in a shirt, and that if the hypocrites tried to make him take it off he was not to take
it off until he met him — and that he said it three times. Everything عثمان ؓ does through twelve
months of siege follows from this one report, and the room cannot understand his conduct without it.

**The statement:**
> "يا عثمان إن الله عسى أن يلبسك قميصًا، فإن أرادك المنافقون على خلعه فلا تخلعه حتى تلقاني" ثلاثًا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۷۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3516
> *English:* "'عثمان, God may well clothe you in a shirt; and if the hypocrites want you to take it off, do not take it off until you meet me' — three times."

**عبرت:** A man's behaviour is unreadable until you know what he thinks he was told.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST9 · Break your fast with me tomorrow
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the night of 17–18 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the house.

**What happened:** On the last night, عثمان ؓ dreamt that he came in upon the Prophet ﷺ with
أبو بكر ؓ and عمر ؓ beside him, and was told to go back because he would break his fast with him
the next day. He rose in the morning fasting, and told the people in the house what he had seen. He
was killed that same day.

**The statement:**
> رأيت البارحة وكأنّي دخلتُ على نبي الله ﷺ وعنده أبو بكر وعمر، فقال: "ارجع فإنَّك مُفْطرٌ عندي غدًا"
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۳۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3477
> *English:* "Last night I saw, as though I had come in upon the Prophet of God ﷺ, and with him were أبو بكر and عمر, and he said: go back, for you will break your fast with me tomorrow."

**عبرت:** He went into the last morning of his life fasting, and told the room why.

### GSA/E-ST10 · The first hand that wrote out the مفصّل
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 18 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the house, closing.

**What happened:** When the sword came down, عثمان ؓ put up his hand and it was cut. الذهبي
records what he said about that hand as it fell: it was the first hand that had ever written out the
مفصّل — the short sūras at the end of the Qur'an. The scribe of the Prophet ﷺ and the man who had
gathered the مصحف died with the copy he had made open in front of him.

**The statement:**
> فأهوى إليه بالسيف، فاتقاه بيده فقطعها، فقال: أما والله إنها لأول كف خطت المفصل
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۲۰۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1348
> *English:* "He struck at him with the sword, and he warded it off with his hand, and it cut it; and he said: by God, it is the first hand that wrote out the mufaṣṣal."

**عبرت:** The Qurʾān in every hand in this room was gathered by the man whose hand was cut for it.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST11 · What he actually said about the pasture
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 34–35 AH, المدینہ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map.

**What happened:** Two complaints against عثمان ؓ were repeated in every city: the reserved
pasture and the مصحف. الذهبي records him answering the first in public, twice, and the answer is
narrow and checkable: the pasture was reserved for the camels of the صدقة, not for his own, and
nothing was reserved that had not been reserved before him.

**The statement:**
> وأما الحمى فوالله ما حميته لإبلي ولا لغنمي، وإنما حميته لإبل الصدقة.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1326
> *English:* "As for the protected pasture — by God, I did not protect it for my camels nor for my sheep; I protected it only for the camels of the ṣadaqah."

**عبرت:** A complaint repeated in four cities is not the same thing as a complaint examined in one.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST12 · What he actually said about the مصحف
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 30 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the four garrison cities lit at once.

**What happened:** The second standing complaint was that he had burned copies of the Qurʾān.
الذهبي records his answer in one sentence: the Qurʾān is from God, and what he had forbidden was
not a reading but a quarrel. On the same run of pages is the instruction he gave the committee —
where they disagreed over a word, they were to write it in the tongue of Quraysh, because that is
the tongue it came down in.

**The statement:**
> أما القرآن فمن عند الله، إنما نهيتكم عن الاختلاف فاقرؤوا على أي حرف شئتم
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء جراشدون ص۱۸۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1326
> *English:* "As for the Qurʾān — it is from God. I only forbade you to differ; so recite upon whichever ḥarf you wish."

**عبرت:** The thing he was most blamed for is the thing every Muslim alive now depends on.

**Hands-up?** yes — *who has ever heard this complaint made against him?*

### GSA/E-ST15 · The visit, and the stipend refused
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH, المدینہ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن مسعود ؓ came back from العراق, buried أبو ذر ؓ at الربذة on the
way, reached المدینہ and fell ill. عثمان ؓ came to visit him and the two men had the conversation
ابن كثير preserves. He had left his stipend untouched for two years and would not take it now;
told it would go to his daughters, he said he had told them to recite سورة الواقعة every night.

**The statement:**
> أنه قال له: ما تشتكي؟ قال ذنوبي، قال فما تشتهي؟ قال رحمة ربي، قال ألا آمر لك بطبيب؟ فقال: الطبيب أمرضني، قال: ألا آمر لك بعطائك؟ -وكان قد تركه سنتين- فقال: لا حاجة لي فيه. فقال: يكون لبناتك من بعدك. فقال: أتخشى على بناتي الفقر؟ إني أمرتُ بناتي أن يقرأْنَ كلَّ ليلةٍ سورةَ الواقعة
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۰۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3451
> *English:* "That he said to him: of what do you complain? He said: of my sins. He said: what do you desire? He said: the mercy of my Lord. He said: shall I not order a physician for you? He said: the physician made me ill. He said: shall I not order your stipend paid to you? — and he had left it two years — He said: I have no need of it. He said: it will be for your daughters after you. He said: do you fear poverty for my daughters? I have ordered my daughters to recite سورة الواقعة every night."

**عبرت:** Two men at their best, in a year the books remember for something else entirely.

**Hands-up?** no

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH, outside البصرة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة, the two camps.

**What happened:** On the night before الجمل, with the two camps in sight of each other, علي ؓ was
asked whether the other side had the same claim on this matter as his own side. He said yes. Then
he said what he hoped would happen to the men who died on either side of the field.

**The statement:**
> إني لأرجو أن لا يقتل منا ومنهم أحدٌ نقَّى قلبه لله إلا أدخله اللهُ الجنةَ
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۱۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3562
> *English:* "I hope that no one of us or of them who has purified his heart for Allah will be killed but that Allah will admit him to the Garden."

**عبرت:** The guardrail of this evening was first spoken by a man who was about to fight the battle.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST27 · What brought you to this land?
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** علي ؓ sent an envoy into the other camp to ask each of the three principals, in
turn, why they had come. He began with أم المؤمنين عائشة ؓ. Her answer was three words long. The
embassy worked: the two camps came within sight of a settlement, and ابن كثير says both sides
passed the best of nights.

**The statement:**
> فبدأ بعائشة أمِّ المؤمنين، فقال: أي أماه! ما أقدمكِ هذا البلدَ؟ فقالت: أي بنيّ! الإصلاحُ بين الناس
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۱۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3560
> *English:* "He began with عائشة, the mother of the believers, and said: my mother, what brought you to this land? She said: my son — setting things right between the people."

**عبرت:** Everybody at الجمل had come to prevent a war.

**Hands-up?** yes — *who thinks either side came to fight?*

### GSA/E-ST28 · The night the settlement nearly held
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the night before الجمل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة, the two camps at rest.

**What happened:** Terms were agreed and علي ؓ announced that he would move on in the morning and
that nobody who had had a hand in the killing of عثمان ؓ would march with him. The men that
excluded then sat up through the night and agreed on a way to stop it: when the two armies met in
the morning, they would start the fighting themselves and not let anybody talk.

> *English:* "So when the people meet, set the war and the fighting going among them, and do not leave them to come together."

**عبرت:** The war was not started by either of the two armies that fought it.

### GSA/E-ST30 · The people know I am no coward
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة, and the road out of it.

**What happened:** علي ؓ called الزبير ؓ out between the lines and reminded him of something he had
heard from the Prophet ﷺ. الزبير ؓ then left the field. Asked afterwards why, الذهبي records his
answer — and the verse he recited after it. He was killed on the road, by a man who had had no part
in the battle at all.

> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۱ ص۶۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1486
> *English:* "He said: the people know well that I am no coward — but علي reminded me of something I had heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I swore that I would not fight him. Then he said —"

**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map — statement slide.

### GSA/E-ST32 · Two men, one killer, the same answer
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH and afterwards `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** وادي السباع marked outside البصرة.

**What happened:** ابن جرموز killed الزبير ؓ on the road after he had left the battle, and then
came to علي ؓ expecting to be received. He was refused at the door. Later he went over to

> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۱ ص۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1490
> *English:* "Then the word came to him: am I to kill ابن جرموز for الزبير? Not for the thong of his sandal."

### GSA/E-ST33 · We temporised in the affair of عثمان
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the morning of الجمل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** طلحة ؓ said two things on the morning of the battle that الذهبي preserves. To
علقمة he said that yesterday they had been one hand against everyone else and today they had become
two mountains of iron. And of himself he said that he had temporised over عثمان ؓ, and asked God to
take the debt out of him that day. He was killed by an arrow within hours.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ طَلْحَةُ: إِنَّا دَاهَنَّا فِي أَمْرِ عُثْمَانَ، فَلاَ نَجِدُ اليَوْمَ أَمْثَلَ مِنْ أَنْ نَبْذُلَ دِمَاءنَا فِيْهِ، اللَّهُمَّ خُذْ لِعُثْمَانَ مِنِّي اليَوْمَ حَتَّى تَرْضَى (٤) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۱ ص۳۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1461
> *English:* "طلحة said: we temporised in the affair of عثمان, and we find nothing better today than to spend our own blood in it. O God, take from me for عثمان today until You are satisfied."

**عبرت:** He did not wait for history to judge him; he said it out loud on the field.

### GSA/E-ST34 · Yesterday one hand, today two mountains of iron
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the morning of الجمل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map — statement slide.

**What happened:** علقمة reproached طلحة ؓ for being where he was. الذهبي gives the answer, and
الذهبي's own abridgement calls the chain جيد. The image in it — one hand, then two mountains of
iron crawling towards one another — is the best single description of the whole fitna that any of
our sources contains, and it is by a man standing in it.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: يَا عَلْقَمَةَ! لاَ تَلُمْنِي، كُنَّا أَمْسِ يَداً وَاحِدَةً عَلَى مَنْ سِوَانَا، فَأَصْبَحْنَا اليَوْمَ جَبَلَيْنِ مِنْ حَدِيْدٍ، يَزْحَفُ أَحَدُنَا إِلَى صَاحِبِهِ، وَلَكِنَّهُ كَانَ مِنِّي شَيْءٌ فِي أَمْرِ عُثْمَانَ مِمَّا لاَ أَرَى كَفَّارَتَهُ إِلاَّ سَفْكَ دَمِي، وَطَلَبَ دَمِهِ (٣) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۱ ص۳۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1460
> *English:* "He said: علقمة, do not blame me. Yesterday we were one hand against whoever was not of us, and today we have become two mountains of iron, one of us crawling towards the other. But there was something from me in the matter of عثمان whose expiation I see in nothing but the spilling of my own blood, and the seeking of his."

**عبرت:** The same men, the same swords, one year apart — pointed the other way.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST35 · You have won, so be gentle
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the evening of الجمل, 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

> *English:* "She said: son of أبي طالب, you have won, so be gentle."

### GSA/E-ST36 · She is the wife of your Prophet ﷺ in this world and the next
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after الجمل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map — statement slide.

**What happened:** Someone reported to علي ؓ what أم المؤمنين ؓ had said about their quarrel — that
it had been no more than what happens between a woman and her husband's kin. ابن كثير gives his
reply. It is the sentence that closes the الجمل block and it is the sentence the room most needs to
hear from him rather than from us.

**The statement:**
> فقال علي: صدقتِ والله ما كان بيني وبينها إلا ذاك، وإنها لزوجةُ نبيكم ﷺ في الدنيا والآخرة.

> *English:* "And علي said: she has spoken truly — by Allah, there was nothing between me and her but that; and she is indeed the wife of your Prophet ﷺ in this world and the next."

### GSA/E-ST37 · He prayed over the slain of both parties
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** after الجمل, 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة.

**What happened:** علي ؓ had his crier forbid three things — no pursuit of a man in flight, no

> *English:* "And علي stayed outside البصرة three days, then prayed over the slain of both parties."

### GSA/E-ST38 · Hard on me to see you under the stars

### GSA/E-ST39 · My pillow
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** الجمل, 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map.

**What happened:** A man came on طلحة ؓ dying, propped against another man, and asked him who had
killed him. ابن كثير gives the answer in one word. On another page he records that the arrow is
said to have come from a man on طلحة ؓ's own side — and adds «فالله أعلم», and elsewhere that in

### GSA/E-ST40 · Not one in a hundred was there
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the Line, with the whole Companion generation marked.

**What happened:** ابن كثير states plainly, and twice, how many of the Companions actually took part
in the fighting of these years. There were tens of thousands of them alive. Not a hundred were
present — indeed, he says, they did not reach thirty. The overwhelming majority of the generation
stayed out of it entirely, and that is the fact the room has never been told.

**The statement:**
> قال: هاجت الفتنة وأصحاب رسول الله ﷺ عشرات الألوف فلم يحضرها منهم مئة، بل لم يبلغوا ثلاثين.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۳۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3583
> *English:* "He said: the fitna broke out while the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ were tens of thousands, and not a hundred of them were present at it — indeed they did not reach thirty."

**عبرت:** A quarrel that has divided the ummah for fourteen centuries was fought by fewer than
thirty of the men who knew him ﷺ.

**Hands-up?** yes — *who thought most of the Companions were involved?*

### GSA/E-ST41 · Neither my she-camel nor my he-camel
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–37 AH, البصرة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** البصرة, a third marker beside the two camps.

**What happened:** When the call to join one side or the other went round البصرة, الأحنف بن قيس
stood up and answered it with one sentence, and then withdrew with his people. ابن خلدون — used
here for framing only — describes the city as being in three parts rather than two: with these, with
those, and a third that stood out.

**The statement:**
> قَامَ الْأَحْنَفُ فَقَالَ: لَا نَاقَتِي فِي هَذَا وَلَا جَمَلِي. وَاعْتَزَلَ الْقَوْمَ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۷۱۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1400
> *English:* "الأحنف rose and said: neither my she-camel nor my he-camel is in this — and he withdrew from the people."

**عبرت:** There was always a third answer available, and men of standing gave it.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST42 · I held my hand back, and I did not regret it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36–40 AH and long afterwards `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ.

**What happened:** عبد الله بن عمر ؓ was not a quietist by temperament — the same ترجمة records him
campaigning in الشام, العراق, البصرة and فارس. He took no part in any of these battles, and he
was asked about it for the rest of his life. الذهبي gives the answer, and the second half of it is
why it is worth a slide: he keeps his own choice and praises the other side in the same breath.

**The statement:**
> قَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ: كَفَفْتُ يَدِي، فَلَمْ أَندَمْ، وَالمُقَاتِلُ عَلَى الحَقِّ أَفْضَلُ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۱۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2822
> *English:* "ابن عمر said: I held my hand back, and I did not regret it — and the one who fights for the truth is better."

**عبرت:** He kept his own position and refused to make it a stick to beat anyone with.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST43 · The God-fearing, the self-sufficient, the obscure
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 35–36 AH, outside المدینہ `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map.

**What happened:** سعد بن أبي وقاص ؓ — the conqueror of القادسية, one of the six of the شورى, one
of the ten — spent the fitna among his sheep outside the city. His son came out and asked him
whether he was content to be a bedouin while the people were contending over the kingship at
المدینہ. الذهبي records the answer, and the hadith it rested on.

**The statement:**
> فَضَرَبَ صَدْرَ عُمَرَ وَقَالَ: اسْكُتْ، فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ -صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ- يَقُوْلُ (٢) : (إِنَّ اللهَ -عَزَّ وَجَلَّ- يُحِبُّ العَبْدَ التَّقِيَّ، الغَّنِيَّ، الخَفِيَّ (٣)) .
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۱ ص۱۰۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/1528
> *English:* "So he struck عمر's chest and said: be quiet — for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'God, mighty and majestic, loves the servant who is God-fearing, self-sufficient, obscure.'"

**عبرت:** Standing out of it was not a failure of nerve; it was a hadith being acted on.

**Hands-up?** no

> *English:* "عمرو said: leave them and it alone; it is not fair dealing that we should be watered and they thirsty."

### GSA/E-ST46 · The palm-fronds of هجر
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH, صفين `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** صفين on the Euphrates, and هجر at the far end of Arabia.

**What happened:** عمار بن ياسر ؓ was an old man at صفين, tall and dark, holding a spear with a
shaking hand. ابن الأثیر gives what he said about the certainty he had, and the distance he was
prepared to be driven without losing it. He asked for a drink of milk, laughed, and said the
Messenger of God ﷺ had told him it would be the last thing he drank. He was killed the same day.

**The statement:**
> وَايْمُ اللَّهِ لَوْ ضَرَبُونَا حَتَّى يَبْلُغُوا بِنَا سَعَفَاتِ هَجَرَ، لَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّا عَلَى الْحَقِّ، وَأَنَّهُمْ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۶۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1349
> *English:* "And by God, if they struck us until they drove us to the palm-fronds of هجر, I would know that we are upon the truth and that they are upon falsehood."

**عبرت:** هجر is at the other end of Arabia; he was measuring his certainty in miles.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST48 · Naming both parties Muslims
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH — the guardrail slide `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map.

معاوية ؓ was transgressing. On the same run of pages he refuses, as a lie against the Messenger ﷺ,
the addition that has been made to the hadith — and gives his reason, which is the reason this
evening exists.

### GSA/E-ST49 · Their claim is one
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** صفين, the two lines.

### GSA/E-ST50 · Deception, cunning, and stratagem
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH, صفين `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** صفين.

**What happened:** When the مصاحف went up on the spears, علي ؓ told his army plainly what he
thought they were for. The men who forced him to stop were not the waverers in his camp: ابن كثير
names them in one clause as the men the army itself called the قُرّاء, the Qurʾān readers, with

its own certainty, citing الحديبية.

### GSA/E-ST51 · Distrust your own opinion
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map — statement slide.

### GSA/E-ST53 · It is men who speak by it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH, حروراء `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** حروراء outside الكوفة.

**What happened:** علي ؓ answered the slogan with an argument rather than an assertion. ابن الأثیر
has the sharp form of it, spoken at حروراء. ابن كثير has him performing the same argument: he
called for a large مصحف, set it in front of him, struck it with his hand and told it to speak to
the people — and the people themselves answered that it was ink on paper and that they were the ones
who spoke by it.

**The statement:**
> إِنَّا لَسْنَا حَكَّمْنَا الرِّجَالَ، إِنَّمَا حَكَّمْنَا الْقُرْآنَ، وَهَذَا الْقُرْآنُ إِنَّمَا هُوَ خَطٌّ مَسْطُورٌ بَيْنَ دَفَّتَيْنِ، لَا يَنْطِقُ إِنَّمَا يَتَكَلَّمُ بِهِ الرِّجَالُ
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج۲ ص۶۸۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1369
> *English:* "We did not make men the judges; we made the Qur'an the judge. And this Qur'an is only writing inscribed between two covers — it does not speak; it is men who speak by it."

**عبرت:** A slogan that cannot be argued with usually cannot be applied either.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST55 · Whoever comes to this banner is safe

### GSA/E-ST58 · What shall I say to my Lord?
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 37–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة and البصرة marked.

**What happened:** معاوية ؓ wrote to أبو موسى الأشعري ؓ in his own hand, offering الكوفة for one
of his sons and البصرة for the other, and an open door for the rest of his life, and asked for a
reply in his own hand. الذهبي prints the reply; the editor traces it through three routes in
ابن سعد and calls the chain سند صحيح. He had come out of البصرة with six hundred dirhams and
nothing else.

**The statement:**
> أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَإِنَّكَ كَتَبْتَ إِلَيَّ فِي جَسِيْمِ أَمْرِ الأُمَّةِ، فَمَاذَا أَقُوْلُ لِرَبِّي إِذَا قَدِمْتُ عَلَيْهِ، لَيْسَ لِي فِيْمَا عَرَضْتَ مِنْ حَاجَةٍ، وَالسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۲ ص۳۹۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2376
> *English:* "To proceed: you have written to me about a grave matter of this Umma. What shall I say to my Lord when I come before Him? I have no need of what you have offered. And peace be upon you."

**عبرت:** The man the room has been taught to laugh at turned down two provinces in four lines.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST59 · No settled state of affairs came out of it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 or شعبان 38 AH, دومة الجندل `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** دومة الجندل, between the two camps.

**What happened:** The arbitration is the part of this window the room already "knows", and the
version it knows is not in our books. الذهبي states the sequence and stops: أبو موسى ؓ deposed
علي ؓ, deposed معاوية ؓ, proposed ابن عمر ؓ — and nothing came of it. He then gives his own
verdict on the man, which the room also has not heard.

**The statement:**
> وَلاَ رَيْبَ أَنَّ غُلاَةَ الشِّيْعَةِ يُبْغِضُوْنَ أَبَا مُوْسَى -رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ- لِكَوْنِهِ مَا قَاتَلَ مَعَ عَلِيٍّ، ثُمَّ لَمَّا حَكَّمَهُ عَلِيٌّ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ عَزَلَهُ، وَعَزَلَ مُعَاوِيَةَ، وَأَشَارَ بِابْنِ عُمَرَ؛ فَمَا انْتَظَمَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ حَالٌ.
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۲ ص۳۹۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2374
> *English:* "There is no doubt that the extreme Shīʿa hold أبو موسى ؓ in hatred, because he did not fight alongside علي, and then, when علي made him arbitrator over his own case, he deposed him and deposed معاوية and proposed ابن عمر — and no settled state of affairs came out of that."

**عبرت:** Say what the book says and no more; the famous version of this story is not in the books
we use.

### GSA/E-ST60 · Weary of them, and they of me
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39–40 AH, الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة, with مصر and الشام lost.

**What happened:** In the last year, with مصر gone, raiding parties reaching into العراق and his

> *English:* "O God, I have wearied of them and they of me, and I have come to dislike them and they me; so give me in exchange for them someone better than them, and give them in exchange for me someone worse than me."

**عبرت:** He asked for the exchange, and the ummah got it.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST61 · Imprison him, and treat his captivity well
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 40 AH, الكوفة `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة, the mosque.

**What happened:** علي ؓ was struck on his way into the mosque at dawn and lived two days. The
people asked whether they should not kill the whole of the tribe the assassin came from. ابن كثير
gives the answer, and on the same page the second instruction: no one is to be killed for him but
his killer. Asked whether he would name a successor, he said he would leave them as the Messenger of
God ﷺ had left them.

> *English:* "He said: 'No; but imprison him and treat his captivity well. If I die, kill him; and if I live, then wounds are subject to retaliation.'"

**عبرت:** Two days from death, and he is still holding the line against collective punishment.

### GSA/E-ST62 · God knows whether we were right or wrong
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map — the guardrail slide.

**What happened:** الذهبي records علي ؓ giving his own account of how he came to the caliphate.
He does not claim it was settled; he says he judged himself the most entitled, took it up, and
leaves the question of whether that was right to God. On another page of the same ترجمة he names
the two kinds of people who are destroyed on his account — a hater who fabricates and a lover who
goes to excess.

**The statement:**

> *English:* "Then I saw that I was the most entitled of them to this affair, so I took it up — so God knows whether we were right or whether we were wrong."

**عبرت:** The principal himself will not settle it. Nobody in this room has to either.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST63 · Two men are destroyed on my account
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 35–40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** no map — QA slide.

**What happened:** الذهبي preserves a sentence of علي ؓ's that names exactly the two failures this

exaggerates. Both destroy themselves, and both do it in his name.

**The statement:**

> *English:* "Two men are destroyed on my account: a hater who fabricates, and a lover who goes to excess."

**عبرت:** Both errors are made out of feeling, and he ruled out both of them himself.

### GSA/E-ST64 · I disliked to kill you over a kingdom
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الأول 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة → المدائن → الشام; the map goes quiet.

**What happened:** الحسن ؓ took the bayʿa at الكوفة on the day his father died, on one condition —
that they would make peace with whomever he made peace and fight whomever he fought. He met
معاوية ؓ with, in الذهبي's phrase, squadrons like mountains, and عمرو بن العاص ؓ said aloud that
these were squadrons that would not turn until they had killed their opposite numbers. He made the
peace instead. Asked afterwards whether he had done it out of fear, he answered in eight words.

**The statement:**
> فَقَالَ: لاَ، وَلَكِنْ كَرِهتُ أَنْ أَقتلَكُم عَلَى المُلْكِ
> — سیر أعلام النبلاء ج۳ ص۲۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/10906/2880
> *English:* "He said: no — but I disliked to kill you over a kingdom."

The editor notes a break in the chain of this report (سیر ج۳ ص۲۷۲); say so once and use it.

**عبرت:** He had the army. He gave up the office. That is the closing image of the session.

**Hands-up?** yes — *who would have fought, with an army like that behind them?*

### GSA/E-ST65 · The Year of the Community
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the closing map — one authority, from خراسان to إفريقية.

**What happened:** The Prophet ﷺ had said, on the منبر with the boy beside him, that this son of his
was a chief and that God would reconcile two great parties of the Muslims through him; البخاري
carries it. ابن كثير gives the hadith that the caliphate after him was thirty years and then
kingship, and observes that the thirty were completed only by الحسن ؓ's six months. The year the
fighting stopped got a name.

**The statement:**
> وسمِّيَ هذا العام عام الجماعة لاجتماع الكلمة فيه على أمير واحد بعد الفُرقة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۸ ص۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3769
> *English:* "And this year was named the Year of the Community, because the word gathered in it upon one commander after division."

**عبرت:** The ummah bought its unity back, and it paid for it with the caliphate.

**Hands-up?** no

### GSA/E-ST66 · The first of the kings of Islam, and the best of them
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 41 AH — the hand-off to session 4 `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the Line, with 41 AH marked as a hinge.

**What happened:** ابن كثير himself draws the line between the caliphate and what follows it, and
he draws it in 41 AH. He does not draw it as a fall: the sentence names معاوية ؓ the first of the
kings of Islam **and the best of them**. Next week begins on the other side of this line.

**The statement:**
> فأيام معاوية أول المُلْك، فهو أولُ ملوك الإسلام وخيارُهم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۸ ص۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3766
> *English:* "So the days of معاوية are the beginning of kingship; he is the first of the kings of Islam and the best of them."

**عبرت:** The line between خلافت and ملوكيت was drawn by ابن كثير, not by us — and so was the
praise on the far side of it.

**Hands-up?** no

## The dates, the frontier, and the gazetteer

*Source note: [`timeline-and-frontier-23-40ah.md`](../docs/research/timeline-and-frontier-23-40ah.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### TAF/E-TL1 · Where we stand when the room walks in
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **The bookend map** — session 2's closing map, unchanged: the shaded extent from برقة to بلخ, no year labels inside it.

**What happened:** The evening opens on exactly the map the room last saw. At the death of عمر ؓ the
Muslim lands ran from برقة and طرابلس in the west to بلخ and the river beyond خراسان in the east.
ابن کثیر sets the whole inventory down in a single running sentence inside عمر ؓ's own obituary — all
of الشام, الجزيرة, الموصل, أرمينية, مصر and الإسكندرية, and «he died with his armies upon the land of
الرَّي».

**The statement:**

> وفتح الشام كلّه، والجزيرةَ والموصلَ، ومَيّا فارقين، وآمد، وأرْمينية، ومصر وإسكندرية. ومات وعساكرُه على بلاد الرّيّ. فتح من الشام اليَرْموك وبُصرى ودمشق والأرْدُن، وبَيْسان، وطَبَريَّة، والجابية، وفلسطين، والرَّمْلة، وعَسْقَلان، وَغَزة، والسواحل، والقُدْس. و (فتح) مصر وإسكندرية وطرابلس الغرب وبرقة، ومن مدن الشام: بعلبك، وحمص، وقنّسرين، وحلب، وأنطاكية و (فتح) الجزيرةَ وحرّان والرُّها والرَّقة ونَصيبين ورأس عين وسُمَيْساط
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۶۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3409
> *English:* "He conquered all of Syria, and al-Jazīra, and Mosul, and Mayyāfāriqīn, and Āmid, and Armenia, and Egypt and Alexandria. He died with his armies upon the land of al-Rayy. Of Syria he took al-Yarmūk and Buṣrā and Damascus and the Jordan, and Baysān, and Tiberias, and al-Jābiya, and Palestine, and al-Ramla, and Ascalon, and Gaza, and the coasts, and Jerusalem. And he took Egypt and Alexandria and Tripoli of the West and Barqa; and of the cities of Syria: Baalbek, and Ḥimṣ, and Qinnasrīn, and Aleppo, and Antioch. And he took al-Jazīra and Ḥarrān and al-Ruhā and al-Raqqa and Naṣībīn and Raʾs ʿAyn and Sumaysāṭ…"

**عبرت:** Before anything else happens tonight, fix the size of what is being governed. Everything
that follows is a question about holding it, not about taking it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAF/E-TL2 · The inventory keeps going
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 23 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the eastern half of the same extent lights, city by city as the names are read.

**What happened:** The inventory does not stop at الشام. It runs on through العراق and فارس and
خراسان, and ends with a clause worth hearing whole: *and his armies crossed the river repeatedly*.

**The statement:**

> وعين وردة وديار بكر وديار ربيعة وبلاد المَوْصل وأرْمينية جميعها، وبالعراق: القادسية والحيرة ونهر شير وساباط ومدائن كسرى وكورة الفرات ودجلة والأُبُلَّة والبصرة والأَهْواز وفارس ونَهاوند وهَمَذان والزَفي وقُومس وخراسان وإصْطخر وأصبهان والسّوس ومرو ونَيْسابور وجُرجان وأذْرَبيجان وغير ذلك، وقطعت جيوشه النهر مرارًا.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۲۶۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3410
> *English:* "…and ʿAyn Warda and Diyār Bakr and Diyār Rabīʿa and the lands of Mosul and all of Armenia; and in Iraq: al-Qādisiyya and al-Ḥīra and Nahr Shīr and Sābāṭ and the cities of Chosroes and the district of the Euphrates and the Tigris and al-Ubulla and Basra and al-Ahwāz and Fārs and Nahāwand and Hamadhān and [al-Rayy] and Qūmis and Khurāsān and Iṣṭakhr and Iṣfahān and al-Sūs and Marw and Nīsābūr and Jurjān and Adharbayjān and other than that; and his armies crossed the river repeatedly."

**عبرت:** A list read slowly is a map. The room does not need to know every name — it needs to feel
how long the list is.

⚠ **Production note, not for the room:** the printed text carries «والزَفي», which is no place. The
reading is الرَّي. Do not project the word.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL3 · Seventeen years
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. The timeline strip alone, with the whole evening's span lit and the rest of the Line dark.

**What happened:** From the بيعة of عثمان ؓ in محرم 24 to the تسليم of الحسن ؓ in 41 is seventeen
years. The whole of tonight sits inside it.

**عبرت:** Everything in this evening happened inside a span shorter than most of the room has held
its current job.

**Hands-up?** Yes — *how many years do you think tonight covers?* Take three guesses, then show the
strip.

### TAF/E-TL4 · The year of the nosebleed
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 24 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. A single year on the strip.

**What happened:** 24 AH has a name of its own in both books — **عام الرعاف**, the year of the
nosebleed — and عثمان ؓ was kept from the حج that year by it. The books name years by what happened in
them, not by numbers alone.

**عبرت:** A calendar that names its years remembers differently from one that numbers them.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL5 · Four reports, and the author ranks them
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** محرم 24 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map. Four lines of text appearing one at a time, the last two greyed as the author grades them.

**What happened:** On what day the بيعة to عثمان ؓ was given, البدایہ prints four reports and does not
leave them equal. Of one it says «وهذا غريب جدًا». Of the next, «وهذا أغرب من الذي قبله». A fourth
gives a year in which عمر ؓ was still alive. What is left standing is the fourth: **3 محرم 24, at the
عصر prayer, between the أذان and the إقامة**.

**عبرت:** The book does not hide its uncertainty and it does not stop at it either. It shows the work
and then says which report it trusts.

**Hands-up?** no
