### TAF/E-TL6 · Twelve years, and what they did to the map
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 24–35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **The high-water map.** The 23 AH extent in one shade, and the 35 AH extent growing out of it in a second — إفريقية, قبرص and the sea, the Caucasus treaties, خراسان to the Oxus, كابل.

**What happened:** In twelve years the frontier reached the far coast of إفريقية, the islands of the
Roman sea, the Caucasus passes, the river beyond خراسان and the gates of كابل. The two books together
carry every stage of it, region by region, with its year.

**عبرت:** The largest expansion in the whole story happens in the years the room is least likely to
have heard about.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAF/E-TL7 · The refusal that was reversed
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 23 → 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the Mediterranean, empty of any Muslim marker at 23, then a fleet marker and قبرص at 35.

**What happened:** At 23 AH there is **no Muslim fleet at all** — عمر ؓ had refused to put Muslims on
ships. By 35 AH قبرص is taken and tributary, a standing fleet raids summer and winter, the Roman
battle fleet has been broken at **ذات الصواري**, and the strait of القسطنطينية has been reached.

**عبرت:** One decision reversed opened an entire direction the map had never had.

**Hands-up?** Yes — *at the start of this story, how many ships do you think the Muslims had?*

---

### TAF/E-TL8 · Three places where it had already gone backwards
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32–35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** three red marks on the 35 AH map — **بلنجر** beyond the Caucasus, **زرنج** in سجستان, and the **جرجان** road.

**What happened:** The high-water map is not all high water. Beyond the Caucasus at **بلنجر** in 32
the army was beaten, the commander killed and the force split in two. At **زرنج** the deputy was
thrown out as 35 closed. The **جرجان** road was unsafe again. All three are on the same pages as the
conquests.

**عبرت:** The frontier had begun to give in three places before a single Muslim raised a sword
against another.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL9 · A treaty that outlasted everyone
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** from 20 AH, still standing at 35 `[SOURCED — الکامل]` · **Map:** the Nile, south of مصر — a line that is drawn but never crossed.

**What happened:** النوبة, south of مصر, was raided and **not beaten**. What stood in place of a
conquest was a standing treaty of mutual gifts, confirmed by عثمان ؓ and by every ruler after him.
الکامل tells it under 20 AH, in the chapter on the conquest of مصر.

**عبرت:** One of the borders on this map was fixed by an agreement, not a battle — and it was the one
that lasted.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAF/E-TL10 · The last king
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 31 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** مرو lights; the whole Sasanian shading goes out at once.

**What happened:** يزدجرد بن شهريار, the last king of the house of أردشير بن بابك, was killed
near **مرو** by a miller. Both books put it in 31. Neither will choose between the four or five accounts
of how it happened, and ابن الأثير says so outright.

**عبرت:** An empire of four hundred years ends in a sentence, and the historian will not even tell
you which version of the sentence is true.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAF/E-TL11 · A hundred men of بدر were still alive
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. A large statement slide: **100**.

**What happened:** عبد الرحمن بن عوف ؓ died in 32 leaving four hundred dinars to **each surviving man
of بدر** — «وكانوا مئة», and they were a hundred. That is the one hard number our pages yield for how
much of the first generation was still in the world.

**عبرت:** Read the number slowly. The people who fought at بدر were still in the room when this story
begins.

**Hands-up?** Yes — *how many men of بدر do you think were still alive at this point?*

---

### TAF/E-TL12 · The heaviest year on the register
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 32 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. Four names appearing on a dark screen.

**What happened:** البدایہ files a full obituary chapter for 32 AH and it is the heaviest in the
window: **العباس ؓ**, the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, at eighty-eight · **عبد الله بن مسعود ؓ** · **عبد الرحمن
بن عوف ؓ** at seventy-five · and **أبو ذر ؓ** at الربذة in ذو الحجة, with nobody present but his wife
and children.

**عبرت:** The generation that had seen it was going, year by year, while the argument about who
should lead was still ahead.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL13 · The years with no register at all
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 24–29, 31, 33–36, 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. The timeline strip, with the years that carry an obituary chapter lit and the rest dark.

**What happened:** البدایہ does not file an obituary chapter under every year. In this window it files
one under **23, 30, 32, 37, 38 and 39** — and for **24–29, 31, 33–36 and 40 there is no chapter at
all**. The gaps are in the book, not in the history.

**عبرت:** When a source is silent about a year, that is a fact about the source. It is worth saying
out loud rather than filling in.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL14 · Where we stand now — the hinge
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 18 ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **The second "where we stand now" map** — the full 35 AH extent, one colour, one command. The last time the map is one colour for thirty years.

**What happened:** On a Friday — البدایہ says **«بلا خلاف»** that it was a Friday — eighteen nights
into ذو الحجة of the year 35, عثمان ؓ was killed in his house at المدینہ. His caliphate had run
**twelve years less twelve days**. The map at that moment is the largest and the last undivided one
the evening will show.

**The statement:**

> ثم كان قتله ﵁ في يوم الجمعة بلا خلاف. قال سيف بن عمر عن مشايخه: في آخر ساعة منها، ونص عليه مصعب (٦) بن الزبير وآخرون. وقال آخرون ضحوة (نهارها)، وهذا أشبه، وكان ذلك لثماني عشرة ليلة خلت من ذي الحجة على المشهور، وقيل في أيام التشريق
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3489
> *English:* "Then his killing was on a Friday, without disagreement. سيف بن عمر said, from his shaykhs: in the last hour of it — and مصعب بن الزبير and others stated that. Others said mid-morning, and this is more likely. And that was when eighteen nights of ذو الحجة had passed, according to the better-known view; and it is said during أيام التشريق."

**عبرت:** The map stops growing on this page. Everything after it is about the line inside the map,
not the line around it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAF/E-TL15 · Three hedges, and then one flat sentence
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 35 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** المدینہ — البقيع, and حش كوكب just east of it.

**What happened:** On the page that cannot settle the hour, or the day, or even the year, the same
author comes to the grave and the hedging stops completely: *as for the place of his grave, there is
no disagreement.* **حش كوكب, east of البقيع** — with a great dome built over it in the days of
بنو أمية, standing when he wrote.

**The statement:**

> وأما موضع قبره فلا خلاف أنه (دفن) بحشّ كوكب -شرقي البقيع- وقد بني عليه في زمن (٩) بني أمية قبة عظيمة وهي باقية إلى اليوم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۳۴۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3490
> *English:* "As for the place of his grave, there is no disagreement that he was buried at حش كوكب — east of البقيع — and a great dome was built over it in the time of بنو أمية, and it remains to this day."

**عبرت:** The same book that gives you three answers to one question gives you one answer to another,
and tells you which is which. That is what a historian's honesty looks like.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### TAF/E-TL16 · The year with the most dates in it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. The timeline strip zoomed to one year, twelve month-ticks, eight of them marked.

**What happened:** 36 AH carries more dated events than any other year of the window: the letter in
صفر · the march in ربيع الآخر · الحوأب · the first engagement at البصرة five nights from the end of
ربيع الآخر · الجمل in جمادى الآخرة · عائشة ؓ's departure on **Saturday 1 رجب** · علي ؓ's entry into
الكوفة on **Monday 12 رجب** · the march up the الفرات in ذو القعدة · and صفين in ذو الحجة.

**عبرت:** A year in a book can be one line or it can be a hundred pages. This one is a hundred pages,
and that itself tells you what the author thought mattered.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL17 · Two dates in one volume, and nobody reconciles them
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** جمادى الآخرة 36 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map. Two dates side by side on one screen.

**What happened:** Both books put the two armies camping outside البصرة at **mid جمادى الآخرة**.
ابن كثير, in the same volume, dates the deaths of طلحة ؓ and الزبير ؓ to **Thursday, ten nights into
جمادى الآخرة**. Both statements are his. Neither book reconciles them.

**The statement:**

> وكان قتله يوم الخميس لعشر خلون من جمادى الآخرة سنة ست وثلاثين وقد نيف على الستين (٥) بست أو سبع.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۳۳ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3579
> *English:* "And his killing was on Thursday, ten nights into جمادى الآخرة of the year thirty-six, and

**عبرت:** The honest date is the wider one. «جمادى الآخرة 36» is true; anything narrower is a choice
the book did not make.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL18 · The capital moves
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Monday 12 رجب 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **المدینہ dims; الكوفة lights.** The seat of the caliphate moves out of the Hijaz for the first time.

**What happened:** After البصرة, علي ؓ went up to **الكوفة** and entered it on **Monday, twelve nights
into رجب of the year 36**, and made it his seat. From this date the caliphate is governed from العراق.

**عبرت:** The centre of the Muslim world moved off the map the room has been looking at since session
one, and it never fully came back.

**Hands-up?** Yes — *where has the capital been until now? Where is it after tonight?*

### TAF/E-TL19 · One watering place
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ذو الحجة 36 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **صفين on the الفرات**, the ford marked, the two camps either side. **Nothing else on the map** — see the warning below.

**What happened:** Both armies converged on the الفرات at a place called **صفين**. The books describe
the ground in six words: *by the الفرات, east of the land of الشام*, *level and wide*, with **one
watering place**. معاوية ؓ's army reached the water first and posted أبو الأعور السلمي on it.

**عبرت:** The first thing two Muslim armies had to negotiate about was water.

⚠ **Production warning, not for the room:** *that six-word description is the entire description
either book gives.* **Any detailed battle map of صفين would be invention** and must be labelled
`[CONVENTIONAL-ESTIMATE]` if drawn at all.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL20 · Seven days, no result
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 1–7 صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. The timeline strip with seven ticks, none of them marked as a win.

**What happened:** From the first of صفر the two armies fought seven days by named champions — الأشتر,
هاشم بن عتبة ؓ, عمار بن ياسر ؓ, محمد ابن الحنفية, عبد الله بن عباس ؓ, قيس بن سعد ؓ — **and no side
beat the other in any of them**.

**عبرت:** Seven days of fighting between Muslims that decided nothing at all. That is the whole
argument against it, and the books make it by simply counting.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL21 · A Wednesday, and a document
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Wednesday 13 صفر 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. One date, large.

**What happened:** The arbitration document was written on **Wednesday, thirteen nights into صفر of
the year 37**. Both books give the same day. It is one of the few dates in this whole window that
carries no disagreement at all.

**عبرت:** The books remember the day a document was signed more exactly than they remember the day a
battle was fought. Paper leaves a better trail than a battlefield.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL22 · Twelve thousand stop at the gate
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37 AH, on the road back `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الكوفة lights; **حروراء** marked just outside it, as a separate camp.

**What happened:** On the road back, as the army neared الكوفة, about twelve thousand men withdrew
from it. They refused to live with him in his town and camped at a place called **حروراء**, outside
the gates.

**The statement:**

> ولما كان قد قارب دخول الكوفة اعتزل (٨) من جيشه قريبٌ من - اثني عشر ألفًا - وهم الخوارج، وأبوا أن يساكنوه في بلده، ونزلوا (٩) بمكان يقال له حروراء
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۲ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3618
> *English:* "And when he had nearly entered الكوفة, about twelve thousand of his army withdrew — and they are the خوارج — and they refused to live with him in his town, and camped at a place called حروراء."

**عبرت:** A split that begins as a camp outside a city and a refusal to come in.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL23 · Nine stages from each
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** رمضان 37 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **دومة الجندل / أذرح**, marked midway between الكوفة and الشام, with the nine stages counted out on each side.

**What happened:** The two arbiters met, each with four hundred horse, at **دومة الجندل at أذرح** —
which the book itself explains is the **halfway point between الكوفة and الشام, nine stages from each
of the two**. Companions came to watch: ابن عمر, ابن الزبير, المغيرة بن شعبة and others.

**The statement:**

> بعث أربعمئة فارس مع شريح بن هانئ، ومعهم أبو موسى، وعبد الله بن عباس، وإليه الصلاة، وبعث معاوية عمرو بن العاص في أربعمئة فارس من أهل الشام ومنهم عبد الله بن عمرو (٨)، فتوافوا بدومة الجندل بأذرح - وهي نصف [المسافة] بين الكوفة والشام، بينها وبين كل من البلدين تسع مراحل
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۴۷۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3623
> *English:* "He sent four hundred horse with شريح بن هانئ, and with them أبو موسى and عبد الله بن عباس — and the prayer was his; and معاوية sent عمرو بن العاص with four hundred horse of أهل الشام, among them عبد الله بن عمرو. They met at دومة الجندل at أذرح — which is the halfway point between الكوفة and الشام, nine stages from each of the two."

**عبرت:** They chose a place that belonged to neither side and was equally far from both. The
geography of the meeting was itself part of the settlement.

⚠ **Production note, not for the room:** دومة الجندل and أذرح are far apart on a modern map. The book
names them together. **Mark one point, label it with the book's phrase, and do not resolve the
pairing.**

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL24 · 37 or 38 — and the author says which he prefers
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 37–38 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** **النهروان** marked east of the Tigris, on the canal.

**What happened:** البدایہ narrates النهروان under 37, then records that **ابن جرير** held it was
in **38** and declared 38 correct — and adds, in his own voice, «**وهو الأشبه**», *and that is the more
likely*. الکامل narrates it inside 37 and adds «وقيل: كانت الوقعة سنة ثمان وثلاثين».

**The statement:**

> كان في سنة ثمان وثلاثين وصححه ابن جرير، قلت: وهو الأشبه كما سننبه عليه في السنة الآتية إن شاء اللّه تعالى.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۲۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3667
> *English:* "…it was in the year thirty-eight, and ابن جرير declared that correct. I say: and that is the more likely, as we shall point out under the coming year, if Allah most high wills."

**عبرت:** Two books, three placings, and an author who tells you which way he leans and why. That is
not a weakness in the record. It is the record working.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL25 · The province that changes colour
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 38 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **مصر changes colour** — the single biggest change on the map between 36 and 41.

**What happened:** In 38 AH **مصر** passes from محمد بن أبي بكر ؓ to معاوية ؓ, with عمرو بن العاص ؓ as
its governor. Read the governor tables for 37, 38 and 39 across and this is the only province that
moves. **الشام never moves at all**; and in 37 **four of علي ؓ's provinces — مكة, المدينة, اليمن and
البصرة — are held by four brothers, the sons of العباس**.

**عبرت:** One province moved in five years, and it moved between Muslims. Nothing was lost to anyone
outside.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL26 · The year of columns
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** arrows running **inward**, out of الشام into العراق — عين التمر, هيت — and not one arrow running outward.

**What happened:** Through 39 AH column after column went from الشام into علي ؓ's provinces — عين
التمر, هيت and others. The حج of that year was contested and had to be settled by compromise, the two
claimants standing aside for a third.

**عبرت:** Look at the direction of every arrow on this map. For the first time in the story, they all
point inward.

**Hands-up?** Yes — *which way are the arrows pointing?*

### TAF/E-TL27 · One column still going east
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 39 AH `[SOURCED — الکامل]` · **Map:** a single thin arrow leaving العراق for **السند**, far to the east, alone on the map.

**What happened:** In 39 AH a **volunteer** raid went out to **السند** by علي ؓ's order under الحارث
بن مرة العبدي. He stayed on campaign until he was killed at **القيقان** in 42 AH. **It is the only
outward movement of the frontier recorded anywhere between 36 and 40.**

**عبرت:** While everything else was turned inward, one column was still going east — and it is the
thread that reaches this room, because that road ends in السند. Session 8 picks it up.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL28 · A truce, in one book only
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40 AH `[SOURCED — الکامل only]` · **Map:** a line drawn between العراق and الشام, with neither side's arrow crossing it.

**What happened:** الکامل records, after long correspondence, a **مهادنة**: the war set down, العراق
to علي ؓ and الشام to معاوية ؓ, neither to enter the other's country on a raid. **البدایہ's pages for
this window do not carry it at all.**

**The statement:**

> وَفِيهَا جَرَتْ مُهَادَنَةٌ بَيْنَ عَلِيٍّ وَمُعَاوِيَةَ بَعْدَ مُكَاتَبَاتٍ طَوِيلَةٍ عَلَى وَضْعِ الْحَرْبِ، وَيَكُونُ لَعَلِيٍّ الْعِرَاقُ، وَلِمُعَاوِيَةَ الشَّامُ، لَا يَدْخُلُ أَحَدُهُمَا بَلَدَ الْآخَرِ بِغَارَةٍ.
> — الکامل فی التاریخ ج٢ ص٧٣٥ · https://shamela.ws/book/21712/1424
> *English:* "And in it a truce came about between ʿAlī and Muʿāwiya, after long correspondence, on the laying down of the war: that al-ʿIrāq should be ʿAlīʼs and Syria Muʿāwiyaʼs, neither of the two entering the otherʼs country on a raid."

**عبرت:** One book has it and one does not. Say which book, and the room learns more about how
history reaches us than any lecture on method could teach them.

⚠ **Attribute it to الکامل by name on the slide.** No date within the year, no place, no negotiators
and no text of the agreement survive.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL29 · A Friday before dawn
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** Friday 17 رمضان 40 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. One dark slide, one date.

**What happened:** علي ؓ was struck going out to the فجر prayer and died of it. ابن كثير sums the
matter up plainly: **Friday, at the last hour of the night, the seventeenth of رمضان of the year
forty** — and notes that it is also said he was killed in ربيع الأول, «and the first is the soundest
and the best known, and God knows best».

**The statement:**

> وحاصل الأمر أن عليًا قتل يوم الجمعة سحرًا وذلك لسبع عشرة خلت من رمضان من سنة أربعين وقيل إنه قتل في ربيع الأول والأول هو الأصح الأشهر والله أعلم.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۵۴۹ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3695
> *English:* "The upshot of the matter is that علي was killed on Friday at the last hour of the night, on the seventeenth night of رمضان of the year forty; and it is said that he was killed in ربيع الأول — and the first is the soundest and the best known, and God knows best."

**عبرت:** The most contested thirty years in the record close on a date the historian is willing to
state flatly.

**Hands-up?** no

**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ربيع الأول 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. The timeline strip: a bracket opening at ربيع الأول 11 and closing at ربيع الأول 41.

**What happened:** ابن كثير makes the handover the completion of the thirty years of the hadith «الخلافة
بعدي ثلاثون سنة ثم تكون ملكًا» — **from the Prophet's ﷺ death in ربيع الأول 11 to ربيع الأول 41**. He
states the arithmetic himself and builds the period out of it.

**عبرت:** The bracket that opened in session one closes tonight. Thirty years, and the room has now
walked the whole of them.

### TAF/E-TL31 · Where we stand now — one command again
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** 41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** **The third "where we stand now" map** — the same extent as 35 AH, back to **one colour**, the two-colour command split of 40 gone.

**What happened:** 41 AH is called **عام الجماعة**, and البدایہ gives the reason twice in almost the
same words: *the word gathered in it upon one commander after division*.

**The statement:**

> وسمِّيَ هذا العام عام الجماعة لاجتماع الكلمة فيه على أمير واحد بعد الفُرقة.
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۸ ص۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3769
> *English:* "And this year was named the Year of the Community, because the word gathered in it upon one commander after division."

**عبرت:** The map ends the evening the same size it was at the start of it and a single colour again.
What happened in between was not about the map.

### TAF/E-TL32 · 40 or 41 — and the book gives both
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** 40–41 AH `[SOURCED, disputed]` · **Map:** No map. Two years side by side.

**What happened:** On the year of the بيعة to الحسن ؓ, ابن كثير sets down two datings and does not
quietly choose: the well-known view is **40** — «and it is for this that it is called عام الجماعة» —
while **ابن جرير and others of the علماء السير** put it at the beginning of **41**. He then narrates
the handover under 41.

**The statement:**

> ثم المشهور أن مبايعة الحسن لمعاوية كانت في سنة أربعين، ولهذا يقال له عام الجماعة، لاجتماع الكلمة فيه على معاوية
> — البدایہ والنہایہ ج۷ ص۶۱۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/30097/3763
> *English:* "Then the well-known view is that al-Ḥasan's giving allegiance to Muʿāwiyah was in the year forty, and it is for this that it is called the Year of the Community, because the word gathered in it upon Muʿāwiyah."

**عبرت:** Even the name of the year has two years attached to it, and the author prints both.

**Hands-up?** no

### TAF/E-TL34 · The register, as a slide
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** across 23–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map. A two-column table: *what one book says* · *what the other says*.

**What happened:** Nine of the years in tonight's story are given differently by the books we are
reading. إصطخر: 22 or 23. قبرص: 28, and 33 is also reported. أرمينية: 25 or 31. النهروان: 37 or 38.
بسر's expedition: 40 or 42. The بيعة to الحسن ؓ: 40 or 41.

**عبرت:** This is not a list of the books' failures. It is the list of the places where they refuse

### TAF/E-TL35 · The gaps we cannot fill, said out loud
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** across 23–41 AH `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Four things this evening will not tell the room, because the books do not: what
the ground at صفين looked like · what the expedition to الأندلس actually did · how many died at ذات
الصواري · and which of the accounts of يزدجرد's death is true, since ابن الأثير himself refuses to
choose.

**عبرت:** «واللہ أعلم» is not a way of avoiding a question. In these books it is an answer, and the

## ابن خلدون: how he reads the fitna (framing only)

*Source note: [`ibn-khaldun-on-the-fitna.md`](../docs/research/ibn-khaldun-on-the-fitna.md) — read it for the pages behind these cards.*

### IKO/E-IK1 · The conquests finish and the state is complete
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the close of the conquest era, no year given on the page `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** the four garrison cities light at once — البصرہ, الکوفہ, الشام, مصر.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون does not open the troubles of this period with a complaint about anyone. He opens them with a change in the shape of the community itself. The conquests are finished, the state is complete, and the Arabs have come to rest in garrison cities along the frontier with the nations they have just defeated. Everything he says afterwards about the agitation is built on that one sentence.

**The statement:**
> لما استكمل الفتح واستكمل للملّة الملك ونزل العرب بالأمصار في حدود ما بينهم وبين الأمم من البصرة والكوفة والشام ومصر
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1383
> *English:* "When the conquest was completed, and the kingship of the community was completed, and the Arabs settled in the garrison cities along the frontiers between themselves and the nations — Basra, Kufa, Syria and Egypt …"

**عبرت:** A community is tested by the end of its emergency as surely as by the emergency itself.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: "When an army stops fighting and settles in a new city, what is the first thing that changes?"

---

### IKO/E-IK2 · Two kinds of Arab, one with صحبة and one with conquests
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the same passage, no year given `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** الحجاز against the frontier cities — the line runs between them.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون now draws the distinction his whole analysis turns on. On one side stand those who had the companionship of the Messenger ﷺ and were formed by his guidance — the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, of Quraysh and of the people of the Ḥijāz. On the other side stand the great tribal bulk of the Arabs: Bakr b. Wāʾil, ʿAbd al-Qays and the rest of Rabīʿa, Azd, Kinda, Tamīm, Quḍāʿa. Very few of the second group had any standing in that companionship, but they had a foremost part in the conquests.

**The statement:**
> وكان المختصون بصحابة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والاقتداء بهداه وآدابه المهاجرين والأنصار من قريش وأهل الحجاز ومن ظفر بمثل ذلك من غيرهم. وأما سائر العرب من بني بكر بن وائل وعبد القيس وسائر ربيعة والأزد وكندة وتميم وقضاعة وغيرهم، فلم يكونوا من تلك الصحبة بمكان إلّا قليلا منهم وكان لهم في الفتوحات قدم
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۶ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1383
> *English:* "Those singled out by the companionship of the Messenger ﷺ and by following his guidance and his manners were the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, of Quraysh and the people of the Ḥijāz, and whoever else attained the like of that. But as for the rest of the Arabs — Bakr b. Wāʾil, ʿAbd al-Qays and the rest of Rabīʿa, and Azd, Kinda, Tamīm, Quḍāʿa and others — they had no standing in that companionship, save a few of them; but they had a foremost part in the conquests."

**عبرت:** Two honours can grow in one community and not be the same honour.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### IKO/E-IK3 · The veins of the جاهلية begin to stir
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the reign of عثمان ؓ, ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** the frontier cities stay lit; nothing moves.

**What happened:** While the memory of prophecy was still fresh, ابن خلدون says, the older loyalties were held down by awe. Then the flood-tide receded, the condition was somewhat forgotten, the enemy was beaten and the kingship grew great. At that point, on his reading, the old tribal solidarities began to stir again. What the tribes found when they looked around was that leadership over them belonged to the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār — and their souls recoiled from it.

**The statement:**
> فلما انحسر ذلك العباب وتنوسي الحال بعض الشيء وذلّ العدو واستفحل الملك، كانت عروق الجاهلية تنفض ووجدوا الرئاسة عليهم للمهاجرين والأنصار من قريش وسواهم، فأنفت نفوسهم منه، ووافق أيام عثمان
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1384
> *English:* "Then, when that flood-tide receded, and the condition was somewhat forgotten, and the enemy was humbled, and the kingship grew great — the veins of the Jāhiliyya began to stir. They found that leadership over them belonged to the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār, of Quraysh and others; and their souls recoiled from that. And it fell out in the days of ʿUthmān."

**عبرت:** What an extraordinary time suppresses, an ordinary time brings back.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### IKO/E-IK4 · And it fell out in the days of عثمان ؓ
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Four words at the end of that sentence carry more weight than anything else in the passage. ابن خلدون does not say the trouble was caused by عثمان ؓ, and he does not say it was caused by what was done in his reign. He says it coincided with his days. On his own reading the pressure had been building whoever held the office, and the reign is when it reached its limit.

**The statement:**
> ووافق أيام عثمان
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1384
> *English:* "And it fell out in the days of ʿUthmān."

**عبرت:** The moment a strain becomes visible is not always the moment it was made.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### IKO/E-IK5 · How the pressure showed itself in the cities
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** the four garrison cities, all four at once.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون lists what the agitation actually looked like on the ground, and every item on his list is a behaviour rather than a charge. Men began to attack the governors openly. They held them to account for a glance or a passing thought, dragged their feet in obedience, and demanded that this governor be replaced and that one dismissed. And they poured out condemnation of عثمان ؓ himself.

**The statement:**
> فكانوا يظهرون الطعن في ولاته بالأمصار، والمؤاخذة لهم باللحظات والخطرات، والاستبطاء [١] عليهم في الطاعات والتجني بسؤال الاستبدال منهم والعزل، ويفيضون في النكير على عثمان
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1384
> *English:* "So they began openly to attack his governors in the garrison cities; to hold them to account for glances and passing thoughts; to drag their feet in obedience to them; to seek grievances by demanding their replacement and dismissal; and to pour out condemnation of ʿUthmān."

**عبرت:** When the will to find fault comes first, the faults are never hard to find.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### IKO/E-IK6 · Four Companions are sent to investigate and find nothing
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** four arrows out of المدینہ — to الکوفہ, البصرہ, الشام, مصر — and four back.

**What happened:** عثمان ؓ did not answer the complaints from المدینہ alone. He sent men to the cities to bring him back the sound report of what was happening there: محمد بن مسلمة ؓ to الکوفہ, أسامة بن زيد ؓ to البصرہ, عبد الله بن عمر ؓ to الشام, عمّار بن ياسر ؓ to مصر, and others to places besides. They came back and told him that they had found nothing objectionable, and that neither the notables of the Muslims nor the common people had found anything objectionable either.

**The statement:**
> وبعث الى الأمصار من يأتيه بصحيح الخبر: محمد بن مسلمة إلى الكوفة، وأسامة بن زيد إلى البصرة، وعبد الله بن عمر إلى الشام، وعمّار بن ياسر إلى مصر وغيرهم إلى سوى هذه، فرجعوا إليه فقالوا: ما أنكرنا شيئا ولا أنكره أعيان المسلمين ولا عوامهم
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۷ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1384
> *English:* "And he sent to the garrison cities men who would bring him the sound report: Muḥammad b. Maslama to Kufa, Usāma b. Zayd to Basra, ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar to Syria, ʿAmmār b. Yāsir to Egypt, and others to places besides these. They returned to him and said: we found nothing objectionable, and neither the notables of the Muslims nor their common people found anything objectionable."

**عبرت:** An inquiry that answers a rumour does not always end it.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: "If a report of trouble reaches you from four cities at once, what do you do first?"

---

### IKO/E-IK7 · The خمس of إفريقية and the charge ابن خلدون refuses
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** the إفريقية campaign under عثمان ؓ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** إفريقية, far west on the North African coast.

**What happened:** One of the heaviest charges in circulation was that عثمان ؓ had handed the fifth of the spoils of إفريقية to مروان بن الحكم outright. ابن خلدون, narrating the campaign, states the matter differently and then grades the other version in his own voice. مروان bought it, for five hundred thousand dīnārs. Some people say it was given to him, he writes — and that is not sound. What was in fact given, he adds, was the fifth of the fifth, to ابن أبي سرح, from the first campaign.

**The statement:**
> وأرسل ابن الزبير بالفتح والخمس فاشتراه مروان بن الحكم بخمسمائة ألف دينار، وبعض الناس يقول أعطاه إياه ولا يصح، وإنما أعطى ابن أبي سرح خمس الخمس من الغزوة الأولى.
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۷۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1371
> *English:* "And Ibn al-Zubayr sent the news of the victory and the fifth; and Marwān b. al-Ḥakam purchased it for five hundred thousand dīnārs. Some people say that he gave it to him outright, and that is not sound. What he did give was to Ibn Abī Sarḥ — the fifth of the fifth, from the first campaign."

**عبرت:** A charge repeated for centuries can fail the first time a historian checks it.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### IKO/E-IK8 · He makes the same correction again when he lists the grievances
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون is not content to correct the إفريقية story once. When he reaches the list of grievances themselves, he states the charge and then attaches the correction to it in the same breath. The sound position, he says, is that مروان bought the fifth for five hundred thousand — and that the sum was afterwards remitted to him. The two passages are not quite the same claim, so a slide takes one of them and not a blend of the two.

**The statement:**
> مع ما كان من إعطاء مروان خمس مغانم إفريقية والصحيح أنه اشتراه بخمسمائة ألف فوضعها عنه.
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1385
> *English:* "…together with the matter of giving Marwān the fifth of the spoils of Ifrīqiya — though the sound position is that he bought it for five hundred thousand, and [ʿUthmān] remitted that sum to him."

**عبرت:** A historian who repeats his correction has measured how far the error travelled.

**Hands-up?** no

---

### IKO/E-IK9 · The charge over the third call and the prayer at منى
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** المدینہ, and منى and عرفہ outside مکہ.

**What happened:** Two of the complaints were about worship rather than about money. The first was the adding of a third call to prayer on the Friday, given from الزوراء. The second was that عثمان ؓ prayed the full prayer at منى and at عرفہ, whereas in the lifetime of the Messenger ﷺ and under the two shaykhs after him the practice had been to shorten it. ابن خلدون states both charges plainly and in order, and adds nothing of his own to either.

**The statement:**
> زيادة النداء الثالث على الزوراء يوم الجمعة، وإتمامه الصلاة في منى وعرفة مع أن الأمر في حياة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والشيخين بعده كان على القصر.
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۵۸۸ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1385
> *English:* "The adding of a third call, at al-Zawrāʾ, on the day of Friday; and his completing the prayer at Minā and ʿArafa, although the practice in the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and of the two shaykhs after him, had been to shorten it."

**عبرت:** A dispute over a matter of judgement is not the same thing as a dispute over a principle.

**Hands-up?** no

### IKO/E-IK10 · "This is a judgement I formed" — and the Companions divided over it
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون gives عثمان ؓ's own answer to the charge, in عثمان ؓ's own mouth: this is a judgement I formed. **عبرت:** Where the Companions themselves differed, reporting the difference is the whole of what we owe.

### IKO/E-IK11 · أبو ذر ؓ and the severity of his زہد
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۲۳–۳۵ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** الشام, then المدینہ.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون reads the friction around أبو ذر ؓ as arising from أبو ذر ؓ's own scrupulousness, which he describes as intense. أبو ذر ؓ pressed people towards severities and towards renunciation of the world. **عبرت:** A standard a man keeps for himself becomes a different thing when a whole city is asked to keep it.

### IKO/E-IK23 · "With what there is no need to mention"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۵ھ, the last hours `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** In the last minutes ابن خلدون narrates a succession of men entering the house, and then he stops narrating. محمد بن أبي بكر came in and disputed with him at length — with what there is no need to mention. Then he felt shame, and went out. ابن خلدون is not a cautious writer, and this is a deliberate refusal: he declines to transmit what was said, on the stated ground that there is no need for it.

**The statement:**
> ودخل عليه محمد بن أبي بكر فحاوره طويلا بما لا حاجة إلى ذكره ثم استحيا وخرج.

> *English:* "And Muḥammad b. Abī Bakr came in to him and disputed with him at length, with what there is no need to mention; then he felt shame, and went out."

**عبرت:** Some words are recorded as having been spoken and still not repeated, and that is a form of honesty, not of concealment.

**Hands-up?** Before the card: "A historian knows exactly what was said in a room. Is there ever a reason not to write it down?"

### IKO/E-IK28 · "It is not fitting that pages be blackened with them"
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** written in the eighth century ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Immediately after naming his source, ابن خلدون states a rule of his craft. There is much to be found in the words of the historians, he says — reports carrying slanders and doubts against the great ones of the community. Most of them come from the people of partisan passions. And it is not fitting that pages be blackened with them.

### IKO/E-IK33 · The printed edition's own footnote sets a report aside
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** after the arbitration, ۳۷–۳۸ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

> [٢] قال ابن كثير في تاريخه: ان هذا لم يصحّ أهـ ولعلّ الدعاء كان لغير اللعن. قاله نصر.

> *English:* "Footnote [2]: Ibn Kathīr said in his history: this is not sound. — end of quotation. And perhaps the supplication was for something other than cursing. So said Naṣr."

**عبرت:** A footnote can carry a correction the main text never accepted.

### IKO/E-IK49 · Ten thousand counted, from both sides together
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** البصرہ, ۳۶ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون gives a figure for the dead and gives it once, without a range and without a source. The slain of both sides were counted, and they were ten thousand; of them a thousand men of ضبّة. It is a large, memorable number, which is exactly why it may not be used on his authority alone. It is recorded here so that it is never re-derived, and it stays out of every artifact unless البدایہ or الکامل carries it.

**The statement:**
> وأحصى القتلى من الجانبين فكانوا عشرة الاف منهم من ضبّة ألف رجل
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۶۲۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1417
> *English:* "And the slain of both sides were counted, and they were ten thousand; of them, from Ḍabba, a thousand men."

**عبرت:** The roundest numbers in a chronicle are the ones to check first.

**Hands-up?** no

### IKO/E-IK52 · The year the community came together
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** منتصف ۴۱ھ `[SOURCED]` — the year is ابن خلدون's and awaits corroboration · **Map:** the whole map, from الشام to العراق to مصر, shown as one for the first time since ۳۵ھ.

**عبرت:** A year can be named after the one thing the people in it most needed.

### IKO/E-IK53 · By contest, where before it had been by coming-together
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۴۱ھ, and looking back over the whole window `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map — this is the turn the whole series is built around.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون explains why the compilers place معاوية ؓ with the Umayyads rather than with the four before him, and the first of his two reasons is his whole analysis compressed. In his time the caliphate was held by contest, on account of the عصبية that had arisen in that age; before that it had been by choice and by coming-together. So they distinguished between the two conditions. معاوية ؓ was thus the first of the caliphs of contest and of عصبية — those whom, he adds, the people of partisan passions call kings.

**The statement:**
> الأوّل أنّ الخلافة لعهده كانت مغالبة لأجل ما قدّمناه من العصبية التي حدثت لعصره، وأمّا قبل ذلك كانت اختيارا واجتماع فميّزوا بين الحالتين، فكان معاوية أوّل خلفاء المغالبة والعصبيّة الذين يعبّر عنهم أهل الأهواء بالملوك
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۶۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1447
> *English:* "The first is that the caliphate in his time was [held] by contest, on account of what we have set out of the ʿaṣabiyya that arose in his age; whereas before that it was by choice and by coming-together. So they distinguished between the two conditions. Muʿāwiya was thus the first of the caliphs of contest and of ʿaṣabiyya — those whom the people of partisan passions call kings."

**عبرت:** What changed first was not who held the office but how the office came to be held.

### IKO/E-IK54 · His second reason is a matter of lineage and arrangement
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ۴۱ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون's second reason is prosaic and he presents it as such. The Umayyad caliphs were people of one lineage, and معاوية ؓ was the greatest of them, so he was placed with his own kin. The first four were of differing lineages, so they were set in one class together. He adds that عثمان ؓ was joined to them, though he belonged to this same lineage, because of his nearness to them in precedence. The printed edition has a typographical defect on this page, writing الخفاء where الخلفاء is meant.

**The statement:**
> الأمر الثاني في ذكر معاوية مع خلفاء بني أمية دون الخفاء الأربعة أنهم كانوا أهل نسب واحد وعظيمهم معاوية
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۶۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1448
> *English:* "The second matter, in mentioning Muʿāwiya with the caliphs of the Banū Umayya rather than with the four caliphs, is that they were people of one lineage, and the greatest of them was Muʿāwiya."

**عبرت:** Some of what looks like a judgement in a history book is only a decision about where to put a chapter.

### IKO/E-IK55 · Two kinds of ملك, and only one of them contradicts the خلافة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** ابن خلدون's own analysis `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون separates two things that are usually run together. The kingship that opposes, and indeed contradicts, the caliphate is tyranny — the Chosroes-like kind, whose outward marks عمر ؓ reproved in معاوية ؓ when he saw them. But the kingship that is dominance and mastery through عصبية and armed strength contradicts neither the caliphate nor prophethood. On his account the second is a fact about how power works, not a charge.

**The statement:**
> واعلم أنّ الملك الّذي يخالف بل ينافي الخلافة هو الجبروتيّة المعبر عنها بالكسرويّة التي أنكرها عمر على معاوية حين رأى ظواهرها، وأما الملك الّذي هو الغلبة والقهر بالعصبية والشوكة فلا ينافي الخلافة ولا النبوّة
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۶۵۰ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1447
> *English:* "Know that the kingship which opposes — indeed contradicts — the caliphate is tyranny, called 'Chosroes-like', which ʿUmar reproved in Muʿāwiya when he saw its outward marks. But the kingship which is dominance and mastery by ʿaṣabiyya and armed strength — that contradicts neither the caliphate nor prophethood."

**عبرت:** One word can cover two different things, and most quarrels about the word are quarrels about which one is meant.

**Hands-up?** no

### IKO/E-IK56 · The criterion: measure the deeds against the sound reports
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ابن خلدون's own analysis `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** Having refused to settle the matter by a label, ابن خلدون gives a rule instead. The rule is to set their deeds against what is sound in the reports, not against what is weak. Whoever's deeds run according to them is the successor of the Prophet ﷺ among the Muslims. Whoever's deeds depart from that is one of the kings of this world, and is called caliph only by a figure of speech.

**The statement:**
> والقانون في ذلك عرض أفعالهم على الصحيح من الأخبار لا بالواهي، فمن جرت أفعاله عليها فهو خليفة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المسلمين، ومن خرجت أفعاله عن ذلك فهو من ملوك الدنيا وإنما سمّي خليفة بالمجاز.
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۶۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1448
> *English:* "The rule in this is to measure their deeds against the sound reports, not the weak ones. Whoever's deeds run according to them is the successor of the Prophet ﷺ among the Muslims; and whoever's deeds depart from that is one of the kings of this world, and is called caliph only by a figure of speech."

**عبرت:** Measure against what is sound, not against what is weak — that is the rule this whole course is built on.

**Hands-up?** no

### IKO/E-IK57 · His reading of معاوية ؓ's motive
**Tier:** CUT · **When:** ابن خلدون's own analysis `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون offers a judgement about an inner motive, and it is recorded here for one reason only: an audience member may quote it, and the speaker should know exactly where it comes from and what kind of statement it is. He writes that معاوية ؓ did not seek kingship, nor its pomp, for the sake of amassing the world — but that the matter of عصبية drove him by its own nature, once the Muslims had taken possession of all the states and he was their caliph. It is a fourteenth-century historian's reading of a Companion's heart. It is not narrated from the platform as a finding.

**The statement:**
> ومعاوية لم بطلب الملك ولا أبّهته للاستكثار من الدنيا، وانما ساقه أمر العصبيّة بطبعها لمّا استولى المسلمون على الدول كلها وكان هو خليفتهم
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۶۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1448
> *English:* "Muʿāwiya did not seek kingship, nor its pomp, for the sake of amassing the world. Rather the matter of ʿaṣabiyya drove him by its own nature, once the Muslims had taken possession of all the states and he was their caliph."

**عبرت:** What was in a man's heart is the one thing a history book cannot hand over.

**Hands-up?** no

### IKO/E-IK58 · The عصبية that Islam does not forbid
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ابن خلدون's own essay opening volume three `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** This is the qualification without which his whole analysis would read as an accusation. What remained after Islam, he says, was the natural عصبية, which does not depart — a man's protective pride over his brother and his neighbour against being killed or wronged. Nothing removes it. Nor is it forbidden; rather it is sought after, and useful in jihād and in the call to the religion. So when he says the veins of the جاهلية stirred, he is not saying that the men of this window relapsed; he is saying a natural solidarity regained its political weight once the extraordinary conditions ended.

**The statement:**
> ولم يبق إلّا العصبية الطبيعية التي لا تفارق وهي بعزّة الرجل على أخيه وجاره في القتل والعدوان عليه، فهذه لا يذهبها شيء ولا هي محظورة بل هي مطلوبة ونافعة في الجهاد والدعاء إلى الدين
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۳ ص۴ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1450
> *English:* "There remained only the natural ʿaṣabiyya, which does not depart — the man's protective pride over his brother and his neighbour against being killed or wronged. Nothing removes this; nor is it forbidden. Rather it is sought after, and useful in jihād and in the call to the religion."

**عبرت:** A loyalty that is good in its place becomes something else when it decides who governs.

**Hands-up?** no

### IKO/E-IK59 · The بيعة in the middle of the year forty-one, and what he says had been forgotten
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** منتصف ۴۱ھ `[SOURCED]` — ابن خلدون's year, awaiting corroboration · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون states the settlement a second time in his own essay, and this time he attaches his explanation to it directly. The community agreed on the بيعة of معاوية ؓ in the middle of the year forty-one — when people had forgotten the matter of prophethood and the extraordinary events, and had returned to the affair of عصبية and mutual contest. The whole causal arc that began with the completion of the conquests closes on this clause.

> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۳ ص۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1451
> *English:* "And the community agreed on the bayʿa of Muʿāwiya in the middle of the year forty-one, when people had forgotten the matter of prophethood and the extraordinary events, and had returned to the affair of ʿaṣabiyya and mutual contest."

**عبرت:** An age ends when the memory that held it together stops being a living memory.

### IKO/E-IK60 · Why one side's forces held together better than the other's
**Tier:** CORE · **When:** ۳۷–۴۱ھ `[STANDARD]` (to verify) · **Map:** العراق's many tribal contingents against الشام's single standing army.

**What happened:** ابن خلدون compares the two armies and the comparison has no moral content at all. علي ؓ's forces were more numerous, he says, by virtue of the caliphate and of precedence — but they were drawn from all the various tribes, from ربيعة and يمن and others. معاوية ؓ's were the army of الشام, of قريش, the armed strength of مضر, settled in the Syrian frontier posts since the conquest. So his عصبية was harder, and his armed strength more decisive. The advantage he names is cohesion, and he grants the caliphate and the precedence to the other side in the same sentence.

**The statement:**
> كانت عساكر عليّ أكثر عددا لمكان الخلافة والفضل إلّا أنها من سائر القبائل من ربيعة ويمن وغيرهم، وجموع معاوية إنما هي جند الشام من قريش شوكة مضر وبأسهم نزلوا بثغور الشام منذ الفتح فكانت عصبيته أشدّ وأمضى شوكه
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۳ ص۵ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1451
> *English:* "ʿAlī's armies were more numerous, by virtue of the caliphate and of precedence — but they were from all the various tribes, from Rabīʿa and Yemen and others. Muʿāwiya's assemblies were the army of Syria, of Quraysh, the armed strength of Muḍar and their valour, who had settled in the Syrian frontier posts since the conquest. So his ʿaṣabiyya was harder and his armed strength more decisive."

**عبرت:** A body of men that holds together outlasts a larger body that does not, and that is a fact about cohesion, not about merit.

**Hands-up?** no

### IKO/E-IK61 · The volume closes, and the next one opens a دولة
**Tier:** GOOD · **When:** the join between volumes two and three `[SOURCED]` · **Map:** No map.

**What happened:** The physical shape of the book carries the argument. The second volume ends, and its closing line announces what the third will contain: the account of the Islamic states, beginning with the state of بنو أمية, following on from the caliphs of the first age of Islam, with their beginnings and the reports of their states one by one until each came to an end. Everything before the join is narrated as خلافة; everything after it is narrated as دولة.

**The statement:**
> تمت تكملة الجزء الثاني ويليه الجزء الثالث وأوّله الخبر عن الدول الإسلامية ونبدأ منها بدولة بني أمية معقبة لخلفاء صدر الإسلام وذكر أوليتهم وأخبار دولهم واحدة واحدة الى انقضائها
> — تاریخ ابن خلدون ج۲ ص۶۵۱ · https://shamela.ws/book/12320/1448
> *English:* "The completion of the second volume is finished. The third volume follows it, and its beginning is the account of the Islamic states — and we begin with the state of the Banū Umayya, following on from the caliphs of the first age of Islam — with the account of their beginnings and the reports of their states, one by one, until their ending."

**عبرت:** Where a historian ends one volume and begins another is itself a claim about where an age ended.

**Hands-up?** no
